items.statement: Full-year FY26 sales volume target of 18.5 million tons for SAIL products, excluding NMDC volumes
items.quote: For the full year, we are expecting somewhere around 18.5 million tons.

items.statement: FY26 capex target of INR7,500 crores approved by Board, with Q1 achievement of INR1,642 crores exceeding quarterly target
items.quote: And this year, we have kept a target of INR7,500 crores throughout the year, which is a higher target, and we are confident that we'll be able to achieve that.

items.statement: IISCO expansion of 4.5 million tons planned with ballpark capex of INR36,000 crores over 3-4 years, order placement expected by end of Q3/Q4 FY26
items.quote: You can say, ballpark 4 x 9,000, it will be INR36,000 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA per ton of saleable steel at INR6,400 vs INR6,000 in Q1 FY25, impacted by INR1,050 crores stock valuation hit due to lower coking coal costs
items.quote: Regarding your -- you're talking about EBITDA per TSS, Which is INR6,400 now as compared to INR6,000 in quarter 1 last year.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 coking coal prices expected to remain flat at Q1 levels with slight variation possible on upside
items.quote: Because so far as Q2 guidance is concerned, the coking coal prices are almost flat as it was in quarter 1. We are hoping that it wil l remain at the same level, a little bit of variation here and there, won't be on the downside, could be a little up or maybe at the same level

items.statement: Rail provisional price for FY26 set at INR74,000 per ton vs INR78,000-79,000 in FY24-25 due to softer imported coal prices; no further revision benefit expected in FY26
items.quote: Now from '25, '26 onwards, the provisional price has been at INR74,000 per ton because of the softening of imported coal prices, so the provisional p rices have been capitalized

items.statement: Domestic steel demand growing at over 8% annually driven by infrastructure, housing, railways, automotive, defense and renewable energy; per capita consumption at 120+ kg
items.quote: domestic steel demand is growing at a rapid pace, over 8% annually. This demand is driven by infrastructure projects, affordable housing, railways, ports, highways, growth in automotive, defens e and renewable energy sectors

items.statement: Borrowings reduced by INR1,100 crores in Q1 FY26 to INR28,741 crores as of June 30, 2025 from INR29,811 crores as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: The company continues its drive towards reduction in borrowings as on 30th June 2025, which stood at INR28,741 crores as against INR29,811 crores as on 31st March 2025. So we have reduced our borrowings by around INR1,100 crores in quarter 1 this year.

items.statement: NMDC steel marketing: 0.373 million tons sold in Q1 FY26 generating ~INR1,800 crores revenue; included in SAIL's 4.55 million ton sales volume; margin positive but small
items.quote: 0.373 million tons we have sold actually and -- so we have got a revenue of around -- in this quarter, around INR1,800 crores odd, that revenue we have sold.

items.statement: Saleable steel production in Q1 FY26 at 4.7 million tons (+12% YoY); sales volume at 4.55 million tons (+15% YoY), best ever Q1 sales performance
items.quote: Saleable steel production during the quarter stood at 4.7 million tons as against 4.2 million tons last year quarter 1 with a growth of 12%. Sales volume stood at 4.55 million tons as against 4 million tons in last year quarter 1 with a growth of 15%.

items.statement: Coking coal inventory at normal levels: 25-30 days at ports, ~5 days at plants
items.quote: coking coal inventory right now is around -- hovering around anything between 25 to 30 days in the ports and could be around 5 da ys in the plants. So those are at the normal levels that we generally expect

items.statement: Finished goods inventory at 1.7 million tons and in-process stock at 1.3 million tons as of June 30, 2025; up from 1.4 million tons finished goods in March quarter
items.quote: We are holding around 1.7 million tons of saleable steel and 1.3 million tons of in-process stock. So these 2 put together steel stock, it is steel stock.

items.statement: Iron ore royalty impact of ~INR173 crores in Q1 FY26 vs Q4 FY25 due to IBM price movement; other expenses higher primarily due to royalty
items.quote: versus Q4, it coul d be somewhere around we had say, around INR250 crores or INR260 crores. Just 1 sec. INR173 crores to be specific. Around INR173

items.statement: Global steel oversupply from China suppressing prices; rising imports (up 24% in 2025 from China, Vietnam, Japan) creating price pressure; trade tensions and protective measures increasing
items.quote: Chinese producers are uploading excess steel in international markets at lower prices, leading to gl obal oversupply and price suppression. This has triggered trade tensions and protective measures across several countries, including India, UAE countries and U.S

items.statement: Q2 FY26 steel prices expected lower than Q1 due to monsoon season, but improvement signs in last 1-2 weeks of July; August-September may offset July decline
items.quote: See, everybody knows about it actually because in the rainy season, which is there in Q2, the prices remained little suppressed. So prices -- steel prices are down in July. But as I have Steel Authority of already given in my opening remarks, that in the last 1 or 2 weeks, it has started improving

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected to jump significantly above INR7,500 crores as IISCO expansion execution begins after order placement in FY26
items.quote: So actually, as we have discussed, after tendering and order placement, the execution activities start and the expenditure will start fro m the next year, we are expecting a good jump as compared to INR7,500 crores next year onwards

items.statement: Operational efficiency improvements in Q1 FY26: improved fuel rate, coal-to-hot-metal ratio, increased CDI, reduced coke rates, reduced basic energy consumption vs previous quarter
items.quote: We have improved the fuel rate, coal to hot metal ratio, increased CDI and reduced coke rates, reduced basic energy consumption in this quarter as compared to the previous quarter, which has given us advantage in the cost front as well as the steel.

items.statement: India-UK FTA signed July 24, 2025 expected to unlock export opportunities for manufacturing and services without compromising strategic interests
items.quote: The recently signaled India-U.K. FTA in July 24 -- 24th July 2025 is expected to unlock opportunities for start-up companies, manufacturing and services exports without compromising India's strategic interest.

items.statement: Vulnerabilities remain: rising protectionism, volatile capital flows from trade disputes, agricultural/rural inflation post-monsoon, climate shocks impacting commodity prices
items.quote: On the front of global and domestic vulnerabilities, will remain with respect to rising protectionism and volatile capital flows due to trade disputes, particularly U.S. tariffs on China and Europe, agricultural and rural inflation spikes post monsoon, climate shocks impacting global food supplies and commodity prices.

items.statement: CO2 emission levels improved in Q1 FY26 vs Q1 FY25; focus on zero liquid discharge, eco-restoration and CSR activities
items.quote: Our CO2 emission levels have also improved in this quarter as compared to the previous quarter -- as compared to quarter 1 of last year; however, we are still having more targets to improve it further.

items.statement: Revenue expected to grow ~25% YoY in FY26
items.quote: I would still stand with the number which I gave that this year, our revenue is expected to be 25% to 30% higher, about 25% higher than the last financial year.

items.statement: OFC revenue expected to double to Rs 2,400 crore in FY26
items.quote: Fiber optic cable business, it will grow by 100%. That is our current estimation. Last year, it was Rs. 1,200 crores. This year, we should be reaching to Rs. 2,400 crores.

items.statement: Defence revenue estimated at Rs 200+ crore in FY26
items.quote: My best estimation could be leading to about Rs. 200-plus crores, Rs. 200-plus crores, something like that.

items.statement: PCS revenue target Rs 450 crore from telcos in FY26
items.quote: our target for revenue from passive connectivit y solutions for telcos, telecom service providers and other operators is about Rs. 450 crores in the current year

items.statement: BharatNet Phase III revenue expected Rs 800-1,000 crore in FY26
items.quote: BharatNet, particularly revenue, I would say, of the total order we have got roughly about Rs. 5,000 crores out of which 20% of that, roughly in the range of about Rs. 800 – Rs.1,000 crores.

items.statement: Order book Rs 10,480 crore as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: Driven by these wins, our order book as of June 30, 2025, stands at ₹10480 crore, compared to ₹9967 crore in the previous quarter and ₹6776 crore in Q1FY25

items.statement: Export order book ~Rs 400 crore; defence ~Rs 1,300 crore (12%)
items.value: Export Rs 400 crore, Defence Rs 1,300 crore
items.quote: our export order book today is above Rs. 400 crores. It's roughly about Rs. 400 crores. And from def ense segment, would be roughly about 12% of our total order book, which is Rs. 10,000 crores, the defen se is about Rs. 1,300 crores

items.statement: ~Rs 3,000 crore of order book executable in FY26
items.quote: This year is out of this particular Rs. 10,000 crores, particularly, I think Rs. 3,000 crores should be executable in the current year

items.statement: Capex ~Rs 250 crore for FY26; Rs 130 crore for IBR expansion
items.quote: CAPEX for this year, give me a minute, I will come back to you before we end this. Roughly, I think currently about Rs. 250 crores because about Rs. 130 crores is going i n IBR cable itself

items.statement: IBR cable capacity expansion from 1.73 to 19.01 mn fkm/annum approved; total OFC capacity to reach 42.36 mn fkm/annum by June 2026
items.quote: its meeting held on 11th July, 2025, approved the expansion of IBR cable capacity from ~1.73 million fiber kilomet ers per annum to ~19.01 mn fkm /per annum at our Hyderabad and Goa facilities. This will enable us to meet rising global demand, particularly from North America and Europe, where we already have orders from major customers. With this planned expansion, our total optical fibre cable ma

items.statement: OFC capacity utilisation reached ~100% in July 2025
items.quote: Optical fiber cable, the capacity utilization has started improving in the first quarter. Particularly May, June it really started improving. July it has further improved and now reaching to almost 100%.

items.statement: OFC margins back to ~15% from July 2025
items.quote: From this quarter itself. In fact, from July which was the last month of the Q1, we started into that kind of a margin. And from this margins would continue to be of that level of roughly about 15% or so.

items.statement: Turnkey margins 6-8%; telecom product margins variable
items.quote: Overall margin level he re is still fiber optic cable, I expect to be about 15%. In turnkey, it is about 6% to 8% or sometimes a little bit more in BharatNet or overall 6% to 8% is in turnkey, I would say

items.statement: New global OFC customers onboarded; repeat orders and product approvals secured
items.quote: This quarter also marked the onboarding of several reputed global customers, along with repeat orders reflecting strong customer satisfaction and trust in our offerings. We obtained product approvals from many leading customers

items.statement: Only second Indian company after Tejas to develop indigenous MPLS routers
items.quote: We are proud to be the only Indian manufacturer, aside from Tejas, to develop such routers.

items.statement: Electronic fuze live testing by DRDO scheduled for August 2025; production expected soon after
items.quote: our electronic fuzes for artillery guns are also scheduled t o undergo live testing in August by DRDO, following the recent receipt of ammunition from Munitions India Limited. This marks a key milestone in our defence roadmap, with production expected to begin soon after successful trials

items.statement: Export orders ~Rs 300 crore secured in Q1 FY26; export revenue ~Rs 210 crore
items.value: Orders Rs 300 crore; Revenue Rs 210 crore
items.quote: During Q1 FY26, we secured export orders worth approximately ₹300 crores and achieved export revenues of around ₹210 crores.

items.statement: Rs 700 crore enabling resolution passed; no decision yet on quantum, timing or instrument
items.quote: Rs. 700 crores was just an enabling resolution we have passed. We have still not decided when to raise, how much to raise, whether to raise. All these things are still under discussion. It's just an enabling resolution.

items.statement: Defence order conversion timing uncertain; BMP-2 tender postponed to Sept 29, 2025
items.quote: BMP-2 orders tender has been postponed twice. Now it is on 29th September. If that had not happened again and if we had won, we would have started seeing revenue in this year itself.

items.statement: FY26 structural EBITDA improvement of INR 600 crores expected, split equally between U.K. loss-making asset shutdown, new project commissioning, and cost improvements
items.quote: our number, which is broadly what I had indicated was INR 600 crores, split equally between reduction in the, let's say, unviable operations in U.K., INR 200-odd crores in terms of additional bottom line contribution from new projects getting commissioned an d another INR 200 crores in terms of cost improvement, still holds fine for the full

items.statement: U.K. business expected to reach breakeven at PAT level by Q3-Q4 FY26 driven by in-house CO2 production and pharma salt qualification
items.quote: We do expect to run the year towards exit, towards the 3rd and 4th Quarter with at least balanced or zero losses at the PAT level in U.K.

items.statement: FY26 maintenance capex of approximately INR 1,000 crores globally, no major growth capex remaining
items.quote: What's going to be this year is only the operational CAPEX for all geographies and roughly around INR 1,000 crores we incur every year on the operational CAPEX. Not much growth CAPEX left to pay, everything is done last year.

items.statement: Kenya 50-kiloton calciner commissioned and in trial runs, expected to deliver products in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We have commissioned the 50 -kiloton calciner and it is going through the trial runs as we speak. So, sometime during the second quarter, it should be delivering products towards the market.

items.statement: U.S. soda ash expansion on pause awaiting clearer market conditions, design work continuing with environmental approvals obtained
items.quote: While the design work in U.S. is continuing, we will press the pedal on that only when the market conditions seem to be clearer to us. As of now, we put it on a pause, but it will be a pause for a couple of quarters or maybe a year.

items.statement: India soda ash expansion of 320,000 tons to be done in two steps of 150,000 and 170,000 tons via low-cost debottlenecking, details by Q2-Q3 FY26
items.quote: As far as India soda ash is concerned, out of the 320,000 broadly, we are looking at doing it in 2 steps of 150,000 and 170,000 tons. We will come back to you by the 2nd and 3rd Quarter in terms of the operationalization of that as soon as the details are clear, but it is going to be more like a debottlenecking at a low cost rather than full expansion.

items.statement: U.K. bicarb expansion of 1.8 lakh tons on hold until existing 80,000-ton unit runs properly, design work ongoing
items.quote: In terms of U.K. bicarb, yes, this year, we will be spending time on making sure our current existing 80,000-ton unit is fully run in a proper manner before pressing the pedal. There, again, design work is on its way.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated EBITDA INR 649 crores, India EBITDA improvement driven by higher volumes and lower variable costs, U.S. EBITDA boosted by favorable domestic-export mix and lower fixed costs
items.quote: Company reported Quarter1 FY26 on consolidated basis revenue from operations of INR 3,719 crores, EBITDA of INR 649 crores and a PAT of INR 316 crores.

items.statement: U.S. EBITDA sequentially higher due to greater domestic sales share and lower fixed costs, but mix will normalize in Q2 with higher exports and increased fixed costs
items.quote: In addition to that, there will be some additional costs in terms of fixed costs. So, U.S. should tend to drop a bit because of the two drivers, which are basically export domestic mix and the maintenance and fixed cost.

items.statement: Soda ash prices range-bound globally, India list prices unchanged, import prices $230-235, U.S. export pricing to Asia balanced, pricing expected to remain at similar levels for next 6-9 months
items.quote: Overall, we expect pricing to remain in the similar levels at least for the next 6 to 9 months.

items.statement: Price reductions marginal at $3-5 per ton in most domestic markets, up to $10 in some pockets, prices believed to have bottomed out
items.quote: The changes in the pricing has been fairly range bound, it's been between $3 to $5 at best, in some pockets, it may be $10, but that's the kind of reduction we have seen in most domestic markets.

items.statement: Power and fuel costs down sequentially due to lower coal, lower gas, and cessation of Lostock operations, considered sustainable with further optimization underway
items.quote: Yes, it is a combination of the two. It is also led by lower gas, lower coal and cessation of the Lostock operations.

items.statement: Global soda ash demand flat near-term due to trade uncertainties, India and China demand stable, Americas excluding U.S. stable, U.S. flat, China slight 1% dip expected
items.quote: Overall, global demand is estimated to be flat in the near term due to uncertainties associated with some of the trading issues. The market condition remains steady in view of the demand being stable in Indi a, China and some parts of other regions, including Americas, excluding U.S.A

items.statement: India soda ash demand growing per projections, no placement issues for expanded volumes, overall demand to grow for first 2 quarters of calendar year
items.quote: Overall demand in India will continue to grow, as per our assessment of the market, at least for the first 2 quarters of the calendar year.

items.statement: Rallis India Q1 FY26 revenue growth 22%, volume growth 9%, price growth 13%, EBITDA margin 16%, PAT growth 100%
items.quote: Rallis saw an overall growth of 22%, a volume growth of 9% and price growth of 13%, driven by growth in Crop Care and Seeds business, and EBITDA margin stood at 16% and a PAT growth of 100% in Q1.

items.statement: India FOS sales volume 869 metric tons vs 614 metric tons in Q1 FY25, bicarb utilization ramping up ~5,000 tons per month
items.quote: Quarterly sales volume of all products increased, including FOS which was 869 metric tons as compared to 614 metric ton in Quarter1.

items.statement: U.K. pharma grade salt plant commissioned, customer qualification process ongoing, expected to contribute in H2 FY26
items.quote: Secondly, the pharmaceutical grade salt plant has been commissioned. But right now, they are going through a process of qualification with customers that should begin maybe in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Kenya margin decline due to reduced local African market sales mix and delayed Southeast Asia shipments at customer request, expected to normalize
items.quote: I think fundamentally, the proportion, the mix of sale in the local African market had reduced. That should be back up as we move through the year again.

items.statement: Global soda ash oversupply persists with high inventories, China inventory $1.8 billion, only two players announced capacity closures (Tata Chemicals and second largest European producer), Chinese unit Shandong Haihua considering idling cap
items.quote: All soda ash markets continue to be oversupplied with high inventory levels in most regions. China inventory remains high at $1.8 billion, a slight increase over prior quarter.

items.statement: India MIP extended but has not significantly impacted prices, Chinese government efforts to rationalize excess capacity being monitored
items.quote: Although MIP has been extended, it has not had much impact on prices.

items.statement: Focus on working capital efficiency and cost optimization, U.S. export shipment of 45,000 tons delayed to Q2 will normalize H1 run rate
items.quote: The export consignment, which got delayed to next quarter was about 45,000 tons, that's the indicator I have already given. If you wait for the second quarter result, the H1 will be fully indicative of what the normalized number is likely to be.

items.statement: U.K. depreciation and finance costs run rate INR 5-10 crores per quarter, expected to decrease as debt is paid down during the year
items.quote: if you take the current quarter number, more or less, it will be somewhere in the range of INR 5 crores - INR 10 crores in terms of depreciation and amortization , a nd finance costs, depending on how quickly we can start to pay down debt, which we will make some effort during the year

items.statement: Soda ash pricing risk limited to INR 50-60 crores downside from modeled INR 600 crore improvement, based on realistic market expectations
items.quote: At best, I expect maybe INR 50 crores or INR 60 crores move from what I mentioned, overall, in terms of numbers, if you put it, not more than that.

items.statement: China natural soda ash capacity additions of 2.8 million tons reported for 2026, monitoring rationalization of synthetic capacity
items.quote: Yes, there is an effort to continue to keep adding capacity, but we are also watching this space. It has to be first looked in the context of whether there's a rationalization of synthetic capacity in China.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 24-25% for FY26
items.quote: So we have already given the margin guidance in the even last quarter. It will be around 24%, 25%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 23.8% due to India mix and tariff absorption
items.quote: The stand-alone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR655 crores with a margin of 23.8%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 sales volume 80,664 MT, marginally lower YoY
items.quote: Despite these testing conditions, we managed to achieve a sales volume of 80,664 metric tons during the current quarter.

items.statement: India business grew 14.4% YoY, contributed 35% of volumes
items.quote: India business continues to be strong and for the quarter contributed to approximately 35% to our sales volumes and approximately 14.4% in growth on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: US tariff at 10%, 60% borne by customers, 40% by company
items.quote: Currently, the tariff is 10%. Out of that 60% is customer bearing and 40% we are sharing.

items.statement: Raw material prices flattish for Q2, rubber up, other basket down
items.quote: So it was very nominal price reduction as compared to last quarter. And the coming quarter, we see the similar type of the prices because rubber is going up and other basket is down.

items.statement: OTR, Carbon Black, PCR and CVR capex on schedule
items.quote: the earlier announced capex of OTR, along with newly announced capex for Carbon Black, PCR and CVR are expected to operationalize as per schedule.

items.statement: Bhuj OTR facility and rubber track line in testing phase
items.quote: It is in testing phase, and we will give you more commentary on that towards the end of this year.

items.statement: India realization 8-10% lower than international, margin impact 0.5-1%
items.quote: Around -- it fluctuates between different product mix, but you can take a range of 8% to 10% lower.

items.statement: Euro-INR realization INR93.60 in Q1, remaining year closer to current rate
items.quote: So for the current quarter, it was INR93.60. And for the remaining year, it is closer to current rate.

items.statement: Hedging policy: 80% of net receivable, ~30-35% of gross euro revenue, no dollar hedging
items.quote: We only hedge 80% of net receivable, which end up probably 30%, 35% of gross euro revenue. We don't hedge anything on dollars.

items.statement: Dealer inventory at normal levels, 2-3 months
items.quote: It's at normal levels. There's no increase or decrease. It's at the normal level.

items.statement: First interim dividend of INR4 per equity share declared
items.quote: The Board of Directors has declared a first interim dividend of INR4 per equity share.

items.statement: Carbon Black revenue not significant, ramp-up expected end of calendar year
items.quote: Not significantly, it is still in the trial stage. And end of the calendar year, we expect to ramp up this business.

items.statement: Rubber tracks in trial stage, nominal revenue currently
items.quote: So tracks is currently in trial stage and -- so it's very nominal.

items.statement: India distributor network ~70 distributors, new PCR/TBR distribution largely fresh
items.quote: We will be having close to about 70-odd distributors distributors.

items.statement: All competitors similarly impacted by tariffs, pricing gap similar magnitude
items.quote: So everybody is in the same boat. I mean we are not sure of how they have done the cost sharing. But the tariff has impacted everybody, even if there's a local manufacturer, his raw materials are coming from Asia, so they would have got impacted with the tariffs.

items.statement: No direct impact from EU sanctions on Russia, no machinery/raw material from Russia
items.quote: We don't buy any machinery or direct raw material from Russia. Oil may be coming and some derivatives of the oils locally, I don't know what way it is coming. But otherwise, we are not impacted from that.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty continues, normalcy depends on permanent structure
items.quote: However, we do believe that the complete normalcy in the ordering cycle will take shape once there is permanent tariff structure in place.

items.statement: Freight cost as percentage of revenue marginally lower QoQ
items.quote: It was marginally lower.

items.statement: Other expenses up 24% YoY/QoQ due to duty impact and marketing
items.quote: It is the duty impact and some marketing impact.

items.statement: No dilution of Off-Highway focus, PCR/TBR strategy targets premium/radial categories
items.quote: So first, there is no dilution of our focus in Off-Highway tires. I'd like to make that statement very, very clearly. Then the second point is we are looking at the market keenly in finding the white spaces and the areas where to play.

items.statement: Blended margins post full commercialization expected 23-25%
items.quote: we expect blended margins post full commercialization to be in the range of 23% to 25% and we will strive to maintain that.

items.statement: Too early to comment on FY26 volume guidance
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier, it's too early to comment on volume guidance.

items.statement: Capex breakup for TBR/PCR not shared, overall INR3,500 cr over 3 years
items.quote: No, we are not sharing the breakup of that. We've announced an overall capex, which we will be doing in the next 3 years -- which will come in line in the next 3 years.

items.statement: EBITDA guidance range 24-25%, some quarters higher/lower, not benchmark
items.quote: And as far as the EBITDA guidance is, we mentioned that we strive to be in this range. There will be a couple of quarters which will be higher and a couple of quarters, which will be lower.

items.statement: Management targets normative EBITDA of INR5,000 per metric ton for FY26
items.quote: On the manufactured margin, our normative EBITDA per metric ton of INR5,000 will sustain during this year. That's our hope, and we'll strive to do that.

items.statement: Committed capex of close to INR2,000 crores for FY26 from internal surplus
items.quote: Close to INR2,000 crores, we'll be spending. That will be dipping out of the surplus what we have generated over the period of time.

items.statement: Additional incremental capex of INR300-500 crores over 2-3 years for specialty nutrients and bio products
items.quote: The investment can be in the range of INR300 crores to INR500 crores across various product categories in these business segments.

items.statement: Backward integration phosphoric and sulfuric acid plant at Kakinada 70% complete, commissioning in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The plant is likely to be commissioned in Q4 of this current financial year.

items.statement: Granulation project adding 7.5 lakh tons capacity on track for commissioning by end of FY26-27
items.quote: Our granulation project that is expected to add 7.5 lakh tons of additional capacity is on track and is likely to be commissioned by end of FY26-27.

items.statement: BMCC rock phosphate output targeting 300,000-400,000 tons in FY26, aiming to double in 2 years
items.quote: If everything goes well this year, FY25-26, besides 2 to 3 months of rainy season when we don't operate, we should come closer to 300,000 tons to 400,000 tons per annum.

items.statement: Record primary sales volume of 11 lakh tons in Q1 FY26, up 31% YoY
items.quote: Coromandel achieved record primary sales volume of 11 lakh tons, marking a 31% growth, establishing itself as a leading marketer of phosphatic fertilizers in the country.

items.statement: NPK market share improved to close to 18% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: establishing itself as a leading marketer of phosphatic fertilizers in the country with an improved market share of close to 18% on the NPK segment.

items.statement: POS consumption improved 46% to 7 lakh tons, market share on consumption basis up to 16% from 12%
items.quote: The POS consumption improved by 46% during this quarter to 7 lakh tons, reflecting improved farm level engagement activities and a favorable agri environment. The market share on the consumption basis has improved to 16% as compared to 12% of last year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 55% YoY to INR782 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stands at INR782 crores against INR506 crores in the previous year, registering a growth of 55%.

items.statement: Crop Protection revenue grew 31% to Rs 725 crores, EBIT up 77% to Rs 111 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Crop Protection and Bio segments of the company delivered robust set of numbers in Q1, revenue growing up by 31% to Rs 725 crores and EBIT moved up by 77% to Rs 111 crores.

items.statement: Phosphoric acid price increased from $1,153 in Q1 to $1,258 for Q2
items.quote: In line with the increase in global prices of DAP, and also India CFR price of DAP, Phos Acid price has also significantly gone up from $1,153 in Q1 and has been concluded at $1,258 for Q2.

items.statement: Sulfuric acid price around $120, sulfur price peaked at $300+ now softened to $275
items.quote: Sulfuric acid is around $120. And sulfur prices peaked to $300 plus, and has started softening now. It has come down to $275.

items.statement: Share of unique grades improved to 34% from 31% last year
items.quote: Share of unique grades, which differentiates us from the rest of the players, stands at 34%, improved from last year level of 31%.

items.statement: Specialty Nutrient volumes up 12%, organic fertilizer volumes up 29% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Specialty Nutrient business as a company had a strong quarter, registering volume growth of 12%, while organic fertilizer volumes has improved by 29%.

items.statement: Expanded domestic formulation presence in additional 40 territories and increased field strength
items.quote: We have also started focusing more intensely on the domestic formulation segments and expanded our geographies by significantly improving our presence in additional 40 territories and also increasing our field strength.

items.statement: Drone spraying covered 25,000 acres in Q1, planning to double fleet to reach 0.5 million acres in FY26
items.quote: In first quarter, we have covered 25,000 acres. The initiative has received highly encouraging response from the farming community, and we are planning to double the fleet size of drones by procuring them from Dhaksha, and we hope to reach at least 0.5 million acres of drone spraying in the current year.

items.statement: Signed long-term DAP supply agreement with Maaden of Saudi Arabia
items.quote: During this quarter, as you all know, the Coromandel signed a long-term agreement with Maaden of Saudi Arabia, a leading fertilizer player, mainly to secure DAP shipments.

items.statement: Government approved continuation of modified Interest Subvention Scheme reducing KCC loan rate to 4% for prompt repayment

items.quote: We got that capacity utilization of Satara. As again, not very impressive because we have added several machines there in view of the Mahad requirement. items.quote: an LTM (Last Twelve Months) basis is a good way for you as an investor to consider a metric, rather than focusing solely on the quarterly numbers.

items.statement: DTC (Digital Technology for Commerce) platforms GPX, CPX, APX in incubation; takes ~5 years to generate big numbers; DTC 3 years from substantial contribution
items.quote: DTC is in the incubation stage, so that will take another three (3) Investors Meeting Transcript years to contribute substantially. It generally takes five (5) years for incubation to start generating a big

items.statement: Targeting 38% CAGR over next 3 years and breakeven at EBITDA level by FY27-FY28
items.quote: In the subsequent, in the coming years, sans the PropTiger business, we are looking to grow at 25% CAGR. With this trajectory, we are also looking to improve our operational efficiency and reach a break-even by FY27 or FY28. Sorry, just to correct myself, we should be looking at growing at a 38% CAGR in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 550-575 crores for FY27 at breakeven, excluding PropTiger
items.quote: That's correct. We are looking to reach INR 550 crores to INR 575 crores of revenue in FY27, which is where we are looking at breakeven.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds of INR 341.29 crores to double organic revenue in 27-30 months
items.quote: This is more than capital, it's a commitment. It gives us the firepower to double our organic revenue in the next 27 to 30 months, while staying true to our principles of capital efficiency and focused deployment.

items.statement: Received SM-REIT registration from SEBI; plan to launch first scheme in Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27 after observing market
items.quote: We will take another two quarters to look at this market very closely and then the subsequent quarter which is either Q4 or Q1 FY27, we will look at entering into the SM-REIT business or launching the first SM-REIT asset.

items.statement: Acquired PropTiger via preferred allotment; REA India gets 5.5% stake; closure by end-August
items.quote: The PropTiger acquisition by nature is in form of a preferred allotment. This will take time till end of August to get concluded. Post the conclusion of it, post the closing date, the revenues and the operations will be in our control and will be coming on to at Aurum PropTech.

items.statement: Targeting INR 2,000 crores AUM for SM-REIT over 3-5 years with management fee 0.5%+ and acquisition fee 1.5%
items.quote: The INR 2,000 crores AUM was required to be built over the next three years to five years in a manner where we start looking at how the space is evolving first and then start on the building.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 28.4% vs 17.4% YoY; profit margins improved 852 bps YoY
items.quote: Our profit margins improved by 852 basis points year-on-year basis. Our EBITDA margins grew by an impr essive 826 basis points and our adjusted EBITDA rose by 395 basis points

items.statement: HelloWorld saw 50% surge in short-stay revenue; blended occupancy 77% across 230+ properties
items.quote: There was a 50% surge in short-stay revenue, driven by rising demand for flexible living. Our customer service turnaround time significantly reduced from 8 days to 2.2 days.

items.statement: Aurum Analytica revenue INR 13 crores, up 64% YoY; sold 75,000+ leads to 120+ clients across 230+ projects
items.quote: Aurum Analytica continued its growth momentum with INR 13 crores in revenue, a 64% year-on-year uplift. They sold 75,000 + leads to 120+ active clients across 230+ projects.

items.statement: PropTiger brings 300+ developer relationships across 8 Tier-1 cities and 350+ sales team
items.quote: PropTiger has 300 + developer relationships across 8 Tier-1 cities in the country with a mandate partnership and 350+ people team engaged in sales and mortgage advisory.

items.statement: Rental 70% of revenue (INR 47.84 cr), Distribution INR 18.88 cr, Capital INR 1.68 cr in Q1 FY26
items.quote: For the quarter, Rental revenue contributed 70% of the total revenue from operations at INR 47.84 crores. Revenue for distribution and the capital segments were at INR 18.88 crores and INR 1.68 crores respectively.

items.statement: Aurum Analytica founder to become PropTiger CEO post-acquisition for integration
items.quote: What we have also done for that same reason, so that the integration is smooth, we have requested one of our founders of Aurum Analytica, to get freed up from Aurum Analytica as a CEO position from there, and take over as CEO of PropTiger, as and when the acquisition is completed.

items.statement: Rights issue fully subscribed; received INR 341.29 crores across three tranches
items.quote: In totality, we have received INR 341.29 crores from the rights issue in three tranches on application, first call and second call.

items.statement: SM-REIT differentiation: supply profiling via group RE expertise, property management/leasing churn, tech platform integration
items.quote: So, there are three parts to it. One is, of course, the profiling of supply that, that is very crucial for onboarding the right supply, which comes in with our group company's real estate expertise and sits on the SM-REIT AMSA business unit.

items.statement: No explicit capex guidance; focus on organic growth and PropTiger integration synergies
items.quote: We are on track to deliver positive adjusted EBITDA in the near future, confidently and sustainably.

items.statement: Conservative revenue booking in Q4 FY25 caused Q1 FY26 dip; no structural change in Distribution
items.quote: So first the Distribution segment, if you are comparing the numbers from March, actually, because the last quarter of the financial year and we are really conservative in booking the revenues and other things, till we know exactly the receipt and other things.

items.statement: PropTiger turnaround in 12-18 months via cutting business support services, royalties, marketing fees to REA group
items.quote: With these three and certain operational efficiencies, we are looking at the next 12 to 18 months to turn around the business and make it profitable, while maintaining the revenue growth and also increasing it in the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: REA Group becomes strategic shareholder with 5.5% stake via PropTiger acquisition
items.quote: In this strategic transaction, REA India Pte. will get 5.5% ownership of Aurum PropTech Limited.

items.statement: SM-REIT launch delayed to observe market; wait-and-watch approach on supply/demand dynamics
items.quote: We would not want to be the market-maker in this segment. We would rather want to wait out, see how the other SM REIT players are unfolding. This is a large TAM and we don't need to rush into it.

items.statement: No top-line or bottom-line guidance provided for FY26 or FY27
items.quote: We typically don't give guidance for top line, bottom line. We can discuss more on the business lines.

items.statement: General staffing recovery visible in June with 6,500 net adds and 42,000 open mandates for festive season
items.quote: June '25 was the first month since December '24, we saw an uptick across headcount, new demand, open mandates and fulfillments.

items.statement: Professional staffing open mandates at 1,200 positions, 68% from GCCs
items.quote: Our open mandate are currently over 1,200 positions, I mean, positioning us well to meet our demand from the sector perspective.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 7 bps QoQ to 1.9%
items.quote: EBITDA margins increased by 7 basis points quarter -on-quarter to 1.9%.

items.statement: Professional staffing margin entered double digits at 10.2%, up 116 bps YoY and 102 bps QoQ
items.quote: The segment margin came at 10.2%, entering double digits for the first time, registering a sharp 116 basis points expansion with respect to Q1 last year and 102 basis points on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Overseas business EBITDA margin at 5.9%, up 30 bps YoY but down 20 bps QoQ
items.quote: Segment EBITDA margin was 5.9%, a 30 basis points increase on a year-on-year basis and 20 basis points down sequentially.

items.statement: General staffing margin expansion limited by flat-fee contracts; expect improvement from Q2 with seasonality
items.quote: Margin is a factor of what we get from the industry, both in terms of a blend between flat fee as well as percentage fee.

items.statement: General staffing added 79 new contracts bringing 9,000+ associates; 42,000 open mandates
items.quote: General Staffing added 79 new contracts during the quarter, which brought in 9,000-plus new associates.

items.statement: Professional staffing added 12 new contracts with promising headcount growth projections
items.quote: During the quarter, we also added 12 n ew contracts, each with promising projection of headcount growth in upcoming quarters

items.statement: Overseas business added 32 new contracts during the quarter
items.quote: We added 32 new contracts during the quarter.

items.statement: Origint GCC-as-a-Service model is asset-light, cost-plus markup, not capex-heavy
items.quote: These are not capex-heavy model. These are a cost-plus markup model.

items.statement: General staffing recruiter capacity ramped up for July-October festive season; ratio to normalize post-season
items.quote: We have gone and ramped up our recruiting capability across. That's one. And I mean, that adds to our headcount.

items.statement: Overseas headcount grew 18% YoY to 5,599
items.quote: Headcount for overseas business was at 5,599 with a growth of 18% year-on-year.

items.statement: Professional staffing revenue mix shifted to 73% from GCCs, up from 23% contribution in FY25 to 29% in Q1
items.quote: GCC expansion within the segment is 73%. The exposure to GCC is 73%, driven mainly by demand from digital, high-tech, telecom, media and technology and electronics sector.

items.statement: General staffing collect-and-pay ratio at 76%, target range 75-80%
items.quote: I think we've often stated that we are happy with keeping it between 75% to 80% and we will remain in that range as f ar as the general staffing is concerned

items.statement: Professional staffing works with 157 GCCs; added 12 new logos in Q1, 10 from GCC space
items.quote: We closely work currently with 157 GCCs. In India, we have roughly 1,800 GCC. So last year, we have acquired 62 new logo and in the Q1 itself, we have acquired 12 new logo.

items.statement: Quess differentiated by AI-driven delivery model and execution capability in GCC niche/super-niche skills
items.quote: We have made huge investment in our AI-driven delivery model. Now we are not only helping the world in solving their technology problem, but we also use a lot of technology internally in getting the sourcing, screening and candidate engagement and all this is giving us better operational efficiency and better margin.

items.statement: ELI scheme approved by Cabinet, effective Aug 1; rules expected Aug 5; cash flow benefits from Q4 FY26
items.quote: On 1st of August, it goes live for the entire country for the next 2 to 4 years, as we've all read the details. On the 5th of August, the fine print and the rules should be given out.

items.statement: Overseas revenue flat YoY at INR284 cr; Middle East, Malaysia, Philippines growth offset Singapore decline
items.quote: Coming to overseas business, revenue stood at INR284 crores, which is broadly flat Y -on-Y basis and down 1% sequentially as growth in the Middle East, Malaysia and Philippines was offset by decline in Singapore business.

items.statement: Gross debt zero at June 30; interest cost INR10 cr due to intra-month borrowings and muted general staffing collections
items.quote: We are 0 at 30th June. But what happens is during the quarter and during the months, right, there will be some borrowings. So based on the average debt, the interest cost comes.

items.statement: Expect interest cost to decline in Q2 with improved general staffing collections
items.quote: As we go along in quarter 2, because of the open mandates and because of the general staffing showing better traction in quarter 2, so that level also will help us in quarter 2. And as we go along, we believe that the interest cost will keep coming down.

items.statement: Exited Q1 at zero gross debt; strong liquidity position maintained
items.quote: We also exited the quarter at 0 gross debt levels, demonstrating continued strength in our liquidity position.

items.statement: General staffing PAPM range INR600-650; professional staffing PPAM range INR23,000-25,000
items.quote: PAPM ranges between about INR600 to INR650. That's the range that we are in.

items.statement: India GCC count 1,800 currently; expected 700+ new GCCs by 2030 at 13% CAGR
items.quote: Currently, India has about 1,600 GCCs. By 2030, it is expected to grow at a rate of about 13% and another 700 -plus GCC are expected to go live.

items.statement: IEX electricity trading volume grew 15% YoY to 32.4 billion units in Q1 FY26
items.quote: During Q1 FY '26, IEX recorded electricity trading volume of 32.4 billion units, a growth of 15% on Y -o-Y basis.

items.statement: Revenue grew 19.2% YoY to INR 184.2 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Revenue for the company grew by 19.2% Y -o-Y, increasing from INR 154.5 crores in Q1 FY '25 to INR 184.2 crores in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: PAT increased 25.2% YoY to INR 120.7 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: PAT increased by 25.2%, rising from INR 96.4 crores in Q1 FY '25 to INR 120.7 crores in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: RTM volumes grew 41% YoY to nearly 13 billion units in Q1 FY26
items.quote: For Q1 FY '26, RTM volumes at nearly 13 billion units were higher by 41% on a year -on-year basis, highlighting the segment's critical role in helping DISCOM and open access consumers efficiently manage their short-term requirements.

items.statement: Green market volume rose 51% YoY to 2.7 billion units in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Green market volume in Q1 FY '26 rose 51% Y -o-Y to 2.7 billion units compared with Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Day Ahead Market supply liquidity increased 45.2% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, supply liquidity in the Day Ahead Market of IEX increased 45.2% on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Average Day Ahead Market price fell 16% YoY to INR 4.41 per unit in Q1 FY26
items.quote: As a result, the average Day Ahead Market price was INR 4.41 per unit, down 16% Y -o-Y, while price in the Real Mime market averaged at INR 3.91 per unit, a 20% drop.

items.statement: REC trading volume grew nearly 150% YoY to nearly 53 lakh in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1, nearly 53 lakh Renewable Energy Certificates were traded, recording a growth of nearly 150% over the same quarter last fiscal.

items.statement: IGX gas volume grew 109% YoY to 24.6 million MMBtu in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our associate company, IGX traded record gas volumes of 24.6 million MMBtu in Q1 FY '26, a growth of 109% over Q1 FY '25, led by demand push from the oil marketing companies, refineries and city gas distribution companies.

items.statement: IGX PAT grew 86.7% YoY to INR 14.1 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, IGX recorded a profit after tax of INR 14.1 crores, which was higher by nearly 86.7% compared with INR 7.6 crores in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: ICX issued over 44 lakh I-RECs in Q1 FY26
items.quote: For the first quarter of FY '26, the International Carbon Exchange ICX, issued over 44 lakh I-RECs compared with 59 lakh I-RECs issued in the previous financial year.

items.statement: ICX revenue was INR 178.8 lakhs in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Revenue for ICX in Q1 FY '26 stood at INR 178.8 lakhs.

items.statement: CERC ordered market coupling implementation in Day Ahead Market by January 2026
items.quote: CERC recently issued an order on implementing market coupling. Order was issued on 23rd July, in which the regulator has decided to initiate process of implementation of market coupling in Day Ahead Market. This is to be done by January 2026 as per the order.

items.statement: CERC to consider RTM coupling at a later stage after DAM coupling experience
items.quote: Given the shorter time for bid submission and running the market clearing engine, the decision to implement the coupling of RTM of power exchanges shall be considered at a later stage.

items.statement: CERC streamlined timelines for ADSS contracts and proposed predefined time slots for TAM contracts
items.quote: In its order in April 2025, the CERC streamlined time -lines for completion of various stages of any day single side (ADSS) contracts across exchanges. Other proposal s include notifying predefined time slots for trade under TAM contracts.

items.statement: CERC proposed modification in price discovery mechanism for day ahead contingency segment to uniform price step auction
items.quote: In its order, the regulator also proposed modification in the price discovery mechanism of the day ahead contingency segment from the current continuous matching to uniform price step auction through draft amendments in the Power Market Regulation 2021.

items.statement: CERC issued draft guidelines for Virtual Power Purchase Agreements recognizing power exchanges as authorized platform
items.quote: In May 2025, CERC issued draft guidelines for Virtual Power Purchase Agreements, VPPAs. These guidelines recognize power exchanges as authorized platform for sale of electricity by RE generators under VPP arrangements.

items.statement: CERC issued draft amendments to Deviation Settlement Mechanism regulations for infirm power charges
items.quote: Recently, the CERC issued draft amendments to Deviation Settlement Mechanism regulations with regards to infirm power charges for thermal stations.

items.statement: Electricity derivatives trading began on MCX and NSE in July 2025 after SEBI and CERC approval
items.quote: Further to the approval in February 2025 of SEBI and CERC to introduce electricity derivatives in India, the much -awaited electricity future contracts began trading on MCX and NSE respectively, earlier in July 2025.

items.statement: Revised Shakti Policy allows coal linkages without PPAs enabling URS power sales on exchanges
items.quote: The policy paves the way for coal linkages to generators even without PPAs, generating unrequisitioned surplus (URS) power, which can then be sold in power markets.

items.statement: India's power consumption was 446 billion units in Q1 FY26, down 1.3% YoY due to early monsoon
items.quote: India's power consumption of 446 billion units in Q1 FY '26 was lower by 1.3% as compared with Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: CEA expects power demand to grow at 6% per annum till 2032
items.quote: CEA expects power demand in the country to grow at a rate of 6% per annum till 2032.

items.statement: CEA forecasts peak demand at 366 GW by 2032 and power consumption at nearly 2,500 BUs
items.value: 366 GW peak demand, nearly 2,500 BUs consumption
items.quote: Nonetheless, with CEA forecast of peak demand at 366 gigawatt s by 2032, and power consumption to reach nearly 2,500 BUs, demand growth will continue to drive exchange volume growth.

items.statement: MOP monitoring thermal capacity addition roadmap of 80 GW by 2032
items.quote: Based on this, MOP has been regularly monitoring the road map of thermal capacity addition of 80 gigawatts by 2032.

items.statement: BESS storage of 47 GW required by FY32 per CEA; 13,200 MWh under implementation, 9,750 MWh awarded, 5,000 MWh in pipeline under first VGF tranche
items.quote: As per the CEA, BESS -based storage of 47 gigawatt shall be required by FY '32. The increased activity in BESS tenders has been driven by a reduction in battery capex cost and declining storage cost.

items.statement: Second VGF tranche approved for further 30,000 MWh of BESS projects
items.quote: More recently, under the second tranche of VGF, approval has been granted for further 30,000 megawatt hour of BESS projects to be implemented.

items.statement: IEX holds over 95% market share in DAM and RTM; competitors lost share over 17 years
items.quote: And we today have more than 95% of market share. And this has happened because of many factors. There is not one reason, there are many factors.

items.statement: PTC India contributes 10-12% of IEX volumes but cannot trade on competing exchange due to 25% equity holding
items.quote: However, their percentage share is almost about 10-12% on IEX platform.

items.statement: Management not worried about competitors using transaction fees to gain share post coupling; fees are small component of procurement cost
items.quote: I don't think customers really will value that part of it because transaction fees is a very, very small component of the total power procurement cost. But if that is the case, then we will deal with that also.

items.statement: DAM constitutes only 35-40% of IEX total volume; 60-65% from other products unaffected by coupling
items.quote: Number one, the present order is for coupling of DAM market. DAM market constitutes only about 35%, 40% of our total volume. So, we still have almost about 60%, 65% volume coming from the other products.

items.statement: Management aims to retain current market share, not just 40-50%
items.quote: I can assure you one thing that we are not working on retaining 40%, 50% market share. We are working to retain the present market share.

items.statement: Imported coal price steady at ~USD 50/tonne for 4,200 GAR coal, down 9% QoQ; imported gas stable at ~$11/MMBtu in Q1 FY26
items.quote: For the quarter, imported coal price for 4,200 GAR coal remained steady at around USD 50 per tonne, lower by 9% as compared with the same period last quarter. Prices of imported gas have also remained stable at nearly $11 per MMBtu in the first quarter of this fiscal.

items.statement: Coal production 247 million tonnes in Q1 FY26, similar to last year; coal inventory at 25 days as of mid-July 2025
items.quote: India's coal production reached 247 million tonnes in the first quarter of FY '26, similar to production during the same period last fiscal. Coal inventory as of mid-July 2025 stood at a high of 25 days.

items.statement: Awaiting CERC approval for TAM contract extension from 3 to 11 months; Green RTM petition hearing completed, awaiting final order
items.quote: In terms of new products, we continue to await approval from the C ERC on our petition to extend the Term Ahead Market contract from 3 months to 11 months. As mentioned previously, hearing for our petition on the Green RTM segment with the C ERC has already been completed and public comments on the petition have also been closed. We await the final order on the matter.

items.statement: IGX traded first 3-6 month long duration gas contract in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The quarter also witnessed the first trade in the 3 to 6-month long duration contract, underscoring market confidence in long -term gas trading on

items.statement: Filed EOI with CPCB for EPR trading platform; awaiting results
items.quote: Through ICX, we have also filed an Expression of Interest with the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) for developing the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) trading platform and are awaiting final results of the EOI.

items.statement: Coal Exchange stakeholder comments closed; awaiting MMDRA Amendment Bill 2025 in Parliament monsoon session
items.quote: On formation of Coal Exchange, stakeholder comments have been closed, and we await further directives with regards to the legislative changes to the Mine and Mineral Development Regulation Act. The MMDRA Amendment Bill 2025 is scheduled to be tabled for discussion in the monsoon session of the Parliament.

items.statement: Other income increased due to mark-to-market gains from target maturity fund redemption after RBI rate cut and NIFTY 50 index fund gains
items.quote: The increase is mainly because of one target maturity fund investments we had in our books, whereby because of the rate cut by the RBI during the first week of June, we got a decent mark-to-market gain, so we capitalized on that gain. We redeemed the funds and recognized that gain.

items.statement: ~75% of other income from own funds, ~25% from float and margin money
items.quote: It will be 2/3 will be from the own fund and around 2/3 to 3/4, about 75% will be from the own fund, around 25% from the float and other income.

items.statement: Management evaluating CERC market coupling order; options include review petition or APTEL appeal
items.quote: We are evaluating this order. We haven't made any view on this at the moment.

items.statement: Market coupling implementation may take longer than January 2026 due to common software, clearing mechanism, and regulatory requirements
items.quote: Based on the activities involved, I feel that it may take longer time. That is about the Day Ahead Market.

items.statement: CERC order mentions only data sharing for coupling implementation, not proprietary technology or algorithms
items.quote: No. This does not talk about technology or any such thing.

items.statement: Targeting 5 GW capacity addition in FY26; on track with one-third completed in Q1
items.quote: If you see on a 5 gigawatt target for the year, we have already done around one-third. What is expected from the next three quarters, if you ask me, we are very well on track.

items.statement: Operational capacity reached 15.8 GW after adding 1.6 GW in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, we added 1.6 -gigawatt of greenfield renewable capacity, totalling 4.9 gigawatt in the past year, a record achievement for India's renewable energy sector.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex was approximately Rs 6,500 crores for 1.6 GW capacity addition
items.quote: So, the current CapEx for the first quarter of current year booking was about Rs 6,500 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 92.8% in Q1 FY26, up 31% YoY to INR 3,108 crores
items.quote: EBITDA rose by 31% to INR 3,108 crores, delivering industry-best EBITDA margin of 92.8%.

items.statement: Energy sales grew 42% YoY to 10.5 billion units in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Backed by a robust capacity addition, Adani Green Energy achieved a record growth of 42% in its energy sales on year -on-year basis, reaching 10.5 billion units in the quarter.

items.statement: Merchant solar price averaged Rs 2.20/unit, wind averaged Rs 5.70/unit in Q1 FY26
items.quote: On the solar side, our average is Rs2.20, but the wind has been nominally well at Rs5.70.

items.statement: Total locked-in capacity of 36.5 GW, of which 31.5 GW under PPA and 5 GW merchant/C&I
items.quote: Yes, we have, as I I talked about 36.5 gigawatt in total, which is coming across. Within that, 31.5 gigawatt is what is currently with the PPA.

items.statement: Gross debt at INR 78,000 crores as of June 30; borrowing cost 9.1-9.2%
items.quote: So, the gross debt as on June 30 is INR 78,000 crores. And borrowing cost is generally, currently the range is 9.1% to 9.2% for us.

items.statement: Solar CUF at 28% overall portfolio; Khavda region CUF higher at 32%
items.quote: I think, you see Khavda has the distinction of one of the best irradiations possible. And so, our CUF there is always higher.

items.statement: Wind CUF at 42.3% in Q1 FY26, adjusted for 95.5% plant availability
items.quote: Yes, so I think it is -- first, I would not say that CUF at Khavda has been only because of the early onset of monsoon.

items.statement: Khavda evacuation constraints causing <5% EBITDA impact; expected to resolve in weeks/months
items.quote: However, having said that, it's hardly less than 5% of our EBITDA as we speak. We are very closely monitoring and largely supporting how the evacuation from Khavda is coming out.

items.statement: ISTS waiver tapered 25% from June 1; 75% remains; no major near-term pricing impact expected
items.quote: All of us knew, this ISTS thing is going on and is going to be off from June 1. And I think we all have built our strategies based on that part. And ISTS has not gone off full. It remains, 75% remains, only 25% have gone off on this.

items.statement: Merchant revenue split: ~50% pure merchant, ~50% infirm/pre-COD power; predominantly solar
items.quote: So, as earlier said, so merchant prices are volatile, and it is basically part of the business case when you talk about pure-play merchant. So, we have two parts, about 50% of it basically pure -play merchant and 50% is infirm revenue.

items.statement: Data center demand significant; targeting 25% of FY30 capacity for C&I/merchant/CFD/hybrid contracts
items.quote: And that's where you see, in our overall mix for FY '30, we have said that 25% of our capacities would be seeing some of these kinds of markets.

items.statement: Adani-Total JV: 4.5 GW portfolio, ~4 GW operational, 500 MW to commission in 6-12 months
items.quote: So, total 4.5-gigawatt portfolio we have, and out of that, roughly 4 gigawatt is operational right now in the JV.

items.statement: No labor issues at Khavda; invested in infrastructure, facilities, and partner ecosystem for 5-year horizon
items.quote: Having created that infrastructure, having given them the facilities, I would really request and suggest please come to Khavda and look at the way we are supporting and facilitating this labour to stay, to play, having the best food for them, and all the other infrastructure which we have created for them.

items.statement: Capex per MW: Solar ~INR 4.5 crores, Wind ~INR 6.5 crores
items.quote: So, the CapEx, see, generally our CapEx is in the range of, for the solar, it is INR 4.5 crores; for wind, it is INR 6.5 crores.

items.statement: Other expenditure increased proportionately with capacity due to higher O&M expenses
items.quote: Yes. So that's proportionately based on the O&M expense that goes up because of the capacity increase and various other expenses which are part of the capacities rising due to that.

items.statement: Evaluating refinancing of operating assets to reduce borrowing cost; gross debt not expected to decrease
items.quote: The borrowing cost, yes, we are looking to refinance certain portion of our assets. So, from that aspect, we will keep on looking at it from that perspective.

items.statement: Selective bidding strategy; not desperate for tenders; focus on value-accretive projects with predictable returns
items.quote: We choose the tenders, which gives us the predictable and better returns. On an overall scheme of things, we are currently, as you know, is 15.8 gigs on our operations. We have 16 gigs on under execution right now.

items.statement: 5 GW PSP target by FY30-31 unchanged; 1.25 GW for UP PCL and 500 MW in Andhra Pradesh announced
items.quote: So, I think, Anuj, let me be very clear, the 5 gigawatt which we have announced, and we made it very clear last time also that when we announced the capacity, those are de-risked from all these considerations.

items.statement: Monsoon impact on Khavda solar generation; better prepared this year based on last year's lessons
items.quote: We are well prepared, much better prepared this time from the monsoon -- for the monsoon. But yes, it is still going on. So, I would like you to be there in the next call for you to share with you how better we were placed this time.

items.statement: Evaluating battery storage for merchant capacity; strategy in place, will announce at appropriate time
items.quote: Oh, yes. Puneet, we are evaluating all options right now. We have a strategy in place; you will hear from us about it.

items.statement: Run-rate EBITDA for 15.8 GW capacity: ~INR 13,600 crores quarterly, ~INR 17,000 crores annually
items.quote: So, the current gross block of the company is INR 89,000 crores approximately, and the run rate EBITDA for the Q1, it is about INR 13,600 crores. And on a yearly basis, it will be about INR 17,000 crores.

items.statement: Associate income of INR 111 crores from 25% stake in Mundra Solar Energy Limited (2 GW manufacturing)
items.quote: It's Mundra Solar Energy Limited, where we have 25% stake within that company. So, whatever profits they generate, we get a 25% share of the same.

items.statement: Receivables growth guidance revised to 10-12% for FY26 from earlier 12-14%

items.quote: Edge data centers will be a smaller one, say, around 0.2 kilowatt - 0.2 megawatts, sorry. And this year, we might think maybe 4 or maybe 5 Edge data centers, we should be able to begin.

items.statement: Non-launch weekly sales target of Rs. 300 crores by end of FY26 from Rs. 250 crores in FY25

items.quote: we continue to maintain that our price growth will be in that range of 5% to 6%, which is somewhat higher than last year.

items.statement: Delhi NCR entry expected in next 12 months with launch targeted in FY27

items.statement: Annuity income target of Rs. 15 billion by end of decade, with visibility of just under Rs. 12 billion from existing assets
items.quote: we are increasing our stake in the digital infrastructure platform in line with our strategy to grow our annuity income to Rs. 15 billion by the end of the decade. And agains t this, we already have visibility for just under Rs. 12 billion from the existing assets.

items.statement: Palava targeting Rs. 80 billion annual sales by end of decade with EBITDA margins approaching 50%
items.quote: we expect that Palava will deliver Rs. 80 billion of annual sales by the end of the decade with EBITDA margins approaching 50%.

items.quote: Combined further with the taxation benefits that have been given for the middle-income households earning up to Rs. 25 lakhs per annum, this will further boost the purchasing power of these households and spur home demand as well as broader consumption.

items.quote: the sales of the top five real estate devel opers who are focused on quality and consumer service, thereby having strong brands are constrained by supply and not by demand.

items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA margin was at about 34.4%. This is an important point to note because the equivalent number in Q1 FY '25 was 33.7%, which shows that our margins continue to grow on a reported basis as well as on an embedded basis.

items.quote: We saw price growth of approximately 2% in Q1 FY '26 on a like-to-like basis, which is in line with our strategy to have price growth at around 6%, which is below wage growth, and therefore keeps affordability getting better each year.

items.quote: on a CAGR basis the cost continues to be reaso nably controlled in terms of the inflation. The impact is generally on a CAGR basis end up in being less than 3%.

items.quote: The Mulund-Airoli Freeway is progressing well and we expect it to be significantly operational in this fiscal year. We also note that the Navi Mumbai Airport is expected to start becoming operational for commercial flights this calendar year.

items.quote: The premium segment contribution in Palava for FY '25 stood at 20%, and this will keep growing towards 50% by the end of the decade, contributing both to a new segment of sales as well as higher blended margins.

items.quote: We tend to focus on homes between Rs. 1 crores to Rs. 5 crores with a particular emphasis on homes between Rs. 1 crores to Rs. 3 crores, but with higher per square feet price. items.quote: The matter is now expected to be decided by the Supreme Court in this quarter, and that will further enable us to scale up our supply and comfortably achieve our overall presales as well as operating cash flow guidance.

items.quote: Because now we hope it maybe around INR550 crores to INR575 crores.
