items.statement: Investing heavily in technology across broking platforms; Stoxkart app rated 4.5+ on app stores
items.quote: We are investing in technology and we are improving, and every time we are making ou r products mor e innovative and research -based and efficiency-wise we are improving our app.

items.statement: Network of 2,137 authorised persons across 412 cities; 6,811 financial distributors
items.quote: In Q1 FY26, our extensive network comprised 2,137 authorised persons across 412 cities, truly reflecting our pan -India presence.

items.statement: Insurance broking revenue Rs 116 crores; 90% from motor insurance (MISP) which declined 8% YoY
items.quote: In the insurance broking division, Q1 FY '26 revenue stood at Rs 116 crore.

items.statement: Life insurance revenue dipped YoY due to high group insurance base in prior quarter
items.quote: Life insurance has also seen a dip in the revenue as compared to the YOY numbers because of the major group insurance climb that we had in the last quarter.

items.statement: Regulatory changes (F&O norms, expiry cycles) caused temporary dip in derivative volumes
items.quote: The broking and financial services industry is undergoing a pivotal transition, shaped by regulatory changes, including stricter F&O norms and revised expiry cycles, alongside global uncertainties.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 43%; open to equity raise when needed; debt facilities ongoing from banks and NCDs
items.quote: Right now, the capital adequacy is around 43%. So, we are very comfortable.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM target of Rs 8,000 crores within one year via technology enablement for distributors
items.quote: So, that is, we have around 4500 mutual fund AUM distribution team. So, we can achieve Rs. 8000 crore in one year.

items.statement: NBFC operating through 42 branches across 9 states; average new LAP ticket size reduced to Rs 10-15 lakhs
items.quote: In our NBFC operations, we are active through 42 branches across 9 states.

items.statement: Micro-LAP book built to over Rs 35 crores; CGTMSE coverage started on unsecured loans
items.quote: We have already implemented that since about two quarters and we have been building the Micro-LAP book, which has reached over Rs. 35 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA boosted by Rs 5.81 cr investment gain vs Rs 9.33 cr loss in prior quarter; arbitrage income improved
items.quote: Actually, our EBITDA margin grew up QO Q because, in the quarter ended March 31, we had an investment loss of Rs 9.33 crores. Whereas in this quarter, we had an investment gain of Rs 5.81 crores.

items.statement: SME sector stress driving secured portfolio GNPA increase; recoveries expected in Q2 and FY26
items.quote: The GNPA numbers have gone up, that is primarily because of stress building up under the SME sector in the market.

items.statement: Stoxkart competing with Zerodha/Groww via SaaS subscription model; activation ratio 100% vs industry 20-25%
items.quote: We are running on a subscription model. As I told you, we provide software subscriptions. A client c an basically pay just Rs.99 per month and do unlimited trading on our platform o n the Stoxkart app.

items.statement: Stoxkart accounts trend tripling in Q2 vs Q1; 1,095 new SIPs added in Q1
items.quote: We added 1,095 new SIPs in this quarter.

items.statement: President of Manufacturing Prashant retiring mid-August after 9 years; Rajesh Naik (ex-Asian Paints, DuPont, BASF) named successor.
items.quote: Mr. Prashant, who was our President of manufacturing . After a wonderful 9-year stint with Laxmi, will be retiring as of middle of August. His successor, we have announced, is Mr. Rajesh Naik.

items.statement: Jitendra moves from Procurement to focus on Essentials business; Dr. Keshav Ruthiya (ex-BASF, 20 years) joins as Head of Procurement on August 1.
items.quote: I am very happy to share that Dr. Keshav Ruthiya joins us as of 1st of August as the Head of Procurement.

items.statement: Acetic acid prices declined from FY24 avg ~450 to ~340 currently; supply side remains long; BIS lifted on acetic acid imports.
items.quote: in FY24, average acetic acid prices across the year was around 450. Last year, it was about 400. And we have continued to see, you know, acetic acid prices dip lower. It was then at one-point 380-370 and today, point in time, is around 340 ballpark.

items.statement: Ethanol prices trending lower: FY24 avg ~840, FY25 avg ~720, currently stable at 690-700; no procurement bottlenecks.
items.quote: On an average in FY24, it was about 840, in FY25, it was about 720 and now as we speak, it is around 690 to 700 and sort of been stable at that level over the last three quarters.

items.statement: Printing & packaging and pharma demand stable QoQ; agro weak to moderate but inventory ebbing; CASE (Coatings, Additives, Sealants, Elastomers) demand muted in North America and Europe.
items.quote: There on a quarter-on-quarter basis, we see that demand to be stable. The second market is pharma. Again, there we continue to see demand to be stable. When it comes to agro, here we continue to notice it remains weak to moderate, certainly not as weak as what it was.

items.statement: Essentials spreads subdued at $120/MT (vs 12-yr avg $220-225); ethyl acetate spreads in $120 range in Q1.
items.quote: as we speak now, it is in the $120 range. That is a point in time. So that's where you see this also getting reflected first on the acetic acid, what I called out, that acetic acid prices are subdued.

items.statement: Essentials revenue grew 4% YoY driven by 11% volume growth offset by ~7% price decline from acetic acid feedstock drop.
items.quote: Essentials grew at 4%. It's led by volume growth of 11% offset by the price decline, which is mainly due to the acetic acid feedstock price declining of nearly 7%.

items.statement: Specialties revenue declined 18% YoY: ~9% from anticipated agro AI phase-out, ~4% from deferred deliveries shifting to H2.
items.quote: Speciality has a decline of 18% and as Rajan called out, there are mainly two factors impacting this. One is anticipated phase-out of a product, which is nearly 9% of our sales of the Speciality product.

items.statement: Q1 adjusted EBITDA margins: Essentials 2%, Specialties 16%.
items.quote: So, adjusted EBITDA for this quarter for Essentials is 2% and for Speciality it is 16%.

items.statement: Q2 performance expected in line with or better than Q1.
items.quote: On Q2 specifically, let me call out, we will continue to see performance which is in line with performance of Quarter 1 or better performance.

items.statement: Dahej project on track for mechanical completion and chemical charging end of Q3/early Q4 FY26; ~Rs 680 cr of Rs 750 cr FY26 capex spent.
items.quote: Dahej: Again, a very important part of our capex puzzle. That project remains on track, in scope, on track with regard to budget and on time horizons. So that is also giving us confidence. So somewhere towards the end of Quarter 3, early Quarter 4 is where we will have the mechanical completion and thereafter chemical charging happening for all the key assets at our Dahej facility.

items.statement: Lote Fluoro Intermediates ramp-up on track for 40-60% of peak revenues in FY26.
items.quote: Our Lote, the Flouro Intermediate site, that building on all the consistent effort over the past quarter, our ramp up continues. And I think we remain on target to achieve, as we have always called out in FY26, somewhere between 40% to 60% of the peak revenues.

items.statement: Hitachi Energy SF6 replacement LOI signed; contract expected to be finalized in Q2 FY26; capex accommodated within Rs 1,100 cr budget.
items.quote: Also, the Hitachi project which with Hitachi Energy, where we signed the LOI for an SF6 replacement, that is also taking good shape. And we are at really the cusp and the target is in Quarter 2 of this year. So, in this quarter, we would ideally like to stitch up the contract with Hitachi.

items.statement: New 200 TPD ethyl acetate line (single largest economy-of-scale line in India) to leverage 40% domestic market share and Europe export opportunity.
items.quote: So, Jigar, that the 200 TPD, first and foremost, this would be the single largest economy of scale line, I think, in India and also one of the economies of scale lines globally.

items.statement: No large change in competitive landscape from China in served segments.
items.quote: So, the simple answer to that, I think, linked to Laxmi, no, we have not seen any large change in the competitive landscape where we are serving, from China.

items.statement: Beijing signalling intervention in producer price wars; potential China capacity moderation could improve margins across value chain.
items.quote: Finally, Beijing has signalled that it will intervene in producer price wars. So, expectations are certainly growing for potential capacity moderation in China.

items.statement: Tariff conversations (India-US, India-UK, India-EU) seen as neutral to positive for Laxmi; ready to tap opportunities.
items.quote: And the ever -present tariff conversations that are happening with US or India with the UK, India with Europe, all of that also has certainly potential to provide opportunities where there could be improvements into margins.

items.statement: Supply chain digitization project started in Q1 (Rs 79 cr one-time cost spanning Q1-Q2); aims to improve efficiency, predictability, reduce costs, improve agility.
items.quote: We have spent on the project for digitization of the supply chain nearly 79 million as well as our Lote operations are now full-fledged.

items.statement: Depreciation policy changed from WDV to straight-line (Rs 24 cr impact in Q1); tax regime changed to new regime (one-time deferred tax gain).
items.quote: We have moved to a straight-line method for depreciation accounting from WDV. It is mainly because the economic benefits are in the increasing trend because we are in a capex mode.

items.statement: Sipchem (Middle East) announced mothballing of 100 KTPA ethyl acetate plant; no formal acetic anhydride capacity shutdowns known.
items.quote: So, there has been one announced capacity, which is in the Middle East called Sipchem. They announced to mothball their 100,000 tons ethyl acetate plant.

items.statement: Electrochemical fluorination platform targets $2.5 bn strategic relevant market within $25 bn fluorination space; Hitachi Energy LOI for SF6 replacement in power transmission.
items.quote: The first and foremost, the fluorination world, I will take it at a macro level, is a $25 billion space. Now, with the technology that we have established here in India, we basically are looking at targeting about a $2.5 billion strategic relevant market.

items.statement: Specialties H2 FY26 anticipated stronger than H1 due to deferred deliveries shifting to H2 and phase-out offset by mapped product by Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Speciality business, given that there is that deferment from Quarter 1, Quarter 2 into second half, our second half for our Speciality business is anticipated to be stronger as compared to our first half

items.statement: Essentials spreads at bottom of cycle (~$120 vs 12-yr avg $220-225); historically never seen spreads go negative; worst ~$100 then rebound.
items.quote: We certainly have not seen in the past also and we have looked over a 12 to 15 year period. We have never seen spreads go into negative territory. I think the worst we have seen spreads going to maybe about $100 and rebounding from those ranges.

items.statement: No full-year FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance given; Dahej ramp-up benefits expected in FY27.
items.quote: Sakshi, one is we really do not give out full year prognosis. So, I would certainly respect your understanding on that.

items.statement: Focus areas: productivity, commercial excellence, execution excellence, cost discipline (zero-based budgeting), growth projects (supply chain digitization).
items.quote: Given the current operational backdrop; we will continue our focus on productivity, commercial excellence, execution excellence, cost discipline and growth project.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 15%+ backed by ~13% volume growth and 1.5-2% price/mix change
items.quote: The guidance would be 15% plus of revenue growth backed by volumes, which will be about close to 13%. And 1.5% to 2% would be the change in the price.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 38-38.5% with 1-1.5% drag from new hubs

So, at a year level, still we want to maintain that guidance of 1%-1.5%, the EBITDA margin around 38-38.5% at a full year level.

items.quote: So, the cash position as on 30 th June is about Rs. 270 crores. And if you take the net cash after the capital creditors, it is about Rs. 220 crores.

items.quote: If you see the wellness share last year, Q1 is about close to 13.5% versus 14.2% now. If you take home collection as a channel, earlier we were at 2.5% of our overall revenue, now we are close to 3.2% to 3.3%.

items.quote: So, we have chosen as a company, our business model is that we stay away from PPP. It's just a choice of the company.

items.statement: Actively scouting acquisitions; will pursue if valuation, asset quality, and integration criteria met; open to opportunities in core and new regions
items.quote: So, we are on the look for acquisitions as and when we get the right opportunity, that's a continuous process. So, as long as that falls, when we have all the boxes ticked in terms of valuation, quality of the asset, other integration aspects, we will be happy to do that.

items.statement: IndAS 116 impact Rs 1.8 crore in Q1 FY26 (interest Rs 0.92 crore, depreciation Rs 0.95 crore)
items.value: Rs 1.8 crore total; Rs 0.92 crore interest; Rs 0.95 crore depreciation
items.quote: So, the IndAS impact for this quarter is around 1%, around Rs. 1.8 crores. So, out of that, the interest impact would be around 0.92 and depreciation will be 0.95. So, overall around Rs. 1.8 crores will be the impact for Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Q2 acute season (fever testing) start delayed due to late monsoon; too early to comment on Q2 trajectory

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 13.7% for FY26

You can see the improvement in the EBITDA as well and some of the customers that will be passed on after September because of the pre-decided formula that the prices for t he April to September will be reviewed by the customers and accordingly they will give the incre

items.statement: Alkop: 50 OEM customers, Tier A rated; new parts for EV (Tesla via Concentric, Porsche via TACO)
items.quote: Currently, we have around 50 customers, OEMs. So we are preferred supp lier for them. For the past so many years, we are in Tier 1. Our cus tomers rate us, it's like an exam. Quality on time, there's PPM, there are so many different metrics to judge on us. So we are Tier A supplier.

items.statement: Brakes: supplying brake pads to Endurance for Bajaj; Eaton P-PAP batch of 300 sets sent this month
items.quote: We already started supplying brake pads to Endurance Technologies in Aurangabad and they are catering to the demand from Bajaj.

items.statement: Railway brake approval pending dynamometer (₹3 crore) arriving end-September; inspection after
items.quote: That is subject to railway approval that is in process, along with that we'll be getting orders from one of the prominent customers, which is catering to OEMs and that is pending just because of testing equipment that is dynamometer, which costs around ₹3 crores, which is under process and we'll getting that dynamometer by the end of September, after which railway people will again come, will insp

items.statement: Alkop export share target 35-40% of ₹120 crore FY27 revenue
items.quote: Export will be almost at 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Aftermarket brake distributor receivables ~90 days; tightening distributor selection
items.quote: Again, there are problems such as recovery of our outstanding as well. That is in the aftermarket, it is delayed to some extent, about 90 days also. So we are locking such kind of customers, distributors.

items.statement: No JV/acquisition plans; rejected Chinese proposal due to geopolitics; exploring EV charging venture
items.quote: Not really as of now. We have received one proposal from a Chinese company. But due to diplomatic relations that we have or we ar e having with the Chinese counterpart. So what the Board felt that we should not go ahead with that proposal. So as of now, there is no plan.

items.statement: Alkop expanding into EV aluminium castings (Tesla, Porsche); bi-metal staying CV-focused, not entering PV
items.quote: In aluminium, we are not only doing engine. We are doing oil and pipe, gas line, two wheelers, tractors, trucks. Wherever aluminium is used, we are getting the right product. It is critical. Goo d value addition is there. We are developing those parts.

items.statement: Brakes aftermarket: 35 distributors now, target 150 next year; building separate team
items.quote: As of now, we are having 35 distributors. And our projection for the next year is almost 150.

items.statement: Japanese exports halted due to environmental bans on [indiscernible] in Japan
items.quote: No, no, Japanese , we are not working with Japanese so far. We are receiving very small orders from them because either they are diverted to somebody else, but what we learned from them that because of environmental problems, the [indiscernible] [ 0:18:59] etc., have been banned there in Japan. And that's why that export has been halted.

items.statement: New Alkop plant commissioned, machine shifting ongoing, fully operational by next month
items.quote: It's actually alr eady completed. We already started shifting the machine. The new plant is getting commissioned. So now I think by the next month, we'll have the whole plant ready.

items.statement: Management expects strong growth in FY26 over FY24 base and reiterates 20% CAGR over 3-5 years as reasonable
items.quote: We have also mentioned in the past that over 3-5 years, 20% CAGR is a reasonable number to look at for a company like Neuland and the kind of phase that we are. But yes, I don't want to connect the words with a number. But yes, we expect to see a strong growth in FY26 as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 14.4% in Q1FY26 due to revenue deleverage; management expects margins to recover as business ramps up but gives no quantitative guidance
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 42.1 crores at a margin of 14.4%. The decreased revenue has led to impact on margins as a result of deleverage, and there has been no other significant factor impacting the profit and loss account.

items.statement: Management believes EBITDA margins will return to strong levels comparable to FY24's 30%+ but refuses to give specific guidance
items.quote: We won't be able to provide any guidance on the margin front, but I think, yes, as you rightly recall, FY24 was in some ways exceptional in terms of very good margins, I think 30% or upwards, I think for various factors. I think we expect as our business ramps up, we should go back to very strong EBITDA margins.

items.statement: One new CMS molecule expected to commercialize in FY26; another CMS drug approved last year is scaling up; peptide projects in Phase-3 and earlier stages in pipeline
items.quote: We really don't wish to break things down at a quarterly level because that is something that we have avoided doing in the past and we do not want to set a new precedent in terms of trying to break things down. But we do remain very clear and confident that you will have that growth that we had indicated in FY26. Yes, the validation of our Unit 3 facility f or the CMS molecule is complete a nd the

items.statement: Pre-registration pipeline dropped from 9 to 8 molecules as one intermediate was dropped due to lack of customer volume traction
items.quote: So I think, Naveen, in terms of the product, it is a product which, I think it was an intermediate, which we have seen that the customer is not really looking to move forward because it hasn't picked up the volume that they expected, even as they had done work with us in the R&D. So since we no longer see that possibility, we have kind of dropped the product, but t hat doesn't really impact anythi

items.statement: Acquiring land adjacent to Unit 1 for integrated expansion including peptide facility; avoids 5-year greenfield timeline
items.quote: The peptide facility is also being built on an acquired piece of land next to Unit 1. That has been already integrated, and some expansion is going on there. But even beyond that, certain additional pieces of land are also being acquired. The idea is to have an integrated large site, rather than have a Unit 4, Unit 5, etc., which might again be operationally challenging, and even from a regulatory

items.statement: Seeing increased customer interest and first-time orders from both existing and new customers; new business expected to fructify over this and next financial year
items.quote: We are also seeing significant growth in terms of new business coming from both existing as well as new customers, which should fructify in the numbers over the course of this and next financial year. We are also excited by the range of customers expressing interest in our services and placing first-time orders.

items.statement: CMS contributed ~44% of Q1 revenue; GDS Prime (Mirtazapine, Ezetimibe) and Specialty (Dorzolamide) were key contributors; Ezetimibe reclassified from Specialty to Prime
items.quote: Revenues this quarter primarily came from commercial products in the CMS business as well as Prime GDS products like Mirtazapine and Ezetimibe. The specialty GDS business was also subdued this quarter with only Dorzolamide contributing significantly.

items.statement: Peptide portfolio includes 10-15 projects across GDS and CMS; new peptide facility expected completion next financial year
items.quote: We continue to garner more projects in this space, which further validates our excitement about the opportunities that the segment holds. Even our peptide scientific team is working on exciting projects.,at the same time, they are also developing capabilities that will help Neuland further differentiate itself as a peptide API manufacturer. We will continue to update you on the progress we are mak

items.statement: Working capital deteriorated to 145 days of sales in Q1FY26 due to higher inventory from uneven order flow; free cash flow negative Rs 66 crores
items.quote: While our focus on optimal utilization of cash remains a top priority, we have seen a deterioration in working capital this quarter as we have higher inventory due to the even nature of order flow. Working capital stood at 145 days of sales for the quarter, and a free cash flow for the quarter was negative Rs. 66 crores.

items.statement: Net debt negative Rs 165 crores (net cash position) as of Q1FY26
items.quote: Our net debt stands at a negative Rs. 165 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin 55.3% in Q1FY26 vs 56.1% in Q1FY25; includes manufacturing expenses directly attributed to product
items.quote: The gross margin for the quarter was 55.3% as compared to 56.1% in Q1FY25. These margins, as always, include manufacturing expenses and other costs that are directly attributed to the product.

items.statement: Peptide margins expected to be in line with CMS project margins; currently 10-15 peptide projects in pipeline
items.quote: I think when we are seeing, see, there is not a critical base, right? We have maybe 10-15 projects in peptides. And if we look at how the margins play out, intuitively you think that they are in line with the margins of the CMS projects. So I think it should be in line with what we currently do.

items.statement: Business lumpiness expected to reduce over 2-3 years as commercialized product base grows; currently driven by young molecule scale-ups and capacity timing
items.quote: I think we have had periods where we made validation batches and they were quarters where we had very strong revenue because we were shipping validation batches. We have had periods where we have had stron g revenue performance because we have had launch quantities being shipped. But things start to stabilize when you are in a commercial mode

items.statement: Management highlights factors that could influence projections: individual product performance, FX fluctuations, raw material cost volatility, business dynamics
items.quote: Another reminder from our previous interactions, we continue to maintain that there are a variety of factors that could influence the projections. These include performance of individual products, foreign exchange fluctuations, raw material cost volatilities, and other dynamics of the business.

items.statement: GLP-1 peptide opportunity: Tirzepatide prioritized for GDS; Semaglutide developed in lab but not pursued without partner; Liraglutide not moving forward
items.quote: So we have in the past looked at both Liraglutide and Semaglutide, but we are not really moving forward with them. I think the molecule that we are looking at in terms of our GDS business is Tirzepatide, while Semaglutide is a molecule which we have developed in the lab, but we decided not to move forward unless we have someone partnering with us on that molecule.

items.statement: Management has not examined stock split or bonus but will consider and discuss the possibility
items.quote: I think at the moment, we have not really examined the possibility of a split or a bonus, but definitely we will consider and discuss it and see if there is something that can be done.

items.statement: COPD drug in CMS pipeline just entering Phase-3; commercialization a couple of years away; new Phase-3 molecule added this quarter was acquired at Phase-3 stage, not internal progression
items.quote: Actually, what we had told is that that is the next big opportunity in the radar for us because it is kind of late in the clinic a nd at least it looks like there i s a high probability of success. But it is still maybe I think a couple of years away. We expect to make large scale API, but I think commercialization is still a little bit away

items.statement: Management open to organizing investor day for factory visits following analyst suggestion
items.quote: Yes, I think we ha ve never had something like that , but definitely we would be very happy to plan for something, maybe. So ye s, I think now that you have given the suggestion, let us also figure out and get back to you. But definitely something we would be happy to do

items.statement: Stand-alone revenue declined 14% to INR63 crores due to delayed government immunisation programs for PPR and lumpy skin disease
items.quote: On a stand-alone divisional product -wise performance, which has stood at INR63 crores, which reflects a 14% degrowth and PAT declining by 7%, mainly on account of delayed government immunisation program in our Animal Health division.

items.statement: Two large immunization programs for PPR and lumpy skin disease deferred but not cancelled; execution expected to pick up in Q2
items.quote: These programs are typically tender -driven and tend to have an organic and a nonlinear time line. While this quarter bore the brunt of those delays, we do expect traction and a return in Q2.

items.statement: Poultry Healthcare division grew 2% led by sustained demand for Newcastle disease and Marek's vaccines
items.quote: Coming to our Poultry Healthcare division, which has been - which has recorded a little bit of a growth of 2% led by our sustained demand for - in our key vaccines, namely the Newcastle disease vaccine and Mare k's vaccine.

items.statement: Stand-alone EBITDA and PAT margins held steady despite top-line pressure due to cost optimization and operational efficiency
items.quote: Despite the top line pressure, our focus on improving internal efficiencies and managing product mix has helped in protect our profitability.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT grew over 100% driven by improved international performance and margin control
items.quote: On a consolidated level, divisional sales has gone up despite of the dip that we see on a stand -alone basis. An d our PAT has grown by over 100%, driven primarily by improved international performance and margin control.

items.statement: Hester Africa turned profitable with INR5 crores profit on INR17 crores revenue, up from INR3 crores last year
items.quote: I'm happy to share that Hester Africa has not only recovered the loss that it had incurred in the same quarter last year, but it has also made profit of INR5 crores in this quarter. And this was on a top line of INR17 crores, up significantly from INR3 crores in the corresponding quarter in the last period.

items.statement: Tanzania facility stabilized; leveraging base to expand presence in high-demand regions for ruminant and poultry vaccines
items.quote: Our facility in Tanzania is now stabilized, and we are leveraging that base to expand our presence in regions wit h high demand for ruminant and poultry vaccines.

items.statement: Avian influenza vaccine launch awaiting regulatory clearances anticipated this quarter; everything from company side is clear
items.quote: One key focus area this quarter has been enhancing our preparedness for our upcoming launch of the avian influenza vaccine, which we had spoken about getting launched in Q1. Everything from our side is clear. We are just waiting for some regulatory clearances, which are anticipated to come in this quarter any time.

items.statement: BSL-3 facility repurposing in progress; permission expected in next few months to use for animal vaccines
items.quote: And we are in progress to getting it repurposed, probably we should get the permission in the next few months. And then we have plans on how to use this BSL-3 facility to increase our product range for animal vaccines.

items.statement: Petcare segment seeing good signals in western India with repeat demand and prescription interest; expected to contribute more meaningfully in coming quarters
items.quote: While early stage, we are seeing good signals in terms of repeat demand and prescription interest, as we believe this segment will start continuing more meaningf ully to the top line in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Plan to optimize capacity across three plants (India, Nepal, Africa) given rising demand in Africa
items.quote: Having said that, going forward, we are going to be needing more capacity given the demand, which is also going to come in Africa. So within our 3 plants, we will look at optimizing our capacity across these 3 plants that we have, given the rising demand that we see in the continent of Africa.

items.statement: Optimistic about remaining FY26 with institutional demand normalizing and momentum in Petcare and Poultry portfolios; confident of returning to growth
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the remaining part of FY '26, with institutional demand expected to normalize combined with increased momentum in newer markets across our Petcare and Poultry portfolio, we are confident of returning to growth in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Objective to gain more market share in poultry segment in coming months irrespective of industry dynamics
items.quote: And yes, but having said that, within the current situation, we are doing our best, and we are definitely now have taken up an objective to gain more market share in the coming months, and that should probably give us an upward trend, irrespective of the dynamics of the poultry industry.

items.statement: Feed supplements and disinfectants launched last year gaining acceptance; contributions expected to improve over next 2 quarters
items.quote: Our feed supplements and disinfectants launched last year are gaining acceptance, and we expect their contributions to improve further over the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: PPR vaccine tender business moved from FAO to African agency; company regularly following up and targeting private market in several African countries
items.quote: The PPR vaccine is mainly tender business. So it is centralized earlier by FAO. Now it has been moved to an African agency. We are regularly in touch with them, and there are absolute follow -ups. And besides that, we are also targeting the private - whatever small the private market for PPR is. We are focusing on quite a few countries in Africa.

items.statement: No visibility on African swine fever vaccine; no vaccine currently available worldwide; company scouting leads but no outer timeline
items.quote: African swine fever, we have not yet got any visibility on the African swine fever vaccine. There is no vaccine currently available in the world, but we are as much scouting to -- how to get into the manufacturing of African swine fever. We have a few leads. But at this point of time, it would be inappropriate for us to talk anything on that vaccine. At thi s point, you can take it. It's - we are

items.statement: No short-term plan to enter FMD vaccine market despite past interest
items.quote: But at this point of time, we are not into FMD, and we don't have any short-term plan of getting into that right away.

items.statement: Expanded technical support engagement with integrators and large poultry players to maintain strong market presence
items.quote: We also expand our technical support engagement efforts with our customers, especially integrators and large poultry players, and that will help us in maintaining strong market presence despite a broader industry volatility.

items.statement: Selectively expanded team in Africa to better address commercial opportunities
items.quote: On the international front, we are focusing on capacity utilization, improving logistics and response time a nd growing local engagement, particularly in Africa, where we selectively expanded our team to better address commercial opportunities.

items.statement: Nepal business consistent but quarterly revenues vary due to timing of institutional orders; market position remains strong
items.quote: Coming to Hester Nepal, it has shown a consistent performance. As typical of this geography, quarterly revenues can vary due to timing of institutional orders rather than underlying demand. That said, our market position remains strong, and we continue to maintain leadership across categories.

items.statement: Urban discretionary consumption under pressure; rural demand showing early signs of recovery.
items.quote: Urban di scretionary consumption continued to remain under pressure, while rural demand showed early signs of recovery

items.statement: Unseasonal rain and early monsoon shortened summer, hurting summer-focused portfolio.
items.quote: However, the unusually soft and shortened summer season driven by unseasonal rain and the early onset of the monsoons adversely impacted consumption across our summer-focused portfolio.

items.statement: Overall revenue broadly flat; core domestic business (ex-talc) grew 6% revenue and 3% volume.
items.quote: Excluding talc and prickly heat powders, our core domestic business delivered a healthy 6% revenue growth and a 3% volume growth, reflecting the underlying strength and resilience of our broader offerings.

items.statement: Talc and prickly heat powder category declined 17% YoY but 2-year CAGR healthy at 13%.
items.quote: The talcum powder and prickly heat powder category, which is highly dependent on summer demand was significantly impacted and declined by 17%.

items.statement: Navratna Oil grew 6% despite subdued summer.
items.quote: It is also encouraging to note that Navratna Oil delivered a 6% growth despite the subdued summer season.

items.statement: Pain management range grew 17%; BoroPlus antiseptic creams grew 60%; healthcare range grew 4%.
items.quote: Our pain management range grew robustly by 17%, while BoroPlus antiseptic creams grew by 60%. Our health care range maintained a steady growth of 4%.

items.statement: Male Grooming declined 9%; Kesh King declined 5%; strategic investments declined 4%.
items.quote: Male Grooming range declined by 9% and Kesh King declined by 5%. And strategic investments declined by 4%, but we remain confident in the long-term fundamentals, supported by ongoing brand and distribution interventions.

items.statement: Launched Dermicool Prickly Heat spray, Navratna and BoroPlus variants, relaunched Navratna Gold and Zandu Roll On, and 3 digital-first innovations on Zanducare.
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched Dermicool Prickly Heat spray and various other variants under Navratna and BoroPlus brands. We also relaunched Navratna Gold and Zandu Roll On. Further, 3 new digital-first innovations were rolled out via the Zanducare portal.

items.statement: Organized channels grew 6% with saliency up 190 bps; quick commerce scaled nearly 3x YoY.
items.quote: On the distribution front, we saw continued traction in our organized channels, which grew by 6%, with saliency improving by 190 basis points. Quick commerce remains a strategic growth channel, scaling up rapidly at nearly 3x Y-o-Y, further validating our omnichannel playbook.

items.statement: International business grew 2% despite macro volatility; rest of business ex-Bangladesh grew ~14%.
items.quote: Our international business delivered a modest 2% growth despite macroeconomic volatility and geopolitical uncertainty in some key markets.

items.statement: Plan to broaden offerings in new Southeast Asian markets as portfolio gains momentum.
items.quote: As this portfolio gains momentum, we plan to broaden our offerings to capture additional growth opportunities.

items.statement: Gross margins expanded 170 bps to 69.4%; EBITDA INR214 cr, down 1% with 20 bps margin contraction due to flat top line.
items.quote: On the financial front, our gross margins expanded by 170 ba sis points to 69.4%. EBITDA stood at INR214 crores, a marginal decline of just 1% with a 20 basis point contraction in margins, primarily attributable to flat top

items.statement: PAT grew 9% to INR164 cr.
items.quote: Profit after tax grew by 9% to INR164 crores.

items.statement: Smart & Handsome extending into other Male Grooming categories this quarter; Kesh King undergoing strategic transformation this quarter.
items.quote: Smart & Handsome is being extended into other Male Grooming categories in this quarter. Kesh King is undergoing a strategic transformation, reimagining the brand for sust ained relevance and future growth. This change is going to take place in this

items.statement: The Man Company returned to growth in June '25; confident of momentum via sharper positioning and 360-degree brand revamp.
items.quote: The Man Company has returned to growth in June '25, and we are confident of maintaining this momentum through a sharper positioning and a 360-degree brand revamp.

items.statement: Digital-first brands gaining traction; amplifying growth on marketplace and Qcom platforms.
items.quote: Our digital-first brands are gaining traction, and we are further amplifying growth on marketplace and Qcom platforms to drive reach and relevance among new age consumers.

items.statement: Confident on margin front; no significant input cost pressures anticipated near term.
items.quote: We remain confident on the margin front, and we do not anticipate any significant in put cost pressures in the near term

items.statement: Macro environment expected to improve gradually on buoyant monsoons, stabilizing inflation, consumption recovery.
items.quote: We believe the macro environment will gradually improve, supported by a buoyant monsoons, stabilizing inflation and ongoing consumption recovery.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion driven by mix shift to higher-margin pain management vs talc.
items.quote: So Nitin it is primarily driven by the mix, because normally, pain management has a higher margin compared to the talc. So it is due to the mix that the margins have gone up.

items.statement: A&P spends to be maintained as per last year's trends; not stepping up as percentage of sales.
items.quote: Not really Harit. I think we will -- we're maintaining our A&P spends as per last year's trends.

items.statement: Kesh King relaunch and Smart & Handsome new launches (10-12 products) expected to drive traction; timing of recovery uncertain.
items.quote: Kesh King is, again, a big relaunch in this quarter. Let's hope that it rebounds. Smart & Handsome was already relaunched. Now this -- from this quarter, we are launching 10, 12 new products under this new umbrella. So that should also bring some traction into the category.

items.statement: Pain management 17% growth attributable to early monsoon; July also good; if monsoon continues, category should do well.
items.quote: This 17% growth in the pain management is attributable to early monsoons. This is the peak season for this portfolio. And we have seen the same results in the month of July also. If the monsoon continues, which is predictable that the monsoons are going to be good this year, hopefully, this category should do well.

items.statement: Healthcare 4% growth slowdown seen as one-off blip in OTC range; initiatives underway for better Q2.
items.quote: Yes. So essentially, it seems to be a one-off issue. As you can see, over the last many quarters, we've been having good growth in health care, but quarter 1 was somewhat challenging, especially for the OTC range, where I think there was a bit of sort of a bit of a downturn in the market.

items.statement: Brand name change Fair & Handsome to Smart & Handsome accepted; both names on packaging to avoid confusion.
items.quote: Entire research was done. And by and large, people have accepted it. There is no place where the new product has not been launched. And we are still writing both the brand names. So Fair & Handome and Smart & Handome, both are on the packaging. So there is no chance of confusion.

items.statement: Kesh King decline due to D2C competition; BCG involved in new strategy.
items.quote: The key reason has been the D2C players. There have been a lot of new D2C interventions in this category. So that is the key reason. Of course, BCG ha s looked into every possible options. And the new strategy will take care of that also

items.statement: Cannot commit to 8-9% full-year value growth; ex-talc good but talc high base makes overall top line challenging.
items.quote: Rahul, I can't really comment at this point of time on 8%, 9% of growth. A lot will -- because first quarter, unfortunately, overall growth was not there and second quarter also has a high base of talc. So July has been pretty muted for talc. So overall numbers may be slightly challenging. But ex of talc, I don't see any challenge. I see good numbers.

items.statement: Man Company and Zandu Care losses to reduce vs last year, adding to consolidated EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Yes, yes, absolutely. I think both the Man company and the Zandu Care will definitely have lesser losses compared to the last year.

items.statement: Corporate logo rebrand for 50th anniversary; no commercial impact at consumer or trade level.
items.quote: Commercially, no, this is more of a corporate logo. So it doesn't have an impact at the consumer or the trade level, very honestly. Because we don't use this logo impacts or in any communication. It was just to celebrate 50 years of Emami and make it more modern, yes.

items.statement: International: new geographies continuous effort; scaled one new geography in last 5-6 months; more to open this financial year with new portfolio.
items.quote: The new geographies are a continuous effort. That will keep on happening along with the development of portfolio and making the current portfolio relevant for the new geographies. So we have been able to scale up one new geography, which has given us some good results in last 5, 6 months. So I don't want to name the country at the moment, but it is showing some decent results to us. But during the

items.statement: The Man Company: improved channel efficiency, media mix shift to top-of-funnel (influencers, product advertising); relooking brand mix and positioning; channel mix ~80% online; organized trade growing handsomely; no GT plans near term.
items.quote: So in both these places, we've tried to improve our efficiency, focus on secondaries so that's the true test of demand. The second thing that we've done is that right now, we've worked on our media mix. Objective, again, is to drive top of funnel. So we've driven media consumption and spend in terms of influencers, in terms of product like advertising.

items.statement: The Man Company targeting growth with reasonable CM2; channel spends expected to come down as brand presence improves.
items.quote: Look, I don't think it's one or the other. If we grow at a margin that's not good, then we will further destroy value. So we are, in fact, working on both fronts where -- and if you look at an online business, I would say it is revenue and CM2. That's what we need to focus on. That's the unit margin that we extract. And quite frankly, as our brand presence improves, we do expect that our channel s

items.statement: Axiom: significant minority stake; no channel consolidation intent short to medium term; digital/organized trade synergies explored.
items.quote: So right now, as far as Axiom is concerned, we have a significant minority stake at this point in time. So in terms of channel consolidation, there isn't any intent to do any channel consolidation in the short to medium term. Longer term, as our entry into the healthy food and beverage space expands, then there could be some synergies.

items.statement: Global advances growth guidance 12-13% for FY26
items.quote: In tune with growth of the global economy, the guidance for global advances growth will be at around 12% to 13% and the global deposit growth would be at around 10% to 11% in FY26.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance 0.70% for FY26
items.quote: As far as the guidance on credit cost is concerned, we are giving a guidance at around 0.70% for FY26.

items.statement: Net NPA guidance 0.70% for FY26
items.quote: So the guidance for net NPA is also 0.70% that we are giving.

items.statement: ROA guidance 0.90% for FY26
items.quote: But we are giving a guidance of around 0.90% for FY26 only because of the fact that the net interest income and net interest margins are under pressure in this financial year.

items.statement: Cost to Income ratio guidance around 51% for FY26
items.quote: The guidance that we are giving it is at around 51% for the simple reason that Q1 normally the income is muted in the books and the interest expenses are also there.

items.statement: CASA ratio internal target 40% for FY26
items.quote: So internally at the Top Management side, we are targeting that we should be at 40% for FY26.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance 1.20% for FY26
items.quote: So last year we had a fresh slippage of around Rs.7,600 crores. So this year, we are saying that we are giving a guidance of slippage ratio of 1.20% only.

items.statement: Global NIM guidance 2.50-2.60% for FY26
items.quote: And as far as the guidance is concerned, we should say that it should be in the range of between 2.50% to 2.60% for the FY26.

items.statement: Gross cash recovery target Rs.9,500 crore for FY26
items.quote: So this year, internal target is that we should do a re covery, gross cash recovery, which includes recovery from written off account, which also includes recovery from UCI and URI, which is the interest which has been applied somewhere at around a similar figure of around Rs.9,500 crore

items.statement: IT, digital and cyber security budget Rs.2,000 crore for FY26
items.quote: This year again , we have kept a budget on IT , digital and cyber security , of nearly Rs.2,000 crore and ag ain this year we'll be spending majority of the money to build more operational efficiency within the system

items.statement: Credit pipeline Rs.80,000 crore, of which Rs.10,000 crore RAM and rest Corporate/International
items.quote: So, we have a pipeline of around Rs.80,000 crores as we speak. Out of that Rs.80,000 crore, Rs.10,000 crore plus is the pipeline in the RAM segment and remaining is in the international and the domestic Corporate book.

items.statement: Global NIM 2.55% in Q1 FY26, domestic NIM 2.82%
items.quote: As far as the NIM is concerned, see, we are showing a NIM of a global NIM of around 2.55%. And the domestic NIM within that is 2.82% as on 30th of June.

items.statement: NIM bottomed out at 2.55%, expected to improve from Q3 FY26
items.quote: We have bottomed out as far as our NIMs are concerned at 2.55%. And as far as the guidance is concerned, we should say that it should be in the range of between 2.50% to 2.60% for the FY26.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of fixed deposits 6.98%
items.quote: The weighted average cost our fixed deposit is around 6.98%.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.92%, Net NPA 0.75%, PCR 92.94% in Q1 FY26

items.quote: When you look at EBITDA per KL, it came in at Rs 7,004 as opposed to Rs 6,935 per KL a year ago.

items.quote: The EBITDA margin came in at around 10% which is marginally lower than what it was in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Resin procurement evaluating alternative minerals and sourcing at better prices, not on contract basis
