items.statement: Business development additions of 5 projects with 9.24 msf and INR 11,400 crores booking value in Q1 FY26
items.quote: we started the year on a strong note by adding 5 new projects in estimated saleable area of approximately 9.24 million square feet and an expected booking value of INR 11,400 crores.

items.statement: Total inventory pipeline of INR 114,000 crores from historical BD and INR 60,000 crores from last 3 years BD
items.quote: we still have close to INR 60,000-odd crores worth of inventory to sell. And from a historical inventory, we are close to INR 114,000 crores of inventory.

items.statement: Launched and unsold inventory of about INR 27,000 crores
items.quote: So, say, about INR 27,000 crores.

items.statement: Pending collections on sold units of INR 51,000 crores
items.quote: So, pending to be collected, the revenue but pending to be collected is around INR 51,000 crores of collection is pending to be collected.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA grew 18% to INR 915 crores, net profit grew 15% to INR 600 crores
items.quote: In the 1st Quarter, our total income decreased by 3% to INR 1,593 crores, EBITDA grew by 18% to INR 915 crores and net profit grew by 15% to INR 600 crores.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly net profit of INR 600 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: We have delivered our highest ever quarterly net profit of INR 600 crores in the 1st Quarter, a growth of 15% year-on-year.

items.statement: Like-to-like price increases of 2-3% in North, 1-2% in Mumbai, <1% in Pune, 2-3% in South markets
items.quote: most projects in North, we have been able to increase price between 2% to 3%. We have been able to increase between 1% to 2% in Bombay, marginally basically less than 1% in Pune market and about 2% to 3% in South market.

items.statement: Demand conditions remain favorable, strong demand across all new project launches
items.quote: The residential real estate sector in India has been strong over the past 4 years, and we believe the demand conditions remain favorable.

items.statement: Selling 70-90% of opened inventory per launch, consciously holding prime inventory for pricing uptake
items.quote: whatever we are opening stock between the towers that we open, the floors we open, give or take, between 70% to 90% is what we are selling. Consciously, we are holding some very, very prime inventory so that we can ride through some amount of pricing uptake, but we are seeing very strong demand, yes.

items.statement: Bangalore sales highest in country and for any developer in Bangalore, strong walk-ins and conversions
items.quote: our Bangalore sales last quarter, of course, was the highest of anywhere in the country, and also I think they have been the highest for any developer in Bangalore.

items.statement: COC run rate increased to INR 1,170+ crores in Q1 FY26 from INR 750 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: COC in Q1 of the previous financial year was about INR 750-odd crores. And the quarter 1 COC was about INR 1,170 plus crores. So, we are seeing a very strong execution uptake.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 deliveries of 0.8 million sq ft against full year target of at least 10 million sq ft
items.quote: operating cash flow slightly declined by 4% to INR 947 crores, largely on account of the relatively low deliveries we had during the quarter of under 1 million square feet against a full year target of at least 10 million square feet.

items.statement: GPL share of booking value 78% in Q1 FY26, lower due to large JV project sales in Bangalore
items.quote: The other question was, the GPL share this quarter was a little bit lower than last year because of the large sales in Bangalore, in our JV project, so that was 78% for the quarter.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR 947 crores in Q1 FY26, down 4% YoY due to low deliveries
items.quote: operating cash flow slightly declined by 4% to INR 947 crores, largely on account of the relatively low deliveries we had during the quarter

items.statement: Balance land payments of INR 900 crores for FY26 deals and INR 1,000-1,200 crores for earlier deals including Ashok Vihar instalment
items.quote: For the deals, which we have signed in this year, balance to spend is around INR 900 crores and around INR 1,000 crores or INR 1,200 crores for the earlier deals, which we have signed in '25 and '24, which are milestone-linked payments.

items.statement: Ashok Vihar launch delayed due to approval authority issues and court views on tree cutting policy, but positive movement seen
items.quote: there has been set of approval authority issues in the government setup on which department grants approval where and how. There has been some views from the court also on the overall tree cutting policy of Delhi.

items.statement: Share price considered at absurd levels given growth momentum, promoters bought back shares over last 6 months
items.quote: we clearly think the share price is at a kind of absurd levels, given the kind of growth and overall operational momentum we have delivered. The promoters have actually bought back some shares on the market over the last 6 months.

items.statement: Group added ~5,000 billable headcount in Q1 FY26; all three businesses grew headcount
items.quote: At group level, we have added 5,000 billable headcounts in Q1 FY '26, including 110 net additions in specialized staffing.

items.statement: General staffing net headcount addition ~3,000+ (5% YoY); 1/3 from new clients
items.quote: Our general staffing business continued to deliver, closing the quarter with a net headcount addition of approximately 3,000+, reflecting a 5% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: Specialized staffing net headcount addition ~115 (India + global)
items.quote: We closed the quarter with a net headcount addition of about 115 resources, a combination of b oth India and global headcount increase

items.statement: Degree Apprenticeship added ~1,700 apprenticeships (1,472 from learning-led program)
items.quote: In Q1, our TLDA added about 1,700 apprenticeships across NAPS, NATS, and WIP, driving an increase in operational PAPM priorities services.

items.statement: ~20,000 open positions in general staffing (lower than ~30,000 last year)
items.quote: we have about 20,000 plus open positions and our continued foc us on driving productivity, especially in sales and hiring, combined with the momentum we are seeing from our digital transformation gives us strong conviction about the year ahead

items.statement: Specialized staffing client pipeline robust with high-quality deals in advanced stages for H2 FY26
items.quote: Our client pipeline remains robust with high -quality deals in advanced stages of closure, reinforcing visibilit y for H2 and FY '26.

items.statement: Group EBITDA grew 39% YoY (34% organic); Q1 impacted by ED Tech seasonality and salary appraisals
items.quote: Overall, revenue grew 12% year-on-year and EBITDA by 39% year -on-year. This demonstrates significant operating leverage and also excluding inorganic contribution, year -on-year EBITDA growth stands at 34%.

items.statement: General staffing EBITDA grew 11% YoY; PAPM flat QoQ; value-added services and operating leverage to drive margins in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: The PAPM has been fla t on a quarter -on-quarter basis, Amit. And as far as tailwinds are concerned, so we are working on other value-added services both to clients as well as associates. So that is going to help us expand profits as well as margins in the next 2-3 quarters

items.statement: Specialized staffing margins diluted by core employee appraisals and lower-margin MSP mandates; target 7-7.2% by year-end
items.quote: So specialized staffing, two reasons. So one is this quarter, we have our annual employee appraisal for core employees. So that has an impact. And also, we are taking up some MSP mandates. So varying the margins, the gross margins are on lower end.

items.statement: Expect at least 30% YoY EBITDA growth for remaining quarters of FY26
items.quote: But for the rest of the quarters in the year, we should be able to maintain at least a 30% EBITDA growth year -on-year.

items.statement: HR Tech expected to turn EBITDA positive by mid-next year (mid-FY27)
items.quote: The HR Tech is really where the investments are happening and we believe that by mid-next year, we will be EBITDA positive there.

items.statement: HR Services segment (RegTech + ED Tech) to maintain 25-30% revenue growth with 6-8% EBITDA margin
items.quote: No, they should maintain a revenue growth of 25 %-30% consistently and with an EBITDA margin of anywhere between 6%-8%.

items.statement: Specialized staffing global revenue share to hold at 8-10% for FY26
items.quote: It will broadly hold at 8%-10% for this year, Amit. Because I think we are expecting the domestic growth also to sustain.

items.statement: Singapore rate cards 5-6x Indian rates; Indian margins currently better but global margin expansion expected
items.quote: In terms of absolute numbers, the rate cards that we are currently getting in our Singapore geography are almost 5-6 times higher than the Indian ones. But in terms of margin percentage, as of now, our Indian clients are doing much better.

items.statement: Added 110+ new logos across businesses; 44 in general staffing (60% variable markup)
items.quote: We also added over 110 new logos across the businesses and despite the persistent macroeconomic headwinds affecting the BFSI and IT services verticals, we have delivered EBITDA growth of nearly 39% year -on-year.

items.statement: Specialized staffing onboarded 11 new clients (5 GCCs) across consulting, life sciences, manufacturing, engineering
items.quote: In the last quarter, we have onboarded 11 new clients consisting of 5 GCCs, including strategic logos across global consulting firms, life science and pharma, manufacturing, and engineering customers.

items.statement: GCC segment contributes ~46% headcount and 64% net revenue in specialized staffing; 75 GCC customers
items.quote: The GCC segment remains a cornerstone of our business, both in terms of volume and stability, contributing approximately 46% of headcount and 64% of net revenue. We continue to de epen engagement across 75 GCC customers of ours.

items.statement: BFSI headcount grew 6.4% YoY; FMCG de-grew 4.4%; FMCD, telecom, retail, e-commerce flat
items.quote: So in summary, Q1 we are seeing a mixed bag of sectoral growth. BFSI grew by 6.4% in terms of headcount, FMCG de-grew 4.4%. The rest of them, FMCD, telecom, retail, e -commerce, all remain flat.

items.statement: 65% of gross joinees from Tier-2/3 cities (avg salary Rs 21k vs base Rs 27k); mix shift marginally impacted QoQ revenue
items.quote: With respect to hiring trend, almost 65% of the gross joinees in the quarter were from Tier -2, Tier-3 cities with an average salary of Rs. 21,000 versus total base average of Rs. 27,000.

items.statement: Staffing DSO 7 days; group DSO 17 days; funding exposure 14%; free cash Rs 310 cr net of capex
items.quote: DSO in staffing business stands at 7 days and the overall group DSO at 17 days. Funding exposure in the staffing business is maintained at 14% with high cash conversion to EBITDA. Free cash balance stands at Rs. 310 crore net of cap expense over the quarter.

items.statement: RBI policy easing (credit risk weights, NBFC norms, rate cuts) driving gradual BFSI hiring recovery
items.quote: We had called out in our May results that the recent positive policy actions from the RBI, such as the revision in credit risk weightages and relaxed norms for NBFCs, coupled with rate cuts, might result in some recovery.

items.statement: Government apprenticeship push: inflation-linked stipend hikes, Rs 60k cr ITI upgrade, SOAR AI readiness program
items.quote: Recent government announcements reinforce our direction. The Central Apprenticeship Council recommendation for inflation -linked stipend increases, the Rs. 60,000 crore ITI upgradation plan, and the launch of SOAR, Scaling for AI Readiness, signals strong policy support for apprenticeships and employability.

items.statement: Specialized staffing expanding build-operate-transfer model, GCC enablement, niche digital skills (AI/ML/cloud/cyber)
items.quote: Our build -operate-transfer model continues to scale as well. In quarter 1, we expanded engagement in verticals such as BFSI, IT, and product engineering. We have also strengthened our GCC enablement offering through ecosystem partners across infrastructure, legal, and technology, positioning us as a full -stack workforce solutions partner.

items.statement: Degree Apprenticeship monetizing learning-linked products; 22% existing clients adopted learning solutions
items.quote: Promotion of learning solutions remains a focus area. Amongst existing clients, 22% have adopted learning solutions. This growing adoption reflects the tangible impact learning has on improving productivity, reducing attrition, and enhancing apprentice engagement.

items.statement: Technology investments in automation-first workflows, hiring systems, recruiter upskilling driving productivity
items.quote: Recruiter productivity continued to improve, aided by automation -first workflows, focused hiring systems, and upskilling of the recruiters.

items.statement: 17,000+ new joinees in general staffing (10% QoQ, 25% non-recruiter channels, 24% first-time employees)
items.quote: On the hiring side, for the quarter we delivered about 17,000 plus new joinees, 10% higher than the last quarter, and 25% of them hired through non -recruiter channels. 24% of these gross joinees are first-time employees.

items.statement: Credit card hiring remains significantly subdued; BFSI recovery pace uncertain
items.quote: Credit card business specifically still remains significantly subdued. It is too early to say how this will pan out, but we are positive about this, combined with the fact that income tax relief will lead to a consumption pickup and the need for asset products from financial institutions.

items.statement: Consumer durables impacted by unseasonal rains; urban demand subdued though rural/semi-urban improving
items.quote: While April in itself started on a good note, we saw unseasonal rains and weather impacting the sale of FMC D goods, which is largely air conditioning, refrigerator parts, which resulted in muted growth for the rest of the quarter in terms of headcount addition for us in that

items.statement: Guided consolidated EBITDA margin at 21% but delivering above that level
items.quote: We always have guided consolidated margins at 21% and never guided beyond that. However, we have shown better results.

items.statement: Q2 CY2025 EBITDA margin improved 82 bps YoY to 28.5% despite new plant fixed costs
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 19,987.7 million with EBITDA margin improving by 82 basis points YoY to 28.5% in Q2 of 2025, driven by operational efficiencies and a strong currency in international operations.

items.statement: India volumes fell 7.1% in Q2 due to unseasonal rains; international volumes grew 15.1% led by South Africa 16.1%
items.quote: In India, volumes were impacted by abnormally high and unseasonal rainfall all through the quarter, resulting in a 7.1% decline in India. However, this was partially offset by healthy growth in international markets where volumes grew 15.1% led by a growth of 16.1% in South Africa.

items.statement: India capex limited to Rs 600-700 crore next year; international capex for South Africa expansion and Zimbabwe snacks plant
items.quote: In India, we are not looking at more than Rs. 600 - 700 crore for next year. In international markets, we do not have the exact numbers, but we are looking to expand in South Africa and some other countries.

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization near 70%; enough headroom for next 2 years in India
items.quote: We are close to 70% capacity utilization, and we believe we have enough room for the next 2 years at least.

items.statement: Four new Greenfield plants commissioned in India (Prayagraj, Damtal, Buxar, Mendipathar) and snacks plant in Morocco; Zimbabwe snacks plant starting October
items.quote: These plants significantly enhance our production capabilities and supply chain agility, laying a strong foundation to capitalize on long-term growth opportunities in the Indian beverage market.

items.statement: Freight cost reduced via distributor consolidation and new plants closer to markets; manpower rationalized; newer lines more efficient; added renewable energy
items.quote: What we have done in terms of freight cost optimization, we have consolidated a lot of distributors of ours, which has helped us send larger load sizes and has helped us in the freight cost per case.

items.statement: Low/no added sugar products contributed ~55% of consolidated volumes in H1 CY2025; water mix up 2% in Q2
items.quote: Low or no added sugar products contributed around 55% of the consolidated volumes in H1 2025, reflecting our continued efforts to evolve with consumer preferences.

items.statement: Reaching ~4 million retail outlets; target to add 300k-400k outlets this year but rains may limit achievement
items.quote: Currently, Devanshu, we are reaching out at about 4 million outlets. This year the goal was to increase it by another 10%, by about 300,000 to 400,000 outlets.

items.statement: Working capital days stable at ~35 days vs 33 days last year despite capacity additions
items.quote: Working capital days remain ed broadly stable at approximately 35 days compared to last year's 33 days, supported by disciplined inventory and receivables management

items.statement: Indian business now net debt-free after QIP proceeds; finance costs reduced significantly
items.quote: Finance costs have been reduced significantly with the Indian business now net debt-free following the QIP proceeds and the remaining costs largely attributable to South Africa.

items.statement: Board approved second interim dividend of 25% face value (Rs 0.50/share) totalling Rs 1,691 million cash outflow
items.quote: In line with our dividend policy, the Board of Directors ha ve approved a second interim dividend of 25% of face value, i.e., Rs. 0.50 per share, resulting in a total cash outflow of approximately Rs. 1,691 million

items.statement: Actively looking for new acquisitions and international expansion; formed JV with Everest for visi-cooler manufacturing; acquired 50% equity in Everest's Sri Lankan plant
items.quote: We are looking for new acquisitions, and we are very actively looking at it and also expansion in the international market.

items.statement: Strong positive currency movement in Africa territories boosted profitability; currency stabilization supported international margins
items.quote: Due to growth in international markets supported by strong positive currency movement in Africa territories, Company ended the quarter with a positive PAT in-spite of 3% decline in consolidated sales volume.

items.statement: Net realization per case improved 0.5% consolidated; international realization up 6.6%
items.quote: Net realization per case at the consolidated level improved marginally by 0.5% supported by a favorable mix in the international markets per case realization recorded a 6.6% increase.

items.statement: Demand outlook dependent on weather; unseasonal rains impacted Q2 and continuing into Q3
items.quote: The real answer would depend on the rain gods, which is very difficult to predict. The rainy season has been quite prevalent in July and it's not been the best of the seasons.

items.statement: Visi-cooler placements up ~15% YoY; plan to continue at this pace
items.quote: We have expanded our Visi placements. Our Visi placements have gone up by approx. 15% from last year. And I think we will continue at this pace going forward.

items.statement: Competition exists but confident of maintaining margins through cost efficiencies, debt-free status, and productive newer plants
items.quote: We don't see any reason why these margins should come down.

items.statement: Awaiting Competition Commission of South Africa approval for land parcel purchase in Boksburg for capacity expansion
items.quote: We are awaiting approval from Competition Commission of South Africa for land parcel purchase adjoining our production facility in Boksburg to further enhance capacity and backward integration.

items.statement: International subsidiary loans converted to equity to strengthen balance sheets (DRC, Dubai, Zambia, South Africa); Zambia stake raised from 90% to 95%
items.quote: These loans have now been converted into equity to strengthen their respective balance sheets. So, it is not that we had to send fresh funds now to sustain their operations.

items.statement: Sting Gold receiving mixed response; not close to Sting Red performance; will push for next two quarters for clearer picture
items.quote: Sting Gold has got a mixed reaction, it's not been anywhere close to our Sting Red. But certain markets have accepted it and certain markets have not accepted it.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain EBITDA margins around Q1 levels (11.61%) but cites rare earth magnet uncertainty
items.quote: we hope that we should be in a position to be around that margin but again as I told you there are unpredictable conditions because of the rare earth magnet we have to wait and see

items.statement: Plans Rs 500 crore capex over next three years on consolidated basis
items.quote: In the next three years, we will be spending somewhere around Rs. 500 crores of CAPEX on a consolidated level.

items.statement: Of the Rs 500 crore capex, Rs 250-300 crore for PRICOL Precision and balance for PRICOL Limited
items.quote: Out of the INR 500 crores of CAPEX, like INR 250 to Rs. 300 crores will be for PRICOL Precision and balance will be for PRICOL Limited.

items.statement: PRICOL Precision can scale up 20-22% more revenue with existing capacities
items.quote: And capacity utilization is something like the Company can scale up for another 20-22% further revenue with existing capacities.

items.statement: Q1 muted due to rare earth magnet shortage from China; headwinds expected to continue in Q2; stable revival expected from Q3
items.quote: The two -wheeler has just grown by 1%. That is primarily because you would have heard in the media about the shortage of rare earth magnet primarily due to the restriction of rare earth magnet from China. It had headwinds during Q1 and we expect the headwinds to continue in Q2 also.

items.statement: PRICOL outperformed market with double-digit growth despite industry growing less than 2%
items.quote: The market has grown only by less than 2% on a consolidated basis. That is, two wheeler, commercial vehicle, personal passenger vehicle, all put together, the market has grown less than 2%. Whereas, PRICOL has grown more than 10%.

items.statement: ABS regulation mandatory from January 2026 for 100cc+ two-wheelers, making disc brakes mandatory and creating growth opportunity
items.quote: the ABS regulation is becoming ma ndatory from January 2026 even starting with the 100cc two -wheelers, it means that the disc brake would be mandatory for all the vehicles in which ABS is going to be used

items.statement: Technology license agreement with Italian firm Domino for control systems (switches, throttles, levers) exclusive for India and Southeast Asia; revenues expected in 12-16 months
items.quote: We have signed the technology license agreement with an Italian firm called Domino for control systems primarily on two-wheeler handlebars components such as switches, throttles, levers, etc. This is an exclusive arrangement for the Indian and Southeast Asian markets and this is also being done primarily on behalf of the customer confi dence that they had in PRICOL and we are quite confident to st

items.statement: E-cockpit and BMS development completed, under testing at customer places; growth plan in couple of quarters
items.quote: e -cockpit and BMS are currently developed and it is testing at various customer places. It is going to take another couple of quarters before we could come in terms of what is going to be the grow th plan and strategy for both e- cockpit and BMS.

items.statement: PRICOL Precision Q1 EBITDA ~7%; last year Q1 was ~5%; profitability improvement plan yielding results from Q2
items.quote: We have clocked a turnover of close to INR 205 crores for the 1st Quarter in PRICOL Precision Products Private Limited. With an EBITDA of close to 7%.

items.statement: PRICOL Precision targeting healthy single-digit EBITDA this year; consolidated EBITDA to be maintained
items.quote: we are quite confident this year we will be launching comfortably a healthy single-digit EBITDA and at a consolidated level to maintain the EBITDA rate for the organization overall.

items.statement: Mitigated most China sourcing since 2020; displays still China-dependent; targeting backward integration/localization of displays in next 4 quarters
items.quote: Our target is that in the next four quarters, we should be in a position to start some kind of backward integration or localization of the displays. Though not fully, we will have a good initiative in terms of backward integration.

items.statement: Revenue mix: ~65% two-wheeler, ~10% passenger vehicle, ~15% commercial vehicle, ~10% off-road/tractors
items.quote: About 65% of our revenue comes f rom the two -wheeler segment. I am giving you a rough estimate. It could be varying here and there, but as a thumb rule, about 65% comes from the two-wheeler segment, about 10% comes from the personal passenger vehicle segment, about 15% comes from the commercial vehicle segment and about 10% comes from the off -road vehicle and tractors.

items.statement: PRICOL Precision leveraging PRICOL's larger customer ecosystem; strategic customers floating RFQs; moving up value chain
items.quote: We are in the process of leveraging PRICOL's larger ecosystem of client pools and our strategic customers which will yield results in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Disc brake market has mature players but ABS regulation opens opportunities for new players like PRICOL; growth expected over next two years
items.quote: There are a number of mature players in the market. But it is going to open up a lot of opportunity for new players like PRICOL because the mandatory regulation is going to be there. It is going to open up a lot of avenues in terms of growth f or even new players like PRICOL . I think the growth is going to be good in the next two years.

items.statement: Consolidated long-term borrowing at Rs 109.7 crore as of Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our consolidated long-term borrowing as of Q1 is at Rs. 109.7 crores.

items.statement: Rare earth magnet shortage from China causing Q1/Q2 headwinds; mitigation plans in place but uncertainty beyond control
items.quote: There have been uncertainties in the market in terms of the model mix change with the various OEMs. PRICOL has put a good amount of resilience in terms of meeting those changing conditions and despite the market being muted during Q1, PRICOL has shown a double- digit growth as you can see. Q2 , also we expect headwinds at from the OEM in terms of model mix changes and primarily they are countering

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty not yet impacting; monitoring situation but no effect on products or export strategy currently
items.quote: As of now, we have not seen any uncertainty because of that because I think the US tariffs have not been firmed up, as you know that there are several different information in the last two to three months and it is keeping on extending. So, at this point of time, we do not see any uncertainties in terms of our product getting affected because of tariffs to the US market.

items.statement: Margin fluctuations due to INR/USD depreciation; 100% of raw material forex indexed back-to-back with customers
items.quote: The margins actually is little fluctuating, but it will become all right, primarily because of fluctuation in the dollar to rupee conversion If you see that even two days back, there has been a steep depreciation of the INR against the dollar and since we are import dependent, there will be some fluctuation in terms of the margins, but it gets regularized because 100% of our external factors like

items.statement: Employee cost ~12% of sales; forward-looking recruitments for new projects launching in next couple of years
items.quote: The employee cost percentage was at around 12% and as we have been telling in the previous earning call, we are making some forward-looking recruitments primarily for many of our new projects which are going to be launched in the next couple of years.

items.statement: ACFMS segment growing steadily with strong export content to marquee customers (Caterpillar, Harley-Davidson, Polaris, Generac, Kohler)
items.quote: We supply both to the Europe and the US market, primarily into many of the marquee customers like Caterpillar, Harley -Davidson, Polaris, Generac, and Kohler . We have got a number of customers with whom we export our ACFMS products to the US and Europe.

items.statement: DIS segment growth driven by value (premiumization) more than volume; mechanical to electronic to high-end electronics conversion continuing
items.quote: PRICOL has been in the last few years having more value growth when compared to the volume growth. And this is expected to continue because of the premiumization happening in the driver information system space and we expect this to continue for a few more years, because a lot of conversion which are happening from the mechanical meters into more of electronics and there upon into the high-end ele

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 is INR 900-1,000 crore; next 2-3 years capex INR 3,500-3,700 crore
items.quote: This year, we are likely to incur a capex of somewhere in the range of about INR900 crores-1,000 crores. So, that is the capex that we are intending to do for this year. As far as the next 2-3 years are concerned, we will land up doing a capex of INR 3500 crores-3,700 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated volume grew 16% YoY to 267 MMSCM; CNG volume up 21% to 185 MMSCM; PNG volume up 6% to 82 MMSCM
items.quote: On the operational side, Adani Total Gas has achieved during this quarter robust year-on-year volume growth of 16% to 267 MMSCM which was largely driven by increase in the CNG volume by 21% to 185 million metric standard cubic metre, MMSCM and achieved 82 MMSCM of a PNG volume which grew by 6%.

items.statement: Higher gas cost due to lower APM allocation replaced by New Well Gas, HPHT and RLNG; calibrated pass-through to consumers
items.quote: This increase in the volume was achieved despite our higher gas cost because we passed through very calibratedly to the end consumers. This higher gas cost was on account of, as you are all aware, lower allocation of APM gas which got replaced or off setted with higher price New Well Gas and high pressure high temperature (HPHT) gas and we also added some portion of domestic or RLNG gas which was

items.statement: Entered agreement with Jio-BP to leverage each other's infrastructure for fuels and EV charging; will accelerate DODO/CODO CNG station additions
items.quote: Further, to enhance customer experience and offerings, you are aware that during this quarter we have entered into an agreement with a Jio-BP which sells MS (Motor spirit)- pet rol, HSD-diesel to leverage each other's infrastructure to provide a complete range of high quality fuels to the consumers. This tie-up will help us accelerate the addition of DODO and COD O CNG station with Jio-BP fuel acr

items.statement: CNG registrations growing: FY23 +12%, FY24 +15%, FY25 +17%; CNG share of fuel mix 65-70%
items.quote: Just to add to that in terms of some data points of registration, the CNG registrations have been growing. So, if I were to look at from FY23 to FY25, registrations in FY23 grew by 12%. These are more from India overall standards, overall numbers. In FY24 grew by 15% and in FY25 it grew by 17%. So, on one hand you are continuing to see registration which is effectively newer conversion of vehicles

items.statement: CNG growth split: existing geographies +12% YoY, newer geographies +30%+ YoY; existing geographies 65% of volume, newer 35%
items.quote: Coming more specifically in terms of the CNG growth rates that we have seen, we continue to see double-digit growth rates even now as far as the existing geographies are concerned. So, adoption continues to be there as far as the existing geographies are concerned. As far as newer geographies are concerned, the growth rates are far more significant higher because of simply the addition of newer ne

items.statement: APM gas allocation for CNG down to ~36%; replaced by higher-cost New Well Gas, HPHT, RLNG; calibrated pricing pass-through impacting net profit
items.quote: The APM allocation has come down to almost 36% for CNG and it has been replaced with new well gas, HPHT and we are buying additional gas to meet the consumer demand. But our pass-through has been very calibrated. That is the reason there is slight dip if you see on the net profit at the end.

items.statement: Capex focused on 11th round geographies: core steel network and CNG stations; precedes PNG/domestic connections
items.quote: Primarily, this capex is aimed towards the network creation especially of the 11th round geographies and we have always preceded the CNG stations over the PNG and the domestic connections in terms of incurrence of capex. So, really, the significant part of this capex will be core network of steel and to add to that on the CNG station.

items.statement: Consolidated JV network: 1,078 CNG stations, 11.7 lakh PNG homes, 10,640 I&C consumers, 25,829 inch-km steel pipeline across 53 GAs
items.quote: Now, if I may take it, our performance along with our 50 -50 JV with Indian Oil Corporation, namely Indian Oil Adani Gas Pvt. items.statement: ESG rating improved by CRISIL from Adequate to Strong, rated CRISIL ESG 61
items.quote: I am happy to report that with the dedicated focus on sustainability and ESG, our ESG rating has been improved by CRISIL from Adequate to Strong. We have been rated at CRISIL ESG 61.

items.quote: PNGRB has notified that August month will continue to have a similar arrangement as it is hitherto and they may come with a new tariff which regulation they have passed. And the good news is that they have also stated in the same notificat

items.quote: The past six months or the past quarter was a bit of a winter month where we have a lot of consumers using water heating through a gas geyser that enhances the consumption. Quarter-on-quarter, you will see there will be some sort of an attraction which is not supporting because of this seasonality pa

If organization has a commitment on emission norms to be followed for their exports, etcetera they are taking commercial vehicle on CNG
