This is a normal increase which takes place by OEMs due to various factors and that has a slight implication on CNG vehicle, but otherwise the difference between petrol and diesel vehicles are being maintained as it used to be because there is a CNG kit and there is a tax on the CNG ki

items.statement: APM gas allocation notice period being extended by government; earlier short notice now extended further for CGD planning
items.quote: Yes. So they have agreed upon giving enough notice so that everybody can plan the shortfall and the shortfall demand what they see. And it is under process and definitely it will be in place in due course. Earlier, it was very short notice that has been extended, but they are trying to extend it further. So, enough timeline is given to the requirements of CGDs.

items.statement: Bio-CNG: Barsana plant commissioned; first DODO CBG station set up in Hodal, Haryana
items.quote: Similarly, on the bio business side, we had already commissioned our Barsana plant and now we have set up the first DODO CBG station in Hodal, Haryana.

items.statement: Amisha Jain appointed as new MD and CEO effective August 13, 2025, succeeding Shailesh Chaturvedi
items.quote: As part of the succession planning of the organization, we will have Amisha Jain join us as the Company's new MD and CEO effective August 13, 2025.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth target of 12% to 15%
items.quote: Our guidance for growth towards medium-term growth of 12% to 15%, we believe that our direct channel will continue to grow close to 15%.

items.statement: Double-digit revenue growth expected in near term with visibility for Q2
items.quote: Based on the business we have seen in the initial days of Q2, the outlook remains encouraging, and we are likely to see double-digit growth, which is higher than the growth we have seen earlier in the last one year.

items.statement: Annual capex run rate of around Rs. 100 crores, asset-light model with franchisee expansion
items.quote: If you look at last year, our capex was around Rs. 100-odd crores. We have a run rate today of around Rs. 25 crores of capex per quarter. And I do not see there is a material shift or change in that strategy of asset-light model.

items.statement: Plan to add nearly 1.5 lakh square feet net retail space in FY26, added 40,000 sq ft in Q1
items.quote: We are gunning for close to 1.5 lakh net addition this year. So, I do not think there is a big news or story there on closure. It's a regular closure, and we will continue to expand square foot very aggressively.

items.statement: Demand environment improving due to government stimulus, festive season onset, and better trading conditions
items.quote: Moving forward, we hope that the demand environment should improve on account of the government's efforts as well as the onset of the festive season.

items.statement: Direct channels (retail + online B2C) now nearly 60% of revenue; online B2C grew >30%, retail grew 15% with 8.1% like-to-like
items.quote: Our strong effort on growing direct channels of retail and online B2C has gained further pace in Q1. This group has now reached nearly 60% of AFL revenue.

items.statement: Adjacent categories (kids wear, innerwear, womenswear) grew >25% on average; footwear business recovering post-BIS, targeting Rs. 500 crores
items.quote: Kids wear, innerwear and womenswear have all grown impressively on an average by more than 25% in Q1. With BIS issue largely behind, inventory situation in footwear business has started to improve.

items.statement: Advertising spend increased 140 bps YoY in Q1; committed to aggressive marketing strategy for FY26
items.quote: We invested 140 basis points higher in Q1 in advertising on a year-on-year basis. And despite that, we saw 20% growth in EBITDA, resulting in a multifold increase in our PAT.

items.statement: Inventory freshness at all-time high; stock turns of 4; working capital tightly managed
items.quote: AFL has continued its focus on tight balance sheet control with stock turns of 4 and steady management of working capital. Our inventory has never been more fresh than it is currently.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs. 225 crores; operating cash flows to be used for debt repayment and growth reinvestment
items.quote: And now given that we have only Rs. 225 crores of net debt left, so would it be fair to assume that you will be a net cash Company by early FY27 in that case?

items.statement: ROCE crossed 20% mark; pre-IndAS EBITDA margin for footwear business target double-digit
items.quote: It is great to leave when the business is at such strong momentum and when the ROCE has crossed 20% mark.

items.statement: Wholesale channel grew 10% in Q1 driven by better inventory freshness, brand salience, and wedding season demand
items.quote: Wholesale channel, with all the efforts we have done have revived. Also, the season was good. We had weddings in April, May. All that also has impacted favorably. So we believe that inherent growth of wholesale will remain in high single digits.

items.statement: U.S. Polo Association grew >20% in Q1, now top 3 denim brand in department stores; gaining market share across channels
items.quote: At brand level, our intense investment into our marquee brand U.S. Polo Association is bearing fruit, and the brand has grown more than 20% in Q1.

items.statement: Board will objectively review Arrow and Flying Machine if they fail to meet ROCE thresholds; next three-year planning cycle underway
items.quote: If that reality fundamentally changes, then as a Board, we would be looking at it very objectively.

items.statement: Management targets ~20% organic revenue growth and ~23% EBITDA margin for FY2026 and medium term
items.quote: We are looking at an organic, sustainable, consistent growth pattern of about 20% on the revenues. Our goal in the medium term is to achieve about 23% EBITDA margin as we continue our margin expansion goals.

items.statement: Q1 FY2026 EBITDA margin expanded 239 bps YoY to 22.5%, marking 5th consecutive quarter of sequential margin expansion
items.quote: We achieved an EBITDA margin of 22.5%, representing a strong 239 basis point expansion over Q1 last year.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target of ~23% reiterated, driven by AI-led productivity gains across all functions and geographies
items.quote: We have already provided the medium-term goal of achieving around 23% EBITDA margin and we are clearly inching towards that on a q-o-q basis.

items.statement: India & Emerging Markets revenue grew 18.1% YoY to 72.3% of total; Developed Markets grew 23.3% YoY to 27.7%
items.quote: India & Global Emerging Markets together contributed 72.3% to our revenue and grew by 18.1% y -o-y. The market tailwinds remain intact affirming our positive outlook for continued growth momentum. Developed Markets registered 23.3% y -o-y growth and contributed 27.7% to

items.statement: CPCU rate increased to INR 58.0 for 107 million conversions; pricing inching up with volume growth
items.quote: Our CPCU business drove 107 million conversions at a CPCU rate of INR 58.0 and we earned CPCU revenue of INR 6,200 million, an increase of 19.8% y-o-y.

items.statement: Opticks AI fully integrated into unified consumer platform stack and rolled out to premium clients; 14th patent granted for ad fraud detection
items.quote: We have enhanced our platform capabilities with integration of Opticks AI into Affle's unified Consumer Platform Stack - a capability we showcased during our Investors Day in April 2025 and we have begun rolling it out to our premium clients.

items.statement: Management confident competitive moat in India is strong vs Trade Desk due to direct customer relationships (75% revenue), first-party data integrations, and CPCU model
items.quote: If you look at the Trade Desk reports, not just perhaps in India, but globally, their business is very agency led. I think about 80% of their business or more comes from ad agencies. So there is a difference there.

items.statement: ~75% of revenue from direct customers; Apple-certified partner status enhances credibility and trust with advertisers globally
items.quote: We are 1 of the 4 certified partners globally listed on Apple's website, and we all know that Apple is very careful on who they partner with, who they promote, who they kind of see as their partner.

items.statement: No material changes in collection risk; efficient working capital management maintained
items.quote: We continue to prioritize efficient working capital management and as such there were no material changes in the collection risk.

items.statement: No additional capital outlay expected for organic platform development in FY2026 vs last year; only inorganic acquisitions would increase capex
items.quote: We mentioned in our last call that we'll be not increasing our capital outlay on the platform development expenses until we have any inorganic acquisition. But for organic platforms, we don't expect additional outlay of budget as compared to last year.

items.statement: Actively evaluating 5-10 acquisition targets; disciplined approach with 20/20 rule (20% EBITDA, 20% revenue growth); no pressure to rush deals
items.quote: At any given time, we are evaluating anywhere between 5 to 10 companies which we watch for many years. We will still wait for the right time. We are not going to make an expensive acquisition.

items.statement: Equalization Levy benefit provided sustainable savings in Other Expenses; change is universal across market participants
items.quote: Some part of the savings is long-term due to benefit of Equalization Levy while certain discretionary expenses or savings might go up and down. But largely, we will be in line with what we have done in this quarter.

items.statement: Geopolitical headwinds (war, tariffs, airline disruptions) did not derail Q1 performance; business model shows resilience
items.quote: Even with these events we certainly did not factor in when we started this financial year or this quarter, we have still delivered the quarterly results that we are presenting to you today. It shows that we are extremely resilient.

items.statement: Mandate for every employee to adopt AI daily across all functions; leadership leading by example to drive authentic intelligence
items.quote: There is a clear mandate that every single employee in the company has to be upgraded in terms of the authentic intelligence, where there has to be a day-in & day-out adoption of AI across all functions and roles in the organization.

items.statement: Localized operating structure across regions insulates from direct tariff exposure and macroeconomic uncertainties; naturally hedged across markets
items.quote: Our localized operating structure across all regions will keep us insulated from direct exposure to ongoing tariff developments or broader macroeconomic uncertainties.

items.statement: Company has very little debt and significant cash; strong balance sheet supports acquisition capacity
items.quote: I think Affle is one of the only ones, which has very little debt, a significant amount of cash, a track record of doing acquisitions and is openly stating that I will do acquisitions.

items.statement: R&D (development expense) stable at ~INR 4 million per quarter; no significant increase expected
items.quote: Coming on to the question of R&D, we don't call it R&D expense, but rather we call it development expense. It is in line with the previous quarter. It's hovering around INR 4 million for this quarter also, and there is no significant increase expected.

items.statement: India's macroeconomic outlook remains strong supported by easing inflation, lower interest rates, healthy monsoon, and benign oil prices
items.quote: India's macroeconomic outlook remains strong, which is supported by easing inflation, which has resulted in a lower interest rate scenario, healthy monsoon, and benign oil prices.

items.statement: Transforming retail broking into full wealth management and financial planning practice leveraging networth, pan-India reach, customer base, technology and research
items.quote: We are trying and transforming our retail broking segment into a full wealth management and financial planning practice.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs.680 crores, up 19% QoQ and 6% YoY
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter consolidated was Rs.680 crores, up 19% quarter-on-quarter, up 6% year-on-year.

items.statement: Institutional and investment banking revenue virtually doubled QoQ
items.quote: Institutional and investment banking revenue virtually doubled from previous quarter, which is Q4 FY25 versus 1st Quarter of FY26.

items.statement: Retail brokerage increased 15% QoQ
items.quote: Retail brokerage also increased 15%.

items.statement: Distribution income decreased 24% QoQ due to insurance March effect spike in previous quarter
items.quote: Distribution income, which is financial product distribution income, has decreased 24% because of the insurance effect, which sees a spike in the last quarter of year because of March effect.

items.statement: Other income increased 73% QoQ to Rs.63 crores from mark-to-market gains on BSE shares
items.quote: Other income has increased 73%, Rs.63 crores in this quarter versus Rs.36 crores in the previous quarter. That is mainly due to mark-to-market on investments, especially the BSE shares which we have.

items.statement: Employee costs increased to Rs.176 crores from Rs.163 crores QoQ due to headcount increase and variable pay provisions
items.quote: Employee costs increased from Rs.163 crores to Rs.176 crores in the 1st Quarter of FY26, mainly because of increase in headcount and some provisions for variable pay.

items.statement: Fees and commission expenses increased 24% QoQ due to payouts
items.quote: Fees and commission income on expense side has increased 24% because of payouts.

items.statement: Admin expenses increased 7% QoQ to Rs.86 crores
items.quote: Admin expenses increased marginally by 7% from Rs.80 crores to Rs.86 crores.

items.statement: PAT increased 37% QoQ to Rs.176 crores
items.quote: As a result, PAT has increased 37% from Rs.128 crores in the previous quarter to Rs.176 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Institutional and investment banking income virtually flat YoY
items.quote: We have seen a virtual flat impact on institutional and banking income, which is virtually flat from Q1 of FY25 to Q1 of FY26.

items.statement: Retail brokerage declined 28% YoY due to regulatory changes reducing expiry dates from December 2024
items.quote: Retail brokerage has declined 28% and that is mainly because of regulatory changes that came into effect in December 2024 and that is primarily to do with the reduction in the number of expiry dates.

items.statement: FPD distribution income increased 37% YoY to Rs.145 crores due to increased focus on asset gathering
items.quote: FPD distribution income has increased 37% to Rs.145 crores in this quarter, basically because of increased focus on asset gathering.

items.statement: Other income increased dramatically YoY from Rs.4 crores to Rs.63 crores due to mark-to-market gains on BSE shares
items.quote: Other income has increased dramatically from virtually Rs.4 crores to Rs.63 crores, again because of mark-to-market gains in investment, especially BSE shares.

items.statement: Employee costs increased 36% YoY to Rs.176 crores due to headcount increase and wealth franchise build-out
items.quote: Employee costs have increased 36% from Rs.130 crores to Rs.176 crores, basically due to an increase in headcount and because of wealth build-up.

items.statement: Depreciation increased 38% YoY to Rs.16 crores due to technology and office investments
items.quote: Depreciation has increased 38% from Rs.12 crores to Rs.16 crores because of the increase in investments in technology as well as office.

items.statement: Fees and commission expenses increased 5% YoY to Rs.134 crores
items.quote: Fees and commission expenses have increased 5% from Rs.128 crores to Rs.134 crores.

items.statement: Admin expense flat YoY in Rs.83-86 crores range
items.quote: Admin expense is flat, virtually in the same Rs.83-86 crores range

items.statement: PAT fell 4% YoY to Rs.176 crores from Rs.182 crores
items.quote: as a result PAT has fallen 4% from Rs.182 crores in 1st Quarter to Rs.176 crores in the current quarter.

items.statement: Average daily turnover Rs.2,23,232 crores with derivatives Rs.2,20,263 crores and cash Rs.2,968 crores
items.quote: Average daily turnover was Rs.2,23,232 crores which was broken down into Rs.2,20,263 crores in derivative and cash was Rs.2,968 crores in this quarter

items.statement: F&O market share 0.62% and cash market share 2.57%, both broadly stable
items.quote: We are at an F&O market share of 0.62% which is broadly in the same range and for cash market share it is 2.57%, which was in the previous quarter 2.51% and again that is broadly hovering around the same range.

items.statement: Added about 50 RMs for wealth management, mix of HNI, ultra HNI and mass affluent with higher proportion of HNI/ultra HNI
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier also, we have broadly added about 50 RMs and they are a mix of both HNI, ultra HNI as well as mass afloat RMs.

items.statement: Plan to increase wealth RMs by 50-60% to 75-100 for full year FY26
items.quote: So, the 50 can go up to any number between 75, 100 in the full year.

items.statement: Wealth management targeting customers with 5-25 crore and >25 crore networth, differentiating from <1 crore base
items.quote: we have a large base of customers with less than 1 crore network and the segment which we are targeting will be say maybe in the 5 to 25, greater than 25 crores.

items.statement: Wealth management using open architecture model, distributing external MF/AIF/PMS while building own manufacturing practice
items.quote: we are also trying to build our own manufacturing practice and if you remember we have a small AIF and PMS business which we have recruited people to scale it up. So, we will be manufacturing also. But having said that, we believe that manufacturing is one of the products we have and as a house, genetically and generically speaking, we are more open for open architecture model.

items.statement: Non-institutional business cost-to-income ratio around 75% for FY26, elevated due to wealth build-out, benefits expected next year
items.quote: so basically we will, as we speak, I think the broad cost-to-income ratio for the retail or the non-institutional side will be in the range of 75% and I think this year it will be elevated and we hope to see benefits of scale trickling in next year.

items.statement: Wealth management revenue Rs.8 crores in Q1 FY26 vs Rs.40 crores full year FY25; cost Rs.70 crores full year FY25
items.quote: So, if you see, I will give you some broad estimates because last year we had a revenue of roughly about Rs.40 crores and cost was about Rs.70 crores. So, we had a hit of about Rs.30 crores and this quarter we have made revenues of about Rs.8 crores

items.statement: Investment banking and institutional equities income roughly Rs.200 crores with Rs.150 crores brokerage and Rs.50 crores banking
items.quote: we have roughly about Rs.200 crores of investment banking and institutional equities income and the rough numbers will be about Rs.150 crores is brokerage and Rs.50 crores is banking.

items.statement: Investment banking pipeline strong for full year FY26 though Q2 may see slowdown due to current volatility
items.quote: For the full year, I am quite optimistic about our deal pipeline and closure.

items.statement: Insurance premium collected Q1 FY26: life and non-life Rs.10 crores (vs Rs.23 crores Q4 FY25, Rs.14 crores Q1 FY25); general insurance ~Rs.30 crores; Livlong wellness business doing well
items.quote: total premium collected for this first year for Q1 was about Rs.10 crores, which for the previous quarter was Rs.23 crores and 1st Quarter of FY25 was Rs.14 crores. So, there has been some dip in this and for general insurance was also in the rough range of Rs.30 crores.

items.statement: No guidance given for FY26
items.quote: No, unfortunately, we have not given any guidance. I am sorry.

items.statement: Distribution AUM at Rs.35,700 crores as of Q1 FY26, focus area for growth
items.quote: So, we are roughly at about Rs.35,700 crores and that is the number which we are targeting to grow.

items.statement: Management maintains volume guidance of 550,000 CBM for FY26 and margin guidance despite Q1 challenges
items.quote: We are not changing anything on the guidance side in terms of volume or margins at this point of time.

items.statement: Domestic MDF demand growing at lower-to-mid double-digit CAGR but channel inventory overhang and peer pricing aggression impacted Q1 volumes
items.quote: On the domestic front, though demand continues to be robust, growing at a lower-to-mid double-digit CAGR, the recent bunching up of capacity additions led to price and credit aggression by peers to quickly gain relative market share, impacting volume growth.

items.statement: Discontinued 37,000 CBM commercial-grade MDF sales in Q1 due to BIS QCO compliance; excluding this, domestic sales grew 47% like-for-like
items.quote: While sequentially our domestic MDF volumes grew by ~2% versus Quarter 4 FY '25, there was a degrowth of ~8.5% versus Quarter 1 of last year, largely due to the discontinuation of 37,000 cubic meters of commercial-grade MDF sales post-implementation of BIS QCOs.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 47% in Q1, up ~2.5% sequentially due to 7% timber price decline; operating EBITDA 4% excluding forex impact
items.quote: Timber prices are on course correction already and were lower by 7% sequentially, leading to an improvement of ~2.5% on gross margins, consolidated gross margins being 47% for Quarter 1.

items.statement: No new capex planned for FY26 or FY27; plywood expansion only after 80% utilization of existing capacity
items.quote: No new CAPEX is planned.

items.statement: New thin panel plant in Andhra Pradesh stabilized, running at 33% utilization in Q1; target 30-35% for FY26; breakeven at 40% utilization
items.quote: I can share something for sure. And maybe Venkatji, please add whatever you wish to. See, I think the idea is to run this plant at least 30%-35% this year. In quarter one, we were running already at 33%, this capacity.

items.statement: Average scheme/discount of ~3% in July; schemes vary by product, geography and month; 6-8% price differential between industrial and commercial grade
items.quote: In July, I think on an average basis, I would say it could be somewhere around about 3-odd percent.

items.statement: BIS QCO implementation for MSME/small players from August 11-12; imports down ~90% in Q1; only 2 importers have BIS licenses so far
items.quote: And since BIS is applicable for MSME players also from August, assuming that implementation happens from that date, they will also not be able to produce the commercial grade.

items.statement: Export volumes flat sequentially but down 40% YoY; Euro/INR forex loss of Rs 27.6 crore on ECB borrowing (Rs 26.5 crore unrealized); export realizations up ~7% YoY
items.quote: the impact of adverse currency movement, the Euro/INR, the FOREX loss on Euro borrowings, which is the ECB, being Rs. 27.6 crores, and on CAPEX, there is another Rs. 2 crore.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 386 crore at June end (flat vs March despite repayments due to forex MTM); net debt Rs 233 crore; comfortable leverage and liquidity
items.quote: Our gross debt at June end was Rs. 386 crore, bulk of which is for the new plant at AP, which is almost at par with the March figures despite repayment of the scheduled tranches in Quarter 1 due to the unrealized FX loss on the Euro-denominated borrowings.

items.statement: Industry capacity 4.25 million CBM (organized 65-66%, unorganized 34-35%); FY25 domestic demand ~2.8 million CBM implying 60-65% utilization
items.quote: Of the total industry capacity, which we estimate at 4.25 million cubic meters, the organized share is 65%-66% and unorganized share is between 34%-35%.

items.statement: Forex volatility on Euro borrowing unhedged for long tenor; hedging only near-term tranches; Euro cooling post EU-US deal to 1.14
items.quote: To get a hedge in place for a full 10-year, A, the markets are not there. B, even if someone wants to sell it to us, it is going to be ultra expensive, even if there is something possible.

items.statement: New sales head joined 4 months ago; some zonal heads added and zones divided for better focus; no major restructuring
items.quote: We do have a new sales head in place who has joined us about 4 months ago. A few of the zonal heads have also been put in place and they have been added as well.

items.statement: Value-added share 50% of domestic volumes from older plants (same as Q4 FY25); new plant producing only industrial grade currently; value-added production from new plant expected from Q3
items.quote: the entire production and sales at the new plant comprised of the industrial grade. There were no value-added products in the new plant. So, if we remove that and look at the value-added contribution from the older plants, it was 50% of the total domestic volumes

items.statement: Peer pricing aggression to gain market share; commercial grade discontinuation was Greenpanel-specific; unorganized players face BIS compliance from August
items.quote: the recent bunching up of capacity additions led to price and credit aggression by peers to quickly gain relative market share, impacting volume growth.

items.statement: Rewarded 150+ top channel partners; strengthened in-shop branding across 2,000+ dealers; revamped loyalty app for partners and carpenters
items.quote: In Quarter 1, we rewarded our 150+ top-performing channel partners at Bali, Indonesia, reinforced our ambitions to scale up via our annual sales conference, re-strengthened our in-shop branding across 2,000+ dealers and sub-dealers

items.statement: EPCG income Rs 5.1 crore in Q1; MDF EBITDA margin below 3% excluding EPCG; plywood EBITDA margin 0.6%
items.quote: Yes, it was Rs. 5.1 crore for the quarter.

items.statement: FY26 double-digit constant currency growth with EBITDA margin 20-22%
items.quote: For the year, our effort is to deliver double-digit growth in constant currency while maintaining our EBITDA margins in the range of 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Three-year double-digit growth cycle through FY27
items.quote: We are confident that this momentum will help us deliver double-digit growth over a three-year cycle that began last year and will carry through FY '27.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 21.4%, up 12.9% sequentially
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, Happiest Minds has powered ahead, delivering 17.5% year-on-year growth in constant currency and maintaining a robust margin of 21.4%, firmly within our guided range.

items.statement: GenAI business unit broke even at operating margin level in Q1
items.quote: Generative AI Business Services has broken even at an operating margin level this quarter. This is a swing from a loss of about ₹ 2.53 crores in the previous quarter to a marginal profit of ₹ 24 lakhs this quarter.

items.statement: Adjusted operating margin 18.4-18.5% excluding GenAI and new sales engine investments
items.quote: Now if you adjust our operating margin for the above number and similar investments in our new sales engine, the number on profitability or operating margin we would guess is about 18.4% to 18.5%.

items.statement: Resilient demand in BFSI and Healthcare; early signs of renewal in TME and Manufacturing
items.quote: Demand remains resilient in key verticals such as BFSI and Healthcare, while Technology, Media and Entertainment and Manufacturing are beginning to show early signs of renewed investment.

items.statement: Robust growth in order book and pipeline across geographies and verticals
items.quote: However, we have observed robust growth across our order book and pipeline, spanning various geographies and industry verticals, which reflects positive momentum.

items.statement: $1M clients increased to 59 from 57; one new $10M+ and one new $3-5M client
items.quote: If you see the number of $1 million customers, has gone up. We have one additional $10 million-plus customer and one additional $3 million to $5 million customer. The $1 million customers have gone up from 57 to 59.

items.statement: Utilization at 78.9%, best in 9 quarters; GenAI unit utilization ~55-56%
items.quote: Utilization for the quarter stood at 78.9%. This has been the best in the last 9 quarters and reflects some of the steps taken towards improving efficiency in delivery and demand-aligned resourcing that we are resorting to.

items.statement: Headcount 6,523, net reduction of 109; gross additions ~150; attrition 18.2%
items.quote: We ended the quarter with 6,523 Happiest Minds, showing a reduction of 109, while gross additions were close to 150. Our attrition has trended upwards to 18.2% and efforts are on to manage this and bring this in line with previous quarters.

items.statement: DSO increased to 91 days; unbilled DSO up due to GAVS integration, expected to normalize
items.quote: Our DSO has slightly increased to 91 days, and we are trying to reign that in and bring it closer to a long-term average of between 85 to 88.

items.statement: Unbilled DSO increase due to GAVS billing system integration, not seasonality
items.quote: The DSO has gone up by about 3 days., It is because of the integration with GAVS, we are getting our billing and systems online with them. So that's part of the process and we should be back to normal.

items.statement: Automation revenue share rose from 25.3% to 28.2% driven by RPA, BPA, low-code/no-code and GenAI
items.quote: Low-code no-code is something that customers are looking at to enable citizen developers and to get applications out faster, and so all of these have contributed to the growth that you see of the revenue from automation from 25.3% to 28.2% in Q1.

items.statement: GenAI business unit grew 14.5% sequentially and 89.8% YoY; utilization improved 34.3% to 40.8%
items.quote: Our GenAI business unit led the way this quarter with 14.5% sequential and 89.8% year-on-year growth while showing significant traction with multiple pilots scaling into long-term engagements and utilization improving sharply from 34.3% to 40.8%.

items.statement: Active customers 285 (up 4); $1M clients 59 (up 2); repeat business 94%
items.quote: Active customers have grown from 281 to 285 and million $ customers have increased from 57 to 59, showing how we are deepening relationships and converting early engagements into multimillion-dollar partnerships. Repeat business remains strong at 94%.

items.statement: US revenue share deliberately reduced from ~75% to ~60% via acquisitions
items.quote: If you recall, a year or maybe 1.5 years back, our share of revenues from U.S. was around 75%, which was uncomfortably high, and through organic means and inorganic means, we've been able to diversify. So, it's a deliberate strategy to get the share of U.S. revenues to around 60%.

items.statement: APAC growth driven by PureSoftware BFSI account targeting $10M by year-end
items.quote: Out of those accounts in the BFSI space, one of them is a leading Banking and Financial Services company. We are doing most of our work with the units in APAC, and that's shown very good growth. We have solid relationships, good track record, and we expect this account to continue growing and get into the $10 million range by end of the year.

items.statement: Arttha banking platform revenue expected to grow 20-25% in FY26
items.quote: For this year, we are expecting the Arttha revenues to go up by 20% to 25%. So that will be one of the growth drivers.

items.statement: Healthcare product on track for potential launch by Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our revolutionary Healthcare product built on unmatched bioinformatics capabilities and collaboration with leading research institutions is progressing well too, with development on track for a potential launch by Q1 of FY '27.

items.statement: GenAI investment intensity remains high; opportunity cost ~₹3-3.5 crores/quarter
items.quote: The investment intensity is high. That's why I highlighted, even though we are at breakeven, if you look at the opportunity costs, it's about ₹3 crores, ₹3.5 crores.

items.statement: Wage hikes planned for Q2; impact being assessed, update next quarter
items.quote: On the compensation increases, I would not give you any specifics because work is in progress. Our typical cycles are in July every year for the C1 to C6 levels. There is limited discussion within the industry regarding this matter. While there are deferrals and general silence, we are assessing the situation very carefully. We plan to provide you with a more detailed update in our next call.

items.statement: $1B revenue target by FY31 under review due to changed market conditions
items.quote: As part of our vision, we had set ourselves a goal of being a $1 billion company by FY '31, and the market environment in which we had set that goal was a more conducive environment. There were several other goals that we have set as part of that vision on which we're progressing well. If you really look at our CAGR from FY '21 to FY '25, we've done a CAGR of 23.5%. And to get to $1 billion by FY

items.statement: No M&A likely to close currently; Q1 growth purely organic
items.quote: Our Q1 revenues is purely organic. We want to look at it because the base we have got no acquisition numbers going into the sequential growth number that I talked about. As of now, we don't have any M&A, which is likely to close. So, you can assume that that's the pace of the business that we are looking to grow organically for the year. But if there is some inorganic, it'll be on top of it is wha

items.statement: Growth ahead of industry peers reporting flat or subdued performance
items.quote: Friends, as you are aware, the global IT industry continues to face its own set of challenges with many peers reporting flat or subdued performance. Our 10 strategic transformation and focused investments have enabled us to navigate this environment with clarity and conviction, driving growth ahead of industry levels.

items.statement: Insurance-in-a-Box ensures compliance for insurers and UMAs
items.quote: In BFSI, our Insurance-in-a-Box is replacing fragmented systems with a unified low-code solution that streamlines insurance operations, accelerates product launches, lowers costs and ensures compliance.

items.statement: Benefit from foreign currency movements helped mitigate cost pressures
items.quote: Efficiency in our established businesses payback start from our new business segments of Generative AI and our new sales engine and some bit of luck or benefit from foreign currency movements will be definitely required to mitigate people cost increases that we'll see in the coming quarters.

items.statement: ROCE 23% and ROE 14% showing substantial improvement
items.quote: Capital return ratios of ROCE and ROE have shown substantial improvement to 23% and 14%, respectively.

items.statement: Management guided for ~45% steady-state EBITDA margin assuming asset growth continues
items.quote: And while we will, we are maintaining our guidance of saying that we will see around 45% of margin on a steady-state basis, there is a little upside in terms of the current quarter.

items.statement: Yield depletion guided at 3-3.5% annually going forward after large AMC repricing largely complete
items.quote: So, we should expect closer or lesser to that going forward in terms of yield depletion. However, because the first quarter has seen a sharper yield depletion than usual, on a year-on-year basis, you could see a 9% kind of a yield depletion.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue growth guided at 25% YoY for FY26
items.quote: So, we stick to that guidance that it will be a 25% growth in non-mutual fund on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Rearchitecture project total cost estimated at INR450-500 cr with similar spend in FY27
items.quote: So, you would expect overall the cost of the project is expected to be around INR450 crores to INR500 crores. So, you will end up spending around, by the end of this year, it will be around, cumulatively around INR125-plus crores. So, we expect a similar amount to be spent in the next year also.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 43.7% despite headwinds; expect to hit 45%+ in coming quarters
items.quote: Margins, again, given all these headwinds, the margin still was at 43.7 percentage, a little down on a quarter-on-quarter basis, year-on-year basis. But again, traditionally, the first quarter has been the, has seen the maximum strain on margins.

items.statement: Non-MF EBITDA margin at ~12% in Q1; MF margin at 45%+
items.quote: The non-MF profitability, we said it's always between 10 and 15 percentage. They were a little lower on this 12% probably in the current quarter. MF continues to be 45-plus percentage.

items.statement: Yield declined ~5% QoQ in Q1; 75% of decline attributed to large AMC repricing
items.quote: We have seen a close to 5% decline in yields. But going forward, as we have taken most of the impact in the base, we expect that barring telescoping, there is not going to be any significant depletion in yields going forward.

items.statement: Overall AuM crossed INR50 lakh cr (INR50 trillion) for first time; equity AuM surpassed INR25 lakh cr
items.quote: Very pleased to share with you that for the first time in history, we've crossed INR50 trillion or INR50 lakh crores of overall assets.

items.statement: 3 of 7 new AMCs now live including Jio BlackRock (INR18,000 cr NFO); 4 more to go live in 3-6 months
items.quote: The good news is that 3 of these are already live, including Jio BlackRock, which did its weight in NFO. This was not in the first quarter. theoretically, the numbers came in the second quarter, so you don't see them in the results.

items.statement: New SIP registrations grew 19% YoY to 1.12 cr; market share jumped 6 percentage points
items.quote: New SIP registrations year-on-year to about a crores and 12 lakhs. These increased 19%. Market share jumped up for new SIP registrations by 6 percentage points.

items.statement: Live SIPs grew 15% YoY; market share improved from 57% to 62%
items.quote: Live SIPs, these are SIPs which are live and which get the monthly collection, which basically adds to gross and net equity sales. That number grew 15% year-on-year and market share improved from 57% to 62%.

items.statement: Unique investor base crossed 41.5 million, grew 27% YoY vs industry 22%
items.quote: Unique investor base crossed the 41 million. So, it's about now at INR4.15 crores grew 27% year-on-year, faster than the industry, which grew 22%.

items.statement: Insurance policy count grew 41% YoY; LIC expected to go live Sep-Oct
items.quote: has seen policies grow by 41% year-on-year. And again, it has, this is straight revenue-bearing metric for the coming quarters

items.statement: Maintenance capex guided at INR60 cr for FY26; INR15 cr spent in Q1
items.quote: So that on a yearly basis, we project the current year capex to be around INR60 crores. We have spent around INR15 crores of it in the, so we're on target in the first quarter.

items.statement: Rearchitecture spend INR14 cr in Q1; expect ~INR100 cr in FY26 and similar in FY27
items.quote: We in Q1. And we expect in the course of the year, this will accelerate, and we will spend close to INR100 crores in the current year. The spend next year will be on similar lines.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR788 cr at quarter end; INR90 cr dividend paid in July
items.quote: We have ended the quarter with a very comfortable cash and cash equivalent of INR788 crores, out of which INR90 crores dividend was disbursed in the current month post the shareholder approval.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR11 per share
items.quote: and the Board was pleased to declare an interim dividend of INR11 per share.

items.statement: Market AuM grew 7% QoQ; equity AuM grew 24% YoY supporting future revenue growth
items.quote: the market has, in spite of choppy markets here and there, the market AuM has grown. It's grown over 7% on a quarter-on-quarter basis, which means from a foundational perspective, it all goes well for the future revenue growth.

items.statement: CAMSPay revenue grew 26% YoY but declined QoQ due to insurance seasonality and payment gateway delay
items.quote: CAMSPay, although from a quarter-on-quarter perspective, wasn't very strong, but 26% year-on-year growth. The payment gateway infrastructure for cards has become operational now.

items.statement: Top 5 AMCs consistently priced; next 6 also in similar band; pricing now tightly banded across clusters
items.quote: So if you see our spectrum of 22 clients, there is a lump of 5 at the top, which is consistently priced. There's a lump of ano ther 6, which is AMC #6 to 11 and which are also in the similar band

items.statement: KRA revenue split: 70% from AMCs, 30% from brokers/DPs; broker share trending up
items.quote: if you see from an AMC to brokers perspective, around 30% of the KYC revenue will be from the brokers and DP's perspective and 70% will be from AMC. And that is a metric that's been trending upwards over the last few quarters.

items.statement: No major repricing expected for next 18-24 months; only 1-2 customers up for renewal tail end FY27
items.quote: And for the next year, towards the tail end, there could be 1 or 2 customers who come in. But again, it's towards the tail end of next year. So you will, that's why when we kind of said to the earlier question that we do see some amount of stability for the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: India restaurant openings target 60-80 per year to reach ~800 by FY29
items.quote: There is no change in our guidance for restaurant openings. We will continue to add 60 to 80 restaurants every year to reach approximately 800 by FY '29.

items.statement: Gross profit margin target 70% by FY29, non-linear progression
items.quote: Our GP guidance is the same as we target a 70% margin by FY '29. Please note that we will not see a linear increase every quarter as we aim to strike the right b alance between sales growth and margin

items.statement: Demand environment similar to last few quarters, tighter market, strength on value layer, softness on premium layer
items.quote: Yes. I think, Pranay, we basically are seeing very similar trends. It's -- there is some limited demand and it's a tighter market than usually we see at this time of year. But the demand on the lower end of the menu at the value layer continues to be strong.

items.statement: India restaurant EBITDA margin improved 0.8% YoY to 9.7% led by utility and IT cost efficiencies
items.quote: Restaurant EBITDA margins improved by 0.8% year-over-year through these initiatives. Also, we have renegotiated a lot of contracts on the IT front. where our technological partners, we have rearranged our technology, the way we have consumed it.

items.statement: Indonesia Burger King store EBITDA turned positive INR 6.4 billion from loss of INR 8 billion four quarters ago
items.quote: And a store EBITDA level where we had lost around INR8 billion in quarter 2 last year or 4 quarters back, we've from there got to a positive store level EBITDA of INR6.4 billion.

items.statement: Indonesia Popeyes gross margin improved 2 percentage points but store loss continues ~INR 6 billion per quarter
items.quote: Gross margin is a journey that is similar to BK. We've improved it by 2 percentage points on gross profits. But because of lower ADS, our loss in Popeyes still continues to be in the region of around INR6 billion for the quarter.

items.statement: India net 63 restaurants added in last year, 6 net in Q1; Indonesia rationalized 4 more Burger King stores, total 159
items.quote: As far as the store count is concerned, Raj mentioned that we added 63 restaurants in a span of over the last 1 year, which translates to 6 more restaurants during the quarter.

items.statement: Several sites already in construction, pace of restaurant openings to increase in subsequent quarters
items.quote: While we have added a net 6 restaurants this quarter, you will see the pace of growth increasing in subsequent quarters as we have several sites already in construction.

items.statement: 93% of India restaurants have self-ordering kiosks, 100% have table ordering and app ordering, 95% sales digital
items.quote: Today, very happy to report to you that 93% of our restaurants have self-ordering kiosks. That's 93%. And that was done in a little over 2 years. We have installed SOKs, trained people, got everyone on speed on our SOKs.

items.statement: Barbell strategy: value 2-for-79/99 and INR 99 cafe promo; premium Kings Collection 2.0 at INR 200 and Korean LTO; middle layer Whopper Deluxe range INR 139-199 launched
items.quote: So this is a barbell strategy. And as we move forward, we'll continue strengthening both these pillars, but also build a very strong middle layer, which we will talk to you about on the next quarter after we have done some work on it.

items.statement: BK app installs up ~50% QoQ, orders up ~60% QoQ; 80-90 daily transactions per store on dine-in app from repeat customers
items.quote: We saw a lift in installs almost 50% quarter-on-quarter and also the orders on the app jumped up by almost 60% quarter-on-quarter. So that continues to be a strong pillar of building engagement with consumers and over time, building frequency and loyalty.

items.statement: Trade payables 30-35 days; supply chain benefit from vendor partnership growth not working capital reduction; cash deployment focused on growth and utility efficiency capex
items.quote: We are having approach, honestly, to our entire supply chain strategy where we kind of working through a 3PL partner from the perspective of holding off. So really speaking, it's not -- honestly speaking, the benefit on the supply chain side is not necessarily through the working capital management, but rather working closely with the vendors as we go deeper, as we kind of expand our portfolio.

items.statement: Surplus QIP funds invested, generating higher other income (finance income up from INR 7 cr to INR 27 cr); Ind AS 116 lease closure reversals also contributed
items.quote: The increase in finance-related income, other income is because of the surplus investments that we had on account of the raising of QIP, which is what has resulted into a higher other income.

items.statement: India store labor cost intentionally increased 0.5% to 11-11.1% for training on SOKs, new menu, cafe; expected to normalize to 9.5-10% as top line grows
items.quote: The labor line, we usually used to run about 10%, 10.5%. We have now intentionally taken that by 0.5% above to about 11%, 11. 1%. And that is on direction from our operations team.

items.statement: India SSSG 2.6%, ADS INR 120; Indonesia Burger King ADS grew 5% YoY Nov-Jul to INR 19.7B, avg +1M ADS over 9 months; Popeyes ADS fell 14.6 to 13.2
items.quote: Looking at SSSG, we've had -- we've been consistently to an extent, largely have been having positive SSSG trends. Those have been in the region of around 2.5% to 3.5%. This quarter as well, we've had a 2.6% SSSG positive growth with an overall portfolio average ADS of 120.

items.statement: Cafe ADS INR 13,000 portfolio average; mature cafes (first 200 stores) at ~INR 20-22K, newer at ~INR 6-7K; 10% cumulative sales improvement in older stores
items.quote: As far as Cafe is concerned, our ADS in Cafe stands at INR 13,000 for the overall portfolio. I also saw some of the earlier participants asking in terms of the trajectory of Cafe. The earlier portfolio, obviously, the growth in any kind of category that we add depends on how the longer the category remains in the store and as part of the portfolio.

items.statement: Gross profit maintained at 67.6% range despite inflation and value strategy; target 70% over 3-4 years
items.quote: As far as gross profit is concerned, we have maintained the gross profit trajectory in a tight range of 67.6% range or thereabouts through these last 5 quarters. We f eel happy about being at this because in spite of strong inflationary pressures, plus being focused to driving traffic through the value strategy, we've been able to kind of maintain the trajectory of gross profit in a tight

items.statement: Utility cost efficiency program rolling out city by city; full 12-month benefit per restaurant after implementation; IT contract renegotiations also saved costs
items.quote: Utilities, Sumit has been talking about utilities now for the last few calls, and that work continues. We can't do that work in 580 restaurants on 1 day. We started those with a handful of restaurants, then we climbed and did a city, went to the next city.

items.statement: Indonesia marketing investment restarted after new government took charge and ceasefire announcement in Oct 2024; consistent ADS growth since Nov 2024
items.quote: You all would be wondering that why did we start the chart from November there. It's honestly, the reason why we put it is because that was really when the new government kind of took charge in Indonesia, and that was -- that there was a symbolic announcement of ceasefire in October.

items.statement: Premium layer demand softness impacting SSSG; Popeyes Indonesia competitive fried chicken market requires scale investment; corporate overhead reduction target 35% (25% done, further 10% planned)
items.quote: It's on the premium layer where we have seen a little bit of a shrink or tighter, and that's reflective in our SSSG, which is only 2.6%. Yes, that is where we are seeing the market overall.

items.statement: Indonesia corporate overheads reduced 25% (INR 15 cr), targeting further 10% (INR 4.5-5 cr) for total 35% reduction
items.quote: As of today, we have reduced already 25% of the corporate overheads. That's about 15 crores. This reduction will continue as we are looking at this year to reduce that by a further 10%, which is another INR 4.5 crores.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,250 crore via first QIP, significantly increasing net worth and capital base
items.quote: First, we raised Rs. 1,250 crore through our first QIP, which has significantly increased our net worth and further strengthened our capital base.

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded to AA (Stable) by ICRA, India Ratings and CARE
items.quote: Also, our long-term credit rating was upgraded to AA (Stable) by ICRA, India Ratings and CARE.

items.statement: AUM grew 28.6% y-o-y and 6% q-o-q to Rs 13,479 crore
items.quote: AUM growth remained strong, growing at 28.6% y-o-y and 6% q-o-q to reach Rs. 13,479 crores.

items.statement: Disbursement guidance for FY26 maintained at Rs 5,600-5,800 crore
items.quote: Our disbursal guidance for FY26 remains in the range of Rs. 5,600-5,800

items.statement: Added 3 new physical branches, total 158 branches; added 75 employees, total 1,709; intend to add 6 branches in Q2
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 3 new physical branches, taking the total to 158 branches as of 30th June 2025. We added 75 employees during the quarter, taking the total employee strength to 1,709 as of June '25. We intend to add 6 new branches in Q2.

items.statement: 1+ DPD 5.4% (+90 bps q-o-q), 30+ DPD 3.5% (+50 bps q-o-q), Gross Stage 3 1.8% (+10 bps q-o-q); seasonal uptick more pronounced in Surat and Coimbatore-Tirupur; Surat turnaround seen in July
items.quote: Asset quality saw a seasonal uptick in 1+ DPD and 30+ DPD. However, we expect the numbers to normalize over the next two quarters. o 1 + DPD is at 5.4% (up by 90 bps on a q-o-q basis). o 30 + DPD is at 3.5% (up by 50 bps on a q-o-q basis). o Gross Stage3 is at 1.8% (up by 10 bps on a q-o-q basis). • The above seasonal uptick was more pronounced in two regions, Surat

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 30-40 bps for FY26
items.quote: Our credit cost is at 40 bps. We continue to maintain a credit cost guidance of 30 to 40 bps, ensuring disciplined risk management even as we scale.

items.statement: Co-lending disbursements up 87.5% y-o-y and 43.3% q-o-q to Rs 78 crore; co-lending book Rs 434 crore (3.2% of AUM); target 10% of disbursements
items.quote: Our disbursement on the co-lending increased by 87.5% y-o-y and 43.3% q-o-q to Rs. 78 crores for Q1, taking the co -lending book to Rs. 434 crores or 3.2% of the total AUM. Co-lending will continue to be an important part of our strategy to strengthen our ability to cater to higher ticket size segments. We aim to take co -lending contribution to 10% of disbursements

items.statement: LAP contribution to disbursements ~16-17%; 80%+ from individual housing loans; not worried about LAP portfolio stress
items.quote: Because the contribution of LAP to disbursement is only about 16% or 17 %, 80% plus is still coming from individual housing loans, which is why we are not worried about the LAP portfolio.

items.statement: Cost to income 34.2%, down 150 bps q-o-q; operating expenses to assets 2.7%, expected to remain range-bound 2.6-2.7%
items.quote: Cost to income at 34.2% in Q1 FY26, decreased 150 bps on a q-o-q basis. Operating expenses to assets was at 2.7% for the quarter, in line with our expectations. We expect this ratio to remain range bound within 2.6% - 2.7% as we focus on growth and expansion.

items.statement: Borrowing mix: 60% private/public banks, 16% NHB, 19% assignment/co-lending, balance NCBs/ECB/NBFC; direct assignment Rs 184 crore in Q1
items.quote: Our borrowing profile continues to be well diversified and cost effective, reflecting our prudent financial management. 60% of borrowings come from private and public banks, 16% from NHB, 19% from assignment and co-lending and balance from NCBs, ECB and NBFC. • During Q1, we executed direct assignment transaction worth Rs. 184 crores

items.statement: Confident of strong housing demand given policy rate cuts, government capex focus, rising disposable income and Housing for All
items.quote: With recent cuts in policy rates and the government's continued focus on CapEx growth, increasing disposable income and "Housing for All", we remain confident of a strong demand for housing and housing finance.

items.statement: Digital adoption: 78% approvals via account aggregator, >80% loans digitally fulfilled, 96% customers on mobile app, 88% service requests digital
items.quote: 78% of our approvals in Q1 were facilitated by the account aggregator framework. More than 80% of our loans are digitally fulfilled through agreements and E-NACH mandates. And 96% of our customers are registered on our mobile app with 88% of service requests now raised digitally.

items.statement: Green Homes certified units increased by 70 to 190 total; ESG ratings reaffirmed/improved by MorningStar Sustainalytics, SES, CRISIL
items.quote: During Q1, we got 70 additional Green Homes certified, taking the total to 190. Our efforts and dedication towards responsible and sustainable financing are evident from our ESG scores. During the quarter, MorningStar Sustainalytics has reaffirmed our "Low-risk" ESG rating. SES ESG Research has assigned a score of 80.8 in 2025 (vs. 78.9 in 2024). And CRISIL has assigned a score of 64 (up from 63)

items.statement: PMAY 2.0: 7 customers received first subsidy tranche, 7 more approved awaiting funds; expect traction to pick up
items.quote: I am happy to share that 7 customers have already received the first tranche of subsidy with another 7 approved and awaiting funds. We expect the scheme to pick-up traction with increasing customer awareness and streamlining of the process.

items.statement: Productivity benchmark ~Rs 3-3.5 crore disbursement per employee per year; slight dip in Q1 due to new joiner seasonality
items.quote: Largely we benchmark disbursement per employee of about Rs. 3-3.5 crores a year. We are in the same ballpark, except that one or two quarters when the employees join. Like Q4 and Q1 is when large number of employees join and the employee count goes up and the volume is also correspondingly lower.

items.statement: Under construction loans ~12-14% of AUM (pre-EMI mode); 87% fully disbursed
items.quote: Under construction on the AUM is generally around 12% to 14%. As you can see from the chart on Page No. 14 of the IR Deck, which shows the pre-EMI versus EMI. So, 13% is under construction, which is in pre-EMI mode, where the loan is fully not fully disbursed and 87% of the AUM is fully disbursed.

items.statement: No repricing on yield side yet; decision parked for mid-Q3 or early Q4; Q2 no changes planned
items.quote: Not yet. What we had discussed to date is that we will first want to see the cost of borrowing line go down and then take the call. So, we have parked that decision for either middle of Q3 or early Q4. Q2, we are not looking to make any changes.

items.statement: Industry disbursement drop in Q1 more substantial than HomeFirst's 2% drop; company better positioned vs peers
items.quote: If you look at overall industry, the industry drop is more substantial than us. We are much better off and we have already corrected that trend in May, June, and July.

items.statement: Guided 20% disbursement growth for full year with monthly run-rate reaching Rs 500 crore by Q4
items.quote: we are saying is that this quarter, we do about Rs. 1,350 crores. Then next quarter, we do about like Rs. 1,450 crores and then Rs. 1,550 crores

items.statement: Guided operating cost to total assets at 2.6%-2.7% for full year and 2.5% over three years
items.quote: What we are guiding is 2.6% - 2.7% for the full year, considering that we are still investing for growth.

items.statement: Guided insurance commission income at Rs 15-20 crore per quarter
items.quote: We had guided a few quarters back that the insurance commission will range between Rs. 15 - 20 crores a quarter.

items.statement: Aim to deliver 15% ROE in next five to six quarters and ROA closer to 4% from leverage benefit
items.quote: We aim to deliver 15% ROE in the next five to six quarters and then build from there. As far as ROA is concerned, we look to go closer to 4%.

items.statement: Expect cost of borrowing to decline 50-60 bps by March to around 8% or slightly lower
items.quote: Broadly, we would expect 50 - 60 bps transition by end of March.

items.statement: Expect spread to be maintained in 5%-5.25% broad range after cost of borrowing benefit
items.quote: We expect the spread to be maintained in the 5% - 5.25% broad range.

items.statement: Disbursement not slowing except April; May, June, July going as planned
items.quote: Otherwise, Ma y, June, July, are going as we have planned. So, we do not see it as a stress on disbursement or difficulty in disbursement

items.statement: Madhya Pradesh growing well on both ticket size and unit volumes; South markets also growing
items.quote: Madhya Pradesh is growing well. Ticket size is growing and number of units is also growing.

items.statement: Industry maintains 5% spread for ROE accretive affordable housing; cost of funds gap vs large NBFCs only 60-80 bps
items.quote: Broadly, the industry has reached the conclusion that this is a business that runs at a 5% spread.

items.statement: Active connectors at 3,600, slightly lower due to 2% lower disbursements
items.quote: Since the disbursal was 2% lower, this number is also slightly lower than last quarter.

items.statement: 1+ DPD uptick in April-June concentrated in Surat and Coimbatore-Tirupur; July shows substantial improvement in Surat
items.quote: Out of these five to six regions, there were two regions which were more pronounced, which is Surat and Coimbatore -Tirupur.

items.statement: Stage-2 assets among lowest in industry; not alarmed by slight movement on small base
items.quote: If you see, our Stage-2, it is one of the lowest in the industry. On that small number, there is some slight movement.

items.statement: Provision coverage at 22%; if 1+ DPD rolls back coverage returns to 25% without reversing provisions
items.quote: If the number rolls back, then the coverage comes back to 25% because we will unlikely reverse the provisions that we have taken.

items.statement: Cure rates: 80-85% resolution in 0-29 DPD bucket, 60-70% in 30-59 DPD bucket
items.quote: Basically, about 70% to 80% of the customers eventually get cured and about 20% then flows forward.

items.statement: Bounce rate ~15%; by 15th collect ~50% of bounces; by 20th only ~20% of initial bounces remain
items.quote: Typically, by the 15th, we collect 50% of that. So, 50 customers, we would collect by the 15th of the month.

items.statement: Ticket size Rs 5-25 lakh; below Rs 5 lakh unviable without 15-17% rates which company avoids
items.quote: We start at Rs. 5 lakhs. We do not even talk about less than Rs. 5 lakhs. Rs. 5 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs is how we define our segment.

items.statement: Connector relationships contracted with company, not RM; reallocated if RM exits
items.quote: Irrespective of the RM, connectors will keep giving business because they are linked to us. There is a contract signed with the company.
