items.quote: For the guidance, we continue to anticipate revenue growth in the late teens to around 20%. With three quarters still to go, we remain quite positive.

items.statement: Capex of INR 41.5 crores incurred in Q1 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, the company has invested approximately INR41.5 crores in the capital expenditure.

items.statement: Pune greenfield hospital capex expected around INR 80 lakhs per bed for 150 beds
items.quote: Based on our current understanding with them, the cost is expected to be well under INR 1 crore per bed. While we're still finalizing the exact numbers, I would expect it to be somewhere around INR 80 lakhs per bed.

items.statement: Rajahmundry 100-bed hospital completed, awaiting government permissions to commence operations
items.quote: Our regional hub hospital in Rajahmundry of 100 bed is completed and are waiting for the final permissions to commence operations from government.

items.statement: Bengaluru Electronic City 90-bed and Hennur 60-bed hospitals on track for Q2 FY26 operationalization
items.quote: In Bengaluru, the construction continues at this pace at Electronic City of 90 beds and the Hennur with 60 beds, both projects are on track to become operational by the end of the Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Coimbatore 130-bed hospital project work in progress
items.quote: At Coimbatore the project work for 130 beds hospital is in progress.

items.statement: Gurugram Sector 44 325-bed and Sector 56 125-bed projects exploration progressing well
items.quote: In the national capital region, the exploration work is progressing quite well at both sectors, Sector 44, which is for 325 beds, on Sector 56 for 125 beds capacity in Gurugram.

items.statement: Pune 150-bed asset-light greenfield hospital in advanced discussions, signing expected in couple of weeks, operations in 2.5 years
items.quote: We are in advanced discussions to finalize an asset-light build-to-suit greenfield hospital in Pune with 150 bed capacity.

items.statement: Warangal acquisition of 76% stake in Prashanthi Hospital (100 beds) completed, integrated from July 2
items.quote: During this quarter, we have achieved a significant milestone by entering Warangal, a Tri-City with a population of 1.1 million with a catchment area of 3 million through the acquisition of 76% majority stake in Prashanthi Hospital Warangal.

items.statement: ~350 beds to be added in FY26 including 250 beds from pipeline and 100 beds from Warangal acquisition
items.quote: So, between those 250 beds and an additional 100 from recent acquisition (Warangal), we're looking at roughly 350 beds getting added this year, not counting any further additions from possible acquisitions.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 29.4% in Q1 FY26, up ~1% YoY due to cost discipline
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the current quarter is 29.4%, which is an improvement of close to 1% from Q1 FY '25 due to effective cost discipline.

items.statement: Q1 seasonally softer for general pediatric outpatient and inpatient volumes, but strong momentum in new hospitals and advanced services
items.quote: Despite Q1 being a seasonally softer, especially in the general pediatric outpatient as well as inpatient volumes, we have delivered a steady financial performance. This growth was supported by strong momentum in the new hospitals and consistent demand for advanced services like pediatric specialty, multi-specialties and quaternary care.

items.statement: Outpatient volumes grew 6% YoY, inpatient and deliveries de-grew 1% and 2% respectively
items.quote: In terms of operational performance, outpatient volumes for the quarter witnessed a growth of 6%, while inpatient and the deliveries de-grew by 1% and 2%, respectively, when compared to corresponding period of last year.

items.statement: No price hikes in insurance or cash tariffs yet for FY26; revisions expected in Hyderabad, Bangalore, Chennai in next couple of months
items.quote: For this year, not yet. We are expecting these revisions to close — at least for Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Chennai — probably sometime in the next couple of months.

items.statement: ARPP increased ~3% YoY in Q1 FY26; long-term trajectory 6-7% growth
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, ARPP has increased by roughly 3%. As we've shared earlier, ARPP is on an upward trend — we've seen 6% to 7% growth over a period of time. We remain on that trajectory, though there could be fluctuations of a quarter or two.

items.statement: ARPOB increased 13% YoY in Q1 FY26 driven by surgical mix and lower ALOS
items.quote: There are two or three key contributors here: pediatric specialties, quaternary care, and pediatric surgeries — all of which reduce ALOS and enhance ARPOB. So, in the absence of the seasonal, lower-value business, these factors drove a 13% increase in ARPOB.

items.statement: ALOS stable at 2.6-2.8 days range
items.quote: Yes. We have a very stable ALOS of 2.6 to 2.8 days. I think in this range, it should be. The ALOS prediction is a very difficult job, Sumit.

items.statement: Overall occupancy rate 40.2% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The overall occupancy rate for the quarter was 40.2%.

items.statement: IVF revenue grew 50% YoY, on track for ~2,000 cycles by year-end, contributes ~3.2% of revenue
items.quote: Growth has been quite impressive. We are on track to perform around 2,000 cycles by the end of the year. Revenue has grown by 50% year-on-year, which is very encouraging.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 735 crores as of June 30, 2025; all planned capex to be funded through internal accruals without debt
items.quote: I am pleased to inform that our company balance sheet remains robust with net cash position of INR735 crores as of 30th June 2025 and will support our ongoing capital expenditure plan. Given our current cash and anticipated internal accruals in the coming years, we remain confident in our ability to complete all planned capital expenditures through internal accruals without any debt financing.

items.statement: Dividend credited to eligible shareholders on July 5, 2025 post AGM
items.quote: I am happy to share that we successfully concluded the AGM on 5th of July 2025 and the dividend to all the eligible shareholders has been credited on the same day.

items.statement: Doctor engagement model: retainer for first 2-3 years then transition to variable fee; Hyderabad mostly revenue-share, Bangalore significant portion, Chennai largely retainer
items.quote: For the first 2 to 3 years, they are usually on a retainer model. Once they start performing well, they transition to a variable fee structure. This is how we've been operating across all geographies.

items.statement: International business challenges persist due to tighter regulations in Bangladesh, Oman, Sudan; adapting strategies to focus on other countries
items.quote: While challenges continue to persist international business due to higher tighter regulations in markets like Bangladesh, Oman and Sudan, we're actively monitoring the situation, adapting to our strategies to focus on other countries.

items.statement: Pediatric seasonality showing 1-1.5 year low-incidence cycles every 5-6 years; disease profile evolving with reduced diarrhoea/respiratory infections due to better vaccines, hygiene, nutrition
items.quote: We do observe these stretches of 1 to 1.5 years that are relatively healthy — what we could call low-incidence seasons. Looking back over my 20 years of experience, we've seen this at least twice before. Typically, once every 5 to 6 years, there's a noticeable slump in pediatric admissions, which eventually corrects itself and picks up again.

items.statement: Delivery volumes muted across regions (2% YoY decline); possibly cyclical due to wedding patterns, socio-economic factors, job instability delaying family planning
items.quote: We've been closely looking at the data from multiple angles. Sometimes, delivery volumes are influenced by earlier wedding patterns, which can create cyclical trends — that could be one factor here.

items.statement: Treasury income higher due to MTM gains from debt fund positioning on interest rate decline; may not sustain
items.quote: The treasury income was slightly better because of the debt funds where we have taken the positioning of interest rates coming down, probably that got captured and you are seeing this MTM gain on that. But yes, going forward, I think that type of performance may not be there.

items.statement: Mature hospital revenue grew 2% YoY despite occupancy dip; tertiary/quaternary care strong, low-ticket pediatric walk-ins softer
items.quote: For mature hospitals, overall revenue grew by 2%. What came down was the seasonal, lower-value footfall — typically a large number of pediatric walk-ins, which were softer this quarter. However, our critical care segment remained strong and steady.

items.statement: Domestic sugar demand estimated at 28 million tons for season 2024-25
items.quote: Domestic demand during the season was estimated at 28 million ton and an export of about close to a million ton will result in the closing inventory of around 5 .4 million tons.

items.statement: FRP increased by Rs 15 per quintal to Rs 355 per quintal for 2025-26 season
items.quote: Looking ahead to the sugar season '25-26, the government announced an FRP adjustment of Rs. 15 per quintal, bringing the rate to Rs. 355 per quintal based on 10.25 recovery.

items.statement: Current UP sugar prices at Rs 4,050 per quintal, Maharashtra at Rs 3,900 per quintal
items.quote: The current sugar prices in UP are at about Rs. 4,050 per quintal and for the Maharashtra mills we are realizing around Rs. 3,900 a quintal.

items.statement: Expect gross sugar production of 34-35 million tons for 2025-26 season
items.quote: For the upcoming sugar season '25-26, we expect an increase in the gross sugar production to about 34 million tons-35 million tons.

items.statement: Global sugar production projected at 189.3 million tons for 2025-26, up 4.7% YoY
items.quote: Global sugar production is projected to reach around 189.3 million tons in the '25-26 season, up 4. 7% year-on-year, resulting in a surplus of about 41.2 million metric tons, the highest in eight years.

items.statement: Ethanol blending reached 18.8% average, peaked at 19.8% in May 2025
items.quote: The actual blending reached 572 crore liters during the seven-month period, resulting in an average blending rate of 18.8%. Monthly perfor mance peaked at 19.8% blending in May 2025, nearing the 20% target.

items.statement: Completed conversion of 100 KLPD molasses distillery at Asmoli to dual-feed facility in June 2025
items.quote: We have successfully completed the conversion of a 100 KLPD molasses-based distillery at Asmoli unit into a dual-feed facility capable of processing both molasses and grain-based feed stock. This conversion, completed in June 2025, provides enhanced operational flexibility and optimal capacity utilization throughout the year.

items.statement: Crushed 35.3 lakh metric tons cane in current season vs 37.93 lakh tons previous season
items.quote: During the current sugar season, DBO crushed 35.3 lakh metric tons of cane compared to 37.93 lakh tons of cane in the previous season.

items.statement: Gross sugar recovery 10.43% for season vs 11.46% last year; net recovery 9.55% vs 10.48%
items.quote: Our gross sugar recovery for the season stood at I 0.43% versus 11.46% last year. Net recovery declined to 9.55% down from 10.48%, reflecting a decrease of approximately 93 basis points.

items.statement: Diverted 3.37 lakh tons cane to juice-derived ethanol vs 0.58 lakh tons previous year
items.quote: We diverted 3.37 lakh tons of sugar cane to juice derived ethanol during the season, a significant rise from 0.58 lakh tons in the previous year, aligning with our ethanol blending strategy.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 cane crush 2.32 lakh metric tons vs 2.00 lakh metric tons Q1 FY25
items.quote: In QI FY'26, we crushed 2.32 lakh metric tons of sugar cane and increased from 2.00 lakh metric tons in QI FY'25.

items.statement: Sugar realizations improved 4.5% to Rs 40,835 per ton in Q1 FY26 from Rs 39,153 per ton
items.quote: Our sugar realizations saw an improvement of 4.5%, increasing from Rs. 39,153 a ton in QI FY'25 to Rs. 40,835 a ton in QI FY'26.

items.statement: Produced 21.67 million liters ethanol in Q1 FY26 vs 13.7 million liters Q1 FY25
items.quote: We produced 21.67 million liters of ethanol during QI FY'26 compared to 13.7 million liters in the same period last year.

items.statement: Ethanol sales 19.33 million liters in Q1 FY26 vs 10.21 million liters Q1 FY25, up 89%
items.quote: Total ethanol sales reached 19.33 million liters up from 10.21 million liters in QI FY'25. Of this, ethanol derived from B heavy molasses accounted for 15.51 million liters compared to 7.28 million liters in the previous year quarter, underscoring our alignment with the government's ethanol blending targets.

items.statement: Country liquor sales 11.24 lakh cases in Q1 FY26 vs 7.75 lakh cases Q1 FY25, up 45.16%
items.quote: Our country liquor segment has witnessed a significant growth, reaching 11.24 lakh cases in QI FY'26 as against 7.75 lakh cases in QI FY'25, reflecting an increase of45.16%.

items.statement: Expect better performance in Q3-Q4 as dual-feed distillery and cane development efforts come on stream
items.quote: Going forward, we do believe the cane development and pest management activities that we put into place more aggressively should help us reverse this trend. And as we mentioned, all our other sort of rationalization efforts with regards to ethanol, dual feed, all of them have now just about come on stream in June. So we hope this will continue to help give us better perfor mances especially in Q3-

items.statement: Cane crop looking healthy with better varietal replacement and pest management; no major red rot outbreak
items.quote: So, these are definitely early times. But what we can tell you is the cane crop is looking really healthy at this point of time, touchwood. We do not see any varietal changes, programs that have been put into place are also beginning to show results. The red rot containment also has been, we do not see any major red rot outbreak.

items.statement: Total distillery capacity 300 KLPD with 100 KLPD swing capacity for feedstock flexibility
items.quote: Our distillery, we have today our distillery capacity, which is about 300 DB® Dhampur Bio Organics Ltd. Dhampur Bio Organics Limited July 29, 2025 kiloliters per day. We have a swing capacity of 100 KLPD. So, we should be able to completely, depending on the feedstock that we use, we should be able to mix and match and

items.statement: BIS agreed on ethanol blending increase to E22, E25, E27, E30; timeframes not yet decided
items.quote: So, the government, there was a recent meeting where the BIS has agreed on an increase ofE20 to E22, E25, E27 and E30. But the exact timeframes are yet to be decided. BIS will be releasing the standards in due course of time.

items.statement: Grain ethanol margins lower under FCI surplus pricing; margins could be higher with current maize prices
items.quote: So, see, we have two principal feedstocks right now. One is FCAI-based surplus price which the government gives. The margins over there are considerably lesser. We have supplied a certain amount of quantity of that. And in the next tender also have to supply some quantities. With the current price of maize, I think the margins could be a little higher.

items.statement: No major capex planned; spend considerably lower than net depreciation
items.quote: So we have pretty much replacement CAPEX or negligible CAPEX. Our overall CAPEX spend will be considerably lower than our net depreciation. I don't think we will have any major CAPEX, we have not planned for any major CAPEXs.

items.statement: Repaid Rs 15 crore long-term loans in Q1 FY26; long-term debt Rs 304 crore as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: We have repaid long-term loans of Rs 15 crores during the quarter. Our long-term loans stood at Rs. 304 crores as on 30th June 2025.

items.statement: Working capital loan Rs 671 crore as of June 30, 2025; long-term debt-equity ratio 0.3x
items.quote: Our working capital loan as on 30th June was Rs. 671 crores. As of 30th June 2025, our Long ter m debt-equity ratio remains at 0.3x.

items.statement: Sugar inventory 1.52 lakh tons valued at Rs 37.39/kg vs 2.02 lakh tons at Rs 34.57/kg year ago
items.quote: Our inventory as on 30th June 2025 stood at 1.52 lakh tons of sugar which has been valued at 37.39 per kg as compared to 2.02 lakh tons of sugar as on 30th June 2024 which was valued at 34.57 per kg.

items.statement: Ethanol stock 6.41 million bulk liters vs 8.63 million bulk liters year ago
items.quote: Ethanol stock as on 30th June 2025 stood at 6.41 million bulk liters as compared to 8.63 million bulk liters as of 30th June 2024.

items.statement: Focus on country liquor segment; decided against IMFL/branded liquor opportunity
items.quote: Udit, we did study the opportunity oflooking into the IMFL or branded segment, but decided it wasn't for us. It seems to be a business which we were not seem to be well geared up for. So, we will be focusing on country liquor.

items.statement: Red rot and pest infestation in West Central UP reduced net recovery by 93 bps, increasing cost of production
items.quote: Our sugar recoveries have taken a beating in two of our factories. Overall, UP, the sugar recoveries have been down by about 0.7% to 0.8% in West Central UP. So the bulk of our cane comes from this region where the red rot infestation and the pest infestation was high which resulted in a lower net recovery which increased the overall cost of production.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guided at 35-37% for FY25 from H2, with opex at ~5% of average assets and credit cost at 1.2%
items.quote: So our belief is the cost to income should stay somewhere around 35% to 37% at least for this year. Subhanu Bangal: From H2? Srikanth Gopalakrishnan: From H2, that's right

items.statement: Loan book growth CAGR of 25% targeted for next 3 years, profit growth 15-18%, ROA ~7%, ROE 18-20% at 2x debt-equity
items.quote: So for now, I think given the situation that we are in, it's a little difficult for us to give you a very long-term guidance. But probably for the next 3 years, we intend to grow at a CAGR of 25% on the loan book.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance raised from 80-100 bps to 1.2% on average total assets due to macro issues and overleverage
items.quote: The only change that we have made is our guidance on the credit cost, which we used to talk about 80 to 100 basis points. We are pushing that number to about 1.2%.

items.statement: July collections in Andhra Pradesh better than April, Karnataka collections improved 2-3% vs April, business growth paused in Karnataka for 2-3 months
items.quote: As we see this month, we are quite 2%, 3% better than where we are in April month collections. So slowly, I think Karnataka is bouncing back in collections first.

items.statement: Legal recoveries from deep delinquent and written-off loans expected at INR 70-80 crore in FY25
items.quote: What I mentioned earlier on that good amount of recovery coming in, I was mentioning about legal recovery. That is you recover your money from the deep delinquent customers, 90-plus customers and written down customers, that will see close to INR70 crores to INR80 crores getting recovered in this financial year is what I mentioned.

items.statement: Quick mortality accounts increased to 150-160 this quarter from 75-100 previously, linked to overleverage stress
items.quote: So in percentage terms, that number will be extremely low. But in terms of the number of accounts, yes, there has been an inch up what used to be maybe 75 to 100 accounts has actually g one closer to 150, 160 accounts for this

items.statement: Disbursements flat despite higher officer and branch count, indicating tighter sourcing and higher credit rejections
items.quote: But despite that, if you look at the disbursements, it's more or less flat. That only shows you that even though the sourcing is -- volume is high, we are that much mo re choosy in terms of whom to give and whom not to give at this point of time

items.statement: Shifting away from INR 1-3 lakh segment to INR 5-10 lakh segment to reduce overleverage risk, moving ~5% of portfolio per year
items.quote: I will not say always, but at current period of time, the INR1 lakh to INR3 lakh segment is avoidable by Five-Star, and we are moving that whatever dip you see in that segment will be added in INR5 lakhs to INR10 lakhs segment.

items.statement: Loan officer attrition 17-18% quarterly (65-70% annualized), mostly from <1 year tenure, stable over last 3-4 quarters
items.quote: As we have said, especially if you look at the officer level, the business and collections, thi s number on a quarterly basis is anywhere around 17% to 18%, which means you're talking about 65% to 70% of attritions happening at the officers on an annualized basis

items.statement: CEO succession discussed at Board, but Lakshmipathy to remain in charge of operations for next 9 months, clarity by end of March
items.quote: Yes, the succession will be -- has been discussed in yesterday's Board, and we will take it to the Board at an appropriate level, appropriate time. But I can surely tell you that next 9 months, the focus in my mind will be only on the operational side, not on the succession side.

items.statement: Fortnightly credit bureau reporting now mandatory for all MFIs (last ~6 months), reducing overleverage risk window to 15 days
items.quote: There is a regulatory necessity for even MFIs to submit data on a fortnightly basis. So this has come in, if I remember right, maybe in the last about 6 months or so. So today, every institution has to submit data to the bureau on a fortnightly basis.

items.statement: Overleverage surprise in Q1 FY25 due to unsecured MFI/fintech lending, but MFIN guardrails and fintech wipeout give confidence no new overleverage will be created
items.quote: So it was a surprise for us, a bit of surprise. But also, I'm confident because finally, MFIN guardrails are put in place, personal loans and fintechs are wiped out. So this gives us confidence that no more overleverage will be created for a time being per iod at least to the customers of Five-Star

items.statement: LGD 15-20% on seasoned portfolios, primarily interest loss not principal; principal write-offs negligible, guided at 25-50 bps credit loss
items.quote: In seasoned portfolios, we typically see a loss given default of anywhere around 15% to 20%. But this is also not on account of the principal that the company loses because the loss given default computations also assumes the time value, which means the ac crued interest will also need to be taken into

items.statement: Tamil Nadu NPA sub-1.5%, Telangana NPA ~2%, both below company average; rest of country slightly worse due to legacy issues
items.quote: So Divyansh, on the data, if you ask Tamil Nadu and Telangana, like I think I mentioned earlier itself, they are doing much better than the company average. Tamil Nadu's NPA is sub-1.5%. And Telangana's NPA is at about a little over 2%.

items.statement: Housing finance launch planning active, not delayed by NPA or leadership transition, update expected next earnings call
items.quote: Nothing is getting delayed here. The planning is quite active. So let me give you some input in the next earnings call.

items.statement: DPD stabilization expected in Q1 FY25, improvement in D1C1 collection efficiency from December and March quarters due to growth denominator effect
items.quote: You will not see much of improvements in DPDs. But as we step into second half, December and March quarter, the growth kicks in. Growth also brings in a good am ount of current customers to the current bucket denominator effect. And you see the collection efficiency and D1C1 are going up in December and March quarter, you will see the improvements coming from December and March

items.statement: CIBIL checks done for all family co-applicants (3-4 per agreement) as Five-Star lends to family, not individual
items.quote: Of course, as Five-Star business model always we see -- we say that we lend to a family rather than to an individual. If you see Five -Star each agreement, you will at least see 3 to 4 co - applicants along with the applicant. So the entire earning family mem bers will be taken into agreement. And for the entire people, the CIBIL Highmark credit bureau checks will be done

items.statement: Unsecured MFI/fintech lending caused overleverage crisis; secured lenders like Five-Star will be prioritized as unsecured collections drop after 1 EMI miss
items.quote: So now the customers will realize and has to realize that he has to pay it promptly to the secured lenders. So now the time has come for him to differentiate between the unsecured and secured lenders, which he was clubbing for last few months.

items.statement: Targeting 2x debt-equity (3x leverage) over next 3 years to achieve 18-20% ROE
items.quote: And assume if you are able to get to a 2x, 2.5x kind of leverage, we should -- rather, I would say, debt equity, maybe a 2x debt equity, which means close to a 3x kind of a leverage, we should be looking at anywhere around 18% to 20% of ROE for the next 3-year horizon.

items.statement: NIM pressure from rate cuts last year, profit growth muted at 12-15% this year but will pick up over time
items.quote: This year may be a little muted because last year, we dropped our rates, so which is why we were guiding for a 12% to 15% for this year, but that number will pick up over time.

items.statement: AUM ended FY24 at ~INR 12,000 crore, targeting ~INR 15,000 crore in FY25 with 25% CAGR thereafter
items.quote: We ended with close to INR12,000 crores last year. So that means we'll probably be at about a little over INR15,000 crores for this year. And from there, we just have to bake in.

items.statement: Opex guidance unchanged at ~5% of average assets despite slower disbursements this quarter
items.quote: Other than that, the guidance that we gave on the opex, which will probably be about 5% -- at 5% levels, continues to hold good. No changes to our guidance on that.

items.statement: Credit bureau scrub available on demand but cost implications limit frequency to quarterly or half-yearly; increased during stress periods
items.quote: Rakesh, we can get it whenever we want because the credit bureaus today have a scrub that they can give us on -- any time we want. But generally, doing this, it has its cost implications also. So we do it at best once in quarter, but there are times when w e probably do it once in half a year

items.statement: No M&A discussed; focus on operational recovery and organic growth
items.quote: As I said in the opening remarks, this is one of the quarters that you see your company standard coming down a little bit on growth, collections and quality. This quarter will be a stabilization quarter and quarters to come, you'll see back -- get back the growth collections and resulting in good quality.

items.statement: Management reaffirms EBITDA growth guidance of more than 20% for FY26 despite Q1 shortfall
items.quote: But our internal target is obviously to achieve our annual targets. But since obviously, the first quarter has not been as per our planning, but we estimate that our growth would continue to be in the range of more than 20%.

items.statement: Management guides for consolidated EBITDA margin of 21% to 22% for FY26
items.quote: Generally, our margins -- our EBITDA margin should range anywhere between 21% to 22% on an annual basis.

items.statement: Long-term target to reach EBITDA margin of 25% over next 4 to 5 years
items.quote: Our long-term target is for the next 4 to 5 years to reach an EBITDA margin of 25%.

items.statement: Export demand dipped temporarily due to tariff uncertainty; domestic market grew over 30% in Q1
items.quote: The exports degrew in the last quarter. However, the domestic market grew by more than 30% in Q1.

items.statement: Order flows from export customers improving in June and July; expect normalization in Q2
items.quote: we have started to already see the order flow from our export customers become much better in the month of June and July and hopefully in the next few -- in the next few months as well.

items.statement: Received first order of INR 7.8 crores for liquid cooling solutions for data centers
items.quote: I'm also happy to share that we have received the first order of about INR7.8 crores for providing these cooling solutions to the data centers.

items.statement: Metal bellows revenue was INR 1.3 crores in Q1; expect 10-20% of revenue from new divisions in FY26
items.quote: Yes. So we had about approximately INR1.3 crores of business in the metal bellows. So we expect that over the next couple of years, at least 10% to 20% of our revenue should come from these businesses

items.statement: Ongoing capacity expansions at Hyd-Air Engineering and metal bellows plant; not yet at optimum utilization
items.quote: One is the ongoing expansion of operations at our subsidiary, Hyd-Air Engineering, which is currently in the scaling phase and also the metal bellows plant, which has not yet reached the optimum capacity utilization.

items.statement: Hoses and assemblies segment margins remain strong at 22-23%; consolidated margin dipped due to scaling subsidiaries
items.quote: From a margin perspective, our hoses and assemblies segment continued to deliver strong margins in the range of 22% to 23%, which is in line with the trends over the past few years.

items.statement: Metal bellows EBITDA margin at optimum utilization is 28-30% with gross margins of 50-60%
items.quote: In metal bellows, the EBITDA margin is around 28% to 30% at an optimum capacity utilization. Obviously, right now, the utilization is not at that capacity. Hence, you're not seeing that those margins in the numbers.

items.statement: Signed long-term agreement with US listed company (>$50B market cap) for liquid cooling solutions for data centers
items.quote: We are proud to announce that we have signed a long-term agreement with a listed U.S. corporation with a market capitalization of -- which has a market capitalization of over USD 50 billion. This agreement is for the supply of liquid cooling solutions for the data centers.

items.statement: Export customer mix: 30% OEMs, 5% distributors, 65% assemblers; Domestic mix: 75% direct to end customers, 25% distributors/assemblers
items.quote: is mostly equal where we have 30% of our business coming in from OEMs, around 5% of the business coming in from the distributors and the remaining from the assemblers. Rahul Kumar: Okay. And is that a similar mix for the domestic business also? Asad Daud: No. So, in the domestic business, about only -- so in the domestic business, only about 20% to 25% of the business comes in from

items.statement: Tariffs on products increased from ~3.5% to 10%; mostly borne by customers; no significant repricing needed yet
items.quote: the tariffs on our products increased by almost 3x. So it was earlier -- approximately about 3.5%, and it increased to 10%. So that was also a significant cost addition to our customers as well, right, where they had to bear an additional duty of 6.5% on the products.

items.statement: Even at 10% tariff, landed cost advantage vs US manufacturers remains significant; disadvantage only if tariffs reach 25-30%
items.quote: Not yet. I think tariffs of 10% doesn't -- because the difference between our cost landed and the U.S. cost is still much more th an 10%. So even if a 10% duty which is there right now, we are not at a disadvantage as compared to European -- sorry, as compared to the American manufacturers

items.statement: Domestic business has better inventory and working capital cycle; profit per unit of time better than exports
items.quote: So, in terms of our margins, yes, export exports have definitely better margins, but domestic has better inventory, better working capital cycle. So, profit per unit of time is better in domestic as compared to the international market.

items.statement: QIP planned only for value-accretive inorganic acquisitions; will proceed once acquisition terms finalized
items.quote: the whole idea for the company for the QIP works primarily for inorganic acquisitions. And to everyone that we will only purchase for the QIP once we have finalized the terms of the acquisition. So -- and any acquisition that we do will be value accretive for the shareholders.

items.statement: Tariff increases cause short-term demand disruption (2-3 months) but demand normalizes thereafter
items.quote: any increase in tariffs just have -- tends to have a short-term impact on the business. Like I mentioned, like the increase in the tariffs in Q1, impact in Q1, but we have already seen that from July, it's coming back to normalcy.

items.statement: Approximately 25-30% of Hyd-Air sales are for internal consumption by assemblies division

items.statement: Equipment fungible across sectors; buying fully loaded models to serve multiple industries
items.quote: Similarly, in the case of cranes or other equipment we buy, there is called a fully loaded model, which is the topmost model of that machine. And we usually are buying the fully loaded models of these machines because we want to use them across sectors rather than them being sector -specific.

items.statement: Depreciation expected to stabilize at INR48-50 crores annually for FY26; further changes depend on next year's capex
items.quote: So this should stabilize on a yearly basis at around INR48 crores to INR50-odd crores of depreciation that we see.

items.statement: Capex deployment timeline ~1 month from order to revenue generation
items.quote: And ideally, within 1 month is the timeline, the highest period that we see the revenue coming in from the capex that we have deployed.

items.statement: Warehousing & transportation revenue INR29.5 crores in Q1, up 82% YoY due to low base from labor standoff in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The warehousing and transportation segment registered an 82% year-on-year growth with a revenue of INR29.50 crores.

items.statement: Power & fuel cost increase driven by 82% revenue growth in warehousing segment; repair & maintenance up due to specialized service contracts and older equipment mix
items.quote: So power and fuel primarily is -- has gone up because of the higher revenue in that segment because power and fuel is in our scope as per our contracts.

items.statement: Not an MSME; does not qualify under government criteria
items.quote: No, we are not an MSME, sir, because we do not qualify in the criteria as laid down by the government.

items.statement: Specialized service contracts require specialized manpower deployment alongside equipment
items.quote: We are focusing on services which require the equipment and the specialized manpower along with it that we are able to deploy.

items.statement: Targeting 30% value-added share in Polyester Films by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our target is that by the exit quarter, which is the last quarter of this financial year, we should be in and around 30% share.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers targeting 20-25% YoY growth for next 3-4 years
items.quote: So let's say, we have been projecting 20% to 25% growth. So we would stick to that kind of growth numbers in this business.

items.statement: Ester Filmtech expected to achieve sustained PAT positivity in a couple of quarters
items.quote: And we believe that in next couple of quarters, we should be in a position where we can start giving sustained positive PAT.

items.statement: rPET capacity of 20,000 tons per annum in Hyderabad expected to start commercial production by September 2025
items.quote: We are pleased to report that the project for installing additional capacity of 20,000 tons per annum in Hyderabad is progressing as per schedule and commencement of commercial production is expected by September 2025.

items.statement: Investing INR 50 crores in recycling extruder for Hyderabad plant
items.quote: And that we are also investing INR 50 crores in the new machine, the recycling extruder.

items.statement: Loop JV land acquisition expected in 4-6 months, commercial production targeted by Q4 CY27
items.quote: We are targeting commencement of commercial production by quarter 4 of calendar '27.

items.statement: Polyester Films capacity utilization improved to 82% in Q1 FY26 from 64% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the capacity utilization improved to 82% as compared to 64% during Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Ester Filmtech capacity utilization improved to 72% in Q1 FY26 from 49% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Capacity utilization stood at 72% as compared to 49% in Q1 FY '25, highlighting operational ramp-up and improved production efficiency.

items.statement: Hyderabad plant targeting 80-85% capacity utilization soon, comparable to Khatima
items.quote: And very soon, we should be in the range of 80% to 85% capacity utilization, which will be then comparable to the Khatima capacity utilization.

items.statement: Indian BOPET capacity 1.35 million tons, domestic demand 850-900k tons, exports ~250k tons, surplus ~200-250k tons
items.quote: So right now, the capacity is in the range of 1.35 million tons per annum. And the domestic demand is in the range of 850,000 to 900,000 tons per annum. And India also exports close to 250,000 per year.

items.statement: Indian BOPET demand growing at 9-10% YoY, adding 80-85k tons annually
items.quote: And the growth in BOPET segment is likely to be nearing double-digit number of 10% year-on-year, which means that the domestic industry itself is - I mean, the domestic demand itself is going to grow almost, let's say, 80 kt, 80,000 to 85,000 tons per year

items.statement: Recycled PET revenue surged from INR 0.5 crore to INR 14 crores YoY driven by volume expansion
items.quote: Our standout performance this quarter has been the remarkable increase in the recycled PET revenue, which surged from just INR 0.5 crores in quarter 1 FY '25 to INR 14 crores during the quarter under review, driven by the significant volume expansion.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 8.35% in Q1 FY26, up 240 bps YoY; would have been 11.8% excluding forex/MTM losses
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, during the quarter under review, revenue grew by a healthy 19% and EBITDA margin improved by 240 bps on a year-on-year basis. The actual EBITDA earned stood at 8.35%. EBITDA margin would have been 11.8%, but for the adverse impact of the exchange fluctuation and MTM losses on FCL or derivative availed by Ester Filmtech.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded 427 bps to 11.21% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 31.94 crores, making an impressive 88.77% increase over Q1 FY '25 with the EBITDA margin expanding by 427 basis points to 11.21%.

items.statement: Commodity film spreads stable at INR 27-28 per kg in Q1 FY26 and currently
items.quote: So previous quarter, it was in the range of , if you take the average, it was in the range of INR 27, INR 28, and this quarter, we expect it on an average to remain in the similar range.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers EBIT margin normalized to 30-35% from exceptionally favorable 43% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Quarter ended June 2024 had an exceptionally favorable product mix that resulted in EBIT margin of 43%. Quarter ended June 2025 is more aligned to usual product mix and EBIT margin of 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Value-added products share in Polyester Films volume increased to 24% in Q1 FY26 from 23% in FY25, VAS volume grew 37% YoY
items.quote: Concerted efforts enabled us to enhance share of value-added products to 24% in total segmental volume. The upward trajectory is clearly evident from the growth of 37% in volume of VAS products achieved on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Specialty Polymers 85-88% revenue from two products (IQ PBT and MB03), new products being promoted with 9-12 month maturity
items.quote: So right now, I think IQ PBT, we are seeing a very strong demand this year. And we expect that with the certain innovations, which are in the pipeline in this product, we expect to see a continued trend of increased demand for this product year-on-year. Now coming to the second product, which is MB03, again, over here, we are in a very good position in terms of our placement in the market.

items.statement: Exports contribute ~35% of revenue, presence in 50+ countries across all continents
items.quote: Close to 35% has come from the exports because -- especially polymer is majorly exported and then certain sizable portion of polyester film is also exported. So close to 35% of our revenue for the quarter has come from the exports.

items.statement: US revenue exposure ~10% of total, specialty products allow full tariff pass-through
items.quote: Also, our revenue exposure to U.S. is about 10% of our total revenue. So we are exposed, but it is a limited exposure for us. And also, what we sell into U.S. are all specialty films products or specialty polymers, where we have a very strong price resilience.

items.statement: Global BOPET capacity additions slowing, Chinese order cancellations seen, Indian operating rates at 80%
items.quote: And in fact, we are seeing that there has been some cancellations on the orders which were already placed. So there is a complete reversal of the trend of capacity addition globally.

items.statement: PWMR rules effective April 2025 enhancing demand for BOPET films with PCR content
items.quote: Implementation of PWMR rules with effect from 1st April 2025 has started to enhance demand for differentiated offering of BOPET films with varied PCR content levels.

items.statement: Evaluating trade remedies to restrict low-priced imports, positive development expected in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We are in the process of evaluating the various trade measures and trade remedies that are available to the domestic industry, and once we have evaluated and explored those remedies, there is a possibility that we would be able to restrict the import at cheaper rates.

items.statement: Sales dollar-denominated (including domestic), INR/USD and INR/EUR expected range-bound till December
items.quote: Our entire sales is dollar-denominated. Even the domestic sale is dollar-denominated because it is mainly marked to the import landed prices. So that way we expect that we should be able to address these foreign exchange fluctuations in a large way.

items.statement: Regular term loan repayments, confident of schedule; finance cost absolute may not drop but will decline as % of turnover
items.quote: Both Ester Industries and Ester Filmtech have been absolutely regular with repayment of term loans as per schedule. Basis the budgeted improvement in profitability, coupled with free cash and bank balance in hand, we are absolutely confident of adhering to the repayment schedule.

items.statement: Euro loan interest arbitrage 1.5-2.5% vs domestic, hedging next 2 instalments (12 months)
items.quote: As a strategy, a foreign currency loan definitely is an arbitrage compared to an Indian loan. The arbitrage can vary from 1.5% to maybe 2.5%, depending upon the commercial understanding.

items.statement: Adequate working capital limits for budgeted enhanced operations at both companies
items.quote: On the working capital front, both the companies have adequate limits to sustain budgeted enhanced operations.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty (25% vs potential 15-20%), 5-6% relative disadvantage vs Asian peers at 19-20%
items.quote: So right now, it's 25%, but then there is also a talk of a 10% penalty. In fact, the penalty is not at all clear, though some reports at 10%, we are not very clear.

items.statement: Low-priced imports limiting margin upside, pursuing government trade remedies
items.quote: One of the challenges which we have been seeing is the imports, which have been coming at quite low rates from the overseas geographies. Those are something that are limiting the upside on the margins.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 6.4 billion as of 30 June 2025 with a pipeline of INR 46 billion for the remaining year
items.quote: As of 30 th June 2025, our order book stands at approximately INR 6.4 billion, providing considerable revenue visibility for the quarters ahead and we have a strong order book pipeline for the remaining year at INR 46 billion.

items.statement: Order pipeline exceeds INR 40,000 crores with significant inquiry activity for value services of INR 9,000-10,000 crores
items.quote: The number is north, so bigger than INR 40,000 crores. So, there is a very big pipeline at this moment.

items.statement: Gross margin and EBITDA margin improved year-on-year in Q2 CY2025; EBITDA doubled to INR 39 million
items.quote: Our EBITDA for Q2 2025 stands at INR 39 million, two times higher than the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Noticeable improvement in gross margin during H1 2025 vs H1 2024 driven by revamps and services business
items.quote: There has been a noticeable improvement in the gross margin during the first half of 2025 compared to the first half of 2024.

items.statement: Expanding Taloja manufacturing facility and setting up Rolls Coating line; facility expected operational by end of December or early January
items.quote: We are investing in the expansion of our Taloja manufacturing facility to increase capacity and better serve our customers' evolving needs. We are setting up the Rolls Coating line at Taloja as well.

items.statement: Rolls Coating facility at Taloja in final negotiation stages for machinery purchase; first orders in hand for refurbishment
items.quote: And the idea is to be operating, let's say, by end of December, early January. So towards the end of the year, we are confident that we will be able to process the first rolls for which we already have first orders in hand from Indian customers for refurbishment.

items.statement: Taloja plant expansion underway to increase manufacturing capacity and support new technologies JVD and Volteron
items.quote: We are investing in the expansion of our Taloja manufacturing facility to increase capacity and better serve our customers' evolving needs.

items.statement: Steady month-on-month improvement in business environment; noticeable uptick in customer inquiries and confidence returning to sector
items.quote: Over the past couple of quarters, we've seen steady month-on-month improvement in the business environment. The early signs of stabilization we observed last quarter have only strengthened further this quarter.

items.statement: Customers committed to long-term expansion roadmaps aligned with India's 300 million ton steel capacity target by 2030
items.quote: More importantly, our customers remain committed to their long-term expansion roadmaps, which are aligned with the Government of India's ambitious vision to achieve 300 million metric tons of steelmaking capacity by 2030.

items.statement: Revamps, spares and services business now 20-25% of order book, targeting 30-35%; growing quarter-by-quarter with shorter cycle times
items.quote: So, right now, we are already well advanced into seeing value services 20%-25% of the overall order book. And I think this is also a percentage that we like to continue to see, if not growing up to maybe 30%-35% if possible.

items.statement: JVD technology commercialized with over 1 million tons coated steel at ArcelorMittal Belgium; first JVD order in India possible this year
items.quote: We have already successfully commercialized JVD with over 1 million tons of coated steel produced at ArcelorMittal's facility in Belgium.

items.statement: Volteron zero-emission iron electrolysis technology; first 40,000 ton pre-industrial plant expected 2026; full industrial scale 800,000 tons/year
items.quote: So the development of Volteron has been accelerated in the last 12 to 18 months. And we have started a new pilot plant in France five months ago, who is giving extremely good results in helping us to define the opex.

items.statement: Major Indian steelmakers (Jindal, JSW, Tata, ArcelorMittal) all have share in order book; recent commissioning at Tata Kalinganagar and AMNS Gujarat
items.quote: So, there were two lines of CAL or a continuous annealing line and a continuous galvanizing line in Tata Steel in Kalinganagar and a CGL or galvanizing line for automotive in AMNS India in Gujarat.

items.statement: MOU with SAIL for decarbonization and high-quality product development; deep-dive discussions ongoing, details confidential
items.quote: So at this point of time, we will not disclose too much into detail the content of the MOU, which is highly confidential. And we are pursuing deep dive discussion with SAIL currently on putting in place different partnerships with them.

items.statement: Market share very high for high-end automotive galvanizing lines; lower for construction-grade; ramping up share in cold rolling mills
items.quote: All the last year's additions that are coming to the market now are of high-end galvanizing lines for automotive are from John Cockerill. So our market share for this sub-segment is actually very, very high.

items.statement: Global downstream steel engineering addressable market EUR 3 billion; JCIL market share 8-10%
items.quote: The addressable market for downstream products, which is basically the scope of supply of John Cockerill India, is EUR 3 billion. So we have currently a market share roundabout of between 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Significant improvement in cash flow driven by collecting outstanding receivables and better inventory rotation
items.quote: Our efforts on collecting of outstanding receivables and better inventory rotation have driven a significant improvement in our cash flow.

items.statement: Cash improved 23% quarter-on-quarter; Q2 profit INR 17 million; H1 net profit positive INR 5.9 million; losses narrowed over last three quarters
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter, we’ve recorded a 23% improvement in cash, culminating in a Q2 profit of INR 17 million. For H1, we are net profit positive at INR 5.9 million, su pported by the strong

items.statement: Managing Director Michael Kotas retiring effective 31 July 2025; Frederic Martin incoming MD
items.quote: I would like to take a moment to extend our sincere gratitude to Michael Kotas, who will be retiring from his role as Managing Director of JCIL effective 31 st July 2025.

items.statement: India installed steel capacity crossed 200 million tons in 2025; 30% flat products implies 30 million tons addition in cold-rolled/coated by 2030
items.quote: But today the installed capacity in 2025 has cro ssed 200 million tons al ready. The demand is less because the steel makers were operating at 75%, 80% capacity utilization. But let's say 200 million tons installed was confirmed by the Ministry of Steel

items.statement: Rule of thumb: US$ 500-600 million capex per 1 million tons downstream capacity addition in India
items.quote: If you say US$ 500 million to US$ 600 million to produce or to cr eate one extra 1 million tons of capacity in downstream is a fairly reasonable approach

items.statement: No future guidance provided per internal policy; order conversion depends on client board approvals for final investment decisions
items.quote: We also do not provide any future guidance.

items.statement: Government of India targeting 300 million ton steel capacity by 2030 with phased roadmap for carbon emission reduction and green hydrogen adoption
items.quote: The Indian government has reaffirmed its ambitious target of achieving a steel production capacity of 300 million metric tons annually by 2030, which will necessitate substantial investments from steel producers.

items.statement: Export orders completed; execution currently focused largely on Indian customers
items.quote: All export orders that we have been working on, there were a few are at this moment completed. So right now, execution is focused to a large part for Indian customers.

items.statement: Partnership with Belgium-based Advanced Coating for thermal spray coating technology at Taloja Rolls Coating facility
items.quote: We have partnered with Belgium-based entity 'Advanced Coatings', wherein JCIL will be able to leverage advanced coatings technology in thermal spray coating to cater the wide installed base of annealing and galvanizing lines in India.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated PAT guidance of INR1,300-1,500 crores reiterated; on track after Q1 INR276 crores
items.quote: For this year, to reiterate, we have guided, specifically on profits, which is INR1,300 crores to INR1,500 crores of PAT at the full year level. And with roughly INR280 crores in the first quarter, I think we are well on track.

items.statement: Medium-term ROA target of ~3% for Growth business; currently at 1.4-1.5%
items.quote: So at 1.5%, we have guided that in the medium term, that needs to get to 3%, right, or close to 3%. That's kind of where we believe our business model can lead us, somewhere around 3% ROA.

items.statement: Medium-term opex to AUM target of 3.5-4% for retail business; currently at 4.2%
items.quote: We aim to continue the strength in line with our medium-term guidance of 3.5% to 4%.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM grew 22% YoY to ~INR85,700 crores; Retail AUM grew 37% YoY to 80% of total
items.quote: Consolidated AUM grew by 22% to ~INR85,700 crores. This compares with a growth of 17% year-on-year in quarter 4 of FY '25 and 10% year-on-year in the quarter 1 of FY '25. Retail AUM grew by 37% year-on-year and forms 80% of our total AUM.

items.statement: Growth AUM (retail + wholesale 2.0) grew 38% YoY to INR79,430 crores; now 93% of total AUM
items.quote: Growth AUM grew by 38% Y-o-Y to INR79,430 crores.

items.statement: Wholesale 2.0 AUM grew 14% QoQ to INR10,425 crores; disbursements up 35% QoQ to INR2,302 crores
items.quote: In the first quarter of FY '26, our AUM for the new business, our 2.0 version of our business, grew by 14% quarter-on-quarter to INR10,425 crores. We disbursed INR2,302 crores during the quarter across real estate and CMML segments. This was an increase of 35% quarter-on-quarter in disbursements.

items.statement: Retail yield broadly stable at ~13.3%; fee income normalizing after processing fee amortization change
items.quote: Slide 20 shows the yield on the retail business, which has been broadly stable at around 13.3%.

items.statement: Growth business credit cost declined to 1.4% from 1.8% in Q4 FY25; aided by INR105 cr ECL rebalancing gain
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, the reported Growth business credit cost was at 1.4% versus 1.8% in Q4 FY '25. Last quarter Q4 FY '25, credit costs included a negative impact of about INR45 crores due to ECL rebalancing mainly in the microfinance business. In quarter 1 FY '26, ECL rebalancing for the overall portfolio had a positive impact of about INR105 crores.

items.statement: Retail 90+ DPD stable at 0.8%; secured products stable; salaried unsecured improved; MSME unsecured and used car finance deteriorated
items.quote: 90-plus days past due in retail was at 0.8% in the very narrow range that we have consistently maintained over the last 3 years. Risk in this quarter was seen at levels comparable to the second quarter of last year.

items.statement: Used car finance (5% of AUM) showed unseasonal uptick in refinance segment, particularly self-employed; needs close monitoring
items.quote: Used cars, which is 5% of total AUM, also showed a slightly unusual uptick, which is unseasonal for the first quarter. This trend needs to be watched closely in the months ahead.

items.statement: RBI notified new prepayment charge rules for floating rate loans to individuals/MSMEs effective Jan 1, 2026; will impact MSME/LAP prepayment fees; time to plan mitigation
items.quote: Recently, RBI has notified some new rules on prepayment charges for floating rate loans to individuals and MSMEs. This rule will become effective from 1st January 2026. This will impact one part of the income stream from our retail business, particularly the prepayment fees in the MSME lending business, the LAP business, that will get impacted.

items.statement: Leverage at 2.5:1 debt-to-equity; internal comfort threshold at 4:1; significant headroom for growth
items.quote: we think right level of leverage or an appropriate level of leverage beyond which we will probably not be comfortable is 4:1 debt to equity. We are currently very far away from t here. So it's not something that's a binding constraint right now. I think we ended this quarter 2.5

items.statement: Wholesale 2.0 repayments at 43% of disbursements; strong sector performance and quality asset selection
items.quote: Repayments were almost 43% of disbursements during quarter 1, and they con tinue to remain at significant rate, signifying better than expected performance of the

items.statement: Mortgages (affordable housing + LAP) grew 38% YoY to INR47,101 crores; 55% of total AUM, 68% of retail AUM
items.quote: In our flagship mortgage business, which comprises the affordable housing loans and loan against property, growth was 38% year-on-year to INR47,101 crores. Mortgages now account for 55% of the total AUM of the company and 68% of retail AUM.

items.statement: Loan against mutual funds at ~INR1,000 crores; secular opportunity; will report separately once >2% of book
items.quote: It's about what INR1,000 crores or something now of book. So yes, it is a business we like a lot. We like that business actually more than we like loan against shares.

items.statement: Gold loan pilot testing both dedicated and co-located branch models; bias toward dedicated branches; will disclose once scaled
items.quote: We are trying both models, Abhijit. Let's see which one is more cost economical. We have not yet figured out which one we want to bet on. We will try both. But right now, the bias is towards doing more gold loan specific branches, let me be clear.

items.statement: Retail customer franchise grew 21% YoY to 4.8 million; 50%+ originations tapped for cross-sell; 25-30% unsecured disbursements from cross-sell
items.quote: Our customer franchise continues to grow. It grew by 21% in the quarter on a Y-o-Y basis to 4.8 million. A significant portion of our customer originations are indeed tapped for future cross-sell opportunities, which you will see on this chart, it's 50-plus percent. And currently, we are sourcing 25% to 30% of our unsecured disbursements from cross-sell.

items.statement: Retail opex/AUM improved from 6.5% (Q4 FY23) to 4.2% (Q1 FY26); driven by tech/AI/GenAI investments and branch productivity
items.quote: For the last 9 quarters, you see that we have consistently reduced the opex to AUM ratio for our retail business, from a high of 6.5% in the fourth quarter FY '23, to where we are today, which is 4.2%.

items.statement: Lantheus/Life Molecular Imaging deal closed July 2025; payment based on 2025 profits expected in Q4 FY26; guidance unchanged
items.quote: The Lantheus and Life Molecular Imaging deal relating to the erstwhile Piramal Imaging business has successfully closed on July 2025. The consideration due to us would be based on 2025 profits of the business to be calculated at the end of the calendar year 2025. We expect to receive the payment subsequently in the last quarter of this current financial year. Our earlier guidance related to this m

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 6-7% for the year
items.quote: We have been giving the annual indication. We have given you a 6% to 7% kind of indication. That's what we had maintained. We will maintain that guidance.

items.statement: Purchased ~1 lakh tons of clinker externally due to extended shutdowns at Mukutban and Maihar
items.quote: We purchased maybe about a lakh tons of clinker from the market, which is 1 lakh tons we have purchased.

items.statement: Central India prices flat to down ~2% YoY; East and North saw price increases
items.quote: Between -- if we were to see in our markets between center region, there has not been too much of a price change between Q1 last year to Q1 this year over there. Or even if we were to compare Q4 of last year to Q1 now, there has been a drop there, but it's a marginal drop. It is not a drop of a very significant level. I think it would be -- it's about 2%.

items.statement: Blended cement share increased to 89% from 82% QoQ; trade sales rose to 78% from 72%
items.quote: Our share of blended cement -- proportion of blended cement this quarter was 89%. That is up from 82% on a sequential basis. So, that is the kind of change we have been able to affect. And coming to the trade sale again, in the immediately preceding quarter was 72%, from there we have taking it to 78% in this quarter.

items.statement: WHRS capacity currently 40 MW, planning additional 10 MW modernization
items.quote: So the current capacity of WHRS is around 40 megawatts, and we are planning for any other modernization on these areas with around 10 megawatt more we are planning. So it w ill be roughly -- you can say that 50 megawatt will be our whole

items.statement: Kundanganj new line to be commissioned during FY26; no clinker capacity addition before FY27
items.quote: The last question, which was asked, I would only like to comment that you don't see a clinker capacity coming before '27. It is all the major change you will find is at Ku ndanganj new line, which is going to -- that is going to get commissioned in the course of the

items.statement: Seeing premiumization and retail upgrading in Central markets; infra-led growth supportive
items.quote: We are seeing an upgrading happening in those markets. Some of them -- you have commented, you have visited Western MP, but similarly, if you go to UP, you are due to go. You'll find all these markets. There is a huge upgrading, which is happening there.

items.statement: Extended shutdowns at Mukutban (heavy rains) and Maihar caused clinker shortage and volume loss
items.quote: Where we have had a problem this quarter is we had two extended shutdowns in Mukutban and Maihar. These shutdowns were planned shutdowns, but their period got extended due to some unforeseen thing. In Mukutban, there was heavy rains in that area. In Maihar, we have faced certain problems.

items.statement: Depreciation fell 10% YoY due to fewer running days from shutdowns and some assets reaching residual value
items.quote: Certain depreciation on limestone, which has come down and second of all many assets have reached its 5% -- decrease in their depreciation, we have stopped charging as per book.

items.statement: Industry volume growth was 5-6% last quarter with regional disparity; some zones performed better than others.
items.quote: Demand/supply side, if you look at last quarter, the volume growth is about 5%-6%. This is what we have seen. And there is regional disparity in terms of volume growth.

items.statement: South prices up 8-9%, East up 6-7%; North, West, Central saw little increase; West prices slipped slightly.
items.quote: On pricing, some of the geographies have witnessed a good price increase, particularly South to the extent of about 8%-9% and East also about 6%-7%. North and west, I think have not witnessed that much increase and also Central part of India. West, in fact, I think prices have been little bit slipped last quarter.

items.statement: Focus on improving efficiency across value chain to be among top companies in EBITDA per ton; directionally on track.
items.quote: We are looking inwardly as to how we can really improve our efficiency across the value chain to be amongst top companies in terms of EBITDA per ton. And I am happy that I think directionally we are all right and we are working on all those levers which is going to take us to that level.

items.statement: Renewable energy focus for savings; Thermal Substitution Rate improving, will improve further after monsoon; digital initiatives on manufacturing front.
items.quote: On the Manufacturing front of course, I think Renewable Energy is one of our areas where we are focused. That is what is going to give us savings going forward. Second is Improvement of (TSR), Thermal Substitution Rate. We are doing better, and in coming quarter, I think things will further improve.

items.statement: Green Plus and Pro Plus brands doing well; UCWL brands Platinum Heavy Duty and Platinum Supremo to improve channel reach and volume.
items.quote: On Top Line front, the recently rejuvenated band of Green Plus and Pro Plus is doing very well. And with this merger of UCWL and those two brands coming to our fold, JK Lakshmi Fold which is Platinum Heavy Duty and Platinum Supremo is further going to help us to improve our channel reach and volume, that is what we believe.

items.statement: Volume growth will be incremental over industry growth; confident of delivering better than industry.
items.quote: As I said before, we will do better than industry and we are well on track. So, we will deliver that, at least incremental over the industry growth, that is we are confident about.

items.statement: Nagore (Rajasthan) 3 MT plant: one mining lease near approval, second lease land exchange in process; plant land identified and acquisition started.
items.quote: two mining lease licenses. In one, I think we are almost through with all those approvals, right. So, I think we are almost there where we wanted to be. In case of other mines, we have some exchange of land, like gochar land and forest land, which we are in the process of now exchanging. So, that process is on. Okay ? Plant land, we have already identified the place and part of land acquisition

items.statement: Kutch (Gujarat) mining: public hearing done, environment clearance in process, government land obtained, rehabilitation in progress; ahead of Nagore.
items.quote: Saurashtra, in fact, I think we are ahead of Nagore also in terms of acquisition.
