items.statement: Customer service being rebuilt in each geography with local language support; single point of contact created for each customer within 10 days of acquisition
items.quote: We believe customer service is a very important priority. And we are bringing customer service back. So what we mean is in each geography location, we would have customer service that customers can reach out, So in Europe, Spanish, Italian, German would be common languages, which we would equip it.

items.statement: Management met over 100 customers personally to rebuild trust; technical marketing and R&D functions rebuilt with rehired specialists
items.quote: I'm glad to tell you that my entire team is in the market, on the ground. In fact, I have met more than 100 customers personally and you know to discuss how we can build this trust and reliability back.

items.statement: Organic pigment market size ~USD5 billion growing at ~3% annually
items.quote: The organic pigment market is about USD5 billion with a growth rate of about 3%.

items.statement: Historical industry EBITDA margin range 8-11%; management confident in projections despite flat demand and destocking
items.quote: I do not want to comment on our competitors' performance, but I think if you look at our industry, I think historical average has been EBITDA margin between, let's say, 8% to 11%.

items.statement: Global manufacturing footprint across 19 facilities in 11 countries on 5 continents provides flexibility to respond to tariff threats
items.quote: However, given our global manufacturing footprint, it gives us the most flexibility now to respond favorably to our customers. So we have options to deliver from Europe, Mexico, Brazil, India.

items.statement: Over 70% of employees covered in purpose-mission-values integration; senior hires made in supply chain, procurement, finance, HR; 200-250 people in technology roles
items.quote: I'm glad to tell you in a short span, more than 70% of the employees have been covered for our purpose mission values going forward.

items.statement: Frankfurt site rightsizing completed before acquisition by administrator
items.quote: The rightsizing of the Frankfurt site has already been done even before the acquisition, which the administrator had initiated.

items.statement: Legacy Sudarshan pigment sales grew 16% in Q4 FY25 and 17% for full FY25
items.quote: For the quarter 4, the Sudarshan legacy Pigment has delivered the sales growth of around 16%. The sales stands at INR744 crores compared to INR644 crores last year

items.statement: RIECO revenue declined 28% to INR228 crores in FY25 with negative EBITDA due to lower order carry-forward and cost overruns
items.quote: Rieco performance during the year was subdued, while revenue dropped by 28%, which is at INR228 crores and also reduction seen in the gross margin, putting entire year EBITDA number under negative.

items.statement: Market environment uncertain due to geopolitical and tariff situation; flat demand and destocking continuing
items.quote: The market is not easy. I mean, that's no secret. Everyone knows, given the geopolitical and the tariff situation, it remains uncertain. There's a flat demand, and there is also destocking, which is happening.

items.statement: Acquired group not audited at consolidated level since 2022; 48 entities with 3 unintegrated ERP systems created data challenges
items.quote: This particular acquired group was not audited at the consolidated level since the calendar year 2022. It has 48 acquired group entities under the reporting coverage with 3 different ERP systems in the acquired group and that is also not integrated, created some data challenge for us to extract as far as the audit is concerned.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 order bookings INR16.2bn, up 57% YoY; backlog INR129.6bn, up 2% QoQ
items.quote: Our order book remains strong in Q1 as we saw bookings of INR16.2 billion, up 57% year-on-year compared to INR10.3 billion in the quarter ended June '24.

items.statement: Backlog INR129.6bn as of June 2025, 97% from private/central/PSU customers, <3% state utilities
items.quote: As a result of strong orders, our backlog continued to expand both sequentially and year-over-year, now reaching INR129.6 billion.

items.statement: Management aims to deliver better EBITDA than FY25's 19.1%; higher confidence after strong Q1
items.quote: With a strong performance in the quarter 1, we have higher confidence to deliver better EBITDA this year.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA 29.1%, up ~1000bps YoY driven by volume, price, productivity; not a new benchmark
items.quote: We reported a strong EBITDA of 29.1% during the quarter, representing an EBITDA expansion of about 1,000 basis points over the EBITDA generated in financial year '24-'25.

items.statement: Export margins ~500bps higher than domestic; domestic margins also strong due to pricing and cost savings
items.quote: Yes, Parikshit, as I mentioned, the pricing has been strong in the last couple of years. As we phase out the old backlog with low margin, then the overall backlog margin has become accretive.

items.statement: India needs 20,000 ckm HV lines and 125 GW substation capacity annually through 2032; >INR9tn investment
items.quote: To meet this surging demand, India's transmission sector must expand rapidly with 20,000 circuit kilometers of high -voltage transmission lines and 125 gigawatt substation capacity required each year through 2032.

items.statement: Non-HVDC pipeline expected to grow 7-8% YoY; HVDC orders (Barmer, South Olpad) expected in FY26
items.quote: As compared to last year, we expect a growth at least in some single digits, somewhere between 7% to 8% as compared to last year.

items.statement: Announced capex INR2.5bn: INR1.4bn for HVDC valves/controls, INR1.1bn for factory debottlenecking
items.quote: declared in our press release and also to the stock exchange that INR 1.4 billion for valves and controls for HVDC and Sushil Kumar: And another INR1.1 billion as a regular capex to debottleneck our capacities in the factory

items.statement: Capacity utilization good for AIS/transformers; grid automation can take more orders; adding people and lean debottlenecking
items.quote: Subhadip, the way our revenues are growing, the capacity utilization is increasing and of course, we are adding people as well as debottlenecking the capacity through lean.

items.statement: Export backlog now ~30% of total; long-term export revenue mix expected ~30%; Q1 export orders 14% of bookings
items.quote: So overall, on the long term, we expect that revenues to the extent of 30% should be contributed by the export on a long-term basis.

items.statement: Export geographies: Europe, Southeast Asia, Middle East, Korea; no regulatory/receivable risks seen
items.quote: I mean, we have orders from Europe, Southeast Asia, partly from Middle East and even Korea as the end destination.

items.statement: Prices stabilizing in most segments; able to pass on input cost increases; disciplined underwriting improved backlog margins
items.quote: I think there is a difference between increasing price and increasing margin today. The more important question is that if the cost is increasing, do we still have the flexibility to pass on that increase to the market? So partially, I would say, yes, that today also, we are able to do that.

items.statement: Q1 cash generation INR1.7bn driven by profit, down payments, disciplined WC despite 40% revenue growth
items.quote: In addition to strong P&L performance, we continue to generate positive cash flow with approximately INR1.7 billion cash generation in the quarter, driven by significant profit during the quarter, down payments on the new orders and the disciplined working capital management despite 40% increase in revenue.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents INR12.2bn as of June 30; zero debt
items.quote: As a result of this positive cash generation, we no w have a healthy cash and cash equivalents of INR12.2 billion with no

items.statement: Dividend INR1.3bn announced for AGM approval in September
items.quote: So far, we have announced a dividend of INR1.3 billion, which is to be paid after the approval of the shareholders in the upcoming AGM in September.

items.statement: Q1 revenue INR13.3bn, up 39% YoY; 39% from export backlog, 61% domestic; no HVDC in backlog currently
items.quote: In this quarter, about 39% of the revenues were generated by execution of highly profitable export backlog, whereas 61% of the revenue was executed from the domestic contracts.

items.statement: Orders from diverse set: utilities, TBCB players, EPCs; state utility exposure <3% of backlog
items.quote: Once again, in this quarter, orders were received from a very diverse set of customers and projects from all our served markets across all our businesses.

items.statement: Transformer deliveries 18-24 months; market seeks 10-12 months; AIS/GIS/Automation competitive landscape stable for 3 years
items.quote: So when I look at 3 years perspective and same is there for GIS, AIS also, we are not seeing any very large expansion of capacities. So going forward on AIS, GIS and Automation, I don't see that the pricing power or the competitive scenario or landscape to change much.

items.statement: HVDC Barmer-II to South Kalamb (6GW, 800kV) approved by NCT on May 30; first of new HVDC corridors
items.quote: In this context, the recent approval of 6 gigawatt 800 kV Barmer -II to South Kalamb HVDC project by the National Committee on Transmission on May 30 marks an important step.

items.statement: Supply chain challenges exist; mitigated by advance booking, multi-sourcing, localization; no orders taken without risk mitigation
items.quote: It is global energy transition story. Supply chain is definitely a big challenge. We have specific teams which keep on working to mitigate those challenges. And when we take orders, we ensure that we are not taking any orders where our risks are not mitigated.

items.statement: Order inflow FY25 had INR30bn one-offs (INR22bn export, INR8bn digital); ex-one-offs ~INR70bn base
items.quote: Last year order intake, we called out that it had about INR30 billion of one -off orders, INR22 billion of export order and INR8 billion of digital orders. So those 2 were the one -off deals. Excluding that, we were in the range of roughly INR70 billion.

items.statement: Backlog INR130bn ~3x FY25 revenue; provides 3-year revenue visibility
items.quote: Nitin, when I said that we have 30% of the backlog and if you look at our numbers, the backlog is about INR130 billion, which is 3x of last year revenue, roughly.

items.statement: SF6-free switchgear: GE Vernova pioneer; only one pilot project in India so far; expecting faster adoption medium-term
items.quote: When we talk about SF6 -free technology, GE Vernova has been pioneer in developing this technology. So, in India, what we have seen is that there is only one pilot project which has come in.

items.statement: Data center demand: currently 220kV GIS; expect 400kV as size grows, 765kV if gigawatt-scale
items.quote: You are correct, Balasubramanian, that as the data center size will grow up and up, so first, we'll see 400 kV demand. And if the data center prices goes into gigawatts, then we'll also see 765 kV demand coming for data centers.

items.statement: Synchronous condenser: provide transmission scope; rotating machine from group companies; talks of introduction in India
items.quote: The synchronous condenser as a product comes from the other companies which are into the power generation side because it's a rotating machine. But yes, when we participate in various forums, etc, yes, there is a talk which is going on that synchronous cond ensers will also be introduced into the Indian market

items.statement: Evaluating options for INR8bn available cash after dividend and capex; will communicate when decision taken
items.quote: Excluding the announced utilization plans, now we have an available cash of INR8 billion for which management continues to evaluate the options.

items.statement: Management targets mid-teens to high-teens revenue CAGR over the long term.
items.quote: So, we have been growing at mid-teens to high-teens growth rate for the last many years. So, our objective primarily is to continue that trajectory, if not exceed it.

items.statement: Annual capex typically Rs 100-150 crore; no further capex planned for Chennai plant this year.
items.quote: But typically, we have been doing Rs. 100 crore to Rs. 150 crore of capex per year over the last several years. One or two years may be higher, one or two years may be much lower, but on average about Rs. 150 crore capex is being incurred.

items.statement: Chennai greenfield facility achieved production stability in Q1 FY26; goal to fill first line this financial year.
items.quote: One of the significant strategic developments recently was the successful operationalization of our new greenfield manufacturing facility in Chennai. This state- of-the-art unit has achieved producti on stability this quarter and is seeing encouraging engagement from customers across South India

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization around 70% in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Yes, something like 70%.

items.statement: Domestic demand improved in Q1 FY26 with encouraging volume growth; festive season expected to support further growth.
items.quote: And we see the domestic demand improving over coming months. Now we are entering into our festive season, and there is certainly a good demand growth at present.

items.statement: Export demand saw slack in recent months due to macroeconomic factors at end-consumer level; no fundamental business loss.
items.quote: We have been seeing some slack in the export the last few months. We don't see any fundamental issue or any share of business loss. I think it is just to do with overall economic factors at our end consumers' side.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 17.1%, down 50 bps YoY due to higher fixed and variable costs and lower revenue growth.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter remained steady at Rs. 72.6 crore with margins of 17.1%, which were marginally lower by 50 basis points year-on-year due to higher fixed and variable costs and lower revenue growth.

items.statement: Paperboard prices increased a few percent in Q1 FY26; no significant fluctuation.
items.quote: So, not much fluctuation. There is a slight increase in the prices in this last quarter, a few percent on paperboard. Yes, not anything very significant.

items.statement: Euro-denominated term loans unhedged; mark-to-market forex loss of Rs 10 crore in Q1 FY26 due to Euro-INR divergence from USD-INR.
items.quote: PBT was impacted by a Rs. 10 crore forex loss arising from mark-to-market adjustments on Euro-denominated term loans.

items.statement: Debt levels growing in absolute terms but stable at 1:1 or sub-1:1 debt-equity ratio; comfortable with headroom for opportunistic investments.
items.quote: And typically, the debt levels are growing in an absolute basis. But on a ratio basis, it is quite stable at 1:1 or sub-1:1 levels. So, we hope to continue that.

items.statement: Export share guidance not provided; exploring new geographies including US, Southeast Asia, Middle East, Africa, Europe.
items.quote: I don't know. It depends really on how things pan out. We don't have any guidance.

items.statement: Chennai plant primarily serving existing and new South-based customers; only 10-20% volume shift from other plants.
items.quote: Most of it will be the latter. And the shifting from other plants would be like maybe 10%-20% or something. But yes, mostly it is customers who are existing customers or like small customers whose major requirements were in South, which we are now tapping.

items.statement: FMCG and food & beverage combined largest segment; tobacco very big; liquor now very small percentage.
items.quote: FMCG, and food and beverage combined are the biggest segment followed by the tobacco business. But we don't give you the breakup, unfortunately.

items.statement: Creative Offset acquisition showing positive trajectory with high double-digit growth; unit expected to turn profitable in FY26.
items.quote: Last year we had a very high double-digit growth, and this year we see that continuing. And so far, things are going positively. So, we are seeing an improvement, and the unit will hopefully turn positive this year.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty a setback for export growth plans; management views it as temporary negotiating tactic.
items.quote: So, that is, of course, a setback if we can't figure things out. But I think we are reasonably positive and most of the people we are speaking to are also feeling that this is more like a temporary thing which will get sorted out.

items.statement: Not averse to raising equity for substantial opportunities; sizing not limited by existing balance sheet.
items.quote: We are not averse to that, if that is the point. I mean, let's say there is a reasonably substantial opportunity, then we are not averse to looking at that. So, that is not a limiting factor, I would say, for us.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 424.7 crore, up almost 5% YoY.
items.quote: FY26 has commenced on a steady note with Q1 delivering consolidated revenues of Rs. 424.7 crore, reflecting a almost 5% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Gravure facility project on track for December quarter commissioning.
items.quote: Yes, that is going on. There is nothing to update, so then we didn't update, but it is going on.

items.statement: Targeting 40-42% export share of revenue by next year
items.quote: I think that's where we will end up by next year, somewhere between 40-42%.

items.statement: Targeting Rs 1,600-1,700 crore revenue run rate by next year
items.quote: we had said that with these expansion projects, we would be looking at about 1,600 to 1,700 crores in about 3 years. I think we are on a run rate to get there. If not this year, then early next year, a quarterly run rate.

items.statement: Long-term target EBITDA margins of 14-15%
items.quote: long-term perspective, we are targeting around 14% to 15% kind of margins.

items.statement: New CAPEX projects to meet 20-25% ROCE threshold
items.quote: we look at, an ROCE of at least 20-25% between that number. Below that, we that's generally our threshold.

items.statement: Export volumes grew 37% YoY driven by new approvals and market share gains
items.quote: there has been a 37% growth in value growth in exports and that has largely come from new approvals. As you know, our Nitrile Latex business, we are at almost now 100% capacity utilization. I would say about 90% capacity utilization, not 100%. So, we are about 90% in Q1. So, obviously a lot of new approvals have come through. We have been aggressive in terms of gaining market share as well

items.statement: Domestic paper and construction demand remains challenging with slowdown feel
items.quote: paper and domestic market overall does remain challenging, no question. There is an overall, it feels like a slowdown, but we have still pushed through.

items.statement: Nitrile Latex industry overcapacity persists, margins under pressure until 80-85% utilization
items.quote: the main issue seems to be capacities that were created for gloves and for latexes in 2022-2023 that slowly obviously the utilizations have improved, but till they get to about 80-85%, these margins will be under pressure for sure.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 operating EBITDA margin improved to 10.3% from 9.45% YoY
items.quote: Operating EBITDA to date around Rs. 39 crores. That's a robust 22% year-on-year growth and the operating EBITDA margin improved to 10.3% up from 9.45% in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Nitrile Latex margins remain low due to industry overcapacity, dragging overall margins down by couple of percentage points
items.quote: the average EBITDA margins for Nitrile Latex are much lower than our average EBITDA margins, and obviously good growth has come from there. So, in spite of getting some operating leverage due to increase in quantities, the truth is that Nitrile Latex margins are still not great because of overcapacity.

items.statement: Nitrile Latex margins deteriorated in Q1 vs Q4, small improvement seen in Q2
items.quote: Q1 was, I mean, again, actually deteriorated in Q1, to be honest, for Nitrile Latex overall margins. Again, Q2, we are seeing some small improvements.

items.statement: Targeting Nitrile Latex EBITDA margins of 12-15% when market improves
items.quote: the market needs to improve for us to go back to about, 12-15% EBITDA margins, as we were expecting

items.statement: Exports contributed 37% of revenue in Q1 FY26, highest ever
items.quote: And overall exports contributed to 37% of the overall revenue. So, the highest ever that we have had in terms of exports.

items.statement: Taloja latex plant at 85% utilization, Valia Nitra latex at 90%, NBR and other products near 100% in Q1
items.quote: our capacity utilization in Q1 for the latex plant in Taloja is at about 85% and our Valia Nitra latex plant was around 90% and for NBR and other products, we are pretty much running at almost 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Planning de-bottlenecking and expansion for latex, SBR latex, styrene acrylics, and NBR; details to be announced shortly
items.quote: we will be planning certain de-bottlenecking and expansion projects which we will announce shortly once the details are finalized.

items.statement: Hybrid power project in Gujarat: Rs 3.5-4 crore investment, good IRR, commissioned next year, mainly ESG driven
items.quote: The total investment from Apcotex side for the Gujarat project is, I think, around 3.5 crores, or give or take 3.5-4 crores. And the payback in the IRR is very good. Obviously, that will start kicking-in from next year once the project is commissioned.

items.statement: Maharashtra wind power project delayed due to MSEDCL rule changes on banking
items.quote: Unfortunately, there have been some rule changes that have been announced recently, as a result of which we are kind of. We are just waiting to see how that lands. MSEDSL has made some rule changes on not allowing banking, etc., which has changed the commercials completely.

items.statement: Freight costs settled post-COVID but remain high on Suez Canal corridors
items.quote: certainly things are not as bad as they were, just during the post-COVID sort of years and there are certain corridors, especially around the Suez Canal, where freight costs are still reasonably high, but they are settled.

items.statement: NBR pricing volatile, linked to crude oil, butadiene and acrylonitrile; prices fell in Q1 vs Q4
items.quote: in the last few quarters, we have had some quarters where prices have suddenly fallen, in Q1, prices have fallen compared to Q4. So, it's very hard to predict because it's all linked to oil and down there, downstream, but not even only oil.

items.statement: Anti-dumping case on NBR imports in advanced stages; decision expected in 2-4 months
items.quote: that is in sort of, I would say, advanced stages of the investigation. Definitely moved forward and it has been about 9 months or so since, or maybe more, 9.5-10 months since we initiated the case. Generally, these cases are disposed within a year. So, if not a year, there might be a delay of a couple of months, I think in the next 2 to 4 months, we should have an idea of how that pans out.

items.statement: China imposes 12-20% anti-dumping duty on Korean NBR imports, renewed for 6th year
items.quote: China has imposed a duty of I think anywhere between 12% to 20% on imports from Korea. So, they have they have levied an anti-dumping duty and it has been going on for the 6th year. It has been renewed after 5 years.

items.statement: Turkey exports affected by Suez Canal logistics and war, not political tensions; volumes dropped over 2-3 years
items.quote: it is more because of the wars and, issue around the Suez Canal that sometimes it is taking longer to get to Turkey, the material. As a result of it, some customers, are not too comfortable with the long lead time. So, that is the main reason why business to Turkey has been affected.

items.statement: Egypt and Turkey carpet industry exports affected by Israel-Gaza conflict; growing Saudi/UAE business
items.quote: yes, certainly our exports, especially to the carpet industry, have been affected. It is not that it has not been affected, but we are still continuing to do business. Maybe our volumes have dropped somewhat over the last 2 years, but we continue to do business. Unfortunately, we cannot make it up specifically in the carpet segment because those are 2 large carpet manufacturing countries. Of cours

items.statement: Japanese Nitrile Latex producer exiting business in FY26; no new capacity announced globally
items.quote: A company in Japan has announced that in 2026, they will come out of the Nitrile Latex business. Maybe it is an old plant.

items.statement: Upcoming capex focused on latex, SBR latex, styrene acrylics, NBR for paper, carpet, construction, textiles, automotive, industrial, agriculture
items.quote: be all our latex products other than Nitrile Latex. So, it's paper, carpet, construction, textiles, and also NBR. So, all kinds of rubber products, whether it is an automotive or industrial applications, agriculture use. So, all of those, wherever NBR is used. So, those are the 2 main thrust areas for now, for the upcoming

items.statement: Construction, carpet, textiles segments have higher margins than paper over last couple of years
items.quote: Construction and carpet have been higher. Construction, carpet, textiles but just because of the nature of the industries and more specialty products in those segments I would say in the last couple of years paper has been the lowest out of these four segments at least.

items.statement: NBR domestic market share low; 70% of NBR still imported, opportunity for import substitution
items.quote: The one opportunity that does remain is NBR where we have a very low market share not very low I would say we have a lower market share and but 70% of the product is still imported from outside the country that remains an opportunity.

items.statement: U.S. tariff uncertainty on Chinese gloves affecting global latex demand and pricing visibility for 2-3 quarters
items.quote: there is a lot of uncertainty around these tariffs and finally where it will land, we won't know perhaps for another couple of quarters and that's affected the glove industry.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target INR 400 crores with EBITDA margin 29-30%
items.quote: Okay, so we should basically be definitely looking at INR 400 crores this year. That is definitely what we have considering Sindoor, considering other things, we definitely have INR 400 crores as our this thing and our margin should remain in the same range that we are in right now.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR 500 crores
items.quote: Yes, we should. If our pace continues at what we are doing and considering the kind of qualitative hotels we are adding, it is very much possible for us to hit INR 500 crores next year.

items.statement: Operational hotels to increase from ~19 to ~25 by FY26 end, targeting 30 by March 2026
items.quote: Currently we are operating around 19 hotels by this year ending. We will be going to approximately running, not signed up but running hotels around 25. So, that is basically it and the company is very buoyant and sure that we are aiming to open 30 hotels by this year.

items.statement: Operational rooms to grow from ~1,850 to ~2,500 in FY26
items.quote: From around right now, we are at around 1,850 rooms, 1,825 rooms. From this, basically, we are this year going to grow to almost 2,500 operational rooms.

items.statement: New signings: Orchid Rishikesh (98+ rooms), Orchid Nashik (April opening), Orchid Panchgani (Sept 15 opening), Orchid Dwarka, Bhavnagar, Hyderabad Hi-Tech City (60 rooms), Dehradun, Gwalior
items.quote: We have good news that we will be opening the Orchid Rishikesh this month and along with that we are happy to inform that we signed another hotel so we will be basically having two hotels there but they are next to each other because of which the overall inventory will be 100+.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 21.91%, full year target 29-30%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR 18 crores, a growth of around 37% year-on-year basis, with an EBITDA margin 21.91%.

items.statement: New hotels may cause short-term EBITDA burn but full-year margins expected stable at 29-30%
items.quote: Definitely, the margins will more or less remain the same because we have now a very good mix of old stable, new coming in and growing. So, definitely, the margins will be, if not stable, if not down, it won't be. But if not growth, at least it will be stable.

items.statement: Blended ARR target INR 7,500 for FY26; Rishikesh targeting INR 15,000-20,000 ARR; Puri targeting INR 10,000 ARR
items.quote: On a target of on a blended basis with our other premium products now coming, we hope to target the INR 7,500 mark.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 brand-wise ARR: Orchid INR 6,300, IRA INR 5,400, Lotus INR 5,500, Fort JadhavGADH INR 8,000
items.quote: We have basically had ARR of around INR 6,300 for Orchid. We have around INR 5,400 for IRA. We have INR 5,500 for our Lotus. We have INR 8,000 for our Fort JadhavGADH.

items.statement: Debt at INR 95-98 crores, interest cost INR 2.86 crores at 10%, targeting 9% or below
items.quote: Our debt is right now sitting at INR 95 crores, just for your knowledge. INR 98 crores. Smita Nanda: Interest cost is coming in at INR 2.86 crores. Gurvinder Juneja: INR 2.86 crores Vishal Kamat: And this is currently at 10%, which the company intends to bring this to 9% or below that

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated revenue INR 83 crores (+12% YoY), EBITDA INR 18 crores (+37% YoY), PAT INR 4 crores (+291% YoY)
items.quote: The consolidated revenue for Q1 FY '26 stood at INR 83 crores representing a growth of approximately 12% on year-on-year basis. EBITDA for the quarter was INR 18 crores, a growth of around 37% year-on-year basis, with an EBITDA margin 21.91%. Profit after tax stood at INR 4 crores, showing a significant increase of 291% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Operation Sindoor impacted May revenue (15-20 days), especially Chandigarh, Himachal, Shimla, Manali
items.quote: While the overall financials are nice, they could have been much better because unfortunately it is our national duty to support our government and our nation and that's basically what has affected us in the first 15-20 days of the month of May and in some cases it has affected even more like in the case of Chandigarh and Himachal, Shimla, Manali.

items.statement: IRA brand outperforming due to smaller base; new Orchid hotels pulling down brand average initially but high ADR markets (Rishikesh, Panchgani) will lift long-term
items.quote: Now that more Orchids have come and many of these Orchids are new because of which they take time to stabilize. So, because of which the overall Orchid average is as you would have rightly pointed out, low.

items.statement: Preference for larger hotels (100+ rooms) with banqueting/MICE capabilities; adding 7,000 and 5,000 sq ft banquet halls at Orchid Pune
items.quote: We actually tend to want larger inventory because we have expertise in running 100-plus, there are very few hotel brands in the country which can claim operation skills of large hotels of 300 plus. We have 2. We have one which is Orchid Mumbai, which is 372 rooms and we have the Orchid Pune, which is 410 rooms.

items.statement: Merger proposal: NSE/BSE approvals received, NCLT process initiated with lawyer appointed
items.quote: We have already got the NSE and the BSE approval. So, now the same has to go to NCLT. So, formally a lawyer has been appointed for (Inaudible) 0:38:36.6 NCLT.

items.statement: Land valuation near Vadhavan Port increased 3-4x from INR 70 crores (16 acres + Mumbai property)
items.quote: So, total value which was there was of INR 70 crores for one is that it has a 16 odd acres is the land, any land. And also along with that, there is a property which is of Mumbai, which is all about 1/8 of an acre.

items.statement: Puri Fort Mahodadhi delayed due to airport height restrictions (40m to 27m); revising plans for 156-room property with 9,500 sq ft banquet hall targeting 2027
items.quote: Our Puri property got delayed because when we had submitted our plans to the government, our sub-building was a 40-meter tower. But now with the new airport coming at Puri and the Puri Airport height restrictions coming in, our plan had to be revised. And now as per law, the height has to come to 27 meters.

items.statement: Conservative FY26 guidance due to Operation Sindoor impact and new hotels opening in H2 (limited wedding revenue in first half-year)
items.quote: The first reason is that had Operation Sindoor not happened and the month of May not so good, it would have definitely been a revised estimate, one. Secondly, the number of rooms which are being added, if you notice, all are being added around September, which means that we are only getting the half year benefit.

items.statement: Achieved debt-zero target ahead of deadline; repaying debt while growing asset-light
items.quote: We are also repaying our debt as promised, we are already a debt zero company in that regard. So, this was our promise to ourselves and our investors and shareholders that we will become debt zero. And we have achieved that before our deadline target.

items.statement: Revenue share model: Kamat Hotels receives 12-20% of total property revenue net of revenue share
items.quote: The company, Kamat Hotels, whatever may be the revenue will get comfortably anywhere between 12% to 18% back apart from the rev share. Between 12% to 20% back apart from the rev share. Net what Kamat Hotel will get. It could get anywhere between 12% to 20%.

items.statement: Hotel GOP assumption 35-45% for Rishikesh property
items.quote: Let's assume that if this hotel does at 100% revenue, the thumb rule is 40% GOP. So, the company 35% to 45% GOP, okay. Actually, let's put it as a range that generally a hotel does 35% to 45% GOP depending on the various things.

items.statement: Order book increased to Rs 703.16 crore from Rs 612.40 crore QoQ
items.quote: order book position is Rs.703.16 crore including Rs. 608.70 crore of product business and Rs 94.46 crore of project and services business and on 31st March, the order book position was Rs. 612.40 crore including Rs. 534.32 crore of product business and Rs. 78.08 crore of project and services business

items.statement: Consolidated revenue was Rs 217.72 crore, down QoQ but up YoY
items.quote: Our consolidated revenue for the quarter is at Rs. 217.72 crore against Rs. 228.96 crore QoQ and Rs. 195.39 crore YoY.

items.statement: EBITDA fell to Rs 33.74 crore from Rs 74.31 crore QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is at Rs. 33.74 crore against Rs. 74.31 crore QoQ and Rs. 28.75 crore YoY.

items.statement: Cost of delivery rose to 70.1% of revenue from 57.3% QoQ
items.quote: As for expenses, cost of delivery including cost of product development for the quarter is 70.1% of revenue against 57.3% of revenue QoQ and 75.5% of revenue YoY.

items.statement: Marketing and sales expenses increased to 6% of revenue from 4.9% QoQ
items.quote: Marketing and sales expenses for the quarter is 6% of revenue against 4.9% of revenue QoQ, 2.2% YoY.

items.statement: G&A expenses rose to 8.3% of revenue from 5.3% QoQ
items.quote: G&A expenses for the quarter is 8.3% of revenue against 5.3% of revenue QoQ and 7.6% YoY.

items.statement: Net profit was Rs 35.20 crore, down from Rs 64.77 crore QoQ
items.quote: Net profit is at Rs. 35.20 crore for the quarter against Rs. 64.77 crore QoQ and Rs. 30.20 crore YoY.

items.statement: Total cash and equivalents increased to Rs 965.93 crore from Rs 877.26 crore QoQ
items.quote: Total cash and cash equivalents as on June 30, 2025, are Rs. 965.93 crore against Rs. 877.26 crore as on March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Receivables decreased to Rs 126.12 crore from Rs 137.41 crore QoQ
items.quote: With regards to receivables, we are at Rs. 126.12 crore against Rs. 137.41 crore previous quarter.

items.statement: Gross fixed asset additions were Rs 3.46 crore, mainly computers and servers
items.quote: During the quarter, there is a gross addition of fixed assets of Rs. 3.46 crore, consisting primarily of Rs. 2.70 crore on computer and servers, Rs. 0.18 crore on furniture and fixtures, Rs. 0.03 crore on office equipment's, Rs. 0.40 crore on building and plant & machinery and Rs. 0.15 crore on software.

items.statement: USD 2.25 million forward contracts at average rate 87.03 with Rs 0.19 crore MTM gain
items.quote: In terms of foreign currency hedges on June 30, 2025, we had USD 2.25 million of forward contracts at an average rate of 87.03. There is a mark to market gain of Rs. 0.19 crore which is taken to the hedging reserve in the balance sheet.

items.statement: Top 5 clients contributed 28.6% of revenue, up from 27.8% QoQ
items.quote: Revenue contribution from the top 5 clients for the quarter is 28.6% against 27.8% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Total headcount was 1,939, down slightly from 1,945 in March 2025
items.quote: Total Head count is 1939 as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Product revenue was Rs 184.91 crore, projects and services revenue was Rs 32.81 crore
items.quote: Product revenue for the quarter is at Rs. 184.91 crore against Rs. 199.56 crore QoQ and Rs. 168.01 crore YoY. Revenue from projects and services for the quarter is at Rs. 32.81 crore against Rs. 29.40 crore QoQ and Rs. 27.38 crore YoY.

items.statement: Order conversion delays due to board-level regulatory involvement, but pipeline building and conversions improving
items.quote: As we had mentioned in the past that, you know, couple of quarters. Here, we did experience some slowdown in the sense that there was traction in the market, but converting orders were taking time a lot of involvement in closure of orders. Typically, we are saying that these decisions are now going up to board levels. The boards are getting involved because I think they are directed by the regulat

items.statement: Confident of regaining overseas revenue share over coming years with globally implementable products
items.quote: We have been very consciously working on our products for the last decade or so to make sure that they evolve into a product which is globally implementable, and I am really pleased to say that we have achieved some degree of clarity on that aspect, and we are working in multiple geographies where the new set of products are getting implemented. Hence, we are very confident that over the coming fe

items.statement: Working on proof of concept with a prospect and consultant partnerships for North America lending platform
items.quote: One, we are having senior sales leader and second, I think we are already in touch with one of the prospects and we are working on a proof of concept with them. So hopefully, we are looking forward to convert that to a deal in this year. And similarly, we also trying to open up a partnership with the consultants' big force so that they also help us in that direction.

items.statement: AI modules embedded in products, not billed separately yet but will be monetized going forward
items.quote: So, these are embedded AI's and part of product offerings, so far, we are not billing AI as a business model, but we are empowering our customers to leverage these AI capabilities and going forward, we will be billing them too.

items.statement: In-house AI models with explainability features satisfy regulator requirements for tier-one geographies
items.quote: So, this is of course. Thanks for asking this question. Again, this goes into the kind of depth we put in during the research and development and the ability to explain about the workings of AI and how AI come to these two are conclusions. So, there is an explainability part of it and that is good enough to be able to suffice the need.

items.statement: FinnAxia seeing strong traction in financial supply chain and trade finance with Federal Bank and HNB live
items.quote: We are seeing a very good, strong traction in the verticals like financial supply chain and trade finance. So quite a few discussions are progressing with different prospects and customers.

items.statement: Created CMO role to strengthen market positioning and thought leadership for products handling $1.2T retail assets and $15T transactions
items.quote: This is an attempt to further strengthen that particular initiative of ours to position this product, this robust product, which is handling more than US$ 1.2 trillion worth of retail assets when it comes to our lending product from the FinnOne Neo, when it comes to our product, FinnAxia, which we also talked about, which is earning more than US$ 15 trillion worth of transactions in one year.

items.statement: Hoshin Kanri is a long-term cultural initiative focused on customer satisfaction and employee development, not immediate cost optimization
items.quote: As far as cost optimization is concerned, that is not the intent of Hoshin Kanri. Hoshin Kanri is a philosophical extremely long term initiative, and which believes in which is sharply focused on customer satisfaction and employee development and delivering value on an ongoing basis. This is something that involves substantial cultural change, which is what we are working on, and it will start sho

items.statement: Continuing price discussions with existing customers based on product value delivered
items.quote: No, we continue to talk to our customers about the value that our products are delivering. And based on that, we look at the pricing of fish.

items.statement: Order book of Rs 703.16 crore expected to be implemented over next 9 months
items.quote: And this order book of Rs. 703.16 Crore, this will be, like, implemented in the next 9 months. Right

items.statement: Aiming to restore margins through top-line growth rather than cost cuts
items.quote: So, we will be an ongoing attempt to increase our top line and that is how we will be wanting to get back to the margins that we had last year.

items.statement: Company does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance
items.quote: As we all or other, Nuclear Software does not provide any specific revenue earnings guidance.

items.statement: Large FinnOne Neo collections transformation went live with 20,000 daily users at a major Indian client
items.quote: This has been an exciting quarter where we have gone live with some of our biggest implementations where more than 20,000 users are re-arranging our system, our product for corrections with one of the biggest players in India.

items.statement: Rural markets sustained growth leadership outpacing urban areas; non-seasonal portfolio remained strong while seasonal categories faced headwinds from shorter summer and unseasonal rains
items.quote: Rural markets sustained their growth leadership outpacing urban areas. Driven by strong performance in branded commodities, personal care, and daily segments, while seasonal categories faced headwinds due to a shorter summer and unseasonal rains.

items.statement: Structural double-digit revenue growth expected over next 2-3 years at company level
items.quote: For sure, we believe that we are on that path. So, over the next 2 to 3 years, we will continue on a structural double-digit growth journey.

items.statement: Gross margin declined 73 bps in Q1 due to product mix impact from seasonal brands; majority of brands delivered strong gross margin expansion
items.quote: In the current quarter, however, gross margins registered a marginal decline of 73 basis points at the overall level. Nonetheless, the majority of our brands continued to deliver strong gross margin expansion, underscoring the inherent strength of our portfolio.

items.statement: Two-year EBITDA margin enhancement journey remains on track despite quarterly volatility; product-by-product gross margin expansion and operating leverage are key drivers
items.quote: A percentage here and there but the two-year journey of enhancing my EBITDA, I do not think we are moving away from that basic view. To my mind, you may find a quarter here and there but directionally, we think we have taken right actions will play out.

items.statement: Input inflation showing signs of easing, providing optimism for margin recovery in coming quarters
items.quote: On the cost front, persistent input inflation is beginning to show signs of easing, providing our optimism for margin recovery in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Excluding seasonal brands, business delivered strong double-digit growth in both volume and value; seasonal brands impact made overall organic growth near flattish
items.quote: The ongoing business without the acquisition, without seasonal brands is both volume and value. So, if I add the seasonal brands back for organic growth, it becomes flattish.

items.statement: Company returned to net cash positive position, strengthening ability to participate in large projects, infrastructure development, and automation initiatives
items.quote: During the quarter, the company returned to a net cash positive position, strengthening its ability to participate in large projects, infrastructure development, and automation initiatives aimed at building the business for the next phase of growth.

items.statement: Direct distribution reach at 6.1-6.2 lakh outlets; target to expand to 7 lakh by end of FY26 and eventually reach 3.5-4 million outlets via Nielsen coverage
items.quote: Our current direct reach is, direct coverage is about 6.1 lakh-6.2 lakh outlet. We are available as reported by Nielsen by 2.8 million outlets. Our wish list is to expand that 2.8 to 3.5 first and maybe eventually 4 million assuming there's no major restructuring of the market that happens. Towards that, we are looking at expanding another 80,000 outlets in this financial year.

items.statement: Rite Bite Max Protein business outperforming acquisition estimates with momentum higher than envisaged; gaining substantial acceptance across all channels including general trade
items.quote: I am happy to share that our actual while we don't give specific brand wise growth but happy to share that the current momentum for six months of actually seven months of acquisition is much higher than what we had accounted for and it is gaining substantial acceptance across all channels.

items.statement: Organized trade saliency improved to 30.9% in Q1 FY26 from 23.3% in Q1 FY25; e-commerce contributed 14.5% and non-trade 16.4%
items.quote: Organized trade saliency continued to improve, reaching 30.9% in Q1 of FY'26, up from 23.3% in Q1 of FY'25, while e-commerce contributed 14.5% and non-trade 16.4%.

items.statement: EverYuth leads scrubs with 48.7% share (+262.3 bps YoY) and peel-off masks with 77.2% share (-56.4 bps YoY); ranks 5th in facial cleansing with 7.8% share (+88.8 bps YoY)
items.quote: EverYuth leads key sub-segments with a 48.7% share in scrubs, which is a positive of 262.3 basis points year-on-year and 77.2% in peel-off masks, a drop of 56.4 basis points. Overall presence, the brand ranks fifth in facial cleansing with a 7.8% share, up 88.8 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Nycil maintained #1 position in prickly heat powder with 33.3% market share at MAT level despite quarterly dip from early monsoons
items.quote: Nycil saw a temporary dip this quarter due to early monsoons, but maintained its number one position with a market share of 33.3%.

items.statement: Glucon D maintained leadership in glucose powder with 58.9% market share at MAT level; category grew 2.8% at MAT but declined for the quarter
items.quote: On the Glucon D front, Glucon D maintained its leadership in the glucose powder category with a market share of 58.9% at the MAT level. The glucose powder category grew by 2.8% at the MAT level. However, the category declined for the quarter.

items.statement: Sugar Free holds 96.1% market share in sugar substitute category which grew 4.9% at MAT level; Sugar Free Green and Delight outperforming
items.quote: On the Sweetness front, Sugar Free brand continues to maintain its dominant position, holding a commanding 96.1% market share in the sugar substitute category, which has grown by 4.9% at the MAT level.

items.statement: Nutralite growth driven by fat spread core, value-added dairy, mayonnaise, and branded fat (butter/ghee); cheese launched in food service with good early response
items.quote: Our base business, our core which is fat spread, continues to drive the momentum. So, that's essential for us to get right and that continues to keep moving up. Having said this, the new part of the portfolio where we want to be a fair dairy and spreads, mayonnaise as well as our branded fat, if I were to say butter and ghee branded ones, that has really helped us also move it up.

items.statement: HFD/nutrition drink category under structural pressure; expected to deliver sustainable low single-digit growth long-term; Complan market share 4% at MAT (Nielsen underreports e-commerce share)
items.quote: In my view, it will in medium to long term still deliver a sustainable low single digit growth. I don't know that's my view still there is good reasons for it. Only time will tell but and we do believe that done right by playing the right segments there is still room for growth and therefore we are still working on it.

items.statement: Tax guidance: zero tax in FY26, marginal 8-10% in FY27, full 25% rate thereafter
items.quote: For this FY'25-'26, there won't be any tax. For next year, there could be some minimum maybe marginal tax, maybe you can take it about 8 -10 % and going forward in the next year it will be at a full tax rate which is at the rate 25%.

items.statement: Seasonal brand impact mostly absorbed in Q1; July-August has much smaller impact; limited impact post July-August
items.quote: So, mostly it is done and dusted. There is some numbers which flow into July because especially Nycil plays out here and a little bit of Glucon D also. Post July-August, there is a very, very little impact. So, some bit you might find in 3Q but not significant. But after that, there's limited impact.

items.statement: Advertising spend to remain at FY25 levels in short-to-medium term to invest gross margin gains into growth momentum; operating leverage expected from overheads and people expenses long-term
items.quote: So, in short to medium term, it will remain at a similar level as FY'25 because we also want to invest back, increase gross margins into helping us increase our growth momentum and it's essential for us. But over a longer term, yes, we will see more efficiencies coming through.

items.statement: FY25 had 12 new product launches; innovation pipeline active with both NPDs and relaunches of existing portfolio planned; no specific number shared for next 18 months
items.quote: FY'25, we had 12 launches. I will tell you, I don't have a specific number to share over the next 18 months but I will tell you two things that will drive our strategy or our choices. One is that consumers' expectations are changing at a much faster pace than most of us can handle.

items.statement: Quick commerce and e-commerce delivering strong growth; Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities emerging as key growth drivers; organized trade saliency rising but general trade expansion continues in under-serviced rural/small towns
items.quote: Meanwhile, the digital channels such as quick commerce and e-commerce continue to deliver strong growth. Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities are emerging as key growth drivers, positioning the business well for its next phase of expansion.

items.statement: Nutralite dairy sourcing from western UP (Aligarh plant) with own farmer network since 1959; no sourcing issues seen for next few years but pricing volatility exists
items.quote: Talking about dairy, we are largely focused on western UP dairy sourcing which is based out of a Aligarh plant which has a history dating back to 1959 when it was started and we have a own network of societies and farmers who provide milk and therefore we have been fairly consistent with them, we have worked and grown with them.

items.statement: Complan HFD category facing structural decline; if premium differentiation and new age relevance doesn't work in next couple of years, strategic calls including exit may be considered
items.quote: If that works and it plays out, I think we should be sorted. If it doesn't, then we will have to do some strategic calls at some point of time in next couple of years.

items.statement: Nycil soap extension is tactical and only directed at Middle East market; no strategic plan for soap in India
items.quote: First of all, soap extension of Nycil is very tactical one and only directed at Middle East which is more opportunistic. At a strategic level in most of our, largely our business is India centric we haven't done it and therefore there is no specific plan ready to share as far as the soap and Nycil is concerned.

items.statement: Sampriti brand converged into Nutralite strategically at acquisition; convergence helped Nutralite grow bigger, faster and more efficiently
items.quote: As far as converging Sampriti brand into Nutralite is concerned, it was a very strategic call taken right at the time of acquisition we had thought through it because we believe that Nutralite is a large brand it has huge potential and consumers don't see it as dairy or non-dairy but it actually meets our all dairy and spreads requirement and can become one of our largest brands in future if we ru

items.statement: Complan Viemax (adult nutrition) in early days; doctor prescribing giving confidence but small scale; expect more updates in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We are seen some doctors really prescribing it and that gives us confidence that a formulation is good, the doctors are happy with our proposition and recommending or prescribing it to their patients and that helps us believe that there is good potential in it, but it's early days. It's still small and it's a long haul. We believe will only strengthen the overall mother brand Complan as a superior

items.statement: Expects NIM around 3.5% for FY26
items.quote: Expecting NIM in the range of 3.5% for FY '25-'26, as discussed in the last con call.

items.statement: Expects ROA to remain at 1.5%+ for FY26
items.quote: ROA is expected to remain at our current level of 1.5 plus.

items.statement: Expects cost-to-income ratio 48-50% for FY26
items.quote: Our cost to income ratio will continue to be in the range of 48% to 50% for financial year '26.

items.statement: Expects credit cost 0.2-0.25% for FY26
items.quote: And to answer your question for the credit cost for the year, we should be somewhere between 0.2 to 0.25.

items.statement: Targets PCR without TW 63-64% for FY26
items.quote: We could move to 63, 64 max because, you know, it's completely a secured business, whatever we are doing.

items.statement: MSME demand stable, no unusual patterns seen
items.quote: The market as of now is flat, I would say. So, when we meet the existing customers, some of the industries are doing well and some are looking flat.
Our NIM for 1QFY26 stood at 3.54%.

items.statement: Advances repricing impact INR135 cr, deposit repricing benefit INR64 cr, net INR71 cr impact
items.quote: My advances have brought down the yield by INR135 crores. My reduction in deposit rate has given me INR64 crores. This means I have INR135 crores on left side and INR64 crores of deposit on the right side, which is giving me a net impact of INR71 crores.

items.statement: Credit growth 16% YoY, advances INR54,020 cr
items.quote: For 1QFY26, we have achieved 16% credit growth, the highest credit growth in June-to-June and our advances have increased from INR46,548 crores to INR54,020 crores in Q1.

items.statement: Deposit growth 20% YoY, deposits INR65,734 cr
items.quote: Our deposits stood at INR65,734 crores for 1QFY26 as compared to INR54,857 crores in 1QFY25, registering a growth of 20%.

items.statement: Average CASA up 6% QoQ to INR16,478 cr
items.quote: The average CASA increased by 6% from INR15,057 crores in Q4 last year to INR16,478 crores in 1QFY26.

items.statement: GNPA 2.99%, NNPA 1.2%, both down sequentially for 9 quarters
items.quote: Our gross NPA percentage had reduced to 2.99% in 1QFY26. Both gross NPA and net NPA, in both percentage and absolute terms, is reducing quarter-by-quarter for the last nine quarters continuously.

items.statement: Slippages INR196 cr, recoveries INR187 cr, expects annual recoveries > slippages
items.quote: For the current quarter, the total slippages is around INR196 crores while the total recoveries is INR187 crores consisting of INR143 crores from live NPA accounts and INR44 crores from technically written-off accounts.

items.statement: SMA2 at 1.59% of advances vs 2.22% YoY
items.quote: Overall, our SMA2 to total advances stands at 1.59% in 1QFY26 as compared to 2.22% in the similar period last year.

items.statement: PCR without TW 61%, with TW 79%
items.quote: For 1QFY26, PCR without TW had improved to 61%, which had improved from 53% last year. Similarly, PCR with TW stood at 79% for Q1 FY '26, which has improved from 73% last year.

items.statement: Yield on advances 9.81%, cost of deposits 5.95%
items.quote: Our yield on advances stood at 9.81% for the current quarter as against 9.59% in 1QFY25. Our NIM for 1QFY26 stood at 3.54%.

items.statement: ROA 1.55%, PAT INR306 cr (first time >INR300 cr)
items.quote: As per the expectations we shared, the ROA is at our long-term average and stood at 1.55% in 1QFY26 compared to 1.51% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Plans 75-80 branch additions in FY26, 8-10 opened in Q2 so far
items.quote: On an average, we have been doing 75 branches per year, and we should continue this. And Q2, Q3 will be more. In fact, as we speak in Q2, we have opened quite a substantial branches in the first week. So, we have already done with, I think, 8-10 branches, and we will continue with that. And we will be around 75-80 branches for the year.

items.statement: Retail disbursements INR825 cr (HL, LAP, Affordable, Micro LAP), 80% branch-sourced
items.quote: We did around INR825 crores for the last quarter, combining all these three. And hence, our retail, whatever we have planned, is taken off well.

items.statement: Gold loan agri portfolio INR7,620 cr, flat QoQ due to seasonality
items.quote: With respect to gold loan book, our gold loan agricultural portfolio is INR76,198 million. If you see the presentation slide number 30, there are details.

items.statement: EBLR 48%, fixed 30%, MCLR 17% of loan book
items.quote: Our EBLR is currently at INR48, fixed is INR30 and MCLR is INR17. So, our EBLR is only 48% of my book as we speak today.

items.statement: Export exposure INR1,000-1,200 cr, 20% to US, mainly textiles
items.quote: So, we have around INR1,000 crores-INR1,200 crores in our total exports. And out of that, even if I take 20% and the margins, they are saying, when we did have a discussion in the morning with few of the seasoned guys and who does a decent export, their version is 2%-3% compression, nothing beyond that.

items.statement: No spike in asset quality stress seen despite industry concerns
items.quote: While we are hearing from multiple financial institutions about building stress in asset quality front, we are closely monitoring the situation and so far, we have not seen any sudden spike in the stress as of now.

items.statement: US tariff impact on textile clients: 2-3% margin compression, manageable
items.quote: Few of our customers are more Europe-oriented and out of my total exposure, only 20% of the customers seem to be with the US. And having said that, their profit margin should get compressed by 2%-3%. That's the number which they are saying on this tariff. So, nothing alarming.

items.statement: Director Shri N. Subramanian retired after 8 years tenure
items.quote: One of our directors, Shri N. Subramanian, had retired from the Board with effect from 19th June 2025 after completing 8 years tenure.

items.statement: AGM scheduled 13 Aug 2025 at Kumbakonam (physical + virtual)
items.quote: I hope all of you have received the notice of ensuring Annual General Meeting to be held on 13th August 2025, which will happen face-to-face at Kumbakonam after 6 years, along with the virtual mode as well.

items.statement: Management does not plan to give forward-looking guidance; aims for top-quartile growth among mid-tier peers
items.quote: In the past, we never gave guidance. I think last year was the first time we gave a guidance for 2 quarters because a variety of reasons. But I don't think we plan to give guidance, forward -looking guidance.

items.statement: Tailwinds from Healthcare, Life Sciences, BFSI, Data and AI; headwinds from Retail Manufacturing, two large clients' budget cuts, SITL IT/ITES softness
items.quote: The tailwind continues to be our large deal win and the tailwinds continue to be our growth in Health Care and Banking. But we also have headwinds much like with the industry. We are seeing continued pressure from Retail Manufacturing clients and also 2 of our large clients are under discretionary budget cut significantly.

items.statement: Q1 order bookings $105 million with 1.28 book-to-bill ratio; AI-led order booking grew significantly; AI pipeline ~$46 million
items.quote: Order bookings stood at $105 million, representing 1.28 book -to-bill ratio. We secured 3 large deals in Q1. The number of clients with more than $10 million annual run rate is now 7. AI-led order booking grew significantly from previous quarter. Our pipeline for AI is now nearly about $46 million in Q1.

items.statement: Additional loan of $35 million taken in Q1 to pay Quant earnout; cash and equivalents INR 600 crore vs INR 707 crore QoQ
items.quote: Quarter 1 '26, net cash balance stood at negative INR 62.5 crores. And we have also taken an additional loan of $35 million during this quarter for helping us to pay the Quant earnout.

items.statement: 7 new enterprise logos added; clients >$10M run rate increased to 7; top 10 client share 56% vs 61% QoQ; clients >$5M run rate increased to 13 from 11
items.quote: We have added 7 new customers in Q1. Top 10 clients contributed a revenue share of 56% this quarter, compared to 61% last quarter. Number of clients with more than $5 million run rate of revenue increased to 13 in Q1 '26 as against 11 in Q4 '25.

items.statement: Microsoft potential direct engagement risk for large SITL accounts; decision pending; mitigating via new AWS, Google, Oracle partnerships and security operations center scaling
items.quote: We have not yet got an update from them because this is a broad global decision for them. And in the implementation, we have not yet got the final decision from them. We may have impact for one of the largest customers in this year, but the decision is still pending.

items.statement: RBI issue resolved enabling fund movement between Sonata entities for growth investments
items.quote: I would like to update you on this RBI issue on which we were working for a long time: This issue has been resolved. This will now help us to move the money between the Sonata entities, helping us to gather the investment required for the growth of the business in the coming days.

items.statement: Net cash negative INR 62.5 crore; $35M loan taken for Quant earnout payment; final Quant earnout tranche paid
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 600 crores at the end of Q1 '26 against INR 707 crores in Q4. This temporary dip is due to final tranche payment of Quant earnout and also incremental loan repayment instalment in this quarter.

items.statement: Declared first interim dividend INR 1.25 per share; expects to pay quarterly interim dividends from this year
items.quote: Company has declared its first interim dividend of INR 1.25 per share and company expects to pay quarterly interim dividend from this year.

items.statement: LTM attrition 16%; gender diversity 31%; hired Head of Retail Manufacturing and Head of BFSI in US; 93.5% workforce AI-trained
items.quote: is at 16%. Our gender diversity remains strong at 31%. Despite challenging macroeconomic conditions, we remain committed to our future -focused talent investments and support our growth ambitions. We have continued to strengthen our sales leadership. We recently hired Head of Retail and Manufacturing vertical in the U.S. and also Head of BFSI vertical in the U.S. Upskilling through Sonata Universi

items.statement: Retail Manufacturing tariff uncertainty ongoing; two large clients (US BFSI, High-Tech) under budget pressure; Microsoft direct engagement risk for SITL; Quant earnout targets confidential
