items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin at 28.5% in Q1 FY26, up 935 bps YoY; management confident of staying north of 25% but not updating guidance yet
items.quote: The operating EBITDA margin stood at a solid 28.5%, a growth, of 935 basis points versus Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Strong order book across all three divisions; CDMO has solid order book for FY26 and calendar 2026 including Fermion label extension and EU major scale-up order
items.quote: Our CDMO division delivered good results last quarter. We have strong revenue visibility backed by robust order book for FY '26.

items.statement: HPP growth driven by increased demand and improved price realizations; refrigerant gas pricing landscape remains firm; R32 demand accelerating globally
items.quote: Growth of revenue in HPP segment is driven by both increased demand and improved price realizations. The pricing landscape for repression gases remains firm

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals to supply 3 new molecules in Q2 FY26; fluoro specialty project in Dahej launched Dec 2024 to contribute meaningfully this year; Chemours partnership for Opteon immersion cooling fluid underway
items.quote: In the Specialty Chemicals segment, we are set to deliver supplies for 3 new molecules in Q2 FY '26. Additionally, our fluoro specialty project in Dahej, which was launched in December '24 is expected to deliver a meaningful contribution this year. We have also announced a strategic partnership with Chemours to manufacture their pr oprietary product Opteon, a 2 -phase immersion cooling fluid

items.statement: Operating cash flows for Q1 FY26 at INR231 crores; net debt to equity at 0.34x pre-fund raise
items.quote: Operating cash flows for Q1 FY '26 is INR231 crores and net debt to equity stood at 0.34x prefund raise.

items.statement: Nectar project has firm order for remainder of year, ballpark INR300 crores; dedicated capacity at 100% utilization representing 50% of overall capacity; half PAR this year, full PAR by FY27
items.quote: Nectar, we have a firm order for the remainder period of the year. And absolutely, it will be ballpark in the number that you talked about, give or take some points here or there, right?

items.statement: Chemours project underway, detailed engineering progressing, commercial production targeted Q1 FY27; small capacity plant expected to reach optimum quickly
items.quote: The work is going on, projects is already underway. The teams are working together, detailed engineering is being progressed on that and we are on track for the first quarter of FY '27 is when we said we would start commercial production, that's when we will start.

items.statement: U.S. tariff exposure limited to ~20% of FY25 sales; refrigerant gases covered under ADD duty; too early to assess impact of new tariffs
items.quote: You've got to think of Navin in 2 ways that we are 20% of sales, fy25 basis, where are we exposed to the U.S. market directly. So in a sense, we've got an exposure to some of our refrigerant gases, which we are covered under ADD duty. So there is not much of an impact there.

items.statement: R32 pricing environment strong; management focuses on basket-level product placement for value across geographies; does not speculate on prices
items.quote: There is a strong demand tailwind here and the focus of the management is to ensure that on a basket level, you place the product in different geographies aligned with our strategic priorities so that overall realizations are better. But we don't second guess on pricing. It's too difficult to know.

items.statement: CDMO Phase 2 capex of INR128 crores to be triggered when capacity utilization hits 60%+; high probability for EU major product
items.quote: Our idea about the CDMO business is actually to make sure that whenever the capacity utilization of the plant hits 60% or more, it start triggering the cost for the next capex investment because you're always going to need that sort of headroom to continue to grow.

items.statement: Continuing to invest in people and capability across verticals to enhance technology platforms and manufacturing infrastructure
items.quote: We continue to invest in people and capability across all the verticals to further enhance our technology platforms and manufacturing infrastructure as we progress in the next p hase of growth

items.statement: CDMO sales have strong export bias; domestic sales sometimes reflect supplies to global customers' other service providers in India
items.quote: No, usually, our CDMO sales have always been with a very strong export bias. In between, we were supplying at the behest of our global customer to another service provider, another of their service provider in India.

items.statement: AHF merchant sales to start this year; solar and high-purity HF dependent on Buss ChemTech detailed engineering completion; focus on electronic over solar applications
items.quote: Merchant sales, some of that will start actually this year itself. Solar and high purity, let the Buss Chem work get done. We are currently in detailed engineering stage. When that sort of gets done and we start putting in more capex, obviously that will come. Our focus will be mainly in the electronic space as opposed to the solar space.

items.statement: Advanced materials incubation ongoing; active dialogues in electronic chemicals, semiconductors, data center applications; electronic-grade HF is stepping stone
items.quote: Absolutely, absolutely. There is a lot of work happening in that space. The exclusive arrangement we announced with BCT in the last quarter was a step in that direction. The Chemours advanced materials is also in the same direction. Additionally to that, there are several other conversations both in the semicon space as well as in the applications that are relevant for high-value environment like

items.statement: Expect modest growth in Radio business over remainder of FY26
items.quote: We remain optimistic about the coming quarters and expect a modest growth in the Radio business over the remainder of FY ‘26.

items.statement: Expect Gaana to break even early next year around similar time
items.quote: we believe early next year, similar time, we could be breaking even.

items.statement: Expect annual net subscription growth of about 25% for Gaana
items.quote: at an annual level, it is safe to say it could be about 25% level.

items.statement: Aim for Gaana plus events to reach 50-50 revenue split with Radio by year end
items.quote: I think it would be by year end, we should be looking at 50% - 50% if not less for Radio.

items.statement: Radio FCT revenue declined 12.1% YoY due to high base from election advertising and geopolitical headwinds
items.quote: The radio FCT advertising segment delivered subdued results during the quarter with a revenue of Rs. 66.1 crores, a decline of 12.1% year-on-year.

items.statement: Non-FCT segment grew 33% YoY with 43.4% EBITDA margin
items.quote: The non-FCT segment stood at Rs. 25.2 crores, reflecting a strong year-on-year growth of 33%, supported by a healthy EBITDA margin of 43.4%.

items.statement: Digital revenues grew 41.2% YoY to Rs. 21.7 crores, contributing 40.7% of total Radio revenues
items.quote: In this quarter, digital revenues stood at Rs. 21.7 crores, contributing almost a record 40.7% of total Radio revenues, up from last year of 24.8%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 3.6% YoY to Rs. 6.2 crores; EBITDA excluding digital at Rs. 16 crores with 17.5% margin
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs. 6.2 crores, registering a year -on-year growth of 3.6%, reflecting continuous focus on profitability. EBITDA excluding digital stands at Rs. 16 crores with a margin of 17.5%.

items.statement: Digital investments declined to Rs. 9.8 crores from Rs. 14.2 crores YoY, improving marketing and operational efficiency
items.quote: Notably, digital investments declined to Rs. 9.8 crores from the last year number s of Rs. 14.2 crores, in line with our guidance during the previous quarters about improving our marketing and operational efficiency.

items.statement: Target content cost at 60-65% of revenue for Gaana break-even
items.quote: Saying up to cost of content, we would expect to be at a good level at 65%, right now it is not. That would be our aim to get the content cost at about 60% to 65%.

items.statement: Event business requires no capex, is people-intensive with variable cost structure
items.quote: from a CAPEX point of view, there is no investment.

items.statement: Radio inventory utilization in 70-75% range
items.quote: It is in the range of 70-75%.

items.statement: Gaana pricing increased from Rs. 299 to Rs. 599; competitors priced higher giving headroom
items.quote: we increased the price from Rs. 299 to Entertainment Network ( Rs. 599, while competitors are a little higher. So, there is a little bit of headspace available

items.statement: Net subscription additions for Gaana increased ~25% QoQ
items.quote: our net ad ds increased by upwards of 25%.

items.statement: 65% of Gaana users from Tier II/III markets, leveraging Radio Mirchi's 63-market presence
items.quote: Just to give you a number, 65% of our users come from Tier II, Tier III markets.

items.statement: Several music streaming rivals shut down (Wynk, Hungama, Resso); paid subscription model seen as only viable path
items.quote: has closed down, Hungama has closed down, Resso has closed down. So, there are very less players now. At one point in time, there were nine music streaming services. And it has been now very clearly seen that if you run only a free service, it is not a viable business

items.statement: Radio Mirchi maintains 25.4% volume share in Radio FCT segment, better positioned than peers
items.quote: we continue to be better positioned than many of our peers with a strong 25.4% volume share in the Radio FCT segment.

items.statement: Radio effective rates (ERs) remain ~25% below pre-COVID levels
items.quote: The ERs still are subdued to pre-COVID level. It is about 25% lower than the pre-COVID levels.

items.statement: Cash balance of Rs. 336 crores as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: The company continues to maintain a robust balance sheet with a cash balance of Rs. 336 crores as of June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Consistent dividend payer, increased dividends over last two years including during COVID
items.quote: we have been very consistent on dividend, even during COVID times also, we have been increasing and though margin increased, but over the last two years, you would have seen we have been very consistent on dividend and have increased that.

items.statement: Evaluating new businesses and acquisition opportunities but nothing material currently
items.quote: We keep evaluating, we keep discussing, but there is nothing material right now.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation caused event cancellations in Q1, impacting event business growth
items.quote: I would have loved more growth had the geopolitical situation not happ ened where we had to cancel a lot of events.

items.statement: Event business margins may face pressure as more players enter the growing experiential market
items.quote: when you see a lot of tailwinds in any industry, a lot of players get into it. So, in a shorter period, there could be some pressure on margins also because a lot of people would want to just take some business from you by quoting a lower margin.

items.statement: Credit cost expected below 40 bps for upcoming quarters
items.quote: On the credit cost, what will the future look like? The future, it will neither be 60% nor will it be within the 45 basis point to 55 basis point, we expect it to be below 40 basis point.

items.statement: Loan and deposit growth to continue at ~20% YoY
items.quote: See, the last four quarters we have been growing by what you have seen and that is the reason why it should not be any less than that, both on the deposit side and the loan side.

items.statement: NIM fell 9 bps QoQ despite 100 bps repo rate cuts; cost of fund management ongoing
items.quote: Despite the three rate cuts across this year financial year, adding up to 100 basis points reduction, our NIM reduction over Q4 was 9 basis points.

items.statement: 100% provision taken on MFI and unsecured DA NPA stock as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: The entire NPA stock of March 31, 2025, of MFI and unsecured DA has been 100% provided in Q1.

items.statement: Slippage ratio rose to 4.6%; non-gold slippage 3.1%; small-ticket secured DA (Rs 2-6 lakh) surprised with higher NPA flow
items.quote: Our slippage ratio has creeped up. This is on account of three items, two of which were obvious. And one which was kind of surprising. There has been a higher slippage on MFI and unsecured DA, both of which we were aware of and that is not a surprise. What really was a surprise was the small ticket secured DAs that we have taken, have taken a higher-than-normal flow into NPA.

items.statement: Co-lending book capped at 15% of total book; Q1 focused on short-term fixed-rate loans
items.quote: So, on co-lending, the co-lending book will be 15% of the bank's book, that we are very clear on. What we have done in Q1 is clearly to focus on shorter-term loans, fixed rate loans.

items.statement: IBPC of ~Rs 1,500 cr executed in Q1 to manage NIM; will return at tenor end
items.quote: There you can see that we have done IBPC of close to Rs. 1,500 crores. So, had we not done the IBPC, you probably would have seen an asset growth in excess of 25%, 26%.

items.statement: LAP share in mortgage book increasing month-on-month
items.quote: Why do we think that the 3 repo rate cuts is resulting only in a 9 bps reduction? A lot of it has got to do with caution deposit. A whole lot of it has got to do with the kind of assets that we have put in. Also, it has got to do with the product mix also, so there is quite a lot of LAP in this

items.statement: Repo rate transmission done as per regulatory norms (quarterly reset)
items.quote: It is a standard policy. There are four calendar quarters, and based on which we pass it on. Pass it on or hike it up depending upon how the rate movement is.

items.statement: Headcount reduced by ~800 YoY while growing 20%; front-end LOS modernized and mobilized
items.quote: Clearly between last year and now, we have reduced our headcount by about 800 odd people. And we have been growing by 20%. So, effectively that is resulting in higher productivity. Plus, there are a lot of technology gains, etc. So, our front-end LOS systems across multiple products have not only been modernized, but also been made into mobile.

items.statement: No immediate capital raise; Tier-1 rose 20 bps despite 21% asset growth; will raise when market price reflects value
items.quote: In the last one year, we have grown 21% assets. And our Tier 1 has increased by 20 bps. Are you with me? Chetan Ginjodia: Right. Praveen Kutty: So, we are super stingy when it comes to cost and when it comes to capital, right . But having said that, our ambition, our hunger, our growth ambition is far higher. At some point in time, we will need to get capital. What we are hoping for is, one is to

items.statement: MFI industry pain expected to continue for 2-3 quarters; PAR 90 at 6.2% still high
items.quote: My personal opinion is that the pain in microfinance will continue. It will take at least two, three quarters. Just because overall at the industry level from 6.8 it has come down to 6.2. 6.2 itself is a big number. So, I do not know. I do not have very positive view on the microfinance industry at this point in time.

items.statement: Core fee income grew 17.5% YoY to Rs 124 cr; Q1 seasonally lower due to lower disbursements and third-party distribution
items.quote: Our fee of Rs. 236 crores is again the highest ever. Of course, it had some one-timers, but what is of equal interest is that the core fee income has registered Rs. 124 crores, a 17.5% increase from the previous Q1.

items.statement: Top 20% deposit concentration kept well below 7%
items.quote: And we still are growing the liability book by 20% and we still are keeping the top 20% well below 7%.

items.statement: Targets NIM of 3.2% on average assets, fee income of 1.1% for full year, cost-to-average-assets of 2.50%, and credit cost of 45 bps to achieve ~1% ROA
items.quote: We closed NIM at 2.99% on average assets, so that is why there is a difference, right, 2.99%. I expect that to be 3.2%, okay? Fee would be, in our opinion, there will be, the one-offs will go away at some point in time. So, over the full-year, probably a 1.1% is a right number to go with.

items.statement: Expects to hire 600-700+ employees across assets and liabilities, including for new branches, but headcount unlikely to cross 11,910 this year or next
items.quote: So, maybe about 600, 700 or more people we can expect to see being hired in the company. They will be across assets and liabilities. Some of them will be for the new branches that we are opening.

items.statement: Plans to add 20-25 branches in FY26, closing at 485-490 branches; growth to be driven by more people in existing branches rather than new branches
items.quote: But having said that, we expect another 25 odd branches to come in this year. Ideal number would have been 35, so that we can close the year at 500 branches. But I would tend to think that we would be closing around somewhere around 485 to 490 branches this year.

items.statement: Gold loan gross NPA increased Rs 8 crore QoQ to Rs 35 crore; slippages and recoveries both high due to auction threat; unsecured DA and MFI recoveries weaker
items.quote: There is a slippage in that segment and the repayment happens at the threat of auction, which is why the repayments are coming through and your net NPA is the way currently it is.

items.statement: Recovery as % of fresh slippages fell to 70% in Q1; focus in Q2 is to reduce fresh slippages and improve recovery ratio
items.quote: And the second is, for the first time in many, many quarters we saw the recovery as a percentage of the fresh slippage going down to 70%. That is not something which we quite like.

items.statement: Full impact of RBI's three rate cuts (25+25+50 bps) not yet seen; NIM impact will be visible in Q2 and fully in Q3; deposit repricing benefit will accrue over 15 months as term deposits mature
items.quote: So, the full impact of the NIM, I do not think is seen in the industry yet, but in Q2. Definitely in Q3 you will get to know the real impact of the rate cut and its impact on the yield and advances.

items.statement: Consciously front-loaded short-term and fixed-rate loans in Q1 ahead of rate cuts; mortgage disbursements lower YoY but expected to pick up from Q2; LAP share in new sourcing rising for 3-4 quarters
items.quote: In April you do a 15-year mortgage, right, and then there is a known rate cut of 25 bps happening and another 50 bps happening in the shape, in the nearby future. Even if it is a semi-fixed loan, two years later, 75 bps will get reduced.

items.statement: Co-lending book to be 15% or less of total assets by year-end; 85% organic; organic growth significantly higher than co-lending growth
items.quote: Our co-lending book, at the end of the year, will be 15% or less of the total asset book. So, 85% will be non-co-lending, normal organic kind of book.

items.statement: Strategic shift to become full financial solution provider for self-employed customers (surplus, deficit, protection, trade finance) rather than product-centric; mindset change is top priority
items.quote: I think it is high time that we change the way we did business in our bank to becoming a full-financial solution provider for the self-employed customer, which will cover his surplus needs, you can read it as CA/SA. His deficit needs, you can read it as overdraft facility. His protection needs, you can call it TPD. His trade finance need, exactly trade finance.

items.statement: Frontline headcount reduced by cutting non-producers; new AI/ML-based hiring process improves selection; expects headcount to rise but stay below 11,910
items.quote: The fall in employees primarily on the frontline and the way you should look at it is that, I mean, I consider them a wrong hire, we should not have hired them in the first place. So, effectively, these are non-producers which we take time in understanding.

items.statement: Cost of deposits reduction is key lever; believes bank can grow 20% without premium pricing; CASA not a true indicator of low-cost funds, SA includes large ticket term deposit equivalents
items.quote: I think the bank has matured enough to attract and acquire liabilities without having to be the highest or one of the highest interest rate provider in the industry. We have reached that level of maturity is my belief.

items.statement: Promoter (Aga Khan Fund) capital infusion pending RBI approval; process restarted after Aga Khan IV demise and succession; expects approval and funds before September results call
items.quote: We had to redo the entire process, we completed the full set of activity, now the ball is in the Reserve Bank's court, they are expecting approval to come in. Hopefully, before our next conference call of September results, we should not only have the approval but also have the moneys in hand.

items.statement: Construction finance book comfortable with NPA and DCCO levels; peak exposure Rs 10-12 cr; targets 30% growth; expertise built over 6-7 years through two credit cycles
items.quote: Would be happy to even to get the book to grow by, let us say, 30% odd. It is something which we are reasonably comfortable with.

items.statement: November 12 RBI circular cited as reason for slippage discipline issues in gold loans; customers from Muthoot/Manappuram/IIFL used to bullet repayment, not regular interest servicing
items.quote: And a lot of the reason why we will have a problem in the slippages is because of the famous November 12 circular.

items.statement: Paper elimination is second priority; views paper as cost, turnaround time issue, and handoff risk; aims to eradicate paper from bank operations
items.quote: And I am frankly allergic to paper. I believe paper is a cost for offsetters, turnaround time issues, hands-offs, cost. Paper is a sin. And I want to eradicate paper from our bank.

items.statement: Corporate loan disbursement Rs 1,200 cr in Q1 but book grew only Rs 200 cr; short-tenor tactical lending to retain pricing power at repricing
items.value: Disbursement Rs 1,200 cr, book growth Rs 200 cr
items.quote: You will see that corporate loans, Rs. 1,200 crores of disbursal has happened. You may wonder, we are not very effusive in terms of corporate, we always say it will be about 10% of the asset book, etc. That is what you always get, 10%. But the fact is Rs. 1,200 crores in one quarter, look at the growth. It is a Rs. 200 crores growth.

items.statement: Term deposit sweet spot 15-24 months; ~Rs 3,000 cr matures monthly for repricing at lower rates; full benefit of liability repricing to accrue over 15 months assuming no further rate cuts
items.quote: 45,000 divided by 15 months is 3,000, right? 3,000 will come up for renewal this month, 3,000 will come for renewal next month. Likewise, for the next 15 months, 3,000 will come up for renewal, theoretically speaking.

items.statement: Branch expansion not critical for growth; deposits mostly from top 10-12 cities and digital; ULI and digitized land records in 7 states reduce need for physical branches
items.quote: Anyway, most of the deposits come from the 10, 12 top cities. And most of it is digital. So, why you need new branches if you want to go to newer cities?

items.statement: Gold loan customers from Muthoot, Manappuram, IIFL accustomed to bullet repayment; struggle with regular interest servicing causing slippages
items.quote: most of our customers come from the Muthoot’s and the Manappuram’s and the IIFL’s, where they are looking at bullet loans which they repay, supposedly, in nine to 12 months. And then they come here, where inter est servicing has to happen quite regularly, which is not something that they are quite used to

items.statement: SME book stagnant; hired head for Rs 3-10 cr segment to fill gap between MSME and corporate; rolling out OD facilities to 100k+ mortgage customers; expects this to exceed mortgage book in 5-10 years
items.quote: Over a five year-time frame, that will be bigger than the mortgage book that we currently have. It is a huge preposition, it will take its own time, and if you were to take a 10-year view of the bank, this would be the game changer for the bank.

items.statement: PSLC income unlikely for rest of FY26 or FY27; small/marginal farmer PSLC has demand but bank not in surplus; growing MFI for PSLC not preferred
items.quote: Do you want to grow your microfinance book at this point in time for that opportunity? Perhaps not. So, if you were to ask in the short-term, are we going to get some PSLC income? Do not think so for the rest of the year or even for the next year.

items.statement: Promoter infusion will take holding above 15% for first time in ~20 years; symbolic milestone
items.quote: It is a small number, but it is a good symbolic thing to happen because it will be the first time in close to 20-odd years that the promoter is infusing money. And secondly, it probably will take the promoter contribution to above 15%, both of which are symbolically a big thing.

items.statement: Operating profit target 2.3-2.5% and PAT above 1.3% for the year
items.quote: Our objective, we have set out -- I mean, set out clearly and have also called it out. We would want to maintain our operating profit between 2.3% to 2.5%, and PAT above 1.3%.

items.statement: Gross margin fell 60 bps YoY to 5.1% due to PayNet divestment, Arena provisions, and TSG large deals plus market pressure
items.quote: if you see between Q1 of last year to Q1 of this year, there is about 60 bps of drop, which was about 5.7%. Now it's about 5.1%.

items.statement: TSG large deals and vendor margin pressure caused 35-40 bps gross margin drop; large deals expected to continue
items.quote: The balance, which is about between 35 to 40 bps is primarily on account of TSG business. That's where the large deals, I mean, it actually comes into play.

items.statement: Mobility Solutions grew 44% YoY on strong premium segment demand in India and Middle East
items.quote: The Mobility Solutions Group led with a stellar performance this quarter at 44% growth and demand on the premium segment of the market across India and Middle East was strong.

items.statement: Cloud Solutions grew 41% YoY driven by hyperscaler business and AI-enabled digital transformation
items.quote: Cloud Solutions continued its momentum, as you've seen over the last few quarters with 41% top line growth and continued success in the hyperscaler business, and we continue to take advantage of the cloud transition and digital transformation enabled by AI.

items.statement: Technology Solutions grew 21% YoY with big deals in India and UAE but margins declined due to mix and market pressure
items.quote: The Technology Solutions Group performed well on top line this quarter at 21%. There were a lot of big deals in India and UAE, though margins declined due to a combination of mix of larger deals as well as general margin stress in the technology solutions space.

items.statement: Software Solutions now ~15% of business, growing ~25% with gross margins 5.5-6%
items.quote: the software solutions piece of the business is about -- roughly 15%of our business, and it's growing at 25% right now. And this quarter grew at 24% as well. So that part of the business delivers a gross margin close to 6%.

items.statement: Closing working capital improved to 37 days, down 2 days YoY; gross debt/equity 0.36x, net debt/equity 0.23x
items.quote: Continued efforts on efficient management of working capital resulted in 37 days closing working capital, which is 2 days lower than the previous year Q1.

items.statement: Factoring plus interest cost fell 18% YoY to INR122 cr; Arena factoring+interest down to INR69 cr from INR90 cr
items.quote: Overall, for last year, factoring plus interest together, it was INR148 crores, which is now in the current quarter is down to INR122 crores.

items.statement: Blended interest cost varies by market; outside Arena it ranges 6-7.5%
items.quote: in the rest of the markets, maybe -- I should say it varies between 6% to 7.5%.

items.statement: No capital infusion planned for Arena; net carrying value of investment ~$30m vs market value ~$40-45m
items.quote: No capital infusion. We haven't invested -- I mean we haven't put any capital. We haven't made any commitment in Arena post our acquisition way back in 2010.

items.statement: Arena took $8m+ one-time provision due to rising concordat cases in Turkey; $20m delayed collections, $8m provided
items.quote: had accordingly done about $8 plus million of provision in Arena, which we think is onetime, and we should be able to manage as we speak now, the rest of the ARs that need to get collected

items.statement: Turkey outlook uncertain; recalibrating strategy, tightening working capital, reducing TRY exposure
items.quote: Our subsidiary, Arena is recalibrating our approach to the business in Turkey and taking proactive steps to manage the business cautiously by tightening working capital, managing overdue credit limits closely and reducing our Turkish lira exposure.

items.statement: Large data center/AI deals are private sector only, in India and UAE; ROCE threshold maintained
items.quote: These deals are happening both in India and in UAE. We don't have a practice of calling out specific deals, but we see an increased number of deals both for data centers as well as the AI space.

items.statement: Vendors restricting margins in TSG; global players pressured on pricing due to local competition in servers
items.quote: vendors also have restricted margins. So all said and done, if there are less margin that we can get in the marketplace, we always go back to the vendor equip with him and then get whatever that we can get from them.

items.statement: Q1 operating profit 2.09% vs historical avg 2.06%; PAT 1.32% vs avg 1.16% (ex-COVID)
items.quote: the operating profit average, pre and post, is about 2.06%, and we are at 2.09%, better than that. The PAT percentage is 1.16%, I mean, pre and post, and we are at about 1.32%.

items.statement: Created Software Solutions Group combining security, SaaS (infra & app), and hyperscaler; multiyear journey
items.quote: With the creation of Software Solutions Group, the focus and investment towards creating additional value add for brands and ecosystems should pave the way for faster growth, though this will be a multiyear journey.

items.statement: Opex grew 6% YoY (ex-AR provisions) vs 22% revenue growth, delivering operating leverage
items.quote: Opex control continues to be good and grew much slower than the revenue growth at 6%, giving us good operating leverage.

items.statement: AR provisions spiked to 0.39% of revenue (normally ~10 bps) mainly due to Arena; opex incl AR grew 19% YoY
items.quote: Our AR provision is about 0.39% this quarter. Normally, it's about 10 bps.

items.statement: Q2 outlook positive with new product introductions in mobility, Technology Solutions and Software Solutions building
items.quote: We are confident as we go forward in Q2, we do see the NPIs in mobility, as well as the Technology Solutions and the Software Solutions business building out a decent quarter for us.

items.statement: India revenue grew 24%, UAE 35%, KSA 32%, rest of Middle East 18%, Africa stable
items.quote: From a geography perspective, the revenue growth was contributed by strong growth in many geographies. India at 24%, UAE at 35%, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia at 32%, rest of Middle East at 18% and Africa was stable.

items.statement: TSG competition intensifying across markets from global and local server players; cloud data center and on-prem both competitive
items.quote: the intensity of competition is going up for both cloud data centers, on-prem with a variety of different players jumping into the mix.

items.statement: Recognized as most trusted company in technology distribution by VARINDIA
items.quote: This year, Redington was recognized as the most trusted company in the technology distribution sector by VARINDIA.

items.statement: Full-year disbursement target of INR4,000 crores maintained; Q1 shortfall to be covered by September
items.quote: The plan for the full year is around INR4,000 crores of disbursement. And at this point of time, we are confident that we'll be able to achieve it.

items.statement: Q2 disbursement target of INR1,000-1,200 crores to make up Q1 shortfall
items.quote: We are targeting something around INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores in Q2.

items.statement: Quarter-on-quarter AUM growth guidance of 7-9% maintained despite Q1 moderation
items.quote: We still hold on to that guidance. The only thing which we would like to ask from each of you is a little bit of patience because we are a small organization.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 reduced from 15% to 10.22%; Net Stage 3 from 6.56% to 4.13% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our Gross Stage 3, there is a lot of improvement, from 15% Gross Stage 3, it has reduced to 10.22%. Our Net Stage 3 reduced from 6.56% to 4.13% in the current quarter.

items.statement: 38% of Gross Stage 3 resolved in Q1; another 30% in advanced resolution stages
items.quote: There have been visible results on the steps taken towards resolving the legacy issue with 38% of our Gross Stage 3 resolved in Q1 FY '26. Now on the remaining Gross Stage 3, another 30% is in advanced stages of resolution.

items.statement: NSL resolved with INR125 crores recovery; Vento INR115 crores (INR20 crores received, balance by August); IL&FS upgraded to Standard
items.quote: NSL- the NCLT gave its verdict and we got the entire amount, INR125 crores back, the winning bidder has paid it towards a successful resolution.

items.statement: Q1 disbursements of INR138 crores entirely to private sector vs INR296 crores in full FY25
items.quote: The total disbursement which we gave in the first quarter is INR138 crores. Compared to the fourth quarter, which was only INR50 crores, it was a significant increase.

items.statement: INR1,200-1,300 crores proposals evaluated in Q1; INR600 crores sanctioned in July; INR1,000+ crores pipeline for August
items.quote: We have evaluated significant number of proposals, i.e., around INR1,200-1,300 crores of proposals in the first quarter. And quite a few of these cases were approved in the second quarter, in July.

items.statement: July sanctions of INR600 crores; pipeline of over INR1,000 crores at various sanction stages for August
items.quote: During the month of July, already, we have sanctioned something around INR600 crores of loans proposals and proposals amounting to maybe a little more than INR1,000 crores are already in pipeline at different stages of sanction and due diligence processes.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing reduced from 9.69% to 9.67% in Q1; targeting further reduction via spread compression and ECB diversification
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing has also reduced from 9.69% to 9.67%, and we have been taking up with all the lenders, existing lenders as well as we have been taking up with the other lender as well to improve our borrowing and reduce the cost of borrowings.

items.statement: Return on assets improved from 4.02% to 9.77% on annual basis
items.quote: Our return on assets, has also improved on an annual basis from 4.02% to 9.77%.

items.statement: IT initiatives underway including new CIO onboarding; technology investment to strengthen systems and processes
items.quote: We are also undertaking a few significant IT initiatives. With all this, we are internally geared up to meet the increased business requirements coming from sourcing.

items.statement: Leadership team strengthened with Director-Operations, SME Head, CIO hires; junior credit/risk team augmentation planned
items.quote: Now the way forward would be how do we augment the team capacity at the junior level, especially in the area of credit and risk so that our ability to process higher quantum of cases is manifested.

items.statement: Target turnaround time from inquiry to disbursement of 30 days vs current 1-1.5 months; larger peers at 3.5 months
items.quote: Our target is -- right from inquiry to disbursement should be finished within 30 days' time.

items.statement: Average disbursement ticket size ~INR35 crores in Q1; targeting INR40-70 crores for newer segments and INR120-150 crores for core infrastructure
items.quote: In this effort, the average disbursement ticket size has been around INR35 crores in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Focus on private sector disbursements, repeat clients returning, group-level borrowings, sector-specific structuring
items.quote: Repeat clients are actually coming back to PFS and sector specific structuring and servicing capabilities are being ramped up to cater the different segments of our customer base.

items.statement: Differentiation via speed (1-1.5 months vs 3.5 months for large peers), smaller ticket sizes, niche segments, structuring/servicing capability
items.quote: Whereas we are delivering in 1- 1.5 months' time, though our ticket size is lower, and we are expecting this to improve even more.

items.statement: INR1,500 crores liquidity available; advanced discussions with existing/new/overseas lenders for fresh sanctions expected in Q2
items.quote: As of now, we have a sufficient liquidity in the system. Close to INR1,500 crores, we have a liquidity.

items.statement: Scheduled repayments of INR553 crores in Q1; full-year scheduled/unscheduled repayments and prepayments expected at INR1,000-1,500 crores
items.quote: So, we expect -- we have said something around INR1,000 - INR1,500 crores prepayments and repayments; scheduled and unscheduled both by the end of this year.

items.statement: Preferential share issuance of INR300-500 crores planned for the year; Board seized of matter, timing dependent on business traction
items.quote: I would just want to caution you that such activity was planned for the course of this year. As and when the time is right, we will take the necessary decision.

items.statement: Rating agency review due August-September; upgrade expected given improved intrinsic health, cleaned surround effects, but external volatility remains
items.quote: Rating agencies that is due in the August, September. So, we have been informing or giving all the updates to the rating agencies. And we are expecting that when this renewal is due in August and September, so things should be in the improvement side.

items.statement: Key hires: Sanjeev Kumar (Director-Operations, 30 yrs exp), Avijit Kishore (SME Head), Sidhartha Dutta (CIO); middle management assessment centers conducted
items.quote: We have got Sanjeev, who joined us as Director-Operations. Apart from coming at the leadership level, he comes with immense experience in the infrastructure space.

items.statement: Small base means 8-12 cases per quarter; few cases can cause quarterly volatility; longer horizon needed for trend evaluation
items.quote: What I would like to caution, since our base is small, the number of cases which we will be sanctioning and disbursing per quarter would be around 8 to 12 cases on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: PAT improved from INR58 crores to INR137 crores QoQ; total income declined from INR155 crores to INR142 crores due to AUM reduction
items.quote: PAT is at INR137 crores. It's an improvement from the previous quarter, i.e, from INR58 crores to INR137 crores.

items.statement: Board will reassess cash distribution decision by end of FY26
items.quote: The Board will continue to monitor the evolving situation closely and reassess its decisio n by the end of financial year

items.statement: Board decided to conserve cash in short term, delaying distributions
items.quote: The Board, based on recommendation of the committee, has decided to conserve cash in the short term.

items.statement: Strong order book visibility supports robust tower additions for FY26
items.quote: We have a visibility on our order book today. And based on the order book availability today across all the customers, we believe the tower additions will continue to be very strong for Indus even in this particular financial year.

items.statement: Capex elevated due to growth, replacement, and tower strengthening
items.quote: The capex, to be honest, I think capex is a factor of multiple things. It's a factor of what we are spending on growth, what we are spending in replacement, what we are looking at an aging infrastructure in terms of deployment, in terms of making sure the towers are strengthened and have a robust setup.

items.statement: Maintenance capex spike due to tower strengthening and lithium-ion battery transition
items.quote: I think the important point to note is, obviously, we have an aging portfolio. And there are basically years when we will see a lot of focus on tower strengthening, maintenance etcetera.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin 54.5% in Q1 FY26, down 7.1 pp YoY and 2.4 pp QoQ
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was lower by 7.1 percentage points year-on-year and 2.4 percentage points quarter-on-quarter at 54.5% in Q1.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA grew 13.6% YoY and 0.6% QoQ excluding write-backs and acquisition accounting
items.quote: Adjusted for the write-backs and common control accounting impact of the acquisition, our EBITDA grew 13.6% year-on-year and 0.6% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Energy margins at -4% in Q1 FY26, improved from -5.5% YoY but impacted by early monsoon
items.quote: Our energy margins were at -4% in Q1 compared to -5.2% in Q4 and -5.5% in Q1 of the last financial year.

items.statement: Added 2,468 macro towers and 5,777 co-locations in Q1 FY26, up 11.4% and 9.7% YoY
items.quote: We added 2,468 macro towers and 5,777 corresponding co -locations during the quarte r, translating into year-on-year growth of 11.4% and 9.7%, respectively

items.statement: Incremental tenancy ratio of 2.3x, portfolio tenancy ratio stable at 1.63x
items.quote: Given the incremental tenancy ratio of 2.3, our portfolio tenancy ratio remained stable at 1.63 after many quarters.

items.statement: Solar site count over 32,000 with 2,250 added in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our solar site count as on 30 th June 2025 stood at over 32,000 , with approx. 2,250 sites added during the quarter

items.statement: Diesel consumption up 10% YoY in Q1 FY26 due to early monsoon disruptions
items.quote: This contributed to an unusually high number of weather-related disturbances in the form of heavy rainfall and thunderstorms among others, leading to a 10% year-on-year increase in our diesel consumption in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Free cash flow INR 15.7 billion in Q1 FY26, trade receivables reduced by INR 4 billion
items.quote: Our free cash flow generation remained strong at INR15.7 billion in Q1, driven by sustained business momentum and the collection of overdue receivables, which also resulted in a reduction of INR 4 billion in trade receivables during the quarter.

items.statement: No aversion to increasing debt when required, cash preservation driving current reduction
items.quote: There is absolutely no attitude of having any averseness to increasing our debt as and when required.

items.statement: Focus on tower industry consolidation opportunities, acquired Airtel towers in Q4 FY25
items.quote: we started some bit of consolidation when we took Airtel Towers in the last quarter. And hence, any other opportunities that are there to consolidate the towers, we'll b e considering during the course of the year

items.statement: RoW rules 2024 adopted by 31 states/UTs, Green Energy Open Access policy notified in 28 states
items.quote: The R oW rules 2024 have now been adopted by nearly 31 states and union territories. The Green Energy Open Access policy has now been notified in 28 states, marking steady progress towards encouraging the ongoing transition to cleaner sources of energy

items.statement: IBS deployments highest ever in Q1, proactive acquisition model for built-to-suit solutions
items.quote: Like the previous few quarters, our IBS deployments in Q1 were the highest ever in our history, which included building sites for Government, institutional and enterprise bodies, thereby expanding our reach.

items.statement: Gender diversity improved to 15.7% in Q1 FY26 from 11.2% YoY, launched safety campaign 'Sankalp'
items.quote: We continue to make efforts to improve the representation of women in our workforce with our gender diversity standing at 15.7% at the end of Q1 compared to 11.2% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Network uptime 99.96% in Q1 FY26 despite severe weather disruptions
items.quote: Despite this, we were able to deliver a high level of uptime of 99.96% in Q1 FY26, largely due to the resilience and commitment of our teams on the ground.

items.statement: 5G base stations at ~487,000, India 5G subscriptions at 245 million by March 2025
items.quote: On the 5G front, the total 5G base stations increased marginally to around 487,000.

items.statement: Rental framework unchanged for 2-3 years, most portfolio renewed, renewals win-win with small decrease
items.quote: The framework that we had agreed 2 or 3 years back, I think we are still sort of working on the same framework. So there's no incremental impact of any renewal.

items.statement: Energy margin reconciliation issues structural, smart meter deployment underway with DISCOMs
items.quote: One effort that is currently ongoing and which we are working with the different DISCOMs is how we can get smart meters installed at our sites. What the smart meters do, they provide you the accurate billing that is reflected on that site.

items.statement: AI and automation being embraced across operations for efficiency and insight-led decisions
items.quote: At Indus Towers, we recognize this shift and are actively embracing AI, automation and digital tools across our operations to drive greater efficiency, agility and insight-led decision-making.

items.statement: Targets double-digit volume growth for full FY26
items.quote: For even the rest of the year, we should see some growth coming in. We're still targeting a double-digit growth for the entire year.

items.statement: Expects rail EBITDA per TEU to recover to INR9,500 in coming quarters
items.quote: So, there is scope to increase double stacking. Possibly, we'll go back to INR9,500 in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Rail EBITDA per TEU was INR9,100 in Q1 FY26, slightly down due to higher empty running and lower double stacking
items.quote: The business remains stable where our EBITDA per TEU for the Rail business was around INR9,100 per TEU, slightly down due to the higher empty and underframe running, lower double stacking and increased imbalance due to lack of exports.

items.statement: CFS EBITDA per TEU around INR1,500 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our CFS business sees some improvement with an EBITDA per TEU around INR1,500.

items.statement: Expects margin improvement going forward as imbalance improves
items.quote: But then this quarter had more underframe and empty running. So, we do expect some improvement in margin going forward, as the overall imbalance also improves.

items.statement: General cost increases in manpower, minimum wage and fuel continue yearly
items.quote: These are general increases. Yearly, there is manpower and minimum wage and fuel increases. The hikes keep happening. So it's part of that only.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing achieved 5-7% price hikes from most customers in Q1
items.quote: Price increase. So price increase, I mean, it's in the range of 5% to 7% in general. Looking at segment to segment, it varies, but that's in general what is coming at present.

items.statement: Evaluating shift from opex to capex model for solar; self-invested solar cost ~INR2-2.5 vs grid INR4.5
items.quote: But now going forward, we're evaluating, doing it ourselves where we invest in the solar and then it will be about INR2 or INR2.5 compared to something in the average is about INR4.5 right now.

items.statement: EV capex nearly double but opex one-third to one-fourth; also evaluating LNG vehicles; running 65-70 CNG vehicles
items.quote: Then we're also looking at electric vehicles for movement. That will also -- it's about -- the capex is almost double, but the opex is about one third, one fourth . So, there are savings there also. Other than this, we're also looking at LNG vehicles. So, that's also in similar lines to EV. We're already running CNG vehicles. We have about 65 vehicles -- 65, 70 vehicles.

items.statement: Snowman adding capacity in Calcutta, Krishnapatnam, Kundli (NCR); plans more own and asset-light capacity; expanding 5PL vertical
items.quote: Snowman continues to maintain its position as the market leader and as it adds further capacity in Calcutta, Krishnapatnam and Kundli in NCR, we have plans to add more capacity in both own and light asset model and continue our expansion in the 5PLvertical as well.

items.statement: Snowman onboarded Calcutta and Krishnapatnam facilities; Kundli asset-light warehouse starts August; more in pipeline
items.quote: We just onboarded our two facilities, which is Calcutta and Krishnapatnam. They will definitely be adding revenues, plus we have taken a warehouse on asset-light model in Kundli, which will also start contributing from the month of August. And then a couple of them are in pipeline as well in new locations.

items.statement: Snowman expects utilization increase of ~7,000-10,000 pallets from new warehouses this quarter
items.quote: I mean, if I say for the quarter, just an estimate, maybe we'll have a utilization percentage increase by approximately 7,000 to 10,000 pallets.

items.statement: Gateway capex ~INR30 cr/year excluding new terminals; INR150 cr avg per new terminal; INR300 cr earmarked for two terminals; Jaipur balance INR60-70 cr
items.quote: The capex plans remain the same. Basically, we are looking at about INR30 crores of capex per year. This is not counting any new terminals. As and when a new terminal comes in, that will be at an average of about INR150 crores per terminal. So, we've earmarked INR300 crores for two terminals. And then the balance works from Jaipur, whenever that comes in will be about INR60 crores, INR70 crores.

items.statement: Snowman plans ~INR100 cr/year for own facilities plus 3-4 asset-light facilities in 2 years, 5-6 in 3 years
items.quote: So, I mean, our plan is to continue to spend something around INR100 crores from our investments into our own facilities and then build couple of asset-light models alongside. So, maybe 3 to 4 facilities in next 2 years and in next 3 years, probably 5 to 6 facilities is what is on the horizon right now.

items.statement: Double stacking at 39% in Q1, down due to lack of exports and trade realignment toward Mundra
items.quote: So it's 39%, and it's basically declined due to lack of exports. There's also realignment of trade. Certain volumes have increased towards Mundra rather than Pipavav, which is further increasing their balance.

items.statement: Q1 volumes stable at Q4 levels despite seasonality; expects growth in remaining quarters
items.quote: Generally, Q1 is weaker. I know last year was weak because of the Red Sea more than so. But for Q1, even to stay at the same level that we did for Q4, it's a good achievement. For even the rest of the year, we should see some growth coming in.

items.statement: Domestic container volumes ~600-700 TEUs/month; expanding domestic segment with new containers
items.quote: We've already Gateway Distriparks Limited & crossed about, say, 600, 700 TEUs on it - last month average. So, we should be expanding on this front

items.statement: Snowman 5PL serves IKEA, Tim Hortons, Kopi Kenangan pan-India; Baskin Robbins and HUL regional
items.quote: Tim Hortons, IKEA and Kopi is pan-India. Baskin and HUL is regional.

items.statement: Snowman transportation strategically reducing low-margin business; will resume growth from next quarter
items.quote: In transportation, we are strategically managing a little lesser numbers because we wanted to weed out the low-margin businesses. So in transportation, as I said, we strategically made a little -- I mean it's an informed decision wherein we wanted to weed out the low-yield margin or negative margin businesses. And thus, the growth is not reflecting. But as per our targets from next quarter onwards

items.statement: Market share stable: NCR 16-17%, Ludhiana 27%, Uttarakhand 37%; no fresh competition intensity
items.quote: At NCR, we have retained between 16% to 17%. And Ludhiana, we have retained 27% and at Uttarakhand, that is 37%.

items.statement: Identified 6-7 new ICD locations over 5-7 years; focused on 2 near-term; exploring asset-light and Gati Shakti models
items.quote: We've identified probably the next 6, 7 ICDs that we want to open up. But it will take some time, and we don't want to get stuck in a situation like Jaipur again. So, we are being extra careful. We're looking at some asset-light models also, apart from domestic, where we mentioned earlier that someone else operates the terminal, but we operate the rail.

items.statement: DFC JNPT last 100 km expected operational by Dec 2025 per DFC, but management expects Mar 2026
items.quote: So, what we are expecting as per DFC, so it will get operational by - - like on the side, we are telling 31st December 2025. B ut when we spoke to them, so we are expecting that it should get completed by 31st March 2026

items.statement: Land acquisition remains key challenge: pricing, clear title, encroachment, road/rail connectivity, proximity to manufacturing hubs
items.quote: Generally, what we say, land acquisition remaining a challenge, that's the same issues that we mentioned that it is either pricing or clear title - that we don't want any encroachment on it. It should have specific road access, connectivity to the railway station, the right length and the width and near a manufacturing hub.

items.statement: Krishnapatnam land registration issue due to 1920s survey records; appeal filed but operations unaffected
items.quote: So basically, GDL sold some land to Snowman and part of it got registered, part of it didn't get registered because there's some old survey from -- old records from the 1920s, whic h are being questioned by the local government over there. So, we filed an appeal over there to get this land registered, but it's not stopped any operations at all

items.statement: CFS land sale discussions ongoing but no distress sale; awaiting right valuation while generating cash flow
items.quote: So, we are in discussion with some people, but we've not found the right valuation. And it's not a distressed sale, so we don't want to sell it at anything. And meanwhile, it's still generating good cash flow. So only when the right valuation comes in, we'll consider selling it.

items.statement: Presales growth guidance of 30-35% for FY26
items.quote: we definitely see a growth which is more like 30%, 35% this year

items.statement: Launch pipeline target of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore GDV for FY26
items.quote: We definitely want to achieve a number between INR3,000 crores to INR4,000 crores of fresh in ventory to be launched within this financial year

items.statement: Business development target of Rs 5,000 crore cumulative topline potential
items.quote: We are on track to conclude the ongoing business plan of adding new projects with a cumulative topline potential of Rs 5,000 crore

items.statement: Investment capacity of Rs 900-1,000 crore over next three quarters
items.quote: we have enough ammunition there to invest more like in the region of INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores in next three quarters

items.statement: Plan for minimum 5 launches in FY26, skewed to H2
items.quote: minimum 5-odd launches that we are talking abou t, and we might actually exceed this number

items.statement: Q1 bookings Rs 175 crore, collections Rs 191 crore
items.value: Rs 175 crore bookings, Rs 191 crore collections
items.quote: Q1 Bookings stood at Rs. 175 crore and Q1 Collections at Rs. 191 crore

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA Rs 24.5 crore, up 205% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for Q1 amounted to Rs. 24.5 crore, up 205% year-on-year basis

items.statement: Net debt negative Rs 50 crore as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: As of 30th June 2025, our net debt stands at negative Rs. 50 crore

items.statement: Unrealized operating cash flow exceeding Rs 4,000 crore from current pipeline
items.quote: We estimate an unrealized operating cash flow exceeding Rs. 4,000 crore coming fr om the current pipeline of projects

items.statement: Vertical mix to increase as Bangalore and Mumbai scale up
items.quote: as a natural kind of outcome of these 2 cities going up, you will see the vertical mix going up

items.statement: MMR redevelopment market 90% occupied by unbranded players, large untapped opportunity
items.quote: many of the large micro markets where redevelopment space is pretty much 90% still occupied by unbranded players

items.statement: Team scaling up from 456 employees to support next year volumes
items.quote: This 450-number has to go up definitely. All this very detailed exercise has already been done

items.statement: Full-year capacity growth guidance maintained at early double-digit
items.quote: on to the capacity guidance, we remain firm on our full year capacity guidance of early IndiGo Jul 30, 2025 double-digit capacity addition

items.statement: Q2 capacity growth expected at mid to high single-digit YoY
items.quote: As a result of these adjustments, we are expecting to add capacity in the mid to high single digit as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Q2 PRASK expected to be similar YoY with recovery in August-September
items.quote: Further, on the revenue side, basis the July trends, we are estimating similar passenger unit revenues (PRASK) for the second quarter as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: CASK ex-fuel ex-forex for FY26 expected to remain at FY25 levels
items.quote: As communicated earlier, CASK ex fuel ex forex for thi s financial year is expected to remain at similar levels as for the financial year 2025

items.statement: Q1 passengers grew 12% YoY to 31 million, double industry growth of 6%
items.quote: During this period, while the industry passengers grew by around 6 percent, we served more than 31 million customers, reflecting a solid growth of 12 percent compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Q1 net profit Rs 21.8 billion with 10.6% margin vs Rs 27.3 billion and 13.9% last year
items.quote: For the quarter ended June 2025, we reported a total income of 215 billion rupees and a net profit of 21.8 billion rupees with a net profit margin of 10.6 percent compared to a net profit of 27.3 billion rupees with a net profit margin of around 13.9 percent during the same period last year.

items.statement: Q1 PRASK down 7% YoY to Rs 4.21, yields down 5% to Rs 4.98, load factor 85% (-2pp)
items.quote: In terms of per unit revenue performance, the passenger unit revenue (PRASK), came in at 4.21 rupees vs. 4.54 rupees in Q1FY25, a reduction of around 7 percent. The yields came in at 4.98 rupees, a reduction of 5 percent as compared to the same period last year and load factors came in at around 85 percent, which is 2 percentage points lower compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Fuel CASK down 21.9% YoY on lower fuel prices, contract negotiations, and older aircraft redeliveries
items.quote: On the cost side, the fuel CASK reduced by 21.9 percent on a year over year basis driven by a reduction in average fuel prices, contract negotiation and redeliveries of older generation aircraft, which were inducted as part of mitigation measures for the AOG situation.

items.statement: CASK ex-fuel ex-forex at Rs 2.89, down 1.5% QoQ, up 1.8% YoY
items.quote: The CASK ex fuel ex forex came in at 2.89 rupees, which is lower by 1.5 percent on a sequential basis driven by reduction in number of damp leases partially offset by annual increases in airport charges and annual increments.

items.statement: Signed MoU with Airbus to convert 30 purchase rights into firm widebody order, deliveries from 2032
items.quote: To unlock the massive long-haul opportunity ahead of us and to enhance connectivity between Indian cities and major international destinations, we signed an MoU with IndiGo Jul 30, 2025 Airbus to convert 30 purchase rights into firm

items.statement: Q1 capacity grew 16% YoY; grounded aircraft stable in forties, 16 damp leases redelivered
items.quote: In terms of fleet, during the quarter we inducted 8 aircraft through our captive leasing unit in the GIFT city. Further, as guided during the last earnings call, the number of grounded aircraft remains stable in forties and with the reduction in number of groundings, we have started returning damp-leases from March onwards and have redelivered 16 damp leased aircraft during this quarter.

items.statement: A321XLR deliveries still expected this calendar year, no change to timeline
items.quote: We still expect our XLR to come in this year. There is no change in that.

items.statement: Order book of more than 900 aircraft across 2015, 2019, and 2023 orders
items.quote: the order book that we have of more than 900 aircrafts, the surety of the supply chain is reflective of the fact that even today we are getting deliveries from our 2015 negotiated order book.

items.statement: June quarter: capitalized operating lease liability Rs 468B, total debt ~Rs 685B, right-of-use assets ~Rs 508B
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, we ended the June quarter with a capitalized operating lease liability of 468 billion rupees and a total debt of around 685 billion rupees. Our right to use assets at the quarter end were around 508 billion rupees.

items.statement: Free cash Rs 348B, restricted cash Rs 146B at June quarter end
items.quote: Further, our liquidity has improved as we ended the June quarter with free cash of 348 billion rupees and restricted cash of 146 billion rupees.

items.statement: Launched Stretch product on international routes (Bangkok, Singapore, Dubai, Phuket) from July
items.quote: Since the beginning of July, we have begun a phased rollout of Stretch product across all frequencies to Bangkok, Singapore, Dubai and Phuket from Delhi and Mumbai.

items.statement: Loyalty programme at 3.8 million members, launched co-branded credit card with Kotak Mahindra Bank
items.quote: Our loyalty programme has received a very positive response with around 3.8 million members already enrolled, and we have onboarded several key brands. Recently, with the aim of elevating the travel and lifestyle experience, we have launched Co-Branded credit card in partnership with Kotak Mahindra Bank.

items.statement: New codeshare partnerships: KLM and Japan Airlines reciprocal, Jetstar, Delta, Virgin Atlantic reciprocal
items.quote: Our existing partnership with KLM has become reciprocal that will enable IndiGo customers enhanced connectivity to 30 destinations in Europe and the UK through Amsterdam . Further, our existing relationship with Japan Airlines has also become reciprocal with us also placing our marketing flight codes on Japan Airlines’ flights between points in Southeast Asia and Tokyo. IndiGo Jul 30, 2025 o In ad

items.statement: International competition from Middle East carriers acknowledged; IndiGo grew 12% vs market 5-6%
items.quote: The fact that the market has grown 5% to 6%, and that's a combination of domestic and international, and IndiGo has grown 12%, I think that speaks for itself in terms of dealing with that.

items.statement: FDTL implementation from July 1; Q1 employee cost reflects annual increments, FDTL impact to be absorbed via efficiencies
items.quote: The implementation of the FDTL starts from 1st of July. Most of it is going to get absorbed through efficiencies that we are IndiGo Jul 30, 2025 looking in-house. The second phase starts off around the November time frame

items.statement: Bilateral agreements updated with Thailand, Indonesia, Kuwait; Indian operators to utilize new frequencies
items.quote: I think the Indian government has concluded bilateral agreements with Thailand, with Indonesia, and I believe there is other discussions underway. So, I think the philosophy here, and we shared that before, if there is a desire on both the foreign and the Indian side to increase the bilateral regime, then there is an opportunity to expand.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions, airspace restrictions, and safety events impacted Q1; Q2 stabilizing, strong rebound expected in H2
items.quote: The June quarter was marked by a series of external impactful events, geopolitical headwinds, tragic safety event in the industry and airport and airspace closures. With these events we still saw a strong growth of around 12% in number of passengers for IndiGo - double the industry growth of 5% to 6% and a very resilient quarter despite industry headwinds and it brought us Rs. 2,200 crores of prof

items.statement: On-time performance leader since November 2024, one of highest technical dispatch reliability
items.quote: In terms of operations, since November last year, we have been the leader in terms of on-time performance and maintain one of the highest technical dispatch reliabilities in the industry, highlighting the core of one of our key customer promises.

items.statement: Launched IndiGo Ventures with first close at Rs 450 crore, invested in Jeh Aerospace
