items.statement: Capacity expansion commissioned by Jan-Feb 2026, revenue from Q1 FY27
items.quote: Yes, sir. We believe that it should be commissioned by January, February, and then trial run. So actual utilization or the revenue generation will happen from the Q1 of '27 -- FY '27.

items.statement: Volume growth of 33% YoY in Q1 FY26 despite weak pricing
items.quote: What's even more encouraging is the 33% growth in volumes, underscoring the robustness of our operations and continued trust of our customers.

items.statement: Price stabilization signs visible after year of correction
items.quote: While the pricing environment remains subdued due to correction over the past year, we are now seeing clear sign of price stabilization, which bodes well for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Auto ancillary segment facing pressure due to policy uncertainty
items.quote: Externally, the chemical industry is currently navigating a phase of policy uncertainty, particularly on tariff and trade, leading to temporary delay in order finalization, particularly in industrial and auto ancillary segments.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 18.01% standalone, 17.02% consolidated
items.quote: Our conscious effort towards product mix optimization have yielded results, enabling us to maintain healthy EBITDA margin of 18.01% on a stand-alone basis and 17.05% ** on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Industrial chemicals EBITDA margin >20%, Consumer chemicals single digit
items.quote: Well, as long as consumers is considered our margins in a single digit on EBITDA side, okay? While in industrial, it is much more than 20%. So the aggregate margin comes to in the range of about 17% to 19%.

items.statement: Auto segment margin pressure from price competition to retain market share
items.quote: Well, see, we have already mentioned that in our industrial segment, some auto ancillary and automobile we see a lot of pressure. And that industry is going through a little bit of turmoil. There our finished goods try to retain the market what we have, we need to compromise on our margins, and that has dragged us for this particular quarter.

items.statement: Expect price stabilization in auto segment by end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: We are expecting in the next 2 quarters that should stabilize with a lot of clarity on the policy and the tariff and trades, what we are challenging today. So at least by end of this Q3, we should have a stabilization on that part of it.

items.statement: Raw material prices declined in some cases but finished goods price competition is main challenge
items.quote: Yes. We did see in some of the cases, raw material also declined, but more of -- we see the price competition on our finished goods rather than the raw material. So we see a challenge there because of the -- somewhere there's a slowdown in some part of the world, which is causing that.

items.statement: Gaining market share globally, especially in Western markets
items.quote: And we are very, very confident that with this, the capacity and also the more and more customers are buying product despite a slowdown in the market, we are regaining the shares from somebody.

items.statement: US revenue share at 25%, not expected to grow beyond that
items.quote: Well, currently, Yasho's revenue share in U.S.A. is about 25% of the revenue.

items.statement: Auto/auto ancillary segment contributes ~25% of revenue globally
items.quote: That's only about -- 25%.

items.statement: Net working capital target reduced from 190 days to below 150 days by March 2026
items.quote: further reduction in net working capital from 190 days to below 150 days, primarily by optimizing raw material and the finished goods inventory.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 200+ to 190 in Q1, targeting 150 by March
items.quote: Currently, our inventory is down to 190 from more than 200 days. So we are down in this quarter 190. As I said in my speech that we will try to bring it controlled by the raw material and the finished goods inventory, we'll try to increase further.

items.statement: 60% of raw material imported, 20-25% of imports from China
items.quote: Well, of our total inventory, almost 60% is import and rest is domestic. We are trying -- we are working a lot of local sourcing where we can buy material locally, we are developing.

items.statement: Long-term debt INR333.28 crores, short-term INR210.98 crores as of June 2025
items.quote: Long-term debt is about INR280 crores and short-term is about INR100 crores.

items.statement: Debt repaid in Q1 FY26, next repayment of INR9 crores from November 2025
items.quote: Well, we have already repaid some debt. So only the repayment will start by November '25 for balance thing, about INR9 crores we repay.

items.statement: Export revenue share 67% currently, targeting 70% going forward
items.quote: Well, we do see the export will grow further. So we are at 67%, and we expect to grow to 70% of our total revenue. The export will contribute 70%.

items.statement: Revenue per kg approximately INR400 on aggregate level
items.quote: It's on an aggregate level about INR400 a kilo.

items.statement: Minor inventory losses from price declines, not quantified
items.quote: I think so. There will be definitely some inventory loss.

items.statement: DGTR initiated ADD investigation on Paste PVC imports from EU and Japan; confident of action before end of calendar year
items.quote: DGTR has since initiated an ADD investigation on these countries and the process is ongoing. We are confident that there will be action on this in the near future.

items.statement: Supreme Court stayed Gujarat HC order excluding certain grades from Suspension PVC ADD; DGTR disclosure statement issued, final findings expected soon
items.quote: The Honorable Supreme Court, in May, stayed the Honorable Gujarat High Court's order dated 25th April 2025, which had excluded certain grades from the ambit of ADD. Consequently, the disclosure statement has been issued by the DGTR and the final findings are expected soon.

items.statement: Hopeful that Suspension PVC ADD will be in place by Q3 FY26
items.quote: We are hopeful that we should see the ADD in place by Q3 of this year.

items.statement: New Paste PVC plant at Cuddalore successfully ramped to full operating capacity with consistent performance
items.quote: On the Paste PVC side, we are pleased to share that our new Paste PVC plant in Cuddalore has been successfully ramped up to full operating capacity and is delivering consistent operating performance.

items.statement: Paste PVC demand steady in India at 40,000-45,000 metric tons during quarter; encouraging signs from automobile sector
items.quote: The demand for Paste PVC remains steady in India at approximately 40,000 to 45,000 metric tons during the quarter and encouraging signs are emerging from the automobile sector.

items.statement: Domestic Suspension PVC demand grew 4% in quarter; pipe demand outlook positive with strong infrastructure pipeline
items.quote: The domestic demand for Suspension PVC registered a growth of 4% during the quarter. The outlook for pipe demand remains positive, supported by a strong pipeline of infrastructure projects.

items.statement: Custom Manufactured Chemicals dispatches on track in Q1; pipeline strong with active customer engagement; FY27 mostly on track
items.quote: On our Custom Manufactured Chemicals business, in Q1, we delivered as per schedule and dispatches remained on track. The agro-chemical sector is showing signs of recovery from the recent slowdown. While the overall business trajectory and pipeline remains strong, sales volumes may reflect timing differences due to prevailing global conditions.

items.statement: MPB 3 Phase 3 and civil works for MPB 4 progressing as planned; completion expected by Q3 FY26
items.quote: Construction activities for MPB 3 Phase 3 and civil works for MPB 4 are progressing as planned with completion expected by Q3 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Environmental clearance received for R32 project; final sizing and siting decision to be taken shortly
items.quote: On Refrigerant gases, we have received environmental clearance for the R32 project. The final decision on sizing and siting of the project will be taken shortly.

items.statement: Suspension PVC variable contribution margin currently INR5,000-7,000 per ton; Paste PVC variable margin around INR24,000-25,000 per ton
items.quote: The variable contribution margin would be anywhere from INR5,000 to around INR7,000. And obviously, anti-dumping duty should positively impact this.

items.statement: Paste PVC variable margin around INR24,000-25,000 per ton; benefit expected from ADD
items.quote: As far as Paste PVC is concerned, today, the variable margin would be around INR24,000, INR25,000 per ton. And that, again, depending on the level of anti-dumping duty that comes in, we should see the benefit.

items.statement: VCM prices follow PVC prices with few weeks lag; availability not an issue as requirements tied up
items.quote: The VCM always tends to follow the prices of PVC. Therefore, the margin between PVC and VCM usually holds good. There could be a lag of maybe a few weeks. But other than that, they would normally follow closely together. Therefore, that is not really a concern for us. Availability is not an issue. We are -- our requirements are tied up.

items.statement: Ethylene prices reasonably soft and continuing at current levels; not a large buyer of ethylene
items.quote: Ethylene prices have been reasonably soft. They are continuing where they are. We are not a very large buyer of ethylene, but ethylene prices are not too strong, let me put it that way.

items.statement: Paste PVC and Suspension PVC capacity utilization at 100%
items.quote: Our current capacity utilization is at 100%, very close to 100%. In both of these products we do operate fully.

items.statement: Suspension PVC sales volume 92,849 tons in Q1, up 17% QoQ driven by destocking of excess inventory
items.quote: We sold 92,849 tons during the quarter, representing a growth of 17% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. This is driven by the destocking of excess inventory that had been built up towards the end of last year.

items.statement: Suspension PVC imports increased ~50,000 tons vs Q4 FY25 due to traders importing low-priced PVC from China amid ADD uncertainty
items.quote: Meanwhile, traders and processors continue to impo rt low-priced PVC from China, capitalizing on the uncertainty surrounding ADD. This led to an estimated increase of approximately 50,000 tons in imports compared to Q4 of last

items.statement: Paste PVC ADD on EU and Japan initiated January 2025; imports from EU jumped from 20,000 tons in FY24 to 36,000 tons in FY25
items.quote: Unfortunately, when this was done, the dumping shifted to European Union, to producers from the European Union. And the imports that were coming in from the European Union, which in FY '23-24 were only around 20,000 tons, in FY '24-25 jumped to 36,000 tons.

items.statement: QCO enforcement likely by December 2025 as certified global capacity expected to reach 14-15 million tons vs Indian demand of ~4 million tons
items.quote: And since that extension, there are a couple of large producers, one in the US and one in the MENA region have got certified. And one more large US player, I believe, has had their plants audited and therefore, they are on track to get certification. So by the time December comes around, I think that we should have at least 14 million, 15 million tons of certified capacities worldwide. And given t

items.statement: Green power PPA covers 35-40% of total power requirement; estimated savings INR50-60 crores annually
items.quote: Actually, we have -- currently it covers roughly around 40% of our total power equipment, between 35% to 40% of our power requirement. And I don't want to get into the specific tariffs, but it will give us a significant saving compared to the grid cost of power. And I think the -- on the company as a whole, the estimated saving is somewhere between INR50 crores to INR60 crores by the contract.

items.statement: China anti-involution campaign targets plants over 20 years old for rationalization based on energy efficiency and carbon footprint in overcapacity sectors including PVC and caustic soda
items.quote: Now they have reduced it to 20 years and said that any plant over 20 years of age, they will look at it, take a hard look based on energy efficiency, based on carbon footprint and then decide whether -- especially in areas where there is overcapacity -- and then decide whether there needs to be some rationalization or some other form of integration or improvement of the plants itself.

items.statement: China carbide-based PVC phase-out linked to Minamata Convention; mercury mining hard stop end of 2031; gold catalyst alternative not drop-in for all existing plants
items.quote: The mining of mercury, however, there is a hard stop. And the mining of mercury hard stop is end of 2031. And since China accounts for around 90% of the total mercury mined in the world, you will have very little mercury available after 2031.

items.statement: R32 project sizing not yet decided; only enabling approvals taken; capex to be determined after sizing decision
items.quote: See, on R32, like I mentioned, the exact sizing of the project is yet to be decided by us. Therefore, the total capex on that will be decided when we decide the sizing. So right now, whatever we have taken is only an enabling approval.

items.statement: Only ongoing capex is MPB 3 Phase 3 of Custom Manufacturing; progressing as per plan and approved limits
items.quote: Yes, there's only one project which is ongoing, which is the multipurpose block Phase 3 of Custom Manufacturing, and that is going as per plan and as per approved capex limits.

items.statement: Capital deployment priority remains CMCD business; next investment triggered when 60% visibility on current block achieved
items.quote: Like we had indicated earlier, whenever we see visibility for 60% of the current block that we have, we will trigger the next investment. And we have also indicated clearly that our first preference for capital deployment is in the CMCD business. So that guidance still holds.

items.statement: Agrochemical sector showing recovery signs; pipeline healthy with active innovator engagement; inquiry acceleration expected next year onwards
items.quote: While the recovery is the turnaround in the ag-chem is happening, we believe sometime next year onwards, again, the speed of the inquiries and the number of inquiries in general will start accelerating and increasing further. But overall, our engagement continues to be on traction.

items.statement: Value-added chemicals volumes fell 16% QoQ due to temporary Caustic Soda operational issues at Mettur reducing hydrogen availability for Hydrogen Peroxide
items.quote: Volumes for our value-added chemicals fell by 16% on a sequential basis. This was due to lower Caustic Soda production at Mettur on account of tempora ry plant operational issues. This resulted in lower availability of hydrogen, impacting the sale quantity of Hydrogen Peroxide as well

items.statement: Caustic Soda prices firm but volatility expected; Chloromethanes prices steady and likely to continue
items.quote: Prices of Caustic Soda were firm, though we expect some volatility going forward. Chloromethanes prices were steady, and this trend is likely to continue.

items.statement: India caustic soda capacity ~6.3 million tons vs demand ~5 million tons; net exporter of ~0.5 million tons; 2 large projects coming FY26-27 may create excess length for 2 years
items.quote: Caustic Soda in India is already -- it's a long market because the capacity for caustic in India is around 6.3 million tons, and the demand is a little under 5 million tons. But then the operating rates of people who are not the caustic producers who are n ot integrated on the chlorine side would be less than 100%. It will possibly be around 75% to 80%. Therefore, the country is balanced with arou

items.statement: Management reaffirmed 25% revenue growth guidance for FY26 with stronger margins
items.quote: Therefore, I'm confident we shall deliver 25% growth with stronger margin this year.

items.statement: Management committed to deliver better margins than FY25 with 50-100 bps improvement potential
items.quote: So with a better operating leverage, there is a scope for improving the margin of 50 to 100 basis points as compared to full year last year.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected around INR250 crores with sufficient cash on hand
items.quote: Overall, the capex for the current year is expected to be around INR250 crores, and we have sufficient cash on hand to fund this capex.

items.statement: Electrolyte additive capex at Jhagadia on track for Q3 FY26 completion
items.quote: Electrolyte additive capex at our site in Jhagadia is on track and expected to be completed by Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Korea JV capex KRW30 billion for 75% stake, completion H2 CY2026, commercial production late 2026/early 2027
items.quote: We expect capex to be completed in second half of the calendar year 2026 with commercial production beginning by late 2026 or early 2027.

items.statement: Additional INR40-50 crores capex for new electrolyte additive products in FY26
items.quote: And of course, there will be some additional capex would be required in terms of additional infrastructure utility as well as some additional capex, which will be around INR40 crores to INR50 crores in total.

items.statement: CDMO projects expected to contribute from Q4 FY26, validation quantities already supplied for one project
items.quote: Our remaining CDMO projects are progressing as per plan and are expected to begin contribution to the top line from Q4 FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: Three new CDMO projects with INR50-100 crores revenue potential each, commercialization by Q4 FY26
items.value: INR50 crores to INR100 crores each
items.quote: We see the revenue potential of INR50 crores to INR100 crores each for those products.

items.statement: Pharma raw material prices stable, demand steadily improving, CDMO segment attracting strong interest
items.quote: Starting with pharmaceutical, raw material prices have remained stable and demand for our products is steadily improving. The CDMO segment continues to attract strong interest.

items.statement: Battery chemicals seeing significant momentum due to US manufacturing incentives driving customer urgency
items.quote: This is driving urgency among manufacturers. And as a result, we are seeing a noticeable uptick in customer interest for our battery chemicals offering.

items.statement: Semiconductor customers diversifying supply chains, seeking partners closer to manufacturing bases
items.quote: Customer wants to diversify their supply chain and are looking for partners closer to their manufacturing basis.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 gross margin expanded 1,117 bps YoY to 53.2% driven by cost optimization and product mix
items.quote: The gross margin expanded by 1,117 basis points Y-o-Y to 53.2%. Gross margin was driven by cost optimization initiatives as well as improved product mix.

items.statement: Segmental margins: Pharma ~28% EBITDA, Specialty ~11% EBITDA
items.quote: So segmental margin for Pharma is around 28% and specialty is around 11%.

items.statement: Pharma growth driven by core advanced intermediates (ex-CDMO) with favorable mix improving realizations
items.quote: Growth volumes are also there, but the realization has improved as compared to Q1 FY '25 because of favorable product mix.

items.statement: Japan PMDA virtual audit completed, Unit II Ankleshwar declared GMP compliant; both pharma facilities now PMDA certified
items.quote: We successfully completed a virtual audit of our Unit II at Ankleshwar by Japan's PMDA. And I'm happy to share that it has been declared GMP compliant.

items.statement: Advanced discussions with large Japanese multinational for semiconductor chemicals; strong engagement in Korea
items.quote: I am pleased to share that in Japan, we are in final stage of discussion with a large multinational customer.

items.statement: Electrolyte additive contracts signed with export customers (Japan/Taiwan), not dependent on domestic Indian battery projects
items.quote: We have already signed agreement in place for this business. And all our capacity, what is I just mentioned, this is for our export business.

items.statement: Solar capacity now 15.8 MW across Sachin, Ankleshwar, Jhagadia; full benefit from Q3 FY26
items.quote: Now we have in total 15.8-megawatt power plant, which will offset majority of our electricity cost at our Sachin, Ankleshwar and Jhagadia unit. Full benefit of this solar power plant will be visible from Q3 FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: Pilot plant capex started at Sachin, completion expected within a year
items.quote: Capex for pilot plant has already started at our Sachin unit. We hope to complete the same within a year time.

items.statement: Q1 working capital 128 days (+14 days vs Q4 FY25) due to advance raw material payments; full year target ~110 days
items.quote: Our working capital for the quarter was around 128 days, which was increased by 14 days compared to Q4FY '25. This is mainly on account of the lower payable days due to the advanced payment for better pricing of raw materials, while for the full year, we believe our working capital would be around 110 days.

items.statement: Strong operating cash flow of INR94.6 crores generated in Q1 despite working capital increase
items.quote: Although there was an increase in working capital, I'm happy to share that we have generated a strong cash flow of INR94.6 crores from the operation during the quarter.

items.statement: Net cash and cash equivalents at INR270 crores
items.quote: Net cash and cash equivalents were at INR270 crores.

items.statement: US One Big Beautiful Bill Act retains/strengthens manufacturing incentives for battery chemicals, accelerates credit sunset
items.quote: While this Act removes subsidies on EVs, which could impact consumer demand, it retains and, in some areas, strengthens the manufacturing-related incentives. The Act restricts participation from a set of prohibited foreign entities and accelerates the sunset of manufacturing credits.

items.statement: Baba Fine Chemicals semiconductor business facing soft demand from end customers
items.quote: On Baba Fine Chemical semiconductor business, the demand has been soft from our end customer side, which was kind of in last quarter also.

items.statement: Pharma intermediates ex-CDMO pipeline strong with R&D visibility beyond 2040 patent expiries
items.quote: For the ex CDMO business we have good visibility in terms of our product pipeline as we have very strong product pipeline, R&D pipeline up to patent expiry of API beyond 2040.

name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: FY2028 IFRS PAT target Rs 2,500 crore with 20% from underwriting and 80% from investment returns; Rs 30,000 crore premium target may be moderated due to corporate business exit
items.quote: As far as the guidance that we have given for FY2028 on Rs. 2,500 crores on IFRS basis, I think the broad split would be 20% on underwriting and 80% on our investment returns.

items.quote: Our retail health GWP grew 18% to INR 3,667 crores in Q1-FY2026, fueled by a 25% growth in fresh retail premiums and a strong renewal persistency of 98% on premiums.

items.statement: Retail market share maintained at 31% despite large base

items.statement: IFRS expense ratio reduced 100 bps to 30.1% from 31.1% previous year; combined ratio 99.6% vs 99.2% YoY; claims ratio 69.5% vs 68.1% YoY
items.quote: Finally, the IFRS expense ratio has also reduced by 100 basis points to 30.1% from 31.1% the previous year.

items.statement: Investing in technology, digital SBU creation planned, fraud detection models, telemedicine and wellness solutions
items.quote: We continue to invest in our efforts to reduce fraud, waste and abuse. Our FWA savings improved by 30% in Q1-FY2026 over the last year.

items.statement: Agency base grew to 7.89 lakh agents (2x next largest competitor) with 14,000 new agents added in Q1; agency productivity improved 13%
items.quote: In Q1-FY2026, we added 14,000 new agents, taking our total agency base to 7.89 lakh, which is the largest in the industry, and agency productivity also improved by 13%.

items.statement: Digital channel fresh business growing 73% YoY, now 20% of new business vs 12% last year; 70% direct digital vs 30% partner; brand search volumes up 75%
items.quote: Our digital business, fresh business is growing at an impressive 73%. We witnessed a 75% year-on-year growth in brand search volumes in Quarter 1.

items.statement: Multi-year policies 30% of new business by policy count, 8% of total retail volume; preferred geographies growing 1.5x faster than overall business
items.quote: On our new business, it is around 30%, in terms of number of policies.

items.statement: Investment income Rs 586 crore vs Rs 388 crore YoY including Rs 292 crore MTM gains on non-debt portfolio (17.5% of book); debt MTM gains Rs 200 crore not in IFRS
items.quote: The investment income in Q1-FY2026 has grown to Rs. 586 crores versus Rs. 388 crores in Q1-FY2025. We accounted for Rs. 292 crores of mark-to-market gains in our investment income under IFRS accounting.

items.statement: Solvency ratio 2.22x vs 1.5x minimum requirement as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: Our solvency as on June 30th of 2025 was 2.22 x versus the 1.5 x minimum requirement.

items.statement: IFRS reporting expected live by April 1, 2027 per IRDAI guidelines; all business decisions now based on IFRS; moving to quarterly IFRS reporting
items.quote: As per the latest IRDAI guidelines, IFRS is expected to go live by 1st April 2027, we would like to emphasize that all our business and investment-related decisions are nowadays taken, considering the IFRS reporting only.

items.statement: Rajeev Kher (former Commerce Secretary) appointed Chairperson; Amitabh Jain (COO) and Himanshu Walia (CMO) elevated to Board as Executive Directors subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: I am happy to announce and extremely pleased to welcome Mr. Rajeev Kher, former Commerce Secretary, as the new Chairperson of our Board.

items.statement: Claims NPS improved to 57 from 46 YoY; claim settlement ratio 90% vs 85.7% YoY; FWA savings up 30% YoY; retail loss ratio 68.5%, group loss ratio 85.1%
items.quote: Star Health claims NPS has improved consistently over the last quarters. We now have a claims NPS of 57 from 46 in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Healthcare cost escalation driving industry claim ratio increases; pricing corrections passed to customers; July claims on expected lines with no abnormal trends
items.quote: The industry conti nues to witness very high healthcare cost escalation in the recent years. We have seen claim ratios increase across industry players, forcing health insurance industry players to pass on a portion of this inflation to the end customers

items.statement: Widest agency-led distribution (2x next competitor); 11,300+ network hospitals with negotiated pricing; lowest claims processing cost (<1% GWP)

items.quote: We have made a significant shift towards our preferred product offerings, which are basically retail and benefit plans, which now contributes 92% of our fresh business versus 74% last year.

items.quote: Our CFS business sees some improvement with an EBITDA per TEU around INR1,500. Our focus on expanding our Inland Container Terminal network continues.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit volume growth for full FY26; expects rail EBITDA per TEU to return to INR9,500 in coming quarters as double stacking improves and export imbalance eases
items.quote: So, there is scope to increase double stacking. Possibly, we'll go back to INR9,500 in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Annual maintenance capex ~INR30 cr; INR300 cr earmarked for two new ICD terminals (~INR150 cr each); Jaipur ICD balance work ~INR60-70 cr; Snowman plans ~INR100 cr/year for own facilities plus 3-4 asset-light facilities in 2 years, 5-6 in 3
items.quote: Basically, we are looking at about INR30 crores of capex per year. This is not counting any new terminals. As and when a new terminal comes in, that will be at an average of about INR150 crores per te rminal. So, we've earmarked INR300 crores for two terminals

items.statement: Snowman adding capacity in Calcutta, Krishnapatnam, Kundli (NCR); two new warehouses onboarded (Calcutta, Krishnapatnam), asset-light warehouse in Kundli starting August; targeting 200,000+ pallets in 3 years from ~150,000 currently
items.quote: We just onboarded our two facilities, which is Calcutta and Krishnapatnam. They will definitely be adding revenues, plus we have taken a warehouse on asset-light model in Kundli, which will also start contributing from t he month of August

items.statement: Rail volumes stable at 92,000-94,000 TEUs/quarter; Q1 typically weaker but held Q4 level; targeting double-digit growth for FY26
items.quote: Generally, Q1 is weaker. I know last year was weak because of the Red Sea more than so. But for Q1, even to stay at the same level that we did for Q4, it's a good achievement.

items.statement: Evaluating self-owned solar (INR2-2.5/unit vs grid INR4.5); exploring EVs (capex 2x, opex 1/3-1/4) and LNG vehicles; already running 65-70 CNG vehicles
items.quote: But now going forward, we're evaluating, doing it ourselves where we invest in the solar and then it will be about INR2 or INR2.5 compared to something in the average is about INR4.5 right now.

items.statement: Double stacking declined to 39% due to lack of exports and trade realignment toward Mundra; domestic rail volumes ~600-700 TEUs/month, expanding with new containers
items.quote: So it's 39%, and it's basically declined due to lack of exports. There's also realignment of trade. Certain volumes have increased towards Mundra rather than Pipavav, which is further increasing their balance.

items.statement: Market share stable: NCR 16-17%, Ludhiana 27%, Uttarakhand 37%; no fresh competitive intensity or discounting; aware of JSW logistics expansion but focused on own 6-7 ICD pipeline over 5-7 years
items.quote: At NCR, we have retained between 16% to 17%. And Ludhiana, we have retained 27% and at Uttarakhand, that is 37%.

items.statement: DFC JNPT last 100 km expected operational by Dec 2025 (DFC target) or Mar 2026 (management view); pan-India license gives advantage once corridor starts

items.quote: Generally, what we say, land acquisition remaining a challenge, that's the same issues that we mentioned that it is either pricing or clear title - that we don't want any encroachment on it.

items.quote: We are already in active discussion with large number of C &I customers and I think the whole 1 ,000 megawatt will get tied up very quickly and that is why we are now also looking at starting work on the another 1 ,800 megawatt.

items.statement: Odisha Discom AT&C losses at 17-18%; targets ~10% in 3 years; collection efficiency improving toward consistent 100%
items.quote: We are still in some places in 17%-18% range. We do expect that in the next 3 years, we will bring down to about 10% range and the type of reductions that we have seen in last 4 years, this trend will continue and that will help us in getting better returns.

items.statement: Mumbai transmission capex ~Rs 600-700 crore annually to augment capacity for rising demand
items.quote: There is huge amount of CAPEX which is happening in transmission projects in Mumbai considering that there is a huge increase in demand in Mumbai city and to augment the capacity of transmission, capital expenditure is being made on a yearly basis of nearly Rs. 600 crores to Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Mundra plant competitive in merit order due to low international coal prices; expects coal prices to remain soft for next few years
items.quote: As all of you are aware with these lower coal prices, international coal prices, the cost of Mundra Power is very attractive in the merit order and we do expect that this price will continue to be softer at least for next few years and hence the attractiveness of Mundra plant is there.

items.statement: Mundra plant on maintenance shutdown with FGD work; will operate all 5 units continuously once Supplementary PPA finalized; expects 80% availability for full year to earn 100% capacity charge
items.quote: So, we have taken maintenance shutdown for all the units and some of the work relating to FGD is going on. We do expect that as soon as the SPPA (Supplementary PPA) is finalized, we will be in a position to operate all the 5 units continuously for the balance of the year.

items.statement: UP Discom privatization bid documents expected this month; keen to pursue after reviewing terms. Resurgent platform stake acquisition still under discussion with partners
items.quote: As far as UP is concerned, the process of discussion within the UP government and UP Regulatory Commission has been going on and they are expected to come with their bid some time in this month. We are very keen to pursue that. But we will do that once we see the bid documents and the terms and conditions for that. As far as the Resurgent platform, that is still under discussion. As you know that

items.statement: Kleros Capital Partners matter sub-judice; cannot comment beyond disclosed notes
items.quote: So, we have already given in the notes, and you can see that since the matter is sub -judice, we cannot speak much on that. So, whatever we have provided in the notes, that is our stand.

items.statement: Arbitration award dated July 1; 90 days to file appeal by Sep 30; high court decision expected in 6-9 months; liability recognition decision after court order
items.quote: So, we are given 90 days to file the appeal. The order was dated 1 st July. So, we have time till 30th of September and we find that much before. Normally, it takes about 6 to 9 months for the matter to be heard and decided. So, that's the timeline that we are expecting.

items.statement: Module manufacturing uses own cells for DCR market; rooftop ~100% own cell/module; internal transfer pricing for own projects lowers reported realization
items.quote: You are 100% right. Right now, very small quantity of imported cells we are using in some of the older projects. But other than that everywhere we are using our own cell and module. Rooftop business practically 100% is now our own cell and module and also in many of our projects we are using our own cell and module.

items.statement: Rooftop module pricing at arm's length based on market demand-supply; different from internal IPP transfer pricing
items.quote: See, every pricing is based on the market demand and supply. Rooftop has a different demand and supply and a different price range in which they operated and you need to compete over there vis -à-vis other players with similar types and quality of modules. So, those prices are at arm's length and is independently negotiated between both businesses.

items.statement: Module capacity expansion under discussion given strong demand and accretive margins
items.quote: We always keep on looking on opportunities. So, continue to consider anything which will help us improve our performance based on the demand supply and how many other plants are coming, similar plants are coming. So, this is definitely under discussion.

items.statement: Solar PLF declined in Q1 due to lower radiation from early rainfall; wind generation higher offsetting some impact
items.quote: So, as I mentioned to you, during the last quarter, because the radiation was less because of early rainfall and all that, the generation was less in solar. But the wind capacity, you see there was more generation in the wind. So, weather changes impact all these things.

items.statement: Tata Projects JV loss Rs 65 crore in Q1 vs Rs 8 crore profit last year
items.quote: Subhadeep, the loss was Rs. 65 crores this quarter compared to Rs. 8 crores profit last year.

items.statement: Cell plant not yet on ALMM-II list as inspection pending; inspection scheduled next week, will be added upon completion
items.quote: On the cell, because they have not completed the inspection. I am told that they are inspecting next week. So, as and when they complete the inspection of plants, they keep on adding. So, they will add as soon as they complete the inspection.

items.statement: Expects existing performance to continue and improve in subsequent quarters as capex returns materialize; no specific numerical guidance given
items.quote: We are also committed that existing performance will not only continue but will also improve in the subsequent quarter considering that there is large amount of capital expenditures that we are doing and the returns of all that will start coming in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth guided at 8-9% if exports recover
items.quote: for the remainder of the year? Management: We have reported 4% growth in Q1 and -- largely arising out of domestic market, but should the exports also revise and conditions improve, and then definitely, 8% to 9% is the direction

items.statement: Capex guided at INR300 crores for FY26
items.quote: And we expect the capital expenditure to be around INR300 crores this year.

items.statement: Renewable energy share target 55%+ for FY26
items.quote: Renewable energy, it's about 51%, 52%, and we are aiming for the year at 55% plus.

items.statement: Domestic outperformed industry across all segments in Q1
items.quote: So we started off well in the domestic segment, and we had growth slightly higher than the industry across all segments, commercial vehicles, engine, passenger vehicles, tractors, all segments we have performed well.

items.statement: Export market hazy; North America confused on EPA 2027 norms and tariffs; Europe better
items.quote: See, I think currently, the export market is a bit hazy. I think things are not clear. If you take North America, there's a lot of confusion regarding the emission norms that are to kick in, EPA 27 norms that are to kick in '27. And also this tariff-related issues have created a demand slump in North America with some of our major customers, while some are holding on.

items.statement: Export improvement expected by Q3 FY26 (post-October)
items.quote: So overall, I would say we are slightly down or on par with what we were last year and hoping to improve by the Q4 of this year, that is post October, the third quarter of this year, we see improvement.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA INR238 cr at 17.5% vs 17% YoY and 15.6% QoQ
items.quote: We have reported EBITDA of INR238 crores at 17.5% compared to 17% for Q1 of last year and 15.6% of Q4.

items.statement: Margin drivers: export recovery, raw material price stability, operational efficiency, aftermarket mix
items.quote: Once the traction improves in the export segment and where the realization are historically higher, the margin will definitely improve. The second factor for margin expansion is the stability or further reduction in raw material price.

items.statement: Steel rod prices stabilised at INR70,000 from INR85,000-90,000 peak; further rollback needed for 19%+ EBITDA
items.quote: The raw material prices, especially steel rods and bars, which were around INR45,000 to INR50,000 2 years back, had moved up to INR85,000 to INR90,000, and now they have stabilized around INR70,000. So until they roll back, this further expansion is unlikely.

items.statement: Room for ~1% EBITDA margin expansion from current levels; 19-19.5% challenging
items.quote: Getting back to 19%, 19.5% may be a challenge, but definitely, there is room for another 1%-odd.

items.statement: GM EV revenue upwards of INR250 cr this year; full run-rate in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: It will be upwards of INR250 crores for General Motors as an individual customer.

items.statement: Stellantis EV ramp shifted by one quarter to year-end
items.quote: See, on the EV orders, I think there has been a further shift in terms of Stellantis, one of our major customers, we see the EV and the EV vehicles getting shifted to over by one more quarter. And earlier, it was supposed to be from July, but then it's going to the end of the year.

items.statement: Wind energy revenue grew from INR200+ cr to INR350+ cr; third phase expansion of INR75+ cr committed
items.quote: While the initial phase of expansion was over, which has helped us to move from INR200-and-odd crores per annum to now INR350 crores plus, I think we are in for the third phase of expansion where already we have committed INR75 crores plus with respect to the expansion.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue grew from $2-3M to $6-7M; targeting INR100+ cr in 2-3 years
items.quote: In terms of the aerospace, while we were doing, say, $2 million to $3 million, I think with the drive and presence in aerospace segment and where we have also got accreditation from NADCAP, that has helped us in terms of moving it to say, $6 million to $7 million. So we are working in that direction, and we should see that growing to INR100 crores plus in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Capex mix: ~25% replacement, balance growth for specific customer requirements
items.quote: Typically, we have seen from experience about 25% of our capital expenditure replacement. So that will continue. And selectively for specific customer requirements, we expand capacity.

items.statement: Capacities well established for ICE, plug-in hybrid and EV; flexible to consumer preference
items.quote: Again, our capacities are well established. And depending on what the customer wants, and depending on the market, the consumer preferences in the U.S. If the demand is for ICE vehicles, we are happy to supply. And if the demand is for plug-in hybrid, we are there. If it's an EV, we are there.

items.statement: Tariff reimbursements negotiated with all customers; no tariff absorption in Q1
items.quote: No. At this point in time, there are no cases where we've been asked to bear and customers have been supportive.

items.statement: Better mix from higher tonnage CVs, SUVs (66% of PV), high-HP tractors, wind energy fasteners
items.quote: The higher tonnage and the SUVs and the high HP tractors, these give us a... Sahil Sanghvi: These are the reasons, okay. Management: Advantage compared to the normal mix. Wind energy fasteners compared to the last year same quarter, I think with the added capacity, which has come on stream, that has also helped in generating additional revenue from this

items.statement: Aftermarket 12-13% of revenue; industrial segment offers large headroom; proportion likely to stay 10-15%
items.quote: The aftermarket business for Sundram overall is around 12% to 13%. And that business, we have been steadily growing, serving the auto segment as well as the industrial segment. We see a good headroom for growth in that segment, which we have been pursuing for the last 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Domestic outperformance due to broad coverage, high share, participation in new platforms
items.quote: We are participating with almost the entire industry. And almost with all our customers, we are the major stakeholders in terms of share of business.

items.statement: Europe 15% of exports, UK 5%; Europe improved vs 2 years ago; UK FTA medium-term opportunity
items.quote: So with respect to Europe, Mukesh, it would be about 15% of our overall exports. And U.K. would be another 5%. So between the larger Europe combining with U.K., we will be looking at 20%.

items.statement: Borrowings declining; receivables and inventory well controlled
items.quote: The borrowings are also showing a declining trend. And not only the borrowing, the working capital components as well the receivables are well under control, so our inventory.

items.statement: Balance sheet parameters improving; gross and net asset turns moved up
items.quote: And like I said, the -- all the balance sheet parameters are looking up, including the asset turns, both gross asset turns and net asset turns have moved up.

items.statement: PBT INR186 cr and PAT INR138 cr - highest ever for a quarter
items.quote: And we have recorded reported PBT of INR186 crores, which is the highest for us, and also profit after tax of INR138 crores, which is again the highest for the quarter.

items.statement: Primary risk: export demand uncertainty; capacity utilisation dependent on overseas schedules
items.quote: The risks at this point in time, we have made investments in our -- creating additional capacity, and we want full utilization in the asset terms to improve. And -- so we expect the export market schedules to improve for some of our parts, especially hybrid vehicles from our overseas customers in Q2 -- our Q2 and for our parts -- electric vehicles to improve from Q4.

items.statement: Demand estimate raised to 7-8% from earlier 6-7% for FY26
items.quote: We are up on our demand estimates by 1% from 6-7% before to now 7-8%.

items.statement: Target EBITDA of Rs 1,500 per metric tonne by 2028
items.quote: we have a blueprint to achieve our targeted EBITDA of Rs.1,500 per metric tonne by 2028.

items.statement: Green power share targeted to reach 60% by FY28
items.quote: Green power share uptake with every passing quarter. It improved by 9.7% to 28.1% and it is targeted to reach 60% by FY28.

items.statement: Power cost targeted to reduce from Rs 5.9 to Rs 4.5 per unit by FY28
items.quote: This will reduce the existing power cost which is around Rs.5.9 per unit to almost Rs.4.5 per unit by FY28.

items.statement: Power consumption per metric tonne expected to improve by at least 5 units
items.quote: The power consumption per metric tonne of cement also is expected to improve by at least 5 units.

items.statement: Heat consumption to improve by 35-40 kcal per kg of clinker
items.quote: Importantly, the heat consumption will improve by at least 35 to 40 kilo calorie per kg of clinker for the various initiatives outlined including mix of the new kilns.

items.statement: Primary lead distance expected to reduce by almost 50 km by FY28
items.quote: Primary lead distance reduced by 8 km this quarter at 269 km and is expected to further reduce by almost 50 km when we achieve 140 million tonnes by FY28.

items.statement: Logistics cost expected to reduce by almost Rs 150 per metric tonne by FY28
items.quote: This will help to reduce the logistics cost by almost Rs.150 per metric tonne, also supported by a higher component of rail and sea logistics.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 estimated at Rs 9,000-10,000 crore including Penna payments
items.quote: You can consider maybe couple of thousands. So, you can actually consider ballpark 1,000 here and there. So, 10,000 is a good amount to assume. I would have considered between say 9-10, but, yeah, 10 is okay. That includes Penna also.

items.statement: Total cement capacity at 104.5 MTPA; target 118 MTPA by end FY26 and 140 MTPA by FY28
items.quote: Our total cement capacity currently stands at 104.5 million tonnes. In our larger aim of achieving 140 million tonnes by FY28, we are well poised to achieve 118 million tonnes by end of FY26

items.statement: Commissioned 5 MTPA grinding capacity in last 3 months; targeting additional 13 MTPA this fiscal year
items.quote: We commissioned 5 million tonnes of grinding capacity over the last 3 months and target additional, another 13 million tonnes this financial year.

items.statement: Capacity utilization around 77-78% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So therefore, on an overall capacity utilization, I am around 77-78%.

items.statement: EBITDA per tonne at Rs 1,069, up 28% YoY; EBITDA margin 19.1%, up 3.8% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA per metric tonne of cement at Rs.1,069 of 28% YOY and EBITDA margin stood at 19.1%, up 3.8%

items.statement: Cost reduction journey ~35-40% complete (Rs 175-200 per tonne of Rs 530 target)
items.quote: if I have to give a broad range, we would have hit almost 35%-40% of that journey by now. So, let us say closer to ₹200 a ton basically; ₹175 -₹200

items.statement: Coal cost improved from Rs 1.73 to Rs 1.59 per 1000 kcal; expected to sustain near these levels
items.quote: Coal cost has improved from Rs.1.73 to Rs.1.59 per 1000 kilo calories and expected to sustain near these levels.

items.statement: Manpower cost at Rs 223 per metric tonne, among lowest in industry
items.quote: We have one of the lowest manpower cost at Rs.223 per metric tonne amongst the peers in the industry.

items.statement: Premium products share of trade sales at 33%, up 43% YoY
items.quote: higher share of premium products as a percentage of trade sales which is now at 33%, up by 43% YOY.

items.statement: Cement demand grew ~4% YoY in Q1 FY26 driven by government infrastructure schemes
items.quote: cement demand grew by almost 4% Y-on-Y in first quarter FY26, driven by Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Sadak Yojana, Bharat Mala, Sagar Mala and other INSA projects

items.statement: Consolidated cash and cash equivalents at ~Rs 3,000 crore end of June 2025
items.quote: overall, basically, right now, we are holding 3,000 odd crores of cash and cash equivalent.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with CRISIL AAA stable and A1+ ratings
items.quote: we continue to remain debt free. Our rating remains highest at CRISIL AAA stable and A1 plus ratings.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition effective 22nd April 2025; integration progressing well
items.quote: Yeah, Naveen, it is 22nd April.

items.statement: Sanghi, Penna, Asian, Tuticorin acquisitions integrated; synergies realized ahead of schedule
items.quote: Our inorganic growth story strategy is progressing seamlessly. Sanghi, Asian, Tuticorin, Penna and more recently, Orient, which we have successfully integrated. The results were out a few days back, accelerating our market presence all across the geographies. Integrating synergies are being realized ahead of schedules

items.statement: Market share increased 2% to 15.5% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Highest ever sales volume of 18.4 million tonnes, up 20% YOY with market share up 2% to 15.5%.

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity at 473 MW (28.1% green power share); WHRS capacity 228 MW
items.quote: In this quarter of 26, we commissioned 57.7 megawatt of wind energy, taking our total renewable power to 473 megawatt. Additionally, our WHRS capacity stands at 228 megawatt. Together, our green energy is contributing close to 28.1%

items.statement: Merger of Adani Cementation Industries Limited received all statutory approvals; Sanghi and Penna received BSE/NSE approvals
items.quote: The merger of Adani Cementation Industries Limited has received all the statutory approvals. For Sanghi and Penna, we have received approvals from both the exchanges BSE and NSE and further process of completion is ongoing.

items.statement: Bhattapada project facing minor delays of couple months due to brownfield execution constraints; no vendor or Chinese engineer issues
items.quote: Of course, projects of this scale, for example, when you have a brownfield expansion, a couple of months here and there, because you are operating for, you are actually executing in an established estate, which is also, should not be derailed in any form and manner. So these are, like, very nominal months, couple of months here and there. I do not see any issue or any anxiety over there.

items.statement: Brand integration of Penna and Orient completed; dealers onboarded to Ambuja/ACC platforms; positive volume and price impact
items.quote: Very positive . W hy Penna , i n fact, now Orient also completely brand penetration has happened and migrated to Ambuja and ACC. So , both, for example, Penna and Orient have done very, very well. Dealers have received it very, very well

items.statement: Simplifying marketing structure to 3 layers; reimagining org and plant structure for positive impact
items.quote: we are simplifying and, as I said, we are reimagining the whole structure, the whole org structure, the whole plant structure and you will see prospectively a positive impact and results out of it.

items.statement: Forex EBIT margin guidance maintained at 40%-45% range for full year
items.quote: Our estimation on this business continues to be the double-digit growth that we've spoken about in the past and with our guidance on EBIT margin between the 40%-45% range.

items.statement: Sterling targets steady-state leisure occupancy of 65%-68% and peak season ARR of INR7,100-7,500
items.quote: So typically, as I mentioned even in the past, at a steady state for leisure across the year, anything between 65% to 68% is actually an ideal occupancy to maintain. Having said that, I've also called out that we do have scope to up the occupancies as we k eep going up. The average rates will range in the -- if we are at a peak season about INR7,100 to INR7,500

items.statement: Q1 FY26 travel demand moderated in May-June due to Pahalgam incident, aviation mishap, Iran-Israel conflict and trade tensions
items.quote: The period April to June quarter marked one of the most volatile periods for the travel and tourism industry since the COVID era, shaped by a convergence of global and domestic disruptions. On the domestic front, traveler sentiment was adversely impacted b y the tragic incident in Pahalgam and the ensuing cross-border

items.statement: Domestic travel recovery seen in July with positive trend from negative territory; international short and long haul trending to double-digit growth
items.quote: Post that, in July, we have definitely seen a bit of a trend reversal, if I use the word so, both on the international side, that is short haul as well as long haul. And on the domestic side, it's more like a recovery. From a negative territory, which is degrowth over last year, we're actually starting to see a positive trend where we are now getting closer to what we were at the same time last ye

items.statement: Consolidated PBT margin improved YoY from 5.1% to 5.2% in Q1 FY26 excluding one-time ex gratia of INR171 million
items.quote: Notably, our PBT margins improved year-on-year from 5.1% to 5.2%, driven by continued operational efficiency.

items.statement: Financial services EBIT margin remained strong at 44% in Q1 FY26 despite revenue decline
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, it is encouraging to note that our EBIT margin continued to remain strong. The business operating performance is resilient and our EBIT margins are at 44%, underscoring the strength of our efficiency and the underlying business model.

items.statement: Travel segment EBIT margin improved from 3.9% to 4.1% in Q1 FY26 with EBIT growing 25%
items.quote: Despite these challenges, our income from operations grew by 18% and our EBIT grew by 25%. Our EBIT margins improved from 3.9% to 4.1%, displaying our strong resilience from the forward booking that we saw and the diversified portfolio across the DMS Group and the various geographies that we operate in.

items.statement: DEI EBIT margin improved substantially from 3.2% to 5.1% in Q1 FY26 driven by cost efficiencies and technology
items.quote: Our EBIT margin has improved substantially from 3.2% last year to 5.1% this year, indicating the benefits of cost efficiencies and productivity led by the usage of technology.

items.statement: Travel forward bookings tapered from 24-25% growth in late March/April to mid-teens for outbound and negative for domestic by May-June
items.quote: By late March and into April of 2025, we were witnessing strong forward booking momentum with outbound and domestic travel trending at about 24% to 25% over previous year. However, the series of external events that I mentioned before impacted our forward booking and our booking curve tapered as we progress between May and June.

items.statement: Sterling inventory increased 21% YoY (approx 50,000 room nights or 540 rooms per day QoQ); occupancy at 62% with headroom to grow
items.quote: Our guest nights grew by 12%. The occupancy stood at 62% with an increased supply of nearly 50,000 room nights this quarter or approximately 540 rooms per day quarter-over-quarter. Having said that, we do have headrooms more in occupancy, and that will put Sterling in a position where we can actually grow further as we keep scaling the company.

items.statement: Sterling average rates at close to INR7,100 reflecting strong pricing strength and upscale leisure positioning
items.quote: Our average rates also stood at close to INR7,100, reflecting strong pricing strength and positioning and the evolving positioning of Sterling in the upscale leisure segment.

items.statement: India Holiday Report 2025 shows 35% prefer group escorted tours, 33% customized private tours, 32% semi-guided; 50% prefer Europe, Southeast Asia dominant for short-haul
items.quote: The survey revealed that 35% of our respondents prefer group escorted tours, followed by 33% opting for customized private tours and 32% choosing semi-guided holidays. And essentially, it means that two -third of our customer base are still looking forward to, in some shape or form, guided tours, and that's a strong reflection of the business model that we operate in. One of the other highlights t

items.statement: Corporate travel saw softness in IT/ITES volumes due to US/Canada tariff uncertainty but grew 2% overall
items.quote: The IT and ITES segment continues to be the largest contributor in our corporate travel business, and we saw some softness as far as volume is concerned because of the uncertainty around the large market like US and Canada. Having said so, our volumes continue to grow. We had a modest growth of about 2% in terms of volume on our corporate travel business.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded rating to AA, highest in India's travel and tourism sector, reaffirming group leadership and Fairfax parental support
items.quote: Before we get into the details of the results, I want to highlight CRISIL recently upgraded our rating to AA. This is the highest in India's trave l and tourism sector, and it's a clear reaffirmation of the group's leadership in the travel segment and strong parental support from Fairfax

items.statement: Sterling remains debt-free with cash reserves crossing INR3,000 million; free cash flow generated in Q1 over INR300 million
items.quote: We continue to remain a debt-free company, and our cash reserves have crossed more than INR3,000 million as we speak today. Our free cash flow generated during the quarter is a little over INR300 million.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; Sterling debt-free with strong cash generation
items.quote: We continue to remain a debt-free company, and our cash reserves have crossed more than INR3,000 million as we speak today.

items.quote: I'm happy to report that Thomas Cook is currently testing our in -house built travel solution for our customers called Travel One, integrated with AI, which is Dhruv, whic h essentially will allow customers to seamlessly manage their travel bookings. items.statement: Digital Imaging profitability improvement attributed entirely to cost control and reduction in indirect overheads, not top-line growth.
items.quote: The growth in profitability can be attributed entirely to the cost rather than on the top line. And this has come through careful cost control and cost reduction initiatives launched by the business.

items.statement: Digital Imaging top line impacted by conscious decision to weed out unprofitable accounts and renegotiate contracts.
items.quote: While we have also ensured that we went out and looked at our portfolio and weeded out some of the accounts where we thought that we weren't actually making a lot of money.

items.statement: Digital Imaging expects top-line growth in second half of FY26 and productivity gains from new software solution from Q3 onwards.
items.quote: We also expect the top line to start growing over time over the next couple of quarters more in the second half of the year rather than in the first half.

items.statement: Company follows asset-light model with no large capex plans; only small technology investments.
items.quote: asset-light model. Deepak, we've always been an asset-light model. Deepak: Or looking at any increase in dividend payout? Mahesh Iyer: No large investments. What we are looking at is only technology, some part of technology investments that we do, but they are small sums of money

items.statement: Management focused on margin management but refuses FY26 margin guidance due to geopolitical uncertainty and tactical competitiveness needs.
items.quote: Difficult, Deepak, to quantify that. I think previously, Mr. Verma asked this question, and I did mention that, look, we have to be a little more tactical at some points in time.

items.statement: Company aims to top industry growth rates (estimated 10-11%) but refuses 3-year consolidated growth guidance of 12-15%.
