items.quote: Typically, on the forex business, we have dependency, both on the Thomas Cook, SOTC because we sell a lot of that to our own customers, and we also deal with third -party, which are other traveler companies.

items.statement: Cash balance ~INR700 crores excluding BPC float; interest income rose from INR14 crores to INR22 crores YoY in Q1.
items.quote: Last year, out of INR266 million, INR140 million was interest income. And this year, out of INR440 million, INR219 million is interest income.

items.statement: Other income components: interest income (INR22 cr), sponsorship income (seasonal, not controlled), convenience fees, and INR11 mn forex gain; no forward range provided.
items.quote: I talked about the increases coming in from interest on fixed deposit, basically interest income. I talked about increase in sponsorship income and about the increase in collecting convenience charge from customers. And I did talk about INR11 million of foreign exchange gain.

items.statement: Thomas Cook India standalone remains in old tax regime (~34%) for next 3 years to utilize MAT credits; other Indian entities at 25% new regime.
items.quote: Thomas Cook, which is the -- or the Thomas Cook is the stand -alone company is obviously the largest contributor to profitability. And it still continues to be the old regime purely because there are some MAT credits that are still available.

items.statement: Sterling Resorts positioned upper mid-scale to upper upscale; strength in family leisure, growing corporate/MICE via Sterling ONE platform, and wedding segment in Rajasthan.
items.quote: We have positioned ourselves, as most of our mid-scale properties have actually moved up to an upper mid-scale level. Some of them have moved into an upscale level and some of the new ones are moving in the upper upscale level.

items.statement: Sterling Resorts tracks repeat guests (~15-18% and growing) and repeat corporate/MICE accounts (~90% hit rate); membership acquisition stopped, servicing existing members.
items.quote: In terms of the guests, it's actually -- in the last 2 years, we've started measuring and managing it pretty well. So actually, our ratio is approx imately 15% to 18% today, and it's growing significantly

items.statement: DMS business operates in highly fragmented market with thousands of local players globally; growth strategy is acquiring more B2B operator customers via trade shows and direct outreach.
items.quote: Praneeth, there are thousands of people like this, okay? Like Asian Trails. In Thailand, probably there are several thousand. I don't know how many thousand, honestly, but there are several thousand travel agents will be there.

items.statement: Disney Cruise Line tie-up for Singapore sailings targets younger generation and kids to build depth in cruise tourism.
items.quote: This is a new cruise line that's starting off to sail from Singapore. This is a new offering, both Thomas Cook and SOTC brands have a tie -up with them, and then we are looking to promote.

items.statement: Dividend payout increase decision rests with Board; management declines to comment.
items.quote: Look, it's a decision at the Board level. I wouldn't want to kind of give any commentary on it. As and when the Board discusses and feels it appropriate, obviously, we'll come to know about it.

items.statement: Digital Imaging building technology software solution expected to go live Q3 FY26, with productivity gains to be assessed over a quarter or two.
items.quote: Now, going forward, obviously, as you know, that we are also building a technology solution, a software, which will probably come into effect possibly from the third quarter onwards, and that should give us some productivity gains.

items.statement: Geopolitical upheavals and uncertain markets may require tactical competitiveness over margin enhancement in near term.
items.quote: The markets are a little uncertain. We are witnessing geopolitical upheavals. So clearly, we want to be staying cautious. We don't want to just say that we will focus on margin enhancements.

items.statement: BPC float growth drives interest income; float continues to grow supporting other income.
items.quote: As far as the interest income is concerned, it will also depend on the cash that we have and the BPC float that we have is -- obviously, is a significant portion of that. So if the BPC float continues to grow, the income will grow.

items.statement: Demand growth estimate raised to 7-8% for FY26 from earlier 6-7%
items.quote: We are up on our demand estimates by 1% from 6-7% before to now 7-8%.

items.statement: Target EBITDA of Rs 1,500 per metric tonne by 2028
items.quote: we have a blueprint to achieve our targeted EBITDA of Rs.1,500 per metric tonne by 2028.

items.statement: Green power share targeted to reach 60% by FY28 from 28.1% currently
items.quote: Green power share uptake with every passing quarter. It improved by 9.7% to 28.1% and it is targeted to reach 60% by FY28.

items.statement: Power cost targeted to reduce from Rs 5.9 per unit to Rs 4.5 per unit by FY28
items.quote: This will reduce the existing power cost which is around Rs.5.9 per unit to almost Rs.4.5 per unit by FY28.

items.statement: Heat consumption to improve by 35-40 kcal per kg of clinker
items.quote: Importantly, the heat consumption will improve by at least 35 to 40 kilo calorie per kg of clinker for the various initiatives outlined including mix of the new kilns.

items.statement: Primary lead distance targeted to reduce by almost 50 km by FY28
items.quote: Primary lead distance reduced by 8 km this quarter at 269 km and is expected to further reduce by almost 50 km when we achieve 140 million tonnes by FY28.

items.statement: Logistics cost targeted to reduce by almost Rs 150 per metric tonne by FY28
items.quote: This will help to reduce the logistics cost by almost Rs.150 per metric tonne, also supported by a higher component of rail and sea logistics.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 estimated at Rs 9,000-10,000 crore including Penna payments
items.quote: You can consider maybe couple of thousands. So, you can actually consider ballpark 1,000 here and there. So, 10,000 is a good amount to assume. I would have considered between say 9-10, but, yeah, 10 is okay. That includes Penna also.

items.statement: Total cement capacity at 104.5 MTPA; target 118 MTPA by end FY26 and 140 MTPA by FY28
items.quote: Our total cement capacity currently stands at 104.5 million tonnes. In our larger aim of achieving 140 million tonnes by FY28, we are well poised to achieve 118 million tonnes by end of FY26

items.statement: Commissioned 5 MTPA grinding capacity in last 3 months; target additional 13 MTPA this financial year
items.quote: We commissioned 5 million tonnes of grinding capacity over the last 3 months and target additional, another 13 million tonnes this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA per tonne at Rs 1,069, up 28% YoY; EBITDA margin 19.1%, up 3.8% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA per metric tonne of cement at Rs.1,069 of 28% YOY and EBITDA margin stood at 19.1%, up 3.8%

items.statement: Cost reduction journey ~35-40% complete (~Rs 175-200 per tonne of Rs 530 target)
items.quote: if I have to give a broad range, we would have hit almost 35%-40% of that journey by now. So, let us say closer to ₹200 a ton basically; ₹175 -₹200

items.statement: Highest ever sales volume of 18.4 million tonnes, up 20% YoY; market share up 2% to 15.5%
items.quote: Highest ever sales volume of 18.4 million tonnes, up 20% YOY with market share up 2% to 15.5%.

items.statement: Revenue crossed Rs 10,289 crore, up 23% YoY with 4% price gain; premium products 33% of trade sales, up 43% YoY
items.quote: Revenue crossed 10,000 crores mark at Rs.10,289 crores, up 23% YOY with price gain of 4% supported by higher share of premium products as a percentage of trade sales which is now at 33%, up by 43% YOY.

items.statement: Coal cost improved from Rs 1.73 to Rs 1.59 per 1000 kcal; expected to sustain near these levels
items.quote: Coal cost has improved from Rs.1.73 to Rs.1.59 per 1000 kilo calories and expected to sustain near these levels.

items.statement: Power consumption per tonne expected to improve by at least 5 units
items.quote: The power consumption per metric tonne of cement also is expected to improve by at least 5 units.

items.statement: Premium products share of trade sales at 33%, up 43% YoY
items.quote: higher share of premium products as a percentage of trade sales which is now at 33%, up by 43% YOY.

items.statement: More than 500 dealers returned to network; CEO se Samvad deepened channel engagement
items.quote: These efforts have sparked a strong homecoming of more than 500 dealers, strengthening our distribution network and reaffirming the mutual confidence.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with CRISIL AAA stable and A1+ ratings
items.quote: We continue to remain debt free. Our rating remains highest at CRISIL AAA stable and A1 plus ratings.

items.statement: Capacity utilisation ~77-78% on consolidated basis
items.quote: So therefore, on an overall capacity utilization, I am around 77-78%.

items.statement: Green power capacity at 473 MW (28.1% share); WHRS capacity at 228 MW
items.quote: In this quarter of 26, we commissioned 57.7 megawatt of wind energy, taking our total renewable power to 473 megawatt. Additionally, our WHRS capacity stands at 228 megawatt. Together, our green energy is contributing close to 28.1%

items.statement: Bhattapada project facing nominal delays of couple months due to brownfield execution complexity; no vendor or Chinese engineer issues
items.quote: Of course, projects of this scale, for example, when you have a brownfield expansion, a couple of months here and there, because you are operating for, you are actually executing in an established estate, which is also, should not be derailed in any form and manner. So these are, like, very nominal months, couple of months here and there. I do not see any issue or any anxiety over there.

items.statement: Merger of Adani Cementation received all statutory approvals; Sanghi and Penna received BSE/NSE approvals
items.quote: The merger of Adani Cementation Industries Limited has received all the statutory approvals. For Sanghi and Penna, we have received approvals from both the exchanges BSE and NSE and further process of completion is ongoing.

items.statement: Manpower cost among lowest in industry at Rs 223 per metric tonne
items.quote: We have one of the lowest manpower cost at Rs.223 per metric tonne amongst the peers in the industry.

items.statement: ACC cost disadvantage vs Ambuja ~Rs 300-400 per tonne due to captive coal mine, power cost, WHRS gap; investments underway to bridge gap
items.quote: Therefore, I said for ACC our primary efforts are to work 27 on the investments and the efficiencies gain on the cost and that will help us to bridge this gap of whatever ₹300-₹400 a ton and come to 4-digits sooner for ACC as well

items.statement: India net realisations expected to be Rs 2,000 per ton lower in Q2 vs Q1; UK and Netherlands flat or slightly higher
items.value: Rs 2,000 per ton lower (India); flat or slightly higher (UK, Netherlands)
items.quote: As far as the price is concerned, the guidance we're giving for India is that the net realisations will be about Rs 2,000 per ton less in 2Q as compared to 1Q. As far as UK and Netherlands are concerned, it will be flat or slightly higher.

items.statement: Coking coal consumption cost expected $10 per ton lower in Q2 vs Q1 across geographies; Netherlands iron ore cost $7-8 per ton lower
items.value: $10/t lower coking coal; $7-8/t lower iron ore (Netherlands)
items.quote: As far as cost is concerned, the coking coal costs are expected to be about $10 per ton lower in each of these geographies from a consumption point of view. And in Netherlands, the iron ore cost is also expected to be about $7 to $8 per ton lower from a consumption point of view for 2Q compared to 1Q.

items.statement: UK EBITDA breakeven targeted by end of FY2026 (Q4)
items.quote: But we still want to ensure that the FY2026 exit in 4Q is on a breakeven. That's actually the focus there.

items.statement: Board approved tinplate capacity doubling at Jamshedpur and investment to sustain captive coking coal mining capacity
items.quote: the Board of the company has yesterday approved the expansion of the tinplate business to almost double the capacity of the existing facilities in Jamshedpur and also invest to ensure sustainability of our captive coking coal mining capacity.

items.statement: UK EAF project at Port Talbot groundbreaking on 14 July 2025; construction started
items.quote: This quarter also marked a significant 3 milestone in UK’s transformation journey with the groundbreaking ceremony on 14th July at Port Talbot, marking the official start of construction for scrap based Electric Arc Furnace

items.statement: Ludhiana EAF (0.75 mt) and Jamshedpur Combi mill (0.5 mt) to add volumes in FY2027
items.quote: What you will see over the next 12 months is, of course, the Ludhiana plant coming into action that will add another 0.75 million tons and the Combi mill in Jamshedpur, which is 0.5 million tons, which converts some of the extra billets we have in the Gamharia plant into steel.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 EBITDA Rs 7,480 crores, up 11% QoQ; margin improved ~200 bps; per ton EBITDA up ~Rs 2,400
items.quote: The consolidated revenues for the quarter stood at Rs 53,178 crores, and the EBITDA was about Rs 7,480 crores. 1Q EBITDA increased by 11% on QoQ basis, translating to a margin improvement of about 200 basis points and per ton EBITDA improvement of around Rs 2,400.

items.statement: India standalone Q1 EBITDA Rs 7,263 crores, margin up 275 bps QoQ, per ton up Rs 2,600
items.quote: Tata Steel standalone revenues for the quarter ended Jun’25 was about Rs 31,014 crores and EBITDA was Rs 7,263 crores, which translates to 4 a margin improvement of about 275 basis points or Rs 2,600 per ton on QoQ basis

items.statement: India Q1 net realisations up Rs 2,600/t QoQ despite early monsoon; driven by April market prices and segment mix
items.quote: We could offset the impact of vol umes by an increase in net steel realisations to the tune of about Rs 2,600 per ton on QoQ basis in India. This is despite an early onset of the monsoons. Higher net realisations are partly on the back of increase in broader market prices in April and partly led by our ability to maximize volumes in certain chosen

items.statement: Coking coal consumption cost down $12/t QoQ in India; leaner coal mix and inventory management drove material cost decline of Rs 2,900 crores
items.quote: Within costs, material costs declined by about Rs 2,900 crores, primarily driven by decline in coking coal consumption cost by about $12 per ton as well as leaner coal mix and inventory management.

items.statement: India domestic demand weak in Q1 due to monsoon and maintenance shutdowns; expected pickup post-monsoon from construction, festival season, good monsoon
items.quote: Domestic demand is traditionally weak in this quarter, as you said, but we expect it to pick up once the monsoon ends for two reasons. One is, it looks like a good monsoon year and secondly, once monsoon is over, construction activity will start, and thirdly, the festival season is on to us.

items.statement: Engineering segment grew 5% YoY on oil & gas and railways volumes; solar steel volumes up 4x YoY
items.quote: The engineering segment grew 5% YoY on improved volumes to oil and gas and railways. Further enhanced product mix [inaudible] to solar (i.e. the steel that we supply for the solar panel supports) increased by 4 times the volume compared to 1QFY25.

items.statement: Kalinganagar continuous annealing line commissioned; grade approvals for high-strength/ultra-high-strength steels including skin panel; continuous galvanizing line first coil June, approvals underway
items.quote: six months of the continuous annealing line being commissioned in Kalinganagar, we have successfully established grade approvals for high strength and ultrahigh-strength steels, including for skin panel applications. We expect to make further progress with the commissioning of the state -of- the-art continuous galvanizing line at Kalinganagar. The first coil from the new co ntinuous galvanizing li

items.statement: Tata BlueScope JV sells ~300,000 tons color coated steel, largely via high-margin Durashine retail brand; 100 KTPA tube mill commissioned with direct forming technology
items.quote: This JV now sells around 300,000 tons of color coated steel, a large part of which is through the high-margin Durashine retail brand. During the quarter, we had also commissioned 100KTPA tubes mill, which utilizes an innovative direct forming technology that offers productivity and quality benefits over conventional mills.

items.statement: Working capital buildup in Q1 due to stock replenishment in India and Netherlands after strong Q4; optimisation expected in coming quarters as production improves
items.quote: There was working capital buildup primarily due to replenishment of stocks in Ind ia and in Netherlands after a strong 4Q. As the production improves in India, we expect that the optimi sation on working capital in the next quarters

items.statement: UK safeguard quotas exceed domestic demand; UK government intervening to align quotas with EU changes; US-UK melt-and-pour discussion ongoing
items.quote: UK steel safeguard quotas by product have been liberali sed every year and are now a larger proportion than even in 2018, when it was started, even as the UK demand has contracted. This meant that quotas for selected products ar e higher than the demand. The EU has already reworked the country quotas and the UK government is currently working to intervene in respect of the quotas

items.statement: Declared 14th consecutive interim dividend at Rs. 7.20 per share, representing ~27% payout on standalone earnings
items.quote: And we have declared the 14th consecutive interim dividend this time at Rs. 7.20 per share, representing a payout of about 27% on standalone earnings.

items.statement: Crude tanker trade flat year-on-year; product trade flat with long-haul East-West trade weak; dry bulk coal trade declining, iron ore up slightly, grain trade down
items.quote: The dirty trade, which is a crude tanker trade, was flat year-on-year in the 1st Quarter. And which means that demand basically has plateaued.

items.statement: Crude tanker rates $33,800/day vs $46,000 YoY; product tankers ~$25,000 vs $37,000 YoY; LPG up to $43,800 from $36,700; bulk carriers ~$15,000 from $18,000 YoY
items.quote: So, you see, Q1 FY '25 we had the crude tankers averaging $46,000 a day, which is down to $33,800 in Q1 FY '26. The product tankers averaging $37,000 versus just under $25,000.

items.statement: Order books at 12% for crude tankers, 20% for product tankers, 10-11% for bulk carriers, 30% for LPG
items.quote: The order books have been building up in the last couple of years. It's still currently at 12% and 20% for crude and product tankers, respectively.

items.statement: No change in switch strategy; eager to replace older ships but delta capital unchanged; currently focused on replacement not expansion; in-chartered one Suezmax in GIFT City
items.quote: We are as eager, as earlier, to continue with the switch strategy. You should just keep in mind that if asset values have come down 20%-30%. Basically they come out for the ships we are going to buy, and the ships are going to replace them with.

items.statement: Standalone net cash ~$600M; consolidated net cash ~$700M; loan of Rs. 450 cr to subsidiary GIL for 2.5 years due to cash trapped overseas
items.quote: We have now net cash of about $600 million on a standalone basis. In the group, we have net cash of about $700 million, including the subsidiaries.

items.statement: Spot exposure: crude tankers 100%, dry bulk 80-90%, product tankers ~70%; offshore vessels mostly fixed through year, 4 of 19 on spot/short contracts
items.quote: The spot exposure in crude tankers is 100%. Spot exposure for dry bulk is probably around 80% to 90%. And when I say spot exposure, that means contracts of less than six months and for product tankers is probably around 85%, sorry for product tankers is about 70% spot exposure.

items.statement: Offshore segment profit rose QoQ (Rs. 82 cr to Rs. 126 cr) despite lower revenue due to idling rigs cutting opex; vessels contribution higher with no extra cost
items.quote: The vessels business has given a much higher contribution in the revenue. And while the rig business, because two of our rigs are effectively idling, the revenue dropped. Now what has happened because of that is that the rigs when they are idling, we bring down the operating expenses to the bare minimum and therefore we save a lot of costs there.

items.statement: US tariff on Chinese-built ships diluted: exemptions within 2,000 nm of US and under 81,000 DWT; impact only 2-3% of world trade; EU lowered Russian oil price cap to $45 from Sep
items.quote: If you are trading within 2,000 nautical miles of U.S., they are exempted. If you are below 81,000 tonnes, they are exempted. So, we have done a calculation to see what is the impact of the Chinese owned, Chinese built and it only comes to about a few percentages meaning like 2% or 3% of the entire world trade that would get liable for this tax or tariff.

items.statement: Outlook: market strong but unlikely to rise further; needs demand uptick or logistical disruption; economies not doing well so cycle may hold or weaken
items.quote: The market's been strong. So, it's tough to see what can drive it upwards. For the market to get stronger, you need either end user demand to go up or you need some logistical disruption which makes the fleet less efficient.

items.statement: Shipping opex Rs. 270 cr vs Rs. 300-330 cr run rate due to 10% smaller fleet, cost reduction efforts, and Q4 high base effect; spares/stores timing may shift to Jul-Aug
items.quote: One is the lower number of ships that we are operating as compared to, we have a 10% lower fleet versus Q1 of last year. The other thing is that we have actually had some reduction in costs, we have been focused on seeing how we can do some cost reductions, so that is one minor thing.

items.statement: Standalone NAV Rs. 1,120/share vs Rs. 1,181 YoY, up slightly from March; consolidated NAV small drop; share price at ~2/3 of consolidated NAV
items.quote: Just here we have the standalone net asset value at the bottom, which is at Rs. 1,120 per share, down from Rs. 1,181 a year ago, which is of course due to the drop in the values of assets, but up from March, up slightly from the March number.

items.statement: Shipping: <15% fleet with PSUs; Offshore: 2 rigs with largest PSU customer, 1 short-term PSU contract; majority of India vessels work for ONGC directly/indirectly
items.quote: In the shipping business, it is a small part. When you say government, I am including PSUs, it is a small part of the business. Maybe less than 15% of our fleet is engaged in PSU business, in shipping.

items.statement: Acquired one Kamsarmax; crude fleet reduced as older ships exited during 2022-23 high asset prices; intend to increase crude fleet again; no incremental purchases currently
items.quote: to increase the crude fleet again. So, what happened was, and another participant asked us on this call on our switching strategy. So, what happened is, in 2022, once the Russian war took place, of course, the market increased substantially along with the asset prices increased as well

items.statement: No management changes discussed; board has not discussed buyback; dividend policy considers capital needs for fleet modernization/expansion
items.quote: No, there has been no discussion around buyback at the board level and when we do that there will be all appropriate disclosures.

items.statement: LPG trade growing strongly; China 10% tariff on US LPG exports rerouted some cargoes to SE Asia/India, China buying more from Middle East; slight tonne-mile improvement
items.quote: If you look at LPG, China has a 10% tariff on exports from the U.S. So, we have seen some of the U.S. exports of LPG go to certain other Southeast countries, including India as well. And then we have seen China pick up more cargoes from the Middle East.

items.statement: Fuel cost only borne on voyage charters (small fleet portion); crew cost largest fixed opex at $3,000-3,500/day; maintenance ~$2,000/day; direct fuel price exposure minimal
items.quote: So, the largest fixed cost component for running a ship is crew expenses, which works out to around $3,000 a day. So, that's the largest, $3,000 to $3,500 a day, that's the largest fixed cost expense.

items.statement: Saudi Aramco suspended 20-25 jack-up rig contracts in Apr-May 2024, causing rate drop from ~$80-90k/day to ONGC tender range below $40k/day; took lower rate to avoid idling
items.quote: What happened in early 2024 is that Saudi Aramco, which is the largest hirer of rigs, customer for jack-up rigs, suspended contracts for between 20 and 25 rigs in April, May 2024, that resulted in a change in the market. And therefore, the market sentiment went down and rates went down as well.

items.statement: No fund raise discussed; ECB refinancing for GIL loan of Rs. 450 cr over 2.5 years using surplus cash (<7-8% of standalone cash) that returns to parent
items.quote: What we felt now is that the amount of cash which is sitting with Great Eastern Shipping is not something that we can deploy within this period. And therefore, this is effectively surplus cash at least for the next two and a half years, and we decided to do it now.

items.statement: No acquisitions/divestments discussed beyond Kamsarmax purchase and in-charter of Suezmax; no M&A activity mentioned
items.quote: We have actually in-charted one of the ships in our subsidiary in Gift City, which is a Suezmax tanker, one of the largest crude tankers. So, we have done that. But at the moment, we are not looking for any incremental purchases.

items.statement: No asset quality metrics discussed (non-bank/insurer); scrapping minimal across sectors due to decent earnings covering opex and dry-docking
items.quote: Of course, with these earnings and the earnings even in dry bulk have been pretty decent. It more than covers operating expenses and even if you have to do a dry dock in that year, and therefore the scrapping has been very minimal.

items.statement: CSR foundation partners with NGOs to transform lives; no further details provided
items.quote: And finally, something that we are proud of which is the foundation which works in the CSR, social sector. We are partnered with many NGOs, and we have hopefully helped to transform many lives.

items.statement: Management does not provide guidance on volumes, margins, or VAVE benefits
items.quote: We don't give guidance.

items.statement: Royal Enfield sold 261,326 motorcycles in Q1 FY26, up 14.7% YoY
items.quote: During this quarter, we sold 2,61,326 motorcycles with a growth of 14.7% as against 2,27,736 in Q1 of FY2025.

items.statement: International volumes grew 41.2% YoY to 32,547 units in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our volumes stood at about 32,547 units, marking a growth of 41.2% over the last year.

items.statement: VECV sold 21,610 units in Q1 FY26, exceeding previous record of 19,702 units
items.quote: VECV, we recorded a quarter sales of 21,610 units, exceeding our previous record of 19,702 units in Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Eicher HD Trucks sold 4,580 units with 8.8% market share in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Eicher HD Trucks, the first quarter sales of 4,580 units and FY '25 Q1 was 4,689 units with a market share of about 8.8%.

items.statement: LMD Trucks sold 8,610 units with 34.45% market share in Q1 FY26
items.quote: LMD Trucks, first quarter sale of 8,610 units against 7,842 units of Q1 with a leading market share of about 34.45%.

items.statement: Bus division sold 6,000 units with 21.5% market share in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our Bus division, our sales stood at about 6,000 units in the first quarter against last quarter -- last first quarter of 5,232 units with 21.5% market share

items.statement: VECV exports grew 20% YoY to 1,436 units in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Exports in Q1 grew to about 1,436 units, registering a robust growth of 20% over Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: EML consolidated EBITDA was INR 1,203 crores vs INR 1,165 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our EBITDA is about INR1,203 crores versus INR1,165 crores in Q1 last year.

items.statement: EML consolidated PAT was INR 1,205 crores, up 9.4% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: PAT at INR1,205 crores, up by 9.4% from INR1,101 crores in Q1 last year.

items.statement: VECV EBITDA was INR 511 crores, 33% higher YoY; EBITDA margin 9% vs 7.6%
items.quote: EBITDA for VECV Q1 FY '26 is INR511 crores, 33% higher versus INR385 crores last year. Our EBITDA margin for Q1 is about 9% against 7.6% last year same quarter.

items.statement: VECV PAT was INR 289 crores vs INR 321 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: PAT for Q1 is at INR289 crores as against INR321 crores last year same time.

items.statement: Commodity inflation impacted margins by 50 bps, offset by 20 bps VAVE and price increases
items.quote: This quarter, we've had an impact of about 50 bps. Out of that, we've got an offset because of VAVE, which was mentioned earlier of about 20 bps. So net impact is about 30 bps.

items.statement: Price increases taken in April and July to offset commodity inflation
items.quote: We have taken a pricing increase in the month of April and now because of the inflationary pressure, to some extent in the first month of July.

items.statement: Rare earth material supply issues affected Himalayan/Scram production in Q1; alternative materials now in use
items.quote: In the first quarter, we had that issue in those products. So there is a bit of a problem on production because those are all performance platforms. In the performance platform, rare earth materials were used in gear sensors, in alternators and other areas. So we had a bit of a pressure point, and we have to stop it, then we have to start with alternative materials.

items.statement: Rare earth risk mitigated; alternative material imports not a major issue
items.quote: Currently, we are back on production with the alternative material, which we have protected. Now that alternative material import is not a major issue for us. We are out of that situation of that challenge.

items.statement: Royal Enfield capacity is 1.2 million units across Oragadam and Vallam plants; currently operating at ~90% utilization
items.quote: Our capacity stated is with both the plants, which is Oragadam and Vallam, which is where we are manufacturing all our motorcycles for across the globe. We have stated a capacity of almost about 1.2 million. And currently, you are right, we are operating at almost about 90% of that.

items.statement: Capacity expansion will be modular; capex focus is on new products rather than heavy capacity enhancement
items.quote: Our capacity build up will take place in modules. We don't need to actually go in for a heavy capacity enhancement. Focus on the capex is more on the new products.

items.statement: Hunter 350 running at 17,000-17,500 units/month; new colors gaining traction
items.quote: Hunter, as of now, if I have to tell you, it is coming around 17,000 to 17,500 numbers per month, which is slightly lower and especially the new colors, which is actually gaining a very good traction.

items.statement: Bullet sold ~50,000 units in Q1; Battalion Black driving growth in rural markets
items.quote: In fact, in Q1, we sold about 50,000 units of the Bullet. That's what -- that's the number. It has received a very Eicher Motors Limited July 31, 2025 solid response from the

items.statement: Rural state mix increased from ~30% to ~50% of sales driven by accessible products
items.quote: Potentially the mix of rural states used to be about 30% of our sales, and now it's closer to 50% of our sales. So even therefore, there is increased sales, which is happening predominantly on the back of some of our more accessible products which are coming.

items.statement: Floor financing enabled for ~575 dealers, majority rural, to support festive season churn
items.quote: I think almost about some 575 dealers already have signed up for floor financing. And majority is the rural customers -- I mean, sorry, rural dealers more because that is where the finance availability was a bit tough for them.

items.statement: Brazil CKD expansion with second assembler; finance schemes being developed with banks
items.quote: In the Brazil market, we wanted to have a product which is at a very accessible price point. In fact, Vidhya and team are actually working on the finance scheme in those markets. items.quote: The EV penetration of two -wheeler industry is at 6.3%. TVS iQube has done pretty well, and it has surpassed 6 lakh unit sales, continuing its market leadership in India

items.statement: EV three-wheeler King EV Max doing extremely well; scaling further with new launches next quarter
items.quote: Our recently launched EV three-wheeler, TVS King EV Max is doing extremely well. Customers are definitely liking it and the response is very positive. We'll be scaling it further.

items.statement: Norton new products to be unveiled in Q3/Q4 FY26, available in Europe from Q1 FY27
items.quote: On Norton, all of you know that end of this financial year, we'll be launching products, multiple new products. And they will be available in the first quarter of next year to many markets in Europe, and this is as per plan.

items.statement: Expect ~0.5% commodity cost increase in Q2; small price increases taken at Q2 start
items.quote: See, commodity, I think there is an increase in Q2. Some of the, like you said, areas like steel, my expectation is about 0.5% -- 0.5% could be the increase. Steel is the predominant one in that and other commodities are small increases are there. We have also taken up small price increases, in Q2 beginning.

items.statement: Facing rare earth magnet supply challenges; managing daily production with local stocks and resized magnets
items.quote: All of us know that there are certain challenges in the availability of magnet. We are trying to mitigate it. There are challenges in the short term, but we are also working along with a certain long-term action.

items.statement: Working on HRE-free, ferrite-based and magnet-free motor solutions for medium-long term resilience
items.quote: But if you look at on a medium- and a long-term basis, we are working on HRE-free, ferrite-based, magnet-free, and we are also looking at alternate countries. And definitely, we'll be also working partnering with some of them in India.

items.statement: Scooterization increasing in rural areas due to better infrastructure; rural growth 3.3% vs 4% overall in Q1
items.quote: Scooterization is pretty well even in the rural. The proportional scooters are also becoming better. I think most important is the infrastructure development, the roads, even in the rural areas are becoming better and better.

items.statement: Growing ahead of industry in both domestic and international markets across ICE and EV
items.quote: Overall, both in domestic and international markets, with the range of products that we have, we are able to do well, and we will continue to do better than the industry.

items.statement: Exports revenue INR 2,487 crores in Q1 FY26; highest ever quarterly export volume of 3.52 lakh units
items.quote: Exports about INR2,487 crores.

items.statement: Africa demand stabilizing and growing; LATAM growing ahead of industry with low share; Sri Lanka recovering
items.quote: Africa market has started doing well. Like I said, last year, we saw the numbers going down primarily because of many geopolitical challenges, inflation and currency challenges. Now things are becoming a bit stable.

items.statement: ABS norms discussions ongoing with government via SIAM; rider safety is highest priority
items.quote: As -- I can talk about because in the two-wheeler category in SIAM, we are all together, we are discussing with the government. I think we will -- as of now, the discussions are going on.

items.statement: NCD issuance planned to meet SEBI 25% capital market borrowing mandate; enabling resolution
items.quote: NCD funding, if you know that the SEBI has mandated the 25% based on the incremental (previous year's ) borrowings has to be only in the form of a capital market funding. And therefore, the current year's requirements is being funded through this raise of NCD.

items.statement: TVS Credit IPO not yet discussed at Board level; book size ~INR 27,000 crores
items.quote: TVS Credit Services, I think the book size is around INR 27,000 crores now, INR 26,898 crores to be precise. And as far as the question is all about IPO, not yet even discussed at the Board level.

items.statement: EV revenue ~INR 1,000 crores in Q1 FY26 on 70,000 units
items.quote: Around INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Rare earth magnet shortage causing daily production management; short-term mitigation via local sourcing
items.quote: See, short term, we are managing with the stocks what we have. We also resized some higher-sized magnets, which are locally available. We are also exploring some alternate strategies in the short term, okay?

items.statement: Monsoon flood risk could impact rural recovery despite early sowing and high reservoir levels
items.quote: But what is a little bit of concern is we cannot h ave, on the other side, a little bit over rain and flood. So we are positive. And rural should come back for the season

items.statement: Management targets 20-30% revenue growth for FY26, with 20% as minimum visible and 30% as aspirational
items.quote: But still, I feel we will happily achieve 20% but the focus I had said earlier, that our new growth will be coming from new titles which will support us. So we have a major releases this year. So we're still trying we should achieve 30% this year as well.

items.statement: Content cost guided at 25-28% of revenue for FY26
items.quote: Yes, 25% to 28%, yes, that is the number, yes.

items.statement: Management expects minimum 20% PAT growth for FY26 on annual basis
items.quote: So annualized basis, minimum 20% PAT growth will be there this year, right? Sushant Dalmia: Yes, yes absolutely right.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 operating margin at 64%, PAT at INR45.7 crores with 5% YoY growth
items.quote: Our revenue for the quarter amounted to INR88 crores, resulting in Y-o-Y growth of 19%. The content cost increased 85% on a Y-o-Y basis as we had new releases, which were expense off during the quarter. Factoring the above, the operating margins came in at 64%, while PAT was at INR45.7 crores, resulting in a Y-o-Y growth of 5%.

items.statement: Content cost written off INR20.5 crores in Q1 FY26 vs INR9.5 crores in Q1 FY25 due to 3 big film releases
items.quote: If you see this quarter last year, it was around INR9 crores, INR9.5 crores. This quarter, we have written off INR20.5 crores. So we have 3 big films came in. So we have written off everything.

items.statement: YouTube growth expectation lowered to 15-18% from earlier 25-30% estimate
items.quote: Earlier, we used to estimate YouTube will grow by 25%, 30%. But now we YouTube will grow by at least 15%, 18%.

items.statement: YouTube Shorts views fluctuate cyclically, impacting overall YouTube viewership trends
items.quote: Yes, that's mainly due to Shorts. So it keeps on fluctuating. So YouTube Short views keep going up and down. That's very cyclical.

items.statement: Catalogue consumption growing steadily across all audio and video streaming platforms
items.quote: We track that, but we'll not be able to disclose the absolute numbers. But we are seeing a growth in our catalogue consumption across all the audio streaming and video streaming platforms.

items.statement: YouTube Shorts monetization currently on lump sum deal for one more year, then may shift to per-view basis
items.quote: Other platforms, we are doing well. YouTube, we have a fixed deal. But even on YouTube, I think this fixed deal is for one more year. And after that, we'll see what will happen.

items.statement: YouTube Shorts contract renewal expected in 6-8 months, management aims for per-stream monetization
items.quote: Next year, YouTube Shorts service contract is getting over. But it's very early to say anything about that. We have not started talking to them. We will finalize in the next 6, 8 months by talking to them, and we'll come to some conclusion. But I feel it will be a raise. But our main target will be on per view or per stream basis.

items.statement: Digital revenue share at 72-75%, non-digital at 25-30%, with Sony Music Publishing deal contributing to non-digital growth
items.quote: We are doing well on other side, nondigital. But ultimately, it will be between 72% to 75%, and that other business will be in the range of 25%, 30%. Here and there, it will keep on happening.

items.statement: Warner Music contribution increased to 25-30% of revenue in Q1 FY26 from 20-25% in FY25
items.quote: As said earlier also, between 25% and 30% will be money coming from Warners.

items.statement: OTT platforms like Resso, Wynk, Gaana, Hungama shut down or moved to paid models, impacting revenue
items.quote: Last year, money came in from Resso, then there wereother apps, such as Wynk which was doing good business. And then there was Gaana, Hungama, so many apps, they had shut down or they had gone behind the paid war

items.statement: YouTube policy changes restricting UGC content usage and monetization, reducing piracy but causing short-term growth slowdown
items.quote: The policies now restrict UGC content usage and monetization. This is good for us as music industry in the longer run, as third-party pirates use our music to monetize from the platform.

items.statement: In-house content management system Pulse built by existing teams, delivers content via DDEX feeds to TikTok and other DSPs, no additional employee cost
items.quote: Our teams have built an in-house content management system called Pulse, which now delivers our content to TikTok and other DSPs via our own DDEX feeds.

items.statement: First interim dividend of INR4 per share declared for FY26; dividend policy distributes previous year's PAT (INR166 crores) as dividends in current fiscal
items.quote: The Board has declared a first interim dividend of INR4 per share for FY 2026.

items.statement: Dividend policy: distribute last year's PAT (INR166 crores) as dividends in current fiscal year
items.quote: And l as a policy, what we have formed is whatever is the last year's PAT, we will distribute as dividend in this fiscal year. So , last year, we earned around INR166 crores in PAT. So that will get distributed this year in form of dividends.

items.statement: YouTube subscribers at 125.8 million with 20% CAGR over 2 years; key songs crossing 100M+ views
items.quote: Additionally, we now have 125.8 million subscribers on YouTube with a compound aggregate growth rate of 20% over the last 2 years.

items.statement: Content payback target 3 years internally, communicated as 4-5 years externally; entire content cost written off in quarter of release
items.quote: We always say internally, we want our payback should be within 3 years. But people like you, we say please keep it for 4 to 5 years. But there is a big catch here. We write off entire content in the same quarter.

items.statement: Industry-wide challenges from OTT platforms moving to paid walls, Spotify restricting free tier, Amazon launching paid service
items.quote: day by day the appsare becoming more strict-- like Spotify, they are not allowing people to new releases again and again, they tell you to come on a paid wall. So that paid wall simultaneously is increasing

items.statement: YouTube policy changes curbing pirated content causing short-term growth impact, but rebounding in July
items.quote: So it is trying curb those activities. So that is a little change that we see over there. But again, that should be not the long-term one. It should be a short-term impact only. And we are seeing slightly growth again rebounding in the month of July.

items.statement: Released 92 songs in FY25 (48 film, 42 non-film); focus on quality over quantity for new acquisitions
items.quote: We released 92 songs in FY '25, including 48 film songs and 42 non-film songs.

items.statement: Content acquisition budget fixed at 25-28% of revenue; per-song metric not used due to cost variance between film and non-film songs
items.quote: Primarily, we have a fixed budget. Let's say, for this year, , we are targeting 25% to 28% of our revenue to be spent on new content. So we go by that budget.

items.statement: Blackstone Funds acquired 14.3% equity stake via preferential allotment infusing Rs. 417 crore, largely for growth capital; SEBI approval awaited for open offer
items.quote: During the quarter Blackstone Funds acquired 14.3% equity stake through preferential allotment infusing Rs. 417 crore in the Company which will largely be used as growth capital.

items.statement: Guiding 30%+ year-on-year presales growth for FY26, building on 23% CAGR over last 3-4 years
items.quote: And with all these thing, we are quite confident that this year as well, we will have 30% plus year -on-year growth in terms of the presale guidance.

items.statement: Launch pipeline of 6-7 million sq ft across Pune and Mumbai for FY26, with NIBM, Wadgaon, Kharadi, Life Republic sectors in Pune and Laxmi Ratan Versova in Mumbai
items.quote: We are looking a total pipeline of around 6 million to 7 million square feet across Pune and Mumbai region.

items.statement: Unsold inventory of ongoing/completed projects at 3.5 million sq ft
items.quote: So as we have already mentioned in our investor presentation, it is almost 3.5 million square feet.

items.statement: Gross margin 35% in Q1 FY26; expect gross margin 25-30% and EBITDA margin in mid-teens for FY26, improving from FY25's 13% EBITDA margin
items.quote: And we see the gross margin in the range of around 25% to 30%, and the EBITDA will remain in the mid-teens.

items.statement: Average realization stable at Rs. 7,337 per sq ft in Q1 FY26; focus on mid-to-mid-premium and luxury segments with 8% CAGR in APR over 4-5 years
items.quote: In Q1 FY26, our average realization stood at Rs. 7,337 per square foot, maintaining stable pricing levels.

items.statement: Residential demand in Pune driven by end-users seeking lifestyle upgrade and infrastructure growth; Mumbai poised for transformation from infrastructure development improving connectivity
items.quote: In Pune, the residential segment appears to be entering a more measured phase of growth with demand driven by end -users seeking lifestyle upgrade and infrastructure growth.

items.statement: Of Rs. 417 crore Blackstone infusion, Rs. 100-105 crore earmarked for general corporate purposes, rest for growth capital including premium and FSI costs
items.quote: But at the same time, Rs.100 crore s- Rs.105 crores is been earmarked for the general corporate purpose. And rest of the capital we are targeting to be for the growth capital, including premium and FSI and all that related cost.

items.statement: Collections at Rs. 550 crore in Q1 FY26, in line with contracted schedule; 4-year collections CAGR of 21%; expect steady CAGR growth in collections for FY26
items.quote: Collections stood at Rs. 550 crore , remaining in line with the contracted schedule. Over a 4 year period, collections have grown at a CAGR of 21% as a result of construction and operational efficiency, healthy pace of project execution and strong customer relationship management.

items.statement: Net debt negative Rs. 320 crore (net cash) as of June 30, 2025, improved from negative Rs. 37 crore a year ago; Blackstone infusion further strengthened capital base
items.quote: Net debt stood at a negative Rs.320 crores as compared to negative Rs.37 crores as on 30 th June 2024. Additionally, the equity infusion from Blackstone during the quarter has further strengthened our capital base, enhancing our liquidity position and supporting our growth ambitions.

items.statement: Wadgaon project (5 million sq ft potential) to launch in 3-4 phases, Phase 1 of ~1.5 million sq ft; Life Republic sectors R10, R31, R17 and Little Earth phase targeting completion in FY26
items.quote: So out of which we have well planned with 3 or 4 odd phases for the entire project to get launched. So the phase 1 will be around 1.5 million square feet of the launch and for which we are in the phase of securing all the approvals.

items.statement: Operating cash flow Rs. 164 crore in Q1 FY26 vs Rs. 247 crore in Q1 FY25; sales volume 0.84 million sq ft (5% QoQ growth); sales value Rs. 616 crore
items.quote: Resultantly, operating cash flows stood strong at Rs. 164 crore.

items.statement: Some Mumbai projects (Goregaon, Vishwakarma Nagar, Jal Nidhi, Dahisar) delayed due to eco-sensitive zone environment clearance and height clearance issues; industry-wide issue
items.quote: However, there are a few projects which are mainly on account of certain eco -sensitive zone related environment clearance approval, which are a little bit getting delayed. There are 2 projects at Dahisar, which are delayed in launches on account of pending height clearance.

items.statement: Actively evaluating strong pipeline of BD opportunities across focus markets; several deals at advanced stages, post due diligence and final documentation; intend to expand footprint in MMR beyond redevelopment
items.quote: Yes, we are looking at quite a few active transactions and much more at an advanced stages. Few documents has reached to a stage, crossed the due diligence and on the final documentation as well.

items.statement: Blackstone partnership expected to strengthen growth; strategic roles and board representation to be determined after transaction concludes

items.statement: Revenue growth target for FY26 revised to 11-13% from earlier 14-15% due to weak Q1
items.quote: So I think about 11% to 12%; 11% to 13% is what we'll be aiming for this current financial year because first quarter has been extremely challenging.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 set at 8.5-9.5%
items.quote: Margins, I think we should be between 8.5% to 9.5% in this financial year. So let's see how it goes.

items.statement: Q1 revenue declined 0.7% YoY to INR 1,466 crore due to weak summer and high base
items.quote: Consolidated net revenue from operations for the quarter is INR 1,466 crores, a marginal decline of 0.7% over the revenue recorded in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

items.statement: Consumer Durables segment revenue degrew 16.3% YoY due to early monsoon curtailing summer season
items.quote: In the Consumer Durable s segment, covering Fan s, Water Heaters, Kitchen Appliances and Air Coolers, we reported a revenue de growth of 16.3% Y-o-Y. Growth was impacted by early onset of monsoon, which curtailed the summer season and caused a sharp drop in demand for cooling products

items.statement: Electronics segment grew 4.5% YoY with Stabilizers subdued but Inverter Battery and Solar performing well
items.quote: The Electronics segment comprising of Stabilizers, Inverter Systems, UPS Systems and Solar Systems delivered moderate revenue growth at 4.5% Y-o-Y in the first quarter. Demand for Stabilizers was subdued in line with the overall demand trends for cooling products. But this is offset by good growth for other products within the segment.

items.statement: Electrical segment grew 7.6% YoY with Wires, Switches and Switchgears performing well
items.quote: The Electrical segment, which remains our largest revenue contributor that includes Wire s, Pumps, Switchgear and Modular Switches, registered a Y -o-Y growth of 7.6%. Hence, the performance was steady, both from a top line and margin perspective

items.statement: Gross margin at 36.7% in Q1 FY26 vs 36.6% YoY, up 110 bps sequentially from Q4 FY25
items.quote: We reported a gross margin of 36.7% this quarter compared to 36.6% in Q1 last year. On a sequential basis, the gross margin improved by around 110 basis points from 35.5% in Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 8.4% in Q1 FY26 from 10.5% YoY due to operating deleverage
items.quote: EBITDA, excluding other income, for Q1 stood at INR 124 crores, declining 20.7% on a Y-o-Y basis. The EBITDA margin was 8.4%, a reduction of 210 basis points from 10.5% recorded in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Electronics segment sustainable margin around 17%, not 18-19%
items.quote: Margin wise, it's been good, but I don't think we should take 18%, 19% as a steady state margin. So there are some quarters where we get better margins than usual. Something like 17% should be okay.

items.quote: So currently, we're at 65%. We have 1 factory, which is 1 more plant for Fan s, which is undergoing development. We expect that to be operational in 18 months' time

items.quote: Initially, we are not looking at manufacturing. I think with regards to most of our categories that we have entered, they have been seeded by the outsourcing model. We are looking at the consumer part of the Lighting and the residential part of the

items.quote: We have also initiated actions to merge Sunflame operations with V -Guard, which will fast track a realization of th e synergy benefits. items.statement: Non-South markets revenue grew 2.1% YoY to 52.3% of total; South market degrew 3.3% YoY
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, revenues from non-South markets grew by 2.1% Y-o-Y now contributing 52.3% of the total revenues, while South market degrew by negative 3.3% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increased across sector; private labels not a major threat in differentiated categories
items.quote: I think the hyper competition today is among our various brands. I don't think private label is such a big worry, at least in India. items.statement: Sunflame CSD channel remains soft but general trade improving; 24-hour call resolution up to 60% post integration
items.quote: For example, we have about 70 days, we have integrated the customer service nationally. And what I would say, the call resolution rates, 24-hour call resolution rates have gone up to almost 60%.

items.statement: Solar PV module and lithium supply chain uncertainty due to potential US antidumping duties and global oversupply
items.quote: So I think definitely it is a supply and demand issue. So we'll wait and see. So for example, if suddenly U.S. is going to ban or slap antidumping duty for Indian PV manufacturers or cell manufacturers, definitely, that would mean lower prices in India.

items.statement: No revenue projections for Lighting segment yet; will update after 6-12 months of capability building
items.quote: No, we wouldn't like to give out any projections as of now. We will update in the next call. I don't think we'll be giving more projections anyway. But our first 6 months to 12 months, we'll be setting up capability and systems and then only we will look at launching.

items.statement: Targets 12% loan growth for FY26 and aims to become net zero NPA company by end of FY26
items.quote: We are very confident that our strong fundamentals will continue to drive a very strong demand in both the power sector, the renewable sector and in the infrastructure sector. And we feel that 12% loan growth can be reasonably achieved in the coming quarters. We are targeting on an overall, this year, we are targeting around 12% growth.

items.statement: Expects spread to remain 2.75%-3% and NIM 3.5%-3.75% going forward
items.quote: Going forward, we are confident that our spread will remain in the region of 2.75% to 3% and our NIM in the range of 3.5% to 3.75%.

items.statement: Strong demand expected across power, renewable and infrastructure sectors
items.quote: We are very confident that our strong fundamentals will continue to drive a very strong demand in both the power sector, the renewable sector and in the infrastructure sector.

items.statement: Sanctioned over INR1 lakh crore in Q1 FY26; distribution 43%, renewables 20% of sanctions
items.quote: During Q1 itself, REC has sanctioned more than INR1 lakh crores worth of projects. The renewable energy remains to be the dominant force wherein we have sanctioned around 20% of the power projects. The distribution remains the largest area with 43% of the total sanctions made in the Q1 FY 26.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly disbursement of INR59,508 crore in Q1 FY26, up 36% YoY
items.quote: REC recorded its highest ever quarterly disbursement in Q1 FY 26, wherein we recorded total disbursements of INR59,508 crores, which was up 36% from the last year.

items.statement: Gross NPA 1.05%, Net NPA 0.24% as of June 2025; resolved TRN Energy INR1,504 crore; 11 remaining NPAs INR6,147 crore with 77.05% provision coverage
items.quote: We are happy to inform you that during Q1 FY 26, REC has resolved one stressed asset, TRN Energy worth almost INR1,504 crores, resulting in gross NPA coming down to 1.05% as of 30th June 2025 and net NPA to 0.24%. The remaining 11 NPAs totalling to about INR6,147 crores have provision coverage of more than 77% , 77.05% to be precise, which are being resolved through NCLT.

items.statement: Targets net zero NPA by end of FY26; expects INR700-800 crore additional provision reversals during FY26
items.quote: We expect that we have already reversed INR270 crores against TRN. And we further expect that in case if all these assets are dissolved, the total reversal would be around INR700 crores to INR800 crores during the year itself. That is the minimum which we are expecting.

items.statement: DISCOM AT&C losses improved to 16.3%; 40 of 63 utilities showed improvement; ACS-ARR gap decreased by INR0.20/unit
items.quote: In the last ratings of the DISCOMs, which we carried out, the high AT&C losses of previous years have come down to 16.3%. Almost 40 out of 63 utilities saw an improvement in their AT&C losses. The ACS-ARR gap has further decreased by INR0.20 per unit.

items.statement: Yield improved to 10.08% from 9.99% YoY; cost of funds 7.12%; spread 2.96%
items.quote: On the key ratios front, the yield has improved to 10.08% from 9.99% in the last financial year. Cost of funds at 7.12%. The interest spread is at 2.96%.

items.statement: Kalinganagar greenfield ferrochrome expansion: first furnace June 2026, second furnace September 2026

items.statement: 120 KLD ethanol project at Therubali construction commenced in Q1, on track for commissioning by Q4 FY26
items.quote: The construction work in our 120 KLD ethanol project in Therubali has also commenced in Q1 and we are on track of commissioning the plant by Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Underground Sukinda Mines expansion progressing as per schedule
