items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the group has reported highest ever quarterly revenue of INR 3,549 crore, which is actually an increase of 13.4% on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: India Security revenue grew 9.2% YoY to INR 1,460 crore in Q1 FY26
items.quote: India Security has reported its highest ever revenue at INR 1,460 crore, which is a 9.2% growth on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Facility Management revenue grew 12.1% YoY to INR 594 crore in Q1 FY26
items.quote: FM has also reported its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR 594 crore, which is 12.1% growth on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: International revenue grew 18.5% YoY to INR 1,513 crore in Q1 FY26
items.quote: International, it has also reported its highest ever quarterly revenue of over INR 1,513 crore and happy to report that International standalone is now 1 billion AUD business on its own, which is a growth of 18.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 10.7% YoY to INR 152 crore at 4.3% margin in Q1 FY26
items.quote: On a consolidated level, EBITDA has grown by 10.7% on a year-on-year basis to INR 152 crore and the margin stands at 4.3%.

items.statement: India Security EBITDA margin at 5.4% in Q1 FY26, similar to Q1 FY25
items.quote: India Security reported an EBITDA margin of 5.4%, which is similar levels as that of Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Facility Management EBITDA margin improved 60 bps YoY to 4.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Now Facility Management reported an EBITDA margin of 4.8%, which is actually 60 basis points higher year -on-year basis.

items.statement: International EBITDA margin declined to 3% in Q1 FY26 from 3.4% in Q1 FY25 due to restructuring costs and absence of grants
items.quote: Coming to International. The EBITDA margin for Q1 FY '26 was 3% compared to 3.4% in Q1 FY '25. The impact is because of restructuring costs and absence of some grants in Henderson in Singapore and some high -margin events, which happened in Australia, which are obviously seasonal, and they all happe ned in Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: PAT grew 44.7% YoY to INR 93 crore at 2.6% margin in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our PAT for this quarter is at INR 93 crore, which is a PAT margin of 2.6% and a jump of 44.7% on a year -on-year basis.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 14.1% from 11.8% a year ago
items.quote: Our ROCE has now improved from 11.8% a year ago to 14.1%.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 540 crore from INR 1,023 crore in June 2025; net debt/EBITDA at 0.87x
items.quote: We are happy to report that our net debt is now at INR 540 crore, which is actually down by INR 483 crore in a similar period last year, June '25, which was at INR 1,023 crore. So this brings the net debt to EBITDA down to 0.87, which was 1.76 in June '25.

items.statement: OCF to EBITDA at 105%; DSOs improved by 6 days to 68 days vs June 2025
items.quote: OCF to EBITDA remains strong. It is at 105%. DSOs have improved by 6 days compared to June '25. Now we are at 68 days.

items.statement: Received SEBI, NSE, BSE approval for Cash JV IPO; 1-year window to proceed
items.quote: Update on Cash JV. As you would have read in the news also, we have now received approval from both SEBI, NSE, BSE for our IPO. We have a 1-year window now to proceed with the IPO.

items.statement: Invested INR 6 crore in preference shares of Adhikosh Financial Advisory (Kosh), a fintech for blue-collar workers
items.quote: As you know that we've been constantly looking out for investments in adjacent small businesses, start-ups. So, this quarter, we have invested INR 6 crore in preference shares of a Company named Adhikosh Financial Advisory Private Limited (Kosh).

items.statement: Won significant contracts in Sydney Trains defence sector and Canberra Airport in Australia; contracts are long-term and recurring
items.quote: You will see that last quarter, we reported significant wins in the Sydney Trains in defence sector and in Canberra Airport. Those contracts have basically come online in the first quarter, and that is what is driving the revenue jump. And these trends are not one-offs. These are long-term contracts.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven by minimum wage escalation, economic activity, and market share gains; all contracts prorated to minimum wages
items.quote: So fundamentally, growth in any environment or any business is a function of volume and price. So if you look at our growth broken down, the first factor that drives our growth is the minimum wage escalation. All our contracts are prorated, all our pricing is prorated to minimum wages.

items.statement: Market share gains from better services, compliance, technology, and national network; aspire to reach 10% market share from current 5%
items.quote: Well, I mean, we acquire market share basis better services, better compliances. We are the largest in this industry. We still only represent 5% odd of the market share despite being the largest in the country, and we aspire to move to a 10% market share.

items.statement: SXP restructuring in Australia: exiting unprofitable contracts, closing offices, letting go senior management; expect turbulence through Q3 FY26, then stable profitable business
items.quote: Effective May, we have let go of the CEO and a few other senior persons concerned. As of right now, we are exiting a significant number of existing contracts, which are not so profitable, closing a few offices and at the same time, letting go of so me key senior management who have not performed in line with

items.statement: Aspirational EBITDA margin target of 6% for consolidated business; India Security and FM targeting 6%, International steady-state at 4-4.5%
items.quote: SIS in the past has demonstrated its capability to deliver 6% EBITDA. We believe that our business model allows us to continue to deliver 6% with some scale benefi ts, also some cost efficiencies that we are working on. So overall, if you ask me what is your aspiration in terms of EBITDA margin, I would say we want to go back to the 6% EBITDA margin mark as we have previously demonstrated

items.statement: Economic activity in India resilient; government procurement strong, core manufacturing stable, IT strong but not booming; no major downturn seen
items.quote: I think if I look at my numbers , in India, across segments, we have continued to pick up contracts, types of contracts also included. So I believe that economic activity in India is fairly resilient. I don't see a downturn or a change.

items.statement: FM DSO at 94 days (hovering around 90-day mark); International Security DSO at 49 days; India Security DSO at 76 days; >1 year receivables mainly from PSUs/Government with 10%+ provision
items.quote: As regards to DSO, you will see that our DSOs overall , for the facility management business, I think you're asking particularly is 94 days. If you see the trends and trajectory even for the past few quarters, it has hovered around 90-day mark.

items.statement: Henderson (Singapore) is breakeven with $50M+ annualized revenue and $20M cash reserves; goodwill impairment was 90% related to Henderson
items.quote: As of right now, Henderson is a breakeven business, and it continues to maintain a $50 million annualized plus revenue. So, I think in the consol scheme of things, it's not a very large business, but we are very happy that it is growing reasonably over the last year, and it has enough cash reserves to support its growth, $20 million of whereabouts on its own books, and it is breakeven already.

items.statement: Pest control business at INR 50 crore annualized; 5-year plan to double scale to ~INR 100 crore; strategic complement to FM services
items.quote: Our FM business at this point in time is INR 50 crore annualized. But still within the FM segment compared to other competitors, we would be in the top 3, top 4 companies in the country. So pest control is a highly profitable business. Unfortunately, it is not a very large business.

items.statement: ELI scheme benefit unclear pending government notification; SIS as large employer stands to gain if scheme rewards job creation
items.quote: Well, at this point in time, I don't think we are in a position to comment on that because we have not received any formal ministerial or departmental notification that specifies exactly how the scheme operates.

items.statement: International EBITDA margin expected to return to 4-4.5% steady-state after SXP restructuring and new contract onboarding; India Security and FM targeting 6%
items.quote: SIS International on a steady -state basis before all the turbulence was reporting 4% to 4.5% EBITDA margin. I think what Murli and I both believe is that we will come back to that broad range at the top end of that range, hopefully, once the restructuring is done.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin directionally moving towards 5.5-6%; currently ~1% short
items.quote: I think the consol level, you should expect 5.5% to 6% is what directionally we are moving towards. As of right now, we are probably 1% short.

items.statement: 80JJAA tax benefit critical for India effective tax rate near zero; discontinuation would be exceptional given government focus on employment
items.quote: I honestly would be shocked to see Government of India, which is trying to address unemploymen t as its number one challenge, discontinue incentives towards job creation. But can I guarantee that or forecast that? Well, I'm not the right person to make comments on that.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 operating EBITDA breakeven target maintained
items.quote: We will be looking at an operating EBITDA level breakeven. That's still the guidance.

items.statement: Mid-single-digit offline top-line growth and ~50% online growth targeted for FY26
items.quote: Look, I think mid -single-digit growth is what we are looking at from the offline business on both the NB and SRL. And online, of course, we are looking at -- the base is much smaller. So, we are looking at how we can have at least close to 50% growth on the online business.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at INR10-12 crore for 8-10 new stores (~100k sq ft) and online tech
items.quote: Ballpark that will be between INR10 crores to INR12 crores is wh at we look at in terms of capex.

items.statement: Plan to add 8-10 Spencer's stores in FY26 (2-3 in Q2, 3 in Q3, 2-3 in Q4) in existing clusters
items.quote: On Spencer's, we are looking, like I mentioned that, look, we are looking at between 8 to 10 stores coming in. Yes, the first -- there was only 1 in quarter one, so one would say where is this thing, but there is sites under, I would say, finalization and even fit out to ensure that we will be able to roll it out.

items.statement: Jiffy online orders at 6,500/day in Q1; target 10,000/day by September
items.quote: We're doing -- if you -- any of you recollect the previous one, we're doing an average for the quarter, we're doing about 6,500 orders per day. We believe, again, there is headroom for us qui ckly to take this up to 10,000 t hat was the stated aspiration. And by September, we would be at that level.

items.statement: Spencer's EBITDA margin improved 119 bps QoQ to 19.1% in Q1; Nature's Basket margin recovered to 28.2%
items.quote: So, on even slightly higher volumes, our ASPs, average selling prices were down. We had a softer FMCG pa rt of it. But however, the margins came in Spencer's Retail July 31, 2025 at a strong 19.1% despite a mix which is now becoming a little smaller on apparel and GM for us because we've kind of toned that now

items.statement: Management prioritizes rupee gross margin (RGM) growth over percentage margin expansion; willing to moderate margins for volume
items.quote: Percentage margins are not -- you really don't bank the margins, you bank absolute money. So, we will look at where there is an opportunity, where there is elasticity, where with the right desired optimal level of price investment we can drive higher volumes.

items.statement: Q2 started stronger in July; festive tailwinds from Rakhi (August) and Durga Puja (September) expected to drive growth
items.quote: But I would say that the larger part of your Q2 momentum will come starting in Augu st and September. I mentioned August -- this is the start of the festive season in Rakhi. And July was also a bit impacted by -- it's localized to West Bengal it's because we were impacted with the higher monsoons.

items.statement: Spencer's mix: ~65% food/FMCG/fresh, 18-20% liquor (West Bengal); Nature's Basket: ~50% staples/F&V/fish/meat/bakery, 25% food FMCG, no apparel/GM
items.quote: In Spencer's, over the last, I would s ay, 4 or 5 quarters, we have become more focused and targeted at what I would say, the food and the FMCG non -food-led categories, which means that if you look at between FMCG, staples, fresh, which is both fresh F&V, fish and meat, bakery, dairy, this is r oughly about 65% of our mix is coming from these categories.

items.statement: Spencer's membership program launched July; 22,000+ paid members by July 31; aims to boost M1 retention to 80%+ and monthly spend
items.quote: Early days, but in July itself, where we launched the program, we have -- today is 31st of July, we've got 22,000 plus members who have paid and signed up for this.

items.statement: Supply chain optimization underway to tighten inventory, reduce days on hand, improve bestseller effectiveness
items.quote: In addition, we are also doing -- building an optimization exercise in terms of our supply chain, where we are looking at our inventory the end objective is to work with a tighter inventory, bring down our days on hand and really focus on your bestseller effectiveness.

items.statement: Spencer's sales per sq ft ~INR1,450; Nature's Basket slightly higher; consolidated ~INR1,523 in Q1
items.quote: Yes. Actually, we don't break it out, but let me give you that for quarter one, Spencer's is at around INR1,450 and Nature's Basket is not that much higher in the number.

items.statement: Jiffy faces high competitive intensity; operational challenges (fleet surges during rain) are daily but solvable; not a 10-min delivery player
items.quote: Yes. So, look, as you rightly said, this is an absolutely high competitive intensity sector. So there are external challenges. But again, we are kind of dealing with it given what our unique positioning in the market is we're targeting our off -line customers. we're looking at categories which work well for us.

items.statement: Staples deflation (especially pulses) hit ASPs in Q1 despite higher volumes; FMCG soft
items.quote: We had some supply issues given plus some deflationary pricing on staples. So, as you all know, pulses and a few other staples were -- they were in a deflationary trend and significant deflation in pulses. So, on even slightly higher volumes, our ASPs, average selling prices were down.

items.statement: Corporate headcount reduced by 100+ over past year; annualized savings >INR30 crore
items.quote: And we've kind of looked at about 100 -plus headcounts, which have been optimized over the course of the last 1 year. So roughly, it's 65 from direct closures and 35% from other efficiency measures and optimization, which we have done.

items.statement: Nature's Basket relaunched 2 stores (Inorbit Malad, Oberoi Goregaon); shut 2 loss-making stores (Defence Colony Delhi, Linking Road Mumbai)
items.quote: For Nature's Basket, they re -launched two stores, one in Inorbit Mall, Malad and the other in Oberoi Group Goregaon. Two high loss-making stores were shut down, one in Defense Colony in Delhi and the other in Linking Road, Krishna Curve.

items.statement: Heavy monsoon in West Bengal impacted July footfall and categories like carbonated soft drinks
items.quote: July was also a bit impacted by -- it's localized to West Bengal it's because we were impacted with the higher monsoons, which does lead to a little bit of not ju st footfall drop, but certain categories which are pretty high on summer, things like carbonated soft drinks, etc . was slower than expected.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY26 to be higher than H1 and growth momentum to return in H2
items.quote: We believe that along with our products and platform strategy and this AI-based solutions, we will be in a position to have certain wins and H2 will be higher than H1. And as we move into the second half, we will start gaining the growth momentum.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margins to be maintained at 21% in foreseeable future
items.quote: Right now, I would say, in a foreseeable future, we believe we can maintain the margins at 21%. I think as you have seen I mean, unless the currency plays very havoc.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 deal wins were $241 million
items.quote: The wins during the quarter have been $241 million.

items.statement: Growth driven by powertrain, connected, and autonomous domains across US and Europe in passenger car vertical
items.quote: The growth has been mainly in powertrain and connected area s, both across U.S.A. and Europe and basically in the passenger car

items.statement: Commercial vehicle, off-highway, India and China pipelines expected to drive growth in coming quarters
items.quote: We believe that in the Commercial Vehicle vertical -- there will also be growth in off-highway and commercial, which will kick in, in the next few quarters. We are also very bullish about China and India.

items.statement: Fixed price projects increased from 60% to 62.5% of revenue
items.quote: In terms of overall quality of the revenue, fixed price projects have moved from 60%, to 62.5%.

items.statement: Headcount decreased to 12,545 from 12,873 in previous quarter; annual attrition around 7%
items.quote: The head count has been 12,545 from 12,873 from the last quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 21% in Q1 FY26; EBIT at 17%
items.quote: We are very happy that in these uncertain times, the EBITDA remained strong at 21%. EBIT was at 17%.

items.statement: JSW Motors engagement won for India program, 3-year duration
items.quote: This is specific to India program. And a lot of work we will be bringing in what assets we have, and we will be adapting it more for India market –This will be about 3 years kind of a program.

items.statement: Advanced engagement with one large European OEM for Qorix JV, decision expected in next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: I think there is one big European OEM, which is in that process where we are in the advanced stage of engaging will probably know in next quarter or 2.

items.statement: Management claims substantial competitive advantage in AI-infused mobility solutions
items.quote: We believe, based on our interactions with the clients as well as overall indust ry players, we are ahead in terms of our AI journey specific to mobility, and this gives us a very substantial competitive advantage as compared to our competition to win more

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty expected to settle in a quarter, providing more certainty for client spending
items.quote: Overall, as you know, the geopolitical issue because of the tariffs and the intense competition between the OEMs and the China competition is still there, but we believe it will settle down in a quarter.

items.statement: Trentar sodium-ion battery commercialization expected to take 2-3 years before license revenue kicks in
items.quote: So if you look at both these things, I think it will take about 2 to 3 years for us to start getting the license revenue till that time, we expect the factory to be stable, the production to start com ing in and achieve a certain threshold from where our royalties kick in

items.statement: Caresoft acquisition pending condition precedents, expected to close in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Yes. So we are -- in that process, we had certain, I would say, condition precedent CPs, which are still not fulfilled. So, we are waiting for that. We do hope in this quarter, it should happen.

items.statement: Revenue per employee has increased over last 3 years
items.quote: And if you see KPIT last 3 years, our revenue per person has increased. And we do hope that the changes will help us to continue to maintain that.

items.statement: China subsidiary transacts in local currency; costs also in local currency providing natural hedge
items.quote: No, you should also note that we already have a subsidiary in China, and that actually does the transaction with our clients, which is in local China currency. Kishor Patil: And the

items.statement: Client reprioritization and cannibalization of existing programs dampening growth despite strong deal wins
items.quote: Even though there is growth on one hand, there is reprioritization in the existing program, right, which is sort of not helped us. And the second part also, for the existing programs, there is a demand to do them in a more efficient, effective manner.

items.statement: OEMs pushing out next-gen SDV architecture programs by 1-2 years
items.quote: The next architecture was supposed to come into play by 2028, for that, the work should have started by now. That's definitely getting pushed out by a year or 2.

items.statement: Strong pipeline in Europe with deals starting to ramp up; India and China expected to contribute meaningfully in next 6 months
items.quote: In Europe, there are many deals in the process. But I think in Europe, some of these deals have started ramping up. As I said, slowly than what we expected, but they have started converting. And the other thing, I must say that as India and China, we believe that they will start contributing meaningfully to our revenues in next 6 months or so.

items.statement: Japan growth currently concentrated in one OEM; advanced conversations with three other potential clients for broad-based growth by year-end
items.quote: We have had tremendous growth over the last couple of years because of our engagement in Japan, and that was on the back of largely one OEM. And the thing that we are doing is there are three other potential clients with whom we have started really advanced conversations. And we believe that towards the end of the year, will start working with them as well.

items.statement: Technica Engineering products gaining traction with 5-6 Chinese OEM partnerships
items.quote: we have certain products through our subsidiary, Technica Engineering. And we are seeing a lot of traction for our products in Chinese OEM ecosystem. So there are 5 or 6 Chinese OEMs with whom we have already built a partnersh ip for our

items.statement: India and China combined revenue expected to reach 3-digit million USD in 2 years
items.quote: I can tell you that in 2 years, this will be a 3-digit number in terms of revenues, India, China together.

items.statement: No revenue growth guidance given for FY26 or next 2-3 years due to market uncertainty
items.quote: I had said it, but right now, I think we'll come back when we have not talked about this year, and we'll not talk about this year. And we'll come back when we believe the markets are a bit stable.

items.statement: Validation services seeing growing demand as OEMs prioritize production programs
items.quote: But the third most important part is when you are putting these features into production, they require extensive validation. So, we are seeing growing demand in terms of validation.

items.statement: AI-driven validation solutions winning priority orders but causing cannibalization of other client spend
items.quote: Now for that, we have brought in a very good solution in terms of a AI driven validation. Now this is a big priority for the OEM, so they have given us reasonably reasonable size orders, prioritizing over other spend. And we have won such kind of deals, but in that case, because they are not in a position to increase their spend, they had to slow down or cut down spend somewhere else, and that has

items.statement: Business model shifting from headcount-linked to productivity-driven with AI and fixed-price models
items.quote: I must say, and I have been saying it from the last 2 quarters, that I think the model where you relate head count to revenue will be difficult in future and while we do expect that in some cases, we will still do in short term. But I think over the period, we believe that we will be in a position to enhance our productivity substantially and move towards more product s and solutions

items.statement: Q1 FY26 orders hit an all-time high of Rs 11,339.2 crore, up 365% year-on-year, driven by the Bhadla-Fatehpur HVDC order.
items.quote: This quarter, ending June 30, 2025, our orders totaled all-time high of Rs. 11,339.2 crores and revenue stood at Rs. 1,529.8 crores, growing 365% on orders and 15.3% on the revenue on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Order backlog closed at a record Rs 29,135 crore, providing revenue visibility for several quarters.
items.quote: And this was primarily because of the large order of Bhadla-Fatehpur HVDC order that we booked in this particular quarter. And that is the result you see we closed the highest ever order backlog of Rs. 29,135 crores, which provides a visibility of revenues for several quarters.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin reached 11.1% in Q1 FY26, with PBT at Rs 176.9 crore and PAT at Rs 131.6 crore.
items.quote: If you see the HITACHI 8/26 operational EBITDA, operational EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 170.2 crores and this has resulted in a double-digit margin of 11.1% for this particular quarter

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved ~650 basis points year-on-year; management targets sustainable double-digit margins long-term.
items.quote: As I said, we are building a Company in a very long-term focus, not on a short-term basis. And we also told you several times that our main focus is to address the domestic market. We believe that the domestic market, the pipeline, and the market visibility are very strong and they will continue to be strong. That's the reason we are investing Rs. 2,000 crores of CAPEX, which I am sure you have no

items.statement: Capex of Rs 2,000 crore underway across transformer, high-voltage, grid automation and HVDC capacities in phased manner over next 18 months.
items.quote: We are investing Rs. 2,000 crores of CAPEX, which I am sure you have not seen this kind of CAPEX from others. So, when I would like to compare, I would like to compare. So, we are improving margins, and you have seen almost 650 basis points were improved Y-on-Y on EBITDA basis and we continue to improve going forward.

items.statement: Post-capex asset turnover expected at 3-5x; current capacity strong in insulation, large power transformers and GIS.
items.quote: So, again, Rs. 2,000 crores CAPEX, if I am going to put it there, once it is complete, the asset turnover is in the range of anywhere between three to four or something like that, four to five, depending upon that. So, you can just look at it, what could be the revenue potential once it completes on that.

items.statement: Expect one to two HVDC project finalizations (Khavda, Barmer, Leh) by 31 March 2026.
items.quote: Talking about finalization, our view is that one project will be finalized in this financial year, but there could also be a potential for the second project to be finalized. So, it's basically one to two projects finalized in this financial year on or before 31 March, 2026.

items.statement: Domestic pipeline very strong across transmission, renewables, data centres, rail/metro and industry; HVDC pipeline expects 2-3 projects per year for next 3-4 years.
items.quote: But this pipeline is extremely good. And HVDC, you all know that. I have been saying in that to manage the network of India, we need to have at least two to three HVDCs per year, at least in a couple of years, at least a couple of years more.

items.statement: Exports contribute ~25% of order book (ex-HVDC); three-pronged strategy targets sustainable 25% export revenue mix over next couple of years.
items.quote: Roughly, we are looking at around 25% of exports. Maybe it might go a few percentage this way that way over a period of time. But it again depends upon the thing. Put in a lot of efforts to serve our domestic demand, and that's what we are going to do that. And then on top of that, if we get an opportunity, we will do more than 25%. But 25% is what I see in the next couple of years, plus/minus a f

items.statement: HVDC constitutes 55-60% of Rs 29,135 crore backlog; non-HVDC backlog 40-45%.
items.quote: Roughly in the range of you can take anywhere between 55% to 60% is the HVDC, the rest is non-HVDC.

items.statement: Order inflow growth in Q1 FY26: transmission +625%, rail/metro +845%, data centres ~100%, industry +23%, renewables -25% (timing).
items.quote: In the Q1 FY '25-'26, both transmission and rail metro experienced a sharp growth of 625% and 845%, respectively. The data center segment witnessed almost a cent percent growth and industry growth is at 23%. However, there's a decline of 25% in renewable, wind and solar, which we feel is a temporary phenomenon and it's a timing issue.

items.statement: Material cost 53.8% of revenue; personnel 9.5%, other expenses 22.7%; royalty ~4% of sales; fixed-cost absorption to improve margins as revenue scales.
items.quote: So, if you see for the three months ended 30 June, 2025 of the total income of Rs. 1,529.8 crores, the material cost was 53.8%. So, in this particular quarter, as we discussed earlier, there is a very good development on the gross margin, which has really helped in the bottom-line development. Personnel expenses were 9.5% and if I compare it with Y-on-Y of last year, 9.2% fairly, I will say we are

items.statement: Finance cost fell to Rs 4 crore in Q1 FY26 due to zero short-term borrowings.
items.quote: Finance cost is Rs. 4 crores, which has come down if I compare Y-o-Y and majorly because we do not have any short-term borrowings in this particular quarter.

items.statement: Exchange and commodity loss of Rs 9.4 crore in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: In this particular quarter, we had an exchange and commodity loss of Rs. 9.4 crores.

items.statement: Uttar Pradesh plans to privatize two of its four power distribution companies, seen as positive for DISCOM modernization.
items.quote: Uttar Pradesh, one of the largest states in India, is looking to privatize two of its four power distribution companies, which is a positive step in the right direction.

items.statement: U.S. tariff uncertainty remains; management expects clarity in coming weeks to assess impact on India and business.
items.quote: Though uncertainty looms over U.S. tariffs, we expect more clarity in the coming weeks to ascertain the impact in India and also for our business.

items.statement: Expanded women-in-engineering program with new batch from Gujarat; upgraded two government schools in Vadodara with smart classes.
items.quote: I am also happy to inform you that we expanded our women in engineering program by welcoming a new batch of students from Gujarat. Also, as part of our commitment to education, we have undertaken the task of upgrading two government schools in Vadodara with smart classes.

items.statement: Service business carved out effective 1 April 2025; service orders grew 90% YoY and contributed high single-digit to order book.
items.quote: Service orders grew 90% year-on-year. This is also our first quarter after we carved out our new service business, effective from 1st of April, 2025, and contributed a high single digit to the overall order book.

items.statement: Mumbai HVDC project for Adani (Rs 2,000 crore) nearing completion; commissioning expected in 6-9 months.
items.quote: Yes, we may be around six months is the one where we are looking at to commission that, six to nine months.

items.statement: STATCOM opportunity estimated at 25-30 projects in India over next four years per National Electricity Plan.

items.statement: Pyridine and Picoline plants running at 80% capacity utilization
items.quote: We run our plants at 80% capacity utilization in Pyridine and Picoline.

items.statement: Diketene derivatives segment characterized by high capacity utilization levels
items.quote: We also witnessed encouraging momentum in our Diketene derivatives segment, characterized by high-capacity utilization levels.

items.statement: Over 70 high-priority opportunities in sales funnel across Pharma, Agrochemicals, Semiconductors, Cosmetics and Nutrition

items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 153 crore, reflecting a 29% rise on a year-on-year basis. The growth in EBITDA was primarily driven by margin improvements in the Specialty Chemicals and Nutrition business segments along with various cost optimization initiatives.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals EBITDA Rs 130 crore, up 52% YoY, margin 27% (highest ever)
items.quote: During the quarter, Specialty Chemicals once again achieved its highest ever EBITDA of Rs. 130 Crore and the EBITDA margin of 27%. The EBITDA of Specialty Chemicals grew by 52% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Chemical Intermediates EBITDA margin improved 170 bps QoQ to 4.4% driven by cost initiatives
items.quote: EBITDA went up by 170 bps to 4.4 bps versus last quarter, driven by our focussed cost initiatives in this segment.

items.statement: Lean 2.0 cost optimization target annualized savings exceeding Rs 100 crore in FY26, progressed well in Q1
items.quote: As part of our Lean 2.0 cost optimization program, we have set a target of achieving annualized savings exceeding Rs 100+ crore in FY'26, and have progressed well in Q1.

items.quote: So, we do hope that in steady state even after Acetyls bounces back which we are hoping in next few quarters as we were just discussing, Specialty will be at least at 65%-70% of our overall company level EBITDA.

items.quote: As a result, we are witnessing a notable increase in revenue contribution from the U.S and Rest of the World markets, with the U.S. revenue growing by 11% year-over-year and Rest of the World revenue surging by an impressive 45% year-over-year.

items.statement: Animal Nutrition specialty portfolio registering double-digit growth in export markets, especially Europe
items.quote: In Animal Nutrition, we are witnessing strong traction in export markets, especially across Europe, with our specialty portfolio registering double-digit growth across markets.

items.quote: The net debt of the company as on 30th June was Rs. 700 crore and the net debt to EBITDA ratio remained stable at 1.18x, calculated on the basis of trading 12 months EBITDA.

items.quote: at least revenue level, we expect 1.2 to 1.3x at least and sometimes even 1.4 to 1.5x on the revenue to CAPEX ratio.

items.statement: Management sees multi-decadal secular demand driven by AI data centers, US manufacturing reshoring, and transportation electrification.
items.quote: The demand, like I said, it's a very secular demand. And I talked about the three demand drivers to an earlier question as well. That is actually a multi-decadal opportunity. It is not for this year, 2 years, 3 years. This is going to be a multi-decadal opportunity. And so, the demand will continue unabated and will only grow because solar energy is one of the cheapest forms of energy.

items.statement: Order book stands at 25 GW (approx. INR 49,000 crores / $5.5-6 billion) at consolidated level including EPC.
items.quote: Our order book is actually 25 gigawatts, which is equivalent to INR49,000 crores which is equal to what, roughly $4 billion about $6 billion roughly of order book. It is not 100 gigawatts, it is a 25 gigawatt of orderbook , roughly translating to about $5.5 billion roughly and so that's the first clarification I wanted to give you.

items.statement: EPC pipeline is 25 GW+ covering domestic and overseas orders.
items.quote: I think we have -- I did in the call of our EPC arm Waaree Renewable Technologies that the pipeline for EPC business is 25-gigawatt plus. And we are pursuing this pipeline which entails domestic, as well as overseas orders.

items.statement: US module capacity fully booked at 1.6 GW; expanding to 3.2 GW with new lines expected to ramp up in 6-9 months.
items.quote: So, Karan we are fully booked for 1.6 gigawatts. In fact, we are bursting through our seams and that's the reason why we are actually going for the next edition, taking the overall capacity to 3.2 gigawatt. In fact, those lines even before they have come into existence, are already fully booked, which is a good problem to have or a problem, nevertheless. And so that we are trying to work at a fair

items.statement: Total capex of INR 15,000 crores over next 2 years for 6 GW integrated facility, 4 GW expansion, and adjacent businesses.
items.quote: So, if you see what we have announced is that our total capex including everything, the recent expansion of 4 gigawatts including our 6 gigawatt integrated facility and the other adjacent businesses like battery and all. The total capex is about INR15,000 crores, which is going to be spread over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Capex for 1 GW cell capacity estimated at INR 750-800 crores per GW.
items.quote: So, 1 gigawatt of cell is ranging anywhere between INR750 crores to INR800 crores per gigawatt.

items.statement: Long-term target: 17-18% EBITDA margin on modules; cells expected to add 300-400 bps due to integration.
items.quote: What we have said is in the long term we should look at around 18% kind of margins on the EBITDA side and 17% to 18%. And with the cell we expect it to go up by 300 to 400 basis points because we have our own in-house integrated facilities.

items.statement: Management commits to maintaining gross margin and EBITDA targets regardless of tariff or cost changes.
items.quote: So, the primary way in which we manage Waaree is as Sonal said a few questions ago, is gross margin. And we'll make sure that we are at the right point from a gross margin and EBITDA perspective. And that we keep delivering those numbers for our investors.

items.statement: Big Beautiful Bill retains 45X manufacturing credit and clarifies FEOC regulations, which management views as beneficial and order-accretive.
items.quote: Number one, 45X has been retained for manufacturing. And so, therefore, that helps us. I mean, it has been advanced by a year, but that has been retained. So, that kind of helps us. Number two, FEOC regulations have been clearly elucidated, and they are actually beneficial to us because we will be in a position to comply to all of these FEOC regulations being completely owned by India and Indian e

items.statement: US ADD investigation on solar cells just begun; management confident of defending case with minimal impact due to global footprint and transparency.
items.quote: So, let's see how does this evolve. But I would say we should be in a position because of our global footprint and because of the fact that we are a publicly listed company, we will be in a position to defend our case well with minimal impact.

items.statement: Contracts include change-of-law clauses to pass on tariff/duty changes; mixed pass-through ability but gross margin target will be maintained.
items.quote: In many cases, there is a potential of actually going back to the customer with change orders and so on and so forth. And in some cases, it is not. So, it is going to be a mixed bag. But net-net, like I said, we will always make sure that we are driving towards a gross margin, which leads to an EBITDA that we have committed to our investors.

items.statement: Supply chain for polysilicon, ingots, wafers, and cells available outside China (including India); solar glass supply balancing with new domestic capacity.
items.quote: There is polysilicon manufacturing outside of China. There is ingots and wafers manufacturing outside of China and so is the case itself. And, of course, those capacities are growing in India itself. We are having ingots, wafers manufacturers coming in India. There is cell manufacturing increasing multifold in India and so enough to say that there is enough capacity outside of China all the way fr

items.statement: Solar glass supply chain not a problem as significant capacity being built in India and other countries.
items.quote: So, there is actually a lot of capacity being built in India as well and other countries also. So, there will be a balancing out of supply chain, and I think it's a very healthy trend from that perspective.

items.statement: Battery storage plant in embryonic stage; reverse integration planned down to cell level; 3.5 GW factory coming online next year.
items.quote: So, we will be actually reverse integrating all the way to the level of cells. So, like you have in modules, in modules, you have the module itself and then you have cell. In batteries, you have got a pack, it's called a pack. And then one step back is a cell. So, we will be reverse integrating to the extent of cell, which is a very substantial amount of manufacturing.

items.statement: Actively evaluating Middle East, Australia, EU for EPC and module exports; following Indian government trade agreements.
items.quote: We are actually extremely keen to expand our base beyond India and the United States. Wherever Indian government goes and signs a trade agreement, we see that as an opportunity being a country based out of or headquartered in India. We are closely observing the geographies where overall as a country, India is making its moves and so we'll definitely try to follow that, those cues sent by the gover

items.statement: Currently debt-free with INR 7,500+ crores cash; capex funded via internal accruals, cash, and bank facilities; comfortable with conservative debt-equity.
items.quote: So, a very strong balance sheet and 0 debt. And the way we look at funding mix in the next 2 years is part of this money which is lying. Second is going forward, I have 2 years of internal accruals which will come in. And also, we also had a tie-up with banks on facilities, which we will draw down as the case may be. And so far, we have been conservative on our debt equity ratio. We feel very comf

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA guidance INR 5,500-6,000 crores; FY27 guidance to be provided in early 2027 after new capacities online.
items.quote: I think let's first get our ducks in a row, make sure that we deliver the INR5,500 crores to INR6,000 crores EBITDA that we talked about. And I can assure you, beginning of 2027, we will tell you what is the guidance for 2027.

items.statement: Standalone module capacity 12 GW; Indosolar 1.3 GW; US subsidiary 1.6 GW; total ~15 GW as of FY25.
items.quote: So, basically, the capacity for Waaree is 12 gigawatts. And 1.3 gigawatt is with Indosolar. So, that's 13.3 gigawatts. And an additional 1.6 is in the US. So, that's what we say 14.9 gigawatts or 15 gigawatts, which was our exist capacity for FY '29, sorry, '25.

items.statement: Indosolar acquired via NCLT ~2.5 years ago for strategic fit (Northern geography) and module capacity; will continue on own growth trajectory.
items.quote: It was, I mean, it was actually a very good opportunity to bring it into the group structure. It has been done what 2 - 2.5 years ago. It's not new. It was a good deal through NCLT and that's how it was taken over. Amit Paithankar: It’s a strategic fit for us. It’s in the Northern region. We can serve our customers in the North from there. So, there's a big strategic element to that as well

items.statement: Promoter holding transfer within family entity is part of broader group structuring; management declines to elaborate.
items.quote: So, this is a broader thought process that the promoters have in overall group structuring how would they want to hold various assets? It's really dependent on how the promoters would like to look at this. Thank you.

items.statement: US ADD investigation timeline minimum 6 months to over a year; existing contracts have features to protect profitability; Trump tariff pass-through mixed but gross margin target maintained.
items.quote: These investigations typically takes at the minimum 6 months, optimally 1 year and sometimes even more than a year. All of the contracts that we have at this point in time, we would actually be by then have fulfilled quite a few of them. And in most of our contracts, there are features in which we can draw back and make sure that our profitability is maintained.

items.statement: US AI data center power share projected to grow from 2.2% to 7.5-8% by 2030.
items.quote: Just to put it in perspective, at this point in time, across the US about 2.2% of overall power consumed is used for data centers associated with artificial intelligence. By 2030, that number is set to grow to 7.5% to 8%, which is a big shift.

items.statement: Management sees room for growth in India cell capacity and even more in ingot/wafer; integrated capacity key due to ALMM and FEOC trends.
items.quote: And when we put all of that together, honestly, the requirement, I would say there is room for us to grow in India in terms of cell capacity. And there is even more room for us to grow as far as ingot and wafers are concerned. So, we are just beginning in my opinion.

items.statement: Instamart contribution margin neutrality expected between December 2025 and June 2026 quarter
items.quote: Our guidance remains that we expect to get to contribution margin neutrality between December and June quarter of calendar year 2026.

items.statement: Instamart contribution margin improved 100 bps QoQ despite network expansion headwinds
items.quote: In line with the same, our contribution margin has improved by 100 bps quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Expect higher contribution margin improvement in Q2 FY26 than Q1 FY26
items.quote: We actually expect to make an even higher contribution margin improvement in the current quarter.

items.statement: Instamart AOV grew 16% QoQ and 26% YoY, ahead of guidance
items.quote: I am happy to report that our focused efforts have led to a substantial change in the slope of the driving AOV, with a movement of 16% quarter-on-quarter and 26% Y-on-Y which is ahead of our guidance that we gave.

items.statement: Instamart GOV grew 108% YoY driven by dark store expansion
items.quote: Our GOV growth accelerated to 108% YoY. This was primarily led by our dark-store expansion, both existing and in the new areas that we went into.

items.statement: Instamart non-grocery share grew from 6.6% to 18.5% YoY
items.quote: Over the last year, if you look from Q1 FY '25 to Q1 FY '26, we have grown from 6.6% to 18.5% of the non-grocery business.

items.statement: Instamart GOV per customer per month increased 8%
items.quote: This growth in AOV with focused efforts led to a consolidation of cuts, while leading to a higher GOV per customer per month by 8%.

items.statement: Instamart network at 127 cities with 4.3 million sq ft; can grow 2x without adding storage
items.quote: We are in 127 cities right now with 4.3 million square feet of store area, which is significant even if you look at, compare it to anybody else in the market.

items.statement: Dark store expansion to be measured and need-based, not for white space expansion
items.quote: We believe that our next network expansion will be based on the need, based on these geographies, and it will not necessarily be for expansion into the white spaces.

items.statement: Capex trajectory to be graded; warehousing expansion ongoing in metros
items.quote: It will be a more graded expansion of CAPEX investments from here on, because again the capacity expansion is largely being done on the warehousing side also.

items.statement: Maxxsaver has 28% MTU penetration; lower take rate initially but improves long-term contribution margin
items.quote: There is a 28% MTU penetration for Maxxsaver and we see those customers coming back again for Maxxsaver orders.

items.statement: Non-grocery commission dilution of 50 bps on contribution margin; expected to improve as relationships mature
items.quote: There is a 50 bps dilution on contribution margin led by lower commissions on non-grocery selection.

items.statement: Competitive intensity remains heightened with new players entering; not an indication of future trend
items.quote: At an absolute level the intensity in the market, we see it being at the heightened level. There are new players also entering the market.

items.statement: Category in early phase of customer penetration with significant growth runway
items.quote: This category is still in an early phase of customer penetration and has a significant runway of growth.

items.statement: Below contribution margin costs increased >50% due to appraisal cycle; will provide leverage going forward
items.quote: The overall increase that you have seen below CM costs, a little more than half is actually due to the appraisal cycle and that is something, which from here on will start giving us leverage.

items.statement: Directionally June EBITDA loss lower than April due to leverage
items.quote: Directionally, June was lower than April. And that is because, as I said, there is a lot of leverage that has come through.

items.statement: Maxxsaver primarily builds grocery baskets; non-grocery growth driven by assortment expansion
items.quote: Maxxsaver actually helps grocery business a lot more. It is a basket building proposition. And for a lot of non-grocery, baskets are not built, right, the unit per order for non-groceries is extremely close to one.

items.statement: Customer acquisition via both standalone Instamart app and super-app; approach is consumer-led
items.quote: It is a mix. The way to think about it is there are two ways we acquire consumers. One is from our existing app, who have, say, never transacted on Instamart. And the others are those who are independently, coming to that.

items.statement: Food delivery GOV grew 18.8% YoY
items.quote: Another very solid performance in terms of 18.8% GOV growth, right.

items.statement: Food delivery remains highly competitive; competitor management changes not factored into decisions
items.quote: Food delivery is always highly competitive. So, we do not watch it from an internal management lens of another company and the point is, we do not have any more information than you have, right.

items.statement: Overall monetization efforts added 240 bps including subsidy reductions
items.quote: Even in the quarter gone by, we have added 240 basis points in our overall monetization efforts, including the reduction of some of the subsidies.

items.statement: Retain flexibility on marketing investments and EBITDA guidance due to competitive intensity uncertainty
items.quote: We will maintain the flexibility to invest for growth for the subsequent quarters as well.

items.statement: Management expects AQuity tail reduction and margin optimization headwinds to complete by end of FY26 (fiscal Q4), after which growth should reflect pure organic trajectory.
items.quote: I think we still have two to three more quarters of AQuity customer tail reduction as well as AQuity margin optimization. And so perhaps fair to assume that the headwinds in revenue associated with Inventurus Knowledge Solutions Limited August 01, 2025 those two endeavors should be completed by towards the end of this fiscal, let's say fiscal

items.statement: EBITDA margin target remains early to mid-30s; Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin was 32%, up 90 bps QoQ.
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter came in at 32% which is a meaningful 90 bps improvement from Q4 where we reported 31.2%.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margins to stabilize at early to mid-30s and does not feel comfortable projecting expansion beyond that range.
items.quote: I think our target still continues to be early to mid-30s. And as you can see from our performance, we feel very confident about achieving that.

items.statement: Top 10 and top 5 customer revenue share continues to improve; vintage remains strong at over 5 years.
items.quote: Our revenue from top 10 as well as top 5 customers continue to improve with our continued winning of client deals that you would have noted both in Q4 as well as Q1 now.

items.statement: AQuity tail pruning continues; customer count down from ~800 in Oct 2023 to ~650, targeting steady state of ~500 over next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: We are now down from a combined customer base of (+800) in October '23 to about 650. And as I have stated in the past, a sort of steady state will probably end up closer to 500.

items.statement: Outsourced TAM growing at 12% vs overall market at 8%; IKS grew 13% constant currency in Q1 FY26, indicating market share gains.
items.quote: If we are growing faster than 12% on a constant currency basis, we are gaining market share. If we are growing slower than 12%, we are losing market share.

items.statement: Launched Scribble Now (fully ambient autonomous clinical documentation), multi-variant Scribble, autonomous medical coding for two specialties, AI denial prediction, and AI patient engagement hub.
items.quote: We launched Scribble Now, which is our fully ambient, autonomous clinical documentation solution. And with that, I think IKS now has the most comprehensive set of variants that meet physicians wherever they are in their journey of choosing the right clinical documentation solution for their needs.

items.statement: Palomar deal progressing ahead of plan; full platform implementation expected by end of fiscal Q2 (Q2 FY26), with peak platform fee revenue at that point.
items.quote: It is totally fair to assume that perhaps by the end of this fiscal, which is fiscal Q2, we would be fully implemented across all the features, across nearly 100% of the physicians at Palomar.

items.statement: Western Washington Medical Group deal: invested $17M for 48% stake in MSO with perpetual contract; full platform implementation expected in ~120 days subject to Epic integration.
items.quote: On Western Washington, yes, I think it's a fair assumption that in about 120-odd days from now, we should be fully implemented. It's subject to us getting the full epic integration going, which we are working on.

items.statement: Added Mission Community as second end-to-end acute RCM customer; expanded OrthoNY to full platform; signed Bicycle Health (behavioral health); cross-sell wins in top 5 health systems.
items.quote: Happy to note that we now have our second end-to-end—we have other acute RCM customers that are also ramping that are not end-to-end, but Mission Community is our second end-to-end—acute RCM customer.

items.statement: Radiology Partners relationship not yet at JV threshold; JV conversion not expected in next couple of quarters.
items.quote: The relationship has not yet grown to that threshold. So, I don't see a JV conversion happening in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Global headcount reduced 7% YoY to 12,368 FTEs (from 13,277 in Q1 FY25); further optimization expected for 2-3 quarters, then headcount may inch up to support growth.
items.quote: human element of what we do now comprises about 12,368 FTEs across the US and India. Again, remember this number in Q1 of FY25 was actually 13,277. So, on a year-on-year basis, our global headcount is down about 7

items.statement: Employee turnover at all-time low in IKS history; added Dr. Garheng Kong to board (Stanford, Duke, McKinsey, HealthQuest Capital, LabCorp board, Duke Health System board).
items.quote: We are actually at a point where I think our employee turnover is at an all-time low in the history of IKS.

items.statement: Net debt improved to Rs 448 crore; finance cost down to Rs 18 crore from Rs 26 crore YoY due to debt repayment and lower rates.
items.quote: As you can see by the end of the quarter, our net debt position stood at Rs. 448 crores and the continued cash generation in the future quarters is where you will continue to see this number improve.

items.statement: Operating cash flow Rs 165 crore, free cash flow Rs 137 crore (net of $5M upfront performance guarantee to a multi-specialty primary care organization).
items.quote: In terms of operating cash flow, we ended the quarter at Rs. 165 crores and free cash flow came in at Rs. 137 crores. These numbers are net of an upfront performance guarantee we have extended to the tune of $5 million to a multi-specialty primary care organization.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA per employee annualized improved to INR 0.8 million in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA number for employee annualized continues to improve quarter-on-quarter. As you can note, it was INR 0.8 million in the quarter.

items.statement: ROE at 31% for Q1 FY26; EPS Rs 9 (58% YoY growth, 2% QoQ growth).
items.quote: Our return on equity metrics again remains very healthy and very strong. For the quarter, our return on equity metrics stood at 31%.

items.statement: Employee benefit expense 52.3% of revenue (up from 51.8% QoQ) despite headcount reduction, due to tech investment and increments; EBITDA margin still expanded.
items.quote: Our employee benefit expense in the quarter stood at 52.3% of revenues compared to 51.8% in the previous quarter. This increase is despite the net reduction in employee count because we do continue to invest in technology as well as increments.

items.statement: Setting up AI Centre of Excellence; about to announce Chief AI Officer; R&D expense increased from traditional 1.5-2% to ~5% of revenue.
items.quote: We were traditionally 1.5%-2% R&D expenses. Today, we are close to 5% R&D expense. And we are setting up an AI centre of excellence. We are just about to announce a chief AI officer under which the centre of excellence will be built.

items.statement: Recognized as #1 partner in AI-driven RCM and medical coding by Black Book; top rankings in clinical documentation by KLAS and Black Book.
items.quote: It's great to receive some recognition from Black Book as the number one partner in AI-driven RCM and in medical coding and then as it relates to clinical documentation, both by KLAS and Black Book.

items.statement: AQuity tail cutting creates material revenue drag but managed to avoid dramatic quarterly impact; transition expected to complete in 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: I think I will refrain from providing those specifics, but I will say that it's material. I am comfortable saying that the drag is material and that is why even as we are continuing to be intentional, we are trying to manage the drag in a manner that the cutting of the tail is real.

items.statement: Palomar deal has contractual change-of-control protection; management sees more opportunity than risk if Palomar is acquired by a large health system (e.g., UC San Diego).
items.quote: So given that we were potentially anticipating a change of control, even when we did the deal, Srinath, we had already built a no out in the event of change of control. So first of all, there's a very penal contractual protection that will probably be a huge deterrent.

items.statement: ETR for Q1 FY26 at 22%; lost tax breaks in one SEZ unit, full-year ETR likely to remain in same range.
items.quote: Our ETR for the quarter stood at 22%. We have lost tax breaks in one of the SEZ units that we operate out of. For the full year, it's likely to remain in the same range.

items.statement: Urea margins expected to remain stable for rest of year due to formula-based pricing
items.quote: The urea is a kind of formula- related pricing, and the margins are not expected to vary much in the remaining part of the year.

items.statement: NPK raw material prices rose sharply last quarter with some signs of abatement
items.quote: But you are right that the prices have shown a degree of rapid upward mobility rather in the last one quarter. Some signs of abatement are there, but we will have to see how it goes forward.

items.statement: Traded fertiliser volumes trending back to original target of million ton plus
items.quote: we are trending back to our original numbers, million ton plus.

items.statement: TAN plant trial production starting early December or late November, commercial production by mid-January
items.quote: Trial production will commence early December or late November and we should be starting production by mid-January.

items.statement: TAN current netback prices Rs.35,000-37,000 per ton, EBITDA per ton in five-digit range
items.value: Rs.35,000 to Rs.37,000 a ton net-back
items.quote: The current prices, if I am not wrong, are between Rs.35,000 to Rs.37,000 a ton net- back. And I would assume that they would be in the region of five- digit plus at the moment.

items.statement: Seed business launched with Rs.6 crore sales, rabi ambitions an order of magnitude higher, total market size ~Rs.50,000 crore
items.quote: We have s tarted with something like mustard, bajra and maize. And we have done about, Rs.6 crore in sales, we just made a small beginning. Of course, our rabi ambitions are much higher. They will be in an order of magnitude higher than what we have done. As far as the total market size is concerned, which includes open pollinated variety and research and hybrid, marketing informs me of the order

items.statement: Seed business via white-label alliances with top manufacturers across crop segments
items.quote: presently we have embarked on the seed journey through the white label business. That means we are buying a very popular product from the top manufacturers. We have tie- ups with the top manufacturers in all crop segments.

items.statement: TAN plant revenue estimate 55,000-56,000 tons at 60-70% utilization in Jan-Mar quarter at Rs.35,000-40,000 per ton
items.quote: assuming that we do about even 60% -70% rate for production, then we are talking about 55,000-56,000 tons product, sells today around Rs.35,000- 40,000 a ton. You can do the math.

items.statement: Normal replacement capex of Rs.250 crore planned for FY26 excluding TAN project
items.quote: Normal CAPEX plans are there. It is about Rs. 250 crore worth of projects we have.

items.statement: Gadepan-II annual turnaround scheduled for March 2026, Q1 shutdown cost Rs.16-17 crore contribution loss
items.quote: Gadepan-II is scheduled to go in March 26 for its annual turnaround since the second year of operation would have completed. As far as this loss of 55,000 odd tons is concerned, the total loss of production would have cost the Company in terms of contribution about Rs. 16 - Rs. 17 crore.

items.statement: Crop protection sales primarily through urea channel, beginning to add pure CPC channel partners
items.quote: We are quite a bit focused on our urea channel. Quite a bit of our people have in the channel width itself, still some way to go in our fertili ser channel itself. However, we are beginning to pick up stray one or two kinds of people who are purely from the CPC channel, not very big participants in the fertili ser channel.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs.1,600 crore as of June 30
items.quote: Around Rs. 1,600 crore as on 30th June.

items.statement: Gas price for quarter at $15.15 per MMBtu on NCV basis
items.quote: It is about $15.15 on NCV basis per MMBtu.

items.statement: Second half demand expected to improve supported by festive season and favorable monsoon impact on farm income
items.quote: Second half could witness better demand supported by the festive season and positive impact of favorable monsoon on farm income.

items.statement: Geopolitical and trade tensions with tariff uncertainties remain key risk across value chain
items.quote: Continuing geopolitical and trade tensions, along with tariff-related uncertainties remain a key risk across the value chain.

items.statement: PTCF approval process currently underway
items.quote: For PTCF, approval process is currently underway.

items.statement: Filament Yarn sales impacted by fire at Bharuch plant in February 2025; plant resumed full operations from June 2025
items.quote: In the Filament Yarn segment, sales were impacted by a fire at our Bharuch plant in February 2025. The plant resumed full operations from June '25.

items.statement: Filament Yarn prices under pressure due to increased Chinese imports at lower prices; focus on value-added products to improve margins
items.quote: Prices remained under pressure due to increased imports from China at lower prices. Our focus continues to be on value -added products to improve margins.

items.statement: Caprolactam prices declining to record low levels causing margin pressure; renewable energy at Bharuch plant helped control power costs
items.quote: On the raw material side, caprolactam prices continue to decline to record low levels, resulting in margin pressure. However, use of renewable energy at Bharuch plant helped in controlling power costs.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 operating revenue INR402 crores, down 24% YoY; EBITDA INR20 crores, down 52% YoY; EBITDA margin 4.96%; PAT INR15 crores, down 37% YoY; PAT margin 3.84%
items.quote: The operating revenue stood at INR402 crores, which declined by almost 24% year -on-year. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR20 crores, which declined by 52% year -on-year. EBITDA margin were reported at 4.96%.

items.statement: Total volume declined 17% YoY to 17,072 metric tons; Tyre Cord Fabrics revenue down 35% YoY to INR181 crores; Filament Yarn revenue down 15% YoY to INR193 crores
items.quote: Total volume for quarter 1 FY '26 declined by 17% year -on-year to 17,072 metric tons. Tyre Cord Fabrics revenue for quarter 1 FY '26 decreased by around 35% year -on-year to almost INR181 crores.

items.statement: Raised issue of Chinese imports and FTA countries lacking duty protection; requested QCO process and minimum import price on Tyre Cord Fabrics
items.quote: Through our association, we have raised this issue of our imports from China and also from the free trade agreement countries where the duty protection is not available. And we have raised this issue in terms of asking one is for either initiating immediately the QCO process so that, first of all, substandard material does not come.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin range 6-8%; current margins below target due to falling raw material prices causing inventory losses and overcapacity across value chain
items.quote: The more likely margins that we commit or we target normally is between 6% to 8%. Yes, our margins are lower than the target between 6% to 8% for this quarter and also for the previous quarter.

items.statement: Caprolactam prices fell ~$400 from April 2024 to June 2025; good correlation with crude oil prices but not direct; overcapacity across value chain squeezing margins globally
items.quote: We are seeing now hopefully that the raw material prices are close to their bottom. These are record low levels with almost a fall of $400 from April '24 to June '25.

items.statement: Polyester tyre cord capacity expansion (not yet commissioned) to enter passenger car tyre segment; NTCF expansion for quality improvement and balancing capacity based on 2022-23 demand
items.quote: our capacity expansion and which is still not commissioned is related to polyester t yre cord. And the purpose of getting into that segment is that we didn't have presence in the polyester t yre cord, which is used in passenger car

items.statement: New polyester tyre cord capacity expected to generate INR100-120 crores revenue at full capacity under normal raw material pricing assumptions
items.quote: From our new capacity, it could be between -- at the full capacity between INR100 crores to INR120 crores.

items.statement: Inventory buildup of INR315 crores was temporary due to tyre companies' inventory correction; expect reduction to normal levels by end of Q2
items.quote: inventory buildup was temporary. So what happens is since most of the raw materials are imported. And suddenly, if the t yre companies take an inventory correction, we have to adjust our production. So the inventory buildup happens both at raw material and FG state. But we are seeing an inventory reduction and hopefully, by end of Q2, we should reach to closer to normal inventory

items.statement: Most large capex projects completed by March 2025; remaining CWIP small, focused on cost reduction, energy conservation and replacement capex; projects must clear 10-12% ROCE hurdle rate

items.statement: Net surplus cash over INR3.25 billion; focus on strategic investments for growth; dividend payout decided by Board
items.quote: The focus is on getting more strategic investments and grow this company. But anyway, the payout is more call to be taken out by the Board, and we can only recommend but the final -- and it has already been for the year being given out in terms of the dividend.

items.statement: Tyre Cord Fabrics has raw material pass-through mechanism; Filament Yarn has pass-through but not always in timelines or quantum due to demand-supply and Chinese imports

And that has been continuing for many years in the past and continues in the current year as well. As far as the Filament Yarn is concerned, ultimately, there is a pass -through, but it may not be in terms of time lines or in terms of quantum

items.statement: Bharuch plant fully commissioned by June end; operating at 90-95%+ capacity; expect full capacity with better festive season demand

items.statement: Domestic pricing with duty paid almost matches Chinese import pricing; quarter-on-quarter may differ due to annualized pricing formula
items.quote: So on -- with the duty paid, it is almost matching. There could be a few -- because the pricing is also an annualized pricing formula based. So on quarter-on-quarter, it could be different. But normally, the pricing is closer to or similar to the duty paid pricing coming from China.

items.statement: Some inefficient/indebted NFY players shut down in past 2 years; but new investments also happening including for value-added products
items.quote: In NFY, yes, there have been some -- I mean, not in the immediate past, but last year and previous year, some of the inefficient players and some players who are possibly more indebted had to shut down. But there is also growth. A lot of people are making some new investments as well.

items.statement: NFY growth strategy: increase value-added products to differentiate from Chinese bulk products; PTCF growth from expansion; NTCF focus on efficiency improvements and equipment replacement
items.quote: For us, particularly in NFY, we would be looking at only increasing our value -added products the way we have done for the last few years. And that is something which has held us against a very high price intensity competition from China.

items.statement: PTCF EBITDA margin range similar to company target of 6-8%
items.quote: Similar. I mean when we say it's similar for the company, between 6% to 8%.

items.statement: Raw material sourced from multiple countries including two domestic sources; no significant supply or pricing risk seen
items.quote: We source from multiple countries, and we don't see any significant risk because like other products, raw material is also available abundantly. So we don't see any risk. And we continue to source from our two sources in India as well.

items.statement: India automotive industry showed upward trend in Q1 FY26, led by tractors and three-wheelers; passenger vehicles, two-wheelers and commercial vehicles saw mild improvements.
items.quote: India's automotive industry has shown an upward trend in Q1 FY ' 26, particularly in tractors and three-wheelers , while passenger vehicles, two -wheelers and commercial vehicles have seen mild improvements , indicating a cautious market recovery.

items.statement: Heavy commercial vehicles grew due to pre-buying ahead of mandatory cabin AC regulation from October 1, 2025, expected to increase cost by 1%-2%.
items.quote: Heavy commercial vehicles experienced positive growth due to pre-buying ahead of the mandatory air conditioning regulations mandated by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for cabins in medium and heavy duty trucks manufactured from October 1st, 2025. This pre-buying is driven by expectations of 1% -2% cost increase due to the new regulation.

items.statement: Passenger vehicle growth in FY26 expected moderate due to high inventory, muted mini/micro demand, and potential EV component shortages from Chinese export restrictions.
items.quote: Passenger vehicles growth in FY ' 26 is expected to remain moderate impacted by high inventory levels and muted consumer demand for mini micro categories and potential component sho rtages for EV due to Chinese export restrictions, a key watch out for the remaining part of the financial year.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle segment projected to grow at moderate single digit in FY26 supported by better financing, infrastructure revival, rural demand and fleet replacement.
items.quote: The overall commercial vehicle segment is projected to grow at moderate single digit owing to headwinds from evolving comfort norms. However, better financing, infrastructure revival, rural demand an d fleet replacement trends will support the growth of this segment.

items.statement: Tractor segment projected to perform better in FY26 supported by strong rural demand, favorable monsoon forecast and rising MSPs.
items.quote: The tractor segment is projected to perform better this fiscal year supported by strong rural demand, a favorable monsoon forecast and rising minimum support prices for key crops.

items.statement: Two-wheeler growth in FY26 expected to reach all-time high fueled by festive season and above-normal monsoon boosting rural incomes.
items.quote: The two-wheeler growth in FY '26 is expected to reach an all-time high fuel by the upcoming festive season and an above normal monsoon that could boost rural incomes.

items.statement: Mobility business grew 14.3% YoY in April-June 2025 driven by power solutions (+13.7%) and two-wheeler business from OBD 2 norms implementation.
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter, the mobility business has grown by 14.3% in April -June 25 as compared to April-June 24 driven mainly by growth in power solutions business by 13.7% on account of higher demand for diesel components mainly from off highway and passenger car segments.

items.statement: Consumer goods business grew 9.3% YoY driven by higher demand for tools and accessories.
items.quote: The consumer goods business grew by 9.3% driven by higher demand for tools and accessories.

items.statement: Building technologies business declined 65.3% YoY due to sale of Video Solutions and Access & Intrusion Communication systems business.
items.quote: Building technologies business declined by 65.3% mainly due to the sale of Video Solutions and Access and Intrusion and Communication systems business.

items.statement: Revenue from operations in Q1 FY26 was INR 47,886 million, up 10.9% YoY; EBITDA was INR 6,393 million, up 23% YoY on revenue growth and material cost improvement.
items.quote: Overall, revenue from operations in April-June 25 stood at 47,886 million INR which grew by 10.9% over April-June 2024. The growth is driven by increase in sales in Power Solutions, Two-Wheeler Powersports, Mobility Aftermarket business and Consumer Goods business as seen in the previous slide.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved YoY due to revenue growth and material cost improvement; PAT margin rose to 23.3% from 10.8% YoY due to improved EBITDA and profit on sale of building technologies businesses.
items.quote: EBITDA in April-June 25 was 6,393 million INR which grew by 23% over the same quarter of the previous year. The improvement in EBITDA margin is mainly on account of growth in revenue and improvement in material cost.

items.statement: Two-wheeler business growth driven by exhaust gas sensor ramp-up from OBD 2 Phase-B implementation from April 1, 2025; localization delivered from Bidadi plant.
items.quote: significant growth in two -wheeler business was seen mainly on account of ramp up in sale of exhaust gas sensors due to implementation of OBD 2 norms from 1st of April 2025.

items.statement: Material cost improvement contributed to EBITDA margin; product mix shift toward manufactured goods in Q1 FY26 favored material cost.
items.quote: And in April-June 25, it was in favor of the manufactured goods. That means the demands from the customers were mainly out of all manufactured goods here in In dia and this is then, of course, also influencing the material cost.

items.statement: Pricing based on customer contracts; localization benefits passed on per contract terms.
items.quote: Just to add on the pricing that you asked, these are all based on customer contracts, so they vary and we do what is agreed with the customer.

items.statement: Johnson Controls-Hitachi acquisition is global, portfolio complementary in HVAC; comes as separate division not within listed company, expected to stay that way.

items.quote: And the reasons could be different for other portfolio decisions and I can't comment on that, but this was how it was felt. But that is the general principle of how we look at portfolio choices.

items.statement: Two-wheeler volumes will stabilize after ramp-up; 40% QoQ growth due to new projects.

items.statement: Rare earth magnet supply risk: inventory coverage until end of August; task forces formed in India and globally; working on multiple mitigation options.
