items.statement: EBO retail network ~1.78 million sq ft globally as of June 2025; focus on flagship stores and SIS openings.
items.quote: As of June 2025, Vedant Fashions EBO retail area network stands at about 1.78 million square feet globally. During the quarter, we strategically scaled up our marketing efforts across multiple channels including social media and our various other brands, which contributed to o ur performance

items.statement: Mohey SSG beating company average; Twamev SSG doing very well; Diwas launched last festive, real test upcoming festive season.
items.quote: We have continuously being beaten the Company average when it comes to Mohey's SSG, and overall growth has also been positive. So, with this strategy in mind and the evolved digital marketing strategy, we feel we are poised to continue growing Mohey.

items.statement: ASP target growth ~3.6-3.7% (3% within categories + 70-80 bps from Mohey/Twamev mix shift).
items.quote: So, all in all, 3.6% - 3.7% is something which we sort of target as ASP growth, which is one lever.

items.statement: Receivables days improved to 71 days (TTM June 2025) from 77 days in FY25.
items.quote: But on an overall level if you look at, in TTM June 2025, our receivables days are 71 days, whereas in FY '25 it was 77 days. So, it has actually come down compared to FY '25.

items.statement: Unorganized 'me-too' brand store openings slowing after 8-10 quarters of high intensity; expect further slowdown.
items.quote: So, like we have been mentioning, over the last 8 quarters - 10 quarters, we have definitely seen a large number of store openings. However, given how closely we track them and monitor them, majority of these Me-too brands, the performance is something which makes us question if the intensity of openings can keep up.

items.statement: Investing in daily 2-3 min training via VFL Parivaar app for fashion advisors; also investing in omni-channel and AI-driven training.
items.quote: The big project being the VFL Parivaar app where we train our fashion advisors almost for two minutes to three minutes on a daily basis, instead of focusing on the two to three times training per year, which was typically done in the retail industry.

items.statement: Retail rental inflation remains high; expanding only in pockets where rental yield makes sense.
items.quote: So, to your second part, retail inflation continues to remain high. So, while we see some pockets, the inflation slowing down, these are the pockets where we are again going strong on expansion.

items.statement: No formal guidance given for revenue, SSG, or store net additions; focus on SSG and retail quality over net square feet growth.
items.quote: So, again, we do not give any guidance as such. But from a qualitative perspective, the goal every year is to do decently well in SSG.

items.statement: Express Parcel service EBITDA margin expected to remain within 16-18% normative range
items.quote: We will remain broadly within the normative range of 16 to 18% in the Express Parcel business as guided previously.

items.statement: PTL service EBITDA margin target of 16-18% expected at 600,000-640,000 tonnes quarterly load
items.quote: Roughly at close to about 600,000 to 640,000 tonnes of quarterly load which translates to about 200,000 to 215,000 tonnes of monthly load whereas currently we are posting an average of about 150,000 tonnes of monthly load, three things will kic k in

items.statement: Supply Chain Services revenue target of Rs. 1,800-2,000 crores in three years (FY29)
items.quote: In your Shareholder Letter you are talking about roughly Rs. 1,800 to Rs. 2,000 crore of revenue in three years which I'm guessing is FY29.

items.statement: Ecom Express integration costs limited to Rs. 300 crores envelope, no further recurring costs expected
items.quote: The integration costs, as we've mentioned, our envelope was about Rs. 300 crores that we anticipated. And we will report that separately in Q2 and Q3, calling out quite clearly what the specific integration costs from the Ecom Express acquisition will be.

items.statement: Express Parcel volumes grew 14% YoY and 17% QoQ to 208 million shipments in Q1FY26
items.quote: Parcel volumes reached 208 million shipments for Q1, which represents a year on year growth of nearly 14% and a quarter on quarter growth of 17%.

items.statement: July Express Parcel volumes significantly higher than June, trend expected to continue through Q2 and Q3
items.quote: I'm pleased to announce that that has continued through June and has gone up significantly into July. Our belief is that this trend will continue through the rest of this quarter.

items.statement: PTL freight tonnage grew 15% YoY to 458,000 tonnes in Q1FY26, broadly flat QoQ
items.quote: We closed at 458,000 tonnes of freight in Q1, which represents a year on year growth of 15% and broadly flat quarter on quarter.

items.statement: Overall service EBITDA margin expanded to 13% in Q1FY26, up 60bps QoQ and 190bps YoY
items.quote: Total service EBITDA came in at Rs. 298 crores or 13%, which is an expansion of 60 basis points versus Q4FY25 and an expansion of 190 basis points compared to FY25 on the whole.

items.statement: Express Parcel service EBITDA margin at 16.3% in Q1FY26, up from 15.1% low point in Q2FY25
items.quote: Express Parcel came in at Rs. 228 crores of service EBITDA at a 16.3% margin. As discussed previously, we expected continued expansion in parcel margins from Q2 of last year, which was a low point at 15.1%.

items.statement: PTL service EBITDA margin at 10.7% in Q1FY26, expected to rise with network utilisation improvements
items.quote: Part Truckload margins continue to remain stable. We brought in Rs. 54 crores of service EBITDA margin in the Part Truckload business in Q1 at 10.7%.

items.statement: Supply Chain Services margin improved significantly from 2.2% in FY25 to 7.2% in Q1FY26
items.quote: Margins in this business have improved significantly from 2.2% as of FY25 to 7.2% in Q1FY26, the business brought in Rs. 15 crores of service EBITDA this quarter.

items.statement: PAT margin expanded to nearly 4% in Q1FY26 from 2.4% in Q1FY25, expected to continue expanding through FY26
items.quote: PAT stood at Rs. 91 crores or a PAT margin of nearly 4%, an expansion of Rs. 18 crores compared to Q4FY25 and an expansion of nearly 60% compared to the same quarter last year

items.statement: Supply Chain Services pipeline at Rs. 300 crores in advanced conversion stages, over Rs. 1,000 crores total pipeline
items.value: Rs. 300 crores advanced, Rs. 1,000+ crores total
items.quote: At this stage, we've got probably close to about Rs. 300 crores of broad supply chain mandates which are in various stages of conversion. Now conversion in this business can take three to four months because it's a long sales cycle but given our visibility of the pipeline we're very confident. Frankly speaking, at this stage Delhivery Ltd Q1 FY26 Earnings Call Aug 1, 2025 from a pure pipeline stan

items.quote: Infrastructure continues to remain at about 20.4 million square feet of gateways and fulfilment centres, as opposed to 20.1 million square feet in Q4. Continue to operate 119 gateways. This includes a few new gateways that have been integrated from the Ecom Express network into the Delhivery network, 45 automated sort centres, 64

items.statement: Express delivery centres to expand from 4,500 to 4,750-4,800 by end of FY26
items.quote: My sense is you should see this number at probably close to about 4,750 to 4,800 by the end of the year.

items.statement: Ecom Express network integration complete, 7 facilities to be retained, non-express businesses to exit by Q3FY26
items.quote: On a final basis, we expect to retain seven facilities in a combinatio n of transportation and fulfilment operations. And so as a consequence of that, yield has shrunk. So it's j

items.statement: PTL yield improvements continue with revenue growth exceeding volume growth
items.quote: Revenue growth being higher than volume growth implies that yield improvements have continued in this business as well.

items.statement: Active customers expanded from 35,000 in Q1FY25 to 43,000 in Q1FY26
items.quote: Total number of active customers have expanded significantly from 35,000 in Q1FY25 to nearly 8,000 customers. As of this quarter, we closed with 43,000 active customers.

items.statement: Ecom Express volume retention at 55-65%, significantly above planned 30%; gained share across D2C, SME, and marketplace clients
items.quote: What I can tell you, without disclosing specifics, is that we have retained significantly more than the 30% that was planned originally, which is reflected in the chart that Apar had shown previously. I think, broadly speaking, we will be close to perhaps somewhere in the 55% to 65% retained volume already.

items.statement: Market share expanded ~25% post Ecom acquisition; consolidation towards quality players (Delhivery, Blue Dart) expected to continue
items.quote: Ecom Express was probably about 50-60 percent of our size so our market share has probably expanded by about 25 percent or so. Possibly higher but I'm not entirely sure. I think that I'll give you a much better answer maybe at the end of Q2, Q3 when things stabilize a bit more.

items.statement: Irrational pricing by other 3PLs reduced due to financial constraints; balance sheet pressures forcing pricing discipline
items.quote: I think what we've seen is a reduction in the intensity of price competition. I wouldn't like to necessarily take credit for us having driven sense into the market. I think it's the financial constraints that companies which price irrationally face in the first place.

items.statement: Express Parcel now 61% of total revenue; PTL 22%; Supply Chain Services de-grew due to quick commerce exit and electronics client seasonality
items.quote: The Express Parcel business has grown as a percentage of our total revenues on the back of increased volumes towards the tailend of Q1 and stands at 61% of total revenues. The PTL business continues to form 22% of total revenues.

items.statement: Category mix: softlines ~50%, FMCG/BPC ~25%, grocery near zero; not intending to play in grocery
items.quote: my sense is maybe softline is probably about half our volumes. You know, FMCG, BPC kind of categories are maybe about a quarter. And the rest of it is just Delhivery Ltd Q1 FY26 Earnings Call Aug 1, 2025 a very broad mix. Grocery is practically zero, unsurprisingly. It's not a category that we intend

items.statement: Ecom Express acquisition completed July 18, 2025 at Rs. 1,369 crores final consideration; volume/client integration complete
items.quote: The acquisition was formally completed on July 18 th and financial consolidation of Ecom Express into Delhivery will be effective from this date. The final purchase consideration as guided previously after the adjustments will be at Rs. 1,369 crores

items.statement: Team size expanded to 65,849 with 52,000 partner agents and 17,000 vehicles daily
items.quote: Team size has expanded to 65,849 people with 52,000 partner agents and 17,000 vehicles on a daily basis.

items.statement: Board changes: Mr. Srivatsan Rajan stepping down September 2025; Prof. Padmini Srinivasan and Mr. Yashish Dahiya joining as new directors
items.quote: I would like to place on record on behalf of the entire team of Delhivery our deepest gratitude to one of our directors, Mr. Srivatsan Rajan, who has served as a director on the Board of Delhivery for the last 10 years and will be stepping down in September. I would also like to extend a very warm welcome to two new directors on the Delhivery Board. Professor Padmini Srinivasan from the Indian Ins

items.statement: Peak season timing shifted to mid-September 2025, impacting Q2 and early Q3 more than Q3 alone
items.quote: Do bear in mind that this is an unusual year. The peak season this year is expected to be in the middle of September. Unlike last year, the impact of a large portion of the peak will be seen in Q2 and the early part of Q3.

items.statement: PTL business targets 20% annual revenue growth for FY26, with Q1 at 17% YoY (higher adjusted for IndAS).
items.quote: the business gives us confidence that it would be able to meet the 20% revenue growth expectations that we have for the business.

items.statement: Ecom acquisition front-loads ~Rs 300 crore capex for sorting equipment, to be warehoused and deployed as long-term capacity needs arise.
items.quote: With the acquisition of Ecom Express, nothing in this changes except the fact that we have front-loaded Capex by roughly about Rs. 300 crores. Now, this Rs. 300 crore rupee Capex is essentially not something we are going to put into active use from day one.

items.statement: Distribution centres grew 1% (4,450 to 4,500) while volumes rose 14% QoQ, implying 14% higher DC utilisation; sort centre utilisation also up 14% with flat count.
items.quote: for whatever 1% increase in delivery centres, we have had a 14% increase in volumes. All those volumes are delivered through distribution centres. And so, therefore, the utilisation of the distribution centres has gone up to that exact mathematical extent.

items.statement: Line-haul tractor-trailer utilisation broadly 60-65%; marginal decline in Q1 due to fleet expansion and double-trailer experiments.
items.quote: Trucking utilizations, because they also depend on the directionality of the loads that one is creating, I think broadly speaking, as I mentioned, have been in that 60% to 65% kind of range.

items.statement: Delhivery handled 208 million packages in Q1 FY26 vs 180 million in Q4 FY25; July volumes significantly higher.
items.quote: We've obviously gotten to 208 million packages in Q1, but July obviously has been significantly higher and we expect that it will continue.

items.statement: Incremental margins on Ecom volumes could exceed 35-40% as network utilisation rises 30-40% with only 6% DC expansion; last-mile fixed costs ~10% of total.
items.quote: if volumes in the network go up 30%-40% in this period, that obviously is going to present a massive increase in utilisation. Our last mile delivery costs, as an example, just the fixed costs that are about 10% of total costs. And so, you will see a pretty significant reduction there.

items.statement: PTL margin path to high-teens supported by yield improvement from retail customer mix shift and existing customers becoming more quality-conscious.
items.quote: as we increase that, which is a higher yielding business, more profitable even for us, whatever lesser we do at this point in time, as we increase that share, the profitability and the yields will continue to go up.

items.statement: Structural 'flight to quality' driven by marketplace volatility, weather variability, and festive-season peaks increasing reliance on high-quality partners.
items.quote: as the volatility goes up, they are finding that other networks don't have the ability to take that on. And, in some senses, I guess, the more variable the weather becomes, the more festive seasons have an impact, and the more these guys go after growth, the more they will have to rely on high quality partners.

items.statement: Customer pricing based on volume charts remains stable; no material changes, adjustments only for mix shifts. Ecom acquisition expected to keep pricing stable.
items.quote: We are not seeing any material changes to that. In some cases, of course, there are adjustments that we do during the year to reflect any change in the client's business in terms of mix, etc.. And hence, our desire or their desire to change the mix for us or to introduce new products at some points, I think, like Sahil mentioned, that has been broadly very, very stable.

items.statement: New FTL value-added services (fuel procurement, on-road assistance, control tower) target strategic supply-chain efficiency, not large standalone TAM; aim to bind quality trucking supply.
items.quote: These are theoretically large TAMs. But just to be perfectly clear, Delhivery's ambition is not to become the largest retailer of fuel to trucks. So, it should not be viewed in that fashion either. We have very specific strategic objectives for our FTL business, which is fundamentally, first of all, to bring down the cost of trucking procurement for Delhivery's own transportation operations.

items.statement: Other income rose to Rs 1.3 billion in Q1 from mark-to-market gains on securities as rates fell; expected to normalise and decline as yields drop and Rs 1,400 crore deployed for Ecom acquisition.
items.quote: the increase in other income is primarily due to increase in value of mark to market securities due to interest rates going down in Q1 of the current fiscal year. In the subsequent quarters, we expect this to normalise to our earlier level and maybe slightly go down because the yield curves have gone down.

items.statement: Paid ~Rs 1,400 crore on 18 July 2025 to acquire Ecom Express; no further interest income on that capital.
items.quote: we have paid close to Rs. 1,400 crores to acquire Ecom Express on 18th of July. And hence, no further interest income is going to accrue on it.

items.statement: Q1 PTL revenue impacted by Operation Sindoor and monsoon rains; monsoon impact easing, July numbers good, Q2 tracking well.
items.quote: there was a material impact because of Operation Sindoor, there was some impact because of the rains in certain places. And it is getting worse, obviously, year on year, but here on at least the monsoon appears to have died down to a significant extent.

items.statement: Ahmedabad Delhivery Direct (on-demand intracity) reached contribution margin break-even in ~4 months; Delhi and Bengaluru 4x larger, still stabilising.
items.quote: is the first city that we launched in Delhivery Direct and we are at contribution margin break even in about four months

items.statement: PTL revenue slightly impacted by IndAS accounting adjustments in Q1; adjusted growth higher than reported 17% YoY.
items.quote: this quarter's revenue got slightly impacted by the accounting adjustment s, the IndAS adjustments that we need to do to follow the statutory requirements. So adjusted for that, the 17% growth would be slightly

items.statement: Evaluating air freight entry; already a large belly-cargo shipper, may make decisive move when timing is right.
items.quote: We do continue to evaluate air freight. We do have a material amount of load that now moves on air freight. We're obviously not as large as Blue Dart yet, but we're a very large shipper on an aircraft belly. So that's something that Ajith and his team continue to evaluate.

items.statement: Non-JLG loan book guided to grow 30%+ in FY26; JLG growth guidance withheld due to uncertainty
items.quote: Non-JLG, we are sure about, certain about 30% plus growth as far as non-JLG book is concerned, other than JLG. Right now, giving a specific guidance on the growth of JLG will be difficult, but non-JLG around 30% plus is what we can guide to the investors.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to drop from Q3 FY26; normalcy in collections and portfolio growth anticipated in 3-4 months
items.quote: Quarter 2 by and large will be the similar type. But Quarter 3 onwards, we should see a drop down.

items.statement: Medium-term target of 15%+ ROE and 25-30% loan growth over 2-3 years
items.quote: If you look at next 3 years horizon or so, we are confident of giving that type of ROE on an overall basis. And a good growth of around 25-30% what we expect, if you look at a medium-term horizon.

items.statement: Medium-term NIM target of 8.5%+ driven by mix change, cost of funds decline and scale benefits
items.quote: Close to 8.5% NIM should be possible with the change of mix that is important, change of mix. But because we will get the operational efficiency, we will get cost of fund decline and overall benefits of scale.

items.statement: X-bucket collection efficiency stable at 98.6% in July, same as June
items.quote: 98.6% was our X-bucket collection efficiency for July also.

items.statement: Fresh NPA slippages reduced in Q1 FY26; further decline expected in next few months
items.quote: Fresh NPA accretion will decline meaningfully in next few months.

items.statement: CGFMU credit guarantee registered from Jan 17, 2025 covering incremental JLG and MBBL disbursements; ~95%+ of new portfolio covered
items.quote: We have also registered with CGFMU for credit guarantee coverage on our eligible JLG and MBBL portfolio with effect from January 17, 2025. Accordingly, incremental JLG and MBBL disbursements from then onwards are getting covered under credit guarantee.

items.statement: JLG loan book declined 7% QoQ due to MFIN Guardrail 2.0 impact and collection focus; non-JLG portfolio grew 39% YoY and 2% QoQ
items.quote: The moderation in overall loan book growth was driven almost entirely by the contraction in our JLG book, which declined by 7% during the quarter. Conversely, the share of secured loans within the overall loan book increased to 45% as on June 25 from 35% as on June 24.

items.statement: Cost of funds declined 20 bps QoQ on savings and retail term deposits; further reduction expected post repo rate cuts
items.quote: We have already reduced our rates on term deposit and our savings account. We have already seen 20 basis point cost coming down on both of these from previous quarter to this quarter. So, the cost of funds should lead to further improvement in terms of the operating profit.

items.statement: No new branch openings planned except few JLG split branches; focus on leveraging existing network for cross-sell
items.quote: This year, other than barring a very few branches, which are basically split branches for JLG, we are not opening branches. Our idea is that we have enough number of branches right now.

items.statement: Board and shareholder approval for Rs. 750 crore equity raise; engagement with investors to intensify post results, targeting completion by end Q2 or early next month
items.quote: We have already taken approval from the board and the shareholders for a fund raise of Rs. 750 crore. I think we will intensify the engagement with the potential investor. We are hoping to do that. If not this quarter end, maybe early month after that.

items.statement: Reverse merger of holding company with bank approved; NCLT petition sequencing being examined alongside equity raise
items.quote: We have also secured all requisite statutory approvals on the proposed reverse merger of the holding company with the bank. With these approvals in hand, we are now examining the optimal sequencing of petition filing with NCLT application in tandem with the equity raise.

items.statement: No short-term borrowings on balance sheet
items.quote: We don't have any short-term borrowing on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio at 19.6% as on June 30, 2025, comfortably above regulatory threshold
items.quote: Despite the losses, our capital adequacy ratio remained at 19.6%, as on June 30, 2025, comfortably above the regulatory threshold.

items.statement: Net loss of Rs. 239 crores in Q1 FY26 due to carry-forward stress in JLG portfolio
items.quote: Nonetheless, the carry-forward stress translated into a net loss of Rs. 239 crores for Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Collection force strengthened with >800 people plus specialized call center for overdue accounts; large MB branches split for better control
items.quote: We continue to build and deploy higher collection force, also established a specialized call center focused exclusively on overdue accounts and implemented stricter oversight of field processes, ranging from center meeting discipline to effective monitoring and supervision. We continue to split large MB branches to

items.statement: Business transformation project underway to make technology architecture and processes future-ready
items.quote: We are also undertaking a business transformation project to make our technology architecture and business processes future-ready for our growth plans.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 saw headwinds from India-Pakistan conflict, Iran-Israel conflict, and Air India crash disrupting peak summer season; July demand recovered quickly in Europe and Middle East, normalizing to pre-headwind expectations.
items.quote: We saw several headwinds through the quarter starting with the India - Pakistan conflict; then the Iran - Israel conflict, and then the very unfortunate Air India crash. This caused repeated disruptions in a very important quarter from the travel industry's perspective.

items.statement: Monthly transacting buyers grew 5% YoY to over 29,500 in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Our monthly transacting buyers grew by 5% to touch more than 29,500 monthly transacting buyers.

items.statement: GTV grew over 2% YoY in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Our GTV grew by over 2%

items.statement: Revenue grew 22% YoY in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: the revenue grew by 22%

items.statement: Like-to-like EBITDA was flat YoY in Q1 FY26; PAT saw marginal growth. Heavy international investment suppressed EBITDA.
items.quote: On a like-to-like basis, the EBITDA was flat and there is a marginal growth in PAT.

items.statement: International monthly active agents rose from 8,600-9,000 in Q1 FY25 to nearly 11,000 in June 2025 after accelerated hiring from February.
items.quote: Starting Feb, this number has started to grow very meaningfully, and we are touching close to 11,000 monthly active agents in June.

items.statement: New travel agent onboarding milestones (T1, T5, T10) more than doubled in Q1 FY26 vs January; T1s hit nearly 750 in June from 300-340 in January.
items.quote: Our T1s were trending at between 300-340 in Jan. This number has more than doubled, and we have hit nearly 750 T1s in June.

items.statement: New travel agents added in Q1 FY26 contributed 4.2% of international GTV ($18M of $435M) vs 2.2% in Q1 FY25 ($7.8M of $361M).
items.quote: Now looking at April-May-June, 2025 out of the $435 Mn of GTV that we have done, $18 million or 4.2% of GTV has been contributed by new travel agents added in the same year.

items.statement: YoY new customer addition rate grew 69% in Q1 FY26; 21% of business now handled by new key account managers hired since February.
items.quote: On a YoY basis there is a 69% growth in new customer addition. Just to be clear, it is not that the total number of customers have grown by 69% but the rate at which we are adding new customers has grown by 69% and 21% of the business is now being handled by the new key account managers.

items.statement: Management expects operating leverage to flow through by Q4 FY26 as new agent cohorts mature and investment pace slows; SG&A growth to slow YoY by Q4.
items.quote: Our hope also is that we continue to believe in the previous hypothesis that by Q4 we should start to see a lot more operating leverage flow through in this part of the business.

items.statement: ~2/3 of planned international hiring investment completed; remaining 1/3 to be timed over Q2 and Q3 FY26, possibly spilling to Q4.
items.quote: about a 2/3 of our investment and hiring has happened. 1/3 is left, which will get timed over the next two quarters.

items.statement: Margins expected to stabilize by Q4 FY26 as investment phase ends and new agent cohorts become productive; hard to predict exact trajectory.
items.quote: Hopefully by Q4 we would have finished our investment, and that is where we should be able to stabilize margins.

items.statement: Hotel revenue growth outpaced GTV due to mix shift toward commissionable suppliers (higher take rate) and in-housing of third-party technology; GP growth lower due to commission sharing with agents.
items.quote: There are a couple of other unlocks that we did in this quarter, Manish and specifically on certain parts of our business there is income that was dependent on a third-party vendor. Let me not disclose too much detail on that and we brought that technology in-house, which had a meaningful improvement in our retention of that revenue within our business, otherwise it was sitting as a cost with the

items.statement: Hotel gross take rate ~8.3% in Q1 FY26 driven by commissionable supplier mix; underlying hotel GP margin ~5.5% (yearly average), nominal improvement vs 5.56% this quarter.
items.quote: if you see, the overall gross profit of the hotel business is around 5.56 so versus last year's same quarter it may look high versus 5.06. But if we take out, iron out the things and we see the yearly average, we were at a 5.5.

items.statement: Management does not provide specific revenue or GTV guidance; Q2 FY26 GTV expected in line with pre-headwind budget, unlikely to fully catch up Q1 shortfall.
items.quote: We don't provide specific guidance on revenue.

items.statement: Middle East GTV grew north of 20% YoY in Q1 FY26 despite lost selling days; growth driven by new customer addition, improved service via Egypt operations, and Ramadan timing.
items.quote: The Middle East saw a very improved growth, and this is in spite of the fact that we lost significant days of sale in Q1.

items.statement: Europe GTV slowed in Q1 FY26 partly due to Israel (top-10 source market) sales going to zero/negative during conflict; July recovery seen.
items.quote: Europe has slowed down in Q1, part of that slowdown is because we count Israel as part of Europe, and Israel is a top 10 source market for us and that is one market that went to zero in fact negative sales for the period of that time.

items.statement: Brazil/LATAM faces structural near-term challenge from new tax and FX volatility; management reducing cost of sales to lower pricing and regain demand share.
items.quote: in the short term, there is a structural challenge in that market, because this is a new tax, as currencies are volatile right now, foreign exchange is getting expensive for most of the developing world.

items.statement: Hosting/bandwidth costs surged >100% YoY in Q1 FY26 due to search traffic growth and AI infrastructure investment; cost per search metric improving, moderating dollar cost growth.
items.quote: We have seen close to more than 100% kind of growth in search traffic, and that's essentially ballooned the cost. Plus, we essentially made significant investments as far as the AI infrastructure is concerned.

items.statement: ESOP expense ~Rs 6.8 Cr in Q1 FY26; full-year FY26 estimate Rs 25-28 Cr (assuming no new grants); ESOP amortized over 4 years, expected to continue as talent tool.
items.quote: the expense that is had in the quarter was around Rs. 6.8 Cr, and we expect that overall, for the full year, it should be in the range of around Rs. 25 to Rs. 28 Cr depending if there is no further grants.

items.statement: Hotel business operates at negative working capital of 3-4 days of GTV at enterprise level; agents on advance or credit models; suppliers paid near check-in or monthly/fortnightly post check-in.
items.quote: at an overall enterprise level, we would generally be sitting on a negative working capital of 3 to 4 days of GTV.

items.statement: Airline GTV share 38% in Q1 FY26 (hotels/ancillary 62%); airline GP contribution only 11-12% vs hotels >85%; air GTV historically grew 10-12% but declined last 3 quarters.
items.quote: For airline GTV, overall, it is currently in this quarter was contributed around 38% in terms of the GTV and 62% was contributed on hotels and ancillary. However, the gross profit numbers there in the airline business would be contributing around 11% to 12% and hotel business contributes more than 85% per say.

items.statement: Hotel take-rate expansion not a focus for next 12-24 months; priority is passing supply-side pricing benefits to agents to stay competitive and drive top-line growth.
items.quote: Nitin that's not a focus area for us right now, because it's hard to drive top line growth as well as margin expansion at the same time.

items.statement: New KAM cohorts expected to drive growth for 2-3 years; each cohort takes ~2+ years to reach full value, doubling in year 2 and outpacing in year 3 before plateauing.
items.quote: we would expect to see at least two to three years of runway of fresh growth because of these KAMs.

items.quote: We have achieved rapid progress in project execution of 4,800 MW of capacity expansion out of our targeted addition of 12,520 MW by 2030.

items.statement: Acquired Vidarbha Industries Power Ltd (600 MW); Mahan Phase-II 66% executed, Raipur Phase-II 25%, Raigarh Phase-II 20%; environmental clearance for Korba Phase-II (1,320 MW)
items.quote: We have also expanded our capacity further by acquiring Vidarbha Industries Power Ltd., which has 600 MW capacity that has been revived by us.

items.statement: Merchant realization Q1 FY26 Rs 6.51/kWh vs Rs 7.60/kWh in Q1 FY25; tariff realization lower due to lower import coal prices and lower short-term tariffs
items.quote: Our merchant realization for 1st Quarter was Rs.6.51 per kWh as against last year's same quarter, it was Rs.7.60.

items.statement: Fuel cost controlled at Rs 7,319 crore in Q1 FY26 vs Rs 8,074 crore in Q1 FY25; imported coal prices lower
items.quote: We were able to exert control over the cost of fuel at Rs.7,319 crores in Q1 FY26 as compared to Rs.8,074 crores in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Received over US $500 million from Bangladesh Power Development Board in June-July; customer now paying regularly; outstanding receivables near normal level
items.quote: Apart from this, we have also received more than US $500 million payment from the Bangladesh Power Development Board towards their outstanding dues in the end of June and in July. The customer has been paying us now regularly.

items.statement: FGD requirement dropped for plants under planning/execution where FGD not started; will continue FGD at Mahan and Raipur where in advanced stage; project cost will reduce
items.quote: After this notification has come , the power stations which are under planning and execution, where we have not started the execution of FGD, do not have a Adani Power Limited August 01, 2025 requirement of FGD now. So we will drop the FGD expenditure from those power plants

items.statement: Total debt Rs 44,372 crore as on 30 June 2025 vs Rs 38,775 crore on 31 March 2025; net debt Rs 37,437 crore vs Rs 31,023 crore; repaid Rs 2,579 crore UPS principal and Rs 1,146 crore distribution; UPS balance Rs 478 crore paid in July
items.quote: Total debt as on 30th June 2025 is Rs.44,372 crores as compared to Rs.38,775 crores as of 31st March '25. The liquidity of our operations remains high with robust cash accruals. As a result of this, net debt position is Rs.37,437 crores as compared to Rs.31,023 crores for the two quarter end.

items.statement: Took interim bridge funding from banks for interim capex requirements; internal accruals expected sufficient for FY26 capex
items.quote: Recently, we took some interim br idge funding from banks, that is only to meet the requirement for interim requirement capital expenditures.

items.statement: Amalgamation of Adani Power (Jharkhand) Limited completed; brings 1,600 MW Godda plant into APL standalone entity; implicit credit rating upgrade to AA Stable
items.quote: Another key development during the quarter was the amalgamation of Adani Power (Jharkhand) Limited. This brings the 1,600 MW God da plant into APL's standalone entity. This has led to an implicit credit rating upgrade of God da to AA Stable, reducing finance costs.

items.statement: Godda plant PLF 73% in Q1 FY26; merchant capacity provides market-linked upside
items.quote: During the quarter, the PLF for Godda was 73%.

items.statement: Dhirauli mine production expected to start by September or October 2025; on track per plan
items.quote: The production should start by September or October, somewhere. So, we are on time as per the plan which we gave earlier.

items.statement: Haryana Discom paying 50% of alternate coal compensation difference; discussions ongoing, expect resolution soon
items.quote: The discussion is still ongoing and for the time being Haryana is making payment of 50% of the difference of bills which we are raising. And therefore, we are also accounting for only 50% of the amounts , which is what we are getting.

items.statement: UPPCL PPA signed at capacity charge Rs 3.73 and total tariff Rs 5.39 per kWh for 1,500 MW net capacity
items.quote: We have signed the PPA with UPPCL where the capacity charge is 3.73 and the total tariff is 5.39.

items.statement: Weather-induced demand softness and high base affected Q1; early monsoon shifted demand impact from Q2 to Q1; expect Q2 demand and merchant rates to improve
items.quote: So, second quarter onwards the demand shoul d pick up and we feel that there should be a good demand and consequently the merchant rates.

items.statement: Lanco Amarkantak: minor ash disposal issue being addressed; Coastal Energen: one unit overhauled, second unit overhauling this month; Vidarbha: machines overhauled, normal availability expected
items.quote: With Lanco Amarkantak, we have very few challenges except a small issue related to ash disposal, which we are taking care of. The second is Coastal Energen. We have already done complete overhauling of one unit and after the complete overhauling, it is now at par with any other power station.

items.statement: Government target raised from 80 GW to 95 GW additional thermal capacity by 2032; financially strong private players ideally positioned to capitalize
items.quote: The Government has already given a target of 80 GW of additional thermal power capacity to meet this demand and now this target is being raised again to 95 GW in view of emerging trends.

items.statement: Sales volume supported by additional 2,300 MW capacity acquired last year and higher short-term sales under bilateral and exchange models
items.quote: While offtake under PPAs reduced due to weaker power demand in Quarter 1 of FY26, APL sales volume was supported by the additional 2,300 MW capacity acquired by us last year and higher short-term sales under bilateral and exchange models.

items.statement: Proven in-house project management capability and experienced team to monitor and execute projects efficiently
items.quote: We also have a proven in-house project management capability and an experienced team which will help us monitor and execute these projects efficiently.

items.statement: Regulatory receivables: no substantial pending claims except small frequent regulatory changes; nothing that can change revenue or profitability substantially
items.quote: There is hardly anything substantial pending now, except for small regulatory changes coming frequently, and therefore, we may be raising those issues or claims in regular course. But there is no claim now pending which can change the revenue or profitability substantially.

items.statement: Bangladesh Power Development Board paying regularly; over US $500 million received in June-July; outstanding receivables near normal
items.quote: As Khyalia ji has already said in his speech, w e have already received more than US $500 million payment from Bangladesh Power Development Board towards outstanding dues in June and July. The customer has been paying us regularly.

items.statement: All land required for expansion already acquired; self-funded, debt-light growth strategy
items.quote: As you would be aware, we already possess all the land required for expansion, which is a result of the foresight employed in identifying this opportunity in advance and acquiring the right resources at the right locations. We are funding these projects mostly from our own cash flows, which removes the reliance on project lenders.

items.statement: Management targets manufacturing EBITDA margin of INR7 per liter on average with reduced volatility going forward
items.quote: With these initiatives in place, we expect that margins will average at about INR7 per liter with reduced volatility.

items.statement: Multi-feed distillery project in Uttar Pradesh progressing as planned with commissioning expected in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our multi-feed distillery project in Uttar Pradesh is progressing as planned with commissioning expected in Q3 of this year.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 81% in Q1 FY26, expected to reach over 90% by end of FY26
items.quote: Capacity utilization was at 81%, and we hope to see improvements in capacity utilization in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Capacity utilization to reach well over 90% by end of FY26 after technology upgrade for corn oil production
items.quote: Certainly, by the end of the year, it will be well over 90%.

items.statement: Consumer business contributed 39% to total revenues with 14% YoY and 9% QoQ revenue growth in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The consumer business contributed 39% to total revenues and revenues in the segment grew by 14% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment achieved 50% YoY and 36% QoQ top-line growth in Q1 FY26, nearly breakeven
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that we have achieved a strong top-line growth of 50% year-on-year and 36% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Regular and others category saw 10% YoY and 5% QoQ growth in Q1 FY26 with EBITDA margin at 17%
items.quote: In the regular and others category, the segment saw almost 10% year-on-year growth and 5% quarter-on-quarter growth in Q1 FY'26. EBITDA margin in this category stood at 17% in line with the long-term average.

items.statement: Recorded 0.13 million cases in Uttar Pradesh in Q1 FY26 with strong growth potential in 10 million cases per month market
items.quote: In Q1 of F Y'26, we recorded 0.13 million cases in the state with strong potential for further growth

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA margin improved to INR6 per liter in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The quarter witnessed notable improvements in the manufacturing business as well with EBITDA margins improving to INR6 per liter.

items.statement: Regular and others segment EBITDA margin expected to sustain at 17% going forward
items.quote: The margin to expect for the next few years in the regular and other segment is going to be 17%.

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment aims to maintain breakeven zone in every quarter going forward
items.quote: Our intent is to be in the same zone where we are in Q1. That's the intention because we have set ourselves that we should -- fingers crossed, should be in the breakeven zone in every quarter as we have been.

items.statement: Received 4.35% price increase in Rajasthan and price revision in Uttar Pradesh effective April 1, 2025, both included in Q1 performance
items.quote: Additionally, we received a price increase of 4.35% in Rajasthan and a revision in Uttar Pradesh effective 1st April 2025, both of which are expected to support impr oved profitability and drive revenue growth

items.statement: No further price increases expected in balance period of FY26
items.quote: There are no further price increases expected in the balance period of the year.

items.statement: Secured 17-18% of annual maize demand through forward contracts at INR24-24.50 delivered, eliminating raw material margin volatility
items.quote: I believe the number is around 17%, 18% of our maize demand for the whole year, we've been able to fix in terms of fixed prices are. And as we go ahead into the future years, we hope to increase this number a little bit more.

items.statement: Prestige & Above growth driven by Mountain Oak, Snoski, Brothers & Company, and luxury brands DOAAB and Terai Gin family
items.quote: As of now, we -- apart from our luxury brands, which are DOAAB as well as the TERAI Gin family comprising of 2 variants Mountain Oak, Snoski, as well as Brothers & Company, all 3 are finding a very strong firm traction with the consumers.

items.statement: Consumer business present in 9 states, identified 3 new states for expansion, exploring duty-free and CSD channels
items.quote: The business is now present in 9 states, and we have also identified 3 new states with plans of expansion in the same as well are exploring the options to enter the duty-free channels as well as the CSD network.

items.statement: Luxury portfolio expanding to 3 additional states in FY26, mainstream also expanding with 1 of 3 states getting full portfolio
items.quote: In luxury, we currently plan to expand our portfolio to 3 additional states this year and are also eyeing duty-free as an opportunity.

items.statement: UP IMIL market has leading players Radico and IGL, but well-distributed among many participants; Globus aims to become formidable player
items.quote: Radico, IGL, they are among the leading players in the IMIL segment. And then there are many, as I said, stable but relatively smaller players. So it's a well-distributed market among many participants with these 2 still being leading the pack.

items.statement: Delhi policy review committed for September 2025; Bihar prohibition policy monitored but bottling not currently permitted
items.quote: Delhi was a bit of a surprise, in September, they have committed to relook at the policy.

items.statement: Reduced net debt net of acceptances by INR40 crores; net debt after cash and equivalents at INR334 crores as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: Net debt after cash and cash equivalents is INR334 crores.

items.statement: Manufacturing business expects average EBITDA of INR7 per liter going forward with reduced volatility
items.quote: From our entire manufacturing business, so not just ethanol, so average of ENA and ethanol, we expect an average margin of INR7 per liter going forward.

items.statement: Prestige & Above steady-state EBITDA margin expected to be 15-18% in line with peers like Diageo, Pernod, Radico
items.quote: I believe it's between 15% and 18%, right, for Diageo, Pernod, Radico.

items.statement: Ethanol business cannot insulate from policy reversal risk, but current policy environment stable for 2+ years with 20% blending target
items.quote: My sense is that for the current year as well as the next year, there is sufficient policy stability for us to say that margins are going to remain less volatile.

items.statement: Beer JV with ANSA McAL launched Carib 500ml strong beer in UP in Q1 FY26 with positive initial feedback; intends to build larger opportunity
items.quote: Globus ANSA India Limited, our joint venture partner with ANSA McAL, entered the beer market with the launch of Carib 500 ml strong beer in Uttar Pradesh in quarter 1. The initial feedback is positive.

items.statement: No capacity expansion capex planned after UP distillery; cash flows to be used for debt reduction unless inorganic opportunities arise
items.quote: Expansion, there is regular maintenance capex that takes place, but no capacity expansion kind of a capex.

items.statement: Phase-I of Pro-tech unit at Sanand, Gujarat completed with Rs.95 crores spent; commercial operations started 1st July 2025.
items.quote: We have spent Rs.95 crores Mallcom (India) Limited August 07, 2025 for Phase-I of the project and we expect a turnover of around Rs.10 to 15 crores from this unit in the current financial year

items.statement: Additional capex of up to Rs.10 crores planned in FY26 for importing more lines and machines at Sanand unit.
items.quote: For that, we have an additional CAPEX of up to Rs.10 crores this year, mainly towards importing more lines and machines.

items.statement: Second phase of Chandipur unit expansion largely complete; new safety shoes facility with 70,000 sq ft built-up area and Rs.25 crores capex now operational.
items.quote: The second phase of expansion of our Chandipur unit is largely complete. This phase involves setting up a new facility for designing and manufacturing of industrial safety shoes with a built-up area of almost 70,000 square feet and a CAPEX of Rs.25 crores.

items.statement: Expect Chandipur safety shoes unit to generate Rs.25-30 crores turnover in FY26.
items.quote: The unit is now operational and we expect it to generate a turnover of about Rs.25 crores to Rs.30 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Targeting 20%-25% growth rate for FY26 and FY27.
items.quote: So, going ahead, we would like to maintain similar or higher growth rate in the range of 20%-25%.

items.statement: Sanand unit targeted turnover of Rs.100 crores at full capacity by FY27.
items.quote: And once this setup is there, then we should be reaching targeted turnover of Rs.100 crores. So, at full capacity, not this year, next year, FY27, definitely we should have better turnover; if not, it is Rs.100 crores, near to Rs.100 crores, maybe around that figure only.

items.statement: Chandipur shoe unit projected Rs.50 crores turnover on full year basis.
items.quote: And the second phase, Ghatakpukur unit in West Bengal for shoe, we are projecting around Rs.50 crores turnover on full year basis from shoe unit.

items.statement: Existing facilities can achieve Rs.500-700 crores revenue with small additional capex.
items.quote: So, anything in the range of Rs.500 crores to Rs.700 crores we can do from the existing facility with some further small CAPEX that apart from this new setup which we have done.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be maintained around 14% range going forward.
items.quote: So, as we have been mentioning, the margin should be in the range of this 14% around this figure only.

items.statement: Domestic market growth driven by government safety policies, MNC requirements, and internal expansion into new product categories and distribution.
items.quote: So, there are some internal reasons and some external reasons. So, external reasons, there are a lot of tailwinds in this industry. You have more better policies from the government for occupational safety and health. You have companies who are becoming more stringent about their requirements. You have MNCs who are asking for such products.

items.statement: Sanand unit started commercial production 1st July 2025; current setup projects Rs.15 crores for H2 FY26, full capacity Rs.100 crores by FY27 after adding more machinery.
items.quote: We have done trial run. We have started commercial production. But again, we have to increase the machinery. So, that is why with the current setup, we have given this projection in the range of Rs.15 crores we will be doing during the next half year.

items.statement: Chandipur shoe unit operational with near 100% capacity utilization expected; Rs.25 crores projected for H2 FY26, Rs.50 crores full year.
items.quote: So, see this Ghatakpukur unit which we have set up in West Bengal, the capacity utilization here would be almost 100%. So, as I said that with this unit, we expect Rs.50 crores turnover. And so we have started with this now. So, current year projection is around Rs.25 crores for the next six months and on full year basis would be Rs.50 crores

items.statement: Established UAE office to strengthen presence in Middle East and Africa as high-potential branded export market.
items.quote: We have also established an office in the UAE to strengthen our presence in the Middle East and Africa region, which we see as a high-potential branded export market.

items.statement: Export order book typically maintained at 2.5-3.5 months; 60% contracted orders, 40% spot orders on average.
items.quote: Usually, we try to keep an order book of at least two-and-a-half to three-and-a-half months and we work on that basis.

items.statement: US tariffs impact all products but exposure limited; more exposed to Europe; awaiting potential trade deals.
items.quote: Tariffs into the US, as we all know, it is very fresh. So, even our products something that will be impacted. But we will have to wait and watch. Our exposure to the US is not as high as maybe some of our other competitors. We are more exposed in the European market than the American market.

items.statement: Added 8-10+ distributors in last two years across domestic and international markets; support includes marketing, credit, sales team visits, escalation matrix.
items.quote: I am sure we have added at least eight to ten or maybe more distributors in the last two years. So, for us, there might be -

items.statement: New domestic customers include first-time buyers, converters from unorganized products, and switchers from other brands; market expanding due to workforce growth and safety awareness.
items.quote: I would say all, both kinds. We have not done a deep dive analysis on this, but I would say all two kinds plus one in the sense there are new customers getting added.

items.statement: Domestic competitors: Bata, Liberty (shoes); Ansell (gloves); Karam (helmets). International competition largely from China, Pakistan, Vietnam; some categories price-sensitive.
items.quote: So, for example, for shoes, even Bata and Liberty are good competition. And, for gloves, there is Ansell also, for helmets, there is Karam. So, it depends on the product category. Internationally, a lot of competition comes from China, Pakistan, and other places also.

items.statement: Pricing competitive with branded peers in India; not competing with unorganized on price. Internationally competitive in some categories, but basic leather gloves and garments price-sensitive.
items.quote: In India, we are competitive when it comes to pricing with these kind of brands. And obviously, because a large portion of the market is still unorganized, so with that, we are not in that price range.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle increased to 150-170 days due to longer credit terms in new geographies (Americas) and higher raw material inventory for timely supply; targeting slight reduction but prioritizing growth.
items.quote: See, basically, it is a need of the industry. So, with the growth in turnover and going to the newer markets, like we started selling into South American countries or going to America also. So, Europe was always nearer and we used to have some maybe CAD or maybe shorter payment terms. But now with going to North, South American markets, they would like to pay only once the cargo reaches there.

items.statement: Sanand facility fully funded through internal accruals; no borrowings; fixed costs low, minor drag on profitability during ramp-up.
items.quote: But again, just to clarify that for Sanand definitely fully invested by us through internal accruals only, we have not borrowed anything. And the fixed cost there also is not very high; it would be not that big drag… minor only.

items.statement: ESG compliance becoming mandatory in Europe/Australia by FY29-30; Mallcom using renewable energy (solar, biomass), recycled materials, circular processes, and digital product passports.
items.quote: And this will become very much like a mandatory thing by maybe FY'29-30. And we are geared up for that, and as a company, as our values stand also, we want to head towards that direction, be it with the product, be it with the facility, be it even with packaging solutions or logistic solutions, we want to head in that direction.

items.statement: Received Silver Category Award from FIEO for FY2021 among 2-star export houses in Eastern Region.
items.quote: I am also happy to share that Mallcom received the Silver Category Award in the Eastern Region among 2-star export houses from FIEO for the Financial Year 2021.

items.statement: US tariffs temporary; limited exposure; other markets (UK FTA, Europe, domestic, Middle East) growing; double supply chain trend post-COVID supports resilience.
items.quote: I do not expect the entire business to get disrupted because of this. There might be some hindrances to it. But I think if we are able to stay in the business for long enough, we will be able to see positives from it. So, whatever the situation is, I think it is temporary and it does not change our growth plans.

items.statement: Target to open about 1,000 new showrooms in FY26; 392 signed and 234 operationalized in Q1 FY26
items.quote: To further capitalize on the brand strength of Kurlon and Sleepwell, we intend to open about 1,000 new showrooms in the current fiscal year. And let me share with you that in Q1 FY ‘26, we have already signed up for 392 new showrooms, out of which 234 are already operationalized.

items.statement: Expect 50% value growth in e-commerce channel in FY26
items.quote: This segment generated a revenue of Rs. 200 crores in FY ‘25 and we expect 50% value growth through this channel in FY ‘26.

items.statement: Target Rs. 100 crores plus revenue from Tarang and Aaram value-driven initiative in FY26
items.quote: We are confident of achieving revenues of Rs. 100 crores plus from this value-driven initiative in the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Furlenco targets Rs. 370 crores revenue in FY26 and Rs. 500-550 crores by FY27
items.quote: FY ‘26 our projection is Rs. 370 crores. We are well on track of that, whatever few months that have gone by. And we do not feel any big challenge towards achieving this goal, this should be on track.

items.statement: Furlenco to raise Rs. 100-125 crores equity to fuel expansion toward Rs. 500-550 crores revenue by FY27
items.quote: To further capitalize on consumer demand, Furlenco will raise around Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 125 crores of equity, which would fuel the expansion and would lead the road to levels of Rs. 500 crores to Rs. 550 crores of revenue by FY ‘27.

items.statement: Aim to grow top line at 15% annually for next three years to reach 14-15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Our intent is to take this growth to at least 15% and run that growth in the next three years. Our fixed cost increased by around 4%, 5%, 6%, this year of course we are not allowing it to increase because of the cost of the initiative. But those 15% growth could lead some portion to the bottom line, which together these two initiatives should take us to a profit margin, EBITDA margin of say around

items.statement: Core EBITDA margin improved to 11.7% in Q1 FY26 from 8.4% in Q1 FY25 for India business
items.quote: Core EBITDA margins also stood at 11.7% against 8.4% for the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 10.4% in Q1 FY26 from 7.4% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margins were reported at 10.4% against 7.4%.

items.statement: Gross margins now stand at 43.5%, almost 400 basis points above pre-acquisition level
items.quote: The various cost initiatives taken by us for integrating Kurlon into our business and increasing efficiencies of both Sleepwell and Kurlon combined a yielding positive results, which are reflected in our gross margins, which now stand at 43.5%, which is almost a 400 to 400 basis point above the pre-acquisition level.

items.statement: Kurlon integration savings of Rs. 190 crores run rate achieved; balanced Rs. 60 crores expected by end of FY26
items.quote: We are hopeful that the balanced savings of Rs.60 crores would also be realized by the end of FY ‘26.

items.statement: Tarang and Aaram products enjoy same or better EBITDA margins than other products on average
items.quote: Tarang and Aaram currently enjoys the same or better level of EBITDA margins than our other products on an average combined.

items.statement: Mattress volumes grew 10% YoY in Q1 FY26; Sleepwell 22%, Kurlon 6%
items.quote: Our mattress volumes in Q1 FY ‘26 grew by 10% year -on-year. While Sleepwell registered a growth of 22%, Kurlon registered a growth of 6%.

items.statement: Tarang and Aaram volume growth around 60% YoY, achieving Rs. 80 crores annual run rate
items.quote: This segment is showing positive results as demonstrated by a volume growth of around 60% year -on-year, thereby achieving an annual run rate of Rs. 80 crores per annum.

items.statement: E-commerce registered 66% value growth YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: E-commerce continues to be another strong growth-oriented value driver segment. It registered a value growth of 66% year -on-year on marketplaces and on our own websites.

items.statement: B2B foam segments saw high single-digit volume growth in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY ‘26, we have seen high single -digit growth in terms of volume in these segments.

items.statement: No fresh capex expected before 2029-2030; only maintenance capex needed
items.quote: Capacity utilization in terms of, let us say, okay brownfield we might need a bit of maintenance CAPEX every year, but any fresh CAPEX we do not see anything before 2029, 2030.

items.statement: Reduced total facilities from 21 to 12 post-Kurlon integration; divided country into five zones with combined foam and mattress capabilities
items.quote: Optimizing the operating facilities of both the companies, resulting in reduction of total number of facilities from 21 to 12.

items.statement: Raw material prices dropped: TDI from Rs. 196 to Rs. 117 per kg, polyol from Rs. 117 to Rs. 110 per kg between Q4 and Q1
items.value: TDI from Rs. 196 to Rs. 117 per kg, polyol from Rs. 117 to Rs. 110 per kg
items.quote: Raw material prices dropped from Rs.196 per kg for TDI between Q4 and Q1, and polyol prices from Rs.117 to Rs.110 per kg for the similar period.

items.statement: Foam segment value growth subdued due to raw material price reductions passed on to customers
items.quote: Value growth conversions were little subdued, primarily because of reduction in raw material prices.

items.statement: Launched new sub-Rs. 10,000 mattress models for Sleepwell and Kurlon to address Rs. 12,500 crore market
items.quote: To address the rising consumer demand in the sub -Rs. 10,000 category, whose market is estimated at around Rs. 12,500 crores, we have launched new mattress models for both Sleepwell and Kurlon.

items.statement: Tarang and Aaram sold through 7,000+ dealers in 4,500 towns; separate rural distribution model independent of mainline network
items.quote: For our small-town initiatives, both Sleepwell Tarang and Kurlon Aaram are being aggressively marketed and now have presence across 7,000 plus dealers in 4,500 towns.

items.statement: Organized distributors' meet in Delhi and 33 dealer meets at 11 locations in Q1 FY26 to strengthen channel relationships
items.quote: In Q1 FY ‘26, we organized a distributors’ meet in Delhi and facilitated 33 dealer meets at 11 different locations across India.

items.statement: Focus on profitable growth; competition raising money grows the market; no need for bizarre actions
items.quote: My belief is that at the moment there is enough market which is available and we can, in spite of whatever activities that are happening, I think that is doing well for this segment for us to continue with spreading our distribution with our retail showrooms and the growth will happen with profitability.

items.statement: Dubai operations growing: 6 EBOs and 7 MBOs; piloting retail formats in GCC; higher gross margins than India
items.quote: Today, we have six exclusive brand outlets and seven multi-brand outlets.

items.statement: No plans to scale down Australia and Spain; contribution reducing naturally as India grows faster
items.quote: So, there is no plans to scale down the businesses there, but just as a natural outcome of our focus, the percentage contribution of Spain and Australia to our overall kitty is a reducing number.

items.statement: Net debt Rs. 700-800 crores at group level; target to reduce by Rs. 300-350 crores via PAT generation and asset monetization
items.quote: Currently if you see, I have a net debt of around Rs. 700 crores to Rs. 800 crores at a group level. If this goes down by Rs. 300 crores, Rs. 350 crores, we would be sitting somewhere around Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 400 crores on a net debt level.

items.statement: No immediate plan to acquire Furlenco; will evaluate IPO or acquisition by end of FY27
items.quote: And at the moment, there is no desire right away to acquire the company. We will let it grow, let it go on as it is at a good high growth level. And at the end of maybe FY ‘27 take a call as to what we want to do, whether it will go through an IPO process or it will go through an acquisition process or whatever.

items.statement: Furlenco subscriber base grew 60% in FY25 (40,000 new subscribers); now operates in 29 cities
items.quote: More than 40,000 new customers got onboarded, resulting in a 60% increase in subscriber base. Furlenco now operates in 29 cities across India.

items.statement: Furlenco achieved Rs. 4 crores PAT in Q1 FY26, exceeding full-year FY25 profitability
items.quote: Another key milestone is that Furlenco registered Rs. 4 crores as PAT achieved in Q1 of this year, which is more than the full -year profitability achieved in FY ‘25.

items.statement: E-commerce growth above 50-60% not sustainable due to logistics, size constraints, marketplace system requirements
items.quote: Therefore, I think if we try and go beyond 50% or 60%, it will not be a sustainable growth. It will go through the hiccups. It will go through the little ups and downs, because one thing or the other would start becoming a constraint.

items.statement: Unusual rains and no heat waves in core markets caused seasonal cooling demand to plummet; OEMs reported 15-30% decline in primary sales
items.quote: This quarter, witnessed one of the most unusual summers in entire history of 26 years of Aditya Vision with unusual rains continuing throughout Q1 with no heat waves in our core markets of Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh.

items.statement: Revenue grew 6% YoY to INR940 crores despite adverse weather; EBITDA margin maintained at 9.5%; PAT grew 4% to INR55 crores
items.quote: However, even under these circumstances and challenges beyond our or anyone's control, I'm happy to inform our shareholders that our revenue grew 6% year-on-year over a strong Q1 FY '25 base to INR940 crores, highlighting our strength of execution and adaptability to adverse situations.

items.statement: Gross margin improved from 15.22% to 15.33% YoY; EBITDA margin maintained at 9.5% despite elevated fixed costs from 29 new stores
items.quote: Despite elevated fixed costs associated with the 29 new stores launched in trailing 12 months, which are expected to normalize as they mature, I'm really happy to report that we have maintained EBITDA margins at 9.5% and our profit after tax grew by 4% to INR55 crores compared to INR53 crores Y -o-Y.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by INR150 crores in Q1 FY26 vs March 2025; short-term borrowings declined sharply from INR278 crores to ~INR115 crores
items.quote: This agile approach helped reduce our inventory levels by INR150 crores in Q1 FY '26 compared to March '25. And your company remains comfortable on stocks of AC, which has now come to company's historically normal levels.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings fell from INR278 crores in March 2025 to ~INR115 crores as of June 30, 2025; cash and cash equivalents at INR141 crores
items.quote: Due to effective inventory liquidation, robust receivable management and disciplined procurement , t he short -term borrowings declined sharply from INR278 crores in March '25 to approximately INR115 crores as of June 30, '25.

items.statement: Opened 4 new stores in Q1 FY26 and 3 more in July 2025; store count at 182 as of date; on track to add 25-30 stores in FY26 targeting 200+ stores by year-end
items.quote: We opened 4 new stores during Q1, consistent with our strategic quarterly pace. I'm pleased to share that we have added 3 more stores in July '25, taking our store count to 182 a s on date. We remain on track to add 25 to 30 new stores in FY '26, aiming to cross the 200 -plus store milestone by year -end.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth was -4% in Q1 FY26 vs +21% in Q1 FY25; AC contributed ~42% of revenue with only 2% degrowth
items.quote: Same -store sales growth for Q1 FY '26 stood at minus 4%.

items.statement: Optimistic on festive season demand due to good monsoon, bumper crop expectations, Bihar's 125 units free electricity scheme, and Union Budget tax relief
items.quote: I think that bumper harvesting will be there in entire geography where we are operating. So I think given that Q1 was not that good, so people will be having so much of disposable income with them. And I think festive season should go realbonuly well.

items.statement: Bihar launched 125 units free electricity scheme effective July 2025, expected to boost consumer durable demand and disposable income
items.quote: In Bihar, as I speak, effective today, the 125 units free electricity scheme has been launched by the government, which will boost consumer durable and electronic demand and support overall consumption.

items.statement: No formal top-line guidance given for FY26; management believes growth can be better than last year but refrains from specific numbers
items.quote: I don't think any guidance can be given on the top line as of now.

items.statement: Minimum 25 stores per year guidance maintained; management confident of adding even more stores given good response in new areas
items.quote: We are quite confident of adding 25, 30 stores, but we are -- in fact, we want to add even more stores because we are getting very good responses in new areas. But these are -- as always, we have guided conservatively, and we always say that it was there in the investor presentation also that we'll be adding minimum 25 stores every year.

items.statement: Historical sales growth guidance of 20-25% maintained; team remains confident of achieving despite Q1 weather impact
items.quote: But we have always been guiding about 20%, 25% of the growth in sales, which even now our team remains confident of achieving.

items.statement: Focus remains on Uttar Pradesh expansion; not currently focusing on other states; Chhattisgarh entry possible by Q4 FY26
items.quote: No, no. We are expanding. Right now, we are -- our focus is Uttar Pradesh,and we are not right now focusing any other state.

items.statement: AC contributed ~42% of Q1 revenue; historically AC represents ~65% of full-year AC volumes in Q1
items.quote: You are aware that in Q1, this is the summer season and AC contributes higher. So our contribution for AC in '26 was around 42% of our entire revenue.

items.statement: No discounting used to liquidate AC inventory; OEMs provided substantial support including free installations; margins not impacted by discounting
items.quote: But I think I never -- Madhu, I never said that we've resorted to discounting. I do not know where you have got this word from. But we never resorted this to any discounting. We -- in fact, we took all the support from OEMs like, as you know, how they support, they give free installations and they give various other facilities to the customers, so these are the things.

items.statement: UP has surpassed Jharkhand as percentage of sales; Central UP presence deepened; Western UP expansion planned
items.quote: So you must have seen from the investor presentation that we have already -- UP has surpassed Jharkhand as a percentage of sales coming to Aditya Vision. So of course, this corroborates our statement that UP is doing very well.

items.statement: BEE norms change for ACs effective January 2026; management not concerned as retailers can sell existing stock, only OEMs cannot manufacture non-compliant units
items.quote: As per our strategy, we -- in fact, from mid -May, we started destocking. And right now, again, what you said that whatever stock left, your question number second is that B EE will be applicable from January next year. So actually, we are not barred from selling whatever we will be carrying at that period.

items.statement: Inventory at ~INR548 crores as of June 2025 vs ~INR380 crores in June 2024; increase attributed to 29 new stores in trailing 12 months and ongoing AC season
items.quote: I may not be able to tell you about last year's inventory level. But what I remember, it must be around, it must be around INR380-odd crores. And in this year, it will be, if you subtract INR698 crores and minus INR150 crores. So it will be around INR548 crores.

items.statement: Cost control measures (reduced advertising, promotions, warehousing, freight, security, employee bonuses) sustained EBITDA margin; expenses will rise when growth returns
items.quote: So we try to keep it as minimum as possible. As you know, if sale is not there, so there are so many bonuses and incentives, these are also not there for employees. So that has also cut down on our expenses.

items.statement: AC sales degrowth only 2% in Q1 despite bad summer; other categories compensated; AC sells year-round with peak in Q1 and gradual decline through July-September
items.quote: No, no, AC has not fallen as such. I told you AC contributed around 42% of our entire turnover, and there was a degrowth of only 2%.

items.statement: Q2-Q4 expected to perform better than last year due to 45 new branches added; AC less dominant in remaining quarters
items.quote: But we are quite confident that with added branches network of around new 45 branches, we'll be able to do much better than what growth we have got in last year's Q2, Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: UP margins similar to Bihar and Jharkhand; no extra discounts or offers in UP impacting margins; margin comes in basket across geographies
items.quote: Not at all, Yash, not at all. It is a basket. The margin comes in basket and UP behaves similarly as Jharkhand or similarly, almost similarly as Bihar.

items.statement: AC volume seasonality: ~65% of full-year AC volumes typically sold in Q1
items.quote: Entire AC, it will be around 65%.

items.quote: it does not look like we will hit operational breakeven this year. And that has been predominantly based on our volumes not getting to the estimate s that we thought that we could basically

items.quote: double digit growth, we are confident. And if exports bec omes a little bit of headwind, we have to devise a strategy how to mitigate

items.quote: In terms of the volume growth, engineering division is around 10%. And in the metal formed division, it is about 3% to 4%.

items.quote: In terms of your query, this financial year the volume is targeted and definitely will be higher as compared to the previous year.

items.quote: This year particularly, we will be completing the sample approval and maybe how to sort out logistics because ultimately supplies are going to be in Latur and next year onwards we will see volumes ramping up for railway division.

items.quote: The steel price increase is already factored in the financials, but recovery from the customers is yet to happen, which will be happening in current quarter and the next quarter. So after that, margins will look like what we used to maintain earlier.

items.statement: If lithium-ion prices rise, entire industry will increase prices as it is the largest cost component
items.quote: If lithium -ion starts moving up, everybody will increa se prices, because it is the largest component of everybody's cost structure

items.quote: The first w as after the 55 Ton tractor trailer. We have now got a, that was a 6x4, and then now we have got a 55 4x2, and then the next will be a tipper product

items.quote: by the end of this year definitely we should have battery swapping available on the truck and I think that tha t is the solution that will then allow for fleets to also start using

items.quote: We are very, very confident that in Q2 we will be, applying for the eligibility of the same. And I think by the time we meet for the next investor call, our application would be underway for the qualification under PM e-drive.

items.statement: Government tightening e-rickshaw safety norms; seen as differentiator for organized players
items.quote: Increasingly government is also making the regulations stringent when it comes to that particular product category in terms of safety and some of the other norms where we feel could be, a differentiator between an organized player versus players like us and some of the other competition.

items.statement: Q1 FY2026 EV volumes: 45 e-trucks, 1,668 three-wheelers, 44 SCVs, 34 e-tractors (total 1,791)

items.quote: As far as the semi-commercial plant is concerned, at this juncture, are doing validation batches for the first DMF, which is likely to come up the next two quarters.

items.quote: I do not think that the group has ever taken an action that affects one group of shareholders negatively. It is not in kind of our ethos or the way we work with things at all. items.quote: so first off I am say ing, the first focus is to ensure that we are successful in these three areas. items.quote: As on date, our order book stood at Rs. 3,051 crores, up by 152.15% year -on-year.

items.statement: Bid pipeline around Rs 700 crore
items.quote: It's close to around INR700-odd crores.

items.quote: Largely, we believe that it should improve our operating cost by -- at least by 1.5% to 2% from next financial year.

items.quote: We have recently been awarded with 2 new rig contracts, and we are adding 2 new rigs in our fleet. So going forward as well, as and when opportunity comes, we'll add new equipment in our fleet.

items.statement: Workover rigs and drilling rigs 100% utilized

items.quote: So with regards to t he demand in the industry pertaining to our kind of services are excellent. And we are anticipating good amount of growth going forward with increasing in demand. So we believe this momentum should continue at least for next 3 years.

items.quote: So that contract will start contributing later on this financial year. So for this financial year, we are expectin g around 5 to 6 months kind of revenue from that particular contract. Full year revenue we can expect from next financial year.

items.quote: Yes. So we have six drilling rigs. So drilling rigs are getting dollar rates. I think five of them are into dollar contracts and rest all other rigs are into rupee contracts.

items.quote: We have given loans to Prabha Energy, which were given in past. They are still standing there and they carry rate of interest of 12%.

items.quote: So we are just reviewing it. And if we'll find it the correct time, we can think of it. So all approvals are in place. So we'll just have to time it.

items.statement: Pursuing selective value-accretive M&A to broaden service capabilities
items.quote: Our strategic priorities for the remainder of FY '26 are clearly defined. items.quote: This was primarily driven by our non-GPL business, which grew 14.5% Y-o-Y and 4.1% Q-o-Q, supported by successful new launches. However, this growth was offset by a 22% Y-o-Y decline in our GPL business owing to inventory rationalization by GPL.

items.quote: So, we should see commercial activity on our onco pipeline, on our high-potent pipeline from late FY '27, okay, as the patents in some early markets start expiring.

items.quote: I'm happy to inform that we have generated strong cash flow from operations of INR100 crores in Q1 FY '26 with cash and cash equivalent of INR660 crores on the books as of 30 June 2025.

items.quote: Additionally, recent U.S. tariff adjustments shall have a similar impact on competition. Hence, Tega shall remain and maintain its competitive edge in U.S.
