items.quote: We have roughly the combination of spares and equipment is about 45, 55 and in the last quarter, the spares part has been about 30 to 35 range. And however, this is just a quarter effect.

items.statement: Investing in capacity and talent in Chile operations to support long-term growth
items.quote: Our Chile operations are scaling well, and we are actively investing in capacity and talent to support long-term growth.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue guidance INR660 cr, EBITDA INR242 cr, PBT INR100 cr, PAT INR80-85 cr
items.value: Revenue INR660 cr, EBITDA INR242 cr, PBT INR100 cr, PAT INR80-85 cr
items.quote: And the projected guidance for FY '23 revenue of INR660 crores across commerce and non-commerce with the EBITDA target of -- reported EBITDA of INR242 crores around that much and PBT of INR100 crores and PAT of INR80 crores to INR85 crores.

items.statement: Commerce vertical FY26 guidance: revenue INR340 cr, EBITDA INR170 cr, PAT INR70 cr
items.value: Revenue INR340 cr, EBITDA INR170 cr, PAT INR70 cr
items.quote: In the major numbers, commerce is a major contributor for the guidance with INR340 crores on the top line and the EBITDA of INR170 crores and the PAT of INR70 crores in the numbers projected for the guidance.

items.statement: Non-commerce vertical FY26 EBITDA expected over INR60 cr; debt-to-EBITDA ~3x FY26, <2x by FY27
items.quote: So the non-commerce space is expected to deliver an EBITDA of over INR60 crores for FY '26. So from a debt to overall EBITDA perspective, we are sort of there at about 3, 3.2x.

items.statement: Total debt reduced from INR510 cr to INR195 cr post QIP; plan to repay remaining via operational accruals, no new debt
items.quote: Coming to balance sheet, we had a INR510 crores debt as on March '25, we are able to -- by raising QIP funds of INR357 crores. Now we carry a debt of INR195 crores, which we are planning to repay through our operational accruals and no additional debt will be planned as such.

items.statement: Interest cost for FY26 projected at INR18 cr for full year on remaining debt
items.quote: So the balance debt for the finance cost for the next 3 quarters will be INR18 crores.

items.statement: Ascertis debt at 17.2% coupon to be refinanced by March 2026 to single-digit or low double-digit rate using owned land/building assets worth ~INR100 cr
items.quote: The balance debt of about INR120 crores, apart from the INR70 crores of promoter debt, which is the total INR190 crores, the INR120 crores is currently running at an interest coupon of just over 17%.

items.statement: Completed INR357 cr QIP, bringing marquee institutional investors and strengthening balance sheet
items.quote: We have successfully completed 2 landmark strategic milestones, the INR357 crores maiden QIP, which helped us bring in marquee institutional investors and at the same time, significantly strengthened our balance sheet.

items.statement: Demerger of commerce vertical into JK Shah Commerce Education Limited; scheme filing by early September, listing expected in 8 months (Mar-May 2026)
items.quote: We'll be filing the scheme by September 1 week and expected to complete it by -- 8 months is the projected time line given by our advisers, which means by March, April 1 or May, we should be able to list the company on the NSE and BSE.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated EBITDA nearly doubled YoY to INR55 cr; net profit INR6 cr up 123% YoY
items.value: EBITDA INR55 cr, PAT INR6 cr
items.quote: Consolidated revenue grew 17% year-on-year to INR139 crores, driven by broad-based growth across the segments. EBITDA nearly doubled year-on-year to INR55 crores and we continue our profitable trajectory with a net profit of INR6 crores, up 123% year-on-year.

items.statement: Commerce vertical FY26 projected EBITDA >INR140 cr, potential INR500 cr by FY30
items.quote: expected not only to grow its margins going forward significantly from potentially an EBITDA of INR140 crores to a possible INR500 crores of EBITDA by FY '30 under the leadership of Pr ofessor JK Shah

items.statement: Academic vertical: 6 operational schools at >85% occupancy; plan to add 5-6 schools in asset-light model this FY, results visible next academic year
items.quote: As far as the existing schools are concerned -- CBSE and the international schools are concerned, we current ly are running at an occupancy of over 85% because these are schools that we have acquired close to 2 years ago

items.statement: Government test prep seeing resurgence due to AI-driven job uncertainty; Q2 strong on Tamil Nadu notification; new Karnataka market showing green shoots
items.quote: Off late, what we have seen possibly in the last 4 to 6 weeks is with the changes a nd the unease that AI and AI-related software is creating in the market, especially in the upskilling space, people are starting to look at the government job as fairly more

items.statement: Vocational: shifting to higher ARPU courses (AI/ML, DevOps, online degrees/certifications); 25+ enterprise accounts (Deloitte, PwC); 150+ placements in Q1
items.quote: Apart from our very strong B2C business, we had 25-plus active enterprise accounts, including top names like Deloitte and PwC. And not only that, these are very strongly outcome-focused programs, and we have delivered more than 150 placements in this quarter alone.

items.statement: Vocational restructuring: combining sales/marketing/ops teams, moving from low ARPU to mid/high ARPU courses; unrecognized revenue from long-duration programs to boost future EBITDA
items.quote: We have rejigged the product and courses portfolio and moving from a low -- very low high ARPU courses to a middle and a significantly higher ARPU courses, which will result in a significant profitability.

items.statement: Commerce: strong traction in global certifications (ACCA, CFA, CMA) rolling out nationally; BB Virtual online courses seeing significant traction
items.quote: We are seeing a significantly higher traction in global certifications like ACCA, CFA, CMA, etcetera, across the country. We had started and piloted that in a couple of regions. Now as we roll it out nationally, that's seen a significant traction.

items.statement: Vocational revenue split: ~85% B2C / 15% pure corporate; including institutional (colleges) ~60% B2C / 40% institutional & corporate
items.quote: So the enterprise as of now in the old vocational segment would be about if we count enterprises pure corporate because this phase also works with colleges, which is institutional business or semi corporate, we can ca ll it. So if we keep institutional business out, it will be about 85-15. But if we include institutional business, it will be almost about 60-40, 60% as B2C and 40% as institutional

items.statement: July collections INR65 cr (INR40 cr non-commerce, INR25 cr commerce) without GST
items.quote: So we are able to -- so collected INR65 crores in the current July, where the INR45 crores came from the non-commerce segment, INR40 crores and INR25 crores came from the non-commerce, this is without GST.

items.statement: Faculty retention de-risked: brands (JK Shah, Race, Edureka) are the draw, not star faculty; long-term contracts, industry-best compensation, stock options for faculty
items.quote: In all our businesses, the faculty is the institution, whether it is JK Shah Classes in commerce or Race in government test prep or for that matter, Edureka in software. It is the institution, our pedagogy, our methodology, our content, which is really the star.

items.statement: ROCE currently 13%, targeting 35% by FY30
items.quote: ROCEs currently stands at 13% for the full segment and is expected to grow to 35% in the FY '30 as we progress.

items.statement: Higher education business had negative EBITDA due to upfront CAC vs multi-year revenue recognition; now maturing to EBITDA positive, cash flow positive since last year
items.quote: The customer acquisition cost is upfront and it is charged to our P&L in the quarter in which the student is onboarded, whereas the revenue gets recognized over 1 or 2 years. So that caused a certain disparity and hence, had a negative EBITDA margin from our higher ed business.

items.statement: Content creation cost for government test prep expansion (Karnataka) negligible, 20-25% state-specific, AI tools making translation fast and cheap; all expensed to P&L
items.quote: The type of monies that we spend on capex for content in the government test prep space is almost negligible and all of it is charged to our P&L. There is no capitalization of content that we do in the government test prep space.

items.statement: Veranda 2.0 strategy: unbundling 4 pillars (Academic, Govt Test Prep, Vocational, Commerce) with independent capital access, no further dilution or leverage, focus on profitable growth and FCF
items.quote: The central idea behind Veranda 2.0 is simply unbundling, creating focused verticals, giving them independent strategies and capital access and unlocking significant synergies across the platform without any operational overlap.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue grew 7% QoQ to INR120 crores driven by Product Display, Energy Solutions and other segments offsetting ODM home lighting softness
items.quote: In Q1 FY 26, continue to diversify our business mix without impacting overall revenue achieving a healthy 7% quarter-on-quarter growth to INR120 crores.

items.statement: Non-ODM home lighting segments grew 35% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR81 crores, now 68% of revenue vs 32% for ODM home lighting
items.quote: Reveres from other business segments grew 35% year-over-year and 10% on quarter-on-quarter to INRS1 crores, now contributing 68% of the overall top line.

items.statement: Single customer ODM home lighting reliance reduced from 52% in Q1 FY25 to 32% in Q1 FY26; second largest customer ~2-2.5%
items.quote: As a result, our reliance on a single customer ODM Home Lighting segment has been significantly reduced from 52% in Q1 FY 25 to 32% in Q1 FY 26.

items.statement: International revenue rose to INR30 crores, up 3% YoY and 84% QoQ, contributing 25% of Q1 FY26 revenue
items.quote: Overall, revenue from outside India rose to INR30 crores marking a growth of 3% year-on-year and 84% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 83% QoQ to INR11 crores; PAT improved to INR2 crores from loss of INR1 crore; cash PAT up 74% QoQ to INR9 crores
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR11 crores, reflccting a robust quarter-on-quarter growth of 83%.

items.statement: IPO proceeds: debt repayment completed, Block 1 operational, Block 2 civil construction nearing completion, ~75% deployed, rest within timeline
items.quote: For Block 2, civil construction is nearing completion. We have now deployed around 75% of the IPO fimd and are on course to complete the deploying of -- to complete deploying the rest within the time line we set for ourselves.

items.statement: Management will provide revenue and margin guidance by next quarter or Q3 FY26; sticking to prior year guidance for now
items.quote: Ithink Nileshii, guidance, we will be able to provide probably some idea in the next quarter. We are just going through the process because a lot of initiatives arc new as of now.

items.statement: Margin pressure temporary due to lower volumes in new verticals and onboarding costs; expect gross margins to return to historical levels as volumes scale
items.quote: However, as volumes ramp up and we achicve scalcs in these scgments, we expect gross margins to gradually return to their historical levels.

items.statement: Signify JV with Dixon opened doors to work with other brands; products approved and trial orders started with multiple new customers
items.quote: And we are also looking at this association very closely. But if you look at the silver lining of the entire procedure, whatever has happened, so that has actually opened the doors for us as well.

items.statement: Hearable/wearable segment launched <1 year ago now profitable; manufacturing actual products in India not just assembling; targeting double-digit revenue this quarter
items.quote: And in fact, we are now getting ready for a sustainable growth in the future with reliance on a single customer on a single product type or a single vertical is gradually coming down.

items.statement: Product Display segment in Middle East started <1 year ago now profitable and doing substantial business; all ODM products designed, developed, manufactured in-house
items.quote: Similarly to that, even if I talk of the export business that we are doing. So again, one more vertical which we started less than a year back, which was the Product Display segment in the Middle East, so within 1 year, again, that has become profitable.

items.statement: Automotive segment (lighting, electronics, building safety systems with Honeywell) certifications and sample approvals done; orders started; promising news by Q2/Q3 FY26
items.quote: And now going forward, in fact, automotive is going to be one more segment. So I think by the next quarter, this quarter 2 or quarter 3, well definitely give you some very promising news when it comes to the automotive segment.

items.statement: US revenue ~60-65% of international (INR18-20 crores), Middle East ~30-35%; US subsidiary opened last year, UAE new market
items.quote: So just to give you an idea, it was close to around -- in percentage terms, T can say U.S.A. was around maybe 60%, 65% and remaining was from the Middle East.

items.statement: US competitiveness vs China: not product-to-product but solution-based (RV lighting, solar, charge controllers, batteries); China labor costs rising; designs and manufacturing in-house
items.quote: So before Hardeep, sir, answers this question. Just one thing I want to add to this is that we are not competing on a product-to-product level when it comes to what we are doing in the U.S. It's more of -- some part of it is definitely product, but it more like a solution that we work on.

items.statement: Target ROCE ~30-32% (historical) by end of next financial year (FY27); current ROCE not disclosed; fixed asset turnover historically 5-5.5x
items.quote: But to reach to that level once again, I mean, we believe that the way we arc working by the end of next financial year, we should be closer to that or comparable to that value, I think, by the end of the next financial year.

items.statement: CFO resigned; Sanjeet Singh (CEO) interim CFO for 2-3 quarters while searching for dedicated CFO; committed to strong governance
items.quote: So we are actively working to identify a suitable replacement over the next 2 to 3 quarters because this is a very important position in the company.

items.statement: US tariff impact uncertain; waiting for situation to settle; believe tariffs on Indian goods will remain lower than on Chinese products
items.quote: So I think we are just waiting for things to settle down so that we can make sense of what is happening around us.

items.statement: New plant revenue expected to kick in within couple of quarters, substantially improving top and bottom line
items.quote: So I think its just a matter of another couple of quarters where the new plant revenue from the new plant will also start kicking in and will substantially improve the top and the bottom line going forward.

items.statement: Hearable/wearable margins to improve with volume as fixed costs absorbed; working with all top brands; adding more space for this vertical
items.quote: So basically, in the hearable, wearables segment, definitely, like you said, the higher the volume, the better the margins become because in order to run the show, your fixed cost will remain the same.

items.statement: Long-term target: EBITDA to reach INR200 crore level (FY20 sales); transition phase ongoing; expect visibility by Q3 FY26
items.quote: So basically, I mean, what you said is correct, that is what the target is. And moving forward, we are just waiting for all these new relationships to come out to that level where the revenues from each one new product category or account becomes substantial.

items.statement: Revenue expected to be flattish or very small single-digit growth for FY26
items.value: flattish or very small single-digit growth
items.quote: We realigned that to being flattish or very small single-digit growth for this year.

items.statement: Advertising and marketing spend to increase to 6-7% in FY26 and 8-10% in FY27
items.quote: We expect our advertising and marketing spend to increase to 6% to 7% in FY '26 and go up to 8% to 10% in FY '27.

items.statement: Benefits of brand investments expected to materialize from FY28 onwards
items.quote: We anticipate the benefits of these efforts to begin materializing from FY '28 onwards, by which time the advertising and marketing spend s are expected to stabilize.

items.statement: New premium store capex estimated at INR32-35 lakhs per store, ~30% higher than previous INR25 lakhs
items.quote: Earlier, our capex cost was around INR25 lakhs. So this is roughly expected to be in the range of INR32 lakhs to INR35 lakhs.

items.statement: Capex for store transformation to be funded from internal accruals, no debt raise needed
items.quote: We don't need to require any -- raise any debt. We will be able to do it from our internal accruals.

items.statement: Plan to open 20-odd premium stores in FY26, close similar number of underperforming stores, net store count flattish
items.quote: Currently, we have about 20-odd stores in the pipeline to open in this year and similar number to even close.

items.statement: Plan to renovate 15-20 existing stores in FY26, mainly in March
items.quote: Roughly 15 to 20 stores also, we will end up renovating.

items.statement: Store count expected to remain flattish for FY26 and FY27, focus on improving productivity per store
items.quote: We expect the store count to remain flattish this year and probably even the next year. However, having said that, when we see the market opening up and wherever we see opportunities, certainly, we will increase them.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 290 bps YoY to 61.6% in Q1 FY26, but expected to normalize to 56-57% by year-end
items.quote: Gross profit stood at INR 73.8 crores with a GP margin of 61.6% for the quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to take a hit in FY26 and FY27 due to higher rental and marketing costs
items.quote: Yes, certainly, because of the increase in rental cost and increase in the marketing spend fo r these next couple of years, certainly, there will be a hit in our margins

items.statement: Q1 revenue steady at ~INR120 crores, reflecting soft discretionary spending in Tier 2/3 markets
items.quote: During this quarter, revenues remained steady at approximatel y INR120 crores, reflecting the continued softness in discretionary spending, particularly across Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets, where consumer sentiment remains muted.

items.statement: No demand recovery seen; Q2 expected to be flattish like last year
items.quote: In fact, we don't see a demand recovery. It's not been a good season. In fact, we also see Q2 to be flattish more in like last year, it's not been a good season.

items.statement: Fashion-forward brands hit harder than basic brands this season
items.quote: So what we feel in hindsight, Apurva, is a little bit that the fashion brands during this season have been hit a little more than the basic ones.

items.statement: Sharpened fashion sensitivity with trend-sensitive seasonal collections, contemporary silhouettes, expressive colors, elevated fabrics
items.quote: We continue to introduce trend-sensitive product str ategy, featuring seasonal collections with contemporary silhouettes, expressive color palettes and elevated fabric choices targeted to enhance Mufti's appeal among style-conscious consumers and reinforce its positioning in the premium menswear segment.

items.statement: Digital sales through own website more than doubled YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: With hyper -targeted campaigns and rising consumer engagement, digital sales through Mufti's website have more than doubled over year-on-year, underlining the impact of these initiatives.

items.statement: Online mix expected at 11-13% for FY26, higher in FY27 but no fixed target
items.quote: However, overall, we expect it to be in 11%, 12%, 13% for this year, and we expect it to rise higher in the forthcoming year.

items.statement: Not losing market share in Tier 3 to value retailers; markets not conducive for mid-premium brands
items.quote: No, we are not losing market share in Tier 3. Some of these markets are not behaving as though they are conducive for mid-premium to premium brands.

items.statement: Product pricing to remain same despite premium store locations; only rental costs higher
items.quote: We are not going to change our prices. At the same price points, we are going to premiumize the brand experience and premiumize the brand perception because that's where we want to see the inflection happen at these price points.

items.statement: Higher Q1 gross margin due to delayed discounting by 2 weeks amid low footfalls
items.quote: This year, looking at the market conditions and how the market was going, there were -- footfalls were very low in the market. So our discount sales started 2 weeks later. Hence, the GP seems to be higher.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 financials: Revenue INR119.9 cr, GP margin 61.6%, EBITDA INR31 cr (25.9%), PAT INR6.3 cr (5.3%)
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter stood at INR119.9 crores. Gross profit stood at INR 73.8 crores with a GP margin of 61.6% for the quarter. EBITDA stood at INR31 crores. Our EBITDA margin stood at 25.9%. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR6.3 crores. Our PAT margin stood at 5.3% for the quarter.

items.statement: Macroeconomic uncertainty and cautious consumer behavior impacting mid-premium to premium fashion segment
items.quote: The broader apparel industry is currently navigating t hrough a phase of macroeconomic uncertainty and cautious consumer behavior.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of 25%
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve our FY '26 guidance and are confident of delivering a revenue growth of 25%.

items.statement: FY26 SSG growth guidance of 7%-8%
items.quote: We expect to deliver SSG growth of 7%-8%.

items.statement: FY26 Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin guidance of 7%-8%
items.quote: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin is projected to be at 7%-8% while Pre-Ind AS PAT margin is expected to be 3%-4%.

items.statement: FY26 store opening guidance of 40-50 new stores
items.quote: Additionally, we reaffirm our guidance of opening 40-50 new stores during FY '26.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin expansion guidance of up to 50 bps for full year
items.quote: So, I believe after all the seasonal adjustments, we anticipate a margin of up to 50 basis point increase because of the inventory efficiency and because of the private label for the entire year.

items.statement: FY26 total capex guidance of INR90-100 crores
items.quote: For everything, it will be around INR90 crores to INR100 crores for this year.

items.statement: FY26 average operating cost guidance of INR180 per sq ft per month
items.value: INR180 per sq ft per month
items.quote: We expect this average operating cost of around INR180 per square feet to hold during the entire financial year.

items.statement: FY26 rental cost guidance of INR56-57 per sq ft per month
items.value: INR56-57 per sq ft per month
items.quote: It will be in similar lines only. It will be hovering around INR56 to INR57 only.

items.statement: FY27-28 EBITDA margin target of 9%-10% on Pre-Ind AS basis
items.quote: And in next 3 years, with the operating leverage kicking in, with the gross margin and the full price through, with all this tech thing that we have done is going to improve, will help us to achieve EBITDA of 9%, 10% by FY '28.

items.statement: FY27 sales per sq ft target of INR9,800-10,000
items.quote: So, Rs. 8654 was the FY '25. And with 7%-8% SSG and with the stores that we are opening, we expect in FY '27, we will be somewhere between Rs. 9800-Rs. 10,000 of SPSF.

items.statement: Payable days target of 90 days by FY26-27
items.quote: Yes, you can expect by FY '26 and FY '27, you will see the numbers gradually going down. And it will be around 90 days as you said.

items.statement: Strong underlying demand continues; festival season expected to drive uptick in Q2 and Q3
items.quote: We anticipate a meaningful uptick in demand during Q2 and Q3 driven by the festival season including Raksha Bandhan, Durga Puja, Diwali and the wedding period which traditionally spur consumption and reinforce our confidence in the outlook.

items.statement: West Bengal demand impacted by reduced cross-border shopper inflow
items.quote: I think the numbers would have been better, if the flow from the neighboring country was there, because there are some pockets in Bengal, where the sales are very good, when they come during the festival seasons, but this year, because of the government policy, and whatever the reason, they have not been able to come into shop.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 Pre-Ind AS PAT INR9 crores, up 531% YoY
items.quote: Profit after tax came in at INR9 crore, representing a year-on-year growth of 531%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 gross margin 36%, up 300 bps YoY due to full price sell-through
items.quote: Gross profit also demonstrated healthy traction rising to INR136 crores reflecting a 49% growth year-on-year and 19% sequentially with healthy margin at 36%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue INR378 crores, up 37% YoY and 9% QoQ
items.quote: We are pleased to report that our strong growth trajectory has continued in Q1 FY '26 with revenue reaching INR378 crores, an increase of 37% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Private label revenue INR229 crores in Q1 FY26, 61% of total revenue, up 59% YoY
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, our portfolio of private labels has contributed 61% to the revenue, amounting to INR229 crores reflecting a 59% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Square brand recorded highest-ever quarterly revenue of ~INR99 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Notably, our brand Square app records highest-ever quarterly revenue, contributing approximately INR99 crores.

items.statement: Store capex INR1-1.25 crores per store; FY26 total capex INR90-100 crores including INR20-25 crores for tech/warehouse and INR10-15 crores for renovations
items.quote: In terms of expenditure, yes, INR50 crores to INR55 crores will be in the new store opening, INR25 crores to INR30 crores will be in the warehouse, infra and technology upgradation. And INR10 crores to INR15 crores will be on the renovation of the older stores.

items.statement: 18 net store additions in Q1 FY26; total store count 232, up 40% YoY; retail area 2.11 million sq ft, up 41% YoY
items.quote: Our expansion journey continues with the total store count in Q1 FY '26 reaching 232, a 40% year-on-year increase and the total retail area now stands at 2.11 million square feet reflecting a 41% growth over the previous years.

items.statement: Warehouse expanded from 86,000 sq ft to 1.86 lakh sq ft in July 2024; all in Kolkata
items.quote: As I said, because lot of store openings have happened in metro and Tier 1, which typically has a higher rental compared to Tier 3, Tier 4 cities, so that is one of the reasons. As far as the back-end, last year versus this year, in last year in Q1, the warehouse that we were having was only 86,000 square feet, whereas this year in Q1, the warehouse that we had was around 1.86 lakhs square feet.

items.statement: Average operating cost INR183 per sq ft per month in Q1 FY26 vs INR180 in FY25; expected to hold at INR180 for FY26
items.value: INR183 per sq ft per month
items.quote: In terms of number, in FY '25, our average operating cost stood at around INR180 per square feet, which in Q1 FY '26 stood at INR183 per square feet. We expect this average operating cost of around INR180 per square feet to hold during the entire financial year.

items.statement: Private label contribution 61% of revenue in Q1 FY26; Square brand ~INR99 crores
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, our portfolio of private labels has contributed 61% to the revenue, amounting to INR229 crores reflecting a 59% year-on-year growth. Notably, our brand Square app records highest-ever quarterly revenue, contributing approximately INR99 crores.

items.statement: Full price sales 92% in Q1 FY26 vs 89% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: So 92% was the full price sales in Q1 FY '26 against 89% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Customer database >1.2 million; dedicated team working on couponing and re-engagement
items.quote: So, we have got more than 1.2 million database and on which the entire team, there is a separate team which is working on that data sets which works on what is the agency, how many times the customer has visited to your stores, why they have not been visiting to your stores to create that couponing offers for thos e people and to make sure that they come again back to the store

items.statement: Organized penetration low in Tier 2-4; competition growing but market large enough; differentiation via tech, product, ambience, talent
items.quote: So, I will want to give you this answer in the two parts. First thing, if you see at the macro level, everyone is doing well. Even the competition is doing well. Okay. So, market is good enough for everyone. And the major reason behind is that as we have told in previous call also, the organized penetration is very less in Tier 2, Tier 3, Tier 4.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced to 116 in Q1 FY26 from 120 in Q1 FY25; trade payable days 111 vs 163
items.quote: Additionally, inventory days were reduced to 116 days in Q1 FY '26 compared to 120 days in Q1 FY '25. Trade payable days stood at 111 days in Q1 FY '26 from 163 days in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Inventory per sq ft INR2,092 at June end vs INR2,700 at March end; 80-20 store-warehouse split
items.quote: So I will just tell you for example, on 31st March, our inventory was at around INR2700 per square feet. Which has come down to again INR2092 at June end.

items.statement: Bank borrowings INR157.43 crores as of Q1 FY26; target INR120 crores by FY26 end
items.quote: So total bank borrowings as on date for the Q1 i s INR157.43 which we have al ready stated in the last earning call that it will be gradually reduced and will be around INR120

items.statement: Operating cash flow post lease INR26 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: It is around INR26 crores after adjustment of lease payment.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 normalized SSG 11% after adjusting for 15-day Eid shift; reported SSG -3%
items.quote: However, after adjusting for the 15-day shift, the normalized SSG for Q1 FY '26 stood at a robust 11%. Therefore, evaluating SSG on a year-to-date basis provides a more accurate and meaningful representation of performance.

items.statement: L2L (mature) store EBITDA margin 14%-16% at Pre-Ind AS; 145 mature stores
items.quote: No. So your estimation is correct. The mature stores gives typically between 14% to 16%. And for the full year, on an average, it gives around 15%.

items.statement: Store payback ~18 months in core/focus; industry 31-33 months; focus markets take 2-3 months longer
items.quote: So on an average on the capex side it takes around 18 months to recover and for the entire industry, it takes around 31 months to 33 months for the recovery.

items.statement: Sales per sq ft: Metro/Tier 1 >INR12,000; Tier 2-4 ~INR8,000-8,500
items.quote: So, on an average, if I tell you, the Metro and Tier 1 cities on an average would give us an SPSF of more than 12,000 per square feet, whereas maybe Tier 2, Tier 3, Tier 4 average will be around 8,000 or 8,500.

items.statement: Buying/merchandising/design team strength 70-75 people
items.quote: So for the entire, see, our buying and merchandising team comprises of designers, merchandiser, sourcing guys, and all together as a collective team they work, the total team strength of them is around 70 to 75 people as of now.

items.statement: Insurance claim for inventory loss pending; INR3.48 crores received against INR4.24 crores asset loss; resolution expected in upcoming quarters
items.quote: See, in terms of insurance payment, we have received an amount of INR3.48 crores including salvage value against the total asset loss of INR4.24 crores. For the inventory thing, we are actively and consistently engaging with the insurance company to expedite the claim processing.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target 20-25% YoY; mid-to-long-term average 20% YoY with EBITDA margin 17-19%
items.quote: We are thinking, on an average, 20% year-on-year, in mid- to long-term, with the similar type of EBITDA margin of 17% to 19%. And for FY'26, we are seeing 20% to 25% type of growth, and we still want to maintain that.

items.statement: Combined Wada and Chennai capacity revenue potential Rs 425-450 crore over next 1.5-2 years
items.quote: Broadly 425-450 type of number, that depends completely on the product mix and all. Beyond that, we actually started searching the land in Chennai or even in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and based on the customer expectation or requirement, we will be finalizing land maybe next 6-month time.

items.statement: Chennai Phase 1 capex completed, commercial production started July 2025; Phase 2 capex Rs 15-20 crore to be reviewed in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: In Chennai, we have completed the CAPEX phase 1 and we just started the production last month. items.statement: Wada plant capex ongoing, POs issued for machines, expect delivery in next 3 months; total deployment 6-9 months
items.quote: A lot of POs have already been issued. And maybe in the next 3 months or so, we will be getting a good number of machines on shop floor. But there is no such delay. And we just keep on as and when we see there is more clarity about the order.

items.statement: Chennai plant peak capacity revenue Rs 120 crore expected by FY27 end or FY28 run rate
items.quote: As we mentioned, the total capex in Chennai is going to be approximately Rs. 48 crores- Rs. 50 crores. And in peak capacity, it will touch around Rs. 120 crore top line. And we are seeing we should be touching this in FY'27 end or FY'28 as a run rate.

items.statement: Gross margin 58-60% going forward; RM cost 40-45%; EBITDA margin target 17-19% excluding FX impact
items.quote: The gross margin will be around 58% - 60% going forward also and even the RM ratio will be around 40% - 45%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 15.21% impacted by Rs 2 crore FX revaluation loss and Rs 1 crore higher operating costs
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was around Rs. 10 crores which declined 12% year-on-year and 35% quarter-on-quarter with EBITDA margins reported at 15.21%.

items.statement: US tariff on fasteners and disc springs increased from 5.5% to 25%; no order cancellations yet but uncertainty for next couple of months
items.quote: I think before this tariff situation, the duty on our component which is fasteners and disc springs was 5.5% and now I think it is 25%.

items.statement: Hedge 65% of Euro and USD export contract value via 12-month rolling forwards; 35% left open; USD naturally hedged by imports
items.quote: We do hedge for Euro exports as well as USD exports. We hedge to the extent of 65% of the total contract value, and 35% we leave it for the open market. And we take a forward cover for the next 12 months, as of now.

items.statement: Import terms exclude import duty; customers absorbed 5.5% duty; will evaluate price adjustment if 25% tariff sustains based on competition from Europe
items.quote: Our import terms with all the customers are without any import duty added in our price. So even when the tariff was 5.5%, sorry, import duty was 5.5%, it was absorbed by customers. And currently there is no legal bounding that whatever tariff comes, we have to absorb.

items.statement: Fastener business 64% sequential growth Q1 FY26 (Rs 12 crore to Rs 20 crore); Chennai plant produces only fasteners; Wada produces all three product lines
items.quote: Our fastener business represents a strong 64% sequential growth with revenue raising from Rs. 12 crores to Rs. 20 crores in Quarter 1 of FY'26.

items.statement: Seat retractor springs: customer buys Rs 20 crore annually in India; global demand 5-7x; Tier-1 testing ongoing, OEM approval next 2-3 months; sole domestic competitor Kern-Lieber
items.quote: Customers whom we are talking, they buy about Rs. 20 crores worth of retractor springs in India. Of course, globally, their demand is at least 5-7 times bigger than this.

items.statement: High customer stickiness: product development to validation takes 9-20 months; customers do not change sources easily
items.quote: The customer and Gala need to put a lot of effort in, start from the RFQ to product development, validation, field trial and all. It takes 9 months- 20 for a year and that is how it brings a lot of stickiness. So, normally, the customer do not change the sources so easily.

items.statement: US fastener competition from Germany, Norway, Denmark, UK; disc springs niche with limited competition
items.quote: For Fasteners, we compete with producers from Germany, Norway, and Denmark and U.K. They are mainly supplying to U.S. apart from India.

items.statement: IPO general corpus Rs 25+ crore in FD; zero long-term debt; healthy cash accruals sufficient for organic growth 3-5 years; inorganic funding premature
items.quote: We have as of now the general corpus which we raised in IPO, almost Rs. 25 crores plus is there in general corpus and lying in FD. Number two, there is no long-term debt, zero long-term debt on the company's book. And number three, there is a healthy cash accrual are there in company year-on-year.

items.statement: Attrition below 10%, well below industry benchmark; existing pre-IPO ESOP scheme active, no new ESOP planned near term
items.quote: It is below 10% and much lower than the industry benchmark.

items.statement: Forward cover SIP mechanism every 10 days for 12-month horizon; export collections hedged, imports not hedged
items.quote: We have an SIP mechanism, which follows every month. Every 10 days, we take forward cover under the SIP mechanism. And we also do forward cover for export for USD, but that is very, very less.

items.statement: Zero long-term debt on books; funding for organic expansion from IPO corpus, cash accruals, and internal approvals
items.quote: Number two, there is no long-term debt, zero long-term debt on the company's book. And number three, there is a healthy cash accrual are there in company year-on-year. With these three, as of now, this is something which should meet.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 63 crore (+19% YoY, -16% QoQ); EBITDA Rs 10 crore (-12% YoY, -35% QoQ); PAT Rs 6.5 crore (+3.2% YoY, -35% QoQ)

items.quote: But of course, uncertainty continues till the time we have the finalised situation for the tariffs or now they are talking about penalties. So, there can be some impact because of this.

items.quote: As of now, the BI is something which is applicable in our fastener products, which we manufacture in India. And for that, we are getting the BI certifications and all.

items.quote: Compared to Q1 FY '25, we were almost doubled from 7.6% to 14.3%. But even compared to Q4, we grew our market share by about 70 bps from 13.6% to 14.3%.
