items.quote: We are aiming to grow it INR400 crores by the end of -- by March '27 new orders into the pipeline. INR445 crores by March '27.

items.statement: Engineering division planning 30%+ organic growth annually plus M&A; evaluated 48 companies for acquisition
items.quote: The plan is that we have to grow organically, minimum 30% per annum. And also we have to grow through merger and acquisition route, which we are actively pursuing. And we have already seen 48 companies.

items.statement: Commodity price control slipped in Q1; pricing committee now corrected to mitigate future increases
items.quote: What we could have done better is the control on the commodity pricing. We have pricing committee with regular follow-ups and why the commodity pricing and what measures we can take to mitigate that we do it properly, we have now corrected.

items.statement: Compressor supply secured for current season requirements despite industry demand-supply gap
items.quote: We are aware of the demand-supply gap in compressor, but we are already discussing with a manufacturer. And as of today, we are secured with the quantities whatever is required in the -- for the season.

items.statement: Refrigerator mix shifting toward higher-end no-frost models; launching 328-liter model soon
items.quote: We are launching the 328-liter very soon. And after that, we will launch other models. Our brand prism ideally should have -- I mean, our ideal structure would have been to launch the higher-end models first.

items.statement: Washing machines fully transitioned to BLDC motor-driven technology
items.quote: We have moved completely to BLDC. We are moving completely to BLDC.

items.statement: Strengthening consumer finance and affordability team to improve credit card tie-ups and reduce cost
items.quote: We are working on this. As you said, we are strengthening our team on consumer finance and affordability so that our cost has to further go down.

items.statement: AC market has 40+ brands; IFB at 3-3.5% market share but in top 10 price points; front load washer #1 in customer selling price
items.quote: In air conditioners, as you know, it is a crowded market. There are more than 40 brands operating. If you look from the price point, we are in top 10.

items.statement: Government import restrictions on chains prompting domestic chain manufacturing plant investment
items.quote: Now the government is imposing some restriction on imports, so our Board has cleared our investment for setting up a chain manufacturing plant in India.

items.statement: E-waste provisioning at INR2 crore/month (INR24-25 crore annually) included in cost base
items.quote: Our monthly cost is around INR2 crores. So annually is around INR24 crores to INR25 crores.

items.statement: IFB Refrigeration (41% stake) consolidation planned in next 6-12 months subject to Board approval
items.quote: Hopefully, we will get there soon. And we hope to at least consolidate it in the near term. Near term meaning maybe in the next 6 to 12 months, hopefully, subject to Board approvals.

items.statement: Engineering division FY25 margins benefited from stable commodity prices; steel prices up INR3,000 in Q1 FY26 with quarter to half-year pass-through lag
items.quote: The last 2 years, we have been blessed with a stable commodity price, it has not been very -- now in quarter 1 this year, the steel prices have been increased by INR3,000.

items.statement: Change management and cost control execution described as 'very, very slow'; commodity team defocused during A&M project causing slippages
items.quote: Whilst we were working with A&M on cost down, the team that was supposed to handle commodity price, etcetera, got defocused and some slippages have happened there.

items.statement: Fixed cost consolidation slower than required; increments given but work consolidation delayed
items.quote: Areas where consolidation of work, etcetera, should have happened, have not happened as fast as it should have. And that's also an area of slippage.

items.statement: Advertising spend clarified at INR100 crore annually (not INR284 crore); includes CSR and customer sales representative costs from IFB Appliances and Genius
items.quote: Our ad and promo cost annually is around INR100 crores and we are working on reducing the ad and promo -- optimizing the ad and promo cost by increasing the visibility with the same spend.

items.statement: Total customer sales representatives increased to ~4,600 (4,000 IFB Appliances + 600 Genius)
items.quote: The total number will be around 4,600-odd 600 are on Genius folks.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target for FY27 is 6.5% to 7%
items.quote: Our target margins for FY27, it would be in the range of 6.5 – 7 %. That's what we are aiming for. 6.5 % would be the bare minimum that we would be looking to do.

items.statement: ROCE target for FY26 is 9% to 12%
items.quote: In terms of ROCE, our aim for ROCE is to hit double digits by end of this year. Anywhere between 9% to Q1FY26 Earnings Webinar Transcript 7 12% is the ROCE aim that we are looking for

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 15% to 16% consistently over next 3-4 years
items.quote: If we want to grow at 15% to 16% consistently over the next 3, 4 years, employee cost will be one of the major factors which will be under pressure.

items.statement: Asset-light model with contract manufacturing expansion; no major capex for own plant
items.quote: For future growth, we've always maintained that our current aim is to be on an asset-light model. So we are working on establishing more capacities with contract manufacturers as our demand goes up.

items.statement: Rajkot plant at 70% utilization, can reach 85% without issues
items.quote: For our main plant, Rajkot, currently we are at about a 70 % utilization. That can go up to about 85 % without an issue. So, there is some headroom over there.

items.statement: Q1 demand challenging due to North India war impact; premium segment weak but recovering in July
items.quote: Overall, this quarter was challenging on the demand front, especially on the premium product range. The war situation in North India had a big impact on our business as North India is our strongest market.

items.statement: Premium segment recovering in July after North India disruption
items.quote: The premium segment will start growing again, the July numbers are in already. So, the premium segment is moving back into the right direction. It was largely, I think, driven by what happened in the North.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 5.8% in Q1 FY26 vs 4.8% YoY and 5.1% QoQ
items.quote: In margin terms, EBITDA margin stood at 5.8% of sales as compared to 4.8% in the same period last year and 5.1% in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Gross margin flat at 34.1% due to mix shift toward lower-margin contract manufacturing
items.quote: Gross margin this quarter stood at 34.1%, similar to Q1 last year and down from 34.9% in Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Duro premium segment grew 2% YoY but fell 18% QoQ; Tower mid-segment grew 45% YoY but fell 5.5% QoQ
items.quote: On the product mix, Duro segment saw a 2% growth rate on a year-on-year basis and a 18% degrowth on a quarter-on-quarter basis. Our mid-segment brand tower continued to showcase robust growth, with a 45% growth on a year-on-year basis and a 5.5% degrowth on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Timber cost flat in Q1; domestic cost may rise seasonally in Q2 but no major shocks expected
items.quote: Our timber cost largely remained flat. For our in-house manufacture, we are dependent on imports, not so much on domestic timber and on imports, we did not see any price escalation. However, in Q2, in the domestic procurement market, there are rumours of a cost increase happening. Timber cost has started going up, which is very consistent with this time of the year with the rains. But nothing out

items.statement: Imported timber landed cost slightly cheaper than domestic due to lower inward freight to Rajkot plant
items.quote: Import on a per unit basis is at par with domestic, but what happens is the inward shipping cost of taking the material from the UP belt or from North Andhra to Rajkot, which is where our plant is located, that makes it very expensive. And that's why we are better off today being on import. Landed cost with the inward freight, the imported is slightly cheaper for us.

items.statement: QCO norms implementation by BIS reducing imports, benefiting both organized and unorganized sectors
items.quote: More than that, I think the challenge is going to come with the implementation of the QCO norms by BIS. A lot of imported material that used to come into the country, that has not happened over the last quarter. That will actually help the branded segment, which will also help the unorganized segment because the unorganized segment was facing tremendous pressure on selling because of these imports

items.statement: Debtor days reduced to 44 from 47 YoY; inventory days 149 vs 165 YoY; creditor days 170 vs 90 QoQ; cash conversion cycle 113 days
items.quote: Debtor turnover ratio is 44 days as compared to 47 days of last year. Inventory turnover days is 149 days as compared to 165 days of Q1 FY26. Creditor days is 170 days as compared to 90 days of Q4 FY25. As a result, cash conversion cycle is 113 days for Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Warrants converting within next month to provide liquidity
items.quote: We also have warrants that were due to convert coming… that will be converted within the next month or so.

items.statement: Adopted Salesforce application for sales team tracking; automating backend processes to reduce manual intervention
items.quote: We recently have adopted a new Salesforce application and using that for better tracking of our sales team and getting them to be more effective on ground. We are also automating a lot of our backend processes to reduce manual intervention.

items.statement: Volume growth of ~9% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Volume growth was about 9 odd %.

items.statement: Marketing spend target ~3.5% of sales for FY26, declining as revenue scales
items.quote: Our marketing spend this year will be at about 3.5% of sales on overall average and over the years, that will start coming down as the revenue starts going up further.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle increasing due to creditor days reduction; management views it as strategic for better procurement
items.quote: The cash conversion cycle is increasing and it is a matter of concern. In a way, yes and no. So our debtor days in the last quarter, fourth quarter, had substantially shot up. So we have reduced our day's debtor Q1FY26 Earnings Webinar Transcript 6 significantly by 3 days and it will continue to come down in this quarter as well

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue Rs 93.5 crore, up 10.3% YoY, down 15% QoQ; PBT Rs 1.88 crore, up ~50% YoY
items.quote: Duroply closed its first quarter revenue at Rs. 93.5 crores, a 10.3% growth over the same period last year and down 15% from the previous quarter. The business reported a profit before tax of Rs. 1.88 crores, up by nearly 50% from the same period last year.

items.statement: Management says it is academic to discuss top-line growth guidance of 10-15% given market uncertainty and tariff-related demand deferment
items.quote: Talking about the guidance on a 10 % to 15% level, we had given guidance on increase of volumes but looking at the market uncertainty, it is very academic right now to talk about the increase in top line at this juncture.

items.statement: Management expects pent-up demand to flow through the rest of the year as chemical portfolio cannot be substituted
items.quote: We believe that once there is a clarity on the tariff front, market stability is likely to return.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin improved 81 bps YoY to ~46%; EBITDA margin stable at 16.1%
items.quote: We are pl eased to report our consolidated gross margin improved by 81 basis points year -on- year basis to close to 46%. And consolidated EBITDA margin remained stable at 16.1

items.statement: Standalone gross margin improved 470 bps and EBITDA margin improved 185 bps sequentially
items.quote: The Company witnessed improvement in gross margins and EBITDA margins during the quarter. As stated earlier, the focus on margins and customer -first approach helped the Company achieve desired improvement of 470 basis points in gross margins in standalone business and 185 basis points improvement in EBITDA margins on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Order book and order flow temporarily affected by tariff uncertainties and cautious customer inventory stocking
items.quote: This caution coupled with subdued global manufacturing activity, I would say, temporarily affected our order book and our order flow.

items.statement: Rs. 46 crore spent on Strontium project till 30 June 2025; production expected to start in Q2 or early Q3
items.quote: On an immediate basis, the Company is working to complete its CAPEX in Vishnu Strontium Private Limited . Of this, Rs. 46 crores have been spent till 30th June 2025.

items.statement: Future investment in Chromium and Barium verticals to be strategized after tariff stabilization
items.quote: We are going to focus on completing the existing projects in hand , including the foray into Strontium chemistry and strategize our future investment in Chromium and Barium vertical once the clarity emerges post-tariff stabilization.

items.statement: Chromium and Barium plants operating at ~80% utilization; target 90% this quarter
items.quote: Again, in terms of our operating levels, we are currently operating at close to 80%, both the products, and we target to get to 90% in this particular quarter as well.

items.statement: Barium capacity utilization improved from mid-60s in FY24 to 80-82% targeted by end of FY26
items.quote: Compared to mid-60s capacity utilization that we achieved in FY '24, our current utilization gives us the momentum to achieve at least 80% to 80%, 82% by the end of this year.

items.statement: Ocean freight rates surged May-June; shipping and forwarding costs increased 88 bps sequentially
items.quote: Ocean freight rates also surged between May and early June driven by tariff -related developments and especially the peak season surcharge has been applied. While freight costs have begun to ease since mid -June, we did experience an increase of 88 basis points in our shipping and forwarding costs sequentially.

items.statement: Barium product realizations unchanged sequentially; no price increases due to macro uncertainties
items.quote: On the pricing front, the realization of nearly all the products in Barium chemicals remained the same on a sequential basis as we did not increase any prices during the quarter, because there were already a lot of uncertainties around the macro factors.

items.statement: Chromium derivative mix shifting toward value-added products (metal plating, wood preservative, pigments, Chromium metal); leather exposure down to 15-20% of sodium dichromate volumes
items.quote: It could be focusing on metal plating, wood preservative, and pigments and dyes, as well as Chromium metal. So, that is what we are going to focus on. It doesn't mean that we are going to do away with the leather business because that is something, we have those long -term relationships. I think it is a moment that this industry is going through a lower business cycle. And it will definitely come

items.statement: Consolidated US exposure ~7% of sales (5% Chromium, 12% of Barium sales); Barium exempt from tariffs under Annexure 2
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our exposure is close to 12%. In that, 7% to 8% is about Chrome and about 3%, 4% is Barium. So, just to give you an update, for our Barium chemicals, there are no tariffs. It is totally exempted based on Annexure 2, which is a very positive.

items.statement: Corrected US exposure: 5% of Chromium sales and 12% of Barium sales from USA; consolidated ~7%
items.quote: Sales of Vishnu chemicals on a consolidated basis from USA is about 7%. 5% of Chromium sales come from USA. And on the Barium side, we have 12% contribution coming from USA.

items.statement: Domestic:Export sales mix 55:45 in Q1; management may shift toward 60:40 domestic focus
items.quote: Consolidated Domestic:E xport sales mix stood at 55 :45 during the quarter. Our balance presents across domestic and export markets gives us the flexibility tha t is valued in times like these.

items.statement: Ripple effect of US tariffs impacting demand from other countries whose end products go to US
items.quote: So, directly or indirectly, we may not be , like you rightly o bserved, we are not like that. I mean, it is not insignificant and not too significant. It is 5% of our Chrome business and close to 4% of our Barium business. But the thing is that, like, we are exporting to over 65 countries. So, you know, there is something called ripple effect where ideally the consumer remains America, right?

items.statement: Chrome faces 25%+3.5% (28%) tariff in US; Barium exempt under Annexure 2
items.quote: Chrome, there is a tariff applied. Right now, it is close to 25% pl us 3.5 %, 28%. We are in constant touch with customers. So, right now, things are still quite fluid at the moment.

items.statement: South Africa acquisition statutory approvals still in progress; expected by November 2025
items.quote: The statutory approvals and clearances are still in progress. And we will update you once we have clarity on the same.

items.statement: Mine acquisition awaiting government approvals; anticipated on or before November 2025 (12 months from Nov 2024 signing)
items.quote: As per our assessment, we had anticipated one year from the time of signing of the agreements last year in November 2024 . So, we are expecting the approvals to come on or before November 2025. That is 12 months from the date of signing the definitive agreement.

items.statement: Net debt ~Rs. 250 crore as of 30 June 2025 (~0.25x net debt to equity)
items.quote: On the debt side, the Company's net debt is about Rs. 250 crores as of 30th June 2025, which is close to about 0.25x net debt to equity.

items.statement: Board recommended 15% dividend on face value of Rs. 2 per share, subject to AGM approval
items.quote: The Company has a continuous track record of paying dividends. The Board of Vishnu has recommended a dividend of 15% on the face value of Rs. 2 per share, which is subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM.

items.statement: Global Chromium chemicals demand CAGR 4.5-5.5%; Barium chemicals CAGR 5.5-6.5%
items.quote: In the range of 4.5% to 5.5%.

items.statement: Sodium dichromate capacity ~80,000 tons; 30-33% sold as primary, 67% converted to derivatives
items.quote: We have a capacity of nearly 80,000 tons of Sodium dichromate, o f which nearly 30 % to 33% is sold as Sodium dichromate in the market. Balanced 67% of Sodium dichromate is converted into derivatives as per the demand

items.statement: Strontium carbonate plant capacity 12,000 tons per annum; commercial sales expected from September 2025
items.quote: I think we already conveyed before, close to 12,000 tons of Strontium carbonate per annum.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty causing demand deferment, inventory caution, and ripple effects across 65+ export markets
items.quote: Quarter 1, while our year -on-year performance remained resilient, we wi tnessed a moderation in sequential performance , largely due to demand deferment arising from ongoing tariff uncertainties.

items.statement: R&D expenditure ~0.5% of consolidated sales, fully expensed monthly, outsourced to third party
items.quote: And it is close to about 0.5% of our total sales, consolidated sales of the Company.

items.statement: Medium-term consolidated revenue growth target of 18-20% with higher standalone growth
items.quote: As we have mentioned in the past, our medium-term growth objective is to be in the range of about 18% to 20% at a consolidated level, and at a standalone level, we will be higher than that.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target of 13-15% in roughly two years from current ~8.5%
items.quote: EBITDA margin, our objective is to be at the range of 13% to 15% at a consolidated level, which today is at 8.5% or so.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin target of 14-15% on yearly basis
items.quote: we should be able to maintain the EBITDA margin, which Nikhil was in dicating, around 14% to 15% on a yearly basis

items.statement: Order book grew to Rs 1,769 crores as of 30 June 2025 driven by new EMS customers and DRDO development orders
items.quote: On the order book front, our order book position grew to Rs. 1,769 crores as of 30th June, 2025, driven by new EMS customers entering into the serial production phase after successful NPI qualifications.

items.statement: Order book split: EMS Rs 710 cr, BTS Rs 886 cr, ER&D services Rs 171 cr
items.value: EMS Rs 710 cr, BTS Rs 886 cr, ER&D Rs 171 cr
items.quote: So, yes, at a high level, we see that about Rs. 710 crores is the order book for EMS, Rs. 886 crores is BTS and ER&D service is Rs. 171 crores.

items.statement: ER&D demand softness over past 18 months led by automotive and aerospace; pipeline improving driven by defense customers
items.quote: We have clearly seen a demand softness over the past 18 months or so, which led effectively by, firstly, the automotive sector, partially also on the aerospace sector. But we are seeing an improvement in the pipeline of opportunities, driven largely by the defense customers.

items.statement: Expect improved ER&D performance in H2 FY26 contingent on pipeline conversion
items.period: second half of this financial year
items.quote: We expect to have some of these pipeline conversions happen over the next few months. And with that, we are targeting to have an improved performance in the year in part at least in the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Standalone Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 14.92% vs consolidated 8.38%; standalone EBITDA grew >100% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter was around Rs. 27 crores, which also grew by more than 100% year-on-year, with EBITDA margins reported at 14.92%.

items.statement: Gross margin variation due to revenue mix across BTS, EMS and engineering services businesses
items.quote: The level of gross margin would be highly dependent on the mix of the three types of business that we have.

items.statement: Rs 40 crore capex planned for FY26 for Indian standalone business only
items.quote: So, the Rs. 40 crore CAPEX that you had announced on the last call will be done purely for the Indian business?

items.statement: Standalone asset turnover currently 6-7x net block, expected to reach 8-9x in next 1-2 years with capex additions
items.quote: Currently, we are running around 6x to 7x, and that may not significantly increase in the current year. But considering the growth from 6x to 7x, we expect this to move about 8x to 9x in the next year or two because significant CAPEX will get added to this.

items.statement: NPI qualifications completed for semiconductor, biometric security, and defense/aerospace export customers; expected to add ~USD 15M revenue in FY26
items.quote: For the current financial year itself, our objective is some of these NPI itself will add about USD 15 million or so, in terms of revenue, U.S. dollars revenue.

items.statement: EMS business well diversified across defense, aerospace, industrial, energy, medical, automotive, semiconductor equipment, biometrics; recurring products with 10+ year lifecycles
items.quote: We address customers in defence, aerospace for exports. We address industrial and energy, some medical customers, and as well as the automotive or mobility kind of customers. So, these are all the sectors that we are in, and now, as I mentioned, some of the newer customers that we have added and we are ramping up are in the semiconductor space, semiconductor equipment and biometrics and security.

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary strategic action decision expected by end of current quarter; loss-making with ~30 employees; FY25 loss €2.4M, Q1 FY26 loss €600-700K EBT
items.quote: We believe we should have a decision for this in the coming months and we hope to basically have a decision for that by the end of the current quarter.

items.statement: UK subsidiary is a pass-through SPV; investments of Rs 33 cr (FY24) and Rs 45 cr (FY25) were into French subsidiary
items.quote: UK is actually a pass through. It is a special purpose vehicle. So, the investment was in the French subsidiary.

items.statement: Consolidated subsidiary loss ~Rs 12 cr in Q1 FY26 split ~50-50 between Canada and France; Canada revenue only Rs 17-18 cr vs loss
items.quote: around Rs. 12 crores loss, we incur from the subsidiary. So, how much loss we incur from Canada? K. S. Desikan: So, it is roughly 50 – 50, 50% in Canada and 50% in France of the Rs. 12 crores

items.statement: BTS order execution timeline typically 2-2.5 years; development-to-production cycle 18-24 months
items.quote: Typically, the BTS orders are in the range of between 2 years to 2.5 year execution.

items.statement: Standalone revenue grew 35% YoY to Rs 180 cr in Q1 FY26; consolidated revenue grew 11.4% YoY to Rs 273 cr
items.quote: At a standalone level, the revenue from operations was about Rs. 180 crores, which increased by 35% year-on-year.

items.statement: Large tri-services orders (Rs 200-500 cr) stuck in government approval processes; no near-term visibility
items.quote: We do not see, in the very short term, some of these major opportunities, coming through. But we continue to work on them and monitor them very closely.

items.statement: Indra Sistemas MOU program stalled with no government update
items.quote: No further update on that program. It is still basically stalled and we have no further update from the government on this program.

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary down to ~30 employees; India team of 30-40 engineers now delivering metro and Vande Bharat orders
items.quote: Yes, there are currently around 30 employees that we have there.

items.statement: EMS exports to Europe, US, Asia including Israel, Malaysia, Singapore; significant export share
items.quote: We are exporting again to Europe, we are exporting to the U.S., to other countries in Asia, including Israel and even now to countries like Malaysia, Singapore, and so on.

items.statement: Revenue recognition for BTS heavily weighted to Q4; Q1 FY26 margins better than prior year Q1 suggesting more even distribution this year
items.quote: If you look at even Q1, I think margin was better compared to last year Q1. So, this year around, maybe it will be distributed not on an equal bas is. Maybe still, the higher margin probably will be clocked in the last quarter. But this year is slightly better than the previous year

items.statement: Canadian subsidiary losses driven by employee costs; product delivery margins insufficient to cover costs
items.quote: The level of product deliveries and the margins associated with that is not enough to justify the costs that we have in Canada. And so, that is part of the reason we are incurring the loss.

items.statement: Space-based surveillance (SBS-3) budgets sanctioned to ISRO; RFQs for private industry at early stages
items.quote: The budgets have just been sanctioned and a big part of it will be going to ISRO, after which these will come out in the form of various RFQs for private industries and so on.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 guidance of 10-15% topline growth and 15-20% bottomline growth
items.quote: We have already discussed and told you in our last conference call that we will be expecting 10%-15% increase in our topline and 15%-20% increase in bottomline.

items.statement: Confirmed efforts to achieve previously discussed FY26 revenue growth of 12-15% and profit growth of 15-20%
items.quote: Yes, we are trying our all efforts to achieve the discussed results in terms of topline and bottomline.

items.statement: Mexico plant capex postponed due to tariff uncertainty; land acquired and planning complete
items.quote: Mexico's status was clear, we decided, we have found out the land and we made all the planning. And we were about to go about it, but suddenly, one month back, this kind of thing has happened. So, we have postponed for the time being.

items.statement: Mexico plant will proceed once tariff confusion settles; US production cost too high
items.quote: As soon as these confusions are completed, we will start it. Everything was done. It was just to push the button, but suddenly, these things have happened, which has created big confusion in the mind. But definitely, the way the requirement is increasing, we are bound to.

items.statement: Exports at Rs 80.05 cr (40% of revenue); Export OEM Rs 53.10 cr, Export General Rs 24.95 cr
items.quote: Export General Rs. 24.95 crores, Export OEM Rs. 53.10 crores, Total exports Rs. 80.05 crores, which is 40% of our total revenue

items.statement: No tariff impact on auto OEM exports as supply goes to Mexico; built 3-month US stock; no worry till 25% tariff
items.quote: So, as far as our OEM business is concerned, there is no impact as such because the material we are exporting to Mexico. And so, there is no direct impact on Mayu r in terms of auto OEM businesses there. We have a business directly for other markets in the US market. So, we have built our stock in the last 3 months over there. Till 25% tariff is there, we see no major reason for us to worry in ter

items.statement: 50% tariff announced for shipments from Aug 27 is a worry; will analyze impact; growing exports to Europe and Middle East
items.quote: 50% was announced yesterday only and it is applicable only for shipment from 27th August. So, that we will understand, analyze and then we can give you a proper answer for 20%-50% tariff. But definitely, 50% tariff is a worry.

items.statement: Domestic Q1 subdued but not bad; expecting improvement in Q2 due to festive season
items.quote: Domestic market, 1st quarter was a bit subdued, but not very bad for Mayur. Obviously, growth was not there. Obviously, July, August, September is always a good quarter for everyone because India is a very festive oriented market. So, we are hoping that sales should improve in this quarter.

items.statement: Replacement market sales down due to 3-4 OEMs' lower sales and design changes; expects improvement but not massive increase
items.quote: Replacement market specifically was with 3 -4 OEMs. Their sale has been down in the last quarter specifically and there has been some change in design also. So, we will not see a massive increase in the sales in replacement market. But yes, the sale which is a little down will improve definitely.

items.statement: Margin improvement expected from export mix change, raw material, operating efficiency and productivity
items.quote: And second question, the margin, change in margin or increase in margin we are expecting, and it is based on the mix of our sales mix and other impacts, say our raw material and operating efficiency, productivity, etc. So, product mix also is getting changed. So, that is why we are expecting increase in our bottomline because of increase in exports and efficiency improvement.

items.statement: Working with Aditya Birla and Adidas for 6-8 months; targeting multinational brands in footwear, garments, leather goods for better margins
items.quote: we are working on these big brands who can give us good price also. But it takes good time. Already we are working on th at. Now, the system is that we have to give them the materials. They will make the end product, and they will show to their customers. Out of that, whatever is decided, they will choose. That has also started coming. They have started giving us the trial orders and we are workin

items.statement: Retail distribution expanding; dealer count around 750-800 (Poddar says ~1000); sales up YoY; adding product lines
items.quote: So, that business is definitely improving. The sales, if you compare to the 1st quarter of FY '25 to the sale of the 1st quarter of FY '26, the sale has gone up. I don't have the exact number, but definitely the number of dealers have gone up also. Maybe around 750 -800. I don't have the exact number on my hand. Mr. Poddar is saying it is around 1000 right now. The sale is also improving. We are a

items.statement: No change in competitive positioning vs Asian peers ex-China; domestic leather cloth manufacturers increasing 10-15/year competing on price
items.quote: There is no change from what it was in the past. So, specifically, if you are not talking about tariffs, so there is no change in terms of our position where we were standing in the market in the past and where we stand right now.

items.statement: No domestic auto OEM market share lost; supplying to Kia via Korean partner; business with Hyundai to increase
items.quote: If you are talking about specific automotive industry in the domestic market, again, we have not lost any market share because of some other people getting Hyundai, Kia market because obviously most automotive companies will not work with a single supplier. They will have multiple suppliers and we are supplying to Kia through our Korean partner and we will continue to supply to them and our busine

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 215.88 cr, PBT Rs 54.97 cr, PAT Rs 40.73 cr; QoQ revenue +1%, PBT +7%, PAT +2%
items.quote: The Company has achieved the revenue from operation on consolidated basis is Rs. 215.88 crores, PBT Rs. 54.97 crores and PAT Rs. 40.73 crores. In the quarter, the consolidated revenue increased by 1%, PBT and PAT increased by 7% and 2% respectively on quarter -on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Standalone revenue Rs 206.41 cr, PBT Rs 55.32 cr, PAT Rs 41.23 cr; QoQ revenue +6%, PBT +21%, PAT +19%
items.quote: The revenue from operation on standalone basis is Rs. 206.41 crores, PBT Rs. 55.32 crores and PAT Rs. 41.23 crores. In the quarter , the standalone revenue, PBT and PAT increased by 6%, 21% and 19% respectively.

items.statement: Export OEM momentum from US and Europe expected to continue for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Further, our endeavor is to make the Company a preferred supplier for the leading O EM especially in US and European regions and in continuation to this, we have received some good export orders from US and O EM supplies, which is resulting into a good contribution in our topline and bottomline and this increased momentum is expected to continue in next 2 -3

items.statement: Automotive OEM sales increasing drastically worldwide; recently won Ford super models order scaling from 10,000 to 100,000+ yards in 2 years
items.quote: Like recently, we got an order from Ford for their super models. They were hardly supplying 10,000 yards. Now, in the next 2 years, we are going to supply more than 100,000 yards.

items.statement: Focus on bottom-line over topline; targeting multinational brands paying 2.5-3x Indian prices; not chasing volume at same profit
items.quote: Now, my thinking is totally different. I have to go to the places where I can get the value of the product. That is why for footwear, leather goods, garments, we are moving all multinational brands. There, they need quality, and they give you a better price. So, far footwear is concerned, I am not worried in next 1 to 1.5 years' time, it will definitely start increasing. Now listen, increasing is

items.statement: 50% US tariff on selected items from Aug 27 is a worry; uncertain if it stays or is negotiation tactic
items.quote: 50% was announced yesterday only and it is applicable only for shipment from 27th August. So, that we will understand, analyze and then we can give you a proper answer for 20%-50% tariff. But definitely, 50% tariff is a worry. We don't know whether it will stay or whether it is just a negotiation skill, time will only tell.

items.statement: Business environment unpredictable; impossible to forecast tariff or demand changes; focus on identifying and satisfying customer needs
items.quote: Situations change every moment. Business is not like that, that what you are doing today, you will keep on doing the same thing. You have to change every moment according to the situation. Then only you will get successful. For that, we are very particular. In business, there are two things, identify and satisfy. I have to identify my customers' requirements and then I have to satisfy that. That i

items.statement: Professionalization efforts ongoing; Poddar asserts company already professionally run
items.quote: We are working seriously on that. Professionalize is very easy. We can do tomorrow. One minute. What do you mean by professionalize? If this Company is not professionalized, how this Company is running?

items.statement: CSR initiatives include plantations, happy schools, healthcare, child skill development, water, sanitation, family planning in nearby villages; state government recognized
items.quote: Under the Corporate Social Responsibility Program, we have contributed towards the regular plantations and have a plan to do it at a large scale in coming years. The Company has also adopted many happy schools for education of children. The Company has worked on education for all and privileged children, various healthcare initiatives especially child skill development, water for all, sanitation a

items.statement: Reaffirmed 20% revenue growth guidance for FY26
items.quote: Yes, that's true. 20% growth has been our past and that is how our future will also look for sure..

items.statement: Targets Rs 5,000 crore revenue and Rs 1,000 crore EBITDA in 3-5 years
items.value: Rs 5,000 crore revenue and Rs 1,000 crore EBITDA
items.quote: This will enable us to achieve our 5,000-1,000 vision, that is Rs. 5,000 crores and Rs. 1,000 crore EBITDA in the next 3-5 years.

items.statement: Expects to maintain EBITDA margins at current 24.8% levels near term
items.quote: EBITDA margins have been an impressive 24.8% for this quarter and we expect to maintain EBITDA margins at these levels going forward in the near future.

items.statement: Committed to north of 20% EBITDA margins as guideline
items.quote: See, our business is based on north of 20% EBITDA margins. I am not saying that even if RMC may go on, go up for some products that we introduced. But when north of 20 % EBITDA will always be our guideline.

items.statement: Overall capex of ~Rs 1,100 crore planned for 5K-1K vision; Phase 1 of Rs 280-300 crore on track for completion by year-end
items.value: Rs 1,100 crore overall; Rs 280-300 crore Phase 1
items.quote: In order to achieve a vision of 5K-1K, broadly as indicated in our last call also, there is an overall CAPEX of about Rs. 1,100 crores, we expect. The first phase we have started with a CAPEX amount of about close to 280 crores to 300 crores.

items.statement: Privi Fine Sciences capex ~Rs 400 crore more to be added; consolidated capex to be funded via internal accruals and debt
items.quote: We have done a great amount of CAPEX in Fine Science already and we have a couple of Rs. 100 crores to be added more to CAPEX. Exactly Rs. 400 may be the number, may be a little lower.

items.statement: Capacity expansion on track for completion by March 2026; plants converted to continuous process yielding augmentation
items.quote: Our plan to expand our production capabilities, which was informed, are on track and we expect this expansion to be completed by March 2026.

items.statement: Prionyl capacity increased; unique green process and economies of scale provide competitive advantage
items.quote: So, Nikhil, we are on track. We have increased the capacity also to answer your very first phase of the question.

items.statement: 70% of business contracted for FY26; demand stable due to FMCG nature; India demand seen growing 8-10% vs global GDP+1-2%
items.quote: So, as we have said on many occasions, about 70% of our business is contracted. So, in terms of looking at this financial year, we already have 70% and more of business contracted.

items.statement: Sustained demand outlook positive; new products target same top 15 F&F customers ensuring wallet share growth
items.quote: In few words, we are extremely positive.

items.statement: US exports only 7% of revenue; tariff impact on margins seen as limited
items.quote: Our export to US is only about 7% of our overall revenue. So, to that extent, know, let us say in case of tariff situation also, we do not really foresee a significant impact on our margins because it's only 7% of our overall revenue.

items.statement: By-product valorisation (Galaxmusk, CST by-products into 1,4-Cineol, 1,8-Cineol, Terpinen-4-ol, Limonene, DDTO) driving margin expansion
items.quote: Basically, as you are aware, a few quarters ago, we had stated that we have been manufacturing certain speciality products from the by-product streams and by-products of some of our products.

items.statement: New products at lab/pilot scale (cyclopentanol from renewable source, flavors for toothpaste) to drive future growth
items.quote: So, one of the key products that we are working on is called as cyclopentanol, which is currently available in the market from petroleum source, we will be making it from renewable source from almost the west.

items.statement: Proposed amalgamation of Privi Fine Sciences and Privi Biotechnologies with Privi Speciality Chemicals to simplify structure and unlock growth
items.quote: We have also proposed a scheme of amalgamation involving Privi Fine Sciences and Privi Biotechnologies and Privi Specialty Chemicals with your Company. This strategic move will simplify our structure and enhance efficiency and unlock new growth opportunities.

items.statement: JV with largest global F&F company in nascent stage; contribution <Rs 100 crore this year; three more expansions planned by partner
items.quote: At the moment, we do face challenges because of, it is a huge, huge project and the turnover ratio is pretty low compared to the size of the investment.

items.statement: Succession plan: grooming 15+ professionals under 40; two attending Harvard; aim to become professionally managed in 3-5 years
items.quote: We have groomed at least 15 new professionals, not 15, existing professionals below the age of 40 right now. In next couple of years, they will be groomed. They have been sent to the best business schools like International School of Hyderabad, IIM Ahmedabad and several others. Two of my colleagues are also going to Harvard for training.

items.statement: Environment clearance applications filed for Phase II/III expansions; parallel processing to maintain 20%+ growth trajectory
items.quote: We have already made applications for the EC, that is environment clearances, etc., wherever it is applicable, because these are new products and that will take some time.

items.statement: Price increases not driver of margin improvement; prices lower vs last year but profitability better due to efficiency gains from continuous plants
items.quote: Lastly, I would also say that the efficiency improvement has been of great use while converting our plants to continuous, which is giving the profitability and not the price increase. Price increase, rather I would say we are lower on price compared to las t year, but yet better profitability, to be honest

items.statement: Utility cost savings from solar power and process efficiencies contributing 100-200 bps to EBITDA margin
items.quote: And we expect to grow on some of the costs on account of the debottlenecking and augmentation and continuous process and some of the savings on the utility cost whether it is the solar power, better efficiencies and all and that is how the EBITDA margins will continue to improve.

items.statement: Supply to top 1-15 global F&F customers; no quality failures in two decades; high dependability drives wallet share
items.quote: And we never had any quality failures, in the last two decades, in fact from the start of the Company. That, all the products that we make, they are also approved by olfactory sensors and we have a team which works on that.

items.statement: Prionyl competitive moat: unique green process, economies of scale at Mahad, best-in-class quality
items.quote: First and foremost, we have a unique process, because it is a green process as compared to what other fellow manufacturers are doing. So, we are unique process in doing that , number one.

items.statement: Capex funding via internal accruals and debt; equity considered expensive; no equity infusion planned
items.quote: It will be a base, a mix of everything. You know, equity is expensive and that is the reason. So, seeing our cash accrual that we are doing and the internal accruals that we are generating, I believe most likely it will happen on a debt and an internal accrual combination.

items.statement: Considering stock split to improve liquidity; promoter sold 3.5-4% stake for personal/family reasons
items.quote: But we will surely look at a split like you suggested, but we are currently, there is a lot of requests come from certain, we also want to consider this maybe in coming times.

items.statement: EcoVadis Platinum rating achieved (top 1% globally) for ESG performance
items.quote: This quarter, we are proud to share that Privi has earned a platinum rating for EcoVadis, placing us in the top 1% globally for ESG performance.

items.statement: Completed QIP in July 2025 raising INR79 crores from institutional investors
items.quote: We successfully completed our maiden QIP in July 2025, raising approximately INR79 crores from marquee institutional investors, including ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, JM Financial Mutual Fund and Bank of India Mutual Fund.

items.statement: QIP funds allocation: INR23 crores debt reduction, INR12 crores solar expansion, INR22 crores recovered carbon black plant, INR19 crores general corporate
items.quote: Deployment of QIP funds has commenced from Q2 FY '26 and will be allocated approximately as follows: INR23 crores towards debt reduction, INR12 crores, I'm sorry, for solar power expansion and INR22 crores for a new plant of recovered carbon black and INR19 crores for general corporate purposes.

items.statement: Incurred INR13 crores capex in Q1 FY26, committed to INR100 crores over 2 years
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, we have incurred capital expenditure of approximately INR13 crores, and we are committed to our plan of approximately INR100 crores of capex over 2 years.

items.statement: Debt reduction from QIP to yield annual interest savings of INR1.5 crores
items.quote: Coming to our cost reduction initiatives, the reduction in debt will lead to annual interest savings of about INR1.5 crores.

items.statement: Expanding renewable energy capacity from 1.26 MW to 4.52 MW, meeting 50% power needs, saving INR3 crores annually
items.quote: We are expanding the existing renewable energy to more than 3x from the current capacity of 1.26 megawatt to 4.52 megawatt. This will lead to total savings of INR3 crores annually and approximately 50% of our power needs will be met through renewable sources.

items.statement: Increased feedstock optionality across TBR, PCR, and off-road tires expected to reduce raw material costs by 10-15%
items.quote: Also, with increased optionality on using different types of tires as feedstock, we expect cost savings of 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Varale plant capacity utilization increased from 30% to 57% YoY, sales grew from INR6 crores to INR27 crores
items.quote: The Varale plant capacity utilization increased from 30% in Q1 FY '25 to 57% in Q1 of FY '26, driving a significant year-on-year sales growth from approximately INR6 crores to INR27 crores.

items.statement: Oman plant operating at 85% capacity utilization, generating $1 million revenue, 35% output sold in GCC
items.quote: In Oman, the plant operat ed at 85% capacity utilization, generating around $1 million in revenue and 35% of our output is now sold within the GCC region.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia land allotment of 20,000 sqm received, targeting commissioning from Q4 2026
items.quote: In Saudi Arabia, we have received allotment of 20,000 square meters of land, and we hope to commence building the facility soon , and we are hoping for commissioning to happen from Q4 of 2026.

items.statement: South Africa JV Phase 1 commenced, consent to export 24,000 tons of end-of-life tires for India and Oman plants
items.quote: Tinna has successfully infused capital into its joint venture, Mbodla Investments in South Africa, where we have received consent to receive and export 24,000 tons of end -of-life tires, whic h will be used as feedstock for our plants in India as well as Oman.

items.statement: Vision 2028: expand from 6 to 10 locations, 25% revenue CAGR to INR1,000 crores by FY28, EBITDA 18%+, ROCE >30%
items.quote: In conclusion, I would like to emphasize that we are firmly on track to achieving our Vision '28, expanding our presence fr om 6 to 10 locations, targeting revenue CAGR of 25% to reach INR1,000 crores of revenue by FY '28 with a targeted EBITDA of 18% plus and ROCE exceeding 30%.

items.statement: Industrial segment revenue grew 15% YoY, steel segment 8% YoY, infrastructure and consumer segments faced temporary slowdown
items.quote: Regarding FY '26 quarter 1 segmental performance, the Industrial and steel segments delivered revenue growth, while the Infrastructure and Consumer segment faced a temporary slowdown. Revenues from the Industrial segment have grown by 15% on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Gross margins improved 344 bps QoQ, EBITDA increased 19% QoQ to INR21 crores at 16% margin, PAT flat at INR12 crores at 9% margin
items.quote: Our gross margins improved by approximately 344 basis points on quarter -on-quarter basis, driven by lower raw material costs, operational efficiency and stronger sales realization. Our EBITDA increased by 19% Q -o-Q basis to INR21 crores and margin stood strong at 16% and improved by 237 basis points on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved from 42 days in FY25 to 38 days in Q1 FY26
items.quote: I'm happy to share that our working capital cycle has improved from 42 days in FY '25 to 38 days in Q1 FY '26, reflecting our unwavering focus on operational efficiency and financial discipline.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR600 crores plus with EBITDA margins at 15% plus
items.quote: We are -- our revenue guidance for FY '26 is INR600 crores plus while maintaining our EBITDA margins at 15% plus.

items.statement: Expect to maintain 15.5% EBITDA margin achieved in Q1 for full FY26
items.quote: Again, we had indicated that we are working towards 15 .5% EBITDA margin, which we have achieved in Q1. I expect for us to maintain this in this financial year.

items.statement: PCMB business reached 100 tons/month sales, targeting INR30-35 crores contribution in FY26, expect 60% utilization by Q3
items.quote: On the PCMB business, while we have now reached a steady state of about 100 tons of sale, but our ambition is far larger than that. We are at early stages of trials, bulk trials, initial supplies with various customers across different sectors. And we are confident that in this financial year, we are expecting approximately INR30 crores to INR35 crores of contribution in our overall top line from

items.statement: Recovered carbon black plant at Varale: 100 TPD feed capacity, INR22 crores from QIP, commissioning end Q4 FY26, expected INR70 crores annual revenue at full capacity
items.quote: The regenerated carbon black plant is being set up inside our existing facilities at Varale, where we already have a passenger car radial recycling plant in the same complex. We expect to begin sales possibly from end of Q4 of this financial year. And in terms of margins achievable, we expect to operate at around 15% to 16% EBITDA margin, very similar to our existing material recycling facilities.

items.statement: Recovered carbon black plant expected to operate at 15-16% EBITDA margin, similar to existing recycling facilities
items.quote: And in terms of margins achievable, we expect to operate at around 15% to 16% EBITDA margin, very similar to our existing material recycling facilities.

items.statement: EPR credits trading at minimum support price of INR2,500/unit, maximum INR8,400/unit; Q1 EPR income INR4 crores vs INR10.5 crores YoY
items.quote: Minimum support p rice is approximately INR2,500 per unit and the maximum price is approximately INR8,400 approximately per unit.

items.statement: End-of-life tire landed costs seeing downward correction; 70% imported, 30% domestic; expect domestic share to rise to 40% in 2-3 years due to EPR
items.quote: See, end-of-life tire landed cost to us, we have created some efficiency in reducing our cost by increasing optionality of different kind of tires we use. But at the moment, we are seeing a bit of a downward correction. So that is where we are at right now.

items.statement: Infrastructure segment weak in Q1 due to early monsoon, delayed fund releases, Iran-Israel conflict disrupting bitumen supply; expect rebound by end of Q2
items.quote: So Q2, at this point of time, it's very difficult. We expect it to be finished off by early September. So the things should come back on the track. That's what we feel on the infrastructure segment side.

items.statement: Consumer segment demand reviving in Q2 as approvals received; road business to recover by end of Q2
items.quote: Q2, and I think this already started picking up because certain application where we were struggling to get approval in the Q1 and that finally are in place. So that already started picking up from Q2 onwards. So you will see some growth in the consumer segment from the Q2 itself.

items.statement: Varale plant expected INR80-90 crores revenue in FY26 at 55-60% utilization; RCB/pyrolysis to add from next fiscal
items.quote: See, this year, we expect it to be around INR80 crores to INR90 crores kind of top line from Varale alone with the existing kind of product portfolio. But going forward, once we see stabilizing our RCB and Pyro, which we are not taking into the account, that will start contributing from the next financial year.

items.statement: No tire manufacturer globally has entered tire recycling; not core competence, limited internal use of recycled rubber (10-15%)
items.quote: We have not seen a ny tire manufacturing company globally, and there are many large international companies, which are even larger than MRF, getting into tire recycling. It is not really their core activity. So for that reason, I don't see that happening in India either.

items.statement: EPR implementation enabling organized domestic tire collection; expect import dependence to reduce from 70% to 60% in 2-3 years
items.quote: I think -- and I'm just guessing here over next -- maybe after 2, 3 years, it could become 60 -40 possibly in favor of domestic. That is possible. So we will see.

items.statement: Raw material cost is primary margin driver; freight and other variables also play role; manufacturing costs stable and predictable
items.quote: Major margin movement for us is on account of raw material cost. Sometimes because freight is a component in it, and it has a few other variables at play as well. As far as manufacturing costs are concerned, it's a fairly stable and predictable cost structure for us.

items.statement: Red Sea disruption normalized, freight rates stable; minimal US exposure so no Trump tariff impact
items.quote: There is no -- see, there is a certain amount of settlement that has happened in the way the trade is being conducted. There is some normalization, I would say. And the whole logistics industry has kind of gotten used to it and settled around it. The freight rates are also stable. So that's what I can tell you. They haven't gone up.

items.statement: Board approved dividend of INR1.60 per share (32% on INR5 par value)
items.quote: I'm glad to announce that Board of Directors has approved a dividend of INR1.60, i.e. 32% on share of INR5 par value that is because of the good performance given by the company.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 throughput 1.29 million TEUs, all-time high for any Q1, up 11.3% YoY
items.quote: Throughput in Q1 of FY '26 has been 1.29 million TEUs, which is all-time high for any Q1 in the company's history. Throughput growth has been excellent, 11.3% in which EXIM's contribution is 12%, and domestic's contribution is 9%.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance unchanged at 13% for FY26 (EXIM 10%, domestic 20%)
items.quote: At this point, I would like to keep the guidance unchanged at 13%, in which EXIM will be 10%, and domestic will be 20%.

items.statement: Rail freight margin improved to 26.96% from 24.36% YoY; operating margin improved to 29.81% from 28.58% YoY
items.quote: Rail freight margin, I'm glad to announce that, despite increase of our market share, we have not sacrificed the rail freight margin and operating margin. Rail freight margin increased from 24.36% to 26.96%. Operating margin increased from 28.58% to 29.81%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex INR202.5 crore; full year capex budget unchanged at INR860 crore
items.quote: Capex achieved in Q1 is INR202.5 crores, and our Capex budget for this financial year remains intact at INR860 crores.

items.statement: Double stack rakes increased 11.2% to 1,505 in Q1 FY26 from 1,353 in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We saw a very handsome increase in double stack rakes, 11.2%. We have done 1,505 rakes this quarter, as compared to 1,353 rakes in last year same quarter.

items.statement: EXIM growth likely to continue; quantum jump expected with WDFC commissioning to JNPT by December 2025
items.quote: I'm glad to announce there is an excellent growth in EXIM stream. It is likely to continue and will further increase. We'll see a quantum jump with commissioning of WDFC up to JNPT by December 2025.

items.statement: Domestic demand robust in Q2 with strong Eastern India gunny bales traffic, new Morbi terminal, and bulk cement in tank containers
items.quote: In domestic, after a muted Q1, now there is a very robust growth we are observing in Q2 with excellent demand from Eastern India, mainly Gunny Bales Traffic, then our new terminal at Morbi, Rafaleshwar in Gujarat also will give boost in business. Than bulk cement in tank containers, which is a new product.

items.statement: Exports growth in auto parts 22%, rice 12%, ready-made garments 14%; imports growth in aluminum scrap 8%, stainless steel 17%
items.quote: Exports growth has been good in auto parts, 22% growth. Rice saw 12% growth, and ready-made garments, 14% growth. Imports, there was a good growth in aluminum scrap, 8%; stainless steel, 17% growth.

items.statement: Engaging with Tata, Jindal, Vedanta, JK Cement, LT Foods for more domestic business
items.quote: I would like to mention again that we are in touch with big corporate houses, Tata, Jindal, Vedanta, JK Cement, LT Foods and they have shown a positive attitude for giving more and more business to CONCOR.

items.statement: Signed MOU with RHS Group Dubai for end-to-end logistics; containers now moving to Dubai, Sharjah, UAE; Singapore service planned
items.quote: We signed an MOU with the RHS Group of Dubai for end-to-end logistics solution. And the containers of CONCOR are now moving across the shores of India. Till now, we were giving service only up to our ports, but now they have crossed the ports and they are reaching Dubai, and we are able to give end-to-end service to our customers.

items.statement: Empty running cost decreased 13.7% YoY, contributing positively to bottom line
items.quote: And one -- another good thing is there has been substantial decline in empty running of flats as well as empty containers, both in domestic and EXIM. Total empty running cost decrease was 13.7%, and which has contributed in a positive manner to our bottom line.

items.statement: Domestic market share fell to 55% from 57.7% YoY due to consciously avoiding low-margin traffic
items.quote: Domestic, actually, we saw a drop in our market share, which was a very big drop. And the reason, as I told in my opening remarks, that low-margin traffic consciously, we have not picked up in domestic.

items.statement: No tariff impact seen on volumes yet; confident in guidance despite global trade uncertainty
items.quote: Till now, we have not seen any impact of the tariffs on our volumes in Q2 also. And as I told you earlier, if one door is closed, there are several other doors which can be opened. India is a very big economy, and it's a very big market. It has got excellent growth prospects. So it cannot be ignored in the world trade.

items.statement: Originating volumes Q1 FY26: EXIM 531,099 TEUs, Domestic 121,624 TEUs, Total 652,723 TEUs
items.quote: Originating volume for EXIM 5,31,099, Domestic 1,21,624. Total 6,52,723.

items.statement: Completed QIP raising INR2,000 crores primary equity capital
items.quote: We successfully completed a Qualified Institutions Placement, raising INR2,000 crores in primary equity capital.

items.statement: Guided 30% AUM growth for FY26 and next 3 years targeting INR50,000 crores by FY2028
items.quote: I think we are quite confident to achieve the 30% growth for the next 3 years by targeting the AUM to be INR50,000 crores by FY 2028 and maintaining our ROAA at 3.5% upward.

items.statement: Guided ROAE 13.5-14% and ROAA not less than 3.5% for FY26
items.quote: So I will say this year, we are confident to deliver RO AE in the range of about 13.5% to 14%. And ROAA will not be less than 3.5

items.statement: Guided ROAA ~4% and ROAE 16-17% for FY27
items.quote: Next year onwards, our strong fee income and coupled with our cost-income ratio further coming down because now operating leverage with scale will kick-in. So then our ROAA will improve to about 4% and ROAE should be in the range of about 16% to 17%.

items.statement: Guided GNPA never above 2% and net NPA never above 1.2%
items.quote: As a company, we have given the guidance that our gross NPA will never cross 2%. Net NPA will never cross 1.2%.

items.statement: Guided credit cost not exceeding 70 bps for FY26
items.quote: Even though on the conservative side, we said this year with the credit cost goes up by 10 basis. It will not cross more than 70 basis for an overall year basis.

items.statement: Guided cost-to-income ratio ~50% for FY26 with 200-250 branch additions
items.quote: I think our cost-to-income ratio on the increased scale of operation; it should come down. However, we are going to add another 200 branches this year. So, we expect this cost-to-income ratio should remain in the range of about 50% for the year.

items.statement: Guided fee income 25-27% of net revenue for FY26
items.quote: Our fee income, we intend to maintain in the range of about 25% to 27% throughout the year.

items.statement: Guided co-lending AUM 18-20% of consolidated AUM for FY26
items.quote: Co-lending AUM, we intend to project in the range of anything between 18% to 20% range. At this range, only we intend to maintain this.

items.statement: Guided overall cost of funds reduction 40-50 bps by end of FY26
items.quote: And by the end of the year, I think our overall cost of the fund should at least come down by 40 to 50 basis points.

items.statement: Guided 200-250 branch additions in FY26, 700-800 over 3 years
items.quote: we are going to add 200 - 250 branches this year, a combination o f the gold, MSME, home loan, etcetera. And this pace will remain for next year. We are going to add about 700 to 800 branches in 3 years

items.statement: Guided AUM mix: gold 37-40%, MSME 20-22%, housing 20-22%, construction finance 17-18%
items.quote: So gold should be in the range of about 37% to 40% kind. MSME will remain in the range of about 20%-22%. Housing will remain in about 20%-22%. Construction finance will remain in the range of about 17%-18%.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM INR24,754 crores, up 42% YoY as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: As of June 30, 2025, our consolidated AUM stood at INR24,754 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of about 42%.

items.statement: Disbursements INR8,458 crores, up 51% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Disbursement for the quarter grew 51% year-on-year to INR8,458 crores, supported by expanding distribution reach improving customer on-boarding.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM INR9,105 crores, up 69% YoY with 821 specialized branches
items.quote: Our gold loan business maintained strong momentum in quarter 1 FY '26 with AUM rising 69% year-on-year to INR9,105 crores. The portfolio is supported by 821 specialized branches with average AUM per branch at INR11.1 crores.

items.statement: MSME AUM INR5,477 crores, up 14% YoY; Housing AUM INR5,490 crores, up 32% YoY
items.quote: MSME loan grew to reach INR5,477 crores, while our housing finance portfolio stood at INR5,490 crores, translating to robust year-on-year growth of about 14% and 32%, respectively.

items.statement: Construction finance AUM INR4,521 crores, up 61% YoY funding 280 active projects
items.quote: Our construction finance portfolio grew 61% year-on-year to INR4,521 crores, now funding our 280 active residential projects with an average sanction ticket size of INR41 crores.

items.statement: Co-lending AUM INR4,681 crores, up 64% YoY, 18.9% of consolidated AUM
items.quote: Co-lending AUM reached about INR4,681 crores, up by 64% year-on-year and contributing 18.9% of consolidated AUM versus 17.8% in Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Yield on net advances 16.9%, spread 7.2% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our yields and spreads on net advances remained healthy in the quarter at 16.9% and 7.2%.

items.statement: Net interest income INR416 crores, up 38% YoY; non-interest income INR166 crores, up 53% YoY, 28.5% of net total income
items.quote: Our net interest income for Q1 FY '26 reached at INR416 crores, marking a 38% year-on-year increase, driven by a robust growth in our loan book. We continue to strengthen our non-interest income streams in Q1 FY '26, reinforcing our strategy of building a diversified and resilient earnings profile. Non-interest income grew 53% year-on-year to INR166 crores, contributing 28.5% of net total income f

items.statement: Intends to maintain spread ~7%, gold loan mix improvement to add 3-4% to composition
items.quote: I think our current spread is in the range of about 7%. We intend to maintain that spread 7%. It can slightly be better because gold loan composition is slightly improving, it will add another 3% to 4% to current composition and which is a high-yield product.

items.statement: Collection efficiency ~97%+ in MSME; 520-person collection team with analytics and automation
items.quote: Currently, our collection efficiency in the range of about 97% upward in the segment. So, we are quite confident that our focus will be to resolve the old NPA faster by doing a lot of settlement and other things.

items.statement: MSME slippages seen in Madhya Pradesh; turning down disbursements there and progressing cautiously
items.quote: As regards to the other segment, we agree that MSME, we have seen some slippage, more particularly from a state of Madhya Pradesh, where we are already turning down our disbursements and we are progressing cautiously on that.

items.statement: One construction finance account INR16 crores slipped to NPA, INR8 crores provision created; INR7 crores write-back from recoveries
items.quote: So, there's one account which has slipped into the NPA. And on account of that, the value of that account was INR16 crores, INR8 crores provisions have been provided for. But already for that account, if you see the last quarter, the recovery has also happened on account of one of the NPA about INR7 crores.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost down 20-25 bps; rating upgrade may add another 25 bps reduction; MCLR reset benefit 30-40 bps over year
items.quote: Incremental borrowing already started coming down by 20 to 25 basis, hoping that we will get some rating update. That will further go down by another 25 basis. Second point is that all the MCLR rates are getting reset on the due date of their 1 year and 6 month if the negotiation done during the time of drawing that loan. So, in that manner, those banks, MCLR, rate reduction benefit will accrue. S

items.statement: Raised INR150 crores NCDs at 9-9.25%; Board approved public NCD issuance up to INR1,000 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully raised INR150 crores of NCDs at competitive rates between 9% to 9.25%. Our Board has also approved a public NCD issuance up to INR1,000 crores, which we plan to tap opportunistically.

items.statement: Branch network 1,138 locations, net addition of 27 branches in Q1 FY26; employee base 11,546
items.quote: Our branch network expanded to 1,138 locations in Q1 FY '26 with a net addition of 27 branches while our employee base remained steady at 11,546.

items.statement: Gold loan expansion into Southern India (Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Telangana, Karnataka, Odisha) in H2 FY26
items.quote: think we are going to add second half of the year, Southern India market, which will be Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Karnataka and Odisha also, we are going to add as far as the gold loan is concerned. So these states we are good, Andhra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Odisha.
