items.statement: Credit rating upgrade exercise ongoing; results expected by mid-September
items.quote: That exercise is on. Exercise is on. We should see the results by mid of September.

items.statement: Incorporated two new companies: investment banking for debt capital markets and securities for bond distribution/platform; cost neutral, accretive from year 1
items.quote: There are two companies we have incorporated. One is going to carry out the investment banking activities only for the debt capital market. And another company is a securities company, which is going to engage in the sales and distribution of the debt placement at institutional level, online bond platform and exchange trading. Both of these will not consume much capital, and they will be from the

items.statement: Intense competition in collateralized segments; differentiation via technology, turnaround time, seamless journey
items.quote: So I think, in all our segments which are collateralized, if you talk about competition, it is a very intense competitive. Your right to win has to be how you use your technology automation and ability to turn around the sanction faster and do a better customer service in terms of how you handle them, how seamless your journey is, how less the paperwork you seek without compromising on the asset q

items.statement: Micro LAP legal recourse via bilateral negotiation (<1 year) or Section 138/arbitration (2-2.5 years) as ticket size ~10 lakh not SARFAESI eligible
items.quote: major effort is by negotiation, we make borrower to agree to come forward and sell his property or find inner ecosystem to give him the money so that we need not to sell the property at much discounted rate. And another option is Section 138 to build the pressure and initiate the arbitration proceedings. And within that, these tools are effective. The combination of bilateral negotiation or using

items.statement: Target around 25% revenue growth in FY26 with high single-digit volume growth base case and double-digit volume growth in some quarters
items.quote: Supported by pricing growth, we will target around 25% revenue growth this year.

items.statement: Expect double-digit profit CAGR over next two years despite challenging double-digit EBITDA growth in FY26
items.quote: We are fairly confident of delivering double-digit profit CAGR over the next two years.

items.statement: Digital-first portfolio on track to reach 2.5x FY24 ARR by FY27 with double-digit EBITDA margins by FY27
items.quote: Given this trajectory, we are on track to reach 2.5x of FY24 ARR by FY27. We continue to operate with a keen eye on the profitability and are striving to deliver double-digit EBITDA margins in this portfolio by FY27.

items.statement: Stable to improving demand trends in India across urban and rural with premium categories outperforming mass segments
items.quote: During the quarter, we witnessed stable to improving demand trends in India across urban and rural. Premium categories continued to outperform the mass segments.

items.statement: Optical margins may be suppressed due to pricing-led denominator effect but structural margins intact; profit growth expected to accelerate in deflationary period
items.quote: While the pricing-led denominator effect may suppress optical margins this year, we are not alarmed by the optical drop in operating margins and firmly believe this is a temporary hiatus and not a structural concern.

items.statement: Digital-first portfolio ARR exited Q1 FY26 at over ₹850 crores scaling ahead of earlier targets
items.quote: The Digital-first portfolio, comprising Beardo, Just Herbs and the Personal Care portfolio of Plix, exited the quarter with an ARR of over ₹ 850 crores, scaling up well ahead of our earlier targets.

items.statement: Project SETU direct distribution expansion ongoing with 0.5 million outlets targeted over three years; impact visible in rural and mid-premium VAHO
items.quote: Over a three year period adding 0.5 million set of outlets, invariably it is the second or third brand that goes into the range selling.

items.statement: Insourced hero SKUs for Beardo into own manufacturing delivering 500-600 bps gross margin improvement
items.quote: For example, in Beardo, when we insourced one or two of the hero SKUs into our own manufacturing system, we straightaway got a 500 bps to 600 bps improvement in gross margin.

items.statement: Parachute effective price increase of 60%+ YoY via price hikes and ml-age reductions; additional 30% price increase taken in Q1 FY26 with no further hikes intended
items.quote: Parachute has exhibited minimal volume impact and consolidated its market share, underscoring its inherent strength in terms of price inelasticity and deep consumer trust, despite multiple rounds of price increases and ml-age reductions amounting to an effective price increase of 60% plus.

items.statement: Copra prices corrected 10-12% from July peak; no further pricing action expected given recent trends
items.quote: The prices level went up in Quarter 1, it went up further in July and now we are seeing about 10% to 12% correction from the peak that we had seen in July. And again, to sort of bring it back to the point which Saugata had mentioned earlier, we do not see any further pricing action at least given the recent trends that we have seen in the copra prices.

items.statement: Foods portfolio targeting 25%+ growth in FY26 with core Saffola growing double-digits; True Elements and Plix sustaining accelerated growth
items.quote: We remain on track to deliver over 25% growth this year and over the medium-term, while steadily improving profitability.

items.statement: Alternate channels (Modern Trade, E-commerce, Quick Commerce) leading growth; General Trade returned to growth after focused initiatives and Project SETU progress
items.quote: Alternate channels like Modern Trade, E-commerce and especially Quick Commerce continued to lead growth. While General Trade also moved into growth after some quarters as a result of focused initiatives, improved execution, and the ongoing progress of Project SETU.

items.statement: Smaller players and unreasonable competitors more impacted by copra inflation; Marico gaining share from organized players in VAHO and coconut oil
items.quote: Yes, the smaller players and other smaller branded players will be far more impacted.

items.statement: Copra import banned; can only import to extent of exports; no wide-scale pest damage to crop per industry body
items.quote: No, we cannot import either copra or oil. We can only import to the extent what we can export.

items.statement: International business delivered high-teen constant currency growth; MENA accelerated with 42% CCG driven by core share gains and NPD; Bangladesh robust; Vietnam muted with recovery expected; South Africa static but full-year double-digit t
items.quote: Moving to our international business , w e recorded high -teen constant currency growth, maintaining a stellar momentum

items.statement: Prudent inventory management and supply chain control providing competitive edge during copra inflation
items.quote: The scale of our operations, coupled with resilient back-end capabilities and prudent inventory management, continues to reinforce a competitive edge.

items.statement: Dependence on Parachute and Saffola for profits reduced by ~1,000 bps over last few years lowering vulnerability to copra and edible oil prices
items.quote: Just to share a number, the dependence on Parachute and Saffola for profits has gone down by approximately 1,000 basis points over the last few years.

items.statement: One or two acquisition spaces available in Foods or Personal Care adjacencies; track record good with playbook ready; see themselves as strategic investor of choice
items.quote: There are one or two spaces which I think are still available. See, we are clearly going into not only market attractiveness but a right-to-win which are adjacencies.

items.statement: Senior leadership collective experience 140+ years with average tenure 8-10 years; Gen Next leadership in place; CEO India Core and CFO with 20+ years each at Marico
items.quote: What continues to anchor us through these cycles is a resilient and experienced senior leadership team with collective experience of over 140 years in Marico and an average leadership tenure of eight to ten years.

items.statement: India underlying volume growth nearing double-digits; 99% of business gaining or sustaining market share; over 80% of business sustaining or improving penetration
items.quote: We have continued to deliver a sequential uptick in underlying volume growth in India, which is nearing double-digits, backed by improving traction in the core aided by GT improvement and sustained momentum in our new businesses.

items.statement: Copra inflation driven by 9% productivity drop, unseasonal rains delaying conversion, and speculative activity; unsustainable current prices expected to settle over fiscal year with good monsoon
items.quote: We understand that the unprecedented levels of inflation in this particular cycle has been due to the supply-demand gap created by a combination of drop in crop yields due to an uneven weather pattern in the first half of 2024 and speculative activities.

items.statement: Aspiration to reach ₹15,000 crores revenue in two years and ₹20,000 crores in five years from current ₹10,000 crores base
items.quote: There is a very fair chance that we could touch ₹15,000 Crores over the next two years. Therefore, we also believe that the ₹10,000 Crores to ₹20,000 Crores leap can be achieved within the next five years if we continue to maintain this momentum.

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 7-9% from previous 8-12% due to challenging US consumer sentiment
items.quote: In light of this, we are taking a cautious approach and guiding to achieve revenue growth of 7% to 9% for FY '26.

items.statement: Mid-teens revenue growth targeted for FY27 onwards assuming macro environment stabilizes
items.quote: For the periods further ahead, we continue to project mid -teens revenue growth, supported by strong operating leverage and our investment into digital marketing.

items.statement: Gross margin held steady at 63.8% in Q1 FY26, within target range of 60%+
items.quote: Our gross margin held steady at 63.8%, which is reassuring given the macro volatilities.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 50 bps YoY to 9.2% driven by employee cost savings, logistics efficiencies and airtime operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved by 50 basis points year -over-year to 9.2%. The improvement was driven by saving in employee cost through headcount rationalization, improvement in efficiencies.

items.statement: Germany gross margin improved from 63% to 68% due to product mix and planning strategy changes
items.quote: Germany, we have changed our product mix and offering and planning strategy in presentation that helped to the gross margin improvement from earlier level of 63% to 68% in Germany.

items.statement: US consumer sentiment deteriorated in June due to Iran strike and tariff uncertainty, leading to downtrading to lower price points
items.quote: We are seeing lipstick effect already in U.S. What do I mean by that? The lower price point, slouchy jewellery is selling more right now.

items.statement: UK consumer confidence fell sharply in April before recovering in June; TJC business impacted by leadership transition
items.quote: Consumer confidence had fallen sharply in April before recovering in June. TJC also went through recent leadership transition, which caused some initial disruption.

items.statement: Germany consumer demand affected by macro challenges early in quarter; tax and interest rate cuts provided partial support
items.quote: Consumer demand was affected by macro challenges, including weaker sentiment early in the quarter. While tax and interest rate cuts supported spending to some extent, these tailwinds were not sufficient to fully offset the broader pressure on discretionary demand.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 14% YoY to INR329 crores, now 43% of B2C sales; on track for 50% by FY27
items.quote: Digital revenue grew strongly by 14% to INR329 crores. This momentum reflects our continued investment in strengthening omni -channel capabilities. Digital now contributes 43% of overall revenue, and we remain firmly on course of reaching 50% by FY '27.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond jewellery scaled to 11% of group sales in Q1 FY26 from 1% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We are pleased with the successful scale -up of our lab -grown diamond jewellery portfolio, which contributes to 11% of group's overall sales in Q1, up from 1% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Lifestyle products now 36% of B2C revenue with medium-term goal of 50%
items.quote: Lifestyle products continue to scale well, now forming 36% of B2C revenue, with a medium-term goal of reaching 50%.

items.statement: Budget Pay option accounts for 39% of total retail revenue
items.quote: Our Budget Pay option remained popular, accounting of 39% of our total retail revenue.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at $3-5 million for routine upgrades; FY27 may be $5-7 million due to UK operations consolidation
items.quote: FY '26, we haven't planned any major capex. It is a routine major capex upgradation of our softwares and the tangible goods, which is around 3 million to 5 million. But FY '27 may be slightly higher as we are consolidating our UK operation in one place. So around 2 million, 3 million higher in FY '27. So we expect 5 million to 7 million capex overall in the business.

items.statement: TV network reaches 127 million households; unique customer base at 713,000 (up 12% YoY); new customer acquisition 400,000 in Q1; retention rate improved to 42%
items.quote: In Q1, our TV network reached 127 million households. As of 30th June 2025, our unique customer base stands at 7 ,13,000, which is up 12% Y -o-Y and the highest ever for VGL Group. New customer acquisition stands at 400,000 in Q1, while retention rate improved to 42%.

items.statement: Proactively shipped advanced inventory to US ahead of 25% tariff announcement; multi-country sourcing agility to redirect India manufacturing to UK/Germany and source US from Thailand, China, Indonesia, Europe
items.quote: Leveraging this model, we have proactively shipped advanced inventory ahead of the tariff announcements, ensuring that we are fairly well stocked for the coming few months. We remain optimistic about a potential reduction or rationalization of tariffs in the future.

items.statement: US tariff impact: 25% on top of existing tariffs (jewellery 5.7% becomes 32.7% from India); different rates by country (Indonesia 19%+5.7%, Thailand 20%+5.7%, Europe 15%+5.7%)
items.quote: Yes. So 25% is on the top of existing tariffs for a different category. For example, jewellery was 5.7%, plus 25%, it will become 32.7% from India ; from Indonesia is 19% plus 5.7% ; Thailand is 20%, plus 5.7%. So different countries have different tariffs. Europe will be 15% plus 5.7%.

items.statement: India-UK FTA to reduce jewellery duty from 3-5% to 0% and lifestyle from 7-15% to 0% around mid-next year
items.quote: Right now, currently, jewellery we import from India. It is contributing 3% to 5% duty and the lifestyle product 7% to 15% duty. So maybe around mid of the next year, it will reflect in terms of the duty cha nging to zero.

items.statement: Working capital cycle extended to 80 days from ~60 days due to strategic US inventory build-up and higher Budget Pay financing demand
items.quote: Major investment is done through our inventory and the recently added up inventory in U.S. increased the working capital days cycle. Also that the recent days, the customer demands towards the budget programming financing option is more prominent.

items.statement: Working capital days expected to improve from current 80 days but not return to 40-50 day levels
items.quote: We expect that it will be slowed down to improve the cash in the business. But not significantly as you have seen in March '21 was 40, 50 days. It will not be bring down to that level, but lower than the current levels.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR174 crores; ICRA upgraded both short- and long-term credit ratings
items.quote: We reported INR22 crores in operating cash flow and INR15 crores in free cash flow with a net cash position of INR174 crores and consistent dividend payouts. Our balance sheet remains strong and resilient. Further, the recent upgrade in both short - and long -term credit rating by ICRA reflects our consistent performance, strong liquidity and prudent capital management.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; strong balance sheet with net cash position
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong and resilient. Further, the recent upgrade in both short - and long -term credit rating by ICRA reflects our consistent performance, strong liquidity and prudent capital management.

items.statement: No active acquisition targets currently; happy with Mindful Souls and Ideal World integrations; open to opportunities if they arise
items.quote: We don't have any other active target that we are looking at right now, but we are always open for possibility. If there's any opportunity comes, we'll look at it.

items.statement: Board recommended first interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity share implying 66% payout ratio
items.quote: The Board has recommended a first interim dividend of INR1.5 per equity share, which implies 66% payout ratio.

items.statement: Germany received Great Place to Work certification; VGL now globally certified; Asia call center attrition reduced from 15% to 1% monthly through talent density and career path initiatives
items.quote: Further, Germany has received the Great Place to Work ® certification. And with this, VGL is now a globally Great Place to Work ® certified group.

items.statement: ROCE 19% and ROE 12% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Return metrics remain healthier, ROCE 19% and ROE 12%.

items.statement: Near-term challenges from US tariff uncertainty and weak consumer sentiment; potential upside if macro improves
items.quote: Current macroeconomic environment and recent tariff development presents near -term challenge, especially in consumer sentiments. In light of this, we are taking a cautious approach and guiding to achieve revenue growth of 7% to 9% for FY '26.

items.statement: Generated 1.4 million kWh solar energy meeting 100% manufacturing power needs; rainwater harvesting capacity 10,000 kiloliters; targeting carbon neutrality Scope 1&2 by 2031
items.quote: On the clean energy front, we generated 1.4 million kilowatt hours of solar energy this quarter, meeting 100% of power needs of our manufacturing units. These steps brings us closer to our target of achieving carbon neutrality in Scope 1 and 2 emission by 2031.

items.statement: Target quarterly fiber home passes run rate of 2.5 million, up from 1.6 million
items.quote: I want to get to a quarterly run rate of 2.5 million home pass es up from 1.6 million

items.statement: Radio capex trending down; transport and fiber capex continue; Cloud capex modular with two live regions and headroom
items.quote: You are right in the assumption that radio capex generally is trending down but at the same time, when you look at transport capex, the investments that are going in fiber, on our core networks, they continue.

items.statement: Home segment capex primarily for CPEs (wired and FWA) and dedicated homes fiber rollout
items.quote: This is primarily towards CPEs both wired as well as wireless, FWAs and the fiber rollout.

items.statement: Airtel Business underlying revenue grew 2% sequentially after discontinuing low-margin commoditized business; strong funnel and order book visibility
items.quote: If you look at the underlying revenue growth stripped off the discontinued commoditized business, we grew at 2% sequentially and the business outlook continues to be strong, with a strong visibility on funnel and the order book.

items.statement: India EBITDAaL margin 51.4%, up 65 bps sequentially; Africa EBITDAaL margin just under 37%
items.quote: India revenues excluding Indus, came in at about 33,820 Crores and EBITDAaL, which is stripped off the lease obligations, margins came in at 51.4%, improving by 65 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Airtel Business connectivity and IoT margins very good; Cloud margins very good but require modular capex; security margins low; wholesale messaging margins under pressure
items.quote: Margins here are very good, in fact, better than what we report as the overall margin for the business because this is what we manufacture ourselves.

items.statement: Mobile added 1.2M customers and 3.9M smartphone data customers; postpaid net adds 0.7M (57% of total); broadband highest ever quarterly net adds 939K including 540K FWA
items.quote: In the broadband business, we delivered a solid quarter, with the highest ever quarterly net ad ds of 939,000. We are seeing strong momentum in FWA net ad ds of 5.4

items.statement: 5G customers reached 152M; 5G sites carry 36% of network traffic; 5G smartphone shipments 86% of total
items.quote: We ended the quarter with 152 million 5G customers. We continue to believe that 5G handset adoption at the bottom end of the market will acce lerate with the launch of more affordable options

items.statement: ARPU Rs 250 benefited from one extra day and mix improvement; feature phone to smartphone upgrades, prepaid to postpaid, data monetization, international roaming drive ARPU growth absent tariff repair
items.quote: ARPU at Rs.250 had the benefit of one day extra in the quarter and continued underlying mix improvement.

items.statement: Launched industry-first all-in-one OTT entertainment pack with 25+ platforms for prepaid; Google One 100GB cloud storage free for 6 months for postpaid and Wi-Fi customers
items.quote: We have further strengthened our entertainment experience for our prepaid cus tomers by launching an industry first all -in-one OTT entertainment pack, with access to over 25 OTT platforms

items.statement: Airtel Cloud launched with two live regions (Delhi, Chennai), third planned; homegrown stack handles 250 PB data, 10K+ servers, 14 large and 120 edge data centers; software platform Xtelify extended to Singtel, Globe Telecom, Airtel Africa,
items.quote: We have launched Airtel Cloud and we believe this will allow our customers to get access to a world-class Cloud, which is telco grade, hosted and held in India and it will additionally save them costs.

items.statement: Airtel Payments Bank monthly transacting users 98M; annualized revenue run rate over Rs 3,100 Cr (+27% YoY); deposits Rs 3,750 Cr (+29% YoY)
items.quote: Our payments bank monthly transacting users stood at 98 million. Annualized revenue run rate is now over 3,100 Crores, growing over 27% year-on-year.

items.statement: Africa constant currency revenue growth 6.7% sequentially; reported revenue growth 6.2%; EBITDAaL Rs 4,456 Cr; net debt/EBITDAaL under 1x
items.quote: Constant currency revenue growth continues to remain strong at 6.7% sequentially and this was also helped by a favorable currency movement, which led to a solid reported revenue growth of 6.2% sequentially.

items.statement: Redeemed $1B senior notes in quarter; India net debt/EBITDAaL 1.3x; Crisil credit rating upgrade received
items.quote: During the quarter, we redeemed senior notes worth a billion dollars. Disciplined capex spending and operational excellence underpins our solid balance sheet. India net debt to EBITDAaL now stands at 1.3.

items.statement: Dividends will increase as leverage goes down; free cash flow generation strong; actively evaluating M&A in Cloud, security, data centers
items.quote: We have always maintained that our dividends will increase, our leverage goes down and we will continue to look for opportunities to grow our business in market around the adjacencies that we are operating in.

items.statement: AGR payments start March 2025; wrote to government seeking same relief as other telcos; will abide by government decision; have room to make required payments
items.quote: On the AGR payments, we have written to the government, as you know, to be extended the same relief as any other telco and that is a decision that the government has to take, we will abide by whatever decision they take.

items.statement: Deployed 1,830 network sites and 8,300 km fiber in quarter; 130,000 km fiber rolled out in last 3 years; 43,500 rural sites deployed in last 3 years; FWA across 2,500 cities
items.quote: Network expansion is happening as planned , with about 1830 network sites and over 8300 kil ometers of fiber deployed during the quarter

items.statement: Submarine cable capacity to increase from 45 Tbps to 180 Tbps; invested over Rs 2,000 Cr in last 5 years; OPGW connecting all metros and major cities; data center and cable landing station links in Mumbai and Chennai
items.quote: On the submarine cables and capacities, we have invested over 2000 Crores over the last five years and we expect a further light up from 45 Tbps capacity to 180 Tbps capacity.

items.statement: Postpaid base only 7-7.5% of total; 90M credit-approved users could migrate to postpaid; 70-75M feature phones on network ready to upgrade to smartphone
items.quote: we have got 90 million credit approv ed users who could be on postpaid and then feature phones, you still have 70-75 million feature phones on our network that are ready to upgrade to smartphone

items.statement: B2B connectivity market 4-5 players; messaging has many aggregators; Cloud has public cloud and domestic players; IoT mainly telcos; security crowded but needs credibility and trust
items.quote: I think in connectivity, you have the big players. You also have some of the newer players coming in, but that market is maybe four-five players.

items.statement: UBR (Wi-Fi band fixed wireless) faces high interference in dense urban areas leading to high churn and poor experience; will not deploy in dense areas; fiber preferred for home connectivity
items.quote: One of the challenges particularly in dense urban areas is there is a very high degree of interference and that happens in the Wi-Fi band so even if you have interference mitigating solutions, you end up with high churn and you end up with poor experience.

items.statement: Women 19% of workforce (up from 11% two years ago); remote work program enables women in smaller towns to take tech roles; Airtel Scholarship 51% women recipients
items.quote: Women represent just under 19% of our total workforce up from 11% two years ago. Our remote work programme has also enabled qualified women in smaller towns to take on tech roles.

items.statement: Anti-spam solution identified over 42 billion spam calls since launch; detects scam/spam across SMS, OTT, calls from India or abroad in real time in local language; added malicious website blocking across OTT apps, emails, browsers
items.quote: Since its launch, the solution has identified over 42 billion spam calls.

items.statement: AI being placed at heart of all digital platforms; Perplexity partnership for AI capabilities seeing strong engagement with 5M+ users and growing daily
items.quote: We are seeing strong customer engagement within a few days of the launch and have already climbed to over 5 million and growing every day.

items.statement: Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex) Rs 11,928 Cr in quarter
items.quote: The operating free cash flow, which is EBITDAaL minus capex, was at 11,928 Crores.

items.statement: Actively evaluating M&A opportunities in Cloud, security, data centers; nothing to report yet but active work behind scenes
items.quote: There is nothing to report as of now but those are active, sort of, work that is going on behind the scenes to identify opportunities.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of INR10,000 crores with INR3,000 crores from defense and INR7,000 crores from non-defense
items.quote: If you look at our annual guidance of INR10,000 crores, so we are still believing that we will definitely cross INR10,000 crores in this financial year. And out of that, INR3,000 crores should be some defense and nondefense should add to around INR7,000 crores.

items.statement: International revenue expected at INR3,500-4,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: So in this year, if we have given a guidance of around INR10,000 crores, so we are expecting around INR4,000 crores from international market, INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Targeting 15% domestic explosives volume growth for FY26
items.quote: So like we said that we are targeting around 15% volume growth in this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target around 27% for FY26 despite higher staff costs and depreciation
items.quote: So these factors, if you take into the account the achieving margin of around 27% is a reasonable expectation from our side.

items.statement: Total defense order book of INR15,000 crores with INR8,000 crores from international markets
items.quote: Like we have already shared that we have a total order book of around INR15,000 crores. And after leaving the Pinaka portion, the order book from international is around INR8,000 crores.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR2,500 crores for FY26 with continued expansion in coming years
items.quote: We have shared in our annual call that we are going to invest INR2,500 crores in this financial year. And in the coming years also, we have a strong strategic program to expand our facilities.

items.statement: Kazakhstan plant expected to start commercial production by October 2025
items.quote: Yes, we are trying to start our Kazakhstan plant in this financial year. Hopefully, by October, we should start the plant.

items.statement: Domestic explosives demand impacted by early monsoon and milder heat waves; recovery expected post-monsoon

items.quote: Sir, if I talk about solar pumps, then indirectly, it will be around 50-50 percentage approximately. It can be 4% - 5% plus or minus on any side. So, broadly speaking, solar pumping around 50% and non-solar pump around 50%.

items.statement: Management unable to identify significant negative factors despite acknowledging business cycles

items.statement: Targets 30-40% year-on-year revenue growth for FY26, driven by IPO proceeds deployment from Q2
items.quote: What we meant was because of the IPO proceeds coming in, debt repayment and unlocking more capital for growth, we will be able to achieve the guidance that we have given, which is about 30% to 40% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Targets ~40% revenue growth for FY26, with focus on sustaining EBITDA and PAT margins and working capital cycle
items.quote: We will be somewhere around 40% to be honest. That is something that we are consciously targeting.

items.statement: Expects monthly rolling demand to reach Rs 90-100 crore in coming months from current Rs 60-70 crore
items.quote: the guidance that I had given before was to reach about a rolling demand of about Rs. 90 crores to Rs. 100 crores on a monthly basis in the coming few months.

items.statement: Expects net working capital days to improve to 85-90 days range over coming quarters from current 97 days
items.quote: we remain focused and confident of bringing it further down to 85 to 90 days range over the coming quarters and sustaining it as we scale.

items.statement: Expects annualized PAT of Rs 30-32 crore before IPO proceeds benefit and interest savings

items.statement: Expects PAT margin of 4-6% for FY26 (before minority interest)
items.quote: So, yes, fair to assume that we will be somewhere around maybe about 4% to 6% of PAT, but that is just the future guidance that we can give.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to sustain at 9%+ as company scales
items.quote: We will look to sustain that number as we grow. And if we are able to do that, I think we will be generating substantial returns in terms of for our shareholders.

items.statement: Expects operating leverage to improve EBITDA margin by 1.5-2% over next 18-24 months as CAPEX as % of revenue declines
items.quote: We will definitely see an improvement of maybe about 1.5% to 2% as we grow in the next maybe 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Expects quarterly interest cost of Rs 1.5-2 crore going forward (mainly lease accounting)
items.quote: On a quarterly basis, primarily interest will be by way of building accounting. And that should be between Rs. 1.5 crores to Rs. 2 crores a quarter.

items.statement: BuildMex subsidiary targeting Rs 8-10 crore monthly revenue by July, annualizing to ~Rs 120 crore
items.quote: based on the capacity that I am talking about, it should be somewhere around July would be close to about Rs. 8 crores to Rs. 10 crores monthly business. So, an annualized business is about Rs. 120 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin reached 9.2%, up from prior periods, driven by services vertical and scale efficiencies
items.quote: EBITDA margins: As I mentioned to you, went beyond 9% to 9.2%, reflecting operational leverage and the structural advantage of our integration model.

items.statement: Services vertical growing in relevance and profitability, moving beyond transactional supply into higher-margin project involvement
items.quote: A key driver of this important improvement is our services vertical, which continues to grow in both relevance and profitability.

items.statement: Announced Rs 300 crore facility with House of W and Rs 400-450 crore of recent contracts and order wins
items.quote: You must have also heard our announcement about Rs. 300 crore facility that we have been able to bag with the House of W.

items.statement: Current monthly rolling demand at Rs 60-70 crore, targeting Rs 90-100 crore in coming months
items.quote: our rolling demand is close to about Rs. 60 crores to Rs. 70 crores a month.

items.statement: Consciously staying asset-light, scaling through contract manufacturing and strategic partnerships instead of CAPEX-heavy assets

items.statement: Net working capital cycle improved from 120 days to 97 days over last 12 months (120 in Dec, 110 in Mar, 97 in Jun)

items.statement: Became net debt-free as of Q1 FY26 (gross debt Rs 113 crore, cash Rs 377 crore), repaid ~Rs 200-240 crore debt
items.quote: We have become completely debt-free by way of net debt is zero as of today.

items.quote: So, as of now, more than 6 months would be approximately Rs. 65 crores to Rs. 70 crores.

items.quote: In a broader view, I am targeting INR300 crores to INR350 crores in between that.

items.quote: If I talk mainly about the last financial year, if we see, we can expect a similar growth vis-a-vis, and I'm sure that would be quite visible to you once you immediately, if you sit down and note down the numbers.

items.quote: We do not have any plans of increasing our fleets heavily. But definitely, see, as and when the business grows, the requirements do come up quite often. And we always try that, whenever we have got an order and whenever we have got a business expansion.

items.quote: See, if -- when I talk about owned, so there is zero owned warehouse, all of them are leased. Why we choose leasing is basicall y I'll tell you normal mindset of people, just to check what will happen if you do this

items.quote: But when you come to Pranik, we have a basket wherein we do warehousing, we do logistics, first mile, middle mile, as well as last mile. Now, last mile is where the criticality comes in, including reverse logistics into our kitty.

items.quote: Definitely, these policies are helping. What it is that when the logistics corridor being made to, you have got time-saving. So the turnaround time of your vehicle increases, which gives you a cost advantage.

items.statement: Debtor days approximately 90 days
items.quote: Data days is, see, I do not have the exact data that I can give you the answer right now, but it's close to 90 days.

items.statement: Client retention rate over 95%; on-time delivery rate over 95%

We operate with a highly scalable and capital-efficient asset-light model, enabled by technology, disciplined execution, and strategic partnerships. Over 95% plus on-time delivery rate.

items.statement: Seasonality managed via pan-India presence across diverse sectors (pharma, auto, retail, FMCG, electronics, e-commerce) ensuring some region/sector always in peak

items.quote: So, going forward, once we think that yes, we are into that position again, we, the management, depending on the planning, they might plan for a second round of fundraising basically towards working capital.

items.quote: Like example, now in Calcutta is the puja season that we are almost entering. So in this season, there is going to be a huge demand. Further, we talk about there will be in the summer season, because there is a huge demand of ACs and refrigerators.

items.quote: this quarter -- last quarter, we've seen -- our commodity prices went up by 0.5%. I think looking forward, we believe that it will be range bound. And with our LEAP program, right, the cost saving program we have, we are confident of neutralizing the impact of that.

items.quote: Looking ahead, while there are ongoing geopolitical and supply uncertainties, as you have heard from the team, we stay confident owing to product launches, the Entry, 125cc impetus, style and technology product, scooter growth, the Xoom 125 and premium launches as well as VIDA variants that will come up.

items.quote: Starting September '25, they will start releasing the funds. This year, they have not released anything so far. But end of September, they will start releasing as per the agreed schedule.

items.quote: INR350 crores we are expecting. Neerad Sharma: It is there in the segmental results

items.quote: We have made reasonably good progress on the installation of these smart meters. We have already installed close to three orders close to 15 lakh meters.

items.quote: So as far as the GMLR tunnel project is concerned, we have received all the clearances. Only we are just waiting for the tree cutting permissions, which is expected very shortly.

items.quote: We do not see any problem in terms of availability of the labour for executing these projects.

items.quote: Generally, the execution in Q2 because of the monsoon, we even expect to do moderately. So that is going to be there.

items.quote: Right now, not. We are expecting the payments to come. As usual, as we discussed earlier also, the payments from Telangana government was a little slower. But otherwise, rest of the places, we are not facing any serious issues.

items.quote: It's likely to remain same. And probably, we are also having discussions with the bankers are also exploring some alternative means of finance also, alternative products.

So, the impact of international disruptions will be limited on us as we do not have direct finished product sales to the US or to other countries. Rather, our customers in turn are exporting.

items.statement: Chhata spinning division (old inefficient machines) being rationalized; machines transferred to other plants or monetized; knitting at Chhata continues and being modernized; limited one-time cost

Fortunately, knitting, we have been able to stabilize, and it is performing; we are able to utilize it nicely, and it is contributing to both revenue and EBITDA for the company.

items.statement: Uncertainty from US tariffs, potential Russia trade penalties, land route closure to Bangladesh impacting mélange yarn exports; raw material cost disadvantage persists
items.quote: The serious concern is about the penalty that the US president talked about for Russia's trade. So that is creating more uncertainty at this point in time. So, this environment of uncertainty definitely is there for textiles as a whole.

items.statement: Knitting modernization expected 18-20% ROI with ~5-year payback; partial revenue in FY27, full revenue thereafter
items.quote: This upcoming investmen t of ₹90 to ₹95 crore in our knitting modernization, as well as the enhancements and adding the new products , which is printed into this, we expect this to clock around 18% to 20% of ROI, and as a result, we will have had payback around five years for this

items.statement: Vendor bill discounting via TReDS platform for MSME vendors yielding 1-1.5% interest arbitrage due to recent RBI repo rate cuts

items.statement: Spinning capacity 6.5 lakh spindles (4.5L synthetic, 1.25L cotton, 1.1L mélange); no plans to add spindles, only modernization for efficiency
items.quote: RSWM is one of the prominent players; we have around 6.5 lakh spindles overall working with us. So, we want to sweat these assets better, we want to use them for a different product mix.

items.statement: Future growth areas: printing in knit (added), full package denim garments, knitted garments; garmenting identified as logical missing link for integrated supply chain
items.quote: Another area for us, which is a logical offering for the market, is a full pac kage offering for denim. So, we are doing only denim fabric, and most of the customers now look for suppliers who have integrated supply chain and also offer denim garments

items.statement: No direct US exports; indirect impact via garmenter customers; UK FTA opens opportunity for finished garment exports to UK (£20B annual imports)
items.quote: We are not directly exporting to the US, because we are not in the finished goods segment. We produce yarn, we produce fabric for garmenting, and we produce fabric for denim garmenting. So, we are operating in a B2B kind of environment where we are not directly exporting to the US.

items.statement: Exploring internal sources and liquidation of non-usable assets to reduce debt burden; no equity raise mentioned
items.quote: We are exploring the internal sources of funds, and we are also focusing on certain blocked assets, and we are planning the liquidation of the non-usable assets so that the debt burden can be reduced.

items.statement: Management withdrew FY26 revenue guidance of INR2,500 crores due to tariff uncertainty
items.quote: Yes, of course, we have given the guidelines of INR2,500 crores. That was given 3 years back, and we continuously move towards that. Even the last year, we did INR2,100 crores. But in the current situation, we will definitely like not to say anything or confirm that, because this is like something which is a very, I would say, again, something dynamic has happened, which is beyond our control.

items.statement: Early monsoon disrupted domestic demand in automotive and beverage sectors, impacting Suncontrol Films and shrink films
items.quote: On the domestic front, quarter 1 is usually a strong volume driver, but the monsoon season started 30, 40 days earlier than expected in the entire country. We have seen demand disruption in end-use sectors such as automotive for Suncontrol Films, and beverage for shrink films.

items.statement: PPF segment grew 28% YoY globally, with domestic growth of 25-30%, unaffected by seasonality
items.quote: Yes. So PPF has grown. Like I said, overall, PPF has grown by around 28% as compared to last year. Because it is -- it does not have seasonality impact, right? So it was unaffected. In fact, we have grown good around 28%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 24.8% from 27.4% YoY due to higher employee and marketing costs as strategic investments
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR123 crores versus INR130 crores in the last year, while the EBITDA margin was 24.8% versus 27.4% in Q1 FY '25. The reduction was primarily on account of increased employee and marketing costs, which is a strategic investment towards the long-term growth of the company.

items.quote: We are also on track with our strategic investments, including the second PPF line and the upcoming TPU plant, both of which are expected to drive our next phase of growth.

But in Industrial Products, because that's a long supply chain and low-margin products in our value chain, so that's why we saw that into our shr

items.statement: Company debt-free with INR700+ crores cash and equivalents, providing headroom for capex and strategic investments
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, we remain in a strong position, debt-free along with INR700-plus crores of cash and cash equivalents. This provides us ample headroom for our ongoing capex initiatives and potential strategic investments.

items.statement: Garware Application Studios franchise model yields 10-15% better margins than normal channel through unique products and value-added services
items.quote: Then we give them the benefit of Bajaj Finance, then insurance, and then a couple of coatings, which we provide and cleaning equipment. So overall, that's a model which is franchisee-based and gives us on an average 10% to 15% better margins that, what we achieved from the market through our normal channel.

items.statement: If high tariffs persist, evaluating long-term options beyond cost savings and efficiency improvements
items.quote: And lastly, if that remains a long-term game, we are also evaluating like what can be done for a longer term, like after the cost savings and better efficiencies and all. So that also evaluation is going on. But at this event unless it is formalized in full, I won't be able to give much light on that.

items.statement: Shipping goods to US before August 27 deadline to avoid new tariff on in-transit inventory
items.quote: Yes. So for that particular thing, we actually honestly, whatever we have, we are trying to shift the goods before it goes onboarded, before 27th of August, right? That works on the Bill of Lading. So we are working hard to supply more products before -- I mean, before the deadline of '27. So we are working on that. I mean, we are doing that rather I can say.

items.quote: As far as balance sheet is concerned, the position, there is no significant change except some capitalization, which is part of working process wi th respect of the ongoing projects and the value attributable is around Rs. 225 crores during the quarter

items.statement: Rural growth double digits; urban high single digits; e-commerce 4% of business but gaining share.
items.quote: Our rural growths have this quarter been double digits and urban is very high single digits. This urban includes the general trade as well as the modern trade as well as the e-com numbers.

items.statement: ESG: renewable electricity consumption up 4%; specific water consumption down 3.5% (ahead of target); women factory workforce up 1.8%; CSR beneficiaries up 3.5%; multiple awards won.
items.quote: We have moved 4% in terms of our renewable electricity consump tion. In terms of specific water consumption reduction, we are ahead of the target and we have had about 3.5% reduction this quarter

items.statement: Sustained margins while competitive; covered inflation via price increases; gross margins to improve as commodity prices stabilize.
items.quote: We have covered most of our inflation in -- through our price increases. We are done with that, and we are in a good position today.

items.quote: And if you were to look at it, it's INR 4,535 crores consolidated revenue for us during this quarter. And this is not a peak quarter usually. So it's good to see the movement here.

items.statement: Volume growth ~2%; transaction growth 12%; volume-revenue delta 6-8% expected for next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: The transaction growth has been 12%. So we are pretty happy with our transaction growth of 12%. And volume will also come back slowly and steadily. But I would say the delta between volume and revenue will remain at about 6%, 7%, 8% for the coming 2 or 3 quarters.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to improve sequentially as commodity inflation mitigated and price increases completed; no high-priced inventory overhang.
items.quote: In Q1, the inflation that we saw was still what we had seen in the previous quarters, and we hadn't been able to mitigate that inflation through the required price increases. Now we've completed that.

items.statement: Palm oil duty cut benefit partially in Q1, largely in Q2; no inventory holding period for duty impact.

items.quote: As I mentioned, we expect Q2 raw material unless we get significantly surprised on the USD rupee exchange rate, we expect Q2 raw material to come a little further down.

items.statement: India opex run rate sustainable at current levels after travel and A&P cuts, A&P spend to be restored for sales growth
items.quote: Currently, we would say Joseph, these levels are sustainable. We did, apart from the cut on travel and various other costs, the only one which was cut also very sharply was the advertisement and promotion spend. At some stage that will have to be released back for the sales growth.

items.statement: ESOP scheme introduced across Tier 1-3 management for talent retention
items.quote: you would have seen in our balance sheet that we've also come out with the ESOP scheme recently. So , to the top tier of the management, T ier 2, T ier 3, T ier 1, we've given ESOPs across the board

items.statement: Reifencom revenue EUR 53mn, up 5% YoY, EBITDA margin ~4%
items.quote: Reifencom did EUR 53 million in revenues, about 5% up year-on-year and an EBITDA margin of about 4%.

items.statement: Europe restructuring asset impairment assessment pending, potential additional non-cash charges
items.quote: We will still have to do a more thorough assessment on the asset side of things. We will send in our team to go through the entire asset list in detail, including a physical examination. So, there might be something more on the asset impairment side.

items.statement: India travel sector growing; domestic air passenger traffic and hotel occupancy encouraging
items.quote: India's travel sector continues to be on the growth trajectory. Leading hotel chains have reported encouraging occupation data. Domestic air passenger traffic has also held on to sustainable growth.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high in lower end and e-commerce; new entrants with exclusive portal partnerships; established brands cutting prices
items.quote: Competitive intensity continues in the sector, especially, in the lower end of the market and more so in e-commerce channels. Multiple new entrants have been establishing exclusive partnerships with major e-commerce portals, leaving established players with a hard bargain.

items.statement: Adjusted gross margin 48% and EBITDA margin 10% excluding one-time costs and marketing spend; sequential improvement continues
items.quote: Without the impact of these one-time non-recurring items, our gross margin stood at 48% and EBITDA margin is at 10%. Without the impact of these one-offs, we continue to report sequential improvement both in gross margin as well as EBITDA.

items.statement: Held adjusted EBITDA at 10% despite double-digit revenue de-growth reflecting structural cost efforts
items.quote: Despite a double-digit de-growth in revenue, we have been able to hold an adjusted EBITDA of 10%. This reflects our structural efforts on costs and expenses.

items.statement: Bangladesh capacity utilization upward of 80%; generated operating profit of Rs. 8 crore vs loss of Rs. 11 crore in Q1 last year
items.quote: Bangladesh capacity utilization in the quarter was upward of 80% and generated operating profits of Rs. 8 crore versus a loss of Rs. 11 crore in quarter one last year.

items.statement: Premiumization strategy showing green shoots; Carlton reported double-digit growth in Q1
items.quote: Our sustainable premiumization strategy continued to show green shoots with Carlton reporting a double-digit growth in quarter one.

items.statement: Hard luggage on growth trajectory; launching industry-first Smart Bag Tag with QR-enabled luggage tag
items.quote: luggage is a key concern for many consumers. To tackle the same, we are about to launch a first -time in industry Smart Bag Tag. Select purchases from House of VIP brands will get a QR -enabled luggage tag, making travel stress free for all our consumers

items.statement: E-commerce and modern trade channels facing competitive intensity at lower price points; cabin luggage selling below Rs. 1,100
items.quote: Both these channels are having a similar issue of lower price point. Like cabin luggage are getting sold at less than Rs. 1,100.

items.statement: Modern trade impacted by one large chain consolidating and reducing store count
items.quote: One of the large chain is actually consolidating and reducing the number of stores, which has impacted our overall modern trade share.

items.statement: Volume loss concentrated at absolute lower end; launching Alfa brand to compete in that segment
items.quote: It is on the absolute lower end where actually we did not exist. But now we are coming there also. So that is where it is. So we are going to have some play with Alfa.

items.statement: Carlton sales disrupted for 30 days due to court order restraining sales from July 1; restriction removed but legal battle continues
items.quote: in July, we had some disruption because of that judgment. I hope you must be following it. There was a judgment whereby we were refrained from selling from 1 st July. And then that order got, I think we started selling from 1st August. So 30 days we were not able to sell

And hopefully, by the next six months to seven months, we are expecting to collect all our legitimate dues

items.quote: if I look from the composition of the basket perspective, it will be somewhere between 15% to 18%, which we are pursuing for liquidations in the coming quarters. Neetu Kashiramka: We have taken a Rs. 15 crore provision also in quarter one

items.quote: The quantum is closer on Rs. 10 odd crore to Rs. 11 odd crore. And this is comprising of many heads. We will not like to spell out very clearly on this front. But these are the one-off and non- recurring in nature. Neetu Kashiramka: Yes, legal and professional

items.statement: Inventory reduction of Rs. 20-22 crore net of provision in Q1 (Rs. 35 crore gross); debt level maintained at March 2025 level; still targeting full year reduction of Rs. 150 crore inventory and Rs. 130 crore debt
items.quote: In terms of the inventory reduction, it was around Rs. 20 crore to Rs. 22 crore. I am talking about the net of provision. Otherwise, if you add the provision, it goes Rs. 35 odd crore and in terms of debt reduction, we remain at the level of March 2025.

items.statement: No major capex planned for FY26; only maintenance capex
items.quote: Nothing major. It will be maintenance capex.

items.statement: Caprese brand maintaining saliency; less focus due to other challenges
items.quote: As of now, it is maintaining its saliency. Nothing big, we have enough other matters. This actually is something where focus is less because of the other challenges.

items.statement: Premiumization trend visible but lower end (below Rs. 3,000) constitutes 80% of market revenue; lower end growth larger in absolute terms
items.quote: there is a premiumization which is playing out, which is already visible because Carlton has grown by double-digit. items.statement: Shareholder transition phase imminent; potential strategy changes; management refraining from forward-looking strategic comments
items.quote: I would like to reframe too much of a future looking statements in this call, mainly because we are in the transition phase where shareholder change is going to happen soon. items.statement: Publication revenue growth of at least 15% expected in FY27 with EBIT margin improvement of at least 2% YoY
items.quote: as far as the revenue growth is concerned, we are confident of at least 15% in publication business next year because there are mo re than two standards changing in both the states

items.quote: we are very confident that we will reach 30%-31% in 2-3 years

items.statement: CBSE textbook business targeting 12-15% growth next year
items.quote: next year 12% to 15% growth in the CBSE textbook business would be definitely achievable

items.quote: the exports grew by around 7% compared to Q1 25. Even during the challenging period , we believe 7% growth was reasonable, not sufficient, but reasonable

items.quote: altogether you can say around Rs. 15 odd crore will be the cost till the curriculum cycle stops. So, Rs. 15 to Rs. 17 crores we would be spending on digital

items.statement: No export order cancellations yet; trade maintaining wait-and-watch strategy until US tariff finalization by end August
items.quote: Thankfully, our company has not faced any cancellation of orders till now , but going forward the trade is maintaining the wait and watch strategy till the final outcome of trade negotiations between the two countries

items.statement: High-cost paper inventory to be exhausted by Q2 FY26 end; currently mix of high-cost and current-price inventory
items.quote: more or less, we are now exhausted with the inventory, but it will be mix - for next one quarter still it will be mix of high-cost inventory and present price cost inventory so by second quarter end, we should be okay

items.quote: Till now it is only 1½% of our total domestic paper stationary sales, but with respect to acceptance or acceptance of the product, I would say it is very, very well accepted

items.quote: for one of the categories, it is in place. For other category, we are at present outsourcing. We will see the volumes. The infrastructure is already in place except the machinery. So, once we achieve certain volumes, we will invest in machineries also

items.quote: as far as the stationary products are concerned, believe me, the cost difference will not be beyond 5%-7% in any country because the raw material prices are international prices

items.statement: Antidumping duty products (Rs 40-50 cr) revived via new product categories; not focusing on those products anymore

items.quote: you can consider around 75% of the exports are to the U.S. It varies a bit 2%-3% every year, but around 75% one can consider for any mathematical calculations

items.quote: per our present information, there will be more than two Grades changing in Maharashtra and similarly in Gujarat. 2

items.quote: The company is looking at the unpredictable developments closely for its future bu siness strategy. I'm sure you all would have understood why I mentioned unpredictable developments

items.quote: See, given where we are, I am staying away from forecast, but the first milestone and what is within our side is doubling ourselves from where we currently are. And that line of sight over the next two to three years is very much on the horizon.

items.quote: See, again, at that level that I am talking about, the idea is to start inching towards the double-digit operating profit level. That is again the first milestone for us to achieve.

items.quote: In the next three to four years, we expect investment to the tune of around INR 500 crore in capital side, which includes investment in construction chemicals and pipes and fittings. items.statement: Greenfield project in Andhra Pradesh for designer and high-density boards and OPVC plant in Patna are on track.

items.statement: OPVC plant in Bihar on track for commissioning and production start in Q4 FY26.

items.quote: Weak demand, early onset of monsoon, pressure on input prices, and excess capacity resulted in both volume and price headwind across most of our product categories.

items.quote: So, I think at least my own expectation is the macro conditions in H2 should start improving. But given where we are, the full improvement to take shape may be a two to three quarters journey from there on.

items.quote: And that's our aim to kind of at least for the next 3 to 4 years that will be our aim to maintain that kind of a growth momentum.

items.quote: So if you see our EBITDA growth at a consolidated level, it is at 23%, which is what one should look at that is this growth momentum being continued or not.

items.quote: But as I told earlier also that we have full visibility of the quarter, almost near to 50%, 60% of the visibility for the subsequent quarters.

items.quote: But we have a feeling that going forward and as we close into the Vietnam crop cycle, we will start seeing a lot more long-term contracts coming in.

items.quote: So at a broad level, both the places and we are taking it as a group only, it's at around 60%, Manish, because the last capacity or, let's say, the existing capacity is now fully utilized, 10% to 15% is the new capacity utilization.

items.quote: As far as the green coffee prices are concerned, they have softened 20% or so or 20% to 30% in the last 2, 3 months. However, there is -- still there is a lot of volatility in the market.

items.quote: Our working capital requirement if the coffee prices remain at the levels that they are, will also come down. So, all of these - so improved cash flow, working capital coming down would mean that the interest outflow will be lower.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR1,671 crores as of June 30 from INR1,812 crores in March and INR1,974 crores in December
items.quote: So, the debt as of 30th June stands at INR1,671 crores. It was INR1,812 crores as at 31st March and INR1,974-odd crores as on December '24.

items.statement: Target net debt of INR1,200 crores by March 2026
items.quote: An additional INR150 crores, so it should be around INR1,200 crores. March '26 would be INR1,200 crores.

items.statement: Interest cost at peak INR34 crores; will trend down with lag as working capital reduces and debt is retired

items.statement: Depreciation at peak levels after commissioning India and Vietnam units in last quarter of prior year
items.quote: First one is about that these are peak levels of depreciation, yes, because after first quarter of last year, we commissioned both our India unit and Vietnam unit in the last quarter.

items.statement: Domestic branded business clocked INR150 crores in Q1 (INR100 crores from brand/retail); continuous market share gain across channels and geographies
items.quote: The domestic market where we sell our branded products continues with its growth momentum and we clocked approximately INR150 crores in the first quarter itself.

items.quote: So I think you have given as broad guidance that we have been giving, INR400 crores to INR500 crores. Definitely, first quarter itself, we have done INR400 crores. So definitely, we are going to touch INR400 crores.

items.quote: This year, we are looking to double the value from last year. So last year, because we were kind of ending the takeover formalities, we were doing around -- just to give you a brief idea on the top line, around INR15 crores, INR16 crores, we are looking to double that this year.

items.statement: Continental brand launched in India 2 months ago; targeting premium niche segment across modern retail and online platforms

items.statement: Increased inquiries from US customers due to Brazil tariffs but conversion uncertain; tariff details still fluid with exemptions
