items.statement: Export geography split: ~10% Americas, 35-40% Europe (incl. Russia/CIS), 35-40% Asia, minimal Australia
items.quote: Out of our exports business, around 10% or so comes from the American market, around 35% to 40% comes from European markets, including Russia and the CIS countries. And the balance 35%, 40% comes from Asian markets with very little business in, let's say, Australian market.

items.statement: Tariff structures fluid with daily changes and exemptions; need to wait for dust to settle before assessing impact
items.quote: The whole world is under confusion and it will take a little bit of a time for us to understand where things are going. But yes, we are getting more inquiries and we are addressing them as far as.

items.statement: Coffee price volatility ($100 daily swings) causing buyer tentativeness; stability needed for long-term contracts and consumption recovery
items.quote: Today, what has happened is that while the prices have corrected 30%, if you see every day, there is almost $100 fluctuation up and down, up and down that is happening. So everybody is in a little guess mode and people are trying to double guess what's going to happen in terms of prices going forward.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward-looking revenue or margin guidance
items.quote: Sorry, we do not give forward-looking guidance.

items.statement: Board approved revised capex plan of ₹321 crores for FY26 for 75-80 cranes, 21 already purchased in Q1
items.quote: The Board of Directors in the earlier meeting held on 20 May 2025, have approved a CAPEX plan of ₹ 246 crores for purchase of cranes, trailers, prime movers and multi-axle lines. Additionally, CAPEX plan of ₹ 75 crores has been approved by the Board of Directors in the meeting held on 6 August 2025, and taking revised CAPEX plan to ₹ 321 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex of ₹114 crores incurred, adding 21 cranes worth ₹94 crores and ₹20 crores other equipment
items.quote: Company has done CAPEX of ₹ 114 crores in Q1 FY '26, and we have added 21 various capacity cranes, aggregating to ₹ 94 crores. And we have done a CAPEX of ₹ 20 crores towards the purchase of other equipment.

items.statement: Fleet stands at 380+ cranes with gross block of ₹2,766 crores as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: As on 30 June 2025, the Company has a fleet around 380-plus cranes aggregating to the gross block of ₹ 2,766 crores.

items.statement: Order book of ₹767 crores as of July 20, 2025, with ₹273 crores revenue booked in Q1, leaving ~₹500 crores for execution in FY26
items.quote: The Company has an order book position of ₹ 767 crores as of 20th of July, out of which we have booked revenue of ₹ 273 crores till June. Therefore, around ₹ 500 crores will be executed in this current financial year.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin 38% in Q1 FY26 vs 41% in Q4 FY25 and 49% in Q1 FY25, decline due to revenue mix shift to lower-margin EPC businesses
items.quote: Our overall EBITDA percentage for the quarter ended June 2025 was 38% vis-à-vis 41% in Q4 FY '25 and 49% in Q1 FY '25. There is a reduction in EBITDA percentage, which is primarily on account of change in revenue mix.

items.statement: Average blended yield improved to 2.11% in Q1 FY26 from 2.03% in Q4 FY25 and 2.04% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our average blended yield for the Q1 FY '26 was 2.11% vis-à-vis 2.03% in Q4 FY '25 and 2.04% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Strong demand across all sectors including renewables, infrastructure, cement, steel, thermal, refinery, highways and metros
items.quote: With every single sector of the economy firing on all cylinders, we see the demand from cranes coming across all sectors, as Gaurang has mentioned.

items.statement: India added 22 GW solar and wind capacity in H1 (56% YoY growth); cement to add 43-45 MMT capacity in FY26; crude steel production ~40 MMT (11% QoQ growth)
items.quote: India has added nearly 22 gigawatts of solar and wind capacity in H1, that's 56% increase over year-on-year. Cement also grew 9.2% in May and June and plans to add another 43 million to 45 million metric tonnes capacity in FY '26. The crude steel production stood approximately 40 million tonnes, registering 11% growth on a quarter-to-quarter basis.

items.statement: Wind energy capacity addition expected at ~5 GW in FY26 vs 4.2 GW in FY25
items.quote: Last year, the renewable wind energy added 4.2 gigawatts of new capacity addition. This year, we believe the country will add anywhere in and around 5 gigawatts.

items.statement: Revenue mix remains 50% wind and 50% non-wind sectors, similar to previous quarters
items.quote: However, we can currently say that 50% of our revenue comes from wind and 50% of it comes from the remaining sectors.

items.statement: First order secured in Saudi Arabia via wholly owned subsidiary Sanghvi Movers Middle East; 12 cranes deployed port-to-site
items.quote: In this quarter, your Company has achieved go-to-market in Saudi Arabia, and we have bagged our first order in a wholly owned subsidiary, Sanghvi Movers Middle East.

items.statement: Saudi yields higher than India but operating costs higher, margins slightly lower; too early to quantify
items.quote: The yield is better in Saudi Arabia as compared to India. However, the cost of operations is higher. And therefore, because there are several regulations, several Saudi ASEAN requirements as well as a higher cost of operating, so the margin will be slightly lower. However, the yields are higher.

items.statement: Saudi capex of ₹100-150 crores planned, not fully backed by firm orders yet but confident in business plan
items.quote: I cannot tell you whether all ₹ 100 crores, ₹ 150 crores are backed by orders. But we are confident in our business plan, which we have not yet disclosed to the public as of right now.

items.statement: Sangreen Future Renewables (wind EPC) contributes ~20% of bottom line; project EPC in hydrocarbon also in nascent stage
items.quote: Today, our step-down subsidiary, Sangreen Future Renewables Private Limited, accounts for nearly 20% of the bottom line.

items.statement: EPC revenue recognition follows percentage-of-completion method causing lumpiness; margins volatile in nascent renewable and project EPC businesses
items.quote: However, in the EPC business, we use the POCM methodology, which is a percentage of completion method. So, revenue recognition will be skewed based on the level of project delivery as per the IndAS accounting standards. And as we scale up these businesses, as we achieve a certain size and scale, we will see the lumpiness in the revenue recognition also smoothen out.

items.statement: Invested ₹131 crores surplus cash in debt funds, mutual funds, short-term corporate bonds, arbitrage funds and commercial paper at 7.73-8.48% average ROI
items.quote: Out of surplus cash generated, the Company has invested ₹ 131 crores in various debt funds and various mutual and short-term corporate bonds, arbitrage fund and commercial paper, which has generated average ROI between 7.73% to 8.48% per annum.

items.statement: Saudi crane market is developing with sizable competition; aim to be top 5 player by 2030 leveraging 35 years IP, safety standards, processes and technology
items.quote: So, the Saudi crane market is not a mature market, but it's a developing market. There's a sizable crane market in Saudi Arabia in terms of competition. We believe we are well placed to enter the market with a unique offering because we bring 35 years of intellectual property, safety, the highest safety standards, operating processes, optimized cost structures and technologies. It is our vision or

items.statement: Cash accruals of ₹81.63 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The total cash accruals for Q1 was ₹ 81.63 crores.

items.statement: Management will not disclose sectoral revenue split going forward due to competitive sensitivity
items.quote: So, going forward, we will not be giving sectorial split of revenue because it is the management's call now that this has now become an issue with respect to our customers, competition and all other players.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue target of INR 400 crore
items.quote: Our target is INR 400 crores.

items.statement: Annual revenue target of INR 2,000 crore
items.quote: We are trying our best to achieve INR 2,000 crores. That's the target. That's the goal, right?

items.statement: Geopolitical issues and expected price decline caused customers to defer orders in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The business for Lebanon, business for Yemen was in jeopardy to some extent. It was back and forth kind of a business going on. That has affected and when the geopolitics situation in the world is bad, it affects every single country's decision making and all that.

items.statement: Customers waiting for new crop prices to fall before placing orders
items.quote: Our customers are hungry. Only thing is everybody is waiting for the prices to come down.

items.statement: Margins stable in Q1 FY26 despite revenue decline; better than corresponding period last year
items.quote: Even in this current quarter, I don't think the margins have declined. The margins remain stable. Only revenue is going to increase in the future.

items.statement: Historical net margin range of 9% to 14%
items.quote: Generally, the company posts a margin between 9% to 14%. It keeps going up and down.

items.statement: Two of three new packing units in Karnal operational; third unit facing teething troubles
items.quote: In Karnal, we have installed two new packing units out of three. The third one is still not ready. It's under some teething troubles. Two have already started.

items.statement: Gandhidham (Mundra) unit opened July 4 and running at full capacity
items.quote: And that Gandhidham unit was opened on 4th of July. So, it's working full. Full capacity is working.

items.statement: Packing unit capex of INR 2.5-3 crore per unit (machinery and erection only)
items.quote: Investment is not big. It comes to about INR 2.5 crores, INR 3 crore. I'm talking strictly machinery, erection and everything. I'm not talking about land and building because that is already there.

items.statement: Karnal new units running at ~50% utilization; Gandhidham unit at full capacity
items.quote: Currently, because we are seeing a decline in the prices, with the new plants, maybe we are running an efficiency of 50%. We have not operated them at 100%. Going forward, things are favorable. We are going to operate them at full swing.

items.statement: Each packing unit can generate INR 100 crore annual revenue; volume capacity ~35-50 tons per day per plant
items.quote: So, these plants can do a revenue of INR 100 crore annually, each one of them.

items.statement: Parboiled rice prices $900-1,000/ton CIF Middle East; Basmati $100-150/ton higher
items.quote: Depending upon the -- if it is parboiled, it is around $900 to $1,000 CIF to Middle East. Of course, packing matters is small. Packing is higher. This kind of prices.

items.statement: Expecting rice prices to decline with new crop arrival; all-time high crop estimate of 151 million tons
items.quote: The crop is all time high expected for rice. Total 151 million ton is the estimate. So, let's see.

items.statement: Zero impact from US tariffs so far; Basmati not grown in US; 75% market share is Indian; ethnic customers allow contract flexibility
items.quote: As of now, the business has not affected. There is zero impact on business, which is happening in USA for my company. This is number one point. The second point is Basmati is not grown in USA. It is an Indian product.

items.statement: Opening Sberbank account in Russia; expecting good business due to rupee reserves and bank promotion
items.quote: And recently this Sberbank of Russia, he had been -- their team has approached us. Not only for opening the account, they say we will promote your product in Russia.

items.statement: Inventory levels down from March 31 peak; selling existing stock and waiting for new crop to rebuild
items.quote: We do have inventory, but not to the levels which it was during 31 March. It is relatively quite down. And it's also sold or likely to sell kind of inventory.

items.statement: No inventory losses in Q1 FY26; purchases and sales at regular market prices with reasonable profit
items.quote: There was absolutely no inventory loss in this quarter because it had happened last yea r when in the beginning the prices were high. And then they came down here to sell at breakeven also. But we never did any loss

items.statement: Company is debt-free with cash deposits
items.quote: The company is totally debt free, rather deposit with the cash flow.

items.statement: Appointed new distributor in Australia; no new geographies entered in Q1 FY26
items.quote: We appointed a very nice distributor in Australia. As I said, we visited him.

items.statement: Japanese delegation visited but no orders yet; talks ongoing
items.quote: So, the delegation of course visited us and it was a very good meeting. But till now they have not started buying. This is the current status. Still in talks.

items.statement: Biggest challenge is unpredictable US tariff policy under Trump administration
items.quote: So, the biggest challenge right now is, you know, Donald Trump, the President of US comes every weekend. He comes up with a new tariff. This is the biggest challenge right now, what the industry is facing.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Russia-Iran war, Israel-Iran conflict) disrupting trade to Lebanon, Yemen, Iran
items.quote: This Russia - Iran war which started somewhere from the June, it started from, I think, yeah, June -- June, it started. And prior to that period, also something was cooking up. The business for Lebanon, business for Yemen was in jeopardy to some extent.

items.statement: Business model: deliberately slow sales when prices falling to protect margins; hybrid model with variable quarterly performance
items.quote: What you're saying is right, but with the model we have, you will see some quarters will become very big. Some quarters will become slow without compromising on the margins. In the future, you're going to see some quarters vary. I mean, maybe we cross INR 500 crore. Maybe we touch INR 600 crores.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 1,800 crore expected within next 3 years, FY27 may be too soon
items.quote: If we can maintain this pace, maybe FY27 is still too soon. But I think in the next 3 years, the Company should be in a position to get there.

items.statement: Alkaline battery plant commercial production targeted by January 2026 internally, March 2026 latest
items.quote: We should be in commercial production by March 2026, as we said, end of the financial year, which is March 2026. But internally, our target is to do it by January 2026.

items.statement: Urban consumption steady, rural demand showing slow recovery, discretionary purchasing subdued
items.quote: Consumer demand held on with urban consumption steady. Inflation was moderate. However, discretionary purchasing remained subdued. Rural demand showed a slow recovery.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin at 14.3%, battery segment ~19%, flashlight ~13%, lighting flat
items.quote: We continue to deliver a strong EBITDA profile at 14.3% thus aligning well with our intent.

items.statement: Segment margins: battery around 19%, flashlight 13%, lighting remains flat
items.quote: Battery is around 19%, flashlight 13% and the lighting remains flat almost

items.statement: Alkaline battery market share grew 50 bps QoQ to 15.3%, carbon-zinc dominant at 59.1% share
items.quote: The category has seen moderate price increases in certain SKUs. We took long strides with our alkaline portfolio, drawing a growth of 50 bps in market share quarter-on-quarter to 15.3% as mentioned earlier.

items.statement: Rechargeable flashlight growth 39% YoY, double-digit growth expected medium term
items.quote: The segment has shown double-digit growth led by our lineup in rechargeable flashlights where growth is 39% year-on-year.

items.statement: Jammu greenfield alkaline battery plant on track, Rs 115 crore spent so far
items.quote: The development of our greenfield facility at Jammu continues to be on target and will strengthen competitiveness as we seek to grow our share aggressively.

items.statement: Jammu plant capex of Rs 115 crore included in total debt of Rs 200 crore
items.quote: This includes the debt for the alkaline plant also. Whatever debt is in the book, it includes around Rs. 115 odd crore that has been spent for the alkaline plant.

items.statement: Jammu plant will be India's only alkaline manufacturing for home consumption, commercial production by March 2026
items.quote: The plant in Jammu will be mostly devoted towards, potentially India's only alkaline manufacturing for home consumption.

items.statement: Zinc prices range-bound, cautious hedging strategy maintained to protect profitability
items.quote: Zinc prices stayed range-bound during the quarter given the tariff concerns and sluggish demand globally. We continue to exercise cautious hedging strategy to protect our profitability.

items.statement: New products (last 36 months) contribute ~15% of revenue, MCBs and wires recently launched
items.quote: Our overall new products and by new products, definitions, I mean products that have been completely new or refurbished in the last 36 months, now, that typically would account for close to 15% of the revenues

items.statement: Alkaline battery revenue growth 50%+ YoY with similar volume growth, carbon-zinc growing in volume and value
items.quote: In this quarter, revenue growth achieved was in excess of 50% year-on-year with similar growth in volumes.

items.statement: Distribution network of 4.5 million outlets for zinc-carbon batteries leveraged for alkaline push
items.quote: Given that in zinc-carbon, we sell 1.2 Billion batteries in India and have distribution which is close to 4.5 million outlets where our batteries are present.

items.statement: BIS certification expected to drive consolidation in favor of branded players like Eveready
items.quote: We expect that the BIS certification will drive consolidation in favor of brands like ours.

items.statement: Settlement with Real Touch Finance (KKR matter) for Rs 15 crore lifts restrictions on asset disposal and capital restructuring
items.quote: Under the terms of settlement, the Company paid Rs. 15 crore to Real Touch and assigned its receivables from the concerned entities, carried in our books at nil value along with associated rights and guarantees.

items.statement: CCI matter status quo, still at NCLAT awaiting hearing
items.quote: With regard to CCI, the matter is status quo. It is still at NCLAT, awaiting the hearing process.

items.statement: Total debt Rs 200 crore includes Rs 115 crore for alkaline plant, no separate debt for plant
items.quote: No. This includes the debt for the alkaline plant also. Whatever debt is in the book, it includes around Rs. 115 odd crore that has been spent for the alkaline plant.

items.statement: New product launches not expected to substantially increase working capital requirements
items.quote: We don't see a substantial investment from a working capital point of view on this new product launches.

items.statement: Separation exercise across multiple plants, ~50 workmen separated, Rs 7.07 crore ex-gratia, 3-3.5 year payback
items.quote: Roughly, I think it is about 50.

items.statement: Ex-gratia payout of Rs 7.07 crore for 50 employees, annual savings ~Rs 4 crore, payback 3-4 years
items.quote: An exceptional charge of Rs. 7.07 crore was incurred towards non-recurring ex-gratia payments to workmen as part of a separation exercise.

items.statement: Land assets Rs 65 crore across 8 locations (Kolkata, Jammu, Noida, Assam, Haridwar, Lucknow), all utilized
items.quote: Most of our lands are actually leasehold land. And it is across all the locations. If you see that starting with our Kolkata head office, recently bought land at Jammu, then we have the value for Noida, Assam, Haridwar, Lucknow.

items.statement: Lighting segment facing value erosion despite volume growth, muting value growth
items.quote: LED lighting has navigated a challenging environment marked by continuing price erosion which tends to mute value growth despite robust volume expansion.

items.statement: A&P spends at 8.3% of revenue, campaigns rolled out across media
items.quote: Spends on A&Ps stood at 8.3% and campaigns were rolled out across media.

items.statement: Capital raise (rights issue) premature to comment, settlement formalities need 2-3 months
items.quote: It is only after that, or you can say that you need not wait till the final that we will have to review, what do we do with whether there is any requirement to raise capital, this is still too raw.

items.statement: Everspark subsidiary under review for discontinuation, no employees, created for China imports
items.quote: This subsidiary has no employees. It is just a Company that was created at one point of time in order to facilitate imports from China.

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth for FY26, low to mid double-digit worst case
items.quote: we should be growing at double-digit in terms of volume. Now, whether it is low double-digit, mid double-digit, I think things will be more clear how quarter 2 pans out.

items.statement: CPVC contribution target above 20% in next 1-2 years from 15% currently
items.quote: we are highly confident that the contribution will improve above 20% in next 1-2 years versus 15% today.

items.statement: Housing segment revenue mix target 70-75% in next 3-4 years from 60% currently
items.quote: eventually, it should settle at around 70% or 75% in next 3-4 years.

items.statement: Market share target ~5% in 3-4 years at Rs 3,000 cr revenue vs industry Rs 50,000 cr
items.quote: at Rs. 3,000 crore revenue with the industry size of like Rs. 50,000 crores, let us assume, right, our market share should be like 5%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex Rs 70 cr; FY25 capex Rs 166 cr; residual capex ~Rs 100 cr to reach 285,000 tons capacity
items.quote: We incurred a CAPEX of Rs. 70 crores in Q1, following a spend of Rs. 166 crores in FY '25. We remain committed to expanding our total installed capacity to 2,86,000 tons over the next 2 years, without adding any debt to our books.

items.statement: Residual capex Rs 100 cr to reach 285,000 tons; Q1 spent Rs 68-69 cr; next 3 quarters Rs 70-80 cr; FY27 residual Rs 30-40 cr
items.quote: the residual CAPEX to achieve this is around Rs. 100 crores. In Q1, we already spent Rs. 68-Rs. 69 crores, correct? And in rest of 3 quarters, we should be another Rs. 70-Rs. 80 crores. And when we enter into FY '26, some residual Rs. 30-Rs. 40 crore may be left over.

items.statement: Current capacity 220,000-230,000 tons; target 286,000 tons in next 1-1.5 years; Varanasi plant to start end of calendar year
items.quote: Our new plant in Varanasi is on track and is expected to commence operations in the coming months. This will significantly strengthen our presence in the Eastern Indian market.

items.statement: West India plant (Kisan) ramp-up steady after 14 months integration; fixed supply chain and distribution issues
items.quote: Kisan has been almost 15 months into our possession, 14 months to be precise. And we have fixed a lot of problems there. One was, of course, the investment what we made. But then other than that, the supply chain, the distribution network, a lot of issues, what the company was grappling for the last 10-12 years, we fixed those issues in the last 13-14 months.

items.statement: UPVC doors/windows order book building; targeting Rs 50 cr revenue for full year, mostly H2
items.quote: For the full year, we should be doing kind of Rs. 50 crores kind of revenue from this vertical. But most of this will come in like second half.

items.statement: Apollo standalone EBITDA spread ~Rs 9,000/ton in Q1; target Rs 10,000-11,000/ton with higher utilization; Kisan target Rs 7,000-8,000/ton
items.quote: If you look at Apollo Pipes on standalone basis, it is at around Rs. 9,000 a ton and Kisan is at Rs. 4,000 a ton in Q1. Definitely, once the capacities are utilized further from Q1 levels, Apollo will go towards Rs. 10,000-Rs. 11,000 a ton, which we have been present at this level for many quarters now.

items.statement: NSR down Rs 2-3/kg QoQ due to resin price decline; competitive intensity high as players cut prices to fill capacity
items.quote: reason is down by Rs. 2-Rs. 3 a kilo if you look at like 1st April versus 30th June, so some decline in the NSR definitely because of low resin prices. And yes, the competitive intensity is high at the moment because demand is sluggish and each of the PVC pipe companies has increased the capacities in last 2-3 years.

items.statement: Q1 volume down 4% YoY; expect improvement from September as construction resumes post-monsoon; government infra spend recovery key for H2
items.quote: Q1 was obviously, I would say, pretty much washed out. April started on a good note. It did continue in May, but then by the time June came because of the onset of early monsoons, the quarter got washed out. And on Y-o-Y basis, our volume is lower by 4% on console basis.

items.statement: Government infrastructure spending slowdown across construction materials for 18-20 months; recovery expected when funds resume for water projects
items.quote: one of the biggest challenges what we are seeing is the overall slowdown in the government spends towards the infrastructure. And this we are witnessing across product verticals, not only in plumbing, but also construction material as a sector, if we look from a macro perspective.

items.statement: Q1 product mix 60% housing, 40% agri; new products: PLB ducts, DWC pipes, PE gas pipes, PVC-O pipes, UPVC doors/windows
items.quote: Yes. So, 60% is housing, 40% is agri.

items.statement: CPVC growing high double-digit after July co-marketing agreement with major resin supplier; supplier approved with real estate developers
items.quote: we have tied up with one of the largest raw material manufacturers of CPVC resin, wherein we are going to co-market the product. And that supplier is already approved with a lot of real estate developers and large projects. So, benefits are already visible that our CPVC sales are growing by a high double digit already.

items.statement: Competitors sacrificing margins for volume; smaller players may exit; organized players' EBITDA spreads down 5-6% vs 2-3 years ago
items.quote: it is clearly visible that the competitors are reducing their NSR and compromising on margins way too much to demonstrate or to try to gain sales volume growth. So, which we at some point stopped, because we are sure that so one is that our fixed costs are under control.

items.statement: Seeing distressed asset deals weekly; weaker players' capacities coming for sale; sector cleanup expected in few quarters
items.quote: we are already seeing a lot of deals on the table, correct, like weaker players, capacities coming for sale. Every day, every week, a banker would show us a deal, right. So, definitely, there is a lot of stress, right? I think it is just a matter of a few quarters that we will see a lot of cleanups in the sector.

items.statement: Working capital cycle disciplined at 38 days; target 30 days by end FY26 or H1 FY27; sustainable 25-30 days
items.quote: Our working capital cycle has remained disciplined at 38 days and we anticipate further improvement as operational efficiency scales up.

items.statement: Working capital at 35-40 days currently; target 30 days by end FY26 or H1 FY27; sustainable 25-30 days
items.quote: Right now, we are at 35-40 days. This will go towards 30 days of cycle, maybe by end of FY '26 or first half of FY '27 and it should remain between 25-30 days at a sustainable rate going forward.

items.statement: Warrants issued to Kitara Capital: Rs 110 cr total, 25% received Q1, balance 75% within 18 months; to fund capex without stretching balance sheet
items.quote: The total investment is Rs. 110 crores, 25% money came last quarter, right. The idea is to, because these are tough times, but we have been into hyper CAPEX mode, Yog. And we want to continue to build capacities for new products to cater into new geographies.

items.statement: Warrant balance 75% (Rs 82.5 cr) to come within next 18 months
items.quote: So, I told you, Rs. 110 crores is the total investment commitments, right. 25% came in last quarter, rest 75% will come in within next 18 months.

items.statement: Committed to expanding capacity to 286,000 tons over next 2 years without adding debt
items.quote: We remain committed to expanding our total installed capacity to 2,86,000 tons over the next 2 years, without adding any debt to our books.

items.statement: Industry size ~Rs 40,000-45,000 cr; Apollo revenue run rate Rs 1,200-1,300 cr; market share ~2.5-3%
items.quote: with the revenue run rate, what we are having today is around Rs. 1,200-Rs. 1,300 crores on a full year basis. And the industry should be like around Rs. 40,000-Rs. 45,000 crores. So, that way, our market share is around 2.5%-3%, Yog.

items.statement: ROCE currently single-digit on Rs 1,000 cr capital employed; target >20% as revenue scales to Rs 2,500-3,000 cr on same capital base
items.quote: Optically, it is like very low and very concerning for us, right? But one thing, what makes us confident that at least we are on the right track, to achieve the desired ROCE levels, upward of like above 20%, which we have always maintained.

items.statement: Demand recovery dependent on government infrastructure spending pickup; not visible to great extent currently
items.quote: FY '26, how we perform or this sector performs in second half, it will depend a lot on how government spending picks up, which right now is not visible to the great extent.

items.statement: Competitive intensity may persist until weaker players exit; sector cleanup expected in few quarters
items.quote: till that time, the pain may continue. But yes, at some point, it will reverse for sure.

items.statement: Evaluating smart metering/IoT plumbing; no concrete plans yet; may become significant in 5-10 years; talking to international players for technology
items.quote: we are evaluating this segment already. But nothing concrete is on drawing board as of now. Maybe in next 3-4 months, we will be in position to tell you that how this segment is going to pan out, what are the government commitments to focus on this segment.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 revised to ₹2,000 crores from earlier ₹1,400 crores
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate our estimated total capital expenditure for the financial year to be in the range of ₹2,000 crores.

items.statement: Three major capex programs underway backed by long-term supply commitments
items.quote: In parallel, we are executing three major capex programs backed by long-term supply commitments, further strengthening our forward visibility.

items.statement: Capitalized assets of ₹261 crores in Q1 FY26, including ₹114 crores for Kakinada Phase 1
items.quote: We have capitalized assets of ₹261 crores during the current quarter, of which assets capitalized for the Phase 1 of Kakinada project amounted to ₹114 crores.

items.statement: Capital work in progress of ₹1,319 crores at end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: We have capital work in progress of ₹1,319 crores at the end of the quarter.

items.statement: Unit 3 Kakinada operational since January 2025, producing key starting materials and intermediates
items.quote: A critical contributor to the ecosystem is our Unit 3 facility in Kakinada, which became operational in Jan uary 2025. This facility is strategically focused on producing key starting materials and intermediates, reinforcing our self-sufficiency, and adding strength to our overall value chain

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 80% in Q1 FY26, consistent with last year
items.quote: Currently, our capacity utilization is at 80% this quarter, which has been consistent in the last 1 year.

items.statement: Solid Phase Peptide Synthesis capacity commissioned with pilot and commercial scale reactors
items.quote: Notably, our newly commissioned Solid Phase Peptide Synthesis capacity has garnered strong interest from large pharmaceutical companies, particularly those developing GLP-1-based treatments.

items.statement: Healthy pipeline of RFPs and customer site visits; multiple projects in R&D, pilot, validation stages expected to commercialize in 12-24 months
items.quote: We are seeing a healthy pipeline of RFPs and customer site visits, alongside multiple active projects progressing through R&D, pilot, and validation stages. Several of these are expected to transition into commercial scale within the next 12 to 24 months.

items.statement: Three dedicated CS projects with long-term contracts and volume commitments on track for commercialization

items.quote: But from a long -term business viability we keep on investing behind our copies, in our Print businesses, and our other various businesses like OTTplay, we are setting up our target, and we have seen 100% growth on a y-o-y basis and we hope to repeat the performance going forward.

items.statement: Net cash remains healthy at INR 976 cr
items.quote: Net cash remains very healthy at INR 976 cr.

items.statement: Radio business facing pricing pressure and tough environment
items.quote: Our Radio business is undergoing a bit of a tough environment right now, where the pricing is under pressure, but we are doing all that is in our hands, to correct the situation.

items.statement: Circulation discounts continuing month-to-month based on competitive environment
items.quote: But at this point in time, the strategy is paying fruits of course, it is a little costly as for the RPCs they tend to depress in the short term, whereas the benefit comes over the long term. So , at this point in time, we are continuing. But suffice to say that we will keep on looking at the performance on a monthly basis and take a real-time call on that.

items.statement: OTTplay achieved 100% YoY growth
items.quote: and our other various businesses like OTTplay, we are setting up our target, and we have seen 100% growth on a y-o-y basis and we hope to repeat the performance going forward.

items.statement: RSU costs charged to salary and wages account per Ind AS
items.quote: So, Gaurav, all the costs have been charged in the salary and wages account, and it's not a 9% dilution currently, I don't know how you calculated that. But the accounting has been conducted as per Ind AS and it's not 9% dilution currently.

items.statement: No dilution yet from RSUs as shares not issued, only rights granted
items.quote: There's a ‘right’ for this and it is benchmarked to certain milestones also. Gaurav Agarwal: I couldn't get you. Can you come again, please? Anna Abraham: It is a ‘right’ at this point of time. The shares have not been issued as yet. So , when the shares get issued, then we will have some level of dilution. But at this point of time, there is no dilution

items.statement: Bollywood box office collections surged 38% YoY in Q1 FY26 with five Hindi films crossing INR100 crore and three crossing INR200 crore.
items.quote: Bollywood box office collections surged by 38% year-on-year, driven by a steady flow of successful titles such as Raid 2, Sitaare Zameen Par, Kesari Chapter 2, Housefull 5 and Jaat.

items.statement: Hollywood collections grew 72% YoY driven by franchises like Mission Impossible, Final Destination and Ballerina.
items.quote: Hollywood movies too, where PVR INOX enjoys a dominant market share, delivered a sh arp 72% year -on-year growth in collections, powered by super hit franchises like Mission Impossible, Final Destination and Ballerina

items.statement: Regional content showed stability supported by hits in Tamil and Malayalam.
items.quote: Regional performance was well supported by hits like Good Bad Ugly in Tamil, Thudarum in Malayalam and sleeper hits like Tourist Family in Tamil.

items.statement: Blockbuster Tuesdays at INR99 brought nearly 1 million new and lapsed transactors back to cinemas.
items.quote: Impressively, it brought nearly 1 million new and lapsed transactors back to cinemas, highlighting its effectiveness in revitalizing weekday cinema going habits.

items.statement: Punjabi film disruptions caused loss of 6-7 lakh admissions in the quarter.
items.quote: the release of Punjabi film like Akaal and the indefinite suspension of Sardaar Ji 3 collectively impacted footfalls, resulting in a loss of nearly 6 lakh to 7 lakh admissions.

items.statement: Admissions rose 12% YoY to 34 million in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Admissions rose to 12% -- by 12% to 34 million, while average ticket price increased by 8% to INR254.

items.statement: Spend per head on F&B reached highest ever at INR148, up 10% YoY.
items.quote: We also achieved our highest ever spend per head on F&B at INR148, reflecting a 10% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Advertising revenue reached INR110 crore, highest post-pandemic quarter, up 17% YoY.
items.quote: Advertising revenue reached INR110 crores, the highest for any quarter post pandemic, marking a 17% increase over the previous year.

items.statement: Total revenue INR1,488 crore, EBITDA INR114 crore, PAT loss INR34 crore vs revenue INR1,209 crore, EBITDA loss INR20 crore, PAT loss INR137 crore YoY.
items.quote: Total revenue for the quarter was INR1,488 crores. EBITDA was INR114 crores and PAT loss was INR34 crores as compared to revenue of INR1,209 crores, EBITDA loss of INR20 crores and PAT loss of INR137 crores in the same period last year.

items.statement: Capex guidance maintained at INR400-425 crore for FY26 including INR250-260 crore for new screens, INR70-75 crore renovation, INR75 crore maintenance/IT/other.
items.quote: We will spend roughly in total about INR400 crores to INR425 crores, which will include about INR250 crores to INR260 crores on new screens, about INR70 crores to INR75 crores on renovation and remaining INR75 crores on maintenance, IT and other related capex.

items.statement: Opened 20 new screens in Q1 FY26 (14 under asset-light/FOCO); signed 55 FOCO and 72 asset-light screens for opening over next 18-24 months.
items.quote: During the quarter, we opened a total of 20 new screens, of which 14 were under asset-light and FOCO models. In addition, we have signed 55 new screens under the FOCO model and 72 new screens under the asset-light model

items.statement: Current portfolio at 1,745 screens across 353 cinemas in 111 cities in India and Sri Lanka.
items.quote: Our current screen portfolio stands at 1,745 screens across 353 cinemas in 111 cities in India and Sri Lanka.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR61 crore QoQ to INR892 crore at end-June 2025; down INR539 crore (38%) since merger.
items.quote: Our net debt stands at INR892 crores at the end of June 2025, marking a reduction of INR61 crores since March 2025 and an impress ive INR539 crores or 38% reduction since the merger

items.statement: Priority to further reduce net debt using surplus operating cash flow.
items.quote: Yes, that's our priority to reduce net debt. I think you should expect the net debt levels to further come down. As the operating cash flow increases, we will use the surplus cash to pay down debt.

items.statement: Confident full-year footfalls will cross FY24 levels (~150 million) given strong content pipeline and July bumper month.
items.quote: Yes, absolutely. In the sense, the way the pipeline is stacked up, there is absolutely no doubt that we would cross. We were very confident when we were starting off the year in April. And now after the end of quarter 1, it's only looking better.

items.statement: Blockbuster Tuesdays at INR99 improved strike rates and SPH by converting value-conscious weekday consumers; unlimited popcorn/Pepsi refills and INR50 Pepsi offer also drove SPH.
items.quote: On the SPH end, as I said, the INR99 menu on the weekday and the unlimited popcorn and Pepsi refill pack, along with that offer where anybody could buy a glass of Pepsi by paying INR50 extra, all these offers really helped us to increase strike rate and get the SPH up.

items.statement: Industry-wide INR99 Tuesday limited to one day to avoid cannibalizing weekend cash-rich audience; Monday-Thursday already lower pricing than weekends.
items.quote: This is an industry-specific program where not only PVR INOX, but the entire industry has been galvanized to actually have this specific one day off. We don't want to start shifting our value customers from other days into INR99 day because that would begin to erode our profits.

items.statement: Advertising revenue driven by big-star films (Kesari, Raid 2, Good Bad Ugly, Sitaare Zameen Par) which attract brand endorsements; sleeper hits don't work for ad business.
items.quote: So from that point of view, we had some big star rer films that came in, which was Kesari with Akshay Kumar. He also endorses a lot of brands. We had Ajay Devgn in Raid 2. We had Good, Bad, Ugly with Ajith again, which -- who endorses a few brands in the South

items.statement: Karnataka price cap draft notification not yet finalized; 700+ objections submitted; applicability across premium formats/weekends unclear; no change to expansion plans.
items.quote: the Karnataka government order is yet not notified. There was a draft notification released in mid-July, where the government sought feedback and objections from the public at large. A lot of feedback and objections have been sent out, more than 700 objections on the price cap has been sent out to the government.

items.statement: Convenience fee growth ~10% YoY vs 22% box office growth due to INR3.5 crore provision reversal in base quarter; adjusted growth ~19-19.5% in line with box office.
items.quote: The growth in convenience fee we have seen is roughly around 10% versus a 22% growth in our box office collections. So actually, there was an impact of a certain provision that we had reversed last year in quarter 1 of roughly around 3.5 crores

items.statement: Cost control from variabilizing staff, utilities, solar deployment; most efficiency levers already in place; benefits visible as operating leverage improves with footfalls.
items.quote: we have leveraged technology, we have leveraged scale to control and variabilize our cost at the ground. So when t here is less number of footfalls or week days, our usage of contractual staff is accordingly monitored and altered

items.statement: Rental cost INR1,250 crore/year mostly from registered leases; renegotiations and waivers on escalations contained Q1 rental growth; benefit visible in Q2 and full year.
items.quote: We have a INR1,250 crores of rental cost a year, and bulk of this is from registered leases in existing properties, which are not FOCO or asset-light. So this will -- this is a priority for us, and we are focused.

items.statement: Hollywood bounce-back and strong Hindi/regional slate expected to sustain ATP growth; FY25 ATP was flat due to Hollywood strike.
items.quote: With Hollywood bouncing back and coming back to its normal contribution the way it used to be earlier, the growth in ATP will be there year-on-year. To what level and how much is -- only time will tell depending on how the films perform at the box office.

items.statement: OTT fatigue driving consumers back to cinemas; shift from star-driven to story-driven content; pan-India appeal of regional films expanding market.
items.quote: what we clearly are getting is that there is an OTT fatigue. Clearly, that's one. The content overall has become a lot sharper and better. And the fact that people do want to come out and understand and enjoy this movie experience is the pivot point.

items.statement: Passport loyalty program discontinued due to film fraternity resistance; blockbuster Tuesday more effective at driving frequency; no plans to relaunch old loyalty program.
items.quote: Passport has been discontinued simply because the film fraternity did not sort of agree to the fact that the film should -- their film should be discounted. They wanted it to be labeled under the marketing structure for PVR INOX and which was really not the way Passport could have survived.

items.statement: Strategy to utilize cinema infrastructure for live events (IPL, comedy, conferences) and re-releases beyond movies.
items.quote: how we can utilize the existing infrastructure for alternative content other than movies. And that is the strategy that we want to focus on, which is to say that if we can do more of live event screenings, IPL matches, comedy shows, conferences in our cinemas, which are not dependent on films only.

items.statement: Yarn segment saw stable demand; home textile order book healthy
items.quote: The yarn segment continued to be key revenue contributor with INR562 crores, supported by stable demand.

items.statement: Gross margin fell 165 bps YoY to 42.4%; EBITDA margin 0.2%
items.quote: Gross margin was at 42.4%, which was lower by 165 basis points on a year-on-year basis. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR1 crore with margin of 0.2% and a reported loss of INR30 crores.

items.statement: Raw cotton prices up ~3% QoQ; polyester volatile on crude; Indian cotton above international prices
items.quote: On cotton, we have seen the prices have moved by about 3% from last quarter to this quarter.

items.statement: Capex split: 20% maintenance, 40% machine upgrade, 40% new product categories
items.quote: On the regular maintenance, about 20% is what is going to go. About the machine upgradation, it's about 40% and balance 40%, we have kind of kept it for entering into newer product segments or newer categories.

items.statement: Home textile capacity utilisation for own products only 40%; rest used for job processing
items.quote: If you look at the overall capacity, which is going only on to home textile is only about 40%. Balance, we are using it, but we are using it for processing. So it is not really value adding to the home textile.

items.statement: Exports 35% of revenue; Bangladesh ~45% of exports; US exposure minimal in yarn, ~60% of home textile exports
items.quote: For the quarter 1, 65% is what was going into domestic and 35% is in exports. In 35%, if we were to look at, roughly about 45% is going into Bangladesh and the balance is going into different other geographies.

items.statement: Evaluating industrial yarns, carpet backing yarns, FR yarns; fiber conversion profitable with functional finishes
items.quote: What we are currently evaluating is industrial yarns. The application of this can be in different industries; which get value-added and can go into different kind of industries. We are evaluating Sutlej Textiles and the carpet industry, where certain specific qualities of yarn go as a carpet backing. And of course, we are evaluating the FR yarns, which is fire-resistance or fire-retardant yarns, w

items.statement: Bangladesh banned land shipment of yarn; now requires sea route via Chittagong
items.quote: Bangladesh, the ban was on the land shipment of yarn into Bangladesh. Normally, the yarn used to take the road route through Benapole, which was banned. Now all the yarn, which is to go has to go through a sea shipment via Chittagong.

items.statement: Cotton inventory maintained at 60-75 days; robust sourcing strategy in place
items.quote: So typically, we maintain a stock of about 60 days, except certain months because cotton is an annual crop. So on an average, we maintain about 60 days to 75 days based on how the forecasts are, how the prices are moving.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio maintained at comfortable 0.95x
items.quote: We are continuously working on cost optimization and strengthening the balance sheet with our debt-equity ratio maintained at comfortable level of 0.95x.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions (India-Pak conflict) caused operational shutdown; US tariff uncertainty; Bangladesh import route change
items.quote: The quarter was particularly impacted by the unfortunate war between India and Pakistan. Our manufacturing unit in Northern India faced operational disruptions on account of war.

items.statement: Exploring Latin America markets for functional yarns to diversify from Bangladesh dependence
items.quote: We are exploring other markets/ other products so that we diversify in any case, including the newer markets of Latin America and all which are becoming more open as far as the functional yarns is concerned.

items.statement: Commodity yarn spreads under pressure; value-added dyed yarn and synthetic yarn segments relatively better
items.quote: There is a lot of pressure on the commodity yarns, and that is kind of evident. What we do is mostly synthetic yarn and also the value-added dyed yarn. So in these segments, while there are pressures, but the pressures are not as much as, let's say, in the basic cotton or polyester yarns.

items.statement: Safety of employees prioritized during J&K unit evacuation; teams commended for restoring operations by July
items.quote: Located close to the border, the safety of our employees was our top priority, leading to temporary workforce evacuation. I would like to place on record and commend our on-ground and leadership teams for their exceptional efforts in restoring operations. By July, we successfully resumed full-scale production at our Kathua unit.

items.statement: Pre-sales value of Rs 1,124 crores in Q1 FY26, up 6% YoY
items.quote: We achieved a pre-sales value of Rs. 1,124 crores reflecting a 6% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: Sales volume of 1.25 million square feet in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Sales volume for the quarter stood at 1.25 million square feet.

items.statement: Customer collections of Rs 857 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The customer collections for the quarter stood at Rs. 857 crores.

items.statement: Average realisation improved 9% YoY to Rs 8,988 per square feet in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The average realisation also improved by 9% Y-o-Y to 8,988 per square feet , underscoring sustained demand and strong pricing traction across our portfolio.

items.statement: Launch pipeline of 12.32 million square feet planned for FY26 including 9.22 msf new projects and 3.1 msf new phases
items.quote: Our launch pipeline for the year remains robust with approximately 12.32 million square feet of planned development, which includes 9.22 million square feet new project launches and 3.1 million square feet of new phase launches.

items.statement: Non-Bengaluru projects account for over 50% of ongoing and planned projects; Mumbai and Pune represent 21% of planned pipeline
items.quote: Notably, non -Bengaluru projects now account for more than 50% of ongoing and planned projects. Reflecting our strategic geographic diversification, Mumbai and Pune together represents 21% of the planned pipeline, underscoring our strong focus and expanding presence in West India.

items.statement: On track to complete 2 million square feet of commercial space in Q1 FY26; signed LOI with IKEA for 80,000 sq ft at Rs 150/sq ft at Purva Zentech
items.quote: We are on track to complete 2 million square feet during Q1 of 2026. In 2026, we have signed LOI with IKEA for 80,000 square feet of carpet area at Rs. 150 per square feet on carpet area for Purva Zent ech.

items.statement: Planned delivery of 4,500+ units in FY26; 3,015 units (3.65 msf) completed with OC received, awaiting e-Khata for handover
items.quote: We remain on track for planned delivery of more than 4500 plus units during this financial year. Out of the planned handovers, 3000 plus units, 3015 units, approximately 3.65 million square feet have been completed and the OC has been received already. Thes e are currently awaiting e -Khata issuance for handover possession.

items.statement: Handed over 667 units (0.68 msf) in Q1 FY26 generating Rs 539 crores revenue
items.quote: During the quarter, we handed over 667 units covering 0.68 million square feet, generating revenue of Rs. 539 crores.

items.statement: Selected as preferred developer for 8 housing societies redevelopment in Chembur, Mumbai with estimated GDV of Rs 2,100 crores and developer area of 1.2 msf
items.quote: We have been selected as the preferred developer for the redevelopment of 8 housing societies in Chembur, Mumbai with an estimated GDV of Rs. 2,100 crores with developer area of 1.2 million square feet.

items.statement: Four key redevelopment projects in Mumbai with collective developer area of 3.63 msf and estimated GDV of ~Rs 7,700 crores
items.quote: This forms part of our broader redevelopment portfolio in the city with four key redevelopment projects collectively with a developer area of 3.63 million square feet, which is expected to generate a GDV of approximately Rs. 7,700 crores, further reinforcing our strategic presence and growth momentum in the Mumbai market.

items.statement: Entered JDA for 5.5 acres in East Bengaluru with estimated GDV potential over Rs 1,000 crores
items.quote: Further strengthening our presence in key micro markets, we have entered into a JDA for 5.5 acres land parcel in East Bengaluru with an estimated GDV potential of over Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Partnered with KVN Property Holdings for 24.59 acres in North Bengaluru with 3.48 msf saleable area and estimated GDV of Rs 3,300 crores; launch expected within six months
items.quote: Earlier this quarter, Puravankara partnered with KVN Property Holdings LLP for a 24.59 acres land parcel with 3.48 billion s aleable area with an estimated GDV of 3 ,300 crores. The project is located in North Bengaluru near the airport and is expected to launch within six months.

items.statement: Revenue Rs 539 crores, EBITDA margin 15%, reported loss of Rs 69 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our revenue was Rs. 539 crores, EBITDA margin for the quarter was 15% while we reported a loss of Rs. 69 crores.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 2,825 crores, net debt/equity 1.68, cash balance Rs 718 crores; gross debt reduced by Rs 138 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: On our debt position, our net debt stands at around Rs. 2,825 crores which is at a net debt equity ratio of 1.68 with a cash balance of Rs. 718 crores, indicating a strong liquidity profile ensuring stability and operational continuity. Gross debt during this quarter actually reduced by Rs. 138 crores

items.statement: Cost of debt reduced to 11.35% driven by focus on funding efficiencies
items.quote: Cost of debt has reduced to 11.35% driven by continued focus on improving funding efficiencies.

items.statement: Chembur redevelopment launch expected in Q2 FY27
items.quote: So, from a launch perspective, we are expecting it only in the next financial year, maybe in the quarter two of next financial year.

items.statement: Bengaluru launch timeline: Bellandur, Hebbagodi, Westend, Mallasandra in Q3 FY26; Grand Hills, Vajrahalli, Winworth Phase 2, Hennur Road in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Bellandur is going to come in Q3 and the other one in Kochi, there is a project called Winworth Phase 2, we said it is going to come in for Q4, Grand Hills in Q4 and Hebbagodi in Q3, Westend in Q3, Hennur Road, probably Q4 or Q3, Mallasandra, that is our one of our project in Kanakapura Road that should be coming up in Q3 and another Kanakapura Road project which is called Vajrahalli, it should be

items.statement: Rs 322 crores equity investment in cash flow: Rs 282 crores drawdown from HDFC Capital (payable/enable, zero-coupon) for Hardware Park; Rs 50 crores from 361 facility for Deccan redevelopment
items.quote: So, we are referring about the drawdown which we have done from HDFC capital, which is Rs. 282 crores, which is payable and enable structure and zero -coupon bond. And we utilize this money in acquiring one of our, which we announced Hardware Park property. And another Rs. 50 crores we have drawn from 361. That facility is also payable and enable in nature. And that is a basis of surplus sharing a

items.statement: No specific pre-sales growth target given; expect growth driven by Q3/Q4 launches across Bengaluru, Kochi, Mumbai micro markets
items.quote: No, we have never given a guidance or a number, but definitely, there will be a growth in that number. With the kind of launches that we have, especially over the quarter three and quarter four, if you look at the kind of locations and the spread that we have within Bangalore, the kind of spread that we have, then even the Kochi project, the following phase, Phase 1 of which has done extremely wel

items.statement: Expect export growth tempo to continue at similar levels in coming quarters
items.quote: Given this performance of the emerging markets, our strengthening competitive position and the return of KTM exports, overall, we expect to continue to maintain the growth tempo in the coming quarters at similar levels as has been achieved this quarter and previously.

items.statement: Domestic motorcycle industry growth of 5-6% conceivable going forward
items.quote: So I would still say, as we had said that a 5% to 6% growth is certainly conceivable going forward.

items.statement: Capex to progressively go up to INR600-700 crores for rest of year split equally between EV and ICE
items.quote: Capex during the quarter stood at approximately INR100 crores, which will progressively go up to about INR600 crores, INR700 crores for the rest of the year, with spend split almost equally to support EV capabilities and ICE innovation.

items.statement: Expect flat cost versus price in next quarter with currency tailwind and margin trending back to FY25 average levels
items.quote: So, in net terms, we are expecting it to be a flat cost versus price quarter. The currency has been very volatile off late, but I expect it to be a tailwind for the quarter given the levels at which it's currently trending.

items.statement: EV supply issues expected to be resolved by end of quarter with full derisking in 6-9 months
items.quote: While complete restoration should happen by end of the quarter, we are keen to derisk the supply chain of this important segment, and that complete derisking should take about six to nine months.

items.statement: BACL AUM expected to reach INR18,000-19,000 crores by year end with profit run rate multiplying
items.quote: I'm anticipating that we will end the year with a book size of anywhere between INR18,000 to INR19,000 crore s. And you will clearly see the current run rate of profit being

items.statement: Domestic motorcycle industry flattish YoY in Q1 with 125cc+ outperforming 100cc segment
items.quote: The motorcycle industry performance in quarter 1 on a Y-o-Y basis was flattish. The 125cc plus segment continued to perform better than the 100cc segment.

items.statement: Export industry grew 17% in top 30 markets with Bajaj outpacing at 27% growth
items.quote: Of these top 30, in 25 markets, the industry grew collectively by 17% in Q1, signalling a continued revival. In these very important markets, Bajaj outpaced the industry growth and grew by 27%.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle industry grew 11% YoY driven by doubling of e-auto volumes
items.quote: The industry saw strong growth of 11% in Q1 on a Y-o-Y basis, driven by an almost doubling of e-auto volumes with the E segment also growing at 11%.

items.statement: Electric 2-wheeler industry averaging close to 100,000 units/month growing over 30% YoY with 20%+ scooter penetration
items.quote: On electric 2-wheelers in Chetak, the industry continues to average close to 100,000 units per month, growing over 30% year-on-year with penetration in scooters reaching to 20% plus levels.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 19.7% in Q1, down 50bps sequentially due to adverse dollar realization
items.quote: Margins for the quarter came in at 19.7%, a sequential moderation of about 50 basis points that I had cued, if you recall, almost entirely on account of the adverse dollar realization that played out mainly through April and May.

items.statement: Material cost pressure landed at 70bps vs estimated 100bps due to cost savings and better steel rates
items.quote: In the end, overall material cost pressure, inclusive of the regulatory cost increases, landed in the range of about 70 basis points relative to the 100 basis points that we had originally estimated, and that flowed through into the reported margins as well.

items.statement: EV portfolio nearing double-digit EBITDA margin with some Chetak models EBITDA positive
items.quote: the electric portfolio is now very close to double-digit EBITDA margin. Thanks to the work done on R&D, localization and procurement, this is now landing well and yielding benefits.

items.statement: Exports volume grew 16% in Q1 with highest ever retails outside Nigeria and highest ever commercial vehicle export retails
items.quote: The BU grew volumes by 16% in Q1 as exports recovered. Our premium brands, Dominar and Pulsar continued to enrich the mix with Pulsar growing at over 21%, delivering obvious benefits to revenue and EBITDA performance.

items.statement: 3-wheeler business maintained 100,000+ unit run rate for 8 consecutive quarters with 75% ICE market share and 35% e-auto share
items.quote: We have maintained a 100,000 plus unit run rate for eight consecutive quarters in our 3-wheeler business, anchored by our undisputed leadership in ICE and the steady scale-up of our electric portfolio.

items.statement: Chetak market share rose to 21% in Q1 from 12% in Q1 FY25 with volumes more than doubling
items.quote: As a result, our market share for the quarter rose to 21%, up from 12% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: BACL acquired 1 million customers with AUM of INR12,000 crores and PAT of INR102 crores in Q1
items.quote: It has now acquired 1 million customers with an AUM of INR12,000 crores and built a business driven by the twin pillars of digital first and robust operational efficiencies, thus delivering a PAT of INR102 crores in quarter 1.

items.statement: EV supply chain constraints causing 50% shortfall in Chetak and 25-30% in e-autos for current quarter
items.quote: July has seen a 50% shortfall. While we expect production in August to be better than July, we may still see a shortfall of similar levels of 50% in this quarter in Chetak and about 25% to 30% or so in e-autos.

items.statement: Chetak portfolio fully transitioned to new floorboard battery platform with 100% of models on new platform
items.quote: with the launch of the 3001 that we've now put o ut that completes the full transition. So the whole portfolio has now with this launch, moved to 100% on the new

items.statement: Net pricing impact balanced out in Q1 with selective price increases and decreases across portfolio
items.quote: On pricing, we were very selective with our approach, taking price up in parts of the portfolio while dropping prices in parts of the motorcycle business to revive its competitive growth momentum. In net terms on pricing, the ups and downs almost balanced out each other through the quarter.

items.statement: Export revenue at all-time high despite volumes 20-25% below FY22 levels due to better dollar realizations and richer product mix
items.quote: Even though volumes are still 20%, 25% lower than the FY '22 levels, the revenue from exports have reached an all-time high. This is the result of better realizations coming in from the dollar and a richer product mix.

items.statement: KTM and Triumph domestic volumes grew 20% YoY to nearly 26,000 units with market share gains in respective segments
items.quote: Together, the two brands built nearly 26,000 units in the domestic market during the quarter, marking a strong 20% year-on-year growth and a gain in market share within their respective segments.

items.statement: ABS mandate for 125cc and below could take 12-24 months for supply chain readiness with high cost implications
items.quote: The estimation of the industry as a collective I'm talking about, not just as Bajaj Auto because as you can imagine, this is a very important discussion within the ind ustry is that it could take anything between 12 to 24 months to just get the supply chain right if every single 2-wheeler has to be equipped with ABS

items.statement: Average export realization at INR85.6/$ in Q1, down INR1 from previous quarter due to dollar weakness in April-May
items.quote: As a result, the average realization for the quarter for our exports stood at INR85.6, about INR1 lower than the previous quarter, translating into a modest drag on both sequential revenue and margins.

items.statement: Surplus cash position at tad under INR17,000 crores after adding INR1,200 crores free cash flow in Q1
items.quote: This quarter, we added about INR1,200 crores in free cash, taking our surplus cash position to a tad under INR17,000 crores, well managed and available to be strat egically deployed across growth

items.statement: Infused INR300 crores into BACL in Q1 taking cumulative investment to INR2,700 crores
items.quote: We remain optimistic about the growth in this business and have infused INR300 crores into BACL this quarter, taking our cumulative investment to INR2,700 crores.

items.statement: KTM restructuring concluded with Austrian court confirmation on June 16, 2025; regulatory approvals underway across multiple jurisdictions
items.quote: the insolvency court in Austria through its orders of 16th of June 2025, confirmed the restructuring plan that was proposed by KTM. And therefore, the entire restructuring proceedings now have been concluded, and the business is back in many ways outside of that legal process.

items.statement: Nigeria market at 50-60% of peak volumes due to currency-led inflation dampening demand and payback periods
items.quote: Nigeria was 50,000 units for us when we did 210,000, 54,000 units we were doing. Today, we are doing 14,000, 15,000. So that's almost a 40,000 gap from our highest peak.

items.statement: No specific revenue or earnings guidance provided
items.quote: As per our usual practice, we would not be providing any specific guidance on revenue or earnings projections.

items.statement: Print advertising revenue grew 17% YoY to INR 255 cr
items.quote: Our Ad. revenues have come to INR 255 cr, which is a 17% improvement y-o-y and a total operating revenue at INR 324 cr, which is an 8% y-o-y improvement.

items.statement: English print ad revenue grew 19% YoY to INR 140 cr
items.quote: Going to the English segmentation , our advertisement revenue which has come at INR 140 cr, is a 19% growth, so very healthy growth on a y-o-y basis.

items.statement: Hindi print ad revenue grew 14% YoY to INR 116 cr
items.quote: Coming on to the Hindi business. Our growth is at 14% y-o-y with Ad. revenues coming in at INR 116 cr and on a quarterly basis it's a decline of 9%.

items.statement: Radio revenue declined to INR 31 cr with -21% margin
items.quote: Radio, as highlighted earlier, has been under a bit of pressure . Segment revenues saw a dip compared to the prior quarter due to the high base effect from big events which we conducted earlier this year. Our revenue came at INR 31 cr, as against INR 36 cr last year, with a margin at -21%.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 21% YoY to INR 56 cr with -38% margin
items.quote: In Digital, we can see the segment revenues rose y-o-y as most digital properties, including OTTplay continued to gain traction. Profitability improvement was owing to broad -based revenue expansion along with business investment rationalization. As a consequence, our operating revenues are at INR 56 cr which is a growth of 21% y-o-y and operating margins are at a -38%.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT improved 59% YoY to negative INR 11 cr
items.quote: As you can see, in the first quarter of FY 2025-26, our total revenues have grown by 6% on a y-o-y basis to INR 451 cr, and PAT is a negative INR 11 cr, which is an improvement of 59%.

items.statement: Government, Education, Real Estate and BFSI drove print ad growth
items.quote: But apart from the government revenue, commercial revenue also has fired for us this quarter. Yash R: So which sectors have contributed the most to it? Anna Abraham: Education is a big segment for Q1 so that would be one of the segments which fired. Across English and Hindi, it would be Education. Among the top 5 segments, 2-3 of them have been firing

items.statement: English circulation revenue down 22% YoY due to pricing discounts, copies flat
items.quote: Circulation revenue, however has been little tepid because of our impetus at recruiting more copies and more readers, it is down by 22% on a y-o-y basis. On a quarterly basis, it's nearly flat.

items.statement: Newsprint prices flat around USD 500/metric ton for last two quarters
items.quote: Newsprint prices are flat for at least the last two quarters, and we don't see any reason for them to spike up. I understand there's a lot of anxiety around the geopolitical events. But we believe that the newsprint prices will remain in a very tight band, which is currently give or take USD 500 a metric ton, and we are currently tracking those prices.

items.statement: Circulation discounts continuing selectively in Hindi, Delhi, Bombay, Chandigarh
items.quote: Now I don't think that this is a carte blanche that we are doing across all our Print locations and all our markets, but there are selective market s where we see that we have to shore up the copies. Now there are 2 routes that we take: one is, as you said price-off; second, is the incentives that we give to our readers. So, we keep on checking them on a monthly basis.

items.statement: Investing in Print copies and OTTplay targeting 100% YoY growth
items.quote: But from a long -term business viability we keep on investing behind our copies, in our Print businesses, and our other various businesses like OTTplay, we are setting up our target, and we have seen 100% growth on a y-o-y basis and we hope to repeat the performance going forward.

items.statement: Net cash healthy at INR 976 cr
items.quote: Net cash remains very healthy at INR 976 cr.

items.statement: AFE revenue substantial part of Print revenue, existing agreements 3-5 years
items.quote: AFE revenue has been a substantial part of the overall Print revenue and remains to be seen, but it doesn't have too much bearing on the new agreements that we would have signed because all the existing agreements that we have, also have a life of three to five years.

items.statement: Warrant conversion based on conviction of upside in invested companies
items.quote: Now the reason that we would convert a warrant into equity is if we basically see that, that equity can give us a substantial upside. Now that will happen because this is all basis the information rights that we have in our invested companies, if we see that a certain company is on a certain track where we believe that there can be a lot of upside, and that is the time that we convert our warrant

items.statement: Radio pricing under pressure, taking corrective actions
items.quote: Our Radio business is undergoing a bit of a tough environment right now, where the pricing is under pressure, but we are doing all that is in our hands, to correct the situation.

items.statement: OTTplay achieved 100% YoY growth
items.quote: and our other various businesses like OTTplay, we are setting up our target, and we have seen 100% growth on a y-o-y basis and we hope to repeat the performance going forward.

items.statement: Management expects sustained domestic demand across segments and aims to improve market shares to offset agri cyclicality
items.quote: we see sustained demand in the domestic market, and it's actually acr oss all of these segments. And specifically, and you mentioned some of these segments like real estate, etc, we're not seeing any cyclicality, we're seeing sustained demand

items.statement: Power generation demand is broad-based across infrastructure, real estate, data centers, QSR, retail, hospitality
items.quote: So yes, I mean, the same segments, which is infrastructure is essentially real estate, and whether it's commercial or residential developments, these are the normal sectors that we look at in terms of demand. And it's actually broad-based, it's across the board that we have seen better demand.

items.statement: B2C margins at low double digits, sustainable and improvable long-term
items.quote: So the margins are at low double digits. And we see that sustaining, we do think that it's a margin that we can sustain over the long term and even improve.

items.statement: Received prototype development order for 6 MW marine main propulsion engine from Indian Navy; further orders contingent on successful execution
items.quote: So this order is for the development of a 6 megawatt ma rine main propulsion medium speed engine. And it's an order for a prototype development. So at this stage, the order is just for prototype development

items.statement: Progressing on strategic projects for NPCIL and Indian Navy; revenue recognition milestone-based and dependent on successful completion
items.quote: Yes, essentially, it's milestone-based, the revenue, milestone-based. And apart from that, I think it depends on successful completion. So, to give you more detail on that would be very speculative.

items.statement: Continuing investments in US subsidiary Kirloskar Americas Corporation to build meaningful presence in largest genset market
items.quote: So, the US business and t he US market is the largest genset market in the world. And it is a m arket where which is new for us a nd we have to continue to invest in building out what we want to build up there to have a significant presence

items.statement: High horsepower portfolio built quickly over last 3 years; tracking market share node-by-node quarterly
items.quote: we have bu ilt out the high horsepower portfolio very quickly in the last 3 years. Normally, these developments take many years to complete. But I think because of some of the innovation, say around Optiprime etc., we were able to introduce products in the high horsepower range

items.statement: Minor pricing corrections only; market stabilizing, no significant price changes
items.quote: If you look at in terms of pricing actions, we're watching the market closely. And we are correcting in case when there are minor corrections required, but there's nothing significant that we have done. And there are no significant changes that have happened. The market is stabilizing.

items.statement: Farm mechanization business reclassified from B2C to B2B industrial segment for operational synergies
items.quote: We already had an agri segment and we saw a lot of operational synergy with the industrial business within B2B. And hence, we decided to consolidate and so the farm business and the agri business are parts of the industrial business now.

items.statement: Gaining volumes with existing construction equipment customers and traction with new customers and applications post BS-V transition
items.quote: We have actually very successfully emissionized our full portfolio on the construction equipment side. And we are not only gaining volumes with our customers that we currently have, but we're also slowly gaining traction with customers that were not there with us earlier. And we're also entering new applications.

items.statement: CPCB IV+ transition made service proprietary, driving consolidation in aftermarket toward authorized dealers
items.quote: All of the platforms, all of the engine platforms have moved to electronic engines. And that means the service has become proprietary. So, certainly, wherever there would have been freelancers or people who are out of our service dealer system who are servicing the engine, that's not really possible anymore.

items.statement: International B2B sales up 13% YoY; Middle East/North Africa traction driven by MySpan GOEM appointment settling down
items.quote: the main traction that we're seeing and the pickup that we're seeing over last year is from the Middle East region and that's because the GOEM that we have appointed, MySpan, which we appo inted about two years ago, is now settled down

items.statement: Payables 76 days, receivables 41 days, inventory 53 days - healthy working capital levels maintained
items.quote: With payable at 76 days and receivables around 41 days, we are maintaining healthy working capital levels. Inventory is now at comfortable level of 53 days, marki ng an improvement over Q2 and Q3 of last year

items.statement: Standalone cash and cash equivalents Rs. 639 crores net of debt including treasury investments
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents of Rs. 639 crores by end of this quarter. Please note that cash position is net of debt and includes treasury investments.

items.statement: Divested Optiqua (tables and pipes business) to focus on core strategy and redeploy capital to higher growth areas
items.quote: Also, within B2C business, we had successfully closed the divestiture of our tables and pipes business, which is called Optiqua. As I had mentioned in my earlier calls as well, we have set out on a strategy that is clear on what is our core and what are the businesses that we will get into and we will focus on those.

items.statement: ARKA building retail distribution: 32 branches opened in Q1, more progress expected in Q2
items.quote: Quarter 1, we focused on building the distribution and the infrastructure and hiring the people. So, as we speak, we have got 32 odd branches open for secure retail. And in Quarter 2, you will see more progress around it.

items.statement: ARKA pivoting from wholesale to retail book; medium-term plan to achieve core-business-level returns on invested capital
items.quote: We are also in a period of time where we are pivoting from going from a largely stable wholesale book to a book that is more has a more retail focus. And that is going to take some time. There are some clear goals that we have stated in terms of the ARKA medium term plan as well.

items.statement: Record highest ever Q1 net sales: standalone Rs. 1,434 crores, consolidated Rs. 1,751 crores
items.quote: We closed Q1 with the highest ever net sales in KOEL's history at Rs. 1,434 crores for the standalone business and Rs. 1,751 crores for the consolidated business.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 order inflow was INR 910 crores, up 42.1% year-on-year
items.quote: We clocked INR 910 crores, which is 42.1% increase over the correspondi ng period of last year

items.statement: Order backlog is 25% higher year-on-year at INR 1,635 crores
items.quote: we have a very strong backlog, which is 25% higher than last year, the corres ponding period and which ensures that whatever lag we have in terms of the sales, we will accelerate sales and catch up in the quarters to come

items.statement: Sales grew 4.8% year-on-year to INR 622 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Sales have been at INR 622 crores, which is close to 5% increase.

items.statement: Gross margin declined 1.5 percentage points year-on-year to 38.8% due to exceptional credits in base quarter
items.quote: Our material margin has been 38.8%, which is 1.5 points lower. And the reason for this is the corresponding period of last year had some exceptional credits.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined 2.4 percentage points year-on-year to 11.8%
items.quote: EBITDA at 11.8%, lower by 2.4 points.

items.statement: Management confident of delivering full-year internal margin guidance despite Q1 dip
