items.quote: whatever guidance we have actually taken internally for the full year, we are confident that we'll be delivering that margin and profitability for the full year.

items.statement: Capex of INR 200+ crores planned plus INR 130 crores started a couple of years ago; all projects on track
items.quote: maybe INR 200-plus crores is what we have planned. And this is besides what we started in -- a couple of years ago, which was another about INR130 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 85-90% with ability to accommodate 10-15% more volume through debottlenecking
items.quote: Currently, we are in the 85%, 90% capacity utilization. But then I always say that even if we are at that level of capacity utilization, it's not that we will not be able to accommodate another 10%, 15% of business

items.statement: No public guidance given; management chasing internal targets for revenue, margin and working capital efficiency
items.quote: When we say guidance, it is the internal targets, etcetera, which we have with us. And of course, because as an organizati on, as Schneider Electric in India, we are all poised for growth in terms of the revenues, in terms of the margin, in terms of the working capital efficiency

items.statement: Power and Grid segment contributes 40-45% of business, predominantly government/PSU clients
items.quote: Power and Grid is our br ead-and-butter business, and that contributes to 40% to 45%. Regarding the other segments, it all depends on what kind of investments are coming and what kind of -- which orders we take

items.statement: Order book mix is selective for better margins, payment terms and collection hygiene
items.quote: We are picking up very good orders in terms of the margin as well as the payment terms, etcetera, which is ensuring not only the growth in the business and the margins, but also the hygiene as far as the collections, etcetera, is concerned.

items.statement: India renewable energy at 50% of power demand 4-5 years ahead of schedule; 75% of Q1 capacity addition from renewables
items.quote: has attained 50% of power demand, about 4, 4.5 or 5 years ahead of the schedule. And they have – three-fourth of what we added in this Q1 is actually coming out of renewable

items.statement: Green hydrogen demand expected at 9 MMTPA by 2032; INR 14,000 crore scheme for 9 GW solar grid integration
items.quote: analysts have said that we expect the hydrogen demand to be roughly about close to 9 MMTPA by 2032. Now what it also means is there are a lot of things, which will start happening.

items.statement: Data center IT load capacity expected to add 2.5-3 GW over 4-5 years on top of existing 1.2 GW
items.quote: we should be adding another 2.5 gigawatts or about 3 gigawatts of IT load capacity on the existing 1.2 gigawatt load in, say, coming 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: EV charging infrastructure grew from 5,000 to 26,000 stations; target of 13 lakh by 2030
items.quote: We have actually grown to about 26,000. And we are expected to be at maybe putting up another close to 13 lakh charging stations and we see them coming up by 2030.

items.statement: Battery energy storage target of 230+ GWh out of 400+ GWh total by 2029
items.quote: in 5 years from now, we would be having a capacity of 400-plus gigawatt hour, out of which about 230-plus gigawatt hour will come out of battery-based energy storage systems.

items.statement: Company focuses on technology differentiation and total cost of ownership rather than volume competition
items.quote: We are the ones who actually are niching ourselves out as one of the technology players with whom our customer engages and is happy to connect and transact with us because of the features and the usefulness and the reduction in the total cost of ownership, which we bring to them.

items.statement: No direct or indirect impact from US tariffs on India
items.quote: No. No, not for us as to best of our knowledge.

items.statement: Employee costs grew 11.8% year-on-year due to inflation, salary hikes, headcount additions and variable labor costs
items.quote: As far as employee costs, which have grown by 11.8%, this is well in control. It has the inflation, the salary hikes as well as the additional expenses with respect to the headcount.

items.statement: Project delays and spillovers caused muted Q1 sales growth; expected to be captured in Q2 and Q3
items.quote: We had some spillovers and some project delays, which were not fully in our control. That is why it has been spilled to the next quarter.

items.statement: New 33kV breaker rated 3,000 amperes launched with withdrawable design, internal arc testing, QR code digitalization
items.quote: we have upgraded our design at 33 kV, wherein we have come out with an upgraded version of breaker, which actually can handle up to 3,000 amperes at 33,000 volts.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance Rs 1,400-1,500 crore and EBITDA Rs 170-180 crore
items.quote: Our top line, we are expecting between Rs.1,400 crores to Rs.1,500 crores and EBITDA we are expecting between Rs.170 crores to Rs.180 crores.

items.statement: Wire complex at Bobbili site estimated at Rs 100 crore, on hold due to land issues
items.quote: Rs.100 crores will be the investment which will line up in that thing. It will be purely galvanized wires and wire products, which will be Steel Exchange India Limited August 06, 2025 mainly for export purposes, like nails and all that

items.statement: SMS capacity raised to 3.6 lakh tpa, rebar to 3.57 lakh tpa; Q1 utilisation SMS 55%, rebar 43%
items.value: SMS 3.6 lakh tpa, rebar 3.57 lakh tpa
items.quote: Earlier, it used to be 2.5 lakh tons in my SMS plant, which has become now 3.6 lakh tons. And even our rebar also, it was 2.25 lakh tons, which has been increased to 3.57 lakh tons now.

items.statement: Re-bar utilisation expected 85-90% after RINL conversion order operational by December
items.quote: by operationalizing that contract, which is likely to be somewhere in December this year. So, after that, our Re-Bar mill utilization will go to more than 85%-90

items.statement: RINL conversion contract for 1.2 lakh tpa billets to TMT bars valued up to Rs 210 crore
items.quote: We are also happy to share that Steel Exchange India Limited has been awarded a contract valued up to Rs 210 crores by RINL for the conversion of 1.2 lakh tons per annum of billets into Vizag Steel Steel Exchange India Limited August 06, 2025 TMT bars

items.statement: EBITDA per ton currently ~Rs 6,660; expected to rise to ~Rs 7,500 on own production at higher utilisation
items.quote: Our EBITDA per ton is around 6,660. So, more than 6,600. We are expecting this will go further once we increase our capacity utilization more because of the fixed cost absorption on the more production.

items.statement: RINL conversion order to add Rs 2.25 crore monthly EBITDA (~Rs 27 crore annually)
items.quote: Monthly additional EBITDA, we should get around Rs. 2.25 crores. So, that means around Rs.27 crores incremental EBITDA will be coming from this going forward on a full year of operation.

items.statement: Total debt Rs 340 crore; plan to repay Rs 75 crore from rights issue proceeds
items.quote: Currently, we have Rs.340 crores outstanding and the reduction plan is that once we complete this rights issue, so, we are planning to utilize around Rs.75 crores out of the rights issue for repayment of this debt.

items.statement: Refinancing term sheet at 13.25% first year, then 12%; benefit from Q3 FY26
items.quote: Currently, we have 18.75% rate, which we are looking at. We have got the term sheet for 13.25% in the first year. Once we complete one year, it will come down to 12%.

items.statement: Rights issue up to Rs 200 crore planned next month, subject to approvals
items.quote: We are planning this rights issue in next month. And you are talking about is there anybody? We are now depending upon our own numbers.

items.statement: Net working capital Rs 350-400 crore funded internally; bank limit only Rs 50 crore; plan to increase limits
items.quote: Our net working capital of more than almost Rs.350, 400 crores but it is funded by internal because my existing limit for the working capital is only Rs.50 crores from the bank.

items.statement: Long-term iron ore contract with NMDC for ~4 lakh tons; long-term coal contract with Mahanadi Coalfields
items.quote: We are having the raw material contracts with NMDC for iron ore, the lumps and all that and with around 4 lakh tons I am having a contract. It comes through this railway lines itself. Similarly, we are having coal contracts also with Mahanadi Coalfields long-term

items.statement: Specialised defence-grade product sold across states; exploring new grades under SIMHADRI brand
items.quote: We have one specialized product which goes to our defense projects across the country. So, we are selling it in the many states. And we are going to look for such products going forward at later stage.

items.statement: SIMHADRI TMT approved for Machilipatnam Port and Mulapeta Port projects in Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: During the quarter, SIMHADRI TMT rebars were approved for two significant development projects in Andhra Pradesh, i.e., Machilipatnam Port and Mulapeta Port.

items.statement: SEIL Infra Logistics subsidiary incorporated June 29, 2025; targeting Rs 14-15 crore net profit annually from Q4 FY26 via leasing 100 acres and railway sidings
items.quote: We are targeting only on the logistics business around Rs.14, 15 crores of net profit minimum annually that by... my model I am right now talking is only leasing it and these things.

items.statement: Additional 100 acres for logistics park and real estate development; joint development model expected ~Rs 3 crore per acre value
items.quote: On average per acre, we should be getting around Rs.3 crores total value. Out of that, our share we will be getting.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion potential to add 1 million tons (to 1.5 million tons total) at existing plant with low investment after debt-free
items.quote: There will be a large scope for expansion in the existing plant because it is having all the required land, power, railway sidings and all that. So, we can easily go up to an additional 1 million ton in the coming times.

items.statement: Q2 typically lull due to monsoon; early monsoon in May may allow some pickup if rain relief occurs
items.quote: Generally, for the steel industry, Q2 is a bit of a lull period because of what you rightly said. We are hopeful this year may be better because the current year Q1 the monsoon came so early; it came in the mid of May itself.

items.statement: Promoter shares 100% pledged to lenders and suppliers; release expected gradually after debt repayment
items.quote: So, these are mostly pledged to the lenders or maybe to some of our material suppliers. So, this slowly we will try to reduce it going forward, but not immediately, it may take some time.

items.statement: Brand promotion via ownership of SIMHADRI-Vizag Lions team in Andhra Premier League
items.quote: Yes, that is mainly as a brand promotion. SIMHADRI-Vizag Lions because SIMHADRI is a premium brand in Andhra where we manufacture the steel, business decision which was taken.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 is Rs 4.5-5.5 per SCM
items.quote: The Company's estimated EBITDA margin will be in the range of Rs. 4.5 to Rs. 5.5 for this financial year.

items.statement: Annual capex planned at Rs 800-1,000 crore for FY26
items.quote: The Company is also planning to incur annual CAPEX in the range of Rs. 800-Rs. 1,000 crores in this Financial Year.

items.statement: Industrial sales volume was 4.71 MMSCMD in Q1 FY26, down 6% QoQ due to Morbi shift to propane
items.quote: In the industrial segment, sales volume were 4.71 MMSCMD for quarter ended 30th June 2025, whereas the sales volume during the previous quarter was 5.03 MMSCMD, an overall decrease of nearly 6%.

items.statement: Morbi industrial volume fell to 2.51 MMSCMD in Q1 FY26 from 2.87 MMSCMD in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The Morbi volume reduced from 2.87 MMSCMD in Q4 FY '25 to 2.51 MMSCMD in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Non-Morbi industrial volume grew 2% QoQ to 2.20 MMSCMD in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The non-Morbi volume of 2.20 MMSCMD for quarter ended 30th June 2025 has grown from 2.16 MMSCMD during the previous quarter that is an increase of approximately 2%.

items.statement: CNG sales volume rose 12% YoY to record 3.72 MMSCMD in Q1 FY26
items.quote: CNG sales volume touched a record high of 3.72 MMSCMD, highlighting sustained demand momentum.

items.statement: CNG vehicle base grew 15% YoY to 15.65 lakh as of June 2025
items.quote: As of June 2025, the CNG vehicle base across GGL's network reached approximately 15.65 lakhs compared to 13.63 lakhs a year earlier, reflecting a solid 15% growth.

items.statement: Industrial gas price cut to maintain Rs 3.5/SCM premium over propane; current industrial price Rs 43.33/SCM
items.quote: The reduction also enabled GGL to maintain the price differential to propane, that is, natural gas premium by Rs. 3.50 per SCM.

items.statement: Current propane-to-gas price discount in Morbi is ~Rs 4/SCM after price cut
items.quote: Yes, it is close to Rs. 4. After the price cut, it is close to Rs. 4.

items.statement: Natural gas price Rs 1,327/MMBtu vs propane Rs 1,207/MMBtu currently
items.quote: Rs. 1,327 per MMBtu would be the gas price and Rs. 1,207 would be the propane price.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin Rs 7.17/SCM vs Rs 5.75/SCM in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The Company's rupee per SCM EBITDA margin for this quarter stood at Rs. 7.17 against Rs. 5.75 in the previous quarter.

items.statement: CNG margins compressed due to higher OMC commission; APM shortfall met via spot gas also impacts margins
items.quote: The margin is basically affected because we have increased the commission of the OMC. And that is the only reason. Otherwise, the CNG business, we are quite bullish about it.

items.statement: Added ~36,000 commissioned domestic customers and registered 39,000 in Q1 FY26; signed PNG agreement with Bathinda Military Station for 11,300 quarters
items.quote: GGL has added ~36,000 commissioned customers in Q1 FY '26 and registered 39,000 customers in Q1 FY '26. Importantly, GGL has signed gas sales agreement with Bathinda Military Station for the supply of PNG to over 11,300 residential quarters and 230 messes.

items.statement: Commissioned 3 new CNG stations in Q1 FY26; 70 FDODO stations under construction, targeting double-digit additions by December 2025
items.quote: During the quarter, GGL commissioned 3 new CNG stations, supporting its commitment to expanding reach and improving accessibility.

items.statement: 52 FDODO applications submitted, 43 approvals received; expect double-digit station additions before December
items.quote: Out of 70-odd agreements which we have already signed, 52 applications already submitted and 43 approvals we have already received, we mean those franchisees. So, I think, as I mentioned earlier in this conversation, that we will see double digit addition in the CNG station under FDODO scheme before December.

items.statement: Board approved sourcing and sale of propane/LPG to industrial customers; targeting 25% of ~167,000 MT/month Morbi propane market
items.quote: The Board of Directors of GGL at its meeting held on 5 th August has approved to undertake sourcing and sale of propane and LPG to industrial customers.

items.statement: Propane business to be sourced via direct imports on spot basis; no capex required except terminal capacity booking
items.quote: So, we will be importing it directly from the international markets.

items.statement: Non-Morbi industrial growth driven by long-term contracts with bulk consumers in Vapi, Valsad and other regions
items.quote: We are in touch with various bigger kind of consumers whom we are now targeting them with some fixed-term contracts rather than having a contract which had termination provisions. So, we are going for long-term contracts in non-Morbi regions like Vapi, Valsad and other places.

items.statement: 370 Morbi units gas-only, 530 dual-fuel capable; export-oriented units prefer gas for quality
items.quote: So, almost 1-1.5 million equivalent gas consuming consumers are only on gas. So, basically, 370 units are only on gas and 530 units are, they have the dual facilities. They can use gas, they can use propane as well.

items.statement: Propane market has 5+ existing players; GGL advantage is working capital relief for customers using existing financial security
items.quote: We are basically targeting close to 25% of this market and what we intend to do is basically we want to become an integrated energy supplier for all their energy needs. So, they don't have to shift from one supplier to the other and the advantage that we think we can bring is basically we can help them reduce their working capital requirements since they already have some financial security alread

items.statement: PNGRB zone reduction from 3 to 2 zones positive for GGL; currently 14/53/21 split, post-change 42% in zone 1, 46% in zone 2
items.quote: Based on the present tariffs which are there, there will be positive impact for us.

items.statement: Morbi ceramic exports >Rs 1,000 crore/month and growing; no current utilization issues despite tariff concerns
items.quote: Exports are already in excess of Rs. 1,000 crore per month and growing at a reasonable rate. So, as we speak, I do not think there is any issue as of now.

items.statement: Credit rating AAA stable and A1+ short-term affirmed by CRISIL, CARE, India Ratings
items.quote: Gujarat Gas continues to have a credit rating of AAA stable and a short-term rating of A1+ affirmed from CRISIL Care and India Ratings.

items.statement: Scheme of arrangement filed with MCA; expecting approval in Q3 FY26; simultaneously pursuing other regulatory approvals
items.quote: The matter is under active consideration of Ministry of Corporate Affairs and we are expecting approval of the scheme in Q3. Considering longer than expected time taken in completing MCA process, we have also simultaneously initiated process for obtaining approval from other regulatory authorities.

items.statement: Priority sector gas allocation 51% overall (100% domestic, 41% CNG) in Q1 FY26; APM shortfall met via New Well, HPHT, long-term and spot
items.quote: During the 1st quarter, the Company received around 100% allocation towards domestic segment and 41% allocation towards the CNG segment. Thus, we have an overall allocation of 51% to the priority segment from the government.

items.statement: Gas sourcing mix: 34% short-term contract, 38% long-term contract, rest domestic (APM, New Well, HPHT ~0.7 MMSCMD)
items.quote: So, coming to your question, the gas from short-term contract is basically 34%, long-term contract is 38% and the rest is all domestic gas, majority of that coming from APM and New Well Gas.

items.statement: Morbi Q2 volumes expected lower at 2.3-2.5 MMSCMD due to Janmashtami festival and propane price correction
items.quote: It could be in the range of 2.3-2.5.

items.statement: Uncertainty on Morbi volumes due to propane price movements, geopolitical dynamics, and consumer demand
items.quote: Persistent uncertainties related to tariffs and geopolitical dynamics continue to cloud the overall business outlook. We continue to monitor the various aspects affecting the volumes, namely price movements of spot RLNG and alternate fuels, and consumer goods demand across all our operating areas and shall adjust to such market dynamics so as to maintain balance between margins and volumes.

items.statement: Management confident of crossing committed thresholds for FY26 given Q1 revenue of Rs 221 cr and order book of Rs 3,000+ cr
items.quote: with a 2.2 gigawatt of orders already on hand, which constitutes roughly about Rs. 3,000 plus crores of order book in terms of value, I am definitely very confident that we will be crossing all the committed thresholds.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book stands at 2.22 GW valued at roughly Rs 3,000+ cr for KP Energy standalone
items.quote: Our current order book stands at about 2.22 GW, inching us closer to the ambitious target of 10 GW on the group level.

items.statement: Order book execution timelines vary: some orders complete by September 2025, some by December 2025, some beyond current financial year
items.quote: there are certain orders which get completed in September '25. There are orders which prolong up to even December and there are some which have the timeline beyond the current financial year as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 220.6 cr, up 63% YoY, highest ever Q1 revenue
items.quote: The Company has reported total revenue on a consolidated basis for the 1st Quarter of FY'26 at Rs. 220.6 crores, as against that at Rs. 135.2 crores during the 1st Quarter of FY'25, thereby reporting an increase of 63%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated EBITDA Rs 49.6 cr, up 63% YoY, highest ever Q1 EBITDA
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the 1st Quarter of FY'26 stood at Rs. 49.6 crores, representing a 63% year-over-year increase in comparison to the 1st Quarter of FY'25, which stood at Rs. 30.4 crores.

items.statement: EPC gross margins 15-18%, IPP gross margins 65-75%, O&M currently 1% of revenue but expected to grow after free O&M period ends
items.quote: typically an EPC contract would have gross margins of about 15 % to 18%. And in case of power sale, the margins would be around 65% to 75%.

items.statement: EBITDA margins roughly same as gross margins for both EPC and IPP segments (1-2% difference)
items.quote: It will be roughly 1 % or 2% plus minus but more or less the same because we hardly have anything which falls between the EBITDA and gross in terms of EPC contracts.

items.statement: Revenue split Q1 FY26: EPC 95%, IPP power sale 5%, O&M 1%
items.quote: With this quarter, we are standing at 95% on the EPC segment. The power sale has been from 3 % to 5%. We are standing at 5% in this quarter and O&M is currently at 1%.

items.statement: IPP portfolio at 48.5 MW (37 MW wind + 11.5 MW solar), fully operational; targeting additional 50 MW IPP in phased manner
items.quote: This quarter we may look for 20 megawatt to be added in the coming months, not maybe this quarter but in the coming months we are looking for that out of the 50 megawatt which we have a target

items.statement: IPP expansion funded through internal accruals, not debt or equity dilution
items.quote: We are trying from internal accruals. We are planning from internal accruals.

items.statement: Primary debt driver is IPP projects; planning to phase 50 MW IPP addition to avoid overloading balance sheet
items.quote: the primary reason for the debt, Darshil, is the IPP project that we have taken up and that is where the long term debt arises from. So, well as I told before as well that we are planning for another 50 megawatt to reach our target of, Company target of 100 megawatt of IPP but we want to phase it out and do it in a planned manner, so that we do not really load our balance sheet with the debt

items.statement: Average realization: solar Rs 7-8/unit gross (Rs 5-5.5 net), wind Rs 6.5-7/unit gross (Rs 4.5-5 net); GUVNL contract Rs 2.43/unit but effective rate higher due to transmission charges borne by GUVNL
items.quote: average realization would be around Rs.7-Rs. 8 per unit in terms of solar on a gross basis and on wind it would be roughly around Rs. 6.5 to Rs. 7 on a gross basis.

items.statement: Demand tremendously high: India needs ~40 GW/year to reach 500 GW target; KP Energy creating resources to meet demand
items.quote: The thing is that, the demand is tremendously high. Why it is high, because today whatever we have completed at the country level, it is 230 gigawatt, another 270 gigawatt, that emulates to 500 gigawatt. So, per year, there is a requirement demand cycle is over 40 gigawatts.

items.statement: KP Energy differentiated by end-to-end wind EPC capability (WRA to grid connectivity), hybrid wind-solar execution, and in-house crane/logistics assets; few pure-play wind EPC peers
items.quote: right from the WRA that is the wind resource analysis , right from the conceptualization of a wind farm until the grid connectivity and the infrastructure whereby the power eventually gets energized and evacuated , the entire set of activities under one EPC contractor is something which is not very easily found.

items.statement: Order book includes 1.3 GW from KPI Green, balance from other entities; executed 92 MW DC capacity for KPI Green (75.2 MW solar + 16.95 MW wind) and 23.1 MW for Aditya Birla
items.quote: About, just a minute, if you allow me a moment, 1.3 gigawatts is from KPI and the balance is from other entities.

items.statement: Expecting order inflow by Q2 FY26 (September 2025) as per CMD guidance; bid pipeline ~3 GW
items.quote: as already announced by our honorable CMD we are expecting an order in flow by Quarter 2 and that is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Other income normalized at Rs 1-1.1 cr per quarter (Rs 4-5 cr annually); Q4 FY25 higher due to insurance claim
items.quote: on a quarter-to-quarter basis, you can expect about 1-1.10 crores roughly on quarterly basis. That will be normalized.

items.statement: IPP portfolio generation: Q1 FY26 unit generation 2.65 cr units vs 0.98 cr units in Q1 FY25; solar PLF 20-23%, wind PLF 35-37%
items.quote: The quarterly unit generation during the financial year '26-Q1 rose to 2.65 crores from 0.98 crores during the 1st Quarter of FY'25.

items.statement: O&M portfolio exceeds 595 MW; NTPC/Indian Oil CPP project (462-464 MW) on track for completion in FY26 with Rs 15 cr value addition
items.quote: With a portfolio now exceeding 595 MW, we offer end -to-end support, including preventive care, data -driven diagnostics, and efficiency enhancements focused on the balance of plant components.

items.statement: Offshore wind at nascent stage; 500 MW each in Gujarat and Tamil Nadu under discussion; viability requires Rs 10-15/unit tariff with VGF; KP Energy in planning stage for participation post 5 years
items.quote: they will declare in my opinion to see that this offshore initiative will come after 5 years from today and we are in the planning stage how to accommodate ourselves for this offshore initiative like be it in the BOP or in a supply chain or some sort of other activities.

items.statement: Monsoon arrived a month earlier in Q1 FY26 affecting execution; seasonality managed through milestone planning but monsoon impact remains
items.quote: this time with almost a month e arlier, the monsoon has arrived a month earlier. So, yes, this has been one of the factors. But more so, I think there are activities which are well planned and they are being taken care of

items.statement: Group CEO Dr. Alok Das and Group CFO Salim Yahoo joined CFO Shabana Bajari and WTD Affan Patel on call
items.quote: We are pleased to have with us the Management Team represented by Mr. Affan Faruk Patel – Whole-Time Director, Dr. Alok Das – Group CEO , Ms. Shabana Bajari – Chief Financial Officer of KP Energy, Mr. Salim Yahoo – Group CFO.

items.statement: No forward-looking revenue or EBITDA guidance provided for FY26
items.quote: I'm afraid we don't give a forward -looking guidance related to our revenues and our EBITDA for the year, but I'd be happy to take any questions in terms of specificity in terms of how the business would grow.

items.statement: DEX signed new long-term contracts including AYUSH Ministry Rs 24 crore, IIBF renewal Rs 14 crore, NISM Rs 15 crore, extended UIDAI contract
items.quote: Some of the new deals we've cracked this year include a deal for the AYUSH Ministry, which is a Rs. 24 crore deal. IIBF is an old customer which we've renewed, which is a Rs. 14 crore deal. NISM is a critical customer through the National Stock Exchange itself. That's another Rs. 15 crore deal.

items.statement: DEX executed 17+ lakh assessments in Q1 for key clients IRDAI, ICAI, NTA, DGT, NISM
items.quote: We executed more than 17 lakh assessments in this quarter alone, including for some of our key clients like IRDAI, ICAI, NTA, and so on.

items.statement: Utsav wedding business closed 5 projects for execution till March with pipeline for Q2-Q4
items.quote: We have closed five projects for the weddings to be executed from now till March as of now. There are a couple of more in pipelines which would, as and when they get closed, would add to the top line.

items.statement: Consolidated operating EBITDA grew 66% YoY to Rs 17.5 crore; DEX EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 12.8 crore
items.quote: Our consolidated revenue rose impressively by 58% year on year, reaching Rs. 149.84 crores, a testament to our expanding footprint and strong market positioning, particularly through DEX. This growth has translated into an equally encouraging 66 % increase in operating EBITDA, now standing at Rs. 17.5 crores.

items.statement: Standalone operating EBITDA fell 33% to Rs 5 crore due to acquisition finance costs
items.quote: From a standalone perspective, our operating revenue was down 9 % to Rs. 77 crores, whereas our standalone operating EBITDA was down 33 % to Rs. 5 crores.

items.statement: MarTech EBITDA declined marginally from Rs 2.8 crore to Rs 2.5 crore due to investment in international and tech teams
items.quote: Due to the slight change of kind of business you do in Q1, the EBITDA declined very marginally from Rs. 2.8 crores to Rs. 2.5 crores, but as we get into Q2 and Q3, these are heavy and high margin businesses, we would see the overall EBITDA broadly coming back on track during the rest of the quarters.

items.statement: 361 DM business reported first positive EBITDA of Rs 8 lakh after many quarters
items.quote: After many quarters, this was the first quarter when that business reported a positive EBITDA, even if it was a small amount of 8 lakhs during the quarter.

items.statement: Test prep industry in churn with shift to self-prep models; students spending same amount but in smaller chunks across multiple programs
items.quote: Test prep industry, especially the graduate student segment is in a churn. And it is a change of habits. Partly it is movement away from a completely guided program to a self-sufficiency kind of program, which is happening.

items.statement: BBA-IPM billing grew 12%; law intake consistent with expectations; CUET shift to self-prep continues
items.quote: We are confident in the continued traction of our BBA and IPM products, which have recorded a 12% increase in billing. Our law intake remained consistent with the last year and on track with our expectations.

items.statement: Launched low-value SKUs (Rs 5,000-8,000) including test series and self-tapped programs; AFA (Attempt from Anywhere) to strengthen classroom programs
items.quote: We have introduced new variants, which are getting a good response. We doubled down on test series. We have self -tapped program, which are Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 8,000 kinds of programs, and which cater to only one section or one part of the segment.

items.statement: MarTech pivoting to AI-first practice; VIRSA AI-driven lead gen tool gaining traction with Salesforce, Infosys, Reddington; AI transformation to complete by year-end
items.quote: VIRSA, which is an automated AI-driven lead gen and lead management tool, which we had just launched at the earlier part of this year, has seen extremely positive traction with Salesforce, Infosys, Reddington.

items.statement: DEX-Career Launcher synergy: MBA online tests configured on DEX platform; first test conducted with positive initial response
items.quote: Then as we speak, right now, we are configuring the tests on the DEX platform. So, for MBA we are doing an online test for all CAT students as of now. This is the first, let's say a synergy between DEX and Career launcher.

items.statement: DEX key client retention successful post-NSE transition; major clients IRDAI, NISM, DGT, NTA, ICAI retained
items.quote: One of the most important things for us as we made the migration from being a NSE parentage company to being a standalone entity, DEXIT Global, was to ensure that all our clients, especially the major ones, continued to move with the organization.

items.statement: MarTech AI-first transformation blueprint defined; completion expected by end of FY26 with margin benefits from FY27
items.quote: We are currently in process with certain processes already beginning to take shape. The blueprint for the remaining processes is defined. And by the end of this year, we would have completed this transformation, which would bring in significant number of efficiencies in pre -sales, sales process, and delivery, resulting in margin expansion, which would probably start reflecting next year.

items.statement: Rs 200 crore loan at 11.9% for DEX acquisition; annual interest cost ~Rs 24 crore (Rs 6-6.5 crore per quarter); targeting significant debt reduction over 3-year window
items.quote: most of our investors are aware, we had taken a Rs. 200 crore loan to fund the acquisition, and we had used about Rs. 32 crores from our internal accruals to fund the acquisition. Interest rate on that is about 11.9%. So, we anticipate an annual interest cost of about Rs. 24 crores for this year, which would translate about six to six and a half crores hitting our P &L every quarter this year.

items.statement: DEX IPO committee formed under Non-Executive Chairman guidance; exploring strategic investments and potential IPO within 3-year window
items.quote: we have formulated an IPO committee in DEXIT global, which is looking at both strategic investments coming into that business and a potential IPO for that business in due course. We're looking at a three -year window for that to fructify.

items.statement: DEX conducted 11 million assessments in FY25; targeting client base expansion in FY26; currently 4th largest standalone digital assessments company globally
items.quote: We're already the fourth largest standalone digital assessments company in the world . And we look to build on the 11 million assessments done in FY25 by expanding our client base over this year.

items.statement: DEX seasonality: annuity contracts ~Rs 20 crore/quarter (IRDAI); date-driven exams like DGT concentrated in Q2
items.quote: Exams like IRDAI work with that kind of format and typically contribute about Rs. 20 crores a quarter, which is almost like a specific annuity business. And then there are other exams which are date specific. For example, the Directed General of Training (DGT) exam that happens in the second quarter of the year.

items.statement: Test prep average pricing decreased due to launch of smaller value SKUs while volumes maintained
items.quote: This has resulted in launch of significant number of smaller value SKUs, which has resulted in decrease in average pricing, though the volumes are maintained.

items.statement: Discontinued operations (NEET, IIT, Bank SSC) only incurring expenses for servicing existing students; small expense for couple more quarters
items.quote: Right now, the discontinued business lines, the only expenses are related to servicing of existing students for whom the IIT exam would happen later this year. There is a small expense related to that which could hit us for a couple more quarters.

items.statement: Walked away from NEET, IIT, Bank SSC business lines in Q4 FY25 to avoid perceived conflict of interest when applying for NTA contracts
items.quote: This, if you recall, is because of our decision in Q4 of last year to walk away from certain business lines – NEET, IIT, Bank SSC on account of the significant business opportunity that exists for DEX as in terms of contracts that would be available for the company as we apply for them and our keenness to ensure that there is no perceived conflict of interest when we apply to the National Testing

items.statement: Short-to-medium term profitability impacted by Rs 12 crore higher finance costs and increased D&A from DEX acquisition intangibles; net loss Rs 3.71 crore
items.quote: As you would recall, there is a sharp increase in the finance costs compared to last year, 12 crores more, owing to the Rs. 200 crore loan that we have taken to fund this acquisition. This, coupled with a significant rise in Depreciation & Amortization on account of the intangible assets created from the DEX acquisition, has resulted in a net loss of Rs. 3.71 crores at the consolidated level.

items.statement: MarTech international and digital revenue trending toward 50% of total (from 40% in FY25); digital/tech revenue Rs 9 crore, international Rs 12 crore in Q1
items.quote: last year in FY25, almost 40% of our total revenue out of Rs. 150 crores came either from international markets or was Technology business or Digital business. Now in this, in the first quarter, digital and tech itself has grown to about nine crores and international business has grown to about Rs. 12 crores. So, we are trending towards closer to 50% in terms of international, technology and digit

items.statement: DEX acquisition completed February 2025; full integration underway; synergy projects announced across CL, DEX, Kestone with benefits visible in 2-4 quarters
items.quote: With the full integration of DEXIT Global, which was earlier called NSEIT, and strategic challenges that have also impacted our bottom line this quarter. Our consolidated revenue rose impressively by 58% year on year, reaching Rs. 149.84 crores, a testament to our expanding footprint and strong market positioning, particularly through DEX.

items.statement: AI dataset licensing pipeline expanded from 2 to 7 companies, opportunity seen for next 2-3 years
items.quote: year, we were speaking to just two companies. At present, we are speaking to seven companie s. So, things are at various stages. We’ve offered our content to multiple people. Decisions are being a bit here and there. But I think the opportunity is huge. It is not on ly about our basic da tasets; it is about converting into a little more complex dataset. So, we are speaking to a lot of people. And

items.statement: Gross margins expected to improve due to lower paper prices and higher-margin AI licensing revenue
items.quote: We expect our gross margins to be slightly better as paper prices are a tad lower than last year. And of course, our digital data licensing revenue which have higher gross margins should also add to that.

items.statement: Paper prices declined 5%-7% since April 2025, currently stable, expected to remain soft
items.quote: So, paper prices have been soft, thankfully. And we have seen a decline of 5% to 7%. Right now, the paper prices are stable. And we are not expecting too much increase in the paper prices. Depending on the foreign poli cies also, tariffs and everything, that will also determine the paper prices. So, it's very difficult to say as of now what will be the paper prices in the next 3 to 4 months. But I

items.statement: Capex of Rs35-40 crore over next 2 years, mainly for printing press setup next year
items.quote: It's about Rs35 crores to Rs40 crores for the next 2 years.

items.statement: Integrated warehousing facility now functional; integrated press project to complete in 12 months, adding 2-3 machines, 15-20% production capacity and efficiency advantage
items.quote: So, I think overall, there would be a 15% to 20% advantage in terms of production capacity increase, plus efficiency, plus cost ad vantages. Exact figures, as of now, it's very difficult to share right now. Bu t as of now, it will be tangible and intangible both, but there will be a substantial improvement in th e next 2-3 years, in the production and efficiency of the

items.statement: New infrastructure capacity sufficient for next 8-10 years including potential acquisitions
items.quote: So, I think the capacities that we will have, will suffice for next 8 to 10 years in terms of infrastructure. There shouldn't be any problem in the next 10 years.

items.statement: NCERT new syllabus books for Classes 4,5,7,8 expected in FY26, full adoption by FY27; Classes 9-12 later in FY27
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect NCERT to release books on the new syllabus for Class 4th, 5th, 7th and 8th over the course of the year. We expect the full adoption of the new syllabus books by FY27 and are fully equipped to utili ze this opportunity over the next 2 sales seasons

items.statement: Q1 FY26 working capital metrics at historic lows: receivable days 89, inventory days 218, NWC days 119
items.quote: Our Q1 Net Working capital days was at 119 days (vs. 132 days in Q1FY25).

items.statement: Net cash position increased to Rs1,161m after Rs141m dividend payment
items.quote: Our Net Cash Position stood at Rs1,161m (vs. Net Cash position of Rs1,036m in Q4FY25), after dividend payment of Rs141m.

items.statement: Actively evaluating 3 M&A opportunities (Test Prep, International Board, Regional) total revenue <Rs50 crore, funded by internal accruals
items.quote: So, Niteen, one opportunity I th ink we've already disclosed. There is diligence going on in one of them, which is in the Test Pr ep segment. We are looking at two other opportunities as well. One is in the International Board segment, which is a small one, and one is in the regional segment. So, these are smaller ones that we are looking at right now, not very huge. In total, I think th e revenue

items.statement: M&A acquisitions to be funded from internal accruals, cash surplus Rs116 crore, max payout Rs50-60 crore
items.quote: No, all internal accruals. We already have about Rs116 crores of cash surplus. We estimate that the maximum payout should be around Rs50crores - Rs60 crores.

items.statement: FY26 growth driven by 4-5% pricing and 6-7% volume; AI licensing and CUET coaching as new verticals
items.quote: So, pricing is about 4%-5%, and then rest of it is volume, about 6-7% volume growth.

items.statement: NCERT segment highly fragmented with organized and unorganized players; S Chand leverages brand, relationships, portfolio, service quality
items.quote: NCERT is a government body and that is also one of our competitors. But there are lots of private players who are in this segment as well. There are smaller players also, bigger players also, organized players also, unorganiz ed players. It is a very diversified, unorganized market, I would say, overall. And we being the largest there, we get an advantage of our brand, of our relationship with the

items.statement: NCERT syllabus rollout delayed and fragmented; Classes 4,5,7,8 in FY26, Classes 9-12 in FY27
items.quote: The implementation of NCERT has taken a long time and it is quite delayed, and it is coming in broken pieces. So, it is not coming in one go. It is coming in different classes, one class, two class, three class etc. So, that whole effect of NCERT is not coming up as we were expecting over a short 2-3 years period of time.

items.statement: Employee count around 1,900, close to 2,000
items.quote: Around 1,900. Close to 2,000.

items.statement: AI licensing revenue potential significant, 40% content sourced externally in last 12 months, vernacular demand rising
items.quote: In the la st 12 months, we've sourced almost 40% of the content from outside. Basically, it’s meeting your customer's requirements and then trying to sell it to them. You're servicing their requirements at the moment

items.statement: NCERT book release timing uncertain; if after December, sales execution becomes difficult
items.quote: Hopefully. Hopefully. All this depends on the timing. If it comes before December, then it will be easier. It comes after December; it will become little tough.

items.statement: Overall premium growth expected at 9-10% YoY for FY26
items.quote: So going forward, we would look at this year, maybe for the entire year, we expect the growth to be between 9% and 10% compared to last year.

items.statement: International premium growth expected at 17-20% YoY for FY26
items.quote: So typically, international would grow about 17% to 20% year-on-year for this year and domestic would be about 6.5% or 7%.

items.statement: Full-year combined ratio expected around 107-107.5% for FY26
items.quote: This year, we are expecting that to come down by at least 1%, maybe slightly more. So the combined should be closer to 107% -- 107.5% is what we believe it will be.

items.statement: International combined ratio expected to improve to 116-118% for FY26 from 126% last year
items.quote: And what we believe is from 126%, we should ideally be coming to around 118%, 116% is what we would be looking at for this year.

items.statement: Domestic combined ratio expected to remain around 104-105% for FY26
items.quote: I think if you see overall, we are looking at a combined of around 107%, 106.8%, 107% for this year, in which overall, the domestic curve will continue to be at around 104%, 105% and Foreign will come much better than what it was last year.

items.statement: Commission ratio expected to normalize to 18-19% for full year FY26
items.quote: Going forward, we will see that it kind of settles down around 18%, 19% for the year.

items.statement: Expense ratio expected to remain stable at 0.9-1.1% for FY26
items.quote: It will only change between maybe 0.9% to 1.1%. So honestly, it's not something that is going to move the needle as far as the combined ratios go.

items.statement: Capital gains expected around INR4,100 crores for FY26 similar to FY25
items.quote: For the whole year of 31/3/25, it was INR4,108 crores. So I mean, going by what we have booked, we can expect it to be around the same level or even slightly higher for the entire year.

items.statement: IFRS/IndAS parallel reporting expected to start from Q3 FY26
items.quote: We'll actually start doing that much earlier. An d we will be in a position to hopefully give you both the figures, the IGAAP as well as the IndAS figures, maybe from the third quarter of this year

items.statement: International growth driven by new business from Jan 1 renewals after credit rating upgrade
items.quote: The top line growth on the international has grown because of our credit rating improvement, which happened in October last year, which gave us a chance to look at really good businesses on the 1st Jan renewals, and we managed to write a substantial amount of increase there.

items.statement: Domestic fire premium expected to be higher than last year despite Q1 accounting change impact
items.quote: So yes, going forward, fire premium would go up, and I think it would be definitely higher than what it was for the entire year last year.

items.statement: Health portfolio de-growth due to non-renewal of underperforming treaties
items.quote: We have not renewed a couple of treaties that we wrote last year. So to that extent, health will be slightly down.

items.statement: New business lines like surety, cyber and trade credit providing diversification and growth
items.quote: But overall, we are also writing in new clauses of business like suret y and cyber and trade credit, et cetera. So that gives us a diversification in our book as well as provides a growth

items.statement: Q1 FY26 combined ratio improved to 106.94% from 109.6% YoY
items.quote: The combined ratio has reduced by 2.66% to 106.94% for the quarter ended 30/6/25 as against 109.6% for the quarter ended 30/6/24 and as against 108.8% for the entire year 2024-'25.

items.statement: Underwriting loss reduced 30% to INR907.76 crores despite two large losses
items.quote: In spite of this, the underwr iting loss reduced by 30% to INR907.76 crores for the quarter ended 30/6/25 as compared to INR1,288.53 crores for the same quarter last year

items.statement: Profit before tax up 61% to INR2,243.54 crores; PAT up 70% to INR1,752.22 crores
items.value: PBT INR2,243.54 crores, PAT INR1,752.22 crores
items.quote: Profit before tax has increased by 61.04% to INR2,243.54 crores as compared to INR1,393.16 crores, for the quarter ended 30/6/24. And the profit after tax has increased by 70% to INR1,752.22 crores as compared to INR1,036.36 crores.

items.statement: Quarterly catastrophic reserve provision of INR143.47 crores reduced PBT and PAT
items.quote: I would also like to inform that we have started the practice of providing for catastrophic reserve on a quarterly basis and not annually as done in the previous years. If this were not done, the PBT and PAT figures would have been higher by INR143.47 crores.

items.statement: Loss ratio improvement driven by Agri, Health and Engineering segments
items.quote: Basically, quarter-on-quarter, Fire is more or less the same. I think the improvement has come from Motor -- no, not really. Motor on a combined, yes. It's more from Agri, maybe a bit of Health. And yes, these are the ones that have contributed to the improvement.

items.statement: Segment combined ratios: Fire 106%, Motor 107%, Health 111%, Agri 86%, Cargo 104%, Hull 44%
items.quote: If I see the overall combined, combined for Fire is at around 106%, Motor is 107%, Health has come down to 111%, Agri at 86%. But honestly, Agri should go up a little as the year goes by. Cargo has come down. It was a class, which internationally we had issues with. That has come down to 104 %. Hull is at 44%, but again, this will be a one -off.

items.statement: Obligatory business combined ratio around 104% reflecting domestic performance
items.quote: So it will be more or less reflecting the combined of our domestic business, okay? So if you look at our domestic business, it currently is at around 104%. For the last couple of years, it's kind of hovering around that figure. And obligatory would also be around that.

items.statement: Life reinsurance is purely voluntary with no obligatory cessions
items.quote: Life, there is no obligatory. It's only for non -life. Life is purely the business that we write voluntarily. There is no obligatory there, yes.

items.statement: Motor runoff from stopped US contract expected to continue for 2-3 years
items.quote: Motor is where we would expect -- I mean, typically, Motor third party is a long-tailed class. We would possibly expect this to go on for another 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Property pricing on direct side held viable; reinsurance to benefit if premiums rise
items.quote: We have been trying very hard to ensure that the primary insurance rates stay and it is more or less held on until now. So we are very confident that, that will continue to happen during the year.

items.statement: International market saw rate softening at Jan 1 renewals despite credit rating upgrade
items.quote: In fact, I would say that for 1st Jan, the market was pretty soft, and we did see rate softening.

items.statement: Air India aviation loss estimated at $400-450 million market-wide; GIC share adequately provided
items.quote: We believe it could be closer to $400 million to $450 million because, again, like I said, there are multiple classes getting involved.

items.statement: Jindal Poly Films fire loss: 100% loss INR2,300 crores; GIC share INR925 crores fully provided
items.quote: Jindal Poly Films, which is a fire loss, where the 100% loss figures are INR2,300 crores and GIC share is about INR925 crores, which is fully provided in our books.

items.statement: Solvency ratio robust at 3.85% vs 3.36% YoY

items.statement: PAT fell 4% YoY from Rs.182 crores to Rs.176 crores.
