items.statement: Average daily turnover Rs.2,23,232 crores (derivatives Rs.2,20,263 crores, cash Rs.2,968 crores) in Q1 FY26 vs Rs.1,92,871 crores in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Average daily turnover was Rs. 2,23,232 crores which was broken down into Rs. 2,20,263 crores in derivative and cash was Rs. 2,968 crores in this quarter which was in the previous Q4 FY25 was Rs.1,92,871 crores

items.statement: F&O market share 0.62% and cash market share 2.57% in Q1 FY26, broadly stable QoQ.
items.quote: We are at an F&O market share of 0.62% which is broadly in the same range and for cash market share it is 2.57%, which was in the previous quarter 2.51% and again that is broadly hovering around the same range.

items.statement: Added about 50 RMs for wealth management, mix of HNI, ultra HNI, and mass affluent with higher proportion of HNI/ultra HNI.
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier also, we have broadly added about 50 RMs and they are a mix of both HNI, ultra HNI as well as mass afloat RMs.

items.statement: Wealth management targeting customers with 5-25 crores and >25 crores networth, differentiating from <1 crore base.
items.quote: we have a large base of customers with less than 1 crore network and the segment which we are targeting will be say maybe in the 5 to 25, greater than 25 crores.

items.statement: Building own AIF/PMS manufacturing while maintaining open architecture model; currently distributing external mutual funds, AIFs, PMS.
items.quote: we are also trying to build our own manufacturing practice and if you remember we have a small AIF and PMS business which we have recruited people to scale it up. So, we will be manufacturing also. But having said that, we believe that manufacturing is one of the products we have and as a house, genetically and generically speaking, we are more open for open architecture model.

items.statement: Non-institutional business cost-to-income ratio around 75% for FY26, elevated due to wealth build-out, benefits expected next year.
items.quote: the broad cost-to-income ratio for the retail or the non-institutional side will be in the range of 75% and I think this year it will be elevated and we hope to see benefits of scale trickling in next year.

items.statement: Wealth management revenue Rs.28 crores in Q1 FY26 vs Rs.40 crores full year FY25; cost was Rs.70 crores full year FY25.
items.quote: last year we had a revenue of roughly about Rs.40 crores and cost was about Rs.70 crores. So, we had a hit of about Rs. 30 crores and this quarter we have made revenues of about Rs. 28 crores

items.statement: Investment banking and institutional equities income roughly Rs.200 crores (brokerage Rs.150 crores, banking Rs.50 crores).
items.quote: we have roughly about Rs.200 crores of investment banking and institutional equities income and the rough numbers will be about Rs.150 crores is brokerage and Rs.50 crores is banking.

items.statement: Investment banking pipeline strong for full year FY26, though Q2 may see slowdown due to current volatility.
items.quote: investment banking pipeline is quite strong and if you remember 1st Quarter of this year, which is Q4 FY 25 was a lackluster quarter. So, now, when the market has revived, it picked up. Maybe given the current volatility, deal pipeline might again witness some slowdown. For the full year, I am quite optimistic about our deal pipeline and closure.

items.statement: Insurance premium collected Q1 FY26: life/non-life Rs.10 crores (vs Rs.23 crores Q4 FY25, Rs.14 crores Q1 FY25); general insurance ~Rs.30 crores; plus Livlong wellness affiliate business.
items.quote: total premium collected for this first year for Q1 was about Rs.10 crores, which for the previous quarter was Rs.23 crores and 1st Quarter of FY25 was Rs.14 crores. So, there has been some dip in this and for general insurance was also in the rough range of Rs.30 crores.

items.statement: No forward guidance provided for FY26.
items.quote: No, unfortunately, we have not given any guidance. I am sorry.

items.statement: Distribution AUM at Rs.35,700 crores as of Q1 FY26, focus area for growth.
items.quote: we are roughly at about Rs. 35,700 crores and that is the number which we are targeting to grow.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer business expected to achieve around 25% growth in FY26
items.quote: Based on current customer discussions and approvals, we are confident of achieving around 25% growth as guided earlier.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer revenue growth expected to continue quarter by quarter in FY26
items.quote: We expect this revenue growth to continue quarter by quarter.

items.statement: R32 commercial production started in Q2 FY26 via retrofitting at minimal capex
items.quote: We are excited to announce the start of commercial production of R32 in Q2 FY '26, which is several quarters ahead of schedule. This has been achieved through strategic retrofitting and at minimal capital expenditure.

items.statement: R32 capacity to reach 20,000 metric tons by end of FY26 through phased retrofitting
items.quote: We aim to ramp up our R32 capacity to 20,000 metric tons in phases by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Further fluoropolymer capacity expansions planned as optimal utilization approaches
items.quote: We will continue to invest in expanding our fluoropolymer capacities to support future growth.

items.statement: EV battery chemicals capex of Rs. 1,200 crores planned for FY26 remains on track
items.quote: we had already indicated that we have invested close to Rs. 1,300 crores in EV till the last financial year, and we are planning to add another Rs. 1,200 crores in this financial year going forward. A nd it remains as per the plan

items.statement: Renewable energy investment of Rs. 190 crores made so far in 450 MW project
items.quote: as a Company, we h ave invested close to Rs. 190 crores till date as an equity. So, the total plan is to be a partner in this 450 megawatt of renewable energy

items.statement: Full Rs. 150 crore annual savings from renewable energy expected from FY27
items.quote: That's right. So, FY '27 will be the first year of full operation, so the full benefit will be available in that year, you are right.

items.statement: Strong traction in fluoropolymers from semiconductor, aerospace, automotive and EV sectors
items.quote: Rising demand from key sectors such as automotive, semicon and electric vehicles and energy storage systems is opening up significant growth opportunities for us.

items.statement: Improved product mix drove 33% EBITDA growth in Chemical segment in Q1 FY26
items.quote: This strong performance was primarily driven by sustained growth in our fluoropolymers business and an improved product mix.

items.statement: Working capital reduced from 188 days to 172 days in Q1 FY26 with further reduction targeted
items.quote: The management is focused on working capital reduction; and thereby, the working capital has reduced from 188 days to 172 days in this quarter, and efforts are on to further reduce over the next few quarters.

items.statement: US tariff impact limited as PTFE, micro powders and most battery materials are exempt; new fluoropolymers face 25% duty but have inelastic demand
items.quote: Products, however, like PTFE and micro powders, and majority of our battery materials, are exempt under the reciprocal duty list. The revised duty, however, appl ies to a few of our new fluoropolymers as these products are highly specialized with very few suppliers globally

items.statement: Fluoropolymer growth driven by volume ramp-up from approved qualifications and legacy player exit
items.quote: It will be largely driven by the volumes. As we were already mentioning that we are under the process of pitching in for the legacy players and also the approvals from coming from the other sectors on the high-end grades.

items.statement: New fluoropolymer capacities added in past years expected to reach optimal utilization by end of FY26
items.quote: The capacity which we have added in new Fluoropolymer segments over the past few years are expected to reach optimal utilization levels by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: LFP chemistry requires almost double the salt per GWh compared to NMC, benefiting battery chemicals business
items.quote: The salt requirement is, Nitin, just as a rule of thumb, is almost double in case of LFP per gigawatt hour compared to NMC chemistry.

items.statement: Battery chemicals revenue to start trickling in H2 FY26 with meaningful ramp-up in FY27
items.quote: We expect the sales from the EV business to start trickling in by the second half of this year. It's been quite a little bit, okay? But we will start seeing more meaningful numbers perhaps in FY '27.

items.statement: PVDF binder capacity for EV batteries in place, final qualifications expected by end of calendar year
items.quote: In PVDF, we are at the very final stages of qualifications. In fact, it's going through the scaled-up trial right now. And we expect the qualifications to be complete by the end of this calendar year.

items.statement: No plans for US manufacturing facility or JV for fluoropolymers due to integrated India facility advantage
items.quote: No, we are right now not looking at US or any JV like that. So, we are not looking at definitely not, if you mean to say in fluoropolymers. So, we are not, not looking at that at the moment.

items.statement: Chemical segment EBITDA margin expanded 495 bps to 28% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 33% year -on-year to Rs. 354 crores, with EBITDA margin expanding by 495 basis points to 28%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved ~500 bps to 27% in Q1 FY26 from 22% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Consolidated revenue from operations stood at Rs. 1,281 crores, reflecting a 5% increase year-on-year increase. EBITDA grew significantly by 31% to Rs. 344 crores, with margins improving around 500 basis points to 27%, up from 22% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: US bill expanding subsidies to energy storage systems creates major opportunity for battery materials as alternate non-China supply chain
items.quote: The bill offer a sub stantial USD 45 per kilowatt hour subsidy, covering approximately two -third of the battery costs, making large-scale battery productions in the US , not just feasible, but highly attractive

items.statement: High-end fluoropolymer approvals received from Western and Far East customers for semiconductor, aerospace, automotive applications
items.quote: We have also got a couple of high-end polymer approvals from the Western countries also and also from Far East countries. So, the commercial business also has started from these applications.

items.statement: US tariff delta of 15% on new fluoropolymers expected to be passed through via price negotiations over time
items.quote: The earlier 10% that we are talking about has already been passed on, so now we are looking at this delta of 15%.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer business achieved highest ever quarterly revenue in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our Fluoro segment revenue has been rising steadily, and we have now surpassed our previous high to achieve the highest ever quarterly revenue.

items.statement: Next fluoropolymer capex phase across PTFE and new fluoropolymers to be detailed in coming quarter
items.quote: we will be looking at more investments in this. And I thin k we will give you a better perspective probably a quarter from now

items.statement: Rights issue oversubscribed 1.45x; proposing further INR80 crore raise via convertible warrants
items.quote: We've also, I think, before I begin the business update, a very strong endorsement from all stakeholders. We have healthy customer satisfaction scores, 90% for care homes, 94% for Care at Home, 86% for AGEasy.

items.statement: Sale of Max Towers non-strategic asset concluded; proceeds used for business growth
items.quote: Further, the sale of units in Max Towers, which is a no nstrategic asset for us, has been concluded now, and the proceeds are being used for the growth of the business

items.statement: Estate 360 inventory 100% sold within 10-11 months; collections on track
items.quote: On the asset side, I'm very happy to inform you that 100% of the inventory for our Estate 360, the first intergenerational project developed by Max Estates is now complete. The collections are on track and receipt of Antara fee is also expected to be in li ne with plan

items.statement: Estate 361 second phase (1.04M sq ft, 360 units) expected launch by September-October 2025
items.quote: On new communities. On the second phase of Estate 360, which is called now Estate 361. It's a 1.04 million square feet development, about 360 units now, expected to be launched by September, October this year.

items.statement: Chandigarh project definitive agreement closed; 1.01M sq ft, 324 units; registry in 10 days
items.quote: The Chandigarh opportunity, definitive agreement has already been closed with the landowner. Registry will happen sometime in the next 10 days. We have begun the groundwork, appointed the architect already. This is a 1.01 million square feet development with 324 units.

items.statement: Total development pipeline now 2M sq ft for FY26, exceeding 1.5M sq ft annual commitment
items.quote: So with that, we are well above the commitment we made to you of doing 1.5 million square feet per year. We're already up to 2 million square feet for this year.

items.statement: Antara Assisted Care Q1 FY26 net revenue INR22.06 crore, 2.2x YoY growth
items.quote: Shifting now to Antara Assisted Care. During Q1 FY '26, overall net revenue of about INR22.06 crores, which represents a year-on-year growth of 2.2x.

items.statement: Care Homes: 45 beds added in Q1 (Chennai ECR); total capacity now 340 beds; 150 beds under fit-out in Bangalore/Chennai launching Aug-Sep
items.quote: On Antara Assisted Care, we've added about 45 new beds and care homes during Q1 FY '26, with the launch of Chennai on ECR Road, which makes our bed capacity now 340 and about 150 in Bangalore and Chennai under fit-out, which will get launched in August and September.

items.statement: Target 500 beds operational by end of Q2 FY26 (August-September)
items.quote: When you say operational capacity, Rajit did mentioned that as per the plan, 500 beds, all full capacity go live by the end of this quarter. So August, September is when we are expecting all 500 to go live.

items.statement: Care Home occupancy ramped from 14% (April) to 18% (May) to 23% (June)
items.quote: If you look at the occupancy trends, I can read them out to you. They vary by location. But on the average, in April, May and June, they went up from 14% to 18% to 23% in June.

items.statement: Each Care Home targets 65-70% occupancy in 8 quarters post launch; memory care home at 45% (10 months old)
items.quote: We are aligned to that. So this what was quoted is an average number. So each Care Home is at a different occupancy, which is leading to this average because we have a Care Home, which is 10 months old, which is at around 45% occupancy, which is our memory care home.

items.statement: Care at Home Q1 FY26 revenue INR4.94 crore, 24% YoY growth; highest ever
items.quote: We have now achieved the highest ever revenue of INR4.94 crores in Q1 FY '26, a strong year-on-year growth of 24%, led by high-margin service offerings.

items.statement: Care at Home contribution margins: Delhi 20%, Chennai -26% to +1%, Bangalore -6% (salary inflation impact); price hikes in 2 months
items.quote: Contribution margins have come down a little bit from 15% to 12%, while Delhi continues to be 20%. Chennai has moved from negative 26% to plus 1%, Bangalore at minus 6% is because the inflation kicks in, in April when we go through our salary actions.

items.statement: AGEasy Q1 FY26 net revenue INR14.2 crore, 2.2x YoY; 40,000 repeat customers (12-13% of total); 3 lakh lives touched
items.quote: On AGEasy, which includes the erstwhile Medcare business now part of AGEasy now, we achieved a net revenue of INR14.2 crores in Q1 FY '26, a strong year-on-year growth of 2.2x.

items.statement: AGEasy NPS improved from 13 to 44 in one year
items.quote: I already talked about the NPS, which has grown from 13 to now 44 in a period of 1 year.

items.statement: AGEasy portfolio expanded to 85 products, 180 SKUs; 3 patents filed
items.quote: On product portfolio, we expanded to 85 products and 180 SKUs. We also filed for 3 patents, which are some innovative products, which we'll share with you once we get the patents.

items.statement: AGEasy ROAS improved 2x YoY to 1.6 from 0.87
items.quote: Our ROAS, which is an indication of profitability, also 2x achievement Y-on-Y. We achieved 1.6 as compared to 0.87 in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Anupam Kher signed as AGEasy brand ambassador; early impact: Google CTR 2.5% to 6%, marketplace conversion 6% to 7.5%
items.quote: We also signed up Anupam Kher, as a celebrity, as a face for AGEasy, and we have seen very early impact. On marketplaces, the conversion has gone up from 6% to 7.5%. And on Google, the CTR has gone up from 2.5% to 6%.

items.statement: AGEasy annual revenue run rate INR70-75 crore; Flipkart contributing 12-13% of revenue, 25% of marketplace
items.quote: So we already crossed an annual trajectory rate of INR70 crores to INR75 crores in this business, 62% coming from marketplaces. Of that, now Flipkart has emerged as another channel, which we signed up. Its already contributing 12% to 13% of our revenues and 25% of marketplaces.

items.statement: Gut health solution launch planned for September-October 2025 with Wellbeing Nutrition partnership
items.quote: Our plans of launching the gut health solution sometime in Q2 remains. We will launch that sometime in September, October. As you know, we have tied up with Wellbeing Nutrition, which will do all the formulations and research for us.

items.statement: China imports initiated, increasing COGS by 20%; supply chain stabilization needed
items.quote: We have initiated imports from China, as you know, which have increased our COGS by 20%. And once we're able to stabilize the supply chain, given the geopolitical situation, we'll explore what more we can do.

items.statement: Patent target addressable market INR700-1,000 crore for 3 filed patents
items.quote: These are going to be cumulatively for these products will be between - INR700 crores to INR1,000 crores market is what we target for these products.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 FY26 net revenue INR41.3 crore (9% lower QoQ due to lower management fee); EBITDA INR23.3 crore vs INR36.9 crore QoQ
items.quote: On a consol basis now, our performance for Q1 FY '26, in line with expectations, so no surprises there. The net revenue of INR41.3 crores, 9% lower than Q4 FY '25, but that is totally attributable to a lower management fee.

items.statement: Consolidated treasury and other assets INR320 crore; net worth INR460 crore as of June 2025
items.quote: Overall, our treasury and other assets now stand at a healthy number of INR320 crores, and the company has a consolidated net worth of INR460 crores, as of June '25.

items.statement: Noida Phase 1 OC pending; INR40 crore paid to Noida Authority, INR100 crore more shortly; High Court petition filed
items.quote: Accordingly, what we have done, the SPV, which is Content Builders has already made a payment of INR40 crores to Noida Authority. Another INR100 crores will go shortly. And therefore, we will then approach the appropriate forum once again for grant of the OC.

items.statement: Noida Phase 2 realization improved from planned INR12,000 to INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft
items.quote: One silver lining I keep on repeating is that the Phase 2 prices have gone much beyond what we had planned for. And if you remember, the last sale in Noida Phase 1 was about INR11,000. We had assumed it will become INR12,000. Now it's touching INR16,000 to INR18,000.

items.statement: AGEasy breakeven targeted FY27-early FY28; rest of businesses by FY28
items.quote: As we had indicated last time in terms of AGEasy breakeven FY '27, early '28 we will envisage a breakeven on the AGEasy part and rest of the businesses by FY '28 is a discussion we have had in the past with you.

items.statement: Zero strategic debt as of June 30; only minor vehicle loans; project-specific debt possible for cash flow mismatch
items.quote: We don't have any debt on our books at all. Ajay Agrawal: Aryan, as we have said, we don't have any debt on our books, except very minor vehicle loans, which are just business as usual. We don't have any strategic debt as on 30th of June.

items.statement: Planning ~$20 million fundraise after second tranche of pref issue next month
items.quote: But as I said earlier, for our growth, we will be looking at a fundraise, which I've been saying about $20 million after we complete the second tranche of the pref issue in the next month.

items.statement: Assisted Care segment cash burn estimated INR90 crore for FY26 (Care Home, Care at Home, AGEasy)
items.quote: We're expecting around INR90 crores between Care Home, Care at Home and AGEasy. Rajit Mehta: For FY '26. Sandeep Pathak: For FY '26.

items.statement: AGEasy gross margin: India-sourced ~40%, China-sourced ~55% (20% COGS improvement)
items.quote: So there is a 20% COGS improvement that we've seen when we import from China compared to what we source from India. So currently, there will be around gross margin of 40% of the India products and around -- currently seen around 55% from China.

items.statement: Estate 360 collections guidance: INR250-270 crore for FY26; INR33 crore collected in June
items.quote: So we are expecting approximately INR250-odd crores of collection in Estate 360, INR250 crores to INR270 crores for the whole year, in which just as a number, we have collected approximately INR33 crores for June and the balance would come.

items.statement: Noida Authority revised project cost to INR1,100 crore (from INR1,000 crore) due to land cost recalculation and holding costs; Phase 2 cost included
items.quote: Yes. So when we had approached the High Court, Noida Authority has given a revised calculation for the land cost and also with the inventory getting extended as held and we are not able to deliver, there are certain costs, which are getting baked in on a m onthly basis. Adding both the two, I have taken that number

items.statement: Demand was positive in April and first half of May but hit by early monsoon from mid-May to end of June, especially in Kerala and Northeast; July shows notable recovery.
items.quote: After a hiatus of over 12 months, it appear ed that the demand in the paint sector was back in April and during the first half of May, only to be cashed by the early onset of monsoons, which rained in full fury from mid -May until the end of June

items.statement: Expects much better Q2 and much better second half FY26, but calls it conjecture; no formal guidance given.
items.quote: So I'd expect to see a much better Q2 and a much, much better second half this year. But I preface it by saying that this is all conjecture.

items.statement: Raw material prices continue to soften marginally; expect margins to be stable going forward.
items.quote: On the raw material front, prices continue to soften, although marginally, and we expect our margins to be stable going forward.

items.statement: Water-based paint plant at Jodhpur expected Q3 or Q4 FY26; solvent-based plant and putty brownfield expansion by end of Q2 FY26. Delays not expected to impact demand fulfillment.
items.quote: As we have mentioned earlier, due to delays in civil construction work in the water-based plant, that plant is now expected to be commissioned sometime in Q3 or Q4 of FY '26, while the solvent-based plant is expected to be up and running by the end of the current quarter.

items.statement: Current capacity sufficient for existing demand; new plants add modernization and mechanization; solvent-based plant at Jodhpur will reduce freight costs for North India.
items.quote: However, these minor delays are not expected to cause any impact as we have more than enough capacity to cater to our existing demand.

items.statement: Apple Chemie order book looks good for August and September; expects bounce back in Q2 as monsoon abates.
items.quote: I think they are making up. I mean they've had a slightly better July and their order book looks good as far as August and September is concerned.

items.statement: Enamel and primer grew in volume and value; putty and emulsions saw volume and value decline; emulsion value degrowth only 0.9% vs volume -5.4%, indicating premium mix improvement.
items.quote: In the emulsion segment, which is the largest segment, although the volume negative growth was 5.4%, the value degrowth was only 0.9%, showing that the product mix has improved more towards the premium range.

items.statement: Active dealers ~18,600; tinting machines ~11,300 as of June 30, 2025; network expanded despite heavy monsoons.
items.quote: As on 30th June 2025, our count of active dealers was around 18,600, and the tinting machine population was about 11,300.

items.statement: New entrant Birla Opus had high dealer incentives and extra grammage but is now pulling back; industry gross margins stable; Indigo not materially impacted, few dealers switched.
items.quote: Now, if the new entrant has chosen to slowly lower its incentive structure and come back to a more industry convergent rate, good to see that happening. But even when they persisted on a very high discount, I don't think it bothered the paint sector too much.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on titanium dioxide increased TiO2 prices temporarily; court case pending in Calcutta High Court filed by Indian Paint Association; judgment awaited.
items.quote: There is a court case pending in the Calcutta High Court filed by the Indian Paint Association for which hearings are over and the judgment is awaited.

items.statement: Call options for remaining 49% of Apple Chemie kick in after April 1, 2026; will take educated decision then. No other M&A on table.
items.quote: Your earlier question about acquiring the remaining 49%, well, the call options th at we have kick in only after 1st of April next year

items.statement: Gross margin 46.1% (sector KPI); EBITDA margin 14.8%; PAT margin 8.8%.
items.quote: We continue to maintain the pole position in terms of gross margin, which stood at 46.1%.

items.statement: Early Diwali (Oct 20) curtails pre-Diwali sales window in North; early monsoon withdrawal uncertain; demand recovery not guaranteed.
items.quote: It is, but what happens is that whenever Diwali is early, and this time, we have one of the earliest Diwalis on the 20th of October. Normally, rainfall in India continues till the first week of October.

items.statement: A&P spend 6.8% of revenue vs 7.2% YoY; 7th straight year of IPL brand investment; launching 50-70 Indigo Color Canvas experiential stores in FY26.
items.quote: During the last quarter, the overall A&P spend as a percentage of revenue decreased from 7.2% in Q1 of last year to 6.8% in Q1 of this year.

items.statement: Guided to 15% CAGR revenue growth, mid-teens PAT margin, and 30%+ EBITDA margin over the long term
items.quote: We have guided to 15% CAGR growth. We have guided to about mid-teens in PAT. We have guided to 30% plus in EBITDA. And we have never strayed from those numbers, not through the highs and not through the lows of the lumpiness of COVID.

items.statement: Expect each format to deliver 15-18% CAGR over the long term
items.quote: We expect close to about 15% to 18% CAGR. I am talking long term, I am not talking short term here, not only through our new formats, but ideally for each of the formats that we have.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 31%, down slightly due to higher marketing spend; PAT margin maintained at 16%
items.quote: Our EBITDA grew 8%, coming in at 31%, slightly behind last year due to increased spend in marketing to enhance our brand positioning for our various business units. Our PAT grew 7% to maintain our mid-teen performance of 16%.

items.statement: Gross margin healthy in high 50% range, achieved almost 60% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Gross margin remained consiste nt and healthy running in the high 50% range as we achieved almost 60% margin for the quarter

items.statement: Marketing spend targeted at 3.5-4% of revenue, slightly higher than last year
items.quote: We target around 3.5% to 4% in that category. And last year, if you looked at it, we did not spend that much in the quarter. So, we really want to continue to invest in our brand building efforts and making sure that all our brands continue to be top of mind.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY despite early monsoon in Gujarat and Maharashtra; 101% growth vs pre-COVID Q1 FY20 (12% CAGR including COVID year)
items.quote: As you all are probably aware, we posted a 9% growth in both our standalone and consolidated numbers. In the quarter, we had an offset ease, a strong season for us that fell into the previous and the early onset of monsoon, which though is key for our crocs business does dampen shopping in the markets.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment consistent; no structural demand concerns; growth trajectory normalizing post-COVID lumpiness
items.quote: We are not seeing anything that causes us great concern. When we sell out of products we expect to sell out, and we sell out some that we did not expect to sell out. And there are some others that do not do well, which is just par for the course.

items.statement: Opened 23 stores, closed 3 in Q1 FY26; opened 4 Walkway stores in Q1 vs 4 in all of FY25; Foot Locker stores opening after BIS stabilization; Fila EBOs planned for H2 CY2025
items.quote: For the quarter, we opened 23 stores and closed three stores. We have been working on repositioning Walkway and are now beginning to open stores for that banner. We opened four Walkway stores just in the last quarter compared to four for the whole year last year.

items.statement: Premium segment (ASP >Rs1,500) at 89% of sales in Q1 FY26, up 1% YoY; Clarks ASP expected north of Rs3,500-4,000; Walkway re-entering sub-Rs500 price points
items.quote: If you even see our last three years' trend, right, this number has gone up by 1% year-on-year. So, FY '24, if I remember correctly, our contribution of sales upward of Rs. 1,500 was around 86%, 87%. Last year it was around 88% and this year for 1st Quarter it is around 89%.

items.statement: Footwear ASP ~Rs2,700, growing 3.5-4%; overall ASP growing ~3%; premium business 56% of revenue
items.quote: So, ASP, if you take ASP only for footwear at our stores, it is somewhere around Rs. 2,700. And we have seen growth of around 3.5%, 4% in that. Overall ASP also we have seen growth of around 3%.

items.statement: Sales per sq ft ~Rs43-50 in Q1 FY26; would be 2-3% higher if Eid fell in Q1; annualization of ~100 new stores (10% of chain) diluting metric
items.quote: Broadly, if we see our sales, we would easily have been higher by about 2% to 3% if Eid was to be in Q1. So, approximately around a similar percentage would get added to the sales per square feet also, the number that you see.

items.statement: E-commerce grew 45% YoY to Rs84 crore in Q1 FY26 (vs Rs58 crore in Q1 FY25); omnichannel and DTC initiatives driving growth without discounting
items.quote: FY '24 Q1 was around Rs. 61 crores. Last year Q1 was around Rs. 58 crores, and this year is 84 crore. So, growth, obviously, 45% over last year is 45%.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth not disclosed separately; long-term target mid-to-high single digits; cannibalization from backfilling stores tempers SSG but gains market share
items.quote: If we see slightly longer period, say 10 years, we have generally seen overall SSGs for all our formats ranging in that mid- to high single digits. So, that is our long-term target for any retailer to ensure that profitability does not get impacted.

items.statement: BIS regulations delayed Foot Locker and Fila launches; supply chain stabilizing; Foot Locker stores now opening; Fila EBOs planned for H2 CY2025
items.quote: We have delayed the opening of Foot Locker and Fitflop to allow for stabilization of sourcing, given the BIS regulations that impeded imports for most of last year. We are starting to see that supply chain gain stability and have started opening Foot Locker stores in this quarter.

items.statement: Signed long-term exclusive agreement for Clarks in India and neighboring countries (Bangladesh, Nepal, Maldives, Sri Lanka); will be sold across all channels including mono-brand stores
items.quote: As we announced mid-quarter, we are excited about the new partnership with Clarks shoes. This premium brand of dress and casual footwear fits very well within our Metro Mochi business and also has the brand recognition to have its own mono-branded stores. We now have a long-term exclusive agreement for India and surrounding countries like Bangladesh, Nepal, Maldives, Sri Lanka, etc.

items.statement: Fila format losses Rs58 crore in FY24; reduced ~40% in FY25; expected to break even in FY27
items.quote: In the first year, FY '24 losses in Fila format were around Rs. 58 crores. Last year, we reduced it by around 40-odd-percent. And this year, it will further go down. Sometimes next year is when we feel we should break even with respect to Fila.

items.statement: Walkway long-term store-level ROCE target 30%+ (vs 40-45% for Metro/Mochi); standalone profitable; good capital deployment
items.quote: For Walkway, if we think from a long-term perspective, ideally, we would like them to deliver somewhere around 30% and upwards.

items.statement: No unusual price hikes; ASP growth driven by product mix (premium brands like Fila, new brands) rather than cost-push; input costs well controlled
items.quote: Nothing out of the ordinary. Sometimes it's more of a mix of goods, Prerna, because you also have to block and now we have other brands that are now kicking in, Fila is also at much higher ASP than the average than most of the other businesses run. It's really a mix of goods more than its anything.

items.statement: No impact from India-UK FTA; 95% sourced domestically, 100% sold in India
items.quote: No. We are 100% India. We source almost 95% of our goods in India. We sell 100% of our goods in India. So, we do not see that impacting us, benefit or otherwise in any way.

items.statement: Regional demand volatility: early monsoon hit Gujarat/Maharashtra; South impacted by tech sector slowdown and real estate; Punjab erratic; but demand cycles back
items.quote: We are seeing some slowness in the South from time to time. We see some erraticness from even states like Punjab. But it goes up, it comes down. And for me, to categorically say that there's one continuous offender, so to speak, that would not be a fair statement.

items.statement: ESG initiative: recycling one pair of shoes for every pair sold; unique in footwear retail globally
items.quote: We may be the only footwear retailer in India, or in the world for that matter, that recycles a pair of shoes for every one that we sell. Let that sink in for a minute. I am really proud of the ESG team that has worked so hard to build this ecosystem for us.

items.statement: Positive signs of improvement in industrial demand in Europe reflected in highest sales for Harsha Romania in several quarters
items.quote: First and foremost, I'm happy to share that we have started getting positive signs of improvement in industrial demand in Europe. Thus, as you might have observed, this is partly reflected in our -- one of the highest sales reported by Harsha Romania in last several quarters -- in quarter 1 FY '26.

items.statement: Significant improvement in sales of large-sized cages and good order inflow in India for first time in several quarters
items.quote: Another pointer to this aspect is the fact that, again, quarter 1 FY '26 for the first time after several quarters, we have reported a significant improvement in sales of large -sized cages, and we have also started seeing a good inflow of orders for large -sized cages in India.

items.statement: No significant improvement in wind market demand despite industrial demand recovery in Europe
items.quote: I believe that this growth in Europe is coming from industrial demand, and we are still not witnessing any significant improvement in demand from the wind market.

items.statement: Overall improvement in industrial demand in India though auto sector remains sluggish
items.quote: We've also started getting signs of overall improvement in industrial demand in India, though auto sector continues to remain sluggish.

items.statement: Long-term bushing contract with peak annual sales of INR117 crores over 2-3 years, incremental sales from Q4 FY26
items.quote: Thus, we have also recently announced that we have entered into a long-term contract with one of our existing key customers for manufacture of supply of bushings. This contract, what we are expecting is peak annual sales to be around INR117 crores and which can take about 2 to 3 years to fully realize, while some incremental sales related to this contract will come in, in fourth quarter current fi

items.statement: Bushing product revenue to grow at least 30% in FY26 over FY25's INR100 crores
items.quote: I believe that as compared to FY 2025 where Bushing product reported a revenue of about INR100 crores, this product should grow handsomely at least 30% in current financial year due to strong tailwinds that we are witnessing in this segment.

items.statement: FY26 target: low-teens top line growth for India Engineering, higher single-digit consolidated growth, better profitability vs FY25 adjusted EBITDA and PAT
items.quote: To conclude, I wish to reiterate overall target for FY '26. This is that it is to be -- is to expect at least a low-teens top line growth in Harsha India Engineering business and a higher single-digit top line growth in a consolidated basis. It will be evident there should be a better growth in profitability as compared to adjusted EBITDA and PAT that we have achieved in FY 2025.

items.statement: INR44 crores capex incurred in Q1 FY26 mainly for Bhayla greenfield site
items.quote: Overall working capital cycle at consolidated level remain at 139 days and company has incurred a capex of INR44 crores in the first quarter, mainly towards the Bhayla site.

items.statement: Total greenfield investment plan INR300 crores over 2.5-3 years, INR200+ crores already invested, ~INR100 crores remaining over next 1.5 years
items.quote: Yes, I think what I understand or what I believe, what we had shared that we will -- over 2.5, 3 years, we will invest about INR300 crore s in this site. We have now already invented about INR200 crores, a little bit more than that already in this. So we a re expecting at least about INR100 crores over next 1.5 years or so

items.statement: Additional marginal capex needed for bushing contract fulfillment towards end of FY26 or early FY27
items.quote: And specifically reference to this contract when this full maturity of this contract takes place in about 2 years, a little bit more, we expect that to achieve those revenue, we will have to invest something in that. So that's a general thing. And this is -- I'm talking to India and then maybe Romania being a little

items.statement: Bhayla greenfield site has 55-60% land free and ~20% building space available for future expansion without new infrastructure spend
items.quote: Yes. So we have about 60% -- almost 55%, 60% land free at Bhayla site as of today. Further, even on the buildings we have built when fully operational by next year, we still believe that on the building space also, there will be about 20% odd space left for us to expand without adding new infrastructure spend.

items.statement: Romania revenue mix: ~20% cages, ~80% semi-finished castings; India: ~70-75% bearing cages, balance bushings and stamping
items.quote: One is semi-finished casting. And another is a cage. Cage is hardly 20% around of our top line in Romania. Vishal Rangwala: In Romania. Maulik Jasani: Yes, in Romania. And 80% is the semi -finished casting. And in India, you can say that almost 70%, 75% is a bearing cage

items.quote: We have achieved consolidated EBITDA for Engineering business at INR65.2 crore s for this quarter against the reported EBITDA of INR38.3 crores and adjusted EBITDA of INR66 crores due to one-off in the last quarter and INR62.4 crores in the last year same quarter.

items.quote: For our Harsha Advantek greenfield site, Bhayla has commissioned the commercialization and production. However, since the plant has n ot scaled up, HEIL has given a negative EBITDA and PAT, mainly due to fixed overheads as well as interest and depreciation charges.

items.quote: Lastly, our effort to increase sales to Japan-based customer continues with same vigor, though it is not yet translating into growth numbers. However, we continue to remain very confident about our potential of increasing the sales in this segment, though it may take a little longer time than we had anticipated.

items.statement: US demand softening in FY26 vs previous year, US ~10% of overall demand, monitoring trade barrier impacts
items.quote: On the trade impact, again, fo r us, U.S., there's a lot of uncertainty there. We see U.S. demand softening already this financial year as compared to previous year. It doesn't consist more than about -- it's about 10% of our overall demand for U.S.

items.statement: Romania restructuring project initiated last quarter, will take 6-8 more months to fully realize cost savings and operational improvements
items.quote: No, we have just initiated that as a project last quarter. And we are continuing that, and that will take at least about 6 to 8 months further to really fully re alize all the work we have -- results of all the work on the cost savings side and also on...

items.quote: Solar division has done a top line of INR16.4 crores with EBITDA of INR0.9 crores in first quarter FY '26 and Solar division continues to have a good order level in Gujarat.

items.statement: Harsha Advantek greenfield site expected to achieve positive EBITDA turnaround by end of FY26
items.quote: I will not be able to comment specifically on the breakeven point, but we expect by this year, it will be positive turnaround. That is our expectation.

items.statement: Good order flow in large-size cages growing handsomely in Q1 FY26 over Q1 FY25, stamping sales flat
items.quote: Similarly, as indicated earlier, I'm also happy to report that we have started witnessing good order flow in large-size cages, which again has grown handsomely in quarter 1 FY 2026 over quarter 1 FY '25. However, sales of stamping has remained more or less flat in quarter 1 FY 2026.

items.statement: New facilities commissioned by customers in India partially attributed to supply chain realignment for global requirements
items.quote: This also includes regular orders that we have started receiving from our customers, new faci lities commissioned in India, which could be partially attributed to their increased sales from these facilities as part of their strategy to realign their overall supply chain for servicing their global requirement.

items.statement: Targets Q2 FY26 higher double-digit revenue growth

items.quote: Looking ahead, we plan to open 25-30 new stores in FY '26, while continuing to optimize the supply chain, enhancing inventory cfficiencies and strengthen our footprint in both existing and cmerging markets

items.statement: Q1 FY26 demand hit by unseasonal rainfall; April-May rainfall 50% above normal in Telangana, 148% above normal in Andhra Pradesh in May
items.quote: Q1 FY '26 turned out to be one of the coolest summer quarters in recent years, driven by unseasonal and widespread rainfall across April and May. This unusual weather pattern significantly impacted summer appliances demand, particularly in the air conditioners and air cooler category, which rely heavily on peak summer temperatures to drive sales.

items.statement: July 2025 saw exceptionally strong sales across ACs, mobiles, TVs, refrigerators with higher double-digit growth
items.quote: July has been an cxceptionally great month, especially for AC and other categorics. We were expecting that o happen anyways because organically last quarter dida't do that well for cooling products. So, ACs have scen the major jump this quarter as well. Whereas mobile, televisions and refrigerators, all categories have seen a higher double digit growth this year in the month of July

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 6.3%, pre-Ind AS 4.4%; North cluster EBITDA margin improved 100 bps YoY to 3.6%
items.quote: EBITDA for Q1 FY '26 stood at Rs. 110 crores. EBITDA margin for Q1 FY '26 stood at 6.3%. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA for Q1 FY '26 stood at Rs. 75 crores with a margin of 4.4%.

items.statement: Expects North cluster EBITDA margin to reach 5%+ by end of FY27
items.quote: But eventually by, say, next year, we should be looking at least a 5% plus EBITDA margin in that cluster.

items.quote: That is how we are hoping to pan out in the coming quarters as well. We are quite optimistic on that as well.

items.statement: AC inventory elevated at Rs 350 crores vs normal Rs 100 crores; ~89,000 units; plans to liquidate by December
items.quote: AC inventory is more than Rs. 250 crores. Usually, sir, from last year this period we have ended with around Rs. 70-odd crores of stocks, which this year it was supposed to be organically 100, this year it is 350 instead of 100. We have more than Rs. 250 crores of inventory.

items.statement: Working capital days at 60 as of June 25; expects to fall below 60 days organically by Dec 31
items.quote: by this end of quarter 2, and probably the middle of quarter 3, we should be liquidating the stocks, especially the ones that are holding up our numbers quite high. So, that number of inventory days anyway, organically by 31st December, it will come down to an organic mumber less than 60 days

items.statement: Total borrowings reduced from Rs 983 crores (Mar 31) to Rs 689 crores (Jun 30); Rs 250 crores for land/building, rest working capital
items.quote: Sure, sir. So, sir, your total borrowing on 31st March was around Rs. 983 crores, which has come down to Rs. 689 crotes, out of Rs. 689 crores, Rs. 250 crores is for land and building. And the rest of it is for the working capital requirement

items.statement: AC price revision expected from Jan 2026 due to star rating change; older stock to clear by Oct-Dec
items.quote: So, the price will be much higher than what the rating saving would be on the ACs.

items.statement: North cluster store productivity lower due to 20 of 30 stores <24 months old; maturity at Rs 25-40 cr/store
items.quote: out of the 30-0dd stores that are operating in that region, 20-odd stores are less than 24 months in that region. So, usually, we take around 3 years plus for a store to get matured and that is where you will see the productivity of the store

items.statement: Market share intact in mature AP/Telangana markets; gaining share in newer Tier-3/4 towns; main competitor Sonovision in Andhra
items.quote: Majorly, any bad quarter in terms of numbers going down, you have to make sure that your market share is intact, so on growing, so that is one thing that is positive clusters where we are new or cities where we are newin AP and Telangana also, we are still capturing the matket there and our market share is increasing definitely there

items.statement: Like-to-like sales growth -18% in Q1 FY26

items.statement: Annualized ROCE 13.4%, ROE 7.7% for Q1 FY26
items.quote: Annualized ROCE and ROE for Q1 FY 26 stood at 13.4% and 7.7% respectively.

items.statement: Union Budget 2025 raised taxable income threshold, putting ~Rs 1 lakh crore into middle class hands, expected to boost consumer durable demand
items.quote: Further, the Union Budget 2025 has provided significant personal income tax relicf by raising the taxable income threshold, cffectively putting an estimated Rs. 1 lakh crore back into the hands of the middle class

items.quote: So as of right now, we maintain our guidance at INR 4,000 crores, but I assure you we will thrill all our investors like we do with our customers.

items.quote: The third milestone that we have is the launch of three projects during the quarter with a GDV of totally INR 3,967 crores, twice the launch value recorded in the same period last year.

items.quote: In line with our proactive approach to business development, we added three projects in Q1 with a combined GDV of INR 7,727 crores. This exceeds the entire guidance of FY '26 for business development by more than 1.25x

items.quote: It is worth noting that we have already achieved 57% of our full year FY '26 launch guidance setting, a solid foundation for achieving our targets.

items.quote: Our construction spends have also increased from INR 191 crores in Q1 FY '25 to INR 238 crores in Q1 FY '26. This is a 25% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: Generated operating cash flow of INR 118 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: During Q1 FY '26, we generated an OCF, operating cash flow, of INR 118 crores.

items.quote: Our liquidity, our gross debt stands at approximately INR 304 crores and with a gross debt -to-equity ratio of 0.11:1 as of 30th June, 2025. This is very well within our guidance. items.quote: So basically, to throw some light on our new launches, fortunately for us, all the projects that we launched in this last quarter were in the Premium segment. And we've seen that about 8% by volume, 9% by value stock has already gotten sold.

items.quote: we have seen deeper relationships with larger HNIs, family offices and even funds that like to invest in our treasury products. And we have expanded our reach nationally as well as globally
