And of course, we will continue to improve our efficiencies using technology. But of course, with sort of paramount consolidation coming in, for about 5 to 6 quarters, we will probably see about 200-250 basis points ki

items.statement: Acquired Paramount Health Services for Rs 412.4 crores equity value; closed July 1, 2025; consolidation starts Q2.
items.quote: Medi Assist Insurance TPA Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary. Your Company has successfully closed the acquisition of Paramount Health Services and Insurance TPA on 1 st July for a final purchase consideration of Rs. 412.4 crores being the equity value of the purchase.

items.statement: Paramount expected to contribute ~Rs 140 crores annual revenue (IndAS) at run-rate; no prior wins included.
items.quote: we expect a little over Rs. 140 crores a year in the IndAS format to sort of accrue from what we have as numbers. So, that's the kind of run rate. There's a little bit of that that we had already won in the open marketplace earlier, but that's sort of the size at which Paramount will conduct.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with Star Health to deploy MAtrix AI-driven claims platform; technology services revenue at 2.5% of total.
items.quote: we have also entered a strategic partnership with Star Health, an allied insurance Company, India's largest retail health insurer, to deploy MAtrix, our proprietary AI-driven automation-first claims platform.

items.statement: Contract liability increased to Rs 288 crores at end of Q1 from Rs 238 crores at end of March.
items.quote: So, on contract liability number is Rs. 288 crores, as of Q1 288 is the number. This was 238 as of March. So, that's the increment in the number, right? for the quarter.

items.statement: SaaS pricing for claims technology on per-claim basis with multi-year fixed fee contracts; outcome-based pricing possible for AI models.
items.quote: the base pricing model for the claims technology on a per claim basis is a SaaS fee. We typically have multi-year contracts with a fixed fee for the entire duration of the contract. Fixed in the sense the fee is fixed at a per claim level, sometimes even with some amount of inflation in the base technology platform. We expect that in some of the other AI-led models, the industry will sort of move

items.statement: Technology services gross margins expected to be better than core TPA margins due to reuse of engineering/infrastructure and no people pass-through costs.
items.quote: Given that, typically in our other contracts where we have people deployments, the cost of people tends to be a pass-through cost, which also dilutes margins. So, this one is a pure technology cost. So, the gross margins are certainly better in the tech services business.

items.statement: Board approved preferential allotment (term sheet accepted) for cap table strengthening, growth capital, and debt retirement; prior in-principle approval for Rs 350 crores in February.
items.quote: we have a term sheet for our preferential allocation that the Board considered today and accepted the offer and approved the preferential allotment. We will predominantly, I think we will talk about the objectives itself when we send out the notice you know, to the shareholders in the next couple of days.

items.statement: No forward guidance given; company aims to grow at industry rate or faster; consolidated financials with Paramount from Q2.
items.quote: See, we don't give any forward guidance, but as you can see, and if from a track record, we have generally always said that we will grow at the industry rate or faster. And we have sort of published our last couple of quarters in terms of improving margin profile. Of course, Paramount is something that is just closed in the current quarter. So, with paramount, how the consolidated numbers will pan

items.statement: Group same-store growth softer on lives/employment growth (~50% historically), offset by benefits expansion and higher opt-in driving ticket size up.
items.quote: Historically, about 50% of our same store growth of mid-teens used to come from lives growth, employment growth, or the membership growth. Right now, I think that's the softer side. But we are seeing a lot of the growth from benefits expansion and a lot of sort of employees opting in for higher kinds of benefits.

items.statement: Group client diversification: ITeS/BFSI now sub 30-35% of top 50 accounts vs 65-70% five years ago; significant presence across manufacturing, automotive, pharma.
items.quote: Maybe 4-5 years ago, we had almost 65%-70% of our premiums coming from ITeS and BFSI, which were the largest, obviously, and the most benevolent employers from benefits perspective. But today, if I am not wrong, I think it should be sub 30%-35% of within the top 50, in fact, which are pretty large.

items.statement: Annualized revenue per average headcount (non-government) at Rs 14.9 lakhs (Rs 3.7 lakhs quarterly).
items.quote: Revenue per average headcount, which again, Satish spoke about, under non-government contracts, was INR 14.9 lakhs annualized, equivalent to 3.7 lakhs for the quarter.

items.statement: Net cash balance Rs 312.6 crores; net worth Rs 577.4 crores; RoNW 15.7% annualized; RoCE 21% annualized.
items.quote: The net cash balance in the books was 312.6 Cr. The net worth was 577.4 Cr. The return on the net worth was a healthy 15.7% annualized, which is equivalent to 3.9% for the first quarter. Return on capital employed was 21% annualized, equivalent to 5.3% for the first quarter.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 2.7%-2.8% annually
items.quote: So, normally, in our kind of business model, 2.7% to 2.8% is what we normally give, barring some operational efficiencies or the customer mix, which has got favorable in this quarter. On an annualized basis, yes, 2.7%, 2.8% is sustainable in long run.

items.statement: Aspiration to grow at 2x market growth rate for full year
items.quote: Going forward, for the entire year, as I said, and we've been maintaining our stance that our aspiration is to have 2x the growth of the market.

items.statement: Q1 PC market grew ~3%, Q2 expected 9-10%, H2 expected 12-14% driven by Windows 10 end-of-support
items.quote: If you see Q1, the market grew by only about 3%, and we are expecting the market to grow in Q2 by about, say, 10%. So, the average is just about 6% in H1, right? Whereas on the annualized basis, we are still expecting the market to grow by 8% to 10%. That means the H2 market will be about 12% to 14% is what is the expectation.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin expanded 140bps to 3.5% due to favorable mix, no large deals, and forex benefit
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 140 basis points to 3.5% for the quarter and PAT margin rose 70 basis points to 2%.

items.statement: No large deals executed in Q1; multiple large and mid-sized deals in pipeline for Q2-Q4 being evaluated for ROI
items.quote: In Q1, there were only 1 or 2 large deals where we decided not to participate. But in Q2, Q3 and Q4, there will be a few large and some small deals also. We have a separate vertical, separate team working on these project businesses.

items.statement: Government GPU order for 10,000 units likely to finalize in Q2; will evaluate margins and ROE before participating
items.quote: Yes. So, this order is likely to get finalized within this quarter, Q2. And it will be available for all of us to grab. But then we as I said earlier, we need to analyze the margins and ROEs before we pick up the order.

items.statement: Added 4 strategic brands: MSI gaming laptops, Norden networking, Riello UPS, ALOGIC accessories
items.quote: So, to name a few, name -- the first brand we have started with MSI gaming laptops. It is a Taiwanese company and the world's leading gaming company. So, only in North India, excluding Delhi, we have started MSI gaming laptops. Second, to strengthen our networking business because in our current networking business, we are doing mainly active components. We needed some passive components like cabl

items.statement: Surveillance business growing strongly, at ~50% of potential, expected to reach 3-digit crore revenue annually
items.quote: I can only say that it will be on a yearly basis, it will be a 3-digit figure in crores, much more than the 3-digit figure.

items.statement: Embedded vertical grew ~38% YoY in Q1 driven by auto demand and project wins
items.quote: Yes, it is doing extremely well. We have more than 30%, 35% growth on a Q1-to-Q1 basis. In fact, I think 38%, especially because the demand of the automobile, again, has grown.

items.statement: Quick commerce business to more than double this year; currently distributing ~10 brands
items.quote: And to answer your question specifically, this year, we will have more than -- we will double -- more than double our business only on the quick commerce space.

items.statement: Working capital days increased to 73 due to 8-day debtor delay and 4-5 day creditor reduction from early payment incentives; expected to normalize this quarter
items.quote: One is, one sizable debtor's payment, which got delayed in this quarter, which is expected in maybe next 10 to 15 days, and that will normalize. That has an effect of around 8 days. And second is certain businesses where we have gone for availing early payment incentive from brands, there, we have paid inventory on record. So, creditors have come down by 4 to 5 days.

items.statement: Exited 51% stake in ZNet Technologies after 4-5 years due to inability to achieve profitability; exploring cloud strategy via software distribution
items.quote: So, that is exactly the disinvestment in the subsidiary. We held 51% shares only. So, entire stake we have sold out.

items.statement: Contingent liability of INR 400 crore from GST show-cause notices; management sees no material risk
items.quote: So, a. first of all, I would like to say that we are fully compliant on all the laws and these contingent liabilities, which are disclosed in the balance sheet or contingent liability list are normal show notices, which are received from GST department inquiring about the details and reconciliations in the returns being filed and all. And those are replied to the fullest satisfaction of the author

items.statement: Inventory obsolescence risk minimal due to brand sell-through support, price protection, and advance notice of tech refresh cycles
items.quote: So, we have minimum risk on inventory obsolescence. Typically, there are 3 types of risk that we factor in for an inventory. First is the technology risk. Second is a competitive risk. And the third one is a refresh cycle of technological risk.

items.statement: Channel business grew fastest in Q1; organized retail grew; online business declined consciously due to low returns
items.quote: And even in from the go-to-market strategy, our channel business has grown the fastest. Organized retail also has grown faster and online business, there is a degrowth. A mix of all this has resulted in improved EBITDA and EBITDA and PAT margins.

items.statement: Large deal margins under pressure due to competition among vendors and distributors; ROCE lower than previous deals
items.quote: But now the competition is hotting up not only amongst the vendor suppliers, but amongst the distribution also. So, at this moment, it appears that the ROCEs are lower, but that does not determine us not to participate in it.

items.statement: Leveraging expansions done 2 years ago for economies of scale; no new capex mentioned
items.quote: See, right now, we are getting opportunity for the economies of scale that we have delivered on the expansions that we have done 2 years ago.

items.statement: Lenovo scaling local manufacturing to produce all India PCs domestically within 3 years including AI GPU servers, aligned with government incentives
items.quote: Lenovo is scaling up its local manufacturing footprint with a goal to produce all its PCs for the Indian market domestically within the next 3 years, including AI GPU servers, aligning with government incentives and solidifying India's role as a global tech manufacturing hub.

items.statement: Organic revenue target of $400 million by FY28; could be significantly higher if inorganic opportunities materialize
items.quote: I'm very pleased to share the progress that we are making on our path to meet the growth aspirations which we have laid out, which is to be a $400 million revenue company organically by FY '28. Or as just mentioned, and he'll give the details later, this number could be significantly higher if the inorganic opportunities come to pass.

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA target to stay below 1.5x during FY26, may temporarily exceed due to accelerated capex
items.quote: As we mentioned earlier, our target debt-to-EBITDA to stay below 1.5x during the course of this year as we are accelerating some of our capex investments. The timing of these investments, there may be a few quarters as we see where this might go slightly higher than 1.5x, but we are fully committed to get back.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA grew 37% YoY to INR 885 million with margin at 27%, up 500 bps
items.quote: The profitability for the quarter EBITDA grew 37% to INR 885 million, with margins improving to 27% in this quarter and translating a 500 bps margin improvement.

items.statement: Order book remains solid; all customers launching in H2 have revised forecasts upward with take-or-pay contracts
items.quote: Our order book remains very solid. And in fact, all of our customers who are going to be launching the product as the markets open up later this fiscal, have actually raised and revised their forecast upwards, in fact, which is very conducive. And the fact that all these contracts are supported by take or pay, this really reinforces our confidence in the trajectory ahead

items.statement: Phase 2 DDC capacity expansion accelerated; full implementation to complete a year ahead of schedule within $100 million plan
items.quote: And while this is still within the overall $100 million capex plan, which we have announced earlier, but the entire implementation will be completed a year ahead of schedule.

items.statement: All DDC capacity to be up and qualified by end of calendar 2026; current capacity 40 million units
items.quote: So we would be having now this capacity, all capacity up and qualified by end of calendar 2026.

items.statement: Poland facility has ample space to expand to GLPs; Baroda facility has captive API conversion capability
items.quote: While we have no capacities available for sterile injectables, the plant has got ample space to expand to GLPs and we believe that it is pertinent for OneSource to have an additional site to take care of the increasing demand or increasing customer concentrations that we have and the risks attached to those what our customers have been asking us to de-risk.

items.statement: Board approved evaluation of acquiring Poland facility and Baroda JV with Brooks; expected to add $100M+ revenue and $36-40M EBITDA in FY27
items.quote: We currently have approximately $65 million of revenues for this year with an EBITDA in the 36% to 40% range and fully booked and committed to deliver $100 million of revenues at the bare minimum in the next year and that's $36 million to $40 million of EBITDA.

items.statement: Combined entity revenue trajectory could exceed $500M and EBITDA exceed $200M post-acquisition
items.quote: We believe that both these assets will add significant value to the long-term plans of OneSource which obviously will also mean that our targeted revenue of $400 million with $160 will now have an upward trajectory in excess of $500 million and in slightly in excess of $200 million of EBITDA.

items.statement: Successful back-to-back USFDA and ANVISA inspections; ~25 total inspections across all sites this quarter, all successful
items.quote: In fact, during the quarter, apart from these two, we have had almost 25 inspections done by either our regulatory agencies or our customers across all our sites, and all these have been successful.

items.statement: 10 molecules in DDC pipeline, only 3 are GLP-1s; first US approval for non-GLP DDC, first EU approval for biosimilar DDC
items.quote: We have got today 10 different molecules in the drug device combination, which we are working for our customers. And only three of these molecules are

items.statement: Diverse customer base including global leaders, regional leaders, country-specific leaders across markets
items.quote: From a customer point of view, I can tell you that we have a large customer base, which includes global customers, regional leaders, country specific leaders. So, we have a fairly diverse customer base.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to A family, reflecting confidence in financial management
items.quote: Proud to say that OneSource is now part of the A family. This development is reflective of continued confidence in our financial management and provides better access to capital and on much better terms.

items.statement: Prepaid significant high-cost debt; balancing leverage with internal accruals and customer participation in capex
items.quote: As you know, over the last few quarters we have prepaid significant amount of high-cost debt and we are consciously balancing our approach to leverage access to capital and debt along with our internal accruals and customer participation in our capex programs.

items.statement: Recent appointments to Board and leadership team added strategic, commercial depth and reinforced governance standards
items.quote: In fact, we have announced recent appointments, which both to our Board and to our leadership team. These have really added strategic and commercial depth to our organization on one side, and on the other, really reinforced our commitment to maintaining a very high standard of governance

items.statement: Poland facility approved by USFDA, European agencies, Australia, Canada; enables de-risking of customer concentration
items.quote: The plant is also approved by all other regulatory agencies like the European agencies obviously being in Poland, but also in Australia and Canada. More importantly, this also gives us the ability to kind of de-risk the concentration risk that our customers have been emphasizing.

items.statement: Novo Nordisk guidance cut noted but customers increasing forecasts, willing to pay upfronts; generic price points expected to expand market
items.quote: We share your concerns, Nitin, but it's just the fact that we are a CDMO and we go by what our customers contract with us, right? And at this time, they are increasing forecasts, willing to pay upfronts, and we can only go by that.

items.statement: Markets like Canada, Brazil underserved due to constrained Novo supply; generics to drive access-led volume growth
items.quote: The numbers which you see right now in IQVIA in both Canada, Brazil, and some of the other markets are primarily a factor of supply. It is not a factor of the inherent demand, the patient population, the incidence of diabetes and obesity, which is very significant in these markets. But the numbers have been really constrained by the supplies from Novo.

items.statement: Poland and Baroda acquisitions not factored into $400M organic FY28 guidance; revised guidance to come post-closure
items.quote: Yes, that's correct. We have mentioned that $400 million revenue we gave was through organic growth. And if we do end up closing these acquisitions, it will be significant. Arun already mentioned that FY '27 numbers for these will be about $100 million revenue, about 40% EBITDA. So these would add significantly to our guidance. And once it is closed, we will be sharing a revised guidance.

items.statement: Xbrane partnership tech transfer initiated; completion expected in 12-18 months triggering European and FDA inspections
items.quote: And the tech transfer, to your question, when the tech transfer will start? I think the, in fact, the process is already initiated. This is a biologics product. It's a pretty long tech transfer process. So, we expect the tech transfer to be completed over the next 12 to 18 months. And that will also trigger our inspection, both from Europeans as well as from FDA.

items.statement: Liraglutide and Teriparatide manufactured in Q1 for Europe; customer launch timing in H1 FY26
items.quote: Having said that, Liraglutide for Europe, we have already manufactured this quarter. And our customer will be launching the product and Teriparatide is exactly the same. In fact, we've already manufactured for our customers and it all, the actual launch will depend upon, again, as I said, customer's options and when they want to launch.

items.statement: Potential to service up to a third of generic Semaglutide market in steady state given customer base
items.quote: To your question on our shares, we have really global who's who of generic companies, whether it is the global leaders, the regional leaders, leaders in specific large markets, and I don't know what next 2 years, but in steady state, if we see looking at our customer base, it could be anywhere up to a third, at least, of the generic market as it develops, could be serviced by the customer segment,

items.statement: Limited players expected at Semaglutide generic launch in Canada due to product complexity
items.quote: We are seeing right now there are a few companies who have filed in Canada. Now which ones will get approval, we really don't know. But our guess is these are complex products. So we don't expect the market to be crowded as when the market gets formed. So, in our view, there will be at least at the time of launch, there will be a limited number of players into the market.

items.statement: Brazil patent regime likely allows simultaneous Ozempic and Wegovy launch; ANVISA site approval received
items.quote: Brazil, obviously, we are seeing both ways, First launch is of Ozempic. But the way the Brazilian patent regime works, they don't normally allow any change, any separate patent expiry for the same molecule. So, it is likely that they will come.

items.statement: NCLT process for acquisitions expected to take 12-18 months including SEBI approval, fairness opinion, shareholder approval
items.quote: The whole transaction is going -- will go through a new NCLT process, which will take approximately 12 to 18 months and go through the rigors of SEBI approval, pre-approval before we file to the NCLT followed by shareholders' approval which will include a fairness opinion by a first class banker and then of course it will be a function of additional shares based on valuation.

items.statement: Acquisitions to be funded via equity dilution only; no additional debt on OneSource books
items.quote: It will not require, apart from an equity dilution, it will not require OneSource to lever any kind of debt or add debt to its books, so this will be accretive from that nature

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 22% to 25% for FY26
items.quote: We are looking at the same growth trajectory as we have said. We are looking at what we had promised earlier in guidance of 22 % to 25% growth. And we are in the same lines of guidance as we speak today.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 11.5% to 12%
items.quote: We are comfortable with the margin announced which is around 12%. If you remember in the RHP when we listed in December last year, we had given a guidance of 11.5% to 12% would be our EBITDA profile. And we are maintaining the same.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 order intake of Rs 1,748 crores, up 72% YoY
items.quote: We secured new orders worth Rs. 1,748 crores in Q1 led by predominantly in power transmission distribution, while these included primary orders for large transmission lines by Indian clients notably, this also includes our largest ever substation project which we will be executing in Africa.

items.statement: Unsecured order book including L1 at Rs 15,637 crores as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: As of June 30th, 2025, our unsecured order book including L1 stands at Rs. 15,637 crores giving us a clear runway ahead going forward.

items.statement: Order book mix: 93% T&D, split equally domestic and international within T&D; total 60% domestic, 40% international
items.quote: In terms of the order book mix, approximately 93% of our un executed order book remains in the T&D segment, within this split remains balanced equally between domestic and international T&D projects. However, the total order book of the company is 60% domestic and 40% international.

items.statement: Phase-I capex of Rs 327 crores progressing; brownfield tower factory almost complete, greenfield commissioning by end FY26 or Jan FY27; Phase-II of Rs 198 crores initiated including Rs 58 crores additional capex by Q1/Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our Phase-I of Rs. 327 crores of CAPEX is progressing well. The Brownfield expansion of our tower factory is almost completed in a staggered manner and greenfield project is on track, commissioning by end of this financial year or by January of '27, which means January '26, and Financial Year '27. Further Phase-II involving Rs. 198 crores of investments have been initiated, including Rs. 58 crores

items.statement: Tower capacity expanding from 84,000 to 196,000 metric tons by March 2026; conductor capacity from 24,000 to 49,500 km by June 2026; factories running at ~95% utilisation
items.quote: From 84,000 metric tons, towers we are going to 1,96,000 tons, which will happen by March of '26. Conductors again 24,000 to 49,500 kilometres, which will again happen by June of next year. So, all this is part of a strategic 3year vision and a plan to meet our existing order book and the future orders.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 12.03%, PAT up 105% YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 200 crores, up by 66% on year -on-year basis and EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 12.03%. Profit after tax for the quarter comes at Rs.106 crores which represents a year-on-year growth of 105%.

items.statement: Market opportunity for next 12 months seen at Rs 100,000 crores (Rs 50,000 crores domestic, Rs 50,000 crores international); planning to bid Rs 25,000 crores in next 3-4 months at 8-10% strike rate
items.quote: I would like to share that the market opportunity, potential of the market, as we see today for the next 12 months is around Rs. 100,000 crores, Rs. 50,000 crores from India and Rs. 50,000 crores from international. And we are looking at bidding at least Rs. 25,000 crores in the next 3 -4 months. The potential is good. We are looking at a strike rate of 8% to 10% in terms of win rate.

items.statement: Domestic bidding: 70-80% government clients, 20% private; international bidding only with multilateral funding agencies
items.quote: Predominantly, if I talk India, 70 % to 80% will be our government client and 20% will be our domestic private client. When we bid internationally, we bid with multilateral funding agencies only and we only bid T&D.

items.statement: Working capital days at 76 days including IPO funds, 69 days excluding IPO funds; net working capital improved from 74 days in March to 70 days now
items.quote: Our working capital days stood at 76 days which includes IPO fund. If we exclude that IPO fund from the working capital days, it will come down to 69 days at the end of the quarter which is well within the industry standard.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 520 crores funded by Rs 90 crores IPO proceeds, internal accruals, and ~Rs 300 crores term loan (sanctions in place)
items.quote: This we are funding Rs. 90 crores from the IPO proceeds. That was earmarked in the IPO and rest of the portion we will do it from internal accruals, and we will avail loan of around Rs. 300 crores odd of which the sanctions are in place.

items.statement: Debt expected to increase by Rs 200-300 crores by March 2026 due to capex term loan
items.quote: Presently, it is around Rs. 600 crores and with the term loan which we are going to avail for the CAPEX, it will further increase by Rs. 200 to 300 crores.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 90-92% T&D EPC, 2-5% manufacturing (towers/conductors), 7-10% civil/railway/poles/lighting; solar EPC focus overseas, building team for domestic
items.quote: We are predominantly a T&D company as we mentioned. So, 90 % to 92% will be T&D. And for us, product will be a small business, towers and conductors which may be 2% to 5%. But our focus is on the EPC bit. And we will continue on the same trajectory. So, our other segmental split will be civil jobs, railway electrification and poles and lighting which is 7% to 10% of our portfolio.

items.statement: Underground cabling margins same as transmission; capabilities built for Suriname, Bangladesh, India projects
items.quote: And the margin profile, as I mentioned, it is as much as what we do for transmission. So, margins are not negotiable. We have to look at jobs and margins in line with what we do currently for other segments.

items.statement: Labour sourcing ramped up in last 3 months for domestic; international labour outsourced locally; labour management and retention a clear focus
items.quote: We have ramped up our labor in the last 3 months for domestic. International also we outsource locally. So, we are facing, of course, it is difficult as part of the EPC as I mentioned. Labor management and labor retention is something which we have a very clear focus on but we are managing well.

items.statement: No PQ issues for HVDC transmission lines (already done 800kV); substation HVDC led by OEM; secured Rs 400 crore HVDC job (KPS-2 to Nagpur)
items.quote: In transmission lines; we have already done 800 KV HVDC jobs. So, we don't have any issue in the transmission line. And substations will be led by the OEM. So, we have no issue. We already got a small job of 400 crores for HVDC this year, this is KPS-2 to Nagpur.

items.statement: Monsoon delays of 15-20 days factored into execution plan; steady execution in non-monsoon areas and international projects
items.quote: So, we have already factored the monsoons in our planning for execution. So, definitely projects which are in heavy monsoon areas and are waterlogged, there will be a delay of 15 -20 days, which are factored into execution plan. But we see a steady state of execution happening in projects which are not under the monsoon arena internationally and parts of India.

items.statement: Management expects volume growth in early double-digits for FY26, below the long-term 18% CAGR
items.quote: we do not anticipate the volume growth to be 18% this year, we expect it to be more, let's say, in the early double-digits.

items.statement: On-ground infrastructure execution slowed with PMGSY road construction down 37% and highways down 9% YoY in FY25
items.quote: in case of PMGSY, the length of road constructed is reduced by 37% from FY '24 to FY '25. The pace of construction of highways similarly has reduced by about 9% from '24 to '25.

items.statement: Gross margin fell to 25.8% in Q1 FY26 from 30.3% in Q1 FY25 due to product mix and CEV-5 cost increase
items.quote: Gross margin for Q1 FY '26 stood at 25.8% compared to 30.3% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: CEV-5 transition increased direct material cost by ~400 bps, accounting for ~60% of gross margin decline
items.quote: On a blended level it's just above 400 basis points at direct material cost, yes.

items.statement: Management plans to nudge pricing up towards end of Q2 FY26 after festivals to recover margins
items.quote: We anticipate that we will be able to start nudging the pricing up towards end of Q2.

items.statement: CEV-5 machines contributed ~Rs 310 crore (90%) of SLCM revenue in Q1 FY26 vs Rs 25 crore CEV-4
items.quote: CEV-5 in Q1 contributed, let's say, roughly Rs. 300 plus crores of revenue versus CEV-4 of around Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: New Adinarayanahosahalli facility near Obadenahalli plant expected to commission in H2 FY26
items.quote: We also have our new facility coming up in Adinarayanahosahalli, which is very close to our Obadenahalli plant, which produces SLCMs. This, we expect to commission in the second half of FY '26.

items.statement: Non-SLCM volume grew 25% YoY driven by batching plants and transit mixers; revenue fell 8% due to absence of slip-form pavers
items.quote: On the non-SLCM front, the volumes grew by 25% on year-on-year basis. However, the revenue declined by 8% due to the product mix change.

items.statement: SLCM market share recovered to upwards of 75% in July after temporary dip in Q1
items.quote: as far as July is concerned, I think we have returned back with a very strong number upwards of 75%.

items.statement: Exports contributed 5% of revenue in Q1 FY26; focus on South Asia, Southeast Asia, Africa, Middle East, Central America, Caribbean
items.quote: Exports contributed 5% of the total revenue in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with strong cash position of ~Rs 680 crore (Rs 650 crore investments + Rs 30 crore sweep-in) as of June
items.quote: Cash balance as of June, I mean, the investment portfolio was about Rs. 650 crores, and we had about Rs. 30 crores, which was in sweep-in accounts.

items.statement: Board has not decided on dividend for FY26; cash retained for organic and inorganic growth opportunities
items.quote: At the current time, the Board has not decided to go forward with the dividend for a reason that we are in the growth phase and they believe that the management and collectively the company should reinvest the money to funnel their growth phase.

items.statement: Segment-I (Electro-Mechanical Projects) targets ~15% revenue growth and 7-7.5% margin for FY26; Segment-II (Unitary Products) aspires 10-15% growth and 8-8.5% margin (7-8% in summer-impacted year)
items.quote: As far as Segment-I is concerned, 15% growth is possible and 7% to 7.5% margin we will be able to maintain. And the situation is highly volatile.

items.statement: Unitary Cooling Products growth aspiration 10-15% for FY26 based on past industry track record after weak summer; margin aspiration 8-8.5% but may be 7-8% this year
items.quote: Unitary Cooling Products, the growth should be 10% to 15%. That is the aspiration going by the past record of the industry. For margin, our aspiration is 8% to 8.5%. But in a summer impacted year, it may be tougher. It may be 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Capital employed rose to Rs 2,821 cr from Rs 1,738 cr YoY; company continues investing in manufacturing capacity, R&D and digitalization
items.quote: The capital employed as of June 30, 2025 stood at Rs. 2,821 cr as compared to Rs. 1,738 crores as of June 30, 2024. We continue to invest in manufacturing capacity, research and development and digitalization.

items.statement: R&D spend at ~1.5% of revenue; product portfolio expansion in data center chillers, VRF, liquid cooling driving Segment-I growth
items.quote: Close to around 1.5% of our revenue is in R&D. That is what is making us grow. We will continue to do that.

items.statement: Inventory is only ~30 days above normal (45 days consistent pipeline, 75 days at Himachal factory); no excess inventory issue; production corrected from April first week
items.quote: Inventory is not an issue at all. That one month inventory will be sold off. And there is the correction in not billing began in April first week itself.

items.statement: No price cuts despite weak demand; normal market operating prices and schemes continue; gross margin not the issue
items.quote: When we have only just one -month inventory, there is no reason for us to cut the prices. Normal schemes, whatever is the market operating prices, that will go on.

items.statement: Copper, aluminum and inventory movements not impacting margins in a major way; margin drop mainly from volume-driven operating leverage loss and fixed costs
items.quote: You know, the movements in copper, aluminum and what are the inventories available So, that is not going to impact it in a major way. Definitely most of this kind of comes from the play of volumes.

items.statement: Segment-III margin improved to 10.8% from 9.9% due to favorable product and service mix change; Segment-I margins influenced by project and product mix
items.quote: Segment margins at 10.8% for Q1 FY26 versus 9.9% in Q1 of last year. The improvement was majorly due to favorable change in product and service mix.

items.statement: Market share gains from products at all price points and surgical distribution expansion in Tier 3-5 cities, especially North; not just channel count but counter-level potential analysis
items.quote: Our goal was to end the year with 14.5% market share. So, this is happening with multiple initiatives. Number one is having products at every price point, and expanding our distribution footprint in Tier 3, 4, 5 cities, specifically in northern region.

items.statement: Blue Star outperformed peers (industry -30%, Blue Star -13.3% revenue decline in Unitary Products); gaining share consistently even during COVID
items.quote: We have been gaining market share. That has been our history. Every year we have, even during the COVID period, we have gained market share.

items.statement: Energy label change effective Jan 1, 2026; R&D and supply chain ready; pre-buying expected in Q3; no concern on compliance
items.quote: From 1st January, you have to make the new label. This energy label change happens in consultation with industry. We all know what is the new norm, and we all know which date it is coming into effect. So, therefore, research and development, supply chain issues are already over.

items.statement: Exports only 2% of revenue (US 1%); tariff uncertainty may delay ramp-up but no financial impact; strategy is OEM for established players, not own brand
items.quote: Our dependence on exports, total, all exports put together is 2% of our revenue. If you take United States, it is 1% of our revenue. So, it is not going to be impacting our operations in either manner.

items.statement: Net cash position declined to Rs 370.9 cr from Rs 1,042.9 cr YoY due to capex and working capital investments
items.quote: The company reported a net cash position of Rs. 370.9 cr as of June 30, 2025 as compared to the net cash position of Rs. 1,042.9 cr as of June 30, 2024.

items.statement: In-shop demonstrator and installation/service staff costs committed for anticipated summer season could not be reversed quickly when demand failed, hurting Q1 margins
items.quote: You are preparing for a huge season, and you are employing additional people for installation and service. Now, then April, when it is disappointing, what you think is that the forecast was, May will be the heat wave.

items.statement: Global volatility (US tariffs, exchange rate, consumer sentiment) may impact B2B demand and festival season; company prepared for both scenarios but not planning for worst case
items.quote: It is going to be an important period and it could be a volatile period as well. And we have to watch out and pray that the festival season goes on and Indian economy maintains its momentum.

items.statement: Room AC industry 3-year CAGR remains positive despite Q1 decline; January-June de-growth only single-digit due to March preponement
items.quote: If you look at it like that, the degrowth will be in single digit. Now, why that is important? While the market should do whatever it is doing, for us, it is connected with the strategic direction.

items.statement: Compressor supply chain secured for 12 months; evaluating options - procure from expanding Indian makers, manufacture in-house, or join JV; QCO extension uncertainty monitored
items.quote: Right now, our supply chain is secured for about 12 months' time, in the sense that till end of next summer season we are covered. So, we will keep reviewing it.

items.statement: Global sugar market projected in mild surplus for sugar year 2025-26 due to higher production in Brazil, India, Thailand
items.quote: The global sugar market is projected to remain in mild surplus through the sugar year '25-26, primarily due to increased production in Brazil, India, and Thailand.

items.statement: Raw sugar prices fell from $0.215/lb in February to ~$0.16/lb currently
items.quote: This has driven raw sugar prices down from $0.215 per pound in February to about $0.16 per pound at present.

items.statement: Ethanol blending program developments and India-U.S. trade talks to be monitored for sector impact
items.quote: Also, developments on the ethanol blending program, particularly on ethanol pricing as well as outcomes of India-U.S. trade talks and any bearings this might have on the ethanol and sugar sector will also need to be monitored.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu plants crushed average 63 days in Q1 FY26
items.quote: As far as the sugar operations is concerned, the Tamil Nadu plants crushed an average of 63 days, during the quarter 1.

items.statement: Cane crushed 2.11 LMT in Q1 FY26 vs 1.93 LMT YoY; recovery 8.02% vs 8.6% YoY
items.quote: In Q1, we crushed about 2.11 LMT as compared to the corresponding quarter of the previous year of 1.93 LMT. Recoveries were under pressure as the recovery for the current quarter was 8.02% against 8.6% of the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Cane cost INR 3,844/MT vs INR 3,491/MT YoY due to FRP increase from INR 3,150 to INR 3,400/MT
items.quote: The cane cost is about INR 3,844 per metric ton against INR 3,491 per metric ton of the corresponding quarter of the previous year. This is mainly on account of the FRP impact, which was declared by the central government from INR 3,150 to INR 3,400 per metric ton.

items.statement: Sugar sales volume 84,000 MT in Q1 FY26, all domestic, vs 1.05 LMT YoY due to lower release quota
items.quote: The sugar sales volume for the current quarter is 84,000 metric tons. This is completely driven by the domestic sales. There is no export quota available for us. We already exported whatever quota was available. The corresponding quarter of the previous year was 1.05

items.statement: Average sugar selling price INR 41.99/kg vs INR 38.60/kg YoY
items.quote: As far as the sugar selling price is concerned, overall average selling price is INR 41.99, against the previous year's corresponding quarter of INR 38.60.

items.statement: Carrying 1.2 LMT sugar inventory valued at average INR 37/kg as of June 2025
items.quote: We are carrying about 1.2 LMT of sugar as at June '25, and we are valued at an average of INR 37.

items.statement: Sugar segment revenue INR 347 cr vs INR 404 cr YoY, down 14% on lower release quota
items.quote: As far as the segment revenue is concerned, sugar revenue for the current quarter is about INR 347 crores as against INR 404 crores of the corresponding quarter of the previous year, registering a decline of about 14% on a lower release quota.

items.statement: Consumer Product Group turnover INR 192 cr vs INR 216 cr YoY, down 11% on lower sweetener quota, staples up 33%
items.quote: The Consumer Product Group delivered a turnover of about INR 192 crores for the current quarter, registering a decline of 11% over the corresponding quarter of the previous year of INR 216 crores, mainly on account of lower release quota for the sweetener category, partly offset by steady performance in the staples segment, which registered a growth of 33% over the corresponding quarter of the pre

items.statement: Co-generation revenue INR 7.53 cr vs INR 11.94 cr YoY; power generated 221 lakh units vs 307 lakh units; tariff INR 3.67/unit vs INR 4.23/unit
items.quote: Co-generation is concerned, the power generated during the quarter was about 221 lakh units as against 307 lakh units in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. We exported about 122 lakh units against 170 lakh units in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Average power tariff for the current quarter is INR 3.67 per unit as against INR 4.23 per unit in the corresponding quarter

items.statement: Distillery sold 413 LL vs 390 LL YoY; realization INR 67.59/L vs INR 64.31/L; revenue INR 296 cr vs INR 263 cr
items.quote: As far as Distillery is concerned, we have sold about 413 lakh litres (LL) against the previous corresponding quarter, 390 LL, of which ENA is 153 LL and ethanol was 260 LL. As far as the realization is concerned, INR 67.59 per litre against corresponding quarter of the previous year's realization of INR 64.31. Revenues were INR 296 crores compared to INR 263 crores during the corresponding quarte

items.statement: Nutraceuticals India turnover INR 5.94 cr vs INR 8.41 cr YoY; consolidated INR 27 cr vs INR 59 cr YoY
items.quote: As far as the Nutraceuticals segment is concerned, turnover of the Indian operations was about INR 5.94 crores against INR 8.41 crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. At the consolidated level, Nutra business turnover is about INR 27 crores as against INR 59 crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Refinery operational revenue INR 908 cr vs INR 1,213 cr YoY
items.quote: As far as the refinery operations are concerned, the operational revenue in this quarter is INR 908 crores as against INR 1,213 crores the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT positive INR 67 lakh vs loss of INR 6.79 cr YoY
items.quote: As far as the PBT is concerned, it is a good story because we made a positive PBT of INR 67 lakhs against the loss of INR 6.79 crores.

items.statement: Long-term loans INR 200 cr to be repaid to parent; short-term loans INR 461 cr vs INR 220 cr YoY
items.quote: As far as long-term loans are concerned, it was about INR 200 crores, to be repaid to the parent company. And as far as the short-term loans are concerned, they are INR 461 crores as against corresponding quarter of the previous year is about INR 220 crores.

items.statement: Short-term debt increased due to molasses forward contracts for distillery and higher CPG receivables
items.quote: Second reason, you have to look at our CPG business as going well, and our receivables also are slightly going up in line with the turnover and the industry standards. Therefore, our working capital requirement is going up. So thereby, correspondingly, your short-term debt is going up.

items.statement: Short-term debt expected to remain around INR 1,100 cr at year-end, similar to current levels
items.quote: More or less it will be at the same levels, Rajesh, because if you look at it today, you are looking at about INR 1,100 crores or something. Even at the year-end, we'll be looking at the same.

items.statement: Closed UAE step-down subsidiary in refinery segment; capital infusion for debt reduction in Kakinada refinery
items.quote: So yes, I can comment on this. Rajesh, so I think, as you know, the refinery business, there is a lot of debt, and this capital has really gone in for debt reduction in order to strengthen the operations of the refinery. And I think that's why we've had these infusions.

items.statement: No current capacity expansion plans; ethanol capex cycle concluded, in consolidation phase
items.quote: Not at present. We've just finished up last year our ethanol capex. So, capex cycle is largely concluded. It is a phase of consolidation right now.

items.statement: Government steering ethanol blending program positively; no visibility on internal discussions for 25-27% blending target
items.quote: The direction the government E.I.D.- Parry ( has been taking on the EBP is highly appreciable. They seem to be steering the industry and the usage of ethanol in the right direction. So, we remain positive about the government's approach on the issue. I may not be able to comment on what the internal discussions that the government is currently doing because we do

items.statement: May consider repurposing 1-2 distilleries to dual feed (grain and molasses) subject to policy clarity
items.quote: If at all, there's something we might consider, we have one dual feed distillery. We might consider repurposing one or two of our other distilleries to operate on both grain as well as molasses-based feedstock. This is perhaps something we might consider. But this is again subject to obtaining policy clarity and subject to further internal evaluation.

items.statement: CPG strategy: focus on value-added browns in sweetener; distribution and brand building in staples; new food products in development
items.quote: In terms of sweetener, the focus is largely on the value-added browns category where we are seeing a potential opportunity to grow. And most of the expansion and growth will come in largely on the browns category for the sweetener. For the non-sweetener, it will be the continued focus on distribution and brand building for the next few quarters.

items.statement: CPG distribution expansion targeting modern trade, e-commerce, general trade; no specific 3-year distribution or revenue targets disclosed
items.quote: We won't have a number at this point in time, but I think we will be growing pretty aggressively in this category. And our expansion plans will include consolidating ourselves largely in modern trade, e-commerce, and the general trade channel.

items.statement: Karnataka crushing expected marginally positive vs last year; Tamil Nadu largely neutral, revival may take 1-2 cycles
items.quote: Monsoon has been good in the states of Karnataka and Maharashtra. So overall, the industry is looking for a good crop this year. Our internal data also is showing robust situation. So, we would expect marginally positive upside in Karnataka crushing this year as compared to last year. Tamil Nadu (TN) will be largely neutral.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue to double in next 3-4 years; auto components to grow low to mid-teens
items.quote: So basically, in terms of aerospace, it will be double. And the automotive business will grow in the low to mid-teens depending on how the macroeconomic situations play out.

items.statement: High-teen growth expected in aerospace and early teens growth in industrial business for FY26
items.quote: So, we have a -- we will look at a high-teen growth basically in aerospace and an early teens growth in our industrial business.

items.statement: Aerospace EBITDA margins expected around 25% as scale increases
items.quote: We are very confident as we scale up, our EBITDA margins continue to grow in that range, which we talked about is around the 25%.

items.statement: Auto components EBITDA margins to reach double digits in a couple of years
items.quote: In a couple of years, it will be there.

items.statement: Operational ROCE expected to return to 20%+ in next 2 years
items.quote: You would see again going back to the 20-plus percent on an operational basis, the ROCE.

items.statement: Commercial aircraft backlog of over 16,000 units provides 12-15 years production visibility
items.quote: Commercial aircraft backlog of over 16,000 units translates to between 12 and 15 years of production visibility.

items.statement: Aerospace contracts span 5-10 years aligning with OEM ramp-ups through 2035 and beyond
items.quote: Our contracts span 5 to 10 years, aligning us with OEM ramp-ups through 2035 and beyond.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 15.7% in Q1 FY26 vs 18.9% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Raymond Limited delivered a steady quarterly performance, reporting a total income of INR555 crores and delivering an EBITDA of INR87 crores and an EBITDA margin of 15.7% in the first quarter of fiscal '26 versus a total income of INR500 crores, delivering an EBITDA of INR95 crores with an EBITDA margin of 18.9% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Aerospace EBITDA margin 23.7% in Q1 FY26 vs 25.1% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Aerospace and defence business reported a robust performance, reporting a revenue of INR87 crores, which is 37% year -on-year growth and an EBITDA of INR21 crores with a 30% year -on-year growth and an EBITDA margin of 23.7% in Q1 FY '26 versus a revenue of INR64 crores with an EBITDA margin of INR16 crores and an EBITDA margin percentage of 25.1% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Precision technology and auto components EBITDA margin 10.6% in Q1 FY26 vs 11% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Precision technology and auto components reported a revenue of INR398 crores, which is a 12% year -on-year growth with an EBITDA of INR42 crores, which is an 8% year -on-year growth and an EBITDA margin of 10.6% in Q1 FY '26. This is versus a revenue of INR355 crores with an EBITDA of INR39 crores and an EBITDA margin of 11% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Land acquired in Andhra Pradesh for aerospace capacity expansion; project timeline 18-24 months
items.quote: We thought appropriate to expand into Andhra. But it is not happening today to tomorrow because any project takes its own course of time, whether it is 18 months, 24 months is something which we look at it in terms of churning the products out of there.

items.statement: New plant inaugurated at Sinnar, Nashik; capacity increase planned for flex plates and bearings
items.quote: We inaugurated a new plant there, which is in Sinnar. And we are now looking to grow those businesses because we have steady products there, which is the Flex plate and the bearings, which are up to capacity, and we're going to increase some capacity there as well.

items.statement: Net cash surplus of INR157 crores as of June 2025; gross debt INR965 crores, cash INR1,122 crores
items.quote: We continue to remain a debt -free business with a net cash surplus of INR157 crores in June 2025. The total gross debt stands at INR965 crores and have cash and cash equivalents of INR1,122 crores as of June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Gross debt increased due to external refinancing of inter-company debt from Raymond Limited
items.quote: The debt was given from Raymond Limited to the engineering business. And now we have got it externally refinanced that debt. And therefore, the gross debt is higher.

items.statement: Focus on deploying cash flows into growth for next 3-4 years; only scheduled debt repayments
items.quote: For the next 3 to 4 years, a significant portion of the cash flow, except for the mandatory repayments, which we are there, scheduled repayments, not mandatory, scheduled repayments are there. Other than that, I don't think so we will have a very big debt reduction.

items.statement: Signed MoU with Safran Aircraft Engines and long-term supply agreement with Pratt & Whitney in Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are thrilled to announce the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding with Safran Aircraft Engines, expanding our existing partnership to manufacture machine assemblies. Concurrently, we also signed a long-term supply agreement with Pratt & Whitney for precision machined and assembled aerospace components.

items.statement: Rising tariffs in key export markets creating challenges for Indian drivetrain and structural component exporters
items.quote: Increasing tariffs in key export markets are creating new challenges, particularly for Indian exporters of drivetrain and structural components.

items.statement: Aerospace SKUs grown from 50 to 1,250; journey from components to higher-value assemblies
items.quote: We started with 50 SKUs, moved to 100, moved to 200 and reaching 1,250 SKUs. So, as you continue, you need to win the confidence of the customer. And there, he keeps increasing you from a component, you go to what you call, assemblies, which is much more value added.

items.statement: Restructuring completed: NCLT order received July 4, 2025; scheme effective August 1, 2025 creating JKMPTL and JKMGAL
items.quote: I'm pleased to announce that we have received the NCLT order on 4th of July 2025, and the scheme is effective from 1st of August 2025. As per the scheme, 2 companies are constituted, namely JK Maini Precision Technology Limited, in short JKMPTL, comprising of erstwhile JK Files & Engineering; RPAL, which is the Ring Plus Aqua; and Auto business of Maini Precision Products Limited. A nd the second

items.statement: Plan to double aerospace business via M&A in next 3-4 years
items.quote: In terms of -- basically, we are trying to see in the aerospace, we are trying to double M&As in the next 3 to 4 years. So, we have a plan for that, and we are going to -- we're working on that plan.

items.statement: Heavy monsoon season poses logistical hurdles and supply chain disruption risks for CV sector
items.quote: Potential supply chain disruptions and logistical hurdles from a heavy monsoon season remain key risks.

items.statement: Emerging protectionist tariff trends in export markets could present headwinds for subsystem and component suppliers
items.quote: emerging protectionist tariff trends in some export markets could present headwinds for subsystem and component suppliers in the

items.statement: Industrial sales grew 13% YoY driven by railways, wind, and heavy sectors; Automotive flat at -0.4% YoY due to model changes and CV/PV decline; Exports down ~1% YoY due to tariffs and weak Southeast Asia/Americas demand
items.quote: Our net sales, as I said, has grown at around 6% year-on-year, primarily driven by a stronger Industrial growth, we have grown 13% in Industrial year-on-year, which is excellent growth driven by railways, wind and some of the heavy sectors. Automotive, on the other hand, has actually declined or is almost flat by around 0.4%.

items.statement: Margins fell 530 bps YoY due to demerger costs (IT, consultants), employee increments, higher depreciation from factory investments, weaker rupee, and adverse mix from higher traded volumes
items.quote: Our margin this quarter has come down by almost 530 basis points. The reasons for this are related to, one, demerger-related costs, onetime costs, both IT as well as IT-related costs as well as consultants.

items.statement: Demerger costs of ~1.5-2% margin impact to continue until H1 FY27; stamp duty/registration costs may further hit Industrial margins in H1 FY27; 16-19% margin range targeted from FY28 onwards
items.quote: So you could expect at least a couple of percentage adverse impact on the margins on account of the demerger cost. Apart from that, there could be some additional cost which the industrial company might incur in first half of next financial year with respect to stamp duty and registration cost for the transfer of assets.

items.statement: Ahmedabad plant (unlisted entity) already commissioned; additional investments to materialize over 2.5-3 years (by end 2027); listed entity continuing capex in Pune for capacity and localization
items.quote: The Ahmedabad plant is already commissioned, right. They are already operating in the unlisted entity. There are additional investments which have been planned, and most of the investments should materialize in 2.5 to 3 years. So sometime by end of 2027 is when we expect all the capex to materialize and production to start.

items.statement: Pune capacity expansions for both Auto and Industrial coming online in FY27-28; Bangalore lines split 7 Auto/3 Industrial, Pune 12 Auto/10 Industrial, Haridwar 4 Auto; capacity to support market share gains
items.quote: We expect that, that will -- we will expand capacity in, again, in the '27-'28 time frame, and that will help us expand more rapidly than our competitors and hence gain share.

items.statement: Industrial growth driven by railways (high-speed rail, metros), wind (select profitable applications), metals aftermarket, general machinery (pumps, drives, gearboxes), and distribution (8-10% steady growth)
items.quote: Other sectors which have grown well in Industrial are, as I mentioned, railways with some of the high-speed rail projects, we are continuing to do well there and metros. In the heavy industry, we are primarily seeing some expansion in metals, mainly in aftermarket, not new projects, but aftermarket.

items.statement: Higher traded volumes at lower margins creating adverse mix impact; Industrial 53% of sales, Automotive 39%, Exports 8%
items.quote: In addition, we also have slightly higher traded volume, which is at a lower margin, and that is creating the mix issue.

items.statement: Weaker rupee (FX) negatively impacted margins; employee costs up due to annual increments; depreciation up from factory investments
items.quote: And finally, FX has also had an impact on our business because of the weaker rupee. So all these are contributors.

items.statement: Net working capital reduced QoQ but up from full year; driven by higher receivables from volume growth, partially offset by inventory decline from Q4 FY25; net cash flow improved 13% YoY
items.quote: In net working capital, we have actually reduced a bit the net working capital from quarter-on-quarter, but up a bit from full year, primarily driven by accounts receivable, higher volume of business, but also partially the decline from fourth quarter '25 to now has come from a decline in our inventory.

items.statement: Demerger scheme approved by shareholders on July 14; NCLT decision expected in September; targeting listing of two separate entities by Q4 calendar 2025
items.quote: The shareholder meeting for the demerger is – has -- was done on 14 th July, and they have approved the scheme as the demerger scheme. So -- and NCLT has noted that also, and the we should hear back from on the decision in the month of September

items.statement: Exports ~8% of total revenue; Industrial ~5-5.5%, Automotive ~2.5-3%; exports down ~1% YoY due to tariffs and weak demand in Southeast Asia/Americas
items.quote: So the overall exports that we have within SKF is around 8% of our total revenue. And a out of the 8%, almost 5% -5.5% is pertaining to Industrial and remaining 2.5% - 3% is pertaining to the Automotive.

items.statement: Gaining business with Mahindra in SUV segment (hub units) and Mahindra Swaraj in tractors; market share gains in Auto 2W, 3W, PV over recent years
items.quote: So we are continuing to gain business with Mahindra, particularly in their SUV segment, and we supply what we call the hub units for them.

items.statement: Aspiration to grow above industry and gain market share in Automotive; capacity expansion in FY27-28 to remove bottleneck and win OEM commitments
items.quote: Our aspiration is to grow above industry, continue to gain market share. And I believe with capacity expansion, one of our biggest bottlenecks in Automotive has been a lack of capacity.

items.statement: Industrial 5-year CAGR ~15%; guided 8-10% long-term growth for Industrial (FY28 target); Automotive guided 10-12% growth for next 3 years; services business growing high double-digits/high teens, currently ~3% of total revenue (~6% of Indus
items.quote: So we -- while in the recent past, we have had a little bit more muted, in the Industrial business where we have had a little bit more muted growth primarily due to portfolio cleanup, meaning we have dropped customers or products which are not profitable, we are -- we expect that growth to come back, right, in -- and then we're being cautiously optimistic here when we say 8% to 10% long-term growt

items.statement: Demerger costs (INR 184M in Q1) to continue until H1 FY27; additional stamp duty/registration costs in H1 FY27; FX volatility; margin pressure from depreciation on new capex
items.quote: So if you look at our current quarter, cost of demerger was around INR184 million. A significant chunk of that cost was on IT implementation, which is as we are going through a demerger between Automotive and Industrial businesses, a significant spend has been made in creating and deploying SAP as well as other softwares that we use within SKF.

items.statement: Strong hotel demand expected for 2025 driven by demographic shift, UHNI growth, and 15% inbound tourism forecast
items.quote: For the outlook perspective, we see a strong hotel demand coming through for the current year 2025, and the factors are already mentioned there on the growth drivers. A lot of factors driving that growth, but majorly coming a demographic shift of the Indian population with good increase in UHNI base, as well as forecast for inbound tourism to grow by 15% in the current year.

items.statement: Industry ARR up 9-11% in Q1 FY26 despite flat occupancy; RevPAR up 11-13%
items.quote: On ARR we saw an increase of 9 -11%, though on the occupancy, it was more or less flat. We saw an increase of 11-13% on RevPAR versus last year.

items.statement: Consolidated RevPAR grew 16% YoY to INR 11,350 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: From INR 9,811 in Q1 last year, we are at INR 11,350 this year, which is a growth of 16% year over year, on RevPAR.

items.statement: Owned and managed hotels RevPAR grew 16% YoY vs industry 12%; Oberoi brand up 21%
items.quote: Industry growth was up at 12% in Q1. Our owned and managed hotels grew @ 16% which was a little higher than the industry growth. Oberoi Hotels continues to lead the pack with a growth of 21% on a RevPAR basis over last year.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 occupancy flat at ~70%, ARR up 18% YoY
items.quote: Overall, in spite of occupancy being flat, we saw a healthy growth on ARR every month. On a net basis, if we look at the overall quarter, we were almost flat at 70%, on occupancy but a good increase in ARR which is at 18% growth.

items.statement: 25 new properties (2,033 keys) by 2030; 8 owned, 17 managed; 1,750 keys domestic
items.quote: List of new hotels pipeline is 25 with 2,033 keys spread out across domestic and international, mainly in domestic. Number of keys in the domestic front would be 1,750 keys out 2,033 in total. Out of the 25 properties, we will be owning 8 and managing 17.

items.statement: Managed hotel delays (Dahabeya, Nepal) due to partner timelines; owned hotels on track
items.quote: So, these hotels are all managed hotels. And, although we work very closely with our partners, if there is a delay, our influence over those on the timelines, because these are managed hotels, is not as much as hotels that we own or have a significant equity interest in.

items.statement: Exceptional item of INR 110 Cr from Mashobra court judgment; no further exceptional items expected
items.quote: INR 110 crores actually constitutes of various elements. We have passed the accounting entries basis the court judgment. The 110 crores net impact on account of equity value, which we are not receiving based on the court judgment and also has an impact of 50% advance against equity, which we'd given to Mashobra. So that constitutes the 110 crores.

items.statement: CFO confirms current Mashobra exceptional item is final; no more expected
