items.statement: No major supply chain constraints; base metals from Vedanta and Hindalco for 20-25 years; scrap buy-back from customers ensures supply
items.quote: We are dependent on three major raw materials. One is the scraps that we need that is used for recycling. Then, we need base metal which we source from Vedanta and Hindalco. So, there is no major constraint in our supply chain and we are dealing with them for last 20-25 years.

items.statement: Subsidiaries' capex underway with term lending secured; production commencement expected Q4 FY26; 5-7% contribution FY26, 35-40% top line growth next year
items.quote: The company's subsidiaries are in the path of making their capexes and we have already secured some term lending from our banker. So that investment is in process. But I am hopeful that in the last quarter of this financial year, we shall be in position to commence our production with those capexes.

items.statement: Zambia copper cathode plant 1,200 tpa capacity; commercial production by end Q2 FY26; first year 700-800 tons; potential scale to 6,000 tpa
items.quote: That plant is having annual capacity of 1,200 metric tons per annum. And initially for first year, I expect it to be doing around 700-800 tons for next financial year. But once everything is streamlined, the supply of ore and all those things are done, then company may think of further doing the capex there and scale up our operations to roughly 6,000 tons a year.

items.statement: Domestic prices better than export due to strong local demand; product mix driven by demand-supply gap
items.quote: Presently, the domestic market is having a substantial demand and rather I will say it's performing better than the international market. So, the prices in India are better than the exports.

items.statement: Cable production awaiting second ISI license; expect licenses in 2 months; commercial production Q3/Q4 FY26
items.quote: We have got one ISI license already we have and we have started fighting that government tender. One more ISI license is awaited for insulated one. expect by two months we will be in position to get all the requisite licenses and then we will be into commercial production.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improving quarter on quarter
items.quote: It is improving, madam. It is improving. It is improving.

items.statement: 25-year hedging practice; sell first, buy later; no impact from metal price volatility
items.quote: We have a proper hedging desk in our company. This is not new. We are doing our hedging for last 25 years. Company has never had any impact of positive or negative growth in me tal prices. We keep ourselves secured by selling first and buying then

items.statement: Zambia production 5% of requirement first year, targeting 20% replacement next year; exploring other international geographies
items.quote: For first year, it will be roughly 5% of our total requirement. And once everything goes smoothly, then next year we are planning to replace it to 20%.

items.statement: Foresees very big demand for winding wires from transformer and EV sectors over next 2-3 years
items.quote: I can foresee a very big demand coming up.

items.statement: Long-term growth target 30-45% CAGR for next 10 years based on historical trend
items.quote: You can see we have been growing at a constant pace of 30% to 40%, 45% around. To maintain that pace, the energy will be there, the money and everything has to be there and I expect this journey to continue for further 10 years.

items.statement: Targets 25% CAGR growth in EPS year-on-year as bare minimum guidance
items.quote: what we have always said and the only guidance that we have given is that we strive for a 25% CAGR growth in our EPS year-on-year. That's the bare minimum that we try.

items.statement: Expects to reach US$ 1.2 billion capex by end of next year and US$ 5 billion aggregate capex by 2030
items.quote: we will already reach a Capex of US$ 1.2 billion by the end of next year and we expect to reach US$ 5 billion aggregate Capex by 2030 which would be funded by a mix of internal accruals and utilization of debt with a prudent debt gearing ratio of 0.6X capped to a 3.5X of EBITDA.

items.statement: JNPT project of Rs. 1,675 crores for liquids, LPG and LPG bottling plant is officially underway
items.quote: we have been allotted an additional 30 acres of land at this port on which a capital expenditure project of Rs. 1,675 crores is being set up for liquids, LPG as well as an LPG bottling plant. This project is now officially underway.

items.statement: Mumbai liquid capacity expansion of 125,000 kiloliters: 50% operational next quarter, balance by end of fiscal year
items.quote: we also have an upcoming liquid capacity of 125,000 kiloliters, 50% of which is expected to be operational in the ensuing quarter and the balance by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Kandla TRL4 liquid terminal of 94,148 cubic meters expected to operate next year
items.quote: In Kandla, we have acquired an additional plot of land, which we are calling TRL4, where a liquid terminal capacity with a capacity of about 94,148 cubic meters will be set up and this is expected to come into operation next year.

items.statement: Pipavav ammonia terminal of 36,000 metric tons static capacity expected completion before Q1 next fiscal year with 15-year take-or-pay contract for Hindustan Zinc DAP plant
items.quote: India's first independent ammonia terminal at Pipavav, of course, as I mentioned, is being set up with a static capacity of 36,000 metric tons and this project is expected to be completed before the 1 st Quarter of the next fiscal year and this ammonia terminal has a take or pay contract for 15 years to service the upcoming DAP plant of Hindustan Zinc.

items.statement: Mangalore cryogenic LPG storage terminal of 82,000 metric tons static capacity added last month, first vessel welcomed
items.quote: At Mangalore Port, we added the cryogenic LPG storage terminal with an 82,000 metric tons static capacity last month and the first vessel was welcomed last month with the inauguration of the LPG loading arm which made its first pilot discharge.

items.statement: Pipavav LPG capacity of 48,000 metric tons added last month, total static capacity now 70,800 metric tons
items.quote: At Pipavav, the LPG capacity with 48,000 metric tons of static cryogenic capacity has been added last month and with this expansion, the total LPG terminal static capacity at Pipavav has reached 70,800 metric tons.

items.statement: Non-binding MoU signed with L&T for ammonia terminal at Kandla for their green ammonia manufacturing facility
items.quote: a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding with Larsen and Toubro; L&T, has been signed up to set up ammonia terminal at Kandla for their upcoming green ammonia manufacturing facility at Kandla.

items.statement: LPG throughput volume increased 15% YoY to 1.16 million tons in Q1 FY26, highest ever Q1 throughput
items.quote: Throughput revenue in Q1 FY26, LPG volume handled at all our terminals was 1.16 million tons versus 1.01 million metric tons in Q1 FY25, an increase of 15%.

items.statement: Distribution volumes of auto, commercial and industrial bulk increased to 1.45 lakh metric tons in Q1 FY26 from 1.28 lakh metric tons in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The distribution volumes of auto, commercial and industrial bulk handled was 1.45 lakh metric tons in Q1 FY26 against 1.28 lakh metric tons in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: LPG distribution EBITDA per ton expected to average Rs. 3,000-3,500 per metric ton for the year, currently at Rs. 2,500 in Q1 due to volume push in new geographies
items.value: Rs. 3,000 to Rs. 3,500 per metric ton
items.quote: distribution margins, please look at on a yearly basis, they are generally around Rs. 3,000. Last year, we clocked Rs. 3,500, this year also we expect to be around the same. So, on an average, we will always end at around Rs. 3,000 to Rs. 3,500 per ton.

items.statement: Liquid division yearly average realization around Rs. 3,000 per CBM and EBITDA margin around Rs. 2,000 per CBM
items.quote: if you look at the yearly realization in liquid, they are always around Rs. 3,000 per CBM. That is how it comes on an average.

items.statement: LPG throughput EBITDA margin generally Rs. 1,000-1,100 per ton over full year
items.quote: over the whole year, it will balance out and you will see generally Rs. 1,000 to 1,100 max is what will be the EBITDA per ton in case of throughput of LPG.

items.statement: KGPL and JLPL pipelines expected to operationalize in Q2 FY26, will boost Kandla volumes
items.quote: this asset will see a jump in the volumes with the operationalization of the KGPL and JLPL pipelines, which is expected in the second quarter of this financial year, to which we are connected to both of these pipelines.

items.statement: VLGCs will start berthing at Kandla Port, enabling larger cargo unloading
items.quote: Another positive initiative at this port is that finally, VLGCs will start berthing at Kandla Port, which will also benefit the operations and as we shall be able to unload a larger size cargoes.

items.statement: Signed cross-selling fuel agreement with Jio BP for distribution business
items.quote: I am really pleased to announce that we have just signed a cross-selling of fuel agreement with Jio BP which I think really could be a very interesting development for our distribution business.

items.statement: Confident on JNPT capacity despite competitor announcements; BW LPG infrastructure reportedly withdrawn
items.quote: we have examined all the macro market conditions, competition, everything and after having confidence on all the parameters, we have decided to go ahead. Another thing which you can notice that the so-called LPG infrastructure that you have referred to, there are news items saying that BW has, of course, withdrawn.

items.statement: City gas distribution company entering LPG marketing in Morbi seen as positive; they may use Aegis terminals for storage
items.quote: you should be happy. Finally, what we have been saying over a number of years is happening that you will find a city gas, natural gas player wanting to get into LPG business. The more the merrier. That's what I always believe. And probably they would come, they don't have their own terminals. So, probably they would be coming to store at our terminals only.

items.statement: Standalone cash balance of Rs. 4,130 crores as of June 30, generating ~Rs. 80-90 crores quarterly interest income
items.quote: You have a very large cash balance of around Rs. 4,130 crores as of 30 th June. So, you can look at 7% per annum is Rs. 290 crores divided by 4 would be somewhere around Rs. 80-90 crores would be interest received only.

items.statement: Capex to be funded by internal accruals and debt with prudent gearing ratio of 0.6X capped to 3.5X EBITDA
items.quote: we expect to reach US$ 5 billion aggregate Capex by 2030 which would be funded by a mix of internal accruals and utilization of debt with a prudent debt gearing ratio of 0.6X capped to a 3.5X of EBITDA.

items.statement: Phase-II equity infusion legally required within 3 years under SEBI regulations post AVTL IPO
items.quote: With the recently concluded Phase-I equity infusion by way of the IPO and as you know we are legally obliged to have a Phase-II equity infusion within the next 3 years under the SEBI regulations, the Capex therefore will be largely funded.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 normalized EBITDA Rs. 256 crores (+2% YoY), PAT Rs. 175 crores (+11% YoY)
items.quote: Q1 FY26 normalized EBITDA stood at Rs. 256 crores, an increase of 2% year-on-year. Profit after tax increased by 11% to Rs. 175 crores for the 1 st Quarter this year versus Rs.158 crores in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Liquid segment Q1 FY26 revenue Rs. 144 crores (+1% YoY), EBITDA Rs. 106 crores stable
items.quote: Liquid Q1 FY26 revenue from Liquid segments stood at Rs. 144 crores compared to Rs.143 crores a year-on-year increase of 1%. We delivered a stable Q1 EBITDA of Rs. 106 crores in Liquid.

items.statement: LPG segment Q1 FY26 EBITDA Rs. 150 crores (+6% YoY), revenue Rs. 1,575 crores (+8% YoY)
items.quote: LPG business Q1 FY26 EBITDA was Rs. 150 crores as compared to Rs. 142 crores in Q1 FY25, an increase of 6% YOY. Revenue from LPG business stood at Rs. 1,575 crores achieving an 8% YOY growth.

items.statement: Achieved highest ever liquid revenue in Q1, highest ever gas EBITDA in Q1, highest ever Q1 LPG throughput volume
items.quote: We achieved the highest liquid revenue in Q1 ever. We also achieved highest gas EBITDA in Q1 ever. And we also achieved highest throughput in Q1 LPG throughput volume ever.

items.statement: New terminal utilization starts at 25-30% and scales to near 100% over 5-7 years; asset life 40 years
items.quote: a gas terminal takes usually, is built with a capacity that should last the customer for 5-7 years. So, it starts with a 25%-30% utilization then scales up and in 5-7 years, you then see almost close to 100% utilization, the life of the asset, both of liquid and gas is 40 years.

items.statement: MSCI ESG rating upgraded from A to AA in calendar year 2025
items.quote: I am just pleased to announce that our ESG rating from MSCI has been upgraded from (A) to (AA) in this calendar year.

items.statement: AVTL successfully listed in June 2025; Aegis holds 44.71% equity with management control and consolidated financials
items.quote: We are pleased to share that our subsidiary AVTL was successfully listed in June, 2025. Aegis Logistics continues to hold 44.71% equity in AVTL and it is important to note that given Aegis Logistics management control over the company, AVTL financials continue to be consolidated into Aegis Logistics financial statement.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 8% to 10% for current year
items.quote: So we stick to that guidance. We would like to kind of cross that guidance, deliver and then come back to the investor community.

items.statement: Incremental sales expected at 1.7x of INR 200 crore investment over 2-3 years
items.quote: In terms of revenue, if I am not completely off target, we have done an investment of around INR 200-odd crores. And so we always say in a very conservative basis that the incremental sales would be 1.7x in a period of 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Capex paused for FY26 to focus on ramping up existing investments
items.quote: So, we are going to go slow. We are going to probably take a pause. We are going to evaluate what's happening with all the CAPEX that we have done and take it to its logical conclusion.

items.statement: All plants except Mahad running at 75-80% optimal capacity; Ambernath fragrance plant on one shift with room to add another
items.quote: So except Mahad, where we are seeing volumes kind of grow in terms of monthly production and monthly sales, we can very safely say that all the rest of the plants across all our sites are running at optimal capacity of anywhere between 75% to 80% of their total peak capacity.

items.statement: Mahad facility currently at 20-30% utilization, targeting optimal levels by year-end
items.quote: No, that is the only facility, which currently is kind of post commissioning. We are ramping up our production. And we have a window of, say, 5 to 6 months where we go through the process of sampling, getting approvals and then starting commercial shipments. So, that facility is currently running at between 20% to 30%.

items.statement: Expecting stronger Q2 driven by festive season demand across camphor, fragrances and aroma chemicals
items.quote: With festive demand ahead, robust capacity and the right product mix, we are optimistic and expecting a stronger Quarter 2.

items.statement: International fragrance demand remains strong, driving specialty aroma ingredients growth
items.quote: International demand from our global customers for fragrances also remains strong. Stronger demand in the fragrance division naturally translates into increased demand for our specialty aroma ingredients division.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 8.03% but below year-ago 10.29% due to Mahad ramp-up impact
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 8.03%. While margins could have been higher, they reflect the initial yet promising ramp-up phase of our Mahad facility, an impact we expect will continue for a few quarters ahead.

items.statement: Core business EBITDA margin (ex-trading) in 8-10% range, below historical 14-17% normalized levels
items.quote: Correct. Yes. In terms of the percentage, it remains in the same range, 1% plus or minus.

items.statement: Camphor pricing firming gradually over past months; broad market range INR 450-550 per kg
items.quote: So, we are seeing a gradual hardening of camphor pricing across the past few months. The raw material prices stay at the elevated level. However, we also will probably have to factor in the impact of FOREX. Hence, to answer your question, we are seeing firming of pricing over the last few months.

items.statement: Stable raw material prices provide cost visibility; disciplined sourcing manages forex pressures
items.quote: Stable raw material prices provide cost visibility, while disciplined sourcing allows us to manage Forex-driven pressures effectively.

items.statement: 60-65% of camphor production internally consumed for formulated camphor, pharma and fragrance divisions
items.quote: Girish, correct me if I'm wrong, but we are at around between 60% to 65% internally consumed.

items.statement: Fragrance division locking in briefs from national and regional brands ahead of festive season; safeguarding large accounts
items.quote: In the fragrance division, our teams are locking in briefs from national and regional brands ahead of key festive season market windows. We are delivering winning fragrances optimized for the theme of premiumization and performance by combining strong creative execution with exceptional service reliability. We will safeguard our large accounts and deepen client trust during this high-demand period

items.statement: 50% tariff on certain Indian exports creates near-term uncertainty for overseas fragrance and aroma chemical shipments
items.quote: Recent developments regarding a 50% tariff on certain categories of Indian exports could create near-term uncertainty in select overseas fragrance and aroma chemical shipments.

items.statement: Evaluating alternate market channels, supply chain adjustments and customer negotiations to mitigate tariff impact
items.quote: We have already begun evaluating alternate market channels, making supply chain adjustments and engaging in customer site negotiations to mitigate any potential impact.

items.statement: US exposure not substantial; wait-and-watch approach on tariff impact with ability to redirect materials to other markets
items.quote: So, I wouldn't get into numbers, but it's something which is not very substantial to really have a large impact on an immediate basis.

items.statement: Trading business revenue details to be shared separately; inventory INR 16 crore against INR 25 crore spent
items.quote: Regarding the trading revenue, I will give you separately.

items.statement: Peak debt lower than earlier INR 360 crore estimate due to Baroda facility optimization and deferred Mahad multi-purpose plant
items.quote: So primarily, your second observation is correct. I mean, when we realized the challenges in terms of output pricing, we went into a massive optimization mode at our Baroda facility and hence, we could actually shave off certain CAPEX, which was scheduled to be done, but we found optimized ways of doing it in our current facility and current site in a very safe and sustainable.

items.statement: Production volume up 10% YoY despite planned Bareilly maintenance shutdown
items.quote: In Q1 FY 2025-26, we achieved a 10% year-on-year increase in production volume even as we undertook a planned maintenance shutdown at our Bareilly site to safeguard long-term asset health.

items.statement: Group sales volume rose 4% YoY driven by hydrogenation plant output, market acceptance and initial Mahad sales
items.quote: Group sales volume rose 4% year-on-year, driven primarily by the enhanced output of our hydrogenation plant, improved market acceptance and the initial sales contribution from our Mahad facility.

items.statement: Mahad facility EBITDA loss INR 38 lakh in Q1; ramp-up timeline uncertain due to customer approval cycles
items.quote: It was around INR 38 lakhs in the current quarter. We expect more to come in the next 38 lakhs in the current quarter.

items.statement: No intention to pursue CDMO/CMO tie-ups with MNCs; prefer freedom to operate in generic space
items.quote: And we are a company that believes a lot in freedom to operate, especially because we are in the generic space. So, it is going to stay that way.

items.statement: Target net debt-to-EBITDA below 0.5x by end of FY26
items.quote: We are targeting to end FY '26 with a net debt-to-EBITDA of less than 0.5x on the back of significant debt reduction through the year.

items.statement: No revenue or EBITDA guidance given for FY26 or FY27 due to price volatility
items.quote: So first of all is that so far as our top line is concerned, we had all throughout refrain from giving any guidance.

items.statement: C-PVC expansion of 20,000 tons commissioned ahead of schedule, balance 10,000 tons progressing as planned
items.quote: Our C-PVC expansion of 20,000 tons was commissioned ahead of schedule and has begun contributing from July-August onwards. The balance 10,000 tons expansion is progressing as planned and will further strengthen our position in this segment.

items.statement: 44.5 MW solar project commissioned in Q1, generation ramping up in phases
items.quote: We also commissioned our 44.5 megawatt solar project during this quarter, as mentioned earlier, with generation ramping up in phases.

items.statement: Annual capex run-rate around INR150 crores; new proposals under evaluation but going slow due to geopolitical uncertainties
items.quote: If you followed us the last 2 years, we have been doing around INR150-odd crores of capex every year we have been announcing.

items.statement: C-PVC capacity to reach 50,000 tons by end of FY26
items.quote: By end of the year or end of the financial year, we are hopeful of completing our capex on C-PVC, where we will be at 50,000 tons capacity.

items.statement: Solar project to meet ~25% of Tamil Nadu units' power requirements when fully operational
items.quote: Once fully operational, this will meet about 25% of our Tamil Nadu units power requirements from renewable sources.

items.statement: EBITDA margin (excl. other income) at 11.3% in Q1 FY26 vs 9% in Q1 FY25 and 10.4% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA margin, excluding other income, stood at 11.3% versus 9% in quarter 1 of last fiscal and 10.4% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Basic Chemicals EBITDA rose to INR11 crores from INR1 crore YoY due to higher caustic soda prices and lower energy costs from solar
items.quote: During the comparative period, the Basic Chemicals EBITDA increased to INR11 crores from just INR1 crore due to the increase in caustic soda prices and lower energy costs on account of solar power substitution.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals EBITDA stable with negative bias due to fall in C-PVC realizations
items.quote: On the Specialty Chemicals, the EBITDA remained more or less stable with a negative bias due to fall in C-PVC realizations.

items.statement: Solar power substitution saved ~INR4.5-5 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: I think roughly what benefits we would have got by now would be around INR4.5-5 crores for this quarter.

items.statement: ECU realization at INR33,000/ton; chlorine/HCl negative not significant due to captive consumption
items.quote: Our ECU is INR33,000 per ton. And chlorine, frankly, since we are the captive consumers of chlorine and HCL, so the negative on chlorine and HCL is not much in our case.

items.statement: Caustic soda realizations mildly softer but market stable; no significant correction expected
items.quote: There has been a mild, I would say, softness on the realizations. But having said that, I think market is more or less stable.

items.statement: Demand robust across products; PVC/C-PVC oversupply causing cautious buying and price correction
items.quote: PVC, C-PVC, there is no death of demand. Only thing is that there is an oversupply of PVC, which has resulted in some sort of, I would say, cautioned buying by the customers.

items.statement: C-PVC demand expected to pick up post-monsoon; India demand ~250,000 tons currently
items.quote: As of now, the C-PVC demand is, I would say, in the upwards of 250,000 tons.

items.statement: Synthetic Rutile sales lower in Q1 due to order book skew; will pick up from Q2 based on firm export contracts
items.quote: While the SR sales will pick up from quarter 2 based on firm delivery schedule from awarded export contracts.

items.statement: Finance cost at INR15 crores, lowest in 32 quarters; expected to decline further on scheduled term loan repayments
items.quote: The finance cost stood at INR15 crores, which was down by 10.6% from INR16.9 crores in last year quarter 1. On a sequential basis as well, it was down by approximately 5%. This was the lowest, as mentioned, lowest in the span of last 32 quarters, and it is expected to go down on scheduled repayments of our term loan.

items.statement: Significant debt reduction through year; on track for balance sheet targets by end of FY26
items.quote: We remain committed to our growth with deleverage strategy and are on track to reach our balance sheet targets by the end of this fiscal.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on PVC from China expected final findings in a month, notification by Sep-Oct; ADD on C-PVC already in place on China and Korea
items.quote: ADD on PVC, we have the disclosure statement. Maybe in a month's time, we expect the final findings. Post that, between 2 to 3 months, we will have the notification by the finance ministry. So maybe September, October is the earliest we can expect this ADD to take place into PVC.

items.statement: U.S. tariffs on Chinese and select Indian chemical intermediates disrupting trade flows; no impact on DCW as U.S. exports only SIOP unaffected
items.quote: The U.S. reimposed tariffs on a broad range of Chinese origin chemical products and also now on select Indian origin intermediates. These developments disrupted traditional trade flows, introduced pricing uncertainty and prompted global buyers to recalibrate their sourcing strategies.

items.statement: New C-PVC capacities coming from Lubrizol (100,000 tons phased) and Reliance (~60,000-70,000 tons first phase); may cause temporary oversupply
items.quote: Lubrizol capacity is 1 lakh tons, but not in one phase. It is going to come in multiple phase. About Reliance also, we hear that we are going to come only in a phased manner.

items.statement: EBITDA mix shifting toward Specialty Chemicals; PAT up 70% YoY despite lower revenue
items.quote: Our EBITDA mix continues to shift in favor of Specialty Chemicals, which now contribute a significant share of our earnings. This reinforces the success of our portfolio strategy and strength of our high-margin, high-value products.

items.statement: Dealer stocking levels for PVC significantly lower due to uncertainty on antidumping duties and Chinese dumping
items.quote: So the stocking levels have come to significantly lower levels of the PVC products at the dealer levels, which has an impact on the overall demand.

items.statement: PVC to C-PVC conversion coefficient 0.8; at full scale ~27,000-30,000 tons PVC internally consumed
items.quote: If you see the coefficients, it's 0.8 of PVC going into C-PVC. So eventually, it will be to the tune of a tonnage of around 27,000 to 30,000 tons at full scale at the end.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties (U.S. tariffs, Ukraine war, China policy) creating price and demand volatility; capex decisions deferred
items.quote: We need to understand that while from a country side, we have a tariff with U.S., which also has a Ukraine war angle for the additional tariff. The government may or may not be going along with U.S. or with U.S. Russia or excluding U.S. with the BRICS country, all has a repercussion.

items.statement: PVC/VCM spread reduction impacted PVC EBITDA; integrated PVC-C-PVC model saves ancillary costs and eliminates inventory timing lag
items.quote: This was partly offset by EBITDA drop in PVC due to reduction in PVC/VCM spread.

items.statement: SIOP utilization dipped due to production of lighter shades requiring more cycle time
items.quote: We have been producing certain kind of lighter shades, which require more cycle time. And hence, the volumes, what you see would have dipped in terms of production.

items.statement: Margin guidance maintained at 24%-25% for FY26
items.quote: Thus, our quarter 1 performance gives us good confidence, to maintain our margin guidance of 24% to 25% for FY'26 as we continue to invest in our distribution channels.

items.statement: NBM expanded from 17.5% to 20.1% in Q1FY26
items.quote: NBM expanded from 17.5% in Q1FY25 to 20.1% quartering Q1FY26.

items.statement: ULIP share reduced from 43% to 36% in Q1FY26
items.quote: This launch has helped us rebalance our product mix, reducing the share of ULIPs from 43% in quarter 1 last year to 36% this quarter.

items.statement: Individual adjusted FYP grew 23% in Q1FY26 vs private sector 8%
items.quote: In Q1FY26, our individual adjusted first -year premium grew by 23%, which is nearly 3x of the private sector growth of 8% and more than 4x of the overall industry growth of 5%.

items.statement: VNB grew 32% to INR335 crore in Q1FY26
items.quote: VNB, which is a measure of profitability for our industry, stands at INR335 crore for the first quarter of FY'26, a growth of 32%.

items.statement: Launched Axis Max Life app with AI-powered chatbots and wellness features
items.quote: We recently launched the Axis Max Life app, a fully in -house developed digital platform that integrates life insurance servicing with wellness benefits, an industry first in the life insurance space.

items.statement: Added 15 new banca partners in Q1FY26
items.quote: Continuing this journey, we have added 15 new partners across retail and group channels during Q1FY26 to further strengthen our distribution network.

items.statement: 13th month persistency at 86%; 25th month persistency at all-time high 75%
items.quote: In terms of premium, 13th month persistency stood at 86% compared to 87% in quarter 1 last year, while 25th month persistency has achieved or reached its all -time high at 75%, reflecting a year -on-year improvement of close to 500 basis points.

items.statement: Individual death claim paid ratio reached 99.7% in FY25
items.quote: We are pleased to share that Axis Max Life achieved its highest-ever individual death claim paid ratio of 99.7% in FY'25, a powerful testament to the deep trust our customers place in us

items.statement: New business strain higher due to non-par product mix in Q1FY26
items.quote: Lastly, your observation on the new business strain is correct. It is product -driven. It is the higher proportion of non -par, and especially in a quarter where we don't necessarily get this equivalent operating leverage advantage because it's a smaller quarter from a sales perspective, the strain has been higher because of this particular product category becoming larger in the mix for the quart

items.statement: Solvency at 199%; will use debt capacity and shareholder capital for growth
items.quote: Our solvency at the end of this quarter stands at 199%. But given this business consumes capital due to the products that we are selling and the growth momentum that we are demonstrating. We do expect, over a medium -long horizon, some capital emergence to happen. Some part of that we will fulfill through the debt capacity that we have at our end.

items.statement: Insurance Bill ready for Parliament; Section 35 allows non-life to merge with life with IRDAI approval
items.quote: The latest update, as far as we know, is that the bill is ready to be presented in parliament. We just need to wait until it goes through. In all likelihood, it will be picked up in the forthcoming parliament session, may not happen this time around. But there is no change as far as the Section 35 provision is concerned. I think it will be allowed for a non-life insurance company might merge or ma

items.statement: Axis Bank wallet share remains 65%-70%
items.quote: It continues to be in that range, bound of 65% to 70% level.

items.statement: Protection repricing done in calibrated manner across segments in Q1FY26
items.quote: On protection repricing, the answer is yes, and protection repricing at various segment cohorts, wherever the opportunity allows you to do it in a calibrated manner, keeping competition and demand in play, we keep doing it. And we have done so even this quarter as well

items.statement: Health segment saw degrowth post Oct 1 regulatory changes
