Tarak Patel: I would say, depends again on geographies, but I would say anywhere between 50 %-70% something like that, maybe a little bit lower also in some cases in China especially

items.statement: FX loss INR 20 crore from Euro appreciation vs USD (unrealised, no cash impact); tax rate 68% due to corporate expenses in no-income entity; India pricing improved in glass lined
items.quote: During the quarter, Euro appreciated by approximately 8% against the US dollar, and this resulted in a notable foreign exchange impact across our financial results. This is due to the fact that we have intra-corporate fund currency borrowings within our international operations and due to this currency movement, we faced an exchange loss of INR 20 crores in the P&L statement.

items.statement: No significant exports from India or Europe to US; US served by local manufacturing and Brazil (GLE exports from Brazil to US not under tariff); Brazil used as low-cost source for US
items.quote: No, so we have no significant exports from either India or Europe into the US. U S, we have a large manufacturing facility which is local and pertaining to the US market. We also have Brazil as a low cost source for the US market. And as we understand today, there is no significant tariff on glass lined equipment that is exported from Brazil to the US

items.statement: Non-glass lined businesses (mixing, filtration, drying) growing well; India non-glass lined near INR 150 crore from INR 25-30 crore five years ago; mixing growing high single digit (double digit ex-China); SEMCO adds metals/minerals/wastewa
items.quote: Just to give you a few examples, we have currently orders on hand which have come from our non-core markets. So even with the slowdown in the chemical market, a lot of the shortfall was made up with orders coming in from things like food and beverage, oil and gas, petrochemical, we are doing work for the battery technology.

items.statement: Large EUR 33.7M (USD 37M) acid recovery order from European defense-related company; India seeing inquiries from large agrochemical players; heavy engineering bidding on large refinery projects
items.quote: During the quarter, we received a very large order from European company in the range of about EUR 33.7 odd million, about USD 37 million, this is more into acid recovery, and kind of spend there and we are seeing that level of investment coming back to industries that are involved in the defense manufacturing, arms and ammunition and so on and so forth.

items.statement: US market leader in glass lined; only two suppliers with local US manufacturing; Brazil as low-cost source; India quality accepted in Europe (100+ vessels sold in Italy, stock-and-sell model in Germany)
items.quote: We are one of the two other suppliers who have local manufacturing in the US so we do have a strong position. The US market is a large market for us and a profitable market as well and being local and having Brazil as a low cost source has worked well for us.

items.statement: US tariffs dynamic; glass lined exports from Brazil to US currently not notified under tariff regime; India exports to US challenged by tariffs; monitoring situation daily
items.quote: Yes, so we basically use Brazil as GLE exports to the US. US also has a small manufacturing for systems a nd some stainless steel and non -glass lined equipment as well, but generally it's mainly glass lined. And as of right now, the glass lined exports from Brazil to US seem to be not notified under this tariff regime

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA 0.7x; target to remain below 1x; SEMCO acquisition adds debt but will use cash on balance sheet
items.quote: I said on the debt we currently, we have a net debt to EBITDA ratio of 0.7. And in our last latest guidance we said that we would like to be below 1, and we will remain below 1, although of course, we add now with another acquisition, it adds some debt.

items.statement: Aseem exited after 4 years; India CEO role under consideration as part of global transformation program; restructuring to align regions globally
items.quote: Yes, so first thing to say is that, obviously Aseem has been with us now for four years. We have enjoyed working with him and we thank him for all the good work that he has done. Obviously, it's a professional the decision to move on.

items.statement: Global uncertainty may delay large project decisions; China market quiet for glass lined and mixing; international demand recovery timing uncertain; tariff situation dynamic
items.quote: Having said that, we must keep in mind that there is obviously global uncertainty. Some of these decisions of large projects may be put on hold considering what's going on in terms of global tariffs

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 15-16% sustainable with upside from better absorption; expect India growth this year; international outlook cautious but pipeline growing; mixing targeting double-digit growth ex-China
items.quote: So, as per our the current estimate, 15%-16% is sustainable. I do believe that when you have incremental revenue flowing through these factories, when we have better absorptions, maybe those numbers might look a little bit better.

items.statement: Heavy engineering order inflow expected to improve over next quarters; refinery oil & gas business in India expected to grow 6% over 5-6 years; SEMCO margin profile ~15%
items.quote: So in India, the refinery oil and gas business is expected to grow over next five to six years around 6%. So that will reflect in order inflow and there are few active inquiries for the refinery projects which are stated to come up.

items.statement: Full-year CapEx planned at Rs. 100 crores for maturation project and operational upgradation
items.quote: For the full year, we have planned a CapEx of about Rs. 100 crores, primarily to support the maturation project and continued with operational upgradation across our facilities.

items.statement: Malt plant commissioned, maturation facility groundwork laid, UP plant land purchased and licensing underway
items.quote: The commissioning of a new malt plant, which will soon be fully operational, marks an important step towards backward integration, helping us ensure quality, manage costs and support innovation, all of which are key to scaling premium whiskeys in the years ahead.

items.statement: Malt plant to be fully operational within a month; maturation revenue to start in 1.5 years
items.quote: See, the malt maturity plant has almost been commissioned. Right now we are running a few trials on the malt maturity. And within a month's time, it will be up and running. The first initial revenue would start coming out from one and a half years from today because we will have to mature the liquid for at least for one, one and a half years.

items.statement: Proprietary IMFL volume grew 31% YoY to 5.67 lakh cases; Licensed IMFL 3.87 lakh cases; Merchant ENA 5 million liters; Ethanol 8 million liters
items.quote: Proprietary IMFL 5.67 lakh cases, up 31% year -on-year. L icensed IMFL 3.87 lakh cases, Merchant ENA, 5 million liters; ethanol 8 million liters.

items.statement: Gross margin 40%, EBITDA margin 14%, PAT margin 9%; OPEX as % of sales declined 50 bps due to efficiencies and full plant utilisation
items.quote: Gross margin was 40%, showing a healthy improvement. EBITDA stood at Rs. 37 crores, up by 32% year -on-year with the EBITDA margin at 14%. PAT at Rs. 24 crores with a PAT margin of 9%.

items.statement: Rice and maize prices stabilized at Rs. 22,000-23,000/ton vs Rs. 24,000 avg last year; glass packaging costs also down
items.quote: Price of key raw material like rice and maize, which remained high last year, have now stabilized. Packaging costs, especially glass have also come down. We anticipate that the key raw material price will hold steady, barring any unforeseen volatility.

items.statement: Premium IMFL growing faster than broader market; RTD market at $72M growing 20%+ CAGR; proprietary IMFL revenue up 21% YoY
items.quote: Premium categories are now growing faster than the broader IMFL market, and that opens significant headroom for value creation. We are aligned to this shift.

items.statement: Launched Central Province Vodka, refreshed Titanium Vodka; RTD brand Culture launching in MP then metros; brandy by Diwali; tequila/agave spirit in 2-3 months
items.quote: More recently, we introduced Central Province vodka, which is off to a promising start. We have also refreshed Titanium vodka with a new model packaging, keeping it in step with evolving consumer tastes and reinforcing its presence in the prestige segment.

items.statement: Entered Maharashtra (10% of IMFL demand) and UP; Goa tie-up plant operational, Pondicherry supply starting next week, Goa supply by early next month
items.quote: Our entry into Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh marks a significant step forward, positioning us in two of the country's most prominent IMFL markets. Maharashtra alone accounts for over 10% of India's IMFL demand, making it a critical part of our long -term growth story.

items.statement: UK-India FTA may increase competition from imported scotch; preparing via backward integration and quality focus
items.quote: The UK India Free Trade Agreement could also influence the India alcobev industry, while it supports the premiumization strategy. We are mindful that it could lead to increased competition. We are monitoring the situation closely and will approach any such development with measured caution.

items.statement: Maharashtra MML policy changes being evaluated; tequila launch delayed by Mexican regulatory approvals, now launching as agave spirit
items.quote: The recent changes in the state excise policy are something we are watching closely. It's still early to fully assess the impact, but we are evaluat ing pricing adjustment across channels to limit any disruption and maintain growth momentum.

items.statement: Working capital well managed due to favorable payment cycles in MP and Kerala; may change as UP scales
items.quote: See, primarily, the working capital is being well managed because of the efficiency of the main money which is coming in from the state of Madhya Pradesh, okay, from the government. It will completely depend on the states and states you enter and what the payment cycle is there on those states.

items.statement: UP plant funding mostly through internal accruals; some preferential shares raised for UP plant
items.quote: Second is the funding, funding would be mostly through internal accruals. And I think we have raised some preferential shares in regards to the UP plant.

items.statement: Hillfort & Nicobar Gin Q1 volume ~2,000-2,500 cases; full-year target 15,000-20,000 cases; CP Vodka captured 5-6% market share in MP in first month
items.quote: So, Q1 FY '26, we have just done around 2,000, 2,500 cases, which will increase substantially. So, we have targeted around 15,000 to 20,000 cases this year.

items.statement: Hired senior ex-Diageo executive to lead Maharashtra sales; building own sales teams in new states; marketing spend to rise from 1% to ~5% of revenue
items.quote: So, in Maharashtra also we have taken one of the senior persons on board from Diageo , so he's joined us. And he is driving the entire sales team, and he's taking distributors on board, he's taking state heads on board.

items.statement: Maharashtra policy uncertainty; potential excise hikes in other states; FTA-driven import competition; grain price volatility
items.quote: See, we cannot say anything per se in terms of excise duty because we are dealing with so many governments altogether. So, what government, what step, at what time takes the steps, we cannot say.

items.statement: Inbrew contract changed from franchise to contract manufacturing; slight top-line impact but compensated by own brand growth; job-work revenue continues
items.quote: So, that will come effective from next month onwards, okay? There will be a slight impact on the top line because the revenue would go in their books. But we are trying and compensating from the increase in sale of our product portfolio, and that should be the focus going forward.

items.statement: Full-year consolidated sales growth guidance revised to 5.5%-6.5% from 6%-7%
items.quote: So overall, last time we said 6% to 7%, we are now looking at 5.5% to 6.5%.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics sales growth guidance maintained at 16%-18%
items.quote: Ceramics sales, we communicated a sales growth of 16% to 18% last time at the full year level at consolidated and we hold our guidance for the consolidated Ceramics segment.

items.statement: Consolidated Electrominerals sales growth guidance retained at 1%-2%
items.quote: EMD sales, we gave a guidance of 1% to 2% growth in Electromineral Division in last call, we retain the same guidance.

items.statement: Consolidated Abrasives sales growth guidance lowered to 4%-5% from 5%-6%
items.quote: Abrasives sales in our last call, we communicated 5% to 6% for the year. This could be about 4% to 5%, considering the lower sales in RHODIUS in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics PBIT margin guidance maintained at 23.5%-23.7%
items.quote: Consolidated margin in the Ceramics section last call, we communicated PBIT margin of 23.5% to 23.7% on a full year basis, we maintain the same.

items.statement: Consolidated Electrominerals PBIT margin guidance lowered to 4.5%-5.5% from 6.5%-7.5%
items.quote: EMD in the last call, we said 6.5% to 7.5% on a full year basis, we currently look at 4.5% to 5.5%.

items.statement: Consolidated Abrasives PBIT margin guidance lowered to 6%-6.5% from 8%-8.5%
items.quote: Abrasives, last time we said the PBIT margin could be 8% to 8.5% on a full year basis. Currently, we are looking at 6% to 6.5%.

items.statement: Overall consolidated PBIT margin drop guidance widened to 250-300 bps from 100-150 bps vs FY25 base of 11.2%
items.quote: We said that last time, the overall consolidated PBIT margin could be a drop of 100 to 150 basis points compared to FY ' 25 base of 11.2%. Now we are looking at 250 to 300 basis point drop compared to that level.

items.statement: Capex plan for FY26 maintained at INR350 crores
items.quote: I think if I remember, it is about INR350 crores was the capex program that we guided last call that we will spend for this year. So that we are sticking to the same one and all the programs are in line with that.

items.statement: Domestic Abrasives retail segment facing inventory correction at major distributors
items.quote: The challenge that currently we are facing is on the Retail side. And as I was telling that there is a reasonable growth in the rest of the segment, which is what is making us confident about it. This is quite a few major distributors have to focus on the stock clearance and that is what caused this decline in sales.

items.statement: Consolidated PBIT margin at 6.7% vs 12.6% in Q1 FY25 and 8% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The PBIT margin for the consolidated was at 6.7% for the quarter compared to 8% in Q4 of FY '25 and 12.6% in Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Standalone PBIT margin at 23.8% including one-off SEDCO dividend of INR68 crores
items.quote: For the quarter, standalone PBIT margin was at 23.8% compared to 11.8% in Q4 of FY '25 and 18% in Q1 FY '25. This also includes the one-off dividend income from SEDCO.

items.statement: Consolidated Abrasives margin fell to 2.2% from 10% in Q1 FY25 due to Rhodius and standalone volume drop
items.quote: Abrasives for the quarter, consolidated Abrasives margin declined from 10% in Q1 of FY '25 to 2.2% in Q1 FY '26 due to a drop in volumes at Rhodius and the standalone business.

items.statement: Consolidated Electrominerals margin fell to 1.1% from 11.4% in Q1 FY25 due to VAW volumes and lower realisation
items.quote: Electrominerals. For the quarter, consolidated Electrominerals margin declined from 11.4% in Q1 of FY '25 to 1.1% in Q1 of FY '26. The decline was mainly attributable to the lower volumes in VAW coupled with lower realisation

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics margin improved to 25% from 24% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Now Ceramics. For the quarter, consolidated Ceramics margins improved from 24% in Q1 of FY '25 to 25% in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Standalone Electrominerals margin dropped to 3.3% from 8.5% in Q1 FY25 due to higher alumina input costs
items.quote: Standalone margins dropped from 8.5% to 3.3%. This is mainly due to higher input costs.

items.statement: VAW sales RUB1.84B (down 25% YoY), flat QoQ; PAT RUB72M vs RUB287M in Q1 FY25
items.quote: VAW sales for Q1 FY '26 was RUB1.84 billion which is a 25% dec line from RUB2.46 billion in Q1 FY '25. Sales for Q1 FY '26 was RUB1.84 billion, which is flat compared to RUB1.83 billion in Q4 FY '25. In Q1 FY '26 in r ouble terms, the profit after tax was RUB72 million as compared to RUB287 million in Q1 FY '25 and RUB110 million in Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Rhodius logistics partner change caused operational disruption; expects stability by end of August
items.quote: Rhodius has shifted its logistics partner in Q1 FY '26 for better efficiency. This resulted in a significant disruption of operation. This resulted in non-fulfilment of orders on hand, resulting in lower sales. We expect the stability of operation to come by end of August, we expect this would impact the full year sales as well.

items.statement: HP SiC pilot plant on track; samples seeded with clients for testing; no major sales expected this year
items.quote: We are very much on target as far as the HP SIC pilot plant is concerned. As I told in the previous question also, our samples that we are working with various clients have been seeded. They're in the process of testing, very much on target. And I just want to repeat the same thing I told in the earlier answer. We do not expect any huge sa les arising from HP SIC business in this year or in the ne

items.statement: DRONCO asset purchase program on track; equipment assembled; capacity ~INR80-100M wheels
items.value: INR80 million to INR100 million worth of wheels
items.quote: So it is not an acquisition. It is an asset purchase, where we had it is roughly about INR80 million to INR100 million worth of wheels we will be able to manufacture. That is our capacity.

items.statement: Alumina price doubled to ~$800 then fell to $350/ton in 3-4 months; high-cost inventory liquidated in Q1
items.quote: The alumina price, literally went up in the 6 months, it doubled. It went up as high as about $800. And then it fell down to $350 per ton and the fall is in the matter of 3 to 4 months. So the inventory that we held because we bought this at a higher price had to be liquidated, and that is what is causing us this problem that we have in Q1.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR172 crores (up from INR120 crores Q4 FY25); debt-to-equity 0.05; standalone debt zero
items.quote: There was no debt in our standalone books and total debt at the consolidated basis was at INR172 crores at the end of Q1 FY '26 compared to INR120 crores at the end of Q4 FY '25 and INR112 crores at the end of Q1 FY '25. The debt -to-equity ratio was at 0.05 at the consolidated level.

items.statement: Consolidated free cash flow 98% of PAT; standalone free cash flow 104% of PAT
items.quote: Free cash flows in Q1 of FY '26 at a consolidated level, 98% to PAT compared to 37% in Q1 of FY '25. At a standalone basis in Q1 FY '26, free cash flow to PAT was 104% compared to 47% in Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: US exposure ~8-10% of consolidated sales; tariff impact uncertain but company in decent position
items.quote: On console sales, roughly about 8 to 10 percentage of our sales is U.S.-based.

items.statement: VAW volumes constrained to Russia sales; future depends on Russia-Ukraine settlement
items.quote: We are constrained to selling only inside Russia. We are continuing to do that. They are profitable within that set of the business. But the future depends on how the settlement as far as Ru ssia, Ukraine is concerned will turn out. And based on that, developments will happen. I don't want to hazard a guess given that multiple forces are at play.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR 1,600 crore for FY26 without smart meters, plus INR 300-400 crore from smart meters
items.quote: we are confident of achieving INR 1,600 crore of revenue in this financial year without the smart meters

items.statement: Smart meter revenue guidance revised to around INR 400 crore for FY26
items.quote: we are working to see how we can get to that level of around INR 400 crore is what we guided last quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 10% in Q1 FY26 expected to continue, targeting 50 bps improvement
items.quote: Yes. I think we expect definitely this margin percentage will continue. And we also hope that we would like to increase this by at least another half a percentage point in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Smart meter business targets 12-13% EBITDA margin at scale
items.quote: We are looking at around 12-13% EBITDA margin in this business.

items.statement: Smart meter order book currently INR 50 crore, expecting another INR 50 crore order this quarter
items.quote: we are expecting the next set of INR 50 crore order from a same customer anytime this quarter.

items.statement: New automotive temperature sensor under validation with two tier-2 OEMs; commercial supplies expected from Q4 FY26
items.quote: We anticipate commencing commercial supplies from Q4 of this financial year, which will open up an additional and promising revenue stream for Sal zer further strengthening our position, not just in the automotive solutions space, but also in the HVAC, home appliance and medical equipment space

items.statement: Smart meter capacity sufficient; all major capex done, only small investments for line efficiency; building in-house electronic manufacturing facility
items.quote: Present capacity is enough and all the CapEx has been done and then we are continuing to invest to, I wouldn't say maintenance CapEx, but to make the line lean, whatever is required, that small Cap ex that we are doing. And we are also establishing an in-house electronic manufacturing facility for the smart meters.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia operations to start from Q3 FY26 on rental basis; capex to begin after location finalized
items.quote: We haven't started any CapEx. As I mentioned earlier in this call, we are close to finding a place to operate on a rental basis. Once that is done, I think the CapEx will start, and we expect that it will happen from Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Smart meter business expected to reduce working capital cycle at full revenue levels
items.quote: Smart meter business won't increase our working capital cycle. If at the full revenue levels, I think smart meter will actually help reduce our working capital cycle. That's what we expect.

items.statement: Smart meter customer reaffirmed commitment to clear INR 50 crore order in Q2 FY26
items.quote: the customer has reaffirmed their commitment to clear the entire order in Q2 of this financial year.

items.statement: Indian electrical market valued at $14 billion, expected to reach $20 billion by 2031 (6% CAGR)
items.quote: Indian electrical market is on a steady growth trajectory as we have told in the last quarter. The market is valued at approximately $14 billion currently and is expected to reach close to $20 billion by 2031, implying a healthy CAGR of close to 6%.

items.statement: India EV charging market to grow from $92 million (2024) to $750 million by 2030 (43% CAGR)
items.quote: India alone is set to grow from $92 million in 2024 to $750 million by 2030, nearly 43% CAGR in the next 6-7 years.

items.statement: Global temperature sensor market size ~$7 billion across automotive, consumer electronics, HVAC, healthcare
items.quote: I think it is close to around $7 billion, the global market size for this temperature sensor. And the sectors that the product can be used is automotive, cons umer electronics, HVAC and healthcare

items.statement: US tariff confusion causing shipment delays and hold requests; near-term revenue impact uncertain
items.quote: Right now, I think we are seeing a knee jerk reaction by all the customers because a 50% tariff is way too high for anybody to absorb in the market. So right now, I think some customers are taking action of taking the shipments quickly before the tariff kicks in. Some customers are postponing their shipments asking us to hold.

items.statement: Promoter stake increased from 33% to 37% over last 2-3 years; no immediate plans for further increase
items.quote: I think, the last 2-3 years, promoters have increased the stake. And I, being one of the part of the promoter, we have gone up from 33% to 37%. And we have no plans immediately but we will definitely let you know as and when we have any idea of doing that.

items.statement: Targets 10-12% consolidated revenue growth and improved bottom line for FY26
items.quote: We are targeting 10 % to 12% growth in revenue and improved bottom line on a consolidated basis over the coming years.

items.statement: Expects Q2 order inflow of INR350 crores plus and FY26 order inflow of almost INR1,000 crores plus
items.quote: For the upcoming quarter, we envisage the order inflow to the tune of INR350 crores plus and are hopeful of achieving an order inflow of almost INR1,000 crores plus for the entire fiscal year.

items.statement: Outstanding order book stood at approximately INR465 crores as of June 25
items.quote: Our outstanding order book as of June 25 stood at approximately INR465 crores.

items.statement: Q1 order inflow was approximately INR270 crores
items.quote: we achieved an order inflow of approximately INR270 crores.

items.statement: INR25 crores capex for foundry and machine shop upgradation fully completed and commissioned end of Q1
items.quote: the capital expenditure of INR25 crores towards the upgradation and expansion of our foundry and the machine shop has been now fully completed with all equipment successfully commissioned in the end of Q1.

items.statement: Plans to install solar system at Surat facility this year for power self-sufficiency
items.quote: one major plan for the current year is to install a solar system for our manufacturing facilities at Surat.

items.statement: Machine Tool division capacity tripled; targets doubling monthly production from 30 to 60-70 machines in 1-2 years
items.quote: we have upgraded our foundry to the latest part of the technology, which will give us a capacity of three times that what we are currently producing. And we are looking at doubling our numbers in the next one year's time.

items.statement: Textile Machinery Q1 order inflow INR167 crores; expects Q2 inflow around INR200 crores
items.quote: the inflow orders in Q1 was approximately INR167 crores and the further order of inflow in Q2 is to be around INR200 crores.

items.statement: Environmental Engineering Q1 order inflow INR34 crores; expects Q2 inflow almost INR50 crores and revenue INR40 crores
items.quote: Going forward in Q2, we anticipate an order inflow of almost INR50 crores an d a revenue of approximately INR40

items.statement: Expects 10-12% EBITDA margin range for FY26 as capex and merger benefits flow through
items.quote: We look at a range of 10%-12% in the fiscal '26.

items.statement: Doubling Machine Tool production will drop most gross margin to bottom line with minimal variable cost increase
items.quote: Now, there'll be no further addition to any variable cost on that, on doubling the production other than the consequent increase in raw materials. So, basically, we would see most of the gross margin that we earn going into the bottom line.

items.statement: Solar plus wind to make power cost negligible from current INR1.5 crores/year, saving INR1.2-1.5 crores annually
items.quote: we'll be having a saving over anywhere between INR1.2 crores to INR1.5 crores at the end of the year.

items.statement: Currently net zero interest-bearing debt; cash credit INR11 crores, term loan INR1.5-1.7 crores, promoter loan INR40 crores to be repaid from land sale
items.quote: currently we are at the moment more or less at zero debt, zero interest bearing level.

items.statement: Promoters ready to dilute beyond 72% stake to fund acquisitions with minimal borrowing
items.quote: the promoters are even ready to dilute further, to raise the necessary funds. Because whatever we look at acquisition, we would rather look at it on the basis of acquisition based on very minimally borrowed funds.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions in capital goods space; evaluates opportunities continuously; avoids turnaround situations
items.quote: we are continuously being approached with possible acquisitions and we evaluate those. So, as we go forward, we will look at it even closer.

items.statement: BEL merger approved by NCLT end of March 2025; enables non-fund-based limits using Batliboi land bank as security
items.quote: Batliboi Environmental Engineering Limited merged into Batliboi Limited following the NCLT approval at the end of March 2025

items.statement: International sales contribute approximately 26% of revenue; products present in over 20 countries
items.quote: Our products are currently present in over 20 countries, with international sales contributing approximately 26% of our revenue.

items.statement: Auto sector exposure only 10-15%; strong in diamond, agriculture, job shops, defense, die-and-mold
items.quote: Our auto sector exposure will be not more than 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Machine Tool industry CAGR expected at 12-14% if GDP grows 6-7%
items.quote: if the GDP of the country goes by 6% to 7% , the machine -to-industry CGR would be in the range of 12% to 14%.

items.statement: QuickMill benefits from zero tariffs under USMCA; order booking and inquiry generation improved significantly
items.quote: Currently, QuickMill machines benefit from no tariffs under the US-Mexico-Canada arrangement called USMCA, which provides a positive outlook going forward.

items.statement: Controllers from FANUC or Mitsubishi; ball screws and linear guideways imported from Taiwan
items.quote: it's either Mitsubishi or FANUC for the controllers. Rest of them are bought -outs, small bought -outs for the lubricant oil systems. Ball screws and linear guideways are imported from Taiwan

items.statement: Environmental Engineering pending orders rose to INR115 crores end of Q1 from INR99 crores at start
items.quote: order bookings remain strong with pending orders rising to INR115 crores at the end of the first quarter up from rupees INR99 crores at the beginning of the quarter.

items.statement: Q1 results impacted by post-merger compliances and subdued textile demand; expects compensation over next three quarters
items.quote: The first quarter results were impacted due to the post -merger compliances of Batliboi Environmental Engineering Limited, as well as subdued demand in sectors such as textiles. Despite this, we are seeing a very strong outlook for the coming quarters

items.statement: Promoters hold more than 72% equity; no management changes mentioned
items.quote: the promoters continue to hold more than 72% equity in the company.

items.statement: Capital goods model: payment received before supply except EPC stage-wise payments; cash flow managed well
items.quote: normally, we will not supply equipment unless we get paid for unless it is like an EPC contract, in which case it payment is a stage wise payment.

items.statement: No sales guidance given for FY26 due to volatility from US tariffs
items.quote: However, I'm happy to discuss possibilities and outcomes.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 trimmed to INR150-200 crores from earlier INR300 crores plan
items.quote: we plan to trim down the capex to between INR150 crores to INR200 crores at best

items.statement: Net term loans expected to stay around INR550 crores with no significant increase
items.quote: We expect to end up this year with no significant increase in borrowings as compared to the previous year. So net term loans will be in the region of around INR550 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 18% ex-other income, 20% including other income; expect to hold with 200bps upward bias
items.quote: EBITDA for this quarter stands at 18% after taking away other income. Including other income, EBITDA is at 20%.

items.statement: Management expects margins to hold at current levels with 200bps upward bias
items.quote: I would say, hold at these levels with a 200 basis point bias -- upward bias.

items.statement: Order book visibility roughly INR100-110 crores per month until October; uncertain beyond
items.quote: Generally, our order books over the next few months look to be at least until October, are roughly in the region of around INR100 crores, INR110 crores a month.

items.statement: Next 6-9 months expected at previous year levels plus/minus small number; improvement after 6-12 months if conditions hold
items.quote: The next 6 to 9 months look to be previous year level, plus/minus a small number.

items.statement: Forging capacity ~120,000 tons; machining capacity ~5.5 lakh parts/month, running at ~3.5-3.75 lakh (60% utilisation)
items.quote: On the forging side, we stand at about 120,000 tons. Machining is a mixed bag. Just -- I'll give you the number, one second hold on. We are doing about 3.5 lakh to 3.75 lakh machine parts a month on a capacity of around 5.5 lakh.

items.statement: 16,000 ton press to be commissioned Q4 FY26 (March-April 2026), production from next year
items.quote: Press is expected to be commissioned in Q1 of next calendar, that is Q4 of this year. Q4 to Q1 -- rather, I would say, between January -- let's say, around March, April.

items.statement: CV share to decline from 80% to 75%; PV to rise from 13% to 18%; domestic/export ~60/40 +/-5%
items.quote: CV would slightly decline to around 75% -- from 80% to 75%. And pass cards, take up the slack from 13%, it would go up to about 18%.

items.statement: Sales per ton fell from INR206,000 to INR192,000 due to product mix change, not tariff impact
items.quote: from INR206, it has come down to INR192. I'll say -- one second, INR 206,000 per ton -- sales per ton is down to INR192,000 per ton. Largely, it's a product mix change.

items.statement: All export contracts are CIF America; customer bears duty, no direct tariff absorption by company
items.quote: Fortunately, for MM Forgings, all contracts are CIF America. There is nothing that is DDU, DDP and all that, where we have to pay the duty is to customer account.

items.statement: US CV order book down from 150-180k to ~90k units; freight demand from ports to distribution centers under question
items.quote: The order book of U.S. CV makers is coming down. Consequently, they will also be more cautious when they order on Tier 1s and then us.

items.statement: Europe truck/off-highway demand growing; company gaining market share there, insulated from US tariffs
items.quote: We are adding market share -- we're increasing market share there.

items.statement: Domestic market will see increased competition as exporters redirect volumes; need to be agile
items.quote: domestic market could and will see increased competition in the months to come.

items.statement: Power costs up due to Tamil Nadu government 5% annual rate hike and lower sales base
items.quote: Power costs have increased on the back of the Tamil Nadu Government increasing the unit rates. They have decided to go ahead and increase power cost by 5% every year.

items.statement: Crankshaft production ramped from 1,500 to ~7,000/month for CV; targeting 10,000; agri at ~16-17k/month
items.quote: It has ramped up quite well from around 1,500 cranks a month for the CV sector. We are now doing close to 7,000 cranks a month.

items.statement: DVS merger could yield significant tax reduction from unabsorbed losses; final numbers pending merger completion
items.quote: Yes, there could be a significant reduction in tax outflow, I would like to qualify at this point and not go wrong with the numbers.

items.statement: Subsidiary (new powertrain) has developed parts for 3-wheeler market; homologation underway; production from Q4 FY26
items.quote: We've gotten the orders. We've got -- parts are being homologated as we speak. And this will all happen -- get into production from Q4 of this fiscal.

items.statement: US tariffs not linear; 12-36 months for local US forging capacity to develop; labor constraints; mixed outcomes
items.quote: It's not linear -- the point I'm trying to make is it's not linear. There is going to be a wide set of repercussions.

items.statement: Peak debt reached unless significant lucrative opportunities arise
items.quote: I would say at this point of time, peak debt, unless the opportunities are significant and extremely lucrative.

items.statement: Inventory super-imposition in heavy truck market causing export sales decline next quarter; expected to dry up by Nov-Dec
items.quote: there is a super imposition of a lot of inventory in the heavy truck market, and that is one reason why sales are expected to be down in the exports in the next quarter. But we also expect over time, the inventories will be dried off.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 total income INR358 crores vs INR375 crores YoY (-6%); EBITDA INR72 crores vs INR78 crores; PAT INR22 crores vs INR32 crores
items.quote: MM Forgings has achieved a total income of INR358 crores as against INR 375 crores in the previous fiscal, a drop of about 4% -- sorry, 6%.

items.statement: Q1 production 17,250 tons, sales 17,780 tons vs previous quarter production 17,332 tons, sales ~20,000 tons
items.quote: 17,250 tons of production, 17,780 tons of sales for this quarter. 17, 332 for the previous quarter and -- production-wise and almost 20,000 tons of sales.

items.statement: US customers single-sourced; competitive advantage holds; Mexico potential threat but 20-30% costlier than India
items.quote: Most customers, they are single source, particularly in the U.S. market. The products that we sell are all single source.

items.statement: AC cabin norms in India (pre-June 10) caused mixed domestic demand; some customers good, some flat
items.quote: Due to the AC cabin norms coming up in India before 10th of June. We've had a mixed bag.

items.statement: Cost reduction efforts across raw material, power, manpower, buying strategies, tool materials; all margin accretive
items.quote: We are working on a wide range of cost reduction efforts, ranging from raw material to power -- manpower, everything and buying strategies, tool materials, the works.

items.statement: Recovery guidance of INR250-300 crores per year for next 3 years to recover entire provision; current NPA ~INR760 crores (ex-home loan ~INR730 crores)
items.quote: So, in terms of the guidance that we had given earlier that we'll have almost INR250 crores to INR300 crores of recovery every year for the next 3 years. And our target is that we want to recover the provision, the entire provision that we have made.

items.statement: Home loan book target INR5,000 crores in 2 years and INR10,000 crores by FY30; IPO planned for 2028 or 2029
items.value: 5,000 crores in 2 years, 10,000 crores by FY30
items.quote: Our plan here remains the same. We plan to grow the loan book to INR5,000 crores in 2 years and to around INR10,000 crores by FY '30. And we will plan an IPO and listing of this business sometime in 2028 or 2029.

items.statement: Corporate Advisory targeting minimum 20% revenue growth in FY26 if markets hold, with strong filed IPO pipeline
items.quote: Yes, in the minimum, if like you said, the first caveat, markets is holding up, we are very confident, like you said, we have a very strong pipeline of already filed IPOs.

items.statement: Filed 45 IPO transactions aggregating INR1 lakh crores; pipeline expected to execute over next 12 months if markets hold
items.quote: We have also had a n INR1 lakh crores worth of filing for IPO transactions . We filed 45 IPO transactions, which aggregate to INR1 lakh crores

items.statement: Wealth management margins lower due to upfront expansion costs; Y-o-Y margin improvement of over 3 percentage points
items.quote: The margins are slightly lower because as you see in the presentation, the expansion plans are being loaded into the P&L. So as Chirag alluded at the earlier part of the call also that a lot of these costs are being upfronted and the revenues, etc, we will see over a period of time.

items.statement: AMC net yield on equity AUM at 25-27 bps, target to cross 30 bps in 6-12 months
items.quote: If I look at our net yield on equity AUM, we are touching around 25 to 27 basis points. So, the target is to cross 30 over the next 6 months to a year.

items.statement: INR2,000 crores cash reserved for investments in wealth management, asset management, and home loans; corporate advisory and private markets fully funded
items.quote: Yes. So, I think in terms of capital requirements, we'll be investing more in wealth management, asset management as well as home loans. And this capital is reserved for investments on that side. On the corporate advisory, capital markets and private markets, we are fully funded.

items.statement: Wealth RMs up 91% Y-o-Y (91 to 174); sales employees up 37% Y-o-Y (563 to 773); most new hires joining during quarter, not yet at full productivity
items.quote: in terms of wealth RMs, the n umber of RMs has increased by 91% on a year -on-year basis from 91 RMs in June 2024 to 174 in June 2025. Our sales employees have increased from 563 in June 2024 to 773 in June 2025, which is an increase of 37

items.statement: Wealth recurring AUM up 37% Y-o-Y to INR31,180 crores; focus on recurring revenue but not ignoring transactional; building own AMC products for cross-sell
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, the wealth management recurring AUM has increased to INR31,180 crores as compared to INR22,000 odd crores in June of 2024. So that is an increase of 37%.

items.statement: Wealth custody assets ~INR20,000 crores at low yield; aim to convert to recurring/transactional revenue; digital 60% of portfolios, 15% of AUM; IFA channel 80% of channel-led sales
items.quote: Yes, the custody includes approximately INR20,000 crores at a low yield. It's not like it doesn't earn us anything, but it does have a low yield.

items.statement: JM Financial led equity capital markets with 10 transactions in Q1 vs peers 3-4; remained #1 in league tables; taking disproportionate market share
items.quote: We've closed 10 Capital Market transactions in the first quar ter. So, it's clearly an effort of JM Financial to take disproportionate market share. Most of the peers may have closed not more than 3 or 4 transactions.

items.statement: Real estate loan book down 56%; ARC cash recoveries INR1,368 crores in 12 months; net impairment reversal INR204 crores; real estate NPA INR620 crores fully provided, net book INR1,400 crores with zero delinquency
items.quote: Our current real estate loan book which I define as the non-core real estate loan book has declined by almost 56%. And in our ARC business in the last 12 months, our share of cash recoveries is almost INR1,368 crores. And so, both the real estate recovery and the recoveries all put together have resulted in a net reversal of impairment of almost INR204 crores.

items.statement: Real estate book bottomed at INR2,000 crores; expect 15-20% Y-o-Y growth on cash flow-backed lending for next 2-3 years; no adventurous loans
items.quote: So, I think real estate has bottomed. You can comfortably assume that real estate should be able to grow at a 15% to 20% loan book growth on cash flow backed comfortably year-on-year for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Borrowings reduced by INR4,300 crores in last year while pre-provisioning operating profit grew 22%
items.quote: We have reduced our borrowing by INR4,300 crores in the last 1 year and still had excellent growth in our pre provisioning operation profit by almost 22%.

items.statement: Increased stake in JM Financial Credit Solutions to 100%; divested 2.1% in home loans to Bajaj Allianz Life for valuation and strategic partnership; may do 1-2 more stake sales before IPO
items.quote: On the home loan business, we divested a small stake of 2.1% to Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance. This helps us value the business and also brings in a good strategic investor, a very long-term, high-quality investor in our business.

items.statement: Corporate Advisory net revenue INR182 crores (+53% Y-o-Y), PBT INR96 crores (+77% Y-o-Y); Wealth & AM net revenue INR225 crores (+29% Y-o-Y), PBT INR44 crores (+54% Y-o-Y)
items.quote: On Corporate Advisory and Capital Markets, the net revenue stood at INR182 crores, which is a 53% increase year-on-year basis. Profit before tax stood at INR96 crores, which is a year -on-year increase of 77%.

items.statement: Private Markets net revenue +62% Q-o-Q; impairment reversal INR212 crores; PBT INR377 crores (4x Q-o-Q); PAT INR278 crores (12x Q-o-Q)
items.quote: There is a reversal of impairment on financial instruments to t he extent of INR212 crores. Profit before tax, including the reversal stood at INR377 crores, which is a 4x growth as compared to the earlier quarter.

items.statement: Affordable Home Loans total income INR100 crores (+8% Y-o-Y), PAT flat at INR14 crores; Treasury PAT INR47 crores (+35% Y-o-Y)
items.quote: Moving on to affordable home loans. The total income increased by 8% to around INR100 crores on a year-on-year basis. Profit after tax was more or less flattish at roughly around INR14 crores.

items.statement: Wealth management in aggressive build-out phase; costs front-loaded, revenues to follow; RMs break even after ~1 year; not overpaying for talent, targeting long-term committed hires
items.quote: On an average, for us, post a decent year of productivity, the RMs start breaking even for themselves any which way. So, we are not in the game of trying to go out and poach people at obnoxious commitments of either payouts or equity in the business or any of that.

items.statement: Ample liquidity may cause mispricing; will stay away from risk-adjusted return dilution; DNA of not chasing growth at expense of balance sheet unchanged
items.quote: And when there is a lot of liquidity, there can be mispricing. And learning from our e xperiences in the past, if there is a lot of mispricing, then we will choose to stay away and that DNA will not change.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio to increase; buyback not tax-efficient currently; focus on decent payout ratio
items.quote: We've always maintained that our pa yout ratio will increase in terms of dividend. But from a taxation perspective, I'm not sure if buyback is as efficient. But I think we will continue to have a pretty decent payout ratio.

items.statement: Syndication efforts started 4-5 quarters ago; tangible mandates in hand; revenue conversion expected in next 3 quarters; mix of fee and interest income to reduce ECM cyclicality
items.quote: What I would say is efforts on the same started 4-5 quarters ago. And I think now we are seeing tangible assignments and mandates in hand, which I think will convert into revenue in the next 3 quarters, and then you will start seeing the revenue flow.

items.statement: ARC Juhu hotel deal: acquired SRs from 3 banks, 50% ownership, partnered with Oberoi Realty; minority investor, Oberoi controls development; bulk realization on SRs after NCLT approval expected Q4 FY26
items.quote: We acquired these SRs from the three banks. We got to a 50% sort of market share of the ownershi p of the hotel that was in distress. And then we chose to partner with Oberoi Realty, which is a very good brand for Bombay real estate in terms of bidding jointly with them to acquire the asset.

items.statement: AMC crossed AUM threshold for bank empanelment 6-8 months ago; small/mid banks (Yes, IDFC, IDBI, RBL) onboarded; large banks in advanced engagement, expected in next 2 quarters
items.quote: We have crossed that threshold. It's just that the process of onboarding in banks takes a bit of time. So, since we crossed that threshold pretty recently in the last 6 to 8 months, I think we are still in the formative phase. And maybe by the end of this year, you'll start seeing banks come along.

items.statement: Brokerage income Q-o-Q up 29%, flat Y-o-Y despite volume decline; fee & commission income up 23% Y-o-Y
items.quote: The brokerage income Q-on-Q is up 29%, and despite the fall in volumes, is almost flat Y-o-Y. And the fee and commission income are up by almost 23% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of around INR 1,900 crores with plus/minus 5% range
items.quote: Yes, we are on track to achieve INR1,900 crores, near INR1,900 crores, about INR1,900 crores. That can be plus or minus 5%.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance of 11-12% with operating income of INR 35 crores
items.quote: Yes. So this is turnover and there is an operating income that can be about INR 35 crores. So overall, you can say that we can cross INR1,950 crores revenue as a top line.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR 2,000-2,100 crores with 12-13% EBITDA margin
items.quote: See, present business model will add about INR300 crore turnover, as mentioned to the current run rate, whatever we are doing about INR 450 crores quarterly. So we can reach to next year INR2,000 crores, INR2,100 crores easily. And over there, 12% to 13% EBITDA, that is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Benzene derivatives revenue target of INR 100 crores for FY26 and INR 300 crores for FY27
items.quote: For the whole current year, I think we should do about INR 100 crores of top line from the benzene business.

items.statement: Benzene derivatives capacity utilization target of 70% by Q3 FY26 and 80% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Currently, it is 30%. For the next quarter, it will be slightly improved. And then by Q3, it should cross 70%. And by Q4, it should be maximum, which is around 80%.

items.statement: Chlor-alkali capacity utilization target of 90-95% in coming couple of quarters
items.quote: We are targeting to improve capacity utilization near to 90% to 95% in coming couple of quarters.

items.statement: Term debt reduction target of INR 150-175 crores by end of FY26 and similar reduction next year
items.quote: So by end of current year, we are targeting at least a reduction of INR150 crores. It can be in the range of INR 150 crores to INR 175 crores reduction in term debt.

items.statement: Target debt-to-EBITDA of 2.5x before considering next growth plan
items.quote: In other words, if I say we are targeting debt-to-EBITDA near 2.5. And then we will consider next growth plan.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next couple of years, only small debottlenecking or brownfield expansions
items.quote: At present, in a couple of years, we are not targeting any c apex. But yes, there are several opportunities which are there available with the company that by doing some capex, we can add to that. We have no major plans for any major

items.statement: Benzene derivatives PNCB/ONCB capacity of 3,000 metric ton per month, currently at 20% utilization, now improved to 30%
items.quote: For PNCB and ONCB whatever we have run, the volume is 1,850 metric ton which is about 20% of the capacity. So PNCB, ONCB has a capacity of 3,000 metric ton per annum per month. And if we consider that, then about 20% utilization is there for PNCB, ONCB products.

items.statement: MCB plant not running currently due to favorable market prices, plan to start soon
items.quote: But because of the lower utilization, we are not running the MCB plant at the moment because we are getting it at a very good price in the market only. The plan is to start that plant also very soon.

items.statement: TCCA demand expected to improve in 1-2 months as pre-duty import inventory clears
items.quote: I think another 1 or 2 months, we should have a sizable share of the Indian market at a good price also.

items.statement: Benzene derivatives demand slower, pharma customer approvals expected by Diwali for volume ramp-up
items.quote: The product is already approved in the major customers. But it takes a long time for the overall approval process to be finished and get a large size orders. So that is expected by Diwali time.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin target of 13-15% in normal market scenario, up from current 10-12%
items.quote: I think in a normal market scenario, I think we can -- our goal is to reach around 14%. So -- but blended, it could be anywhere between 13% to 15%.

items.statement: TCCA and benzene derivatives not yet contributing at margin levels, expected to add 2% to blended margins in 3-6 months
items.quote: We are already in the range of around 10% to 12%. Still there are 2 businesses which are yet to contribute at the margin levels, which are benzene derivatives and TCCA business. So with time the TCCA, the imported quantities will not last for too long, I think another 1 or 2 months only. And then we should get good volumes from the local markets. We are also working on the export business as well.

items.statement: TCCA pricing increased by INR 50-60 to around INR 160 after anti-dumping duty implementation
items.quote: Pricing has definitely increased a lot. It has increased by the duty amount. So the pricing of TCCA in the market is now around INR 160. It has increased by around INR 50, INR60.

items.statement: Sulfur pricing stable at INR 27,000 and sulfuric acid at INR 12,000, same as Q1
items.quote: It is still in the same range. The sulfur is around 27,000 only and the sulfuric is also around INR12,000 only.

items.statement: Chlorine prices negative at INR 1,500-2,000 in North India, better than historical lows
items.quote: Chlorine prices are still negative, but not too much. They are around INR 1,500 to INR 2,000 negative at the moment in the North Indian part.

items.statement: Benzene derivatives revenue of INR 13 crores in Q1 FY26 at 20% utilization of PNCB/ONCB
items.quote: Yes, it has contributed INR13 crores as far as top line is concerned.

items.statement: TCCA revenue of INR 3.2 crores in Q1 FY26 with production of 187 metric tons
items.quote: TCCA has contributed INR 3.2 crores as far as revenue is concerned. And production was INR187 crores only metric ton.

items.statement: Export contribution 22% of revenue, US exposure negligible at 1%
items.quote: See, our export for the last quarter was 22% of the total revenue. And out of that from U.S. was hardly 1% or so. So it's a negligible when we consider at the total level.

items.statement: Textile dependency reduced to 35-40% of sales due to diversification into benzene, TCCA, chlor-alkali
items.quote: Our dependency on textiles is -- has been decreasing with the diversification into other businesses like benzene, like TCCA, like chlor-alkali. Earlier, a major chunk of the sales was dyes and dye intermediates, so they were kind of depending too much on the textiles. But now I would say the textile sales will be not more than 35%, 40%.

items.statement: Asset sales planned for Vatva and Punjab land to repay debt, Rajpura land sale of 8 acres for INR 5 crores in process
items.quote: So we have -- we are selling almost about 8 acres of land to them. And this is not only -- this is not a real estate deal. This is more of a business deal, which is going to benefit both of us. So the prices -- the price of the land is not really too much because it's an invested area. So it's around INR5 crores that we will get for the land.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on TCCA implemented, but meaningful impact delayed due to pre-duty import inventory
items.quote: Till date, we have not got meaningful advantage of introduction of an antidumping duty on TCCA by Indian government. This is because of the huge import quantities of the product done by the importers of India in the anticipation of the duty coming up.

items.statement: Global uncertainties since Ukraine-Russia war affecting margins, structural shift from 18-20% historical margins to 13-15% normal range
items.quote: Last -- since 2022, since the Ukraine-Russia war, there's a lot of disturbances and uncertainties globally. So since the last 3 years, the overall margins are very cyclical, and there are definitely -- there's pressure on the margins. So we are back to around 11%, I think which is very healthy. With the addition of these two projects when we reach the good utilization numbers, I think going back t

items.statement: Management expects muted FY26 with no near-term revival in antibiotics market
items.quote: At this stage, we see no revival in the near future, at least not in the current year.

items.statement: Global oral antibiotics exports fell ~30% in volume and 15-20% in price in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our analysis of exports out of India show that for the quarter, overall quantity of oral antibiotics exports fell by about 30%, while average export prices dropped by about 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Gross margins maintained around 42% despite 29% sales decline
items.quote: Despite this, we have tried to maintain our g ross margins at around 42% and have consciously chosen not to participate in the ongoing price war

items.statement: Orblicef domestic brand performing steadily with consistent demand patterns
items.quote: Our domestic brand, Orblicef continues to perform steadily. The combination of Cipla's extensive hospital coverage and our AMS division's targeted engagement ensures we are building sustained prescriber awareness. Demand patterns remain consistent with our expectations.

items.statement: Acquired global rights to Enmetazobactam and Exblifep trademark from Allecra via insolvency process
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that following our update last quarter on Allecra's insolvency and the resulting uncertainty around Orchid's royalty stream, Orchid has now acquired the global rights to Enmetazobactam and the trademark Exblifep from Allecra.

items.statement: Dhanuka Labs merger expected to complete in next 6 months with hearing in end September
items.quote: I think next 6 months, it should be -- I mean, the results of the EGM have already been accepted by the judge. And now the final formalities will have to be done. We have a hearing in end of September.

items.statement: 7ACA project in Jammu on track for Q1 FY27 commissioning; Cefiderocol project on track for December 2026
items.quote: 7ACA commissioning is Q1 FY '27. Is that correct? Manish Dhanuka: Yes -- There is no change in what we mentioned last time. Yes. Rupesh: Okay. And Cefiderocol is December '26? Manish Dhanuka: Yes, yes.

items.statement: Enmetazobactam royalty from Advanz Pharma in Europe at ~15% (14-18% range) on sales
items.quote: It's around 15%. So depending on the sales, it ranges from 14% to 18%. If the sales go high, the royalties will increase. But I mean, we can assume 15% is on an average.

items.statement: Enmetazobactam patent expiry early 2034 in US and Europe; pediatric study may extend exclusivity
items.quote: U.S., I can confirm its '24 -- early '24 -- '34, sorry. Yes. So other countries, Europe also is similar 2024 because the patents are filed similar time and exclusivity periods are also similar.

items.statement: 7ACA PLI scheme benefits based on oral commitments only, no written approvals
items.quote: There are no written approval. There are only oral commitments that this will be honored.

items.statement: Insolvency acquisition carries limited due diligence risk; Allecra acquisition on 'as is where is' basis
items.quote: As you are aware, insolvency acquisitions are conducted on as is various basis in a court -driven process, there is limited time to perform detailed due diligence.

items.statement: US commercialization of Enmetazobactam targeted within 1 year of acquisition completion
items.quote: The most prudent thing would be to close the deal within a year definitely because the NDA, the registration whole process has been completed.

items.statement: Long-term contracts stable with +/-10% variation; no significant change in Q1
items.quote: So wherever we have long -term commitments, generally, p lus/minus 10% variation is there. They give annual forecast. So I don't see any significant change happening there

items.statement: Penicillin (PenG) prices down significantly; raw material cost decline suggests demand flattening
items.quote: Yes. So the penicillin prices have gone down significantly. So that's why I feel that there is a demand flattening because the raw material prices have also gone down.

items.statement: Market consolidation to 3 players in cephalosporin space expected to support pricing discipline
items.quote: That's right. It leaves the 3 players in the market now.

items.statement: Ceftaroline and Cefovecin API DMF filing certain; FDF timeline not confirmed
items.quote: The API DMF will be filed for sure. For the FDF, I cannot give a time line at this time. Rupesh: For both the products, is that correct? Manish Dhanuka: Yes, both the products.

items.statement: No FY26 guidance for Dhanuka Labs due to uncertain market conditions
items.quote: But considering the market conditions that are prevailing, I think it would be difficult to give a guidance on that at this point of time.

items.statement: German IBC process for Allecra acquisition expected to complete in ~3 months
items.quote: We are expecting about 3 months. Rupesh: So you will have ownership of asset in 3 months? Mridul Dhanuka: Hopefully, yes.

items.statement: Avibactam US generic launch: first-to-file in August 2027; Orchid product 6 months later
items.quote: The first to file launch date would be sometime in August 27, and Orchid product should be available 6 months after that.

items.statement: Enmetazobactam API manufactured in-house for domestic use; FDF facility needed for regulated markets
items.quote: Yes, we are manufacturing for our domestic consumption. Vishal Manchanda: Okay. And you will need to kind of wait for the fixed dosage facility to be commercialized? Manish Dhanuka: That's right. That's right.

items.statement: Royalty claim on Enmetazobactam from Advanz Pharma starts after July 31, 2025
items.quote: We will have claim on royalties after 31st July.

items.statement: Consolidated topline growth guidance maintained at 9-10% for FY26; consolidated EBITDA margin improvement guidance reduced from 100 bps to 75 bps
items.quote: Only if you have consolidated EBITDA margin, there would be a little bit lower than what the guidance was gi ven. Instead of 100 bps increase, it will be about 75 bps. But topline, we are not changing any guidance

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance of ~1.5% increase for FY26 maintained; Q1 achieved 23.82% vs 22.22% last year
items.quote: Our guidance was also to increase overall standalo ne margin by almost around 1.5%. So, that has happened in 1st Quarter and that trend will con tinue overall in the current financial year

items.statement: Q1 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin improved to 23.82% from 22.22% in Q1 FY25; consolidated EBITDA margin declined marginally to 18.39% from 18.52%
items.quote: q1 FY '26 standalone Ipca has improved its margin f rom 23.82% as against 22.22% in Q1 FY '25. However, the consolidated EBITDA margins are a t around 18.39% in Q1 FY '26 as against 18.52% in Q1 FY '25

items.statement: Unichem margin decline due to loss of market share on 4 high-margin US products, Asia business drop (Myanmar license issues), Brazil decline, Rs 12 cr Euro provision, Rs 10 cr Ireland closure cost
items.quote: On 4 major products, they have lost the market share in this quarter where the profitability was better and on other products, they have gained the market again. So, overall number-wise, the overall business growth is appearing to be 12%, but overall margin-wise, there is a decline because some of the profitable products, the market shares are lost.
