items.statement: Focus on quarter-on-quarter growth and order book delivery; target $850M+ order book for FY26 to enable FY27 growth commitment
items.quote: So, my entire focus and my management team's focus is first deliver growth in Q2, and then like we discussed, if there are not too much furloughs, deliver growth in Q3 and then Q4. But at a larger scope, if I can deliver this, what I just said, focus on quarter-on-quarter, and deliver above 850 million of order book, then at least next year, I can commit to a solid growth year.

items.statement: Expects sequential improvement in FY26 with H2 margins better than H1; standalone EBITDA margins in H1 below range but improving in H2
items.quote: As guided during our latest investor meet in May2025, we expect performance to improve sequentially in FY26 with the second half performance better than the first half performance in terms of margin. Standalone EBITDA margins in H126 is likely to be below our range but is expected to improve in the second half.

items.statement: Targets mid-to-high single-digit UVG for standalone, high single-digit consolidated INR revenue growth, and double-digit consolidated EBITDA growth for FY26
items.quote: We believe for FY26, we are on track for mid-to-high single-digit UVG for standalone business, high single -digit consolidated INR revenue growth and double -digit consolidated EBITDA growth for the full year.

items.statement: A&P savings of 150-200 bps on track as guided at investor meet
items.quote: Furthermore, as guided in the investor meet, we are on track to deliver 150 bps to 200 bps of savings in A &P investments.

items.statement: Standalone ex-soaps delivered mid-teens underlying volume growth; India volume growth 5% but ex-soaps mid-teens; HI high single-digit volume growth
items.quote: In particular, our standalone ex-soaps business has had an excellent performance delivering an underlying volume growth of mid-teens, led by robust broad-based performance.

items.statement: Indonesia impacted by macro headwinds and competitive pricing pressures; expects transitory improvement in few months
items.quote: Our Indonesia business has been impacted by macro headwinds and competitive pricing pressures. However, we expect this to be transitory in nature with the situation improving in a few months.

items.statement: New launches (Block, AirPlug, Amazon Woods 4X, Aer Pocket) seeing good consumer traction and repeat sales
items.quote: All our products like Block, the anti-perspirant, AirPlug, and Amazon Woods 4X, have been launched successfully and are seeing good consumer traction and repeat sales.

items.statement: Took 5% price increase on Fab with no volume impact despite competition; not playing pricing game on Fab
items.quote: In fact, we have taken up prices by 5% on Fab in the last quarter and have seen no impact of it despite a lot of price competition in the market.

items.statement: Price cuts of 7-8% in Indonesia HI and air fresheners to match competition; corrected within quarter
items.quote: Compared to where we should be, I think we were about 7%, 8% higher than where we should have been, which we took corrective action in the quarter itself.

items.statement: Price drops in aerosols (CIK) and hair color large pack (5%) to aid volume growth; ex-soaps strategy is aggressive pricing with cost recovery
items.quote: Largely, we've taken some price drops in the non -soap part of the portfolio, especially on aerosols on what we call CIK, which is crawling insect, flying insect, which is mosquito and cockroach. And also on hair color, we brought down the price of our large pack by about 5%.

items.statement: Palm oil prices fell 30% from peak but rallied 10% recently; soap margin benefits expected from Q3 due to inventory lag
items.quote: However, in the last few weeks, there has been a bit of a rally again in soap -- in palm oil prices. So palm oil prices fell back up, not hugely up, but they've gone back up 10 %. So from their peak, they fell 30%, they've gone back up 10%.

items.statement: SLES costs (linked to palm complex) increased; passed through via 5% Fab price hike
items.quote: We have, in fact, as I said, gone the other way around and taken up prices on Fab, because actually raw material costs have gone up, SLES, which is a big component, linked to the palm complex and so on.

items.statement: Gaining market share in soaps but at reduced pace; still gaining share despite grammage cuts and poor May season
items.quote: See, we're still gaining in this quarter market share on soaps, despite all this, but it is less than we usually gain. So I have to say that we have for a long time been gaining significant share on soaps.

items.statement: RNF molecule provides competitive moat in Electrics; exclusivity period and long lead time for new molecules in India
items.quote: The RNF molecule is a competitive mode for us, because as I said, when we launched RNF, you guys were here in the last analyst call, we have exclusivity for some time on this and the lead time for new molecules in India is long.

items.statement: Indonesia price competition seen as temporary response to macro slowdown; priority is defending market share over margins
items.quote: Our objective is always to defend our shares and to grow our shares. That is number one priority in a when the macros are poor. So whatever the consequence of defending shares, you have to bear it, you have to bear it.

items.statement: HI volume growth trajectory at high single-digit; expects this to persist with seasonal variance between low single-digit and double-digit
items.quote: I think we have achieved a certain kind of momentum on HI which we're convinced of, which is kind of moving from a zero to low single digit volume growth to a high single digit volume growth in HI.

items.statement: Long-term soap volume growth expected at 2-3% (low single-digit) as category is inelastic; grammage cuts temporary
items.quote: I do expect that the long term volume growth on soaps to be in the low single digit, which is 2% odd, 2 to 3% is what I expect the long term volume growth on soaps to be.

items.statement: Aggressive cost saving programs including supply chain and new factories to recover ex-soaps margins
items.quote: We have very aggressive cost saving programs, including in the first quarter, a lot of it has come through media negotiations. But we have some big budget savings, including from supply chain, from our new factories, etcetera.

items.statement: Indonesia margin pressure may be temporary; expects improvement by Q3 but not 100% certain
items.quote: I have a feeling again, look again, Percy, I'm not 100% sure here, but I have a feeling that this is a bit of a temporary drop and it should come back in the next few months.

items.statement: Monsoon impact on Q2 HI uncertain; July poor in South but August recovered; cannot predict seasonality
items.quote: But sitting here today, I don't think this is going to be a particularly good or bad season sitting here today. I don't know what August and September will bear.

items.statement: Soap grammage cuts sharp (56g to 43g on Godrej No.1 INR10 pack); unit growth likely double-digit despite 5% UVG
items.quote: For example, on Godrej number one, INR10. Last year, same quarter, I think we were 55 grams or 56 grams. This year, we're about 43 grams. That's the kind of gra mmage cut that we've had to take, which is almost 20% gra mmage cuts, right

items.statement: Deodorant channel margin revamp in Tamil Nadu (MRP INR230 to INR99) doubled volumes, volume shares and NSV growth
items.quote: In Tamil Nadu, what we did is the category MRP was INR230 and the trade price was INR100. In Tamil Nadu, what we did is we brought down the MRP to INR99 and we bought down the trade price to INR90 and converted 150 ml to 125 ml so that the gross margins remain the same. That has had explosive growth in terms of volume shares, volume growth and even NSV growth.

items.statement: Bloq antiperspirant at INR99 disruption; long gestation, not expecting significant revenue in next two years
items.quote: But to answer your question, is Bloq going to give us a lot of revenue in the next two years? I doubt it. But it is one of the key reasons why we did this acquisition, which is to build the antiperspirant category.

items.statement: Pet food (Ninja) launched in Tamil Nadu; product acceptance good among consumers; long gestation like Bloq
items.quote: We've launched it in TN. We've sold in, again, I was in Chennai yesterday both to look at b loq and to look at our pet business a nd the first question I ask more than anything else is, is the product acceptance good a nd among consumers whose pets have used Ninja, the product acceptance is

items.statement: Africa margin compression due to Aer Pocket launch investments across markets; pivoting to FMCG model
items.quote: I think the primary reason is that one of our products, which is Aer Pocket, has been doing well across the world and we have been -- launched it in many countries in Africa and invested quite a lot in Aer Pocket in terms of media and on-ground activities and BTL.

items.statement: Completed QIP of INR 4,500 crores, first equity raise since 2004 IPO, oversubscribed with global and domestic investors
items.quote: we successfully completed a qualified institutions placement or QIP, of INR 4,500 crores, which is our first equity raise since Biocon's IPO in 2004.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt ~USD 1.15B: Biocon Biologics USD 1.15B, Generics USD 100M, Syngene USD 100M cash positive
items.quote: Biocon Biologics has a net debt of USD 1.15 billion, USD 100 million debt in generics, USD 100 million cash in Syngene. So when you add the se 3, it's USD 1 .15 billion, which is primarily the debt in Biocon Biologics

items.statement: Generics: strong double-digit revenue growth for full year FY26 driven by multiple launches in coming quarters
items.quote: Multiple product launches are planned in the coming quarters, which will support strong double-digit growth for the full year.

items.statement: Syngene (CRDMO) remains on track to deliver FY26 guidance despite macroeconomic uncertainties
items.quote: Despite macroeco nomic uncertainties, Syngene sees robust demand from large and midsized pharma clients and remains on track to deliver FY '26 guidance

items.statement: Biosimilars: five products ready for launch in next 12-18 months; four already launched/approved; fifth (bevacizumab) US approval expected shortly
items.quote: We've got five products ready for launch in the next 12 to 18 months is what we had guided. Four of those five are already now getting to launch, four of them we've launched. Fifth is on the way from an approval standpoint.

items.statement: US FDA approved Kirsty (biosimilar Insulin Aspart) - first and only interchangeable rapid-acting insulin in US
items.quote: The U.S. FDA approved Kirsty ™, our biosimilar Insulin Aspart, making it the first and only interchangeable rapid-acting insulin in the U.S.

items.statement: Launched Yesafili (biosimilar Aflibercept) in Canada - 10th biosimilar to reach commercial markets globally
items.quote: We launched the first biosimilar Aflibercept, Yesafili™, in Canada. And this marks our tenth biosimilar to reach commercial markets globally

items.statement: Secured EU and UK approvals for biosimilar Denosumab (bone health) - new therapeutic segment entry
items.quote: We also secured approvals for biosimilar Denosumab from both the European Commission and U.K. MHRA. And these approvals mark Biocon Biologics anticipated entry into the bone health therapy area

items.statement: Yesintek (Ustekinumab) strong US launch with formulary coverage across CVS, UnitedHealth, Express Scripts, Blue Cross Blue Shield; early prescription uptake leading
items.quote: Yesintek™, our biosimilar Ustekinumab, emerged as a leader in early Immunology uptake with strong formulary coverage across major payers, including CVS, UnitedHealth, Express Scripts and Blue Cross Blue Shield plans.

items.statement: Oncology biosimilars Ogivri (Trastuzumab) and Fulphila (Pegfilgrastim) each maintain 27% US market share
items.quote: Our Oncology portfolio delivered strong performance with Ogivri ®, our biosimilar Trastuzumab and Fulphila®, biosimilar Pegfilgrastim, both maintaining 27% market share.

items.statement: Hulio (Adalimumab) 18% market share in Germany; Abevmy (Bevacizumab) and Ogivri showing strong EU tender momentum
items.quote: Hulio®, which is our biosimilar Adalimumab, continues to be one of the market leaders in Germany with a market share of 18%.

items.statement: Syngene Unit III biologics facility in Bengaluru operational; Bayview US facility on track for commissioning later this year
items.quote: Biologics manufacturing has made good progress in terms of capacity expansion. Unit III, which is our biologics facility in Bengaluru, is now operational. The Bayview facility in the U.S. remains on track for commissioning later this year.

items.statement: Biosimilars EBITDA margin (ex-FX) 24%, up ~300 bps YoY on operating leverage and economies of scale; gross margins steady
items.quote: EBITDA margin, excluding For ex and other items, was at 24% with an approximately 300 basis points year-on-year expansion, reflecting improved operating leverage and the benefits of economies of scale.

items.statement: CRDMO (Syngene) EBITDA margin 25%, up 19% YoY; pilot programs transitioning to long-term contracts
items.quote: EBITDA of INR 224 crores , which is 19% year-on-year increase with a 25% margin, and growth was driven by pilot programs transitioning into long -term contracts

items.statement: NHS UK: secured 4 of 7 regional awards for Yesafili (100% success rate in national tenders)
items.quote: we have had a successful outcome with NHS, securing 4 out of 7 regional awards for Yesafili. This marks a 100% success rate across our national tender submissions in the U.K.

items.statement: Liraglutide US FDA: all queries addressed, facility cleared (VAI), target action date assigned, awaiting outcome
items.quote: We have addressed all the queries. We had two open points with the FDA in the last CRL. One was related to the facility clearance, which, of course, the facility has been subsequently cleared, received VAI. And there was some specific data that the FDA asked, which we had responded to, and we have a target action date being assigned by FDA

items.statement: Biosimilars regional split: Emerging Markets 23%, Advanced Markets 77% (full year 75/25); within Advanced, North America 40%+, balance Europe
items.quote: Emerging Markets is about 23%. Advanced Markets is about 77%. But on a full year basis, you should factor 75%, 25%, Damayanti. And within 75% of the Advanced Markets, U.S., then North America will be 40% plus and the balance will be Europe.

items.statement: No compulsion for Biocon Biologics IPO; Viatris exit commitment is best effort with few years timeline
items.quote: No, there's no compulsion. I think we have said that IPO is -- I mean the commitment to Viatris that we had was the best effort, and we have time to give exit to investors, which is in few years.

items.statement: Trading margin maintained at 3.37 paise per unit with 8% increase in trading income
items.quote: This was achieved while maintaining a trading margin of 3.37 paise per unit. Notably, 60% of the trading volume came from short term and exchange-traded products, while the remainder came from bilateral long-term and medium-term contracts.

items.statement: Received encouraging response for 500 MW renewable energy EOI, working with developers to finalize agreements
items.quote: Just to recall, in the last quarter, we informed you that we have floated an invitation of expression of interest for 500 megawatts of renewable energy capacity. The response has been encouraging, and our team is working with project developers to finalize a purchase and sale agreement at competitive rates.

items.statement: Expect power demand to grow steadily at 6% to 8% per annum with short-term volatility from weather
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect power demand to grow steadily at 6% to 8% per annum, although short-term volatility may arise due to transient weather conditions.

items.statement: Cross-border operations stable with Bangladesh payments regular, Bhutan demand rising, Nepal import/export commenced
items.quote: In the cross-border market, our operations continue across all three grid-connected neighboring countries, which is Bhutan, Nepal, and Bangladesh. Energy flows to Bangladesh remain stable under the agreed contextual framework, with regular flow of payments to our accounts.

items.statement: Short-term volume 13.9 BU, long-term including cross-border 8 BU in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So, in Q1 '26, the short term volume including the exchange trade was around 13.9 billion units. And as far as the long term trade including the cross border is concerned, so the total was 8 billion units for the first quarter of FY'26.

items.statement: Short-term margin 0.8 paise/unit, long-term margin 7.49 paise/unit, overall 3.37 paise/unit
items.quote: And the margin is 3.37 paise per unit. Manoj Kumar Jhawar: In short term? Pankaj Goel: And in short term, the margin is 0.8 paise per unit. Long term margin is around 7.49 paise per unit

items.statement: Market coupling favorable for HPX, could unlock Rs 240 crore annual revenue potential from DAM segment
items.quote: So, in the DAM component, the volume traded is roughly around 80 billion units and if we multiply the Rs. 0.04 per unit margin which is earned on all power traded in the DAM market, that gives us a revenue potential of around Rs. 240 crore per annum.

items.statement: PFS disinvestment under active Board consideration, not cancelled, no timeline given
items.quote: Now, again that question has come up for consideration of the Board and it is under active consideration of the Board. Right now, unless and until a decision has been taken by the Board, I cannot really give a strait jacketed answer to this question.

items.statement: Special dividend from PFS subject to Board consensus, will announce when decided
items.quote: Two things regarding any special dividend. I mean, the matter has to be considered by the Board. Whenever a consensus emerges that any dividend is to be declared, we shall definitely be making an announcement.

items.statement: Evaluating deployment of PTC Energy divestment proceeds into core-adjacent businesses, no concrete announcements yet
items.quote: We have retained a large portion of the divestment proceeds. And we intend to deploy that into meaningful businesses, which are not far off from our core area of operations. But right now, the, CAPEX allocation for next 25 years is the kind of decision which we are going to take.

items.statement: No formal revenue/margin guidance for 2-3 years, aim to maintain volume growth momentum above national generation growth
items.quote: Forward-looking statements, I would not like to venture into. But, I mean, what I can say is, we would like to maintain the momentum. Our trading volumes have been growing at a rate which is faster than the total energy generation rate in the country.

items.statement: Virtual PPA draft notification seen as interesting opportunity, awaiting final CERC guidelines
items.quote: It is a very interesting emerging area. And being a trader, we see a lot of value. But we have to wait for the final guidelines to appear in this regard.

items.statement: URET withdrawal has no impact on PTC as not designated REIA, positive if REIA assignment received
items.quote: Basically, it has to be understood that this mechanism was instituted by the government because under the REIA nomenclature and REIA framework bids, the states were unwilling to enter into power purchase agreements. Now, PTC not being designated as REIA, i t has got no impact on the business of the PTC

items.statement: MBED implementation would be 100% positive, exponential growth opportunity for traders
items.quote: It is 100% positive. If MBED comes, then what it would entail is that all the capacity which has been tied into the long-term context, which are almost 85% of the power being traded, generated and consumed in the country, would also come to some kind of market mechanism.

items.statement: HPX stake reduction below 5% to enable trading under market coupling under evaluation, no definitive timeline
items.quote: Our investment in HPX was a strategic one. Now, when to divest, whether to divest would be a call to be considered at an appropriate point of time. At this point of time, we would be basically interested in watching the market as it evolves post this market coupling thing.

items.statement: Surcharge income declined due to improved receivables management, Bangladesh making timely payments
items.quote: So, we took a concentrated efforts in that direction. And then, as a result of that effort, the outstanding position against many clients has reduced significantly. Now, the Bangladesh is making the timely payment and sometimes it is even availing rebate.

items.statement: HPX revenue Rs 12.42 crore, PAT Rs 6.41 crore in Q1 FY26
items.value: Revenue Rs 12.42 crore, PAT Rs 6.41 crore
items.quote: Revenue of the HPX, its total revenue from operations is Rs. 12.42 crore for this quarter. And PAT for this quarter is around Rs. 6.41 crore.

items.statement: Standalone volume up 13% to 23 BU, operating margin up 8% to Rs 78 crore, total operational income down 13% to Rs 111 crore
items.quote: So the volume for the quarter has increased by 13% to 23 billion units from 20.5 billion units. Volume has increased mainly because of an increase in exchange trade and cross border trade. The operating margin from sale of electricity has increased by 8% to Rs. 78 crore from Rs. 72 crore.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT up 42% to Rs 289 crore, PAT up 61% to Rs 243 crore, EPS Rs 6.59
items.value: PBT Rs 289 crore, PAT Rs 243 crore
items.quote: Profit before tax from continuing operation has increased by 42% to Rs. 289 crore from Rs. 203 crore. The profit before tax has mainly increased on account of higher share of profit before tax from PTC Financial Services. Profit after tax from continuin g operation has increased by 61% to Rs. 243 crore from Rs. 151 crore

items.statement: 60% short-term/exchange volume, 40% long-term/cross-border in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So, the overall volume for short term is 60% and long term is 40%.

items.statement: Shareholder approval sought at AGM for participation in electricity futures on NSE and MCX
items.quote: In today's AGM itself, we had put up a proposal before our shareholders to allow us to participate in this market in a significant manner and represent our clients and trade on their behalf.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue guidance of INR4,000-4,100 crores, implying ~15% growth over FY25 base of INR3,550 crores
items.quote: I want to reaffirm that we are well positioned for long -term value creation and expect our FY '26 revenue to grow to INR4,000 crores to INR4,100 crores at a consolidated level.

items.statement: FY26 order inflow guidance raised to INR10,000-11,000 crores from earlier INR9,000-10,000 crores
items.quote: So overall, I'm very confident that over the next eight months, we will book fresh orders in the range of INR10,000 crores to INR11,000 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR13,665 crores including INR4,400 crores O&M contracts; WMEL order book INR2,805 crores with 3x book-to-bill
items.quote: As on 30th of June 2025, our stand-alone order book stands at INR11,960 crores, I correct myself INR11,962 crores, while our subsidiary, WMEL holds an order book of INR2,805 crores, bringing the consolidated order book to INR13,665 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 377 bps YoY to 23.8% in Q1 FY26; EBITDA grew 8% YoY to INR208 crores despite 9% revenue decline
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 23.8% compared to 20.1% in Q1 FY '25, an expansion of 377 basis points year-on-year. Despite the top line decline, EBITDA grew 8% year-on-year, reaching INR208 crores.

items.statement: WMEL Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 21.8% with revenue up 45% YoY to INR208 crores
items.quote: In quarter 1 FY '26, WMEL reported revenues of INR208 crores, reflecting a 45% year-on-year growth with an EBITDA margin of 21.8%.

items.statement: Actively pursuing INR12,000-13,000 crores of projects to be bid in next 30-45 days; NHAI pipeline of INR3 lakh crores over 8 months; water opportunities in Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan
items.quote: Further, we are actively pursuing new projects worth of INR12,000 to INR13,000 crores, which are likely to be bid over the next 30 to 45 days.

items.statement: Equity investment of INR137 crores in HAM projects in Q1 FY26
items.quote: This is equity investment in HAM project.

items.statement: Bhandup water treatment plant and Dharavi Ghatkopar tunnel moved past pre-implementation stage; execution to accelerate in Q3/Q4 FY26 post monsoon
items.quote: As mentioned earlier, FY '26 will see a back -ended execution cycle, projects such as Bhandup Water Treatment Plant, and Dharavi Ghatkopar tunnel have moved past the pre- implementation stage and will now be under execution post monsoon.

items.statement: Revenue mix in Q1 FY26: Transport 37%, Water 37%, Tunnelling & Rehabilitation 26%; Water segment grew 38% YoY, Tunnelling grew 53% YoY, Transport declined 43% YoY
items.quote: Segment by revenue distributions; Transport, INR316 crores, 37% share; Water, INR310 crores, 37% share. Tunnelling & rehabilitation INR218 crores, 26% share. The Water segment registered robust 38% year-on-year growth, whereas the Transport segment declined by 43%.

items.statement: UP Jal Jeevan Mission receivables: INR30 crores collected in Q1, INR237 crores stuck per books (INR330 crores per contract); collections expected to improve in Q3
items.quote: Vaibhav, the UP JJM cash flow for this quarter, we have received around INR30 crores in this quarter. And money stuck till now is INR237 crores as per our books of accounts. However, we talked about the contract, as per contract receivable is INR330 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt INR378 crores; standalone net cash INR988 crores; consolidated cash reserves INR1,068 crores
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, net worth is INR2,811 crores with a net debt of INR378 crores.

items.statement: Open to value-accretive acquisitions/mergers in water space; Smart Ops institutionalized as separate JV company (50% WMEL, 30% WEL effective) with CEO to join soon
items.quote: We are always looking for opportunities where we can collaborate, innovate and bring in cutting-edge technologies, which are value accretive for the stakeholders. So always open for any acquisition or merger in case it brings value to our stakeholders.

items.statement: Aunta-Simaria bridge received provisional completion certificate (PCOD); expects 2x equity return on monetization vs 1.5x previous deal; MCP project completion certificate received, 51% stake transfer to Actis to proceed
items.quote: In this project, we have invested equity of INR160 crores. It would not be appropriate to talk about the valuation at this moment. Since it is a marquee project, we expect that this would provide us return in 2x, which is better from the last monetization deal, which was at 1.5x.

items.statement: Smart Ops order intake guidance INR80-100 crores for FY26; WMEL direct order intake ~INR600 crores; bid pipeline 50:50 water:transport for next 30-45 days
items.quote: Smart Ops will remain small. It will be in the range of about, for the FY '26, it will be in the range of INR80 crores to INR100 crores. So that's what we expect it to be.

items.statement: Oil & gas evacuation discussions with ONGC/DGH ongoing; draft infrastructure sharing rules out; expect clarity in 60-90 days, better info by Q3 FY26
items.quote: We expect the evacuation discussions to conclude in next 60 to 90 days hopefully. These are government companies and this is government. And as you know that government has come up with the rules for sharing of infrastructure.

items.statement: Smart Ops management team in place except CEO; WEL investing in leadership development, reskilling, LITE values, young talent from top institutes
items.quote: The management team other than the CEO is already in place. And it is a joint venture with the Smart Ops U.K. So it is going to be a very separately housed business vertical.

items.statement: Early monsoon onset caused 10-day execution loss (~INR30 crores revenue impact); Q2 revenue may be at 20% of guidance or slightly lower due to monsoon
items.quote: The early onset of monsoon has also impacted our revenue this year, and we have lost approximately 10 days on our road projects. This led to fewer operational days and consequently impacted our revenue.

items.statement: Digitalization: migrated to S/4HANA, implemented WEL-Darpan project management system, 3D/4D/5D BIM for Dharavi/Bhandup, AI tools for operational efficiency
items.quote: We have already implemented and migrated to S/4HANA, which is SAP 4HANA. We have also digitized the entire project management system, which is an in -house developed system called WEL-Darpan.

items.statement: Full-year marketing expenses expected around same level as last year, plus/minus a few percentage points
items.quote: These expenses are partly seasonal, and we expect full-year marketing expenses to remain at around the same level, plus/minus a few percentage points, compared to last year.

items.statement: Operating PBT margin could improve sequentially in coming quarters subject to top-line growth returning to healthy levels
items.quote: Therefore, the operating PBT margin, with some moderation in Q1, could improve sequentially in the coming quarters, subject to top-line growth returning to healthy levels.

items.statement: Recruitment billings growth moderated to 9% due to macro events and demand slowdown across certain sectors impacting hiring investment decisions
items.quote: Billings growth in Q1 moderated compared to the mid-to-high-teens growth witnessed in the previous few quarters. This was primarily due to multiple macro events during the quarter and a general demand slowdown across certain sectors which impacted investment decisions relating to people amongst companies.

items.statement: Contract deferrals by clients towards quarter end impacted renewal activity and overall billings growth
items.quote: We observed a trend of contract deferrals by some clients towards the end of the quarter, which is usually the peak period for closures. As a result, renewal activity was impacted, leading to a moderation in overall Billings growth.

items.statement: GCCs, technology companies, retail, healthcare, manufacturing posted double-digit growth; recruitment consultants, IT services, BPM, BFSI, infrastructure saw low single-digit growth
items.quote: Several segments and sectors such as GCCs, technology companies, retail, healthcare, and manufacturing, continued to post double-digit growth. On the other hand, segments like recruitment consultants, IT services, BPM, BFSI, and infrastructure experienced a moderation with growth tapering to low single digits in Q1.

items.statement: Naukri platform hosts approximately 108 million resumes with average 26,000 new resumes added daily in Q1 FY26
items.quote: On the job seeker front, the Naukri platform now hosts approximately 108 million resumes and added an average of 26,000 new resumes daily during Q1 of FY26.

items.statement: Niche businesses IIMJobs/Hirist, Naukri Gulf, Naukri Fast Forward grew billings 41%, 18%, 15% YoY respectively
items.quote: Niche and adjacent businesses like IIMJobs and Hirist, Naukri Gulf, and Naukri Fast Forward, the candidate services business, sustained their growth trajectory in Q1 of FY26, with year-on-year Billings growth of 41%, 18%, and 15% respectively.

items.statement: Recruitment operating profit grew 12% YoY to Rs.284 crores with 53% operating margin
items.quote: The operating profit improved by 12% year-on-year to Rs.284 crores and the operating profit margin was 53%.

items.statement: Marketing expenses elevated in Q1 due to IPL campaigns, job seeker database strengthening in emerging cities, and investments in smaller businesses
items.quote: Marketing expenses were elevated in Q1 and can be broadly classified into the following buckets. IPL-related branding campaigns, which are once-a-year activities; focus efforts to further strengthen our job seeker database, especially in emerging cities and non-IT segments; and some increased investments in smaller businesses such as IM Jobs, Naukri Gulf, and Job Hai as they gain scale.

items.statement: July collections growth 19% and billing growth 13-14% in Naukri; 99acres also much better than previous quarter
items.quote: July collections growth were actually pretty solid, 19% collection and 13% billing.

items.statement: Average CTC of CV viewed on Naukri has gone up substantially over last five years, enabling potential price increases; credit model based on CTC tiers possible but not yet implemented

items.quote: It has increased from Rs. 117 last year at this time to Rs. 123, thanks to the innovative packaging and pricing strategies we've implemented.

items.statement: DSO 69 days, up 9 days YoY due to timing; no past-due collections
items.quote: DSO for Q1 FY '26 is at 69 days, up 9 days from the previous year, which I believe was more a result of timing issues. As of now, I think there are no past-due collections from our customers, and we have collected them.

items.statement: Net worth Rs. 7,980 crores, debt Rs. 1,186 crores, net cash surplus Rs. 5,140 crores
items.quote: We are maintaining a strong balance sheet with a total net worth of approximately Rs. 7,980 crores and debt of around Rs. 1,186 crores, which again reflects healthy gearing ratios. The net cash and treasury surplus is approximately Rs. 5,140 crores.

items.statement: Market cap Rs. 2,500 crores vs cash Rs. 5,000 crores; investor concern over promoter-linked investments
items.quote: The cash balances are not with the promoters. Instead, this cash is invested in various companies, and these decisions are made after careful risk assessment.

items.statement: TRA regulations increased broadcaster costs in April-May; price hike expected September
items.quote: In terms of cost, the broadcaster's expenses typically increased in April and May due to TRA regulations. However, there is a delay in passing on these increases on the ground. The price hike is expected to occur in September.

items.statement: Broadband subscriber base 40M expected to double in 3-5 years; 6 lakh villages fiber plan
items.quote: The current subscriber base of about 40 million in India is expected to more than double in the next 3-5 years.

items.statement: Hired key personnel across broadband functions; building performance-driven team nationwide
items.quote: We have hired key personnel across various functions in broadband, including business development, regional sales, product development, business intelligence, and analytics.

items.statement: Focus on Tier 2/3/4 markets with lower entry barriers to avoid price wars in metros
items.quote: Our focus is on stabilizing ARPUs in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets, where service quality is the key driver.

items.statement: Organic business contribution increased to 32% of revenue in Q1
items.quote: Over the past four quarters, or even the previous year, we've been able to increase its contribution to 32% in this quarter alone.

items.statement: Media segment loss due to Rs. 30 cr marketing deals unbilled, Rs. 15 cr excess provision reversal, Rs. 7-8 cr cable decline
items.quote: Firstly, we have marketing deals with broadcasters, worth Rs. 30 crores, that could not be closed in Q1. Although the work was completed, we were unable to bill them due to a lack of confirmation from the broadcaster's side.

items.statement: Expect better media performance in coming quarters as marketing deals are seasonal
items.quote: The marketing deals with broadcasters are essentially seasonal. The marketing work has been done, but the billing couldn't be completed due to confirmation issues. Therefore, it is seasonal and will be addressed in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Urban demand soft with consumers down-trading or deferring non-essential purchases; rural markets outperformed urban.
items.quote: Consumers, particularly in urban centers, continue to either down trade or defer non-essential purchases. These behavioral shifts have been a recurring theme across the sector over the past 5-6 quarters.

items.statement: Expect demand environment to firm up meaningfully from Q3 FY26 onwards driven by monsoon, fiscal measures, and rate cuts.
items.quote: If these tailwinds sustain, we expect the demand environment to firm up meaningfully, especially from Q3 onwards.

items.statement: Early signs of urban demand recovery emerging from July onwards in secondary sales.
items.quote: July, we saw some towards the second half of the month, we saw some improvement on the secondary side.

items.statement: Gross margin at 48%, down 330 bps YoY due to input cost pressures and competitive intensity in Dish wash.
items.quote: Gross margin was at 48%, down 330 bps year-on-year due to input cost pressures and increased competitive intensity in Dish wash.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at 16.5% in line with guidance despite elevated input costs.
items.quote: Despite elevated input cost and volume pressures, we maintained our EBITDA margin at 16.5% in line with our guidance.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin expected between 16% and 17%.
items.quote: But an overall basis for the year, we still believe that between 16% and 17% margin is possible.

items.statement: Household insecticide category targeted to turn profitable by H2 FY27.
items.quote: by second half of the next financial year is what we are aiming to turn this category profitable

items.statement: Crude oil prices softened but derivative costs (LAB, SLES, PFAD, PKFAD) yet to correct proportionately due to lag effects.
items.quote: Crude oil prices have softened, although derivative costs such as LAB, SLES, PFAD and PKFAD are yet to correct proportionately due to lag effects and processing costs.

items.statement: Calibrated price increases implemented in some product categories to partially offset input cost pressures.
items.quote: We implemented calibrated price increases in some of the product categories to partially offset these pressures.

items.statement: Price-volume gap of ~2.2% expected to narrow from Q3 FY26 as base effects of last year's higher grammage and promotions kick in.
items.quote: Q3 would be the fair timeframe. Q2, more or less, it will be the same. But Q3 onwards, it should start narrowing because last year the extra grammages, higher promotions, etc. intensity increased Quarter 2 onwards.

items.statement: Liquid detergent more than doubled growth YoY and delivered strong sequential double-digit value growth.
items.quote: Our liquid detergent range continues to stand out. It more than doubled its growth versus the same period last year and delivered strong sequential double-digit value growth.

items.statement: Pril liquid posted double-digit volume growth; Exo bars grew high single-digit.
items.quote: Pril liquid posted double-digit volume growth and Exo bars grew in high single-digit.

items.statement: Jovia beauty soap gaining market acceptance; Margo brand showing encouraging signs through enhanced visibility and consumer recall.
items.quote: Jovia, our new beauty soap, is gaining market acceptance and our intensified efforts behind Margo brand are already showing encouraging signs through enhanced visibility and consumer recall.

items.statement: Ujala Young & Fresh fabric conditioner gaining traction in select markets; TV commercial launched featuring Keerthy Suresh.
items.quote: We are pleased with the early market response to our fabric conditioner Ujala Young and Fresh, which is gaining traction in select markets. During the quarter, we successfully launched a TV commercial in select markets featuring actress Keerthy Suresh endorsing the product.

items.statement: Modern trade and e-commerce including quick commerce sustained double-digit growth; general trade faced volume pressures.
items.quote: General trade faced volume pressures, while modern trade, including e-commerce and quick commerce, sustained double-digit growth.

items.statement: Quick commerce largely substitutes traditional outlets rather than driving incremental consumption; pricing is primary differentiator.
items.quote: While its share in the overall mix is expanding, it largely substitutes traditional outlets rather than contributing to incremental consumption. Pricing remains the primary differentiator on these platforms due to similar user experiences.

items.statement: Rural contributes ~40% of business; urban growth driven by modern trade and e-commerce, not traditional retail.
items.quote: rural contributes around 40% for us. And urban is the one that is right now, while we are putting all our efforts to see that both urban and rural both perform. For us, rural is the one that is currently performing.

items.statement: General trade largely cash-and-carry; modern trade and quick commerce extended credit averaging 30-35 days across the basket.
items.quote: overall, we can say a basket approach if you see about 30-35 days credit.

items.statement: Competitive intensity rising across all categories; Dish wash saw intensive grammage offers impacting value growth.
items.quote: The Dish wash segment faced intensive competitive activity, particularly in terms of grammage offers. This impacted value growth despite healthy volumes.

items.statement: No new D2C brands breaking into top 3-5 positions in quick commerce or e-commerce; usual suspects remain category leaders.
items.quote: No, these are the usual suspects.

items.statement: No intention to sell or divest household insecticide business; focused on turning it around in a capital-efficient manner.
items.quote: as of now, there is no intention to sell or divest this particular line of business of the Company.

items.statement: Actively evaluating a few assets for acquisition; will share information at appropriate time.
items.quote: we are in pursuit of finding the right fit, and in that regard we are evaluating few assets and at an appropriate time, the information will be shared with the investor community.

items.statement: Marketing spend at 7.8% in Q1; committed to annual brand investment between 8% and 9% of revenue.
items.quote: our spends are more or less in line with our overall stated strategy, which is between 8% and 9%. And on an annualized basis, you see the number hovering between 8 and 9.

items.statement: Revenue from operations Rs 751 crore, 1.4% value growth and 3.6% volume growth YoY.
items.quote: Revenue from operations for Q1 stood at Rs. 751 crore, reflecting 1.4% value growth and 3.6% volume growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA Rs 124 crore; PAT Rs 97 crore.
items.quote: Operating EBITDA stood at Rs. 124 crore and PAT at Rs 97 crore.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East triggering raw material supply disruptions and cost volatility.
items.quote: global uncertainties, particularly the geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, have triggered raw material supply disruptions and increased cost volatility

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin target is to match FY25 level of 13.7%
items.quote: Our intention is this full year, if we could manage to the last year's EBITDA, that will be ultimate satisfaction to us.

items.statement: Volume growth target of 8-9% for the year
items.quote: As in my last investor call, I said we expect 8% to 9% volume growth. So this is in line with that.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 10.8% from 10.2%
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA for the quarter was at INR 103 crores, a 10% increase over Q4 FY '25, a sequential improvement in EBITDA margins to 10.8% from 10.2% last quarter.

items.statement: High-cost alumina inventory to be consumed by September; margins to improve in Q2 and Q3
items.quote: By September, this high-cost inventory should be consumed. And Q3 will see, Q2 will also, I assume from Q1, there will be some uptick on Q2 and Q3 will still be better.

items.statement: Secured key price increases with customers; benefits expected in coming quarters
items.quote: We had productive discussions with our customers and secured key price increases, and we are expecting to see these benefits in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Alumina prices have fallen; high-cost inventory moving through P&L will taper down
items.quote: The reason for this is due to the elevated high - cost alumina prices moving from our inventory to P&L, and this will taper down in the upcoming quarters as the alumina prices have f allen down

items.statement: Strong order book in iron making and steel segments; regained market share in PSU plants
items.quote: We have a very strong order book in iron making area and also in the steel area as well. Steelmaking, especially with our integrated steel plants on the TRM side.

items.statement: Full-year capex planned at INR 150 crores, nearly double last year
items.quote: It is about INR150 crores, total.

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved to 66% in Q1 from 55% previously
items.quote: Capacity utilization improved to 66%, ensuring that additional market demand was met through planned inventory increases.

items.statement: 4 PRO model progressing from planning to execution; first robotic solution deployed at JSW
items.quote: This quarter, we have moved from planning to execution and the early results are very encouraging. Our teams have achieved multiple operational milestones at customer sites.

items.statement: 4 PRO contracts are long-term (5 years); two more in final pipeline stage
items.quote: we are in a very final stage of having two more 4 PRO o contracts in the pipeline

items.statement: Regained market share across almost all segments; now 42-43% in cement vs 12-13% pre-Dalmia
items.quote: We have increased our market share from 12%, 13% prior to acquisition of Dalmia to almost 42% -43%.

items.statement: Iron making market share grew from 2% to 13%; aspiration 25-30% in 2-3 years
items.quote: We were having 2% market share, and now we have 13% market share, and aspiration is 25% to 30% in next 2-3 years' time.

items.statement: Chinese traders undercutting prices in magnesia carbon bricks; 8-9 new small Indian players entered
items.quote: Almost 50% of the commodity business if we talk about the ladle business or so, the Chinese traders are coming because China is having overcapacity.

items.statement: Export trials in advanced stage; meaningful ramp-up expected in 2026 for flow control
items.quote: We have quite a reasonably good plan to increase our export in flow control in 2026.

items.statement: Acquired Ashwath Technology via subsidiary Intermetal Engineers effective 1 Aug 2025
items.quote: We also enhanced our steel flow control capability through a small acquisition of Ashwath Technology by our subsidiary, Intermetal Engineers, effective from 1st August '2025.

items.statement: Generated INR 88 crores operating cash flow; net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.2x
items.quote: We generated INR 88 crores in operating cash flows in Q1, increase of 36% QoQ and invested INR 28 crores in capital expenditure, all funded through our balance sheet.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA improved from 0.3x to 0.2x quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: This reflects consistent improvement in our net debt-to-EBITDA ratio from 0.3x to 0.2x quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Employee benefit cost expected to hover around 10% of revenue for full year
items.quote: So it will be hover somewhere about 10 % employee benefit cost is what you can model

items.statement: TRM/4 PRO share of steel revenue at 32%; steel is 81% of total revenue
items.quote: So out of this 81%, you have to take out 32%.

items.statement: Geopolitical challenges slowing export demand in key Asian markets
items.quote: There's quite a bit of geopolitical challenges. So there's not a lot of production happening in the key export market in Asia.

items.statement: Industrial refractory projects deferred to 2026-27; no project pipeline this FY
items.quote: Unfortunately, for non-ferrous or glass, all the projects are shifted to '2026-2027. So unfortunately, there is no project in the pipeline for this FY.

items.statement: Capital allocation priority: maintenance capex, dividends, strategic capex, then M&A, then buybacks
items.quote: first thing, we will do capital allocation if we have a positive cash flow. That's the first requirement. If it is there, our first investment would be on the maintenan ce capex

items.statement: ROIC hurdle ~10% average across segments; used for all capex and M&A decisions
items.quote: On an average, you can assume that if it's more than 10%, this is where we kind of put our money there.

items.statement: Working capital intensity target of 25%; launching Project Everest for supply chain planning
items.quote: Parmodji has given a very stringent target that consistently, we should be able to reach 25% as working capital intensity.

items.statement: Goodwill write-off of EUR 35 million taken last year; no further impairment expected
items.quote: Last -- we took a write-off of EUR 35 million worth of it because we believe that the export business that were embedded in the business plan of the acquired entity, we were not able to fulfill.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM grew 6.8% YoY to INR 12,499 crores; standalone gross loan portfolio grew 4.5% YoY to INR 10,956 crores
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, in terms of growth, our AUM grew by 6.8% Y-o-Y to INR 12,499 crores. On a sta ndalone basis, our gross loan portfolio stood at INR10,956 crores, reflecting a growth of 4.5% on Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: Consolidated disbursements up 6% YoY to INR 2,242 crores; standalone disbursements up 3.4% YoY to INR 2,065 crores
items.quote: We also maintained consistent disbursement momentum with INR2,242 crores disbursed on a consolidated basis, up 6% on a year -on-year basis and INR2,065 crores on a standalone basis, marking a growth of 3.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated branch network expanded 10.5% to 1,599 branches across 519 districts in 29 states/UTs; standalone branches up 14.3% to 1,487
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we now operate through a network of 1,599 branches, reflecting a growth of 10.5%, covering 519 districts across 29 states and union territories. On a standalone basis, the branch count increased by 14.3% to 1,487.

items.statement: Planning to open ~188 branches in Q2 FY26 to continue growth plans
items.quote: we are now opening close to about 188 branches this quarter to move forward and continue with our growth plans.

items.statement: On-book provisions of INR 316 crores (3.6% of on-book portfolio) vs RBI requirement of INR 177 crores; management overlay of INR 8 crores added in Q1
items.quote: As of June '25, we hold on -book provisions of INR316 crores, which is 3.6% of the on -book portfolio, s ignificantly higher than the RBI requirement of INR177 crores. In addition to this, we have created a management overlay of INR8 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Stage 3 coverage ratio improved to 63% from 61% in June '24; recovered INR 8 crores against written-off pool
items.quote: Our Stage 3 coverage ratio has improved to 63% compared to 61% in June last year, which again reinforces our focus on prudent provisioning. During the reporting period, we have recovered around INR8 crores against the written-off pool, another marker of the strength in the system.

items.statement: Credit evaluation tightened post guardrails 2 implementation from April; application rejection rates increased to 67% (up ~300 bps since March '25)
items.quote: Following the implementation of guardrails 2 from April onwards, we tightened our credit evaluation framework, which led to an increase in application rejection rates to 67%, up by approximately 300 basis points since March '25.

items.statement: Only 6.1% of clients had exposure to >3 microfinance lenders; 0.1% had loan exposure >= INR 2 lakh at disbursement
items.quote: As of June '25, only 6.1% of our clients had exposure to more than 3 microfinance lenders and just 0.1% had loan exposure of INR2 lakh or more at the time of disbursement.

items.statement: Net interest margin stable at 13.48% vs 13.38% in Q1 FY25 and 11.81% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Net interest margin remained stable and consistent, standing at 13.48% during the reporting quarter compared to 13.38% in Q1 '25 and 11.81% in Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: Operating expense ratio 6.80% consolidated and 6.68% standalone; sequentially improved due to cost rationalization as conditions stabilize
items.quote: Our operating expense ratio stood at 6.80% on a consolidated basis and 6.68% on a standalone basis. While the ratio remains elevated when compared to the same period last year, largely due to sector-wide challenges, it has shown sequential improvement.

items.statement: Standalone loan loss ratio at 4.84%, slightly elevated due to seasonality and QoQ AUM reduction from muted disbursements and write-offs
items.quote: Loan loss ratio on a standalone basis stood at 4.84%, slightly elevated due to the inherent seasonality of the period, along with a reduction in AUM on a quarter -on-quarter basis caused by muted disbursements and write -offs.

items.statement: Consolidated ROA 1.50% and ROE 7.06%; standalone ROA 1.51% and ROE 5.97%
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, return on assets and return on equity stood at 1.50% and 7.06%, respectively, while on a standalone basis, they stood at 1.51% and 5 .97%.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT INR 45 crores; standalone PAT INR 43 crores; 16th consecutive profitable quarter
items.quote: We reported a PAT of INR45 crores on a consolidated basis, whereas INR43 crores on a standalone basis for the quarter, reinforcing our ability to maintain profitability even in a stress first quarter, establishing us as an outlier.

items.statement: CRAR 26%; adequate liquidity ~INR 2,000 crores plus undrawn sanctions of INR 401 crores; total borrowings INR 8,328 crores; debt-to-equity 2.9x
items.quote: The company's financial position remains strong with CRAR of 26%. During the quarter, the company has adequate liquidity of approximately INR2,000 crores, coupled with undraw n sanctions of INR401 crores.

items.statement: Marginal cost of borrowing ~11.1% (slightly decreasing); finance cost increase in P&L due to hedge accounting (INR 27-28 crores impact on both top line and finance cost)
items.quote: Otherwise, the marginal cost of borrowing is slightly going down. We are close to about 11.1% or so in terms of marginal cost. It is because of the hedge accounting that both the top line and the finance cost is slightly showing as a higher number.

items.statement: Targeting credit cost reduction in FY26 vs FY25 (4.6%); no specific ROA, ROE, or growth guidance given
items.quote: On our targeted credit cost for the financial year '25-'26, we are targeting a reduction compared to FY '25, wh ere it stood at 4.6%.

items.statement: No growth guidance, no ROA guidance; current ROA ~1.51%, ROE ~5.6%, consolidated growth ~9%; historical 6-year average ROA 2.1%, ROE 9.1% expected to remain stable in that range
items.quote: No growth guidance, no ROA guidance. We are only giving you the present picture of what where we are right now. And I think where we stand right now, I think it will probably be stable enough. We said the ROA was about 1.51% and ROE was about 5.6%. Overall consolidated growth was about 9%-odd.

items.statement: Average MFI ticket size increased to INR 56,000 from INR 53,000; driven by lending to existing high-quality customers rather than new-to-credit clients
items.quote: See, for us, we are looking more at of our existing customers basically who have a better credit quality and a better score. And that is the reason why I think that has jumped up from INR53,000, which is pretty negligible in terms of if you look at the ave rage EMI, which comes every 14 days.

items.statement: Satin Housing Finance AUM INR 961 crores (+25% YoY), 100% retail book, GNPA 3.1%, CRAR 48.3%, gearing 2.3x, PAT INR 57 lakhs
items.quote: Satin Housing Finance Limited has no w reached an AUM of INR961 crores, which grew by 25% Y-o-Y, having presence across 20 states with 9,432 customers. SHFL has a 100% retail book. GNPA of 3.1% as of June '25.

items.statement: Satin FinServ (MSME) AUM INR 582 crores; MSME on-book portfolio grew 56%; CRAR 36.8%, gearing 2.4x, PAT INR 1.9 crores; running down BC book, building retail MSME book
items.quote: Satin FinServ Limited, the company's MSME lending arm has reached an AUM of INR582 crores. We are running down the business correspondent book and focusing on building the retail MSME book. MSME on -book portfolio grew by 56%.

items.statement: Management sees no need to de-risk from top 4 states (56-60% AUM concentration stable for 5-7 years); delinquency in these states negligible historically
items.quote: And we would like to concentrate our whatever it's been steady at about 56% to 60%. This has been steady across the last, I think, 5, 7 years. And we would like to concentrate on these states only. No reason for us to de -risk ourselves from there.

items.statement: Satin-plus-3 lender exposure only 6% of portfolio (Satin-only 48.5%, Satin+1 29.7%, Satin+2 15.6%); post guardrails 2, new lending at Satin-plus-3 is zero
items.quote: If you look at the composition for us, close to about if I have the figures, only Satin customers are technically 48.53%. These are the numbers. Satin plus 1 is 29.66%. Satin plus 2 is 15.6%, which means Satin plus Satin plus 1 and Satin plus 2 are close to about 94%. There's hardly just 6%, wh ich is at Satin plus 3.

items.statement: Board strengthened with two new Independent Directors: Mr. Ashok Kumar Sharma (former ED, LIC) and Mr. Anupam Kunal Gangaher (seasoned CA)
items.quote: We further strengthened our Board with the induction of 2 highly distinguished professionals, Mr. Ashok Kumar Sharma, former Ex ecutive Director of the Life Insurance Corporation of India; and Mr. Anupam Kunal Gangaher, a seasoned chartered accou ntant as Independent Directors.

items.statement: First quarter seasonally muted due to agriculture-linked portfolio, harvesting cycle, heat waves; sector reported ~21% degrowth (peer average) but Satin maintained 16th consecutive profitable quarter
items.quote: However, since a significant portion of our portfolio is linked t o agriculture and allied sectors, the first quarter typically experiences a slowdown due to the harvesting cycle and heat waves, which naturally makes this period more challenging in terms of credit demand and operational efficiency. Despite these factors, we are pleased to report our 16 th consecutive profitable quarter.

items.statement: Launched Satin Growth Alternatives, a women-led AIF debt fund focused on underserved MSMEs in rural/semi-urban areas with women and ESG focus
items.quote: Now carrying that same spirit forward comes our newest initiative, Satin Growth Alternatives. A women-led AIF debt fund, this venture marks another forward-looking move. The fund will focus on enabling access to capital for underserved MSMEs across India, particularly in rural and semi -urban regions with a strong focus on enterprises led by women and ESG.

items.statement: Strategic entry into Mizoram in July 2025, strengthening Northeast footprint; region shows strong portfolio quality and customer engagement
items.quote: Building on this approach, we marked our strategic entry into Mizoram in July 2025, further strengthening our leadership footprint in the Northeast, a regi on that has consistently demonstrated strong portfolio quality and customer engagement.

items.statement: Consolidated top-line growth maintained at early teens for FY26
items.quote: So, after the first quarter, I think we still maintain the top -line growth to be in early teens.

items.statement: Profit growth expectation maintained for FY26 after 25% YoY growth in Q1
items.quote: But we maintain the same expectation for profit. And you must have seen that we have grown profit in Quarter 1 by 25% over Quarter 1 last year.

items.statement: Ashitaka herbicide launched in July 2025 with theoretical potential of Rs 200 crore in 3-4 years
items.quote: The theoretical potential of Ashitaka is about Rs. 200 crores. And we believe that we will get there in three, four years.

items.statement: Corn acreage up 7% YoY; targeting 45 million tons production requiring 11 million hectares
items.quote: Corn acreages are going up. You know, this year also till now, about 7% acreage in corn has gone up.

items.statement: Gracia in-licensed product now shared with other competitors by Nissan; salience dropped from 18% to 5% in Q1
items.quote: Gracia is also shared by the principal with other companies . So, definitely when competition grows, we cannot enjoy same level of margins .

items.statement: Gracia salience was 18% in FY25 and 29% in FY24; expected to exceed 18% in FY26 with new labels
items.quote: The salience of Gracia last year in Quarter 1 was 18%. This year Quarter 1 is about 5%.

items.statement: Astec LifeSciences targeting EBITDA break-even and Rs 500 crore turnover in FY26
items.quote: Yes. So, we should report EBITDA break -even this financial year, which is a significant improvement over last financial year. And we are aiming for turnover of Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Astec CDMO revenue target over Rs 300 crore (65% of sales) in FY26; aim to grow >30% annually beyond
items.quote: So, we are aiming for a revenue of over Rs. 300 crores in CDMO business, CDMO and new products. And that should be about 65% of our total sales.

items.statement: PKO refinery to start in Q3 FY26; inter-esterification and hydrogenation in Q4 FY26 for bakery fats
items.quote: We are in the process of setting up a PKO refinery, which will come into production in Q3. And in Q4, we will also be starting inter -esterification and hydrogenation.

items.statement: FFB arrivals up 52% YoY to 178k tons in Q1 FY26; full year FY26 growth expected 15-18% over FY25's 536k tons
items.quote: FFB improvement is 52% over last year. And Q1 FY '26, we got 178k tons. Q1 FY '25, we got about 117k tons, which is a 52% increase.

items.statement: Oil extraction ratio 18.37% in Q1 FY26 vs 17.98% YoY; expected to be better than FY25's 19% for full year
items.quote: In Quarter 1 of FY '26, we had 18.37% oil extraction ratio as compared to Quarter 1 of FY '25, which is 17.98%.

items.statement: Government cut CPO import duty by 10%; refining margin differential widened from 8.75% to 18%+ making refining profitable
items.quote: Today, there is a , actually, government dropped the import duty on CPO by 10% . So, if earlier, the differential between refined and CPO was 8.75%, which went to about 18% plus.

items.statement: Refinery incremental profit 1-1.5% depending on prices; will decide monthly whether to sell CPO or refined oil
items.quote: The incremental profit of the refinery segment is about 1 % to 1.5 % depending on prices.

items.statement: Higher vendor invoice discounting increased material cost and lowered finance cost in Animal Feed segment
items.quote: Now, what it does is that whenever you take extended credit on our purchases, that cost goes and sits as part of the material cost, thereby impacting the segment results.

items.statement: Dairy EBITDA margin including working media at 6.5-7% for FY26; excluding media 5.5-6% annually
items.quote: Lastly, I must tell you that our EBITDA margins, including working media, are close to 6.5% to 7%. And we will be able to maintain that easily.

items.statement: Dairy VAP salience at 42% in Q1 FY26; targeting 50% in two years with higher ad spends (Rs 5 crore more YoY)
items.quote: We are glad to say that our salience continues to be at 42%, which was at the last year level, considering there was a lot of unseasonal early rains.

items.statement: Poultry live bird share reduced to 15% of sales; 85% now value-added products (Yummiez, RGC)
items.quote: So, live bird share, as a strategy, we have started bringing down live bird significantly. And that is why the top line growth of this business has affected. But we are glad to say that live bird share is 15% of the total sales. 85% today are value-added products.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds used primarily to repay debt on Astec LifeSciences books
items.quote: As far as the utilization of the recent rights issue is concerned, the same is being used to repay our debts which were there in the books.

items.statement: Invested Rs 1,250 crore in last six months to buy out partners in Godrej Foods and Creamline Dairy for 100% ownership
items.quote: In total we have invested close to Rs. 1,250 crores in last six months and buying out partners in these two businesses.

items.statement: Balram Yadav stepping down as MD; Sunil Kataria appointed as CEO and MD-Designate
items.quote: I would also like to take this opportunity to welcome Sunil Kataria, who will take over from Balram.

items.statement: Crop protection Q2 returns expected to exceed provisions due to erratic rainfall impacting PYNA season
items.quote: We expect that in Q2, since the PYNA season has not gone well, because of erratic rainfall, we might have some returns in Q2, which will be more than what we had provisioned for.

items.statement: US tariff impact uncertain; Astec's US export exposure only 7-10% of sales; major markets are South Korea and Japan
items.quote: Regarding impact of U.S. tariffs, there is a lot of uncertainty prevailing in terms of what the final tariff rates will be. We understand that trade negotiations are still in progress.
