items.quote: The Kansas order in America is still ongoing, and I expect to complete it by January–February. This Kansas order is the only legacy order that carries a negative outlook for us.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation benefits entire export book (not just US), partially offsetting tariff hit on PAT
items.quote: If I get hurt by tariff, I also get benefit by depreciation of rupee. But the benefit of depreciation of rupee is on the whole export order, not only America.

items.statement: US BABA Act requires 90% US value addition by 2029 driving Houston plant investment
items.quote: there is the BABA Act in America, and B ABA Act in America mandates that for certain type of projects by 2029, 90% of value addition has to be done in America

items.statement: US cost inflation affects all players equally; India engineering team (25-30 engineers) gives cost advantage vs US competitors
items.quote: Compared to our competitors in America, our position is favourable because we have a team of 25 -30 engineers in India supporting estimation, project management, and design Jash Engineering Limited engineering at a comparatively lower

items.statement: Shivpad Chennai facility commissioned Aug 1; combines with WesTech for Rs.100 cr process equipment division targeting Rs.200 cr in 3 years
items.quote: Once we acquire WesTech, which has a revenue of Rs.55 crore, and combine it with Shivpad's Rs 44 crore revenue, the process equipment division will have a total combined revenue of around Rs 100 crore.

items.statement: Targets Rs 110-120 crore revenue for FY26 with PAT margin of 25%
items.quote: Moving forward to about it, we are targeting around Rs. 110 crores of orders in the financial year, and keeping the PAT level at what we have been doing it.

items.statement: Expects Rs 120 crore revenue from existing plant in FY26 and Rs 200 crore from bogie plant at full capacity
items.quote: So, the boogie plant, we would be doing capex of around Rs. 50 crores from that. And we can do revenue of around Rs. 200 crores from that plant wherein we will be making 500 bogies monthly.

items.statement: Targets Rs 250 crore revenue in FY27 with Rs 150 crore from bogies and rest from coaches and tracks
items.quote: So, what we are targeting is around we are targeting Rs. 250 crores, around Rs. 150 crores would be from the bogie and rest would be the coaches product and the track products.

items.statement: Current order book exceeds Rs 115 crore with monthly order inflow of Rs 10-12 crore
items.quote: So, what we are targeting is, order book, right now we have got more than Rs. 115 crores plus order. So, each month we are executing orders and we are getting orders of more than Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 12 crores each month.

items.statement: L1 in tenders worth over Rs 25 crore pending approval
items.quote: We are L1 in more than Rs. 25 crores worth tenders.

items.statement: Bogie plant capex of Rs 50 crore from IPO funds; spring plant capex of Rs 12-15 crore from internal accruals
items.quote: Rs. 50 crores is from the IPO funds which we have raised.

items.statement: Existing plant utilisation was 70% in FY25; can reach 110-150% with new 3,000 sqm shed for tracks
items.quote: Last year we did 70% utilization of that. So, this year we can do 110% from the same facility which we have. But since we have added one more shade and we are planning to do track from that, so we can do around 150% from that.

items.statement: 27 RDSO-certified products; 15 new products in pipeline for bogies/coaches; 36 track products awaiting approval
items.quote: There are 27 products which are RDSO certified. And for the tracks, there are another 32-odd products which we have developed. But right now, they are not RDSO certified. We are getting them certified by RDSO.

items.statement: Coach products (axle box housing, buffer assembly) sell at Rs 220-250/kg vs wagon at Rs 110/kg and track at Rs 140-150/kg
items.quote: So, the products which we are doing in the wagons, they are selling in Rs. 110 per kg, wherein the product which we are doing for the coaches, they are selling for around Rs. 220 to Rs. 250 per kg. Wherein the product which we are doing for the track, they are selling Rs. 140 to Rs. 150 per kg.

items.statement: Targets 25% PAT margin for FY26; confident bogie manufacturing will maintain similar margins
items.quote: At the PAT level, we are targeting 25%. And we are confident that we will be able to do that.

items.statement: Spring plant for coaches expected to yield good margins; smaller springs have lower margins
items.quote: Springs, depending upon the springs you are making for. For the coaches if you are making the spring, there we have got good hefty margins in that. For the small spring, if you are making, yes, margins are a little lesser in that.

items.statement: Received Rs 10 crore orders in July from Railways and private players; major orders from Railways directly
items.quote: In July itself, we received orders of around Rs. 10 crores from the Railways of the component which we are manufacturing right now, even from the private. The Rs. 10 crores orders are including the Railways and the private, but this time major orders have come from the Railways directly, then the private.

items.statement: Track orders from Rahi Engineering, RV Rail, Veera Techno Trec, Anviratech, Anjali Rails
items.quote: Whereas in the track is considered, we have got very huge orders from the company which are into tracks, which are like Rahi Engineering and RV Rail, Veera Techno Trec. So, there are four companies, we have got huge orders from them for fittings.

items.statement: Competes with unlisted players Atul Engineering, Frontier Alloys, NKIRL Industries; similar EBITDA margins
items.quote: So, they would be all unlisted players which are Atul Engineering, Frontier Alloys, Steels, NKIRL Industries. So, these all are like the players which are quoting the tenders with us, floating the inquiries with us.

items.statement: Sources scrap from railway auctions and prefab companies; sand from Allahabad
items.quote: So, basic raw material which we have is the scrap and the sand. Sand is procured from the Allahabad. And the scrap is required from the various railway side and various prefab structure companies which are around.

items.statement: Nearly debt-free with only Rs 2-3 crore term loans; spring plant funded internally, bogie plant from IPO proceeds
items.quote: As of now, we are almost debt-free, sir. We have got term loans of around Rs. 2 crores to Rs. 3 crores, that's all.

items.statement: Raised Rs 77.04 crore via IPO for bogie manufacturing unit in Kanpur
items.quote: And we went for our IPO this year, raised around Rs. 77.04 crores to establish a complete bogie manufacturing unit in Kanpur.

items.statement: Indian Railways targets 10,000 wagons/month implying 20,000 bogies/month plus maintenance demand
items.quote: So, the bogie is what we are targeting, like what all wagon manufacturers are targeting is 10,000 wagon manufacturing per month. That leads to a 20,000 bogie requirement per month.

items.statement: RDSO Class A certification allows application for safety component approvals; each product requires separate STR approval
items.quote: So, first is the (Inaudible 0:19:25.9), Class A, Class B, Class C. So, that is one approval which you get for the company. So, Neetu Yoshi is approved as a Class A, you are allowed to make these critical safety components.

items.statement: No major execution challenges seen; operational issues like inspections, production, electricity managed daily
items.quote: That's what I am telling you, right now I do not see any challenges in execution. We are sorted in terms of orders, we are sorted in terms of plant approvals and everything, so I do not see as such challenge anywhere to implement this.

items.statement: Long-term goal to become wagon manufacturer by FY29-30; engaged Crescendo for technology tie-ups
items.quote: So, our our aim definitely what we see as a long term is in financial '29-'30 to be a wagon manufacturing company and that is what we went for IPO right now.

items.statement: Plan to add nine new hotels and double total key count over next four to five years
items.quote: With the successful completion of our IPO and the availability of funds coupled with operations, we are well positioned to add nine new hotels and double our total key count over the next four to five years.

items.statement: Average construction cost per key: Rs 65 lakhs for Fairfield; Rs 1.75-2 crores for Grand Hyatt, InterCon, Ritz-Carlton
items.value: Rs 65 lakhs to Rs 2 crores per key
items.quote: On average construction cost for brands such as Fairfield is around Rs. 65 lakhs a key, that is the cost of construction per key. And for the higher end hotels like what we have already declared like the Grand Hyatt, InterCon and Ritz-Carlton, on an average basis, the cost of construction per key could be around Rs. 1.75 crores to Rs. 2 crores a key.

items.statement: Q2 demand healthy and as per expectations; October may see dip due to Dusshera and Diwali in same month, November-December robust
items.quote: We expect that the second quarter to also go as per expectations. I mean, I am happy to say that there was good recovery in Q1 despite the geopolitical issue. But in Q2, we are seeing healthy demand, as we expect to see in Q2 of every fiscal year.

items.statement: October occupancy likely lower due to Dusshera and Diwali in same month; November and December should be robust
items.quote: Typically, if you look at October, you have Dusshera and Diwali coming in the same month. So, it is likely that we will see lower occupancies for the month of October, because Dusshera and Diwali come in the same month and there are long weekends.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 33.4%, up 56 bps YoY from 32.9%
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the Quarter 1 FY '26 stood at 33.4%, against 32.9% in Q1 FY '25, an increase of 56 basis points.

items.statement: Portfolio revenue grew 22% YoY and EBITDA grew 24% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that our portfolio has grown by 22% in revenue and 24% in EBITDA for Q1 FY '26 compared to the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Bangalore and Chennai RevPAR grew 12% and 13% YoY; GIFT City RevPAR grew 44% YoY
items.quote: Bangalore and Chennai performed as per expectations with a 12% and 13% year-on-year RevPAR growth respectively. The GIFT City market in Gujarat is gaining momentum and with sustained demand driven by increased development activity and the entry of high pedigree IT and finance companies. Our hotel in gift city delivered a 44% RevPAR growth for the quarter.

items.statement: Ibis Styles Mysuru achieved 68% occupancy in third quarter of operations
items.quote: A special mention to our newly launched Ibis Styles in Mysuru, which is ramping up and managed to achieve a 68% occupancy in just its third quarter of operations.

items.statement: Operational breakeven targeted by Q2-Q3 for new hotels; overall breakeven depends on rate and occupancy
items.quote: For the first part, the operational breakeven, we try to get in quarter two or quarter three itself. So, operationally, we expect the hotel to breakeven in quarter two. But overall, for the entire hotel, it is hard to say at what occupancy it will breakeven, because it depends on the rate.

items.statement: Consolidated gross debt Rs 633 crore; cash Rs 16 crore; net debt Rs 617 crore as of 30 June 2025; repaid entire institutional debt of Rs 468 crore from IPO proceeds
items.quote: The consolidated gross debt of the company stood at INR. 6.33 crores as on 30 th June, 2025. The cash and cash equivalent stood at INR. 16 crores. Therefore, the company's net debt outstanding as on 30th June, 2025 is INR. 617 crores. Based on the object of the issue, we have repaid the entire institutional debt of INR. 468 crores.

items.statement: Corporate segment kept at ~one-third of business; rest retail, groups, crew; no softening in corporate demand seen
items.quote: Our corporate segmentation, I mean, the business from corporate segment is we have kept it at around one-third and the rest of it is a mix of retail and the groups and crew. So, I would say, our dependency on corporate business per se is not that much. And having said that, during the quarter, we have not seen any softening of corporate demand as well that has remained at a very healthy level.

items.statement: Bengaluru demand resilient despite IT job cuts; GCCs, co-working, financial services, pharma, biotech, deep tech diversifying demand base
items.quote: Bengaluru used to be very dependent on just the IT services industry. But now, with the advent of the number of GCCs, Bengaluru is the city in India with the highest number of GCCs entering the market. Apart from that, co-working brands - a lot of office requirement is being taken up by co-working brands and India facing brands and India-led companies. So, the dependency, I would say on IT and IT

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions caused some room cancellations in Q1; offset by ADR growth and overall revenue growth
items.quote: There was some dip in occupancy also because, some rooms might have gotten canceled because of the geopolitical issue. But we have made it up in terms of the ADR and the overall revenue.

items.statement: Portfolio-wide occupancy at high 70%+; expected to be much higher by end of fiscal year
items.quote: Overall, the portfolios are at a very healthy 75% occupancy, which we expect that by the end of the fiscal year, it will be much higher than this. So, portfolio-wide, having a high 70% plus occupancy is still very healthy.

items.statement: No new hotels planned with Ibis Styles; focus on upscale 4-star, 5-star, 5-star deluxe categories with Accor, Marriott, IHG, Hyatt partnerships
items.quote: Currently, as you know, we have the nine hotels planned and none of them are with the IBIS portfolio. So, I am sure all the hotel chains are growing quite rapidly. So, we already have a strong partnership with Accor, Marriott, IHG and of course now, Hyatt as well. As of now, we are not signing any new hotels with Ibis Styles.

items.statement: Future land acquisitions focused on strong leisure/pleasure markets or Tier-I cities; not actively pursuing Tier-II business cities
items.quote: We are currently evaluating multiple opportunities. We are looking at some potential leisure markets. We are also open to looking at other locations in Tier-I cities. We are not currently looking at too many Tier-II markets, I would say, unless it is like a major leisure destination.

items.statement: Return expectations similar across asset classes; target hotel to repay debt and stand on own feet by year 3; high IRR thresholds
items.quote: Typically, we do our IRR thresholds and we also do the payback period, etc. But generally, by the third year, we expect that the hotel should at least start repaying its debt, should be able to stand on its own two feet. And we have high team return expectations from all asset classes, annuity income asset classes, etc. I would say. So, it is no different for hospitality.

items.statement: Demat accounts grew by 67 lakh in Q1 FY26 vs 71 lakh sequentially, while combined ADTO on BSE and NSE rose 15% QoQ to INR1 lakh crore
items.quote: The Demat accounts for this quarter grew by about 67 lakhs as compared to about 71 lakhs in the previous sequential quarter. Interestingly, we saw an uptick in the average daily turnover. The combined ADTO on the BSE and NSE was INR1 lakh crores, which is 15% over the sequential previous quarter.

items.statement: NSDL's incremental Demat market share improved to 15.5% in Q1 FY26 from 9.4% in Q1 FY25, a 610 bps increase
items.quote: NSDL's market share in recent terms on BO account on a run rate basis for quarter 1 stood at 15.5% and this improved compared to 9.4% incremental market share in Q1 of FY 2025, marking a 610 basis points increase on a run rate basis.

items.statement: NSDL crossed 4 crore Demat accounts as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: And again, as at June 30th, 2025, we have crossed 4 crores Demat accounts with NSDL.

items.statement: Unlisted companies admitted rose to 10,392 in Q1 FY26; equity demat market share increased to 73.2% from 70.8% a year ago
items.quote: The number of companies admitted during Q1 FY26 stood at 10,392 with our overall market share in the equity dematerialized segment increasing and reaching 73.2% compared to 70.8% in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Standalone total income grew 21.7% YoY to INR190.4 crore; operating income up 19.5% YoY to INR161 crore; PAT up 24% YoY to INR82.6 crore
items.quote: Total income for the company on a standalone basis was up by about 21.7% in quarter 1 over Y-o-Y quarter 1 of last year and came in at about INR190.4 crores, while the operating income increased by about 19.5% in quarter 1 FY26, which on a Y-o-Y basis came in at INR161 crores. Profit after tax for Q1 FY26 stood at INR82.6 crores up by about 24% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Consolidated total income fell 5% YoY to INR346.8 crore; consolidated net profit rose 15.16% YoY to INR89.63 crore
items.quote: Moving on to our consolidated financials, total income for Q1 FY26 stood at INR346.8 crores, compared to INR364.9 crores in Q1 FY25, a drop of 5%. Net profit for the quarter stood at INR89.63 crores, up from INR77.8 crores, registering a growth of 15.16% compared to the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Launched DLT-based bond covenant monitoring platform which started generating revenue in Q1 FY26; implemented common contract notes via Steady platform; launched proxy advisory on e-voting; API-based mutual fund conversion; unified investor
items.quote: Recently we launched a product called DLT, a Distributed Ledger Technology platform, which fundamentally gave bond issuers the platform for monitoring of covenants. So, this bond monitoring covenant platform never used to earn us revenue. It has started earning us revenue from this quarter onwards.

items.statement: Working capital cycle longer than peers due to unlisted business (90,000+ companies) which takes longer collection periods; business is more labor oriented
items.quote: Our business is such that some of our business has a shorter working capital and some of the businesses that we do with regards to, let's say, which are more effort that we have to take with regards to our unlisted space where that typically takes a longer period of time with regards to the working capital. That's where you would have seen when we compare, you would see ours slightly longer.

items.statement: Cash and investments of INR2,000 crore as of Q1 FY26, including INR281 crore in subsidiary/associate investments; remainder deployed in G-Secs, mutual funds, corporate bonds
items.quote: Currently, we have about INR2000 crores under investments out of which 281 is pertaining to the subsidiary investment as well as investment in associates. So the remaining is the deployable cash, which has been deployed into GSEC, mutual funds, and corporate bonds.

items.statement: Board increased dividend from 50% to 100% of face value in previous quarter as indicative gesture; no further capital allocation guidance
items.quote: Apart from the fact that the board has demonstrated its intent by increasing dividend, which was declared last quarter, from 50% on face value to 100% on face value as an indicative gesture, nothing more to report on that front at this stage.

items.statement: Common contract notes made mandatory for brokers via Steady platform; trade details upload now mandatory (was optional) attracting charges paid by brokers to NSDL; revenue impact seen in first full month
items.quote: A common contract note, one of the thing which has been made mandatory is that the broker has to upload the trade details mandatorily, which was previously optional. And trade details attract some charges which are required to be paid by the broker to the NSDL. So we definitely expect impact on the revenue and some we have already seen in the last month when it was the first full-fledged month of

items.statement: DP allocation decision rests with DPs; most DPs choose depository for investors rather than offering choice; NSDL focuses on service quality to win DP preference
items.quote: It's purely most of the DPs leave it, I mean, leave it to themselves to decide. There are a few DPs who give both the options for the investor to decide. But most of the DPs in the market take a call and based on what they want to, what they are comfortable with, they decide to split between us and the competition. That's their call actually.

items.statement: NSDL Payments Bank: 3 million customer accounts acquired; decent CASA base built; focusing on higher CASA quality customers; acquisition business added in Q1; 3-in-1 account discussions with brokers at conversation stage; subsidiaries contr
items.quote: It has built a business around, you know, through the BC partners that they have a large number of customer base, which is now in the ballpark of about 3 million. So 3 million customer accounts have been acquired, there is a decent CASA base that has been built up. So and we have also mentioned to you that we will continue to ramp up customers, but our focus really is on ramping up such customers

items.statement: Market cyclicality risk remains; cannot completely eliminate impact of market movements; diversification across 9 revenue lines helps minimize impact
items.quote: We need to appreciate that NSDL is a capital markets player and as a capital markets player, and as a regulated entity, these are the risks that remain associated with our business. And one can only look to bring about some diversification and reduce the cyclical effects and the impact of market movements. But to completely say that we would be able to completely wish away the impact of market wou

items.statement: Depreciation normalized in Q1 FY26 after accelerated depreciation in Q4 FY25 due to office move from Kamla Mills to BKC premises
items.quote: There was in a quarter 4, there was an accelerated depreciation that happened in the last quarter. And that's why you see there is a slightly uptick in the last quarter with regards to quarter 4. And now it's more of a normalized number.

items.statement: No future guidance provided on financials, tech spend, Payment Bank margins, or revenue splits; disclosures limited to standard practice for now
items.quote: We are specifically not giving out information related to EBITDA, combined us and NDML. So whatever we have, we have disclosed as part of our standard disclosures. Maybe as what Vijay mentioned, at some point in time, we will come up with disclosures that will help you to do much more analysis

items.statement: Revenue expected to grow around 50% in FY26
items.quote: We expect revenue to grow at around 50% for this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to stabilize around 19-20% from Q2 FY26
items.quote: we expect our EBITDA margins to remain around the 19% to 20% level.

items.statement: Additional capex of INR7-8 crores for capacity expansion within FY26
items.quote: So additional capex will be somewhere around INR7 crores to INR8 crores for the new additions.

items.statement: Production capacity to expand to 38,000 pieces per day within FY26
items.quote: We plan to expand our production capacity to 38,000 pieces per day.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at around 80% expected to remain stable
items.quote: We are currently at around 80% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Distributor network expanded by 8 to 194 in Q1 FY26, targeting 205 by year-end
items.quote: We have expanded our distributor network by adding eight new distributors during the quarter, increasing our total to 194.

items.statement: Launched travel wear collection, enhancing sportswear and adding infant wear categories
items.quote: We recently launched a travel wear collection, which ha s been very well received by our distributors

items.statement: EBO expansion targeting 5-6 stores in FY26, focused on Mumbai market
items.quote: we are definitely targeting around five to six EBOs for this year.

items.statement: Two existing EBOs broken even after 1.5 years, revenue ~INR800/sq ft/month
items.value: INR800 per square feet per month
items.quote: So for one of the EBOs, the revenue was around INR800 per square feet per month in one area.

items.statement: Export revenue ~4% of total, targeting 5-6% next year
items.quote: Export is somewhere around 4% for our total revenue and we expect it to grow up to 6% -- 5% to 6% in the next year.

items.statement: FirstCry contributes ~8% of revenue, own website not yet significant
items.quote: FirstCry is around 8% of our overall revenue.

items.statement: Raised INR47.5 crores via rights issue, allocated to working capital, team expansion, EBOs, B2C, product categories, embroidery and printing machines
items.quote: Recently, we have also successfully raised capital t hrough a rights issue totalling INR47.5 crores, which will be strategically allocated to support our growth initiatives

items.statement: Capex allocated for embroidery machines, printing machines, production enhancement and technology upgrade
items.quote: We're expanding our capex by adding embroidery machines to our portfolio. We are adding printing machines to our portfolio.

items.statement: Average selling price at MRP level around INR480, distributor discounts fixed rate
items.quote: Our average selling price at the MRP level is somewher e around INR480. However, our distributor discounts are fixed rate

items.statement: Gross margin impact in Q1 due to one-time sales promotion event
items.quote: So this is a onetime impact. It was a big sales promotion e vent that we did and multiple other factors

items.statement: Working capital cycle target still being finalized, to be shared next call
items.quote: That is something that we are still working around. I think we'll be able to give you a better answer at the end of next call.

items.statement: Allotted bonus equity shares in 1:1 ratio on 7th July 2025
items.quote: Also, company has allotted bonus equity share in the ratio of 1:1 to the membe rs of the company on 7th of July 2025

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue INR37.4 crores (+19% YoY), EBITDA INR5.3 crores, PAT INR2.6 crores (+8.7% YoY)
items.quote: our total revenue witnessed a remarkable increase of 19% year-on-year, reaching INR37.4 crores, up from INR31.4 crores in Q1 FY '25 while our EBITDA for the quarter was INR5.3 crores.

items.statement: Expects 10-12% annual growth in freight forwarding and LCL consolidation business
items.quote: For total transport, we have our budget in place , and we expect a steady rise of 10 % - 12% per annum for freight forwarding and LCL consolidation business.

items.statement: Expects 5-6% growth in FCL and 3-4% in LCL volumes in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We do not expect an increase of more than 5% to 6% in the full container load business and about 3% to 4% in LCL in this quarter.

items.statement: Plans 20% volume growth for Abhilaya last-mile delivery in FY26
items.quote: However, year -on-year, the volumes of Amazon go up, and we also plan to increase our volumes by about 20% in this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps to 3.0% in Q1 FY26 driven by operational efficiency
items.quote: EBITDA increased to ₹4.4 Cr from ₹1.4 Cr in Q1 FY25, with margins expanded by 200 basis points to 3 .0%, driven by operational efficiency improvements .

items.statement: Abhilaya subsidiary turned profitable with ₹13.34 lakhs net income in Q1 FY26
items.quote: A key highlight was the performance of sub sidiary One World Logistics Private Limited operating as Abhilaya, which turned profitable for the first time, posting a net income of ₹13.34 lakhs compared to losses in the prior year and preceding quarter.

items.statement: Expects Abhilaya profit to increase by ₹3-4 lakhs monthly from new Amazon warehouse contract
items.quote: This month, we have recently got a contract from Amazon for managing five of their warehouses. I do not know the actual revenue increase, but the profit will be at least three to four lakh rupees per month, additionally on this.

items.statement: LCL consolidation volumes reached 98,700+ CBMs in Q1 FY26 with 13% growth
items.quote: LCL consolidation volumes reached 98,700 plus CBMs, with imports of 40,456 CBMs and exports of 58,282 CBMs.

items.statement: Airfreight volumes improved to 368 tons in Q1 FY26 from 312 tons in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Airfreight volumes improved to 368 tons in Q1 FY26 from 312 tons in Q1 FY25, supported by increased time-sensitive export shipments.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty causing exporters to hold back shipments, reducing freight levels
items.quote: The causes of the drop in volumes or dropping trade levels are mainly because of the uncertainty of the US tariffs.

items.statement: Freight levels directly impact margins - at $2,000/container can make $150, at $800 only $30-40
items.quote: Say, for example, on a full container load, if the freight level is $2,000, I can make up to $150. But when the freight level drops to $800, my margin comes down to maybe $30, $40.

items.statement: Fuel cost moves with freight levels - when freight goes up fuel cost goes up, when freight goes down fuel cost goes down
items.quote: When the freight level comes up, then the fuel cost increase is not a problem because we overall get the benefit of that. When the freight levels are high, our profitability is high, both for LCL and FCL business. When the freight levels go down, that time even the fuel cost also goes down.

items.statement: Cargo mix significantly affects profitability - concentrated volumes at preferred ports yield higher margins
items.quote: When there is a good cargo mix, for example, I get 55 cubic meters, and my overall volume is, say 10,000 cubic meters or say 20,000 cubic meters. But if I get 20,000 cubic meters to the ports where I want, my profitability will be high.

items.statement: Secured Amazon contract for managing five warehouses in last-mile delivery
items.quote: This month, we have recently got a contract from Amazon for managing five of their warehouses.

items.statement: Targeting freight forwarders, custom house agents and global MNCs for LCL/FCL business
items.quote: We have a very aggressive sales team and we are also tapping the freight forwarders or the custom house clearing agents who are our customers and we also offer our services to some of the global MNCs for the LCL and for the FCL.

items.statement: Investing in automation, digital platforms and supply chain visibility across LCL, FCL, Airfreight and last-mile
items.quote: The company continued strengthening capabilities across LCL, FCL, Airfreight and last-mile delivery through investments in automation, digital platforms, and enhanced supply chain visibility.

items.statement: Consolidating last-mile delivery centers to increase density rather than adding new centers
items.quote: Going further, at this point of time, we do not plan to increase the number of centres that do the delivery. We are consolidating our position to ensure that we get more dense deliveries.

items.statement: PM Gati Shakti and National Logistics Policy improving efficiency and expanding capacity
items.quote: Government initiatives such as PM Gati shakti and the National Logistics Policy, along with sustained investment in road, rail and port connectivity, are improving efficiency and expanding capacity.

items.statement: Does not expect freight levels to rise in next six months due to global tariff uncertainty
items.quote: We do not expect the freight levels to go up , at least in the next six month s. But I at least expect that at least steady freight levels will help us to at least plan something.

items.statement: India logistics sector expected to grow 8-10% annually driven by express parcels, 3PL and cold chain
items.quote: Looking ahead, the sector is expected to grow at 8% to 10% annually, driven by express parcels, integrated 3PL and cold chain services, with strong fundamentals and supportive policies positioning India's logistics industry for continuous expansion.

items.statement: Revamped department, trained staff and deployed bots to improve operational efficiency
items.quote: We have revamped our department, we have trained our people to extend. We are also using bots wherever possible. And because of tha t, the efficiency has gone up , and that is being seen in the increase in profitability.

items.statement: Guided 800 COCO store openings in FY26, on track to achieve target
items.quote: Just to clarify we had earlier guided 800 stores not 900, and we remain on track. As of now, we're aligned with the 800-store mark, and we're confident of reaching close to 800 stores within this financial year.

items.statement: Guided 150-200 FOFO store openings in FY26
items.quote: Nearly 150 to 200 stores in current time.

items.statement: Expect overall business to turn strongly profitable in 12-18 months as 600-700 stores reach maturity
items.quote: For us to see a meaningful shift in profitabil ity, we believe around 600 to 700 stores need to enter that mature bracket say, 18 to 36 months old. Once that happens, the economics will change significantly, and we expect the business to turn strongly profitable. We estimate this transition will take another 12 to 18 months

items.statement: Store-level breakeven at INR 2-2.2 lakhs monthly GMV with INR 1.2 lakhs monthly expenses
items.quote: So, all together it is INR1.2 lakhs per month per store expense. And in COCO store, we have a handsome 60% gross margin. So, roughly at INR 2 to 2.2 lakhs revenue, the store comes near to breakeven.

items.statement: DavaIndia network expanded to 1,745 stores (986 COCO, 759 FOFO) as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: Our DavaIndia store network expanded to 1,745 stores nationwide as on 31 June 2025, comprising 986 COCO and 759 FOFO outlets.

items.statement: Added 163 new stores in Q1 FY26 (134 COCO, 29 FOFO)
items.quote: During this quarter, we added 163 new stores, including 134 COCO and 29 FOFO, reflecting our balanced approach of strengthening the company on infrastructure while advancing our Asset-light expansion model.

items.statement: Quarterly footfall more than doubled to 35.35 lakhs from 17.5 lakhs year-on-year
items.quote: This expansion drove a more than two-fold jump in quarterly footfall to INR35.35 lakhs versus INR17.5 lakhs last year, supported by heightened brand awareness and aggressive rollout.

items.statement: GMV grew 88% year-on-year to INR 87.78 crores
items.quote: The robust traffic translated into an 88% year-on-year GMV to INR87.78 crores, compared to INR46.58 crores in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 4.7% from loss in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA at INR4.83 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 4.7%.

items.statement: Mature COCO stores (36+ months) deliver ~30% store-level EBITDA margin; 24+ month stores at ~20%
items.quote: we currently have 29 stores that are over 36 months old, each generating an average GMV of INR6.56 lakhs per store per month. These stores deliver a store-level EBITDA margin of approximately 30%. In addition, we have 54 stores that have been operational for more than two years, and their store-level EBITDA margin is around 20%.

items.statement: Marketing expenses currently not more than 5% of total revenue, will moderately increase
items.quote: Currently, it is not more than 5% of total revenue.

items.statement: Nutra, OTC and ayurvedic contribute ~27% of revenue across store vintages
items.quote: So, what happens is that the nutra, the OTC and the ayurvedic all gives the equivalent push for the drug, which closely consumes to close to around the 27%.

items.statement: Conversion rate over 90-95% as most patients visiting are aware of generic availability
items.quote: Since this is a generic pharmacy, most patients visiting the store are already aware that they'll find generic medicines here. As a result, the conversion rate is exceptionally high. For instance, if the daily footfall is around 20 customers, nearly 19 of them end up making a purchase. This translates to a conversion ratio of over 90-95%.

items.statement: 80% repeat customer rate confirmed
items.quote: Yes. Absolutely, right!

items.statement: Mature store (36+ months) average monthly GMV INR 6.56 lakhs; 9-12 month stores at INR 2.05 lakhs
items.quote: we currently have 29 stores that are over 36 months old, each generating an average GMV of INR6.56 lakhs per store per month.

items.statement: Store maturation trajectory: Year 1 INR 2-2.25L, Year 2 INR 3-3.5L, Year 3 INR 4.5L, Year 4 INR 6L monthly GMV
items.quote: Typically, a store in its first year achieves monthly sales of around INR 2 to INR2.25 lakhs. In the second year, this increases to INR 3 to INR 3.5 lakhs. By the third year, stores reach INR4.5 lakhs per month, and in the fourth year, they go up to INR 6 lakhs per month per store.

items.statement: 9-12 month vintage stores (136 stores) at INR 2.05L monthly GMV, expected to reach breakeven INR 2.4L next quarter
items.quote: These stores are now averaging INR 2,05,000 in monthly GMV. Based on their growth trajectory, we expect them to reach breakeven INR 2,40,000 per store per month in the next quarter.

items.statement: Hyperlocal B2C model complies with state-level online pharmacy regulations
items.quote: Now, you see the regulations of the way how it's been drafted for the online business for India. It is more so to ensure that we deliver in the respective state and similar. So, our hyper local model would ensure that it not only enhances, builds efficient supply chain and robust management, but it would also increase the speed.

items.statement: DavaIndia is India's only 100% private-label generic pharmacy chain; Jan Aushadhi is government-backed competitor
items.quote: So apart from the government, there are no purely generic pharmacies in India at this level. The rest of the companies also provide branded along with generic. There are many such small companies. But purely in the generic space, Jan Aushadhi backed by Government, and apart from this, DavaIndia is the only player in 100% Private label Generic medicine in India.

items.statement: Appointed Suniel Shetty as brand ambassador; plan TV commercial and advertising campaign
items.quote: To further strengthen visibility and connect with consumers, we appointed a renewed actor and entrepreneur, Mr. Suniel Shetty, as our brand ambassador during this quarter.

items.statement: May potentially pause growth if environmental factors or unforeseen situations arise
items.quote: We are not really planning to slow down unless there are some environmental factors or unforeseen situation that comes in, which you and me don't know at this point of time.

items.statement: B2C hyperlocal delivery app launched PAN India on Android and iOS
items.quote: The platform is now launched. The B2C portal is what it is. It is also in the form of an app, both in Android and the iOS. It is available and it is full through.

items.statement: Closed 19 COCO stores lifetime (all in FY25), 6 relocated, 12-13 permanently shut; zero closures in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So far, we've closed a total of 19 stores. Out of these, 6 have been relocated to better-performing locations, while the remaining 12 to 13 stores have been permanently shut down.

items.statement: FOFO store reductions in some states due to franchisee non-compliance with terms
items.quote: So, any franchisee who does not adhere to the terms and conditions of the organization does not fit on to stay as a franchisee. And we have to be careful and cognizant about the fact, and accordingly, the decisions are taken for that.

items.statement: 5,000 stores possible in next 2-3 years per management
items.quote: Okay. So, yes, it may be possible.

items.statement: Management expects 20% ethanol blending to be achieved in FY26, ahead of the original 2030 target, with potential for 25-30% blending by 2030.
items.quote: And as far as I know, we are well on track to deliver in '25. Now when we say 20% blending, it does not mean that 20% is happening throughout the country. There are some portions, for example, in Northeast where blending is lower. But it means that in several big states up to 20% blending has been achieved. An empowered set of personnel from ministry, along with NITI Aayog, are looking at enhancin

items.statement: Capex for FY26 will be limited to rollover and maintenance capex of Rs. 40-50 crores, with no major new capex planned.
items.quote: But number two, regarding the CapEx, we are not planning to do any huge CapEx in the current year. So, hopefully, the current year CapEx will be the rollover CapEx, which are coming from last year or maybe maintenance CapEx, which will be about Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 50 crores per year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 128 bps to 17.7% in Q1 FY26, driven by Potable Spirits and Chemicals segments.
items.quote: EBITDA margins have increased to 17.7%, to be precise, to Rs. 151 crores from Rs. 128 crores. And as I mentioned, that has expanded by 128 basis points.

items.statement: Potable Spirits EBIT margin improved from 17.5% to 21.1% in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: For Potable Spirits, our EBIT margins have improved from 17.5% to 21.1%.

items.statement: Chemicals EBIT margin expanded from 9.9% to 10.9% in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: For Chemicals, our EBIT margins have expanded from 9.9% to 10.9%.

items.statement: Potable Spirits revenue grew 22.4% YoY in Q1 FY26, driven by Country Liquor and IMFL premiumization.
items.quote: In the Potable Spirits business, our revenue is up to Rs. 342 crores, up 22.4%. EBIT at Rs. 72 crores is up 47.4%, and margins are up at 21.1%.

items.statement: Performance Chemicals business targets over 150% volume-value contribution growth, focusing on oilfield chemicals, crop protection, and bio-based amines with global partners.
items.quote: Broadly speaking, we are looking at significant, kind of ballpark I am saying, so keep that in mind, in excess of 150% volume value contribution growth in that small segment.

items.statement: Paramilitary supplies business won contracts for 5 brands, ranking among top 4 suppliers out of 66 companies, with all-India supply footprint.
items.quote: It is noteworthy that out of 66 companies who tendered, less than half of them got approval, including IGL. And we are the number four company already in India. And just to mention that this is all-India supplies so it has a snowballing effect on the civil sales as well.

items.statement: Amrut partnership launched Maqintosh White Label at Rs. 850 and Black Label at Rs. 1,100, achieving over 10% market share in Delhi within first year.
items.quote: So, we have made two brands, one is Maqintosh White Label, which is at Rs. 850 and one is Maqintosh Black Label which is at Rs. 1,100. These two segments are growing, and we are able to capitalize on the growth, and we are able to get more than 10% market share. We have not even completed one year of its launch.

items.statement: Bacardi partnership manufactures 200,000 cases per month at Kashipur plant for North and East India, including RTD Breezer and premium brands.
items.quote: Just to give you a perspective, we do as many as 200,000 cases per month for Bacardi International, which is a very, very high degree of volume, considering the fact that they do all premium products.

items.statement: Ethanol pricing follows government's administrative price mechanism based on feedstock (sugarcane juice, molasses, rice, corn), ensuring balanced margins for producers.
items.quote: And it is not a completely free market kind of system because the government has come up with very well thought through administrative price mechanism. They recognize what the various feedstocks costs are. And accordingly, if you see, different prices are given for ethanol, which is produced for using different feedstocks to make sure that there is balanced growth.

items.statement: Bio-Fuel capacity utilization not explicitly stated, but management indicates no significant excess capacity in the country relative to demand.
items.quote: Now, we also keep track of overall capacities that the country has. So, the country has put up capacity but we do not have much excess capacity compared to the total demand. The market will continue to grow and people will continue to add steady capacity, but there is no huge excess capacity which will impact.

items.statement: Bio-Fuel feedstock includes sugarcane juice, C-heavy molasses, B-heavy molasses, damaged food grain rice, surplus food grain, and corn, with government-administered pricing.
items.quote: There are multiple sources which the government has allowed, which includes sugarcane juice, C-heavy molasses, B-heavy molasses, rice, which is DFG, damaged food grain rice, surplus food grain as well as corn.

items.statement: Record date fixed for 12th August 2025 for equity share subdivision (stock split).
items.quote: And as you know, 12th August 2025, has been fixed as a record date for determining the entitlements of eligible equity shareholders for the purpose of subdivision split of equity shares of the company.

items.statement: Liquor segment Q1 profit impacted by new excise policies in UP and Uttarakhand causing trade destocking in April-May; expected recovery from Q2.
items.quote: See, there were two changes that have happened in our heartland of UP and Uttarakhand, both the states underwent new policies which start from April. So, April and May, I mean, end of last year, that is from 31st March there was a lot of lifting and a lot of dumping of stocks naturally by the trade because they were not sure about the new policy.

items.statement: Ennature Biopharma plant certified as GMP with EAR and NSF approvals; planning branded nutraceuticals launch in US and Europe from Q3 FY26.
items.quote: So, for that, our plant has also been certified as GMP plant. We have got the EAR and NSF for that particular plant. So, as this quarter performs, another one quarter could be on the same line. But from the third quarter, we are having a certain planning to introduce our branded nutraceuticals in U.S. market and in European countries directly on our own.

items.statement: Country Liquor brand Bunty Bubli holds 24-25% market share in UP, with 16% share from this single brand, maintaining leadership for 3 consecutive years.
items.quote: And our size is currently approximately we are holding more than the 24% to 25% the share. And amongst the share, this brand is around 16%. So, this is undoubtedly the most favored brand in the Country Liquor segment, especially in UP.

items.statement: Management expects normal ARPOB growth of 3-7% annually for mature hospitals
items.quote: when we look at this on an annualized basis, we do see typically anywhere in the range of at least in the Medanta ecosystem, maybe 3% to 7% is our normal.

items.statement: Noida 550-bed hospital expected to be operational in coming weeks, starting with 300 beds
items.quote: We are excited about the upcoming launch of our 550-bed Medanta Noida facility, which is expected to be operational in the coming weeks.

items.statement: Ranchi 110-bed hospital operationalized in July 2025 under long-term lease
items.quote: In July 2025, we successfully operationalised our 110-bed hospital in Ranchi, further deepening our presence in the eastern region of India.

items.statement: Broader expansion pipeline includes 2,000 beds over 3-4 years, with near-term target of 1,000 beds
items.quote: Our broader expansion pipeline now includes 2,000 beds over the course of three to four years.

items.statement: Mumbai project received additional FSI approval, building plans under preparation; Pitampura building plans submitted for approval
items.quote: for example, in our Mumbai project, we have received the addit ional FSI approval that we were seeking. And that actually allows us to build the kind of beds and get the kind of scale that we are looking for

items.statement: Onboarded over 150 doctors in Q1 FY26, including 30 senior clinicians across specialties
items.quote: During the quarter, we have had on-boarded over 150 doctors, including 30 senior clinicians across specialties.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 24.3% YoY, PAT margin improved to 15.1%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR2,553 million, an increase of 23% year-on-year, with an improved EBITDA margin of 24.3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Inpatient volumes grew 14% YoY, outpatient volumes grew 13% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our inpatient volumes during the quarter increased by 14% and the outpatient volumes increased by 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: ARPOB grew 4% YoY to INR66,584 driven by Gurugram realisation increase and specialty mix change
items.quote: Average revenue per occupied bed for the quarter was INR66,584 compared to INR64,035 in the same quarter last year, an increase of 4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Mature hospital ARPOB grew 9% YoY to INR73,256 driven by Gurugram realisation and specialty mix
items.quote: ARPOB grew by 9% to INR73,256 in Q1 FY 2026, primarily driven by increase in realisation in Gurugram and change in specialty mix.

items.quote: The combination of these factors resulted in developing hospital ARPOB declining by 3% to INR56,704.

items.statement: International patient revenue grew 34% YoY to INR636 million, driven by Africa and CIS countries offsetting Bangladesh/Iraq/Afghanistan challenges
items.quote: During the quarter, revenue from international patients was INR636 million, an increase of 34% year-on-year.

items.statement: Noida Q1 FY26 costs of INR30 million (50% employee cost) with no revenue; costs to scale up in Q2
items.quote: Noida expenses of approximately INR30 million, of which 50% are attributable towards employee cost and the remaining towards other expenses, have been included in Q1 FY 2026

items.statement: Majority of 150 doctors onboarded for existing units; only 15-20 for Noida, negligible for new Ranchi unit
items.quote: the major ity of the 150 doctors is actually for our existing units. That includes almost all the units, Gurgaon, Lucknow, Patna, even some additions in Indore and Ranchi

items.quote: During the quarter, 20 beds were added on the 9th floor of Tower A at Medanta Patna Hospital, marking the completion of Tower A.

items.quote: We will possibly look at some amount of tariff hike in Gurgaon as we come into the two years from our last tariff hike, especially with respect to the insurance companies, etcetera.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions, O&M contracts, and asset-light models if they meet quality, geography, and valuation criteria
items.quote: we are very much open to acquisitions, and I will just qualify that to confirm that acquisitions of every kind of variety, the pure typical M&A which we are maybe more used to in the financial world but also acquisitions in the nature of O&M contracts, asset-light models, etcetera.

items.statement: Group ALOS at ~3 days, among best in industry; management focuses on throughput over occupancy
items.quote: if you look at our ALOS, it is amongst the best in the industry and something which we've always maintained.

items.quote: our PPP business in Patna is somewhere in the range of about 15% to 17% of our total volumes. So, to answer your question, have we reached the maximum of 25%? The answer is no.

items.quote: the margin reduction is largely the impact of the salary increments which come in typically in quarter one.

items.quote: Our ambition is not merely to grow, but to grow profitably and sustainably. We reaffirm our structural targets of RoE above 15% and RoA of 1% through the cycle.

items.statement: Expect credit expansion to outpace nominal GDP and industry growth driven by retail, government capex and green energy
items.quote: Looking ahead we expect credit expansion to outpace both nominal GDP and industry growth driven by calibrated exposure to consumption linked retail loans, government CapEx pipeline and green energy projects.

items.quote: While we still are sticking to our guidance that the cost to income ratio, our effort is to keep below 50. I am not giving any number whether it is 47, 45. The effort is through the cycle, we would like to maintain the cost to income ratio below 50.

items.quote: Recovery, yes, we had given a guidance of around ₹7,000 - 8,000 crores in recovery from AUCA, which means that ₹2,000 crores every quarter, but it is not uniformly distributed.

items.quote: • Our net NPA ratio has also declined by 10 bps YoY and stands at 0.47%. • Slippage ratio has improved by 9 basis point YoY and stands at 0.75%. • PCR was 74.49%.

items.statement: Wire rod mill to produce 700-800K tons wire rod, 300K tons TMT, 200-300K tons alloy/carbon steel bars

items.statement: Iron ore sales volume 3.45M tons in Q1 FY26, up 2% YoY and 107% QoQ

items.statement: DRI margins under pressure for next 6-8 months due to strong supply growth vs demand

items.statement: Thriveni integration underway, no new contracts won last quarter; focusing on consolidation

items.statement: Expect to collect entire $85 million MEL arrears before end of FY26
items.quote: We expect to receive the entire $85 million in arrears before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Zambia tax exemption reduced: 50% tax rate (15%) for FY26-28, 75% tax rate (22.5%) for last two years
items.quote: For the next three years, which is FY '26, FY '27 and FY '28, we will be taxed at 50% of the tax rate, which is 15%. And the last two years, we will be taxed at 75% of the tax rate, which is 22.5%.

items.statement: MEL Phase II incremental capex Rs.600 crore, bulk over next four quarters, commissioning end Q1 FY27
items.quote: It is about Rs.600 crores. And the balance works will happen over the next four quarters. We expect the bulk of that CapEx getting incurred in that period with the balance towards the commissioning phase, which is end of Q1 of FY '27.

items.statement: 100 MW solar plant commissioning by July 2026, 300 MW thermal plant by August 2026
items.quote: Yes, these are correct. That is the plan.

items.statement: Ferroalloys: better realizations from Japanese long-term contract and ferrosilicon exports to US, silico manganese realization lower YoY

items.statement: Full-year FY26 revenue growth guidance of 15-20%
items.quote: So that's correct. I think the forecast for the current year is, continues to be anywhere between 15% to 20% in terms of the top line growth.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin target of double-digit
items.quote: And for the full year we remain to maintain the forecast of a double-digit growth of total EBITDA of the company on the back of a 15% to 20% top line growth.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin target of 9.5-9.8%
items.quote: And in terms of the next, the coming quarter, we are maintaining the margin on the upward side only, in the range of, 9.5% to 9.8%, that's what we are focusing on.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 manufacturing EBITDA margin improvement of 30-50 bps
items.quote: We do maintain that I think, as Ravi mentioned, a 30 to 50 bps improvement on our EBITDA margins going into Q2.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 tooling margin guidance of 12-15%
items.quote: Yes, we are continuously maintaining that, that between a 12% to 15% margin on the tooling is what we expect in the current full year.

items.statement: SL Lumax share of profit growth estimate of 10-15% for FY26

items.statement: Order book of nearly INR 2,000 crores as of date

items.quote: Almost I would think, close to about INR50 crores to INR70 crores out of this total order book would be of new models of HMSI.

items.statement: 84% of order book is LED-based
items.quote: Importantly, 84% of our current order book is now LED based, which gives us strong visibility and confidence in further expanding this segment and increasing our market share in the quarters ahead.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 9.2%, up 10 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 9.2%, up 10 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBITDA margin improved ~100 bps YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: We've seen almost close to 100 bps expansion on the manufacturing EBITDA compared to year-on-year Q1 FY '25.

items.quote: we should be able to maintain our raw material consumption between 64% to 65.5% or so.

items.statement: No new long-term debt in FY26; scheduled repayment of INR 70-75 crores
items.quote: So, we are maintaining that in the current financial year, we are not looking at any new long-term debt. So, we will continue to pay our long-term debt as per schedule, which is somewhere around INR70 crores to INR75 crores.

items.quote: HMSI, we continue to maintain a very strong wallet share of almost more than 50%. Specifically on the front lighting, I do believe our share is anywhere between 60% to 70%.

items.statement: TVS revenue expected to double in FY26 vs FY25

items.statement: Low optimism on MG Motor due to declining volumes and low localization
items.quote: And I don't see much of optimism on MG Motors account with the company.

items.quote: So we've already got price corrections to the tune of almost INR1,3 crores in quarter 1, which was pending from quarter 4. And again, this is a recurring phenomenon in the subsequent quarters also, we continue to perhaps expect certain realizations.

items.statement: Localization efforts started showing benefit from Q1 FY26, driving raw material consumption lower

items.statement: Passenger vehicle content per vehicle ~7x two-wheeler content
items.quote: The value, the content per vehicle on a passenger vehicle for lighting is almost close to 7x that of a 2-wheeler.

items.statement: Hypercompetitive lighting market may force strategic low-margin order acceptance
items.quote: because lighting in India has a very hypercompetitive situation, there could be certain strategic calls from our competition, which kind of forces us to also take the order at a lesser margin than what we should have ideally wished for.

items.statement: Confident of achieving targets set for FY26 and FY27

items.quote: We continue to evaluate a bunch of acquisitions, both in terms of consolidation as well as backward integration. I, obviously, don't have anything specif ic to talk about as of now. But yes, that's a structural trend that you've rightly identified

items.quote: Out of the dedicated manufacturing assets that we have, our average contract tenure as of today will be between 8 and 9 years. items.statement: Domestic ethanol greenfield demand slowed due to excess capacity and no new blending mandate beyond EBP20
items.quote: The excess installed capacity has led to temporary slowdown in conversion of new inquiries into firm orders and new greenfield ethanol plants.

items.quote: Despite good inquiry basket from America, there are some delays in order bookings. Some of these are due to the tariff-related developments.

items.statement: US 45Z tax credit policy clarity is positive; 25% tariff uncertainty remains a headwind

items.statement: Ashish Gaikwad recently took over as Managing Director

items.statement: Construction expenditure Rs.39.3 crores in Q1 FY26, up 10% YoY; expected to ramp up significantly in coming quarters

items.quote: No, unless, this will have to go to the board and all that. But we expect it to get unbound in the next couple of quarters. We have not received the money back, but we expect it to happen.

By how much it's tough to say as of today.
