items.quote: in beginning only we said our EBITDA margin will be 13% to 14%, and quarterly, it will vary based on the project execution, which work we do. So that we will continue to -- we are confident that we will be able to maintain that kind of margin.

items.statement: Order book target of INR20,000-25,000 crores by end of FY26
items.quote: Our target is to increase the order book to around -- by INR25,000 crores by this year-end. So we expect another INR 8000 crores to INR10,000 crores addition in the order book.

items.statement: Debt reduction target of INR150-200 crores for FY26
items.quote: Current year, our target is to reduce around INR150 crores to INR200 crores debt. Out of that INR75 crores, we have already achieved in the first quarter itself.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 10-15%
items.quote: considering that from FY '27 onwards, we are hopeful to achieve around 10% to 15% growth going forward.

items.statement: Internal target to double revenue in next 4-5 years
items.quote: internal target is like next 4, 5 years, we want to double from here.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR16,285 crores as of June 30, 2025, excluding Teesta V project
items.quote: As of June 30 th, 2025, our order book stands at INR16,285 crores, which excludes the Teesta V Hydropower Project of around INR240 crores, for which LoA was received recently in Q2.

items.statement: Received LoAs worth INR2,250 crores in Q1 FY26 plus INR240 crores post quarter
items.quote: Thus, altogether, orders of around INR2,250 crores have been received in the first quarter. Besides these projects, recently post Q1, we have also received LoA for the Teesta V Hydropower Project from NHPC located in Sikkim, valued at INR240 crores.

items.statement: Tender pipeline of INR40,000-50,000 crores identified for bidding this year
items.quote: We currently have tenders submitted of around INR11,000 crores, which are yet under evolution and further identified projects of around INR40,000 crores to INR50,000 crores, for which bids are expected to be submitted this year.

items.statement: Expect INR8,000-10,000 crores order wins from pipeline based on 20-25% success ratio
items.quote: Next 2 to 3 quarters, we are expected to be around INR40,000 crores to INR50,000 crores of work, which mainly -- majorly hydro, civil and tunneling and irrigation only. And considering our success ratio in the past, which is 20% to 25%, so we are fairly estimating that around INR8,000 crores work we should be able to get.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 13.4% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the quarter is INR165 crores, a margin of 13.4%.

items.statement: Net profit margin at 6.09% in Q1 FY26, up from prior year
items.quote: Profit after tax has increased by around 56% and stands at INR75 crores with a margin of 6.09%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain 13-13.5%, net profit margin to improve with revenue growth
items.quote: Margins, more or less. EBITDA margin, we said it will be around 13%, 13.5%. That we should be able to maintain. And based on the growth of the turnover, and we are fairly hopeful that our net profit margin will increase.

items.statement: Total debt reduced by INR76 crores to INR1,527 crores as of June 30, 2025
items.quote: Our total debt as on 30th June '25, is INR1,527 crores, out of which working capital debt is INR981 crores and term debt is INR546 crores. The debt as on March was INR1,603 crores, that's implying a reduction of INR76 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity improved from 0.42 to 0.40
items.quote: Overall debt to equity has improved by -- from 0.42 in March to 0.40 in 30th June.

items.statement: Finance cost reduced from INR84 crores to INR73 crores year-on-year
items.quote: The finance cost has accordingly reduced from INR84 crores to INR73 crores in this quarter, compared to Q1 last year.

items.statement: Interest rate on debt between 11-11.5%, expected to decrease further
items.quote: See interest expense currently is between11% and11.5% , so -- and it may go lower also. Right now, we are looking at talking to all lenders to get the interest rates going down.

items.statement: Credit rating improved from BBB+ to A-
items.quote: Our rating also has improved from BBB minus to A minus -- BBB plus to A minus now.

items.statement: Net working capital days at 168 days, adjusted to 110 days excluding land, arbitration claims and cash
items.quote: The net working capital days is almost similar at around 168 days. And after adjusting of land, arbitration claims and in cash and bank balances, the net working capital is around 110 days.

items.statement: Expect working capital improvement trend to continue with faster government payments
items.quote: as we are achieving the turnover, as I mentioned, that government also has taken various steps to release the payments fast and everything, so yes, yes, we are hopeful that this trend will continue.

items.statement: Book-to-bill ratio at 3.3x providing strong revenue visibility
items.quote: Our book-to-bill ratio currently stands at around 3.3, providing strong revenue visibility.

items.statement: Indus Water Treaty suspension accelerating hydro project clearances and tendering
items.quote: with the suspension of the Indus water treaty, we are now witnessing a significant acceleration and execution and tendering of several long-stalled projects.

items.statement: Government not issuing approvals until 90-100% land acquisition completed, reducing execution risk
items.quote: Unless and until land acquisition is done 90% to 100%, they are not issuing the So we have overcome this risk. So going forward, we see that there will not be unnecessary delay in execution of the project because government is also proactive resolving all issues -- timely resolving all of our issues.

items.statement: Only 4-5 major players in hydro segment, limited competition supports margins
items.quote: There are many less players in hydro, 4 or 5 only maximum. And there are a number of projects coming in. So each person would get their own share of projects. So we don't see a challenge there.

items.statement: Order book mix: 61% hydro, 20% irrigation, 7% tunneling, 12% urban infra and others
items.quote: Out of this, 61% of the order book comprises hydropower projects, around 20% is irrigation, 7% tunneling and the remaining 12% from urban infra and other segments.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 55% hydro, 19% tunneling, 19% irrigation, 7% roads and others
items.quote: Sector-wise revenue breakup, hydro is 55%, tunneling is 19%, irrigation is also 19% and roads and others are 7%.

items.statement: Implemented SAP across all projects, using IoT and digital platforms for efficiency
items.quote: See, we have implemented SAP across all projects. We are also using IoT and other available digital platforms to improve the efficiency.

items.statement: Arbitration claims of INR3,000 crores expected to recover 50-60% over 5-7 years
items.quote: We have arbitral claims and awards of combined around INR3,000 crores, so this is all -- when we get awards, we get with the interest and also, we expect -- even if you consider 50%, 60% of this value coming in, with interest, the number will be much higher.

items.statement: No major execution delays or cost escalation issues; cost escalation is pass-through in contracts
items.quote: So there are no major delays anywhere. And cost escalation whatever is there, it is a pass-through for us in terms of contracts.

items.statement: Expect INR150-200 crores from arbitration awards and land monetization in FY26
items.quote: Yes, we are expected to have around INR150 crores to INR200 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: Promoter pledge at 85%, expected to reduce significantly as discussions with lenders begin
items.quote: The promoter pledge is expected to come down eventually. Right now, our rating is A minus, and numbers are all are good. So now we'll start talking to the lenders to reduce the pledge.

items.statement: Added 10 new client accounts in Q1 FY26
items.quote: This momentum was supported by the addition of 10 new client accounts, improved margins, and greater operational efficiency, even as we continue to invest in retaining key talent and strengthening our strategic capabilities.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 7.2% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA was ¥6.61 crores, up 61.1% from last quarter and 18% from last year, with margins improving 7.2%.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 14.2% in Q1 FY26 from 5% last quarter
items.quote: Margins improved to 14.2% from 5% last quarter due to better utilization and tighter cost control.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by decline in other expenses and lower ESOP costs
items.quote: So, there is a sharp decline in other expenses, that contributed to that margin. Last quarter, it is %166 lakh, other expenses, so now it is 122 lakhs. And ESOP expenses also, last quarter, we booked ¥154 lakhs, now this quarter, Z60 lakhs only.

items.statement: Aiming for margin enhancement as utilization improves, attrition stabilizes, and hiring remains disciplined
items.quote: Looking forward, we are aiming for margin enhancement as utilization improves, attrition levels stabilize, and hiring remains disciplined.

items.statement: Network Objects became a subsidiary, adding $22M revenue; 51% profit share to XTGlobal
items.quote: Now, that has become subsidiary to XTGlobal Infotech Limited. It is also an US company. So, since it has become a subsidiary, we have to add the top line as well. So, that revenue is also added. That is one of the factors for that drastic increase in the top line

items.statement: Actively looking for acquisitions in Europe, Australia, and India to grow top and bottom line
items.quote: definitely looking in other countries like Europe and other Australia, and other things when we find the right company at the right price tag. And within India also, we are looking at the right 10 Q1 FY26 Eamings Conference Call Transcript XT GLOBAL) companies to acquire, to grow our revenue top line as well as bottom line

items.statement: Won Texas Department of Transportation contract; expanding into US government sector
items.quote: We were able to win this good contract. And we are actually in the toll industry, supporting toll clients. So, the windage, what we got is the Texas Department of Transportation division.

items.statement: Won $5M+ blanket PO for 5-year US IT modernization project; work started Monday
items.quote: In our contract, particularly, they have shown $5 plus million dollars or whatever that amount we shared on the news release, right? As part of a blanket PO with the first win just happening last week, which we shared, and then the actual work has started this Monday, 2 days back.

items.statement: Submitted $1M+ AI RFP response to existing customer; expect small AI wins in 8-12 months
items.quote: as we speak last, this Monday itself, we submitted over a million dollar plus AI RFP response to an existing customer that we believe that there are chances of winning, as well as we believe that this AI, over a period of next 12

items.statement: Strong deal pipeline in cloud services, automation, AI-driven solutions, and US finance offshoring
items.quote: Our strong deal pipeline is concentrated in high-potential areas such as cloud services, automation, and AlI-driven solutions. We also see meaningful growth potential in the offshoring of finance and accounting roles from US companies.

items.statement: Most clients on 3-year contracts with very low attrition; revenue is sustainable quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: We sign most of our accounts that we are signing services with, we sign a 3-year contract, but we only recognize when we do get the revenue. So that is what you see, but most of our accounts are long-term in nature.

items.statement: Minimal impact from US H-1B policy changes as business model shifted to offshore delivery since 2016-18
items.quote: Our revenue has last started in 2016 - 18 timeframe, where our focus has been mostly with less dependency on the H-1B or visa-related opportunities. So, right now, when you look at it, our revenue in that segment is very less, and we have a very less number of employees who are actually dependent on that.

items.statement: Strengthened on-site sales team for government sector; increased consolidated expenditure
items.quote: We have already strengthened our on-site sales team to approach different government sectors and also to back these big contracts. So, we are focusing. And that increased expenditure in the consolidated to that extent is increased in that sales force.

items.statement: Appointed senior executive to lead AI practice; investing in specialized talent retention
items.quote: We have hired and appointed one of our senior executives to lead our AI team. And, in fact, right, we are actually submitting quite a few responses in RFP for the Al-related projects, which we expect to win in the near future.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 87% YoY to ₹92.30 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Revenue came in at ¥92.30 crores, up 6% from Z87.04 crores in the previous quarter, and 87.2% higher than ¥49.30 crores a year ago.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT nearly tripled QoQ to ₹3.73 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Net PAT reached Z3.73 crores, almost triple the last quarter, and 72.4% higher than last year.

items.statement: Guidance unchanged: high single-digit growth and EBITDA expansion of 1-1.5%
items.value: high single digit growth and EBITDA expansion of about a 1%, 1.5%
items.quote: Our guidance, we are not changing the guidance. We are still guiding for high single digit growth and EBITDA expansion of about a 1%, 1.5% and we are very, very confident of the EBITDA expansion, if we have a better capacity utilization .

items.statement: Domestic demand under pressure but not declining further; exports trending lower at Rs 16,000-17,000 crore industry level
items.quote: So, the demand has not further gone down. It is under pressure. We have grown , even in July, we have grown. So, from that perspective, I would not say that demand is further muted in India.

items.statement: Operating margins mildly impacted by low capacity utilization; gross margin up 3.2% QoQ, down 1.8% YoY; confident of 0.5-1% margin improvement with better utilization
items.quote: Operating margins are mildly impacted due to reduced capacity utilization. Gross margin increased by 3.2% in Q1 quarter-on-quarter and it declined 1.8% Y-o-Y, largely I would think it is flat.

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization fell to 77% from 81%; standalone at 72%; Max plant at 51-52%; sanitaryware kiln back to 100%; expect significant improvement in H2
items.quote: console capacity utilization reduced from 81% to 77%. There were three plants which were underutilized. One was the Max plant with high end tiles. We have been extremely patient to make sure that that plant only produces high end tiles currently.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 50 crore for Max plant upgrades (presses, balancing equipment, warehouse) to improve utilization; maintenance capex unchanged from last year
items.quote: We have taken approval from the board of Rs. 50 crores, it is not that we are going to spend the entire amount. It is an approval which has been taken. This has been taken to further augments, Max, to make sure that I am running at full capacity.

items.statement: Net dealer addition of ~65 in Q1; targeting 200-250 net additions for FY26, focused on Tier-II/III towns
items.quote: We are at 65 dealer additions and we will be adding approximately 200 - 250 net additions of dealers. And we have targets for that as to what our net addition of dealers will yield us in terms of sales.

items.statement: Ceramic 34% (down 1% YoY), PBT 26% (down 2%), GVT 40% (up from 37%); realization dip due to mix, not price cuts; small price increase taken in July
items.quote: As far as the tile segment revenue is concerned, ceramic consisted of 34%, down 1% from last year same quarter Y-o-Y. PBT is at 26%, down 2% and GVT is up 40% up from 37%.

items.statement: JV with Durabuild concluded; go-to-market in September for waterproofing; targeting Rs 11,000-12,000 crore market (waterproofing + admixtures); option to buy up to 75% then 100% in 3-4 years
items.quote: We have concluded the JV with Durabuild. That is a starting, the go to market will be next month. We are concentrating on all the waterproofing products currently. And then we will move to other patents and other IPs which Durabuild has to offer.

items.statement: Industry exports declined to Rs 18,000 crore last year, trending to Rs 16,000-17,000 crore this year; Morbi tax evasion at peak, 70-80 plants shut, more closures expected
items.quote: As far as export is concerned, current trends are showing that it will be in that same Rs. 17,000 crores - Rs. 18,000 crore range. But the kind of quality which is being compromised from Morbi is really not competing with us anymore.

items.statement: B2C 77%, B2B 23%; aiming to increase B2B by 5-6% for utilization but cautious on receivables; retail expansion in Tier-II/III towns
items.quote: It is the same. It is about 77 % percent is B2C and the rest is B2B. And all efforts are on to see how we can increase the B2B by at least 5 % - 6% percent so that we are able to use capacity utilization.

items.statement: Not competing on price; focused on value addition and innovation; market share gains from consolidation of tax-evading Morbi players; 70-80 plants already shut
items.quote: Market share cannot be gained beyond the point with just reduction in prices. That is a knee jerk. It happens for a quarter or two and then you are back to square one. So, that is my answer on the market share. And I do not need to fortify myself.

items.statement: Max plant loss ~Rs 6.5 crore in Q1; expected to reduce significantly and disappear next year; sanitaryware kiln shutdown resolved
items.quote: Yes. Approximately Rs. 6.5 crores has been the loss from the Max plant. We are going to reduce this loss significantly. And that is, yes, that is been the impact on profitability, which over age two will reduce and next year would probably be not there.

items.statement: Employee costs flat despite increments; not filling some attrition gaps, extending responsibilities; travel costs being optimized via videoconferencing
items.quote: We have given increments. Unlike some of the people who have given non increments, we have given increments, but we have been very, very cautious of that. And touchwood, our team also, has been very, very cooperative on that front.

items.statement: Morbi players surviving on large-scale GST evasion (billing at Rs 10-11/sq ft); evasion peaked, no further scope; driving industry consolidation
items.quote: And frankly, Morbi is only and only surviving. Most of the Morbi brands, I obviously do not mean the industry leaders from Morbi, but 95% of the brands in Morbi are only surviving because of extremely high scale evasion of taxes, of GST.

items.statement: Export demand uncertain; monsoon impact on Q2; B2B receivables risk; Max plant turnaround execution risk; Durabuild JV build-out pressures in years 1-2
items.quote: Q2 is already looking slightly better. Although there is been incessant rains across north , but still it is slightly better than last year, July was. August is yet to be seen. It is early days in August.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guided at INR75-80 crores
items.quote: This year, we will be doing around INR75-80 crores.

items.statement: Base business EBITDA margin guided around 15% for FY26
items.quote: For the base business at the EBITDA level, we should be around 15-odd percent.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve in FY27 as new products mature
items.quote: So what we see is the first batch of products will turn matur e in, say, FY '27. So , we see the EBITDA margins to improve in that year

items.statement: Capex for FY26 remains as previously disclosed; FY27 too early to comment
items.quote: And as far as the whole year FY '26, the numbers would remain as disclosed in the previous quarter and FY '27 would be too early to comment as of today.

items.statement: Pune plant commercial license expected this month; commercial production by end of month or first week of September
items.quote: We are expecting the commercial license in this month itself, and the commercial production will start by the end of this month or the first week of September.

items.statement: SPL Infusion plant expected to start this month and ramp to 65-70% capacity in first year
items.quote: We see the plant starting and ramping up to 65% to 70% capacity in the first year.

items.statement: CDMO business order book supports 20% growth this year
items.quote: Yes, what we did last year, 20% minimum.

items.statement: Underlying demand intact; logistics easing; Q1 lean quarter, pickup expected in Q2-Q4
items.quote: However, the underlying demand remains intact and the logistical situation is already showing signs of easing.

items.statement: Q1 injectable revenue drop due to order lumpiness; Q3 and Q4 historically stronger
items.quote: As you know, the total size of the company's revenue is not that large. It is just order lumpiness. This quarter, it has dropped. The next quarter, it will pick up.

items.statement: Eight new products added in Q1 and Q2 combined
items.quote: In Q1 and Q2, both put together, we have added around eight products.

items.statement: Injectable share reduced to 50% from 70% YoY as oral solids scaled for top-line growth
items.quote: So, you're seeing only from the mix perspective, but you see our revenue is also growing. We have to grow the top line of the company. So, oral solids are much simpler to enter the market with, and then we pitch the injectables to our customers.

items.statement: LATAM region is growth driver for current and next year; Africa registrations pending
items.quote: Currently, for this year and the next year, LATAM is going to be the growth driver for the company.

items.statement: Rank in top 8-10 injectable players in Latin American markets
items.quote: In Latin American markets, we have a healthy share of the market in the injectable space. It is not product-specific, but dosage form-specific. In injectables, we would rank in the top 8, top 10 players in those markets.

items.statement: Gross margin declined due to market pressure; offset by controlling other expenses
items.quote: Due to this, we had to face a little decline in the gross margins. However, we made up the gap by controlling our other expenses. So all in all, we stood at a stable level.

items.statement: Logistics issues: container shortage, vessel diversion via Red Sea, Chinese carrier choke, Middle East tensions
items.quote: What we experienced when shipping products to Latin America was a lack of container availability. And this might have happened due to the ship shortage -- the vessel shortage that is heading in that direction. Secondly, we feel that there is some kind of choke that the Chinese carriers also create. And in the Middle East area, where we ship our product, the Iranian aspect has affected the movement

items.statement: Pune plant delay due to Government of India's new GMP and revised Schedule M guidelines
items.quote: And this takes time because of the Government of India's new guideline on GMP and Schedule M revised has come into effect. And that is the reason for the delay in this.

items.statement: Export-domestic mix 73.7% to 26.3% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The export-domestic mix was 73.7% to 26.3%.

items.statement: Trade receivables in range of INR8 crores
items.quote: The current trade receivables are in the range of INR8 crores.

items.statement: Current debt levels INR6 crores, down from INR8 crores last quarter due to working capital repayments
items.quote: So the current debt levels are INR6 crores as of now.

items.statement: PAT flat YoY at INR1.7 crores due to higher depreciation and interest expense
items.quote: Profit after tax was at INR1.7 crores, flat year-on-year basis due to higher depreciation and interest expense.

items.statement: Depreciation up 13% YoY due to recent capex; steady going forward unless major new capex
items.quote: Yes. So whatever capex we had done recently, the depreciation on those has kicked in the current quarter. So this would be a steady number going forward, unless there is another major capex, which we do.

items.statement: Prague JV small order processing started; income expected in Q4 FY26 (December year-end)
items.quote: Regarding the Prague JV, we have already started the small order processing has already started. Commercialization is on. And since it's Europe, a lot of restrictions are there due to the geopolitical situation, but things will be improving within a month's time, and those will be reported once the year ends in December for the European markets.

items.statement: Dividend declared for first time in company history in Q4 FY25
items.quote: During the last quarter of FY '25, the company successfully declared a dividend for the first time in its history.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East and Red Sea disrupting shipping routes and increasing costs
items.quote: Geopolitical tensions, especially in parts of the Middle East, directly impacted major shipping corridors. The security situation in Red Sea continued to disrupt the Suez Canal route, a key artery for moving goods between Asia, Africa and Europe.

items.statement: Revenue growth 8.9% YoY to INR17.9 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The company reported a revenue of INR17.9 crores and a growth of 8.9 % year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Q1 revenue subdued due to slow order intake in FY25; deals shifted across quarters due to budgetary and geopolitical reasons
items.quote: Our Q1 results are subdued from a top-line perspective. Our business has always been H2 heavy, but one of the key reasons for muted Q1 is that there was slow order intake in the last financial year.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA INR 43M vs INR 53M previous quarter; Normalized PAT INR 128M vs negative INR 6.6M previous quarter
items.quote: Normalized EBITDA for the quarter is at INR 43 million as against INR 53 million for the previous quarter. Normalized PAT for the quarter is at INR 128 million as against negative INR 6.6 million for the previous quarter.

items.statement: Launched FraudZap lightweight AI fraud detection platform for Tier-3 telcos and MVNOs; HyperSense platform now GenAI enabled with investigative agents in POCs
items.quote: We recently launched FraudZap, a lightweight AI -powered fraud -detection platform. This product is mainly targeted to Tier-3 telcos and MVNO and customers with specific single use case requirement.

items.statement: Device fraud market size $2-3 billion growing at ~18% CAGR; three Tier-1 commercial engagements for handset fraud product
items.quote: So market size, the device fraud itself will be in the $2 billion to $3 billion range. But I think amongst the overall fraud, this is growing at about almost 18% CAGR or so.

items.statement: Group DSO holding around 98-100 days; working capital framework remains same; Middle East entity funding for contract viability
items.quote: The working capital cycle will remain same in the sense group working capital is holding around 90, DSO as such is holding around 98-100 days around.

items.statement: Proposing INR 35 crore investment in Subex Middle East subsidiary to make net worth positive for contracting eligibility
items.quote: Yeah. So, this side Sumit here, you're bang-on on that, positive to just make this capitalize that entity because there are certain orders coming to that entity. And it has to be net-worth positive.

items.statement: Marketing head replaced with Poonam Wadhwa from Comviva/Tech Mahindra; long-tenured employee Suraj left; revamping sales team per shareholder feedback
items.quote: So, this is also our effort to see if we can bring people from outside and bring people who come from, I would say, related industries, but not exactly, people who are really doing the same thing.

items.statement: Increasing margin pressure with customers extending RFP negotiations to 4-5 BAPO rounds vs typical 1-2, elongating decision cycles by weeks
items.quote: Now, more and more, I'm seeing that in deals, people are going to four or five BAPOs. But what that does is that it keeps elongating the decision time.

items.statement: Currency challenges in some geographies where countries lack hard currency reserves; shying away from deals with currency risk
items.quote: What that means is that I have the deal, but there might be currency challenge because t hat country may not have USD or that country may not have euros or USD or fixed currencies to give us in hard currency

items.statement: Consolidated Bengaluru office from two floors to one; lease termination gain of INR 2.6 crore recognized in other income
items.quote: So, we used to own two floors to that office. So, one floor, we have given up. For that, we got some lease termination gain. Okay? That is, again, rooted to our P&L. So, INR 2.6 crore is towards that.

items.statement: No specific numerical guidance given; management expects to make up Q1 shortfall in subsequent quarters as order booking returns on track
items.quote: We also have a strong pipeline, which gives me confidence that we shall make up for the shortfall in subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Telco sector growing only ~2% globally; elongated sales cycles (9-12 months); currency and margin pressures impacting deal closures
items.quote: They're only growing from I would say about 2% globally. So, it's not that telcos themselves have high growth right now. So, telcos themselves have quite a bit of challenges at their end.

items.statement: Recognized as front-runner in TM Forum Catalyst project 'Quality of Trust: Eliminating Spam and Enabling Growth' at DTW Ignite Copenhagen
items.quote: This is where our catalyst project, so we had participated in a catalyst project and it was called Quality of Trust: Eliminating Spam and Enabling Growth. So this was well received, and we were recognized as one of the front runners in this.

items.statement: Sectrio: first contract provided for last quarter, recovery ongoing; second contract in active negotiations for exit; employee count reduced from 57 to 2
items.quote: first one we provided for last quarter, and we continue to try and recover that amount. So, that track is ongoing. The second contract, again, we don't have any exposure there per se, but what we are trying to do is exit that contract

items.statement: Cash position significantly stronger due to sharper working capital management and one-time income gains; INR 135 crore in fixed deposits and safe assets
items.quote: And our cash position, you have seen it. It's significantly stronger, thanks to sharper working capital management and one -time income gains.

items.statement: Five to six deals spilled over from Q1 to Q2, including one or two significant deals awaiting final administrative formalities.
items.quote: The number of deals, if I were to speak in terms of numbers, I would say it's about five or six, thereabouts.

items.statement: Sectrio contract recovery is underway with legal process initiated in a foreign jurisdiction; timeline uncertain.
items.quote: We have sent multiple reminders. There is a legal firm also involved. So, there is a process that we are following. And should it come down to that, there might be a lawsuit.

items.statement: Core telco business churn is low at around 2%; revenue decline driven by loss of managed services contracts to in-house customer teams, not competitors.
items.quote: Our churn is quite low. It's around 2% or so. It's not more than that. So, it's not like we have churned a lot of customers, but, yes, you are right. We have lost some along the way.

items.statement: Shift from license-based to subscription pricing model for HyperSense caused revenue cannibalization and contributed to three-year revenue decline.
items.quote: HyperSense's entire pricing was a subscription led whereby customer has to pay an implementation component, and then whatever the license and the AMC is factor as a part of our subscription.

items.statement: R&D spend is approximately 15% of revenue annualized; setting up a fraud innovation lab likely outside India.
items.quote: Annualized, we do 15% or so, and we are also naturally setting up an innovation app specifically for fraud.

items.statement: Adjacencies like telco fintech, wallets, and device commerce are active in revenue mix; FraudZap and AI agents deployed in Tier-1 telcos with gain-share models.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 448 crores, cash Rs 87 crores, net debt Rs 361 crores, net debt-to-equity 0.4x; repaid Rs 62 crores in Q1
items.quote: Yes, we have repaid close to Rs. 60 crores of debt from March onwards till June. That is part of the normal procedural aggressive debt repayment policy that we adopt. So, we have repaid close to Rs. 62 crores of debt in the first quarter of the financial year.

items.statement: Did not bid for BMC Deonar bio-mining project due to stringent technical qualifications (18.5M tons in 3-4 years) and sub-optimal pricing
items.quote: So, the contract specifications were too stringent, one. Second is, we technically didn't qualify because one of the main conditions is the Company should have handled 18.5 million tons of waste in 3-4 years, which we have not done.

items.statement: Ground staff strength ~10,300+; continued investment in skilled workforce
items.quote: Our ground staff strength totaled around 10,300 plus, underscoring our continued investment in a skilled workforce to drive operational excellence and advance our sustainability goals.

items.statement: EPR credits monetized: 20% of first-year allocation of 94,400 metric tons at PCMC WTE; material at operating company level
items.quote: With the PCMC -WTE project registered to qualify for EPR credits, we have monetized 20% of the first-year allocation of over 94,400 metric tons.

items.statement: Auto scrapping and tyre recycling under consideration but slower pace due to market maturity and margin profile
items.quote: We have already been given a market study report; we have started scouting the areas and the management view that we would like to go slightly slower given the market maturity at this point of time.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected in early teens if US tariff uncertainty persists; mid-teens if resolved. FY27 higher growth expected.
items.quote: if not, then my top line may be having a marginal impact and we would be what you say early teen growth kind of thing in this fiscal 26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 is 21-22% excluding other income; 23-24% gross EBITDA.
items.quote: Without other income, it would be in the range of 21 to 22 percent.

items.statement: Monthly order book at Rs 110-120 crore; auto components Rs 60-65 crore, bearing rings Rs 45-50 crore.
items.quote: as of now, what we can have an order book broadly in the range of 110 to 120 crore on a monthly basis, wherein you can say some almost 60 to 65 crore rupees is towards the auto components and 45 to 50 crores is for the bearing rings.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 guided at Rs 30-35 crore; Rs 16-18 crore spent in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: This year in totality for fiscal 26, if I tell you, it will be in the range of 30 to 35 crores.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization at 62-64%; auto components at 75-80%; adding forging lines for high-volume products.
items.quote: Overall, we are at the range of 62 to 64 percentage of utilization.

items.statement: Domestic auto components grew 20% YoY in Q1; domestic bearing rings up 5-6% YoY; export bearing rings subdued due to industrial demand weakness.
items.quote: Same way in auto components. Let me tell you, this quarter, March 20, sorry, June 25, we recorded 53 crore of revenue, which was in last June 24, it was 46 crore. Again, almost a jump of 20% in domestic auto components.

items.statement: US revenue share 25%; Europe at 20% in last 4 months (up from 14-16%); 30% of new orders from US currently on hold due to tariff uncertainty.
items.quote: Today, as of date, we have almost 25% of our revenue. It is from the USA, 20 odd percentage something from the Europe.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA Rs 77 crore (26.5% with other income); operating EBITDA margin 23-24%; PAT Rs 49 crore.
items.quote: we have recorded 77 crore rupees of EBITDA for this first quarter, which was 22% in the previous quarter and it was 24.6% corresponding quarter of previous fiscal.

items.statement: First incremental US tariff adjusted and accepted by customers; final tariff outcome awaited by end of month.
items.quote: The first incremental tariff it has already been adjusted and the customers have accepted that it has and we are going to get the implemented tariff at the end realization at Rolex level.

items.statement: New programs 50% for Europe; US customers holding orders but not diverting; domestic top 3 bearing customers expanding capacity.
items.quote: One thing I want to add that new program which we have been nominated are 50% for Europe only.

items.statement: USMCA rules may exempt products with <40% import content; China 30% duty, Mexico/Canada 35% duty makes switching suppliers difficult.
items.quote: Suppose we are supplying semi-finished component and it is used in gearbox. For the complete gearbox, if the content of import is only 40%, then this tariff will not be applicable.

items.statement: Net debt negative; surplus funds in FDs; CDR settlement of Rs 50.6 crore provided, Rs 227 crore claimed by lenders, resolution expected by end of Q2 FY26.
items.quote: we have provided the maximum as per our view, which is 50.6 crore. And which is mentioned in our CDR approval letter also that has been provided.

items.statement: Revenue split: bearing rings 46%, auto components 54%; exports 47%, domestic 53%; passenger vehicles 50%, industrial 16.5%.
items.quote: In terms of revenue bifurcation, we have recorded bearing rings contributed almost 46% of our revenue and the auto components is growing and it has reached to 54% in this first quarter.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty may defer 25-30% of new orders; bearing ring export demand weak in Europe industrial segment; EV transition traction not visible.
items.quote: if this thing settled down positively, we do not foresee any kind of problem as far as to getting these numbers. But if not, then marginally we would be on the lower side compared to our overall expectation of 15-16% growth.

items.statement: Auto components driving growth; bearing rings suppressed in industrial/infrastructure but stable in auto applications; EV/hybrid share unchanged.
items.quote: Our growth as of now, it is auto driven, auto component driven only. And we expect that bearing ring business, which has been suppressed, but down the line couple of quarters, it will gradually improve.

items.statement: Cash flows averaging Rs 225 crore annually for last 3 years; strong liquidity with surplus investments.
items.quote: Company has good sound cash flows averaging almost 225 crore rupees of cash flow on year on year basis for last three years.

items.statement: Signed Off-White franchise agreement for apparel, footwear and accessories; plans 5 COCO stores in 2-3 years starting Jan 2026
items.quote: We signed a good brand, a marquee brand in our portfolio, which had promised that we would be signing a few brands in this year. So first quarter, we've signed Off-White, a very, very proud moment for us because it is a very marquee brand recognised for its streetwear fashion into the luxury space, and that marks our foray into the luxury space.

items.statement: Launched Juicy Couture in Q1 FY26; response very encouraging both online and offline
items.quote: Then in terms of, again, new brands, we launched Juicy Couture, primarily the launch campaign and everything happened in this quarter. So we've launched Juicy Couture, which we had signed last year. And Touchwood, I'm happy to say that the response that we are getting in Juicy Couture as a brand is very, very encouraging.

items.statement: Hard luggage manufacturing facility trials successful; full production commenced July 2025 at 50-60% utilisation, targeting 20,000+ units/month by next month
items.quote: Then Q1 also marked the successful trial of the hard luggage manufacturing facility. So all trials were successful, even the lab for our quality control, that also is completely functional, fully operational, and we have a state-of-the-art facility even for our internal quality control.

items.statement: Revenue declined in April-May; June contributed >40% of Q1 sales with growth vs prior year; July also growing; expect recovery from Q2
items.quote: And hence, in the month of June, we said we will also have to rationalise our pricing. And from June onwards, we've rationalised our pricing. We've corrected certain prices in the market, and we've started seeing an uptick. We've started seeing -- in fact, just to share a figure that June alone contributed to more than 40% of the entire quarter sales, right?

items.statement: Rationalised pricing in June after 1.5-2 years of competitor predatory pricing; price cuts of 10-20% on existing models; new normal pricing accepted
items.quote: So from ₹23,500, we now have models starting at ₹18,000 even in the off-line, right? In terms of online, we are now available at ₹14,500, ₹15,000, ₹15,500. We are also populating models at ₹19,000, ₹22,000.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 4%; exit margin target 10% by Q3 FY26; manufacturing expected to offset margin pressure in 6-9 months
items.quote: I think for the full year, I wouldn't be able to comment right now. I'll be definitely working towards it. But exit, yes, 10% for sure. Probably we should be able to hit that in Q3 itself.

items.statement: In-house luggage manufacturing yields ~27% gross margin improvement vs outsourced; targeting >15% improvement sustainably
items.quote: So from a gross margin perspective, for example, one of the programmes that we shifted to our factory we saw almost 27%, 28% betterment in terms of margin from another factory that we were buying.

items.statement: Ordered PP machine for polypropylene luggage manufacturing; expected operational in few months
items.quote: PC is the one that I told you about that we've done the successful trial everything. We've already ordered a PP machine also. So we sort of very soon, another few months, and I'm very hopeful that we should be able to start PP manufacturing as well.

items.statement: Backpack manufacturing backward integration operational; supply chain improved driving >50% volume and value growth in Backpacks
items.quote: Having said that, if I remove trolleys luggage per se from the picture, we also see that we have grown in all other categories, including One Hero which has come out is probably Backpack with manufacturing coming as a backward integration, our supply chain improved.

items.statement: Institutional business degrew ~₹10 crore in Q1; Q2 showing positive uptake with deliveries started in July
items.quote: And if I can quote figures, the degrowth is almost of INR 10 crores. So if I take that off, in our retail channels, we've grown, right?

items.statement: Marketplace e-commerce recorded highest ever sales in July 2025
items.quote: Last month, July is the month that I'm quoting, we've done the highest ever in our marketplace business. So it's really been a good, good month for us.

items.statement: Traditional trade (distribution) reeling under pressure; modern trade, e-commerce and own stores growing; EBO like-to-like growth ~12% in Q1
items.quote: See distribution, which is the traditional trade, as I said, it still continues to, because these are small mom-and-pop stores, we were sort of making a very, very good headway. But with this kind of a pricing, it is very difficult for us to sort of sustain that.

items.statement: Plan to open 15-20 stores in FY26 (total 60-65); focus on marquee COCO locations; new 1,200 sq ft Bagline identity store opening end of August; 2,000 sq ft flagship planned
items.quote: I think we should be able to cross 60-plus store mark, between 60, 65. So attempting to open about 15 to 20 stores within this year.

items.statement: Employee cost ₹12 crore/quarter run-rate expected to remain flat for FY26; major hiring done for manufacturing, new brands and stores
items.quote: Yes. So a few people here and there, but majorly, our team is in place now. And I think, yeah, INR 12 crores a quarter, I think you can safely assume that it's going to remain in this sort of vicinity.

items.statement: Marketing spend increased in Q1; will continue investing despite margin pressure; green shoots visible
items.quote: See, we have, in Q1 also, we have expanded our marketing. And we are seeing green shoots of marketing also, Resha. So see, as a company, I think marketing is something that I would say that you don't have a choice of not spending over there, right?

items.statement: In-house production cost ~₹5,000-8,000 per 3-piece set vs ₹8,000 realisation; royalty ~10-12%; target EBITDA 13-14% at scale
items.quote: 13%, 14% of EBITDA asset.

items.statement: VIP Industries acquisition by new management seen as positive for industry; course correction on pricing would benefit Brand Concepts most
items.quote: I think with VIP's acquisition and I think it's a good news for the industry overall because now they'll be on a path to reset the brand, they'll be on a path to course correct, right?

items.statement: Aeropostale underperforming; one more attempt online then may exit; Off-White luxury brand signed for 5 COCO stores in 2-3 years
items.quote: Aeropostale, to be honest, we've not been able to crack. It's not a brand that has done well for us. The contribution and everything is also really minuscule. So, Aeropostale is something that we're going to take one more attempt.

items.statement: Expect return to growth trajectory from Q2 FY26; annualised growth target ~20% to drive EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: So if we are able to for example, this year, from a 270, if we are able to grow at annualised, if I say that if we cross a 20% kind of a growth, you will start seeing those kind of numbers happening in the bottom line.

items.statement: Premium luggage demand weak due to low brand aspiration (luggage checked in) and massive price gap vs mass brands (3x); new normal pricing accepted
items.quote: On top of it, suddenly with this price war, the gap between the premium and the entry was almost three-folds, right? So three years back, the gap difference between various different players was to the tune of somebody being higher by 10%, 15% and the next player being higher by another 15%, another 15%.

items.statement: Direct tie-up with Hinomoto wheels (Japanese patented technology); component supply chain localisation underway; benefits in 6-9 months
items.quote: For example, we'd be probably the first factory in the country to get into a direct sort of an arrangement with one wheel supplier, which is Hinomoto wheels. We were the first ones to use Hinomoto wheels.

items.statement: Benetton contributing >10% of sales; small leather goods #2 brand after Tommy; Travel Gear 45%, SLG 40-45%, Handbags 10% of Benetton revenue
items.quote: Benetton, I would say that is now contributing almost more than 10% of our overall sales. So I think we're sort of happy with the way Benetton business is going.

items.statement: Institutional, handbags and government business each targeted as ₹100 crore revenue buckets; institutional head hired, distributors appointed
items.quote: 100%. I would still say that handbags is a INR 100 crore bucket for us. Institutional is a INR 100 crore bucket for us. Government business is a INR 100 crore bucket for us.

items.statement: Tommy Hilfiger license renewal initiated for 10+ year term; current license expires 2026
items.quote: We are, again, for example, our license was coming to our listing in 2026. And we've initiated the entire dialogue with them for renewal of the license as per their international listing. And now we're talking about obviously a long-term sort of license. So, and by long-term, I mean at least a 10-year kind of a period

items.statement: Retail secondary sales > primary sales in Q1; strong momentum in June-July; airport stores (Bangalore T1, Mumbai T2) performing exceptionally
items.quote: format stores, Q1 as in the first quarter, our secondary sales Brand Concepts Limited (BCONCEPTS) Q1 FY26 Post Earnings Conference Call August 14, 2025 is much higher than our primary sales. So that goes on to prove that there is a strong secondary momentum now you have not paid in Q1 and whatever correction you have done, but Q2 you will fill that space up

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue growth guidance to around 25% from earlier 20%
items.quote: We believe definitely with this we will be able to touch at least 25% growth in this financial year.

items.statement: Maintained EBITDA margin guidance range of 16-18%
items.quote: We have maintained that & We maintain the same.

items.statement: Expect at least 20% top-line growth in FY27 after full capacity commissioning
items.quote: FY '26 to '27, again as all the capacity would be there, so we believe at least on the top line level 20% growth should be there.

items.statement: Order book healthy at ~Rs 560 crores with strong inquiries from power sector
items.quote: On the order book side, our pipeline remains healthy at ~ Rs. 560 crores with a particularly strong inquir ies coming from the power sector, an area where we expect to see sustained momentum in the months ahead.

items.statement: Export order book constitutes ~35% of total order book
items.quote: Out of the total order book of Rs. 560 crores, there is around 35% from export side.

items.statement: Secured Rs 190-200 crore order from leading integrated power plant equipment manufacturer
items.quote: We recently secured a large order from one of India 's leading integrated power plant equipment manufacturers.

items.statement: Value-added fittings and seamless pipes capacity to commission in H2 FY26; piercing lines for backward integration
items.quote: Our projects for value added fittings and seamless pipes and tubes are progressing as planned , and we expect the new capacity to be commissioned in the second half of FY '26, along with seamless as announced previously. We will also be the installing piercing lines to ensure we remain fully backward integrated.

items.statement: Total FY26 CAPEX spend ~Rs 120 crores
items.quote: In this entire year, it will be spending around Rs. 120-odd crores.

items.statement: Blended capacity utilization expected near 80% in FY26 on 42,000 tons; higher in FY27
items.quote: The blended utilization should be near to 80%, what we believe, and for the coming year FY '27 it should be probably higher than that, keeping all the capacity would come by end of FY '26.

items.statement: Welded:seamless capacity ratio ~60:40
items.quote: And again, the blended utilization if you see the capacity ofwelded and seamless , it will pan out a bit somewhere 60-40 ratio would be there probably sort of that.

items.statement: Strong power sector demand with many tenders floated; expecting more orders from oil & gas, chemical, engineering
items.quote: But see power, but again from power there is a very huge amount of demand which is coming , number of tenders floated for power, which is a new demand in the system, which was not there in the system in such quantity, I think that should also help.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 16.2% vs 19.9% YoY; decline due to capacity increase, new export market penetration, subdued domestic demand
items.quote: On the EBITDA front, EBITDA for Q1 FY '26 stood at Rs. 44.9 crores compared to Rs. 47.9 crores in Q1 FY '25. EBITDA margin for the quarter was 16.2%.

items.statement: Margin improvement expected from value-added products (condenser tubes, fittings) in coming quarters
items.quote: More value added products are coming into play. So, those should help us to improve the margin in the coming forward quarters to come.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 55% seamless, 38% welded, 7% others; seamless grew 13%, welded 10% YoY
items.quote: The revenue mix for the quarter stood at 55% from seamless pipe and 38% from welded pipe. Seamless pipe registered a revenue growth of 13% and welded grew by 10%.

items.statement: Fittings business expected to be higher margin than pipes; less competition in India
items.quote: We generally see when you developed this business, it can be a slightly higher margin business as compared to the other business what we are currently doing. So, those rooms for margin are there because there are less number of fitting manufacturer in the country.

items.statement: Raw material prices more or less stable currently
items.quote: More or less, not too much change. It is more or less stable currently.

items.statement: Welded pipe pricing under some pressure; seamless pricing stable
items.quote: See, not much on the side of seamless. We are able to get the orders for the rates we are generally trying to get. On the side of welded, there is a bit pressure.

items.statement: US tariff increased from 25% to 50% in June under Section 232; US ~15-20% of export order book
items.quote: Out of the current order book of export, we have around 15% to 20% from USA side of the total export portion of order what we are currently carrying with us.

items.statement: Export diversified across Europe, USA, Middle East, SE Asia, Africa; intent to reduce geographic concentration
items.quote: We are supplying in Europe, USA, Middle East, South East Asia and African countries. But again, in case of USA, cautious of tariff , because nobody knows what tariffs will come tomorrow, today or someday after. So, those risks we see definitely from the U.S. side. But we think if it is there it will be for every company, it should not be much effective. But we are keeping a close eye on the scenar

items.statement: ADNOC already approved; receiving approvals from other companies quarterly but not disclosed individually
items.quote: ADNOC is where we are already approved, so we keep on getting those approvals. And as you see, we do not categorically give the name of those approvals that are being received by the company.

items.statement: Started receiving welded pipe orders from Saudi Arabia after anti-dumping duty on China; pursuing more clients
items.quote: In welded segment , we had already started to receive some of the orders from Saudi market, but still, we are pursuing with a number of clients and discussing ongoing orders with a number of clients. So, we are expecting good demand from the Saudi market in the coming months.

items.statement: BHEL Rs 190 cr order not working capital heavy; payment schedule manageable
items.quote: No, it is not working capital heavy.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty creates anxiety among distributors/traders; further duties could hinder exports
items.quote: But again, there is a lot of confusion about what will happen in the coming forward days or quarters to come. So, that is creating a lot of anxiety amon g all the distributors and traders. So, that is definitely a factor which needs to be considered.

items.statement: No extrusion facility currently; may consider in future if high-grade product demand justifies high CAPEX
items.quote: But extrusion facility requires a very high CAPEX or very high payback period. So, once we have the capacity to establish for the high grade of product, which will be able to do the better utilization of the extrusion. So, definitely we will plan. We are not denying that we will not plan. We may plan. It depends on the circumstances and in future capability of the venus.

items.statement: Target to handle 1 million laden TEUs in next 3 years
items.quote: Our 3-year plan, which we have been talking about in the last couple of investor calls, aims at getting us to 1 million laden TEUs in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Current capacity 8.3 lakh TEUs across 7 facilities; plan to expand to 1.25-1.3 million TEUs
items.quote: All these capacity enhancement initiatives will increase our capacity from the current 8.3 lakh TEUs to over 1.25 million, 1.3 million TEUs. So that's about 13 lakh TEUs.

items.statement: Estimated capex outlay of INR 280 crores for Mundra CFS Phase 1 and Farukhnagar ICD over 1-1.5 years
items.quote: We are overall estimating INR280 crores of capex outlay between these 2 projects. Because these projects are spread over like 1 year or 18 months of period.

items.statement: Total 3-year capex estimate INR 450-500 crores including Farukhnagar, Mundra, JNPT and Chennai expansion
items.quote: We expect a capex outlay of around INR450 crores to INR500 crores over the next 3 years. Part of it has already been spent and a lot of it will be met by internal accruals.

items.statement: INR 38 crores raised via fully convertible warrants to kickstart expansion plans
items.quote: The recent fund raise that we have done of INR38 crores in effect, kickstarts our plans for expansion.

items.statement: Additional borrowings limited to INR 50-70 crores as bridge capital for capex; plan to repay existing INR 100 crores debt
items.quote: The dependency on borrowing would be limited, and it would be only required to the extent of kind of bridge capital, which we are estimating in the range of INR50 crores to INR70.

items.statement: EBITDA per TEU target maintained at INR 2,000-2,200 level; Q1 FY26 at INR 2,292
items.quote: We would maintain our EBITDA at INR 2,000 level, which we are currently. And some of the measures which we have already taken, that would only help us to improve from here on.

items.statement: EXIM trade growth expected at 6-6.5% linked to GDP; no significant impact from US tariffs on CFS addressable market
items.quote: I think it should be in the range of 6%. There will be seasonal variations that you would see typically in Q2, Q3, then the Q4 variations with regard to the Chinese New Year and all those things.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 volume 1,51,100 TEUs; 5% YoY growth; H2 expected to accelerate with new capacity
items.quote: The total volume handled for Q1 FY '26 stood at 1,51,100 TEUs.

items.statement: Revenue per TEU improved from INR 11,800 to INR 12,500; gross margin from 32% to 36% over last 12 months
items.quote: Revenue per TEU, we have been able to improve from INR11,800 in March '24 quarter to INR12,500 -- close to INR12,500 in June '25 quarter. Even gross margin from 32% has gone up to 36% in this particular quarter.

items.statement: Strong cash flow generation with DSO of 18-20 days supporting capex funding
items.quote: Our existing CFSs continue to generate strong cash flow with a good DSO of 18 to 20 days.

items.statement: Received regulatory permission for Mundra CFS outside SEZ and IMC in-principle approval for Farukhnagar ICD
items.quote: I'm happy to share with you that the last month, this is after Q1, we have received the necessary regulatory permission to set up the CFS in Mundra. The third thing that we've been talking about is the Farukhnagar greenfield ICD. Again, I'm happy to share with you that we have received the regulatory permissions, which is the IMC in principle approval to set up an ICD in Farukhnagar.

items.statement: PAN-India presence in 5 locations covering 80% of India's EXIM trade; market share 12-12.5% in CFS markets
items.quote: We currently estimate a market share of about 12% to 12.5% in the CFS markets that we operate in the 5 locations that we are in.

items.statement: Differentiation via PAN-India presence, digital myCFS portal, scale efficiencies in transport/equipment contracts, and Allcargo Group integration
items.quote: The digital enablement is in the form of a myCFS portal, which is the first of its kind in the industry. This enables customers to log on to the myCFS portal or the app on the mobile phones, see what is happening to their cargo on a real time and do the basic stuff that they need to do for cargo clearance through the mobile phone or through the portal.

items.statement: Current throughput multiple 2.5-3x; expected to improve with DFCC faster turnaround times
items.quote: The multiple would currently be around 2.5 to 3, which can only become better with faster throughput and faster evacuation, as you kind of mentioned.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty may impact overall business sentiment but not CFS addressable market significantly
items.quote: But as in everything, uncertainty is not good for business sentiment. To that extent, I think whatever uncertainty which hits because of this tariff stop-start kind of a thing, which is there, might have an overall impact on the economy and things like that and on the sentiment.

items.statement: Management says 25% consolidated revenue CAGR is achievable with current capacities and strategy, citing historical ~18% CAGR plus ~5-6% from injectables and ~6-7% from CDMO over 5-6 years
items.quote: So on our baseline growth of 18 plus 5% and plus 5% kind of gives us somewhat of a clarity that, yes, 25% can be done.

items.statement: Formulation revenue CAGR of 35-40% expected given lower base and 80-20 API-formulation mix target
items.quote: And when we talk about the formulations, if we have to grow at this kind of a growth that we speak about with an 80%, 20% way that we are looking at, those numbers automatically translate to 40% growth if you're looking at from a formulation, which has a relatively lower base.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue declined 5% YoY to INR 204 cr due to lumpiness from strong Q4 FY25 and customer procurement patterns
items.quote: We reported a moderate quarter with revenues down 5% to INR 204 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 30.1% in Q1 FY26 vs 37.7% YoY; excluding Valthera injectable facility start-up costs (~INR 12-13 cr), margin ~37% in line with last year
items.quote: EBITDA margins for this quarter stood at 30.1% against 37.7% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Valthera injectable facility start-up costs ~INR 12-13 cr in Q1 (INR 4.27 cr employment, INR 2.77 cr power/fuel, rest other); expected to weigh on margins until revenue scales through FY26
items.quote: So yes, around INR 12 crores to INR 13 crores is the expense that is related to the injectable facility.

items.statement: Valthera injectable facility commercialized in March 2025; validation batches taken for 2 products in Q1, 2 more lined up for Q2-Q3; domestic launches underway, emerging market filings by end FY27
items.quote: We have already taken validation batches for a couple of our products in the first quarter only. We have a couple more products that are lined up for validation in quarter 2 and quarter 3.

items.statement: Capacity utilization Q1 FY26: Dholka API 75%, Limbasi API 57% (up from 52.6% Q4 FY25), Valthera injectable 26%
items.quote: In the Dholka unit, in this quarter, the capacity utilization is 75%, and in Valthera unit, it is around 26%, and for the Limbasi, it's around 57%

items.statement: CDMO: one commercialized project with midsized innovator (vet product) started sales in Q2 FY26; advanced discussions with several clients; targeting $40-50M total opportunity from 4-5 projects over medium term
items.quote: We currently have commercialized CDMO project and have started our sales to them in Q2 FY '26. We are also currently in advanced discussions with several potential clients to expand our CDMO engagement.

items.statement: API revenue down 10% YoY to INR 153.8 cr; formulation revenue up 12% YoY to INR 50.2 cr; domestic 55%, export 45% of revenue (US ~15% of export, RoW ~30%)
items.quote: Revenue from the API business stood at INR 153.8 crores against INR 171.1 crores in Q1 of last year, down by 10% Revenue from the formulation business h as grown by 12% in this quarter from INR 44.8 crores to INR 50.2 crores

items.statement: Dholka API facility cleared US FDA (EIR received), EU GMP (Jul 14-18, 2025), Russian GMP (Jul 22-25, 2025) inspections; US FDA approval received for teriflunomide tablets 7mg/14mg
items.quote: During the period, our API facility in Dolka underwent an inspection by the US FDA, and we are pleased to report that we have received the EIR report from the US FDA for this inspection

items.statement: Export revenue split: ~45% of total revenue; of exports, ~15% to US, ~30% to rest of world
items.quote: So as far as the bifurcation of exports revenue is around 45% of the total revenue is exports and 55% is domestic. Out of the export revenue, around 15% % is to the US and 30% is to the rest of the world.

items.statement: Incorporated Stellon Biotech Inc. (US) for formulation marketing/distribution/commercialization; incorporated Concord Lifegen Ltd (India) for domestic marketing/sales/distribution
items.quote: We have further strengthened our presence in the US through the incorporation of Stellon Biotech, Inc., which will focus on the marketing, distribution and commercialization of Biotech pharmaceutical and biotech products in the US market.

items.statement: Prices largely stable for existing customers/products; second-source entry for new products/customers may involve pricing discounts (e.g., recent launch at ~25% discount to $350-400 market price) but margins remain healthy
items.quote: For one of our products, which we have recently launched, the market price was close to around $350, $400. We launched it at almost a 25% discount.

items.statement: R&D spend ~2.3% of sales (down from 3.5-3.6%); fermentation R&D differs from formulation - expertise-driven, small scale, low KSM cost (agro-based, locally sourced); R&D headcount 180 across two centers (API at API unit, formulation at Valt
items.quote: In fermentation, what we do is that much of the R&D actually happens at a very, very small scale. And the best of the results are only the ones that we kind of take it to a larger scale.

items.statement: Pipeline: 10-12 products under development (antibiotics, oncology); 2-3 expected launches this year (2 antibiotics, 1 oncology); combined market size ~$500-700M; niche with 2-3 player competition
items.quote: The pot ential market size for each product, I can come back to you with the exact numbers because, again, IMS doesn't provide it at the API level. But I would say this would put together all the three products, I would say, close to around $500 million to $700

items.statement: Injectable facility: 2 products launched in India, 2 more coming in coming months, ~10 products in Phase I (mostly backward integrated)
items.quote: We have currently launched two products from the injectable facility. We have another two, which are expected to be commercialized in the coming months. And we have around 10 products in our Phase I that we intend to launch

items.statement: Fermentation API portfolio: 30+ products across immunosuppressants, oncology, anti-infectives, antibacterials; limited global competition (2-3 players for niche molecules like Nystatin)
items.quote: Concord remains one of the few companies globally producing more than 30 fermentation APIs across multiple therapeutic areas, including immunosuppressants, oncology, anti-infectives and antibacterials.

items.statement: No formal supply contracts with most customers; stickiness from being primary/secondary source; quality contracts only for regulatory compliance
items.quote: So typically, we don't have any contracts with the clients. And the reason for that is that once you start working with a formulation company, there is a lot of stickiness between the two.

items.statement: No price increases or decreases passed to customers in recent years; pricing pressure absorbed via R&D cost improvements
items.quote: we've neither increased our prices nor decreased our prices. In One of the earlier discussions, I mentioned that in case there is a pricing pressure on us, we kind of compensate it through our R&D.

items.statement: R&D headcount 180 (includes all staff); two R&D centers (API at API unit, formulation at Valthera); no management changes or attrition discussed
items.quote: The number is 180 and this 180 number includes everyone.

items.statement: Target 4% PBT by Q4 FY27
items.quote: we remain committed on our growth targets and to achieve our target of 4% PBT by quarter 4 FY '27.

items.statement: ISCS medium-term EBITDA margin target 10-10.5%
items.quote: As we said, as of now, the ISCS segment is hovering around 8.3% adjusted EBITDA margin. And in the medium term, we expect this to go to around, say, 10%, 10.5%.

items.statement: ISCS revenue growth target mid-teens
items.quote: The revenue growth would be around mid-teens. Yes.

items.statement: GFS normalized EBITDA margin 3-3.5%
items.quote: GFS on a normalized basis should be somewhere around 3%, 3.5%, Kunal. If you look at the past -- 3%, 3.5%. Correct.

items.statement: Project One annualized cost savings INR110-120 crores
items.quote: Project One is expected to deliver about INR110 crores to INR120 crores in annualized cost savings, with about INR50 crores to INR60 crores benefits starting to reflect in FY '26 itself.

items.statement: TVS ILP plans to develop 20 million sq ft warehouse assets
items.quote: So, they have in their prospectus said that they have a plan to develop about 20 million square feet. But there's no definite time period. I would say in the next -- in the medium term, that is their plan.

items.statement: Order pipeline INR5,300 crores
items.quote: Our order pipeline remains strong at INR5,300 crores, giving us solid revenue visibility going forward.

items.statement: New business wins INR124 crores in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, we secured new business wins of INR124 crores, representing around 5% of Q1 FY '25 revenue.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 6.7% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR173.3 crores, translating to a margin of 6.7%.

items.statement: ISCS adjusted EBITDA margin currently 8.3%
items.quote: As we said, as of now, the ISCS segment is hovering around 8.3% adjusted EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Underlying adjusted PBT margin improved to 0.7% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our adjusted PBT before share of profit from TVS ILP was INR19 crores, up from INR14 crores last year, a growth of 35% year-on- year and reflecting margin improvement to 0.7% from 0.5%.

items.statement: GFS segment faces macro pressures and tariff uncertainty
items.quote: Our GFS segment continues to face macroeconomic pressures. particularly around uncertain tariff environment and softening freight rates, which all of you are well aware of.

items.statement: India business muted in Q1 reflecting broader India Inc slowdown
items.quote: if you see the Q1 numbers from India Incit itself has been muted. So in a way, I would say that from a supply chain side that we reflect that.

items.statement: GFS pricing under stress sequentially and year-on-year
items.quote: Pricing continues to remain under stress, both sequentially and year-on-year and macroeconomic uncertainties and tariff volatility continue to weigh on this segment.

items.statement: Freight rates tapered during Q1 FY26
items.quote: This reduction primarily reflects the lower freight rates within the GFS segment as both ocean and air freight rates tapered during the quarter in response to the subdued global trade.

items.statement: Debt primarily for working capital, comfortable with position
items.quote: Saumil, as of now, I think we are comfortable with the debt and most of the debt is only for working capital. So, we are comfortable with the debt position actually.

items.statement: TVS ILP transferred 11 million sq ft to InVIT backed by global and domestic investors
items.quote: In Q1, TVS ILP transferred approximately 11 million square feet of developed assets into an InVIT platform backed by marquee global and domestic investors.

items.statement: Recorded INR177 crores share of profit from TVS ILP InVIT transaction
items.quote: We recorded INR177 crores as our share of profit in this quarter.

items.statement: Project One involves rightsizing, right-shoring, management restructuring
items.quote: Under the new structure, we have taken significant steps to simplify and strengthen our operating model anchored around the key pillars: rightsizing, simplifying and bringing leaner organization layers through integration, right-shoring, transitioning certain roles and activities from high cost to optimized cost locations; management restructuring, which is streamlining leadership to support the u

items.statement: GFS volatility may risk 4% PBT target if sustained
items.quote: Correct, Darshil. I think we assume that the GFS probably in 1 or 2 quarters, it will return to some kind of a normalcy once this uncertainty tapers off, and we'll hit the 3%, 3.5% PBT margin, the EBITDA margin for the GFS segment. But as Ravi mentioned, I think right now, the situation is a bit uncertain.

items.statement: Win rate approximately 22%
items.quote: We -- as a company, our win rate is about 22%. We continue to see how we can improve that.

items.statement: Segment reporting changed: ISCS includes IFM, GFS standalone freight forwarding
items.quote: We have made 2 changes in our segment reporting. One, ISCS now includes integrated final mile services, while GFS reflecting freight forwarding business will be a stand-alone segment.

items.statement: AI deployment scaled in select engagements across UK, US, India
items.quote: We actually have scaled the deployment of AI in select engagements in U.K., U.S. and India, where we use a fair amount of visual computing and bringing in orders of efficiency.

items.statement: Agentic AI initiatives planned for process automation
items.quote: Agentic AI is something, which we will talk about over the next few quarters. We believe that there is a great scope for us to improve process efficiency and bring down the ability or bring -- increase our ability to drive more volumes with less using Agentic AI.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 guidance of 20% gross margin growth and 30% adjusted EBITDA growth
items.value: 20% gross margin growth, 30% adjusted EBITDA growth
items.quote: So the guidance that we had given last time around, right, we had given a 20% growth guidance on gross margin and 30% growth for adjusted EBITDA. We remain firm on that, and we would let our numbers do the talking.

items.statement: Targets FY26 gross booking growth of ~15% and ~20% from FY27 onwards
items.quote: FY '26, we will see maybe closer to about 15% for the full year in terms of gross booking growth. And going forward, our endeavor is to be closer to about 20% in terms of gross booking growth.

items.statement: EBITDA-to-gross-margin ratio target 25% in 12-18 months, 30% in under 36 months, North Star ~35%
items.quote: So firstly, in terms of the gross margins, right, our gross margin to EBITDA ratio, which is currently at about 21%, we think in the near term, right. So let's say, in a 12- to 18-month horizon, we should be able to get this to 25%. And in under 36-month period, we do expect this to be closer to 30%.

items.statement: Onboarded 34 new corporate clients in Q1 FY26 with annual billing potential of ~INR200 crores
items.quote: In Q1, we onboarded 34 new corporate clients, collectively adding an annual billing potential of approximately INR200 crores.

items.statement: Cumulative new corporate billing potential ~INR1,300 crores over last 2 years; ~INR600-700 crores implemented so far
items.quote: So out of the INR1,300 crores, about INR750-odd was in the last fiscal year, right. And what was signed up in the last 6 months of last fiscal year is typically what would currently be in the process of implementation.

items.statement: B2B share of gross bookings ~66-67% currently, targeting 70% by FY27; hotels & packages mix rose from 15% to 20% of gross bookings YoY
items.quote: At this point of time, our B2B, B2C mix is about late 60s of gross bookings coming from B2B and early 30s in terms of percentage of gross bookings coming from B2C. Our expectation would be that by next fiscal year, this would be closer to about 70-30.

items.statement: Air take-rate improvement driven by discount optimization with banking partners and higher corporate mix yielding better net retention
items.quote: First, optimization of discounting. So we've been working quite closely with our banking partners and other marketing partners and affiliate partners through whom we are able to now drive customer acquisition without needing to discount to the same level from our side.

items.statement: Cash flow positive in FY25 (~INR7.3 crores) and Q1 FY26; internal accruals cover corporate working capital needs; corporate card and other solutions being evaluated to further optimize
items.quote: Even in the current quarter, we would be positive when it comes to cash flow as well. So while you're right that the corporate business does consume working capital, but we ar e at a size and scale today in terms of profitability where the internal accruals being generated are taking care of the working capital needs

items.statement: Gross debt reduced from INR546 million (Mar 2025) to INR29 million (Jun 2025); cash and term deposits INR2,208 million as of Jun 2025
items.quote: Gross debt has been significantly reduced from INR546 million as of 31st March '25 to just INR29 million as on the 30 June 2025.

items.statement: AI assistant DIYA expected to optimize work of 70-100 people by end FY26 and ~200 people by end FY27
items.quote: Early indications are that we would be able to optimize the work of about 70 to 100 people by the end of this fiscal year and about 200 people by the end of next fiscal year.

items.statement: Corporate travel market expected to reach US$20 billion by FY27; online penetration ~20% in FY24 vs ~45% overall travel
items.quote: The corporate travel market is expected to reach around US$20 billion by FY '27; however, online penetration in this segment remains low at just around 20% in FY '24 compared to almost 45% for the overall travel industry in India.

items.statement: Top 100 corporate clients: 73 retained >5 years; annual retention rate >97%; integrated self-booking tool with ERP/HRMS creates high switching costs
items.quote: If I look at our top 100 customers, right, 73 of our top 100 customers have been with us for more than 5 years, right. So that gives you the kind of retention that we have, right. And our annual retention rate is upwards of 97%.

items.statement: Competitors largely service corporate clients offline with minimal integration; Yatra leads online penetration and benefits from mass digital adoption
items.quote: Most of our competitors still service customers in the offline manner, right, with minimal amount of integration. That is why for us, there is a large opportunity right now to go and penetrate into the digital adoption that's happening in mass across the industry.

items.statement: US Holdco (Nasdaq) requires minimum $1 share price by Oct 13; can comply via reverse stock split if needed; no penalty
