items.quote: No, no, there is no real complication in that. Khush, you can simply as a company, you can do a reverse stock split.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisition opportunities on corporate side and technology solutions; working on US Holdco delisting process across multiple jurisdictions
items.quote: We continue to keep our eyes and ears open for good opportunities that we come across especially on the corporate side or on technology solutions that can fit in within our corporate platform.

items.statement: Worst quarter for corporate business is Q3 due to Diwali/Dussehra and Christmas/New Year breaks; best quarters Q2 and Q4
items.quote: The worst quarter for corporate business will typically be the third quarter because that has then the Christmas New Year break and the Diwali, Dussehra break, right. So you see a large number of corporates being off during those days.

items.statement: Expect positive ROA by end of FY26 as operating performance strengthens and provisions normalize
items.quote: We expect to achieve positive ROA by the end of FY '26 as operating performance strengthens and provisions normalized.

items.statement: FY26 will be a year of consolidation targeting moderate business growth while improving operational metrics
items.quote: FY '26 will be a year of consolidation, one where we target moderate business growth while sharply improving operational metrics and building a robust financial foundation for next phase of expansion.

items.statement: Target secured assets share of 70% by March 2027
items.quote: We are well on track to achieve our long-term goal of increasing the share of secured assets to 70 percentage by March 2027.

items.statement: NIM moderated to 6% from 9.4% YoY due to portfolio mix shift, excess liquidity, rate cuts and micro loan delinquencies
items.quote: Net interest margin moderated to 6 percentage from 9.4 percentage last year. This was primarily due to the shift in our loan portfolio mix towards secured assets, reduction in repo rates by RBI, the strategic decision to maintain excess liquidity, controlled loan book growth and higher delinquencies in the high-yielding micro loan portfolio.

items.statement: Expect NIM improvement going forward as slippages reduce and fresh disbursements at moderated rates pick up
items.quote: On the margins, definitely, there will be an improvement going forward once the slippages comes down and also the fresh disbursements taking up at a moderated rates after the rate cuts, then definitely the NIMs will definitely improve.

items.statement: Total business INR42,507 crores, up 4.82% YoY; underlying growth 8.74% adjusting for write-offs and NPA sales
items.quote: As of 30th June 2025, our total business stood at INR42,507 crores compared to INR40,551 crores a year ago, reflecting a Y -o-Y growth of 4.8 2 percentage. Adjusting for the impact of technical write-off and NPA sales during the period, the underlying growth in total business was a robust 8.74 percentage.

items.statement: Micro loan book declined from INR13,236 crores to INR9,095 crores YoY in line with de-risking strategy
items.quote: Our micro loan book declined from INR13,236 crores in Q1 FY '25 to INR9,095 crores in Q1 FY '26 in line with our strategy to de-risk the portfolio.

items.statement: Gold loans grew 16% QoQ and more than doubled YoY
items.quote: Gold loans were the standout performer growing 16% quarter -on-quarter and more than doubling in Y-o-Y, reflecting consistent demand from our rural and semi-urban customer base.

items.statement: Secured assets now 54.79% of loan book, up sharply from 32.69% a year ago
items.quote: As of now, secured assets account is 54.79 percentage of our to tal loan book, up sharply from 32.69 percentage a year ago.

items.statement: Disbursements INR7,694 crores, up 71% YoY with secured loans forming 90% of total disbursements
items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter were INR7,694 crores, a sharp, 71 percentage Y -o-Y growth from INR4,503 crores last year with secured loans forming 90 perce ntage of total disbursements aligned with our derisking and portfolio quality strategies.

items.statement: Gross NPA 7.5%, Net NPA 3.8%, PCR improved to 73.2%
items.quote: On asset quality, as of FY '26, gross NPA stood at 7.5 percentage and net NPA 3.8 percentage reflecting both the prevailing macroeconomic conditions and other cautious stand on micro finance lending. importantly, our provision coverage ratio improved to 73.2 percentage demonstrating our continued focus on strengthening the balance sheet and improving the quality of our loan book.

items.statement: NPA sales of INR733.4 crores executed comprising INR362.43 crores NPA and INR371 crores technical write-offs, resulting in net P&L benefit of INR45.76 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, we executed NPA sales of INR733.4 crores comprising NPA of INR362.43crores and technical write -offs INR371 crores, resulting total concentration of INR733.34 crores. This resulted in the net P&L benefit of INR45.76 crores for the quarter, and the meaningful reduction in gross NPA INR362.43 crores.

items.statement: Slippages primarily from micro banking book in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu contributing almost 50% of micro loan slippages; SMA levels moderating substantially
items.quote: See, primarily the slippages are mainly from the micro banking book, mainly from 2 states, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu contributed almost 50 percentage of the mic ro loan slippages. However, the positive thing is that the overall SMA levels are moderating substantially over the last quarters.

items.statement: Microfinance stress likely peaked in Q1, expected to stabilize in Q2 and show positive traction from Q3
items.quote: We believe stress levels have likely peaked in Q1, but stabilize in Q2 and show positive traction from Q3.

items.statement: Microfinance collections on bank-run portfolio at 98-99%; BC portfolio showing stress but direct intervention yielding good results
items.quote: When we look at the figures for the last 1 year and what we have disbursed in the last 1 year, we see that our collections in that portfolio is close to 98%, 99% or so.

items.statement: Raised Tier 2 bonds of INR65 crores with 6-year maturity in July 2025 to strengthen CRAR
items.quote: Further, bank has also raised Tier 2 bonds with 6 -year maturity amounting to INR65 crores during July 2025 to further strengthen the CRAR position.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio at 22.7%, Tier 1 at 18.4%; have aggressive asset growth plans requiring capital but no concrete fund raise decisions yet
items.quote: Yes. Because always banks are capital hungry because we are a growing bank. And for the last 1 year only, the business growth was only muted. But going forward, we have got aggressive plans for increasing the asset book and which requires capital. And we have certain plans, but no concrete decisions have been taken so far.

items.statement: Deposits INR22,698 crores, up 8.7% YoY; retail deposits INR21,763 crores, up 13.17% YoY; retail deposit share improved to 96% from 93%
items.quote: INR22,698 crores, up from INR20,887 crores in Q1 FY '25, representing an 8.7% Y-o-Y increase. As part of our strategic focus on stability, we have consciously reduced our share of bulk deposits. Retail deposit growth to INR21,763 crores as on 30th June '25 from INR19,230 crores a year ago, making a robust 13.17 percentage Y-o-Y growth. The share of retail deposits in total deposits improved furthe

items.statement: CASA balances INR5,628 crores, up 14% YoY; CASA ratio 24.8%
items.quote: CASA balances remain a key pillar of our deposit franchise reaching INR5,628 crores in Q1 FY '26 compared to INR4,927 crores in Q1 FY '25, translating to 14 percentage Y -o-Y growth.

items.statement: Excess liquidity reduced from INR3,000 crores to around INR2,000 crores
items.quote: Apart from that, we were continuously holding around INR3,000 crores of excess liquidity throughout last year, which has moderated to around INR2,000 crores as of today.

items.statement: Deposit rates corrected but full transmission of RBI rate cuts on liability side will take 1-1.5 years; loan rates already corrected for fresh disbursements
items.quote: But the fresh loans, we have already corrected the extending loan rates. However, it will take some more time to get the full benefit of it. And also, the interest rates -- on the liability book also, we have moderated after the rate cut by RBI. However, the repricing of deposits will be happening over a period of time. So the full impact will be received over a period of 1 to 1.5 years.

items.statement: Operates 788 banking outlets, 1,095 customer service centers, 713 ATMs, 33 institutional BCs across 24 states and 2 UTs
items.quote: ESAF Small Finance Bank today operates 788 banking outlets, 1,095 cust omer service centers, 713 ATMs and 33 institutional business correspondents, across 24 states and 2 union territories, enabling deep penetration in rural and semi-urban markets.

items.statement: 662 branches (80% of network) offer gold loan product; engaged external valuers and use RBI-specified strong rooms or FBR safes
items.quote: Right. So to start with , 662 branches of ours are offerin g the gold loan product. So that would be roughly 80 -odd percent of the network. This is one part of it. Second, we have engaged appraises or valuers across the system.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio: ~25% small ticket (INR1-1.25 lakhs), ~10% to microfinance segment; 80% of gold loans for 1-year tenure, 15-20% premature closure
items.quote: Roughly, I think about 25% of our loans are small ticket gold loans. And when we say small tickets, it will be about INR1,00,000, INR1,25,000 or so. And if you are asking more from a segment point of view, whether we are lending the gold loans to the micro finance segment, then it is even less. It is more -- about 10% or so of the portfolio will be to the micro finance segment.

items.statement: Gold loan tenures: largely 1-year (80% of portfolio), offerings for 2-4 months also; 15-20% premature closures
items.quote: There can be. However, if you see our portfolio in terms, generally, the large part of the 80% or so is for a 1-year tenure. We do have offerings for 2 months, 3 months, 4 months, etcetera. But largely, they are taken for 1 year. In terms of premature closures, I would say, about 15% to 20% of our loans tend to get close prematurely.

items.statement: Asset concentration in Kerala down to 35%; present in 25 states and expanding into newer geographies; liability concentration in Kerala to continue due to NRI deposit base
items.quote: But the asset concentration has significantly come down. It has come down to 35 percentage. But we are well diversified now. We are present in 25 states. We are expanding into newer geographies. So the asset building is hap pening. But on the liability side, the Kerala concentration will continue for some more time because of the NRI deposit base we have originally from Kerala.

items.statement: RBI lowered priority sector lending requirement for SFBs from 75% to 60%, providing greater portfolio flexibility and improved capital allocation
items.quote: On the regulatory front, the RBI decision to lower priority sector lending requirements for small finance bank from 75 percentage to 60 percentage is a welcome development, offering greater portfolio flexibility, improved capital allocation and enhanced diversification.

items.statement: Fully implemented MFIN Guardrails 2.0 supporting stronger, more resilient loan book
items.quote: In parallel, ESAF SFB has fully implemented MFIN Guardrails 2.0, which will support the building of a s tronger, more resilient loan book.

items.statement: Microfinance industry facing asset quality pressure and book degrowth leading to accelerated provisions and revenue softness
items.quote: The microfinance industry is currently facing newer challenges, asset quality pressure and book degrowth leading to accelerated provisions and revenue softness.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth outlook of 15-18% driven by new business wins, contingent on market recovery
items.quote: So, we remain bullish on a medium-term basis on kind of 15%-18% kind of a growth, which we have been doing in the last 10-12 years.

items.statement: FY26 capex plan of Rs.300 crores excluding solar, with Rs.120 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: So, this year's plan is close to Rs.300 crores excluding the CAPEX on the solar side. In Q1, we have done close to Rs.120 crores.

items.statement: Rs.650 crores capex for heavyweight forging infrastructure with 10,000-ton and 4,000-ton presses adding 20,000 MTPA capacity
items.quote: We also remain on track with our Rs.650 crores CAPEX plan to create a best-in-class forging infrastructure for heavyweight precision components.

items.statement: Total forging capacity to reach ~150,000 tons after current expansion with 10,000-ton and 4,000-ton presses
items.quote: With this, our total forging capacity will be close to 1,50,000 tons.

items.statement: Forging utilization at 59% tonnage basis, 74% unit basis with 18-20% headroom; machining utilization at 77% expected to return to 84-85%
items.quote: So, as I have understood you correctly, yes, the forging utilization right now is around 59%. And that is in terms of tonnage. But in terms of numbers if you see the forging utilization is close to 74% in Happy Forgings Limited August 11, 2025 terms of

items.statement: Domestic CV flat, exports down 8-10%; domestic farm equipment strong with 9% tractor sales growth; off-highway weak globally; industrials growing on wind, power, oil & gas; PV scaling rapidly
items.quote: From a reported geographical market segments perspective, our domestic business grew by almost 7% year-on-year, while the export segment saw a decline due to continued weakness in commercial vehicles and off-highway and farm equipment segments as well as tariff-related uncertainty.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 28.6%, gross margin at 57.9%, both near peak levels; confident of sustaining margins
items.quote: Our gross profit margins remain healthy at 57.9% while our EBITDA margins stood at 28.6%, both around peak levels. This performance comes at a time when the industry is facing pressures on both growth and margins. We remain confident of sustaining these margins going forward as well.

items.statement: Realizations flat at Rs.245/kg despite 3% raw material price correction, supported by higher value-addition share
items.quote: Realizations remain strong at Rs.245 per Kg on a year-on-year basis, despite of moderation in raw material prices, supported by higher share of value-addition components.

items.statement: Machining share at 88% of revenue; PV segment at 6% of revenue expected to reach 8-10% in two years; front axle beam realizations Rs.180-220/kg vs crankshaft higher
items.quote: The machining share o f our revenue remains strong at 88% with focus on value addition and precision -engineered components gaining ground

items.statement: Direct US exposure 3-4% of revenue; CV exports 9-10% of total revenue; farm direct exports 1%; deemed exports ~10%; tariff impact minimal due to CIF terms
items.quote: So, our direct exposure to US currently is around 3% to 4%, where at the moment, we are not selling on the basis of DAP. So, we are not in discussions for the tariffs at the moment for this business.

items.statement: Strong balance sheet with >Rs.350 crores liquidity and healthy internal accruals
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, we continue to maintain a healthy financial position with strong internal accruals and adequate liquidity of more than Rs.350 crore s to support ongoing investment

items.statement: Volume growth 3.8% YoY to 14,457 MT; realization Rs.245/kg; front axle beam target 35,000 units in FY26 (3,000-4,000 in FY25)
items.quote: Our volume for the quarter increased to 14,457 MT compared to 13,933 MT in the same quarter last year, marking a 3.8% increase. Importantly, realization per Kg held steady at Rs.245 per Kg

items.statement: Rs.80 crores committed for PV capacity expansion; Rs.110 crores invested in Q1 on new machining lines; solar CAPEX Rs.60-70 crores expected Q1 FY27
items.quote: To support this growth, we have committed a capital expendi ture of Rs.80 crores, which will go towards enhancing production capacities and strengthening our position in the evolving

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty in US/Europe may temper industry revenue growth; CV and farm equipment export markets weak; off-highway recovery expected 2026
items.quote: Although tariff-related headwinds could temper revenue growth trends across the broader industry, our endeavor will be to protect revenue growth by focusing on securing new business, maintaining our margins, which we are confident of sustaining going forward.

items.statement: Participating in defense tenders with initial approvals received; awaiting green signal for defense orders
items.quote: We have quoted certain projects, but yet to receive the green signal, but we have started participating in the tenders for some of the parts, sir, and we are hopeful that we will have a breakthrough very soon.

items.statement: Industrial genset order for North America (Rs.145 crores total, ~Rs.30 crores/year) ramping up in Q2 FY26, 50% utilization by Q3, full by Q4
items.quote: This is for the industrial genset business I think you are talking about which is for the North American market and for which the testing is almost over the line is ready with us and we are expected to start ramp up in this quarter.

items.statement: 25 MW solar captive power plant: 40 acres land acquired, agreement signed, commissioning expected Q1 FY27
items.quote: And on the second question regards to the solar project, yes, the solar CAPEX is ongoing. And we have already acquired 40 acres of land on this, already signed agreement for this. We expect the project to commence by first quarter of next financial year.

items.statement: Domestic CV growth to outpace industry in H2 FY26 on new product ramp-up; domestic farm equipment high single-digit growth; PV segment scaling with SUV platforms
items.quote: On the domestic side, I think we will be outpacing the growth on the CV side in the third and fourth quarter depending on the ramp up for the new products that we have launched on the CV side and should be expecting a good high single digit kind of growth on the CV side.

items.statement: Front axle beam business targeting 35,000 units in FY26 (Rs.30-40 crores revenue), ramping to Rs.50-60 crores in FY27
items.quote: And the front axle beam business is ramping up because of the ongoing slowdown in the domestic market the units are little less, but we expect to deliver close to 35,000 units in this year.

items.statement: Benefiting from China+1 sourcing shift in industrial engines (casting to forging conversion); no threat to US PV ramp-up as testing complete and no OEM capacity investment
items.quote: So, the plan for them is not to manufacture it in-house, which they have already offloaded. And that is the reason the projects which is going for the industrial engine side, the line is almost ready, the testing is kind of about to be over, which will be ramping up very soon. The business shifted from China.

items.statement: Raw material price impact ~Rs.4-5/kg (3-3.5%); realizations held flat showing improvement despite falling steel prices
items.quote: It was close to Rs.4 to 5 a Kg. If you see in percentage terms, it is close to 3%, 3.5%.

items.statement: 14,000-ton press utilization at 46-48% tonnage, 55% units; heavy press capacity for wind shafts (150-300kg) and data center components
items.quote: We are at around 46-48% in terms of tonnage basis, and around 55% in terms of units, because we do a lot of industrial production on these lines.

items.statement: New business delivering 15-18% revenue growth; Q1 growth excluding steel price impact ~6.5-7%
items.quote: And so basically, the way we have seen is that almost 15% growth is there in the company just on account of new product developments that we have done. So, the way we look at is that we are generating 15%-18% kind of a growth from the new businesses.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance INR700 crores and PAT guidance INR45 crores maintained
items.value: INR700 crores revenue, INR45 crores PAT
items.quote: So this year, we have given the projection of around INR700 crores of revenue and INR45 crores of PAT. I think we will be meeting those guidance.

items.statement: FY27 aspirational targets INR1,000 crores revenue and INR55 crores PAT
items.value: INR1,000 crores revenue, INR55 crores PAT
items.quote: For FY '26, INR700 crores top line and INR45 crores bottom line. And for FY '27, INR1,000 crores top line and INR55 crores bottom line.

items.statement: Q1 revenue declined 8% YoY due to absence of festivals and preponement of Akshaya Tritiya demand to Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our revenue from operations has declined by 8% year-on-year for quarter 1 financial year '26, primarily due to the absence of major festivals or wedding -related demand during the

items.statement: Strong advanced order booking in wholesale segment from IIJS exhibition for upcoming festival and wedding season
items.quote: We participated in IIJS exhibition held in Mumbai during July and August, where we have received a strong response in B2B segment with a significant ad vanced order booking in wholesale segment for the upcoming festival and wedding season

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA INR13 crores, down 8% YoY; EBITDA margin improved 9 bps to 17.2%; PAT INR7 crores at 9.39% margin
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR13 crores, also lower by 8% Y-on-Y, while EBITDA margins improved marginally by 9 basis points to 17.2%.

items.statement: Retail revenue INR45 crores slightly higher YoY; wholesale revenue INR29 crores down 20%; job work revenue grew 8%
items.value: Retail 45 crores, Wholesale 29 crores, Job work up 8%
items.quote: In terms of segmental performance for quarter 1, our retail revenue stood at INR45 crores, which was slightly higher than the last year's revenue. Wholesale revenue was INR29 crores, reflecting 20% decline in the same period, while job work revenue grew by 8%.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity 2,000 kg annually; current utilization ~900,000 kg; sufficient for 2-3 years; no capex needed now
items.quote: We have enough manufacturing facility for the coming 2, 3 years. And also the expansion is going on in the retail segments with the addition of 2 stores, Rajkot and Surat, which will be one of the largest store in the city. So I think with this said, there is no -- right now, we don't feel that there is a requirement of -- we already have enough capacity for sustaining this, and there is no need o

items.statement: 35% more walk-ins at IIJS; new retail clients acquired; strategic partnership with Titan and Malabar continuing strong
items.quote: We got 35% more walk-ins; means we captured the new additional retails very well. Demand, which is there, means, we are very happy with the IIJS performance.

items.statement: Volume mix 50% B2C / 50% B2B by FY27; revenue mix ~75% retail, 25% wholesale+job work
items.quote: In terms of quantity, it will be 50%, 50% because we have a job work volume, which is quite high, around 600 kgs plus. But in terms of revenue, it will be -- more or less, retail would do around 70%, 75%.

items.statement: Volume growth expected single-digit in FY26; FY25 volume grew 18% with 20-25% price increase
items.quote: So this year, we are expecting the volume to remain flat as gold prices have itself spiked up by around 25%, 30% or maybe a single -digit growth of volumes can be seen.

items.statement: Surat store ~80-90% of Ahmedabad potential (INR400 cr); Rajkot ~65-70%; Baroda similar to Rajkot; 4 stores target INR1,000 cr+ revenue
items.quote: So we are in a clear set lines , see a potential store of Ahmedabad or Surat should be around INR400 crores each. But even if you are not reaching a potential, if you're reaching at even 75% to 70% of that same, still, I don't think so there is any guidance, which is less than INR1,000 crores if all the four stores are up and pumping.

items.statement: Surat and Rajkot stores LOI signed; lease agreements pending; expected operational in 6-8 months; one in Q4 FY26, one in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Mr. Sancheti for both showroom LOI has been signed. We are lease agreement and all are to sign and with a matter of six, eight months this showroom both of them should be less.

items.statement: Inventory turnover target 2-2.5x; IPO proceeds INR100 crores fully utilized in FY25; funding via retained earnings and debt up to 1:1 debt-equity
items.quote: I think the inventory will be in line with the retail turnover that is approximately 2x, 2.5x.

items.statement: Sanctioned debt limit INR150 crores; finance cost increased due to one-time debt rise; debt-equity ratio low, targeting 1:1
items.quote: One time cost where is an increase in debt. So our sanction limit is INR150 crores. So because of that initial rises because of one time, their financial cost has increased.

items.statement: Income tax notice from private company era (bonus share issuance); CIT appeal filed; management confident no material impact
items.quote: We are very strong that this notice does not have any base. And I have repeatedly told that in my previous two earnings call also. We have signed a CIT appeal. We are waiting for a very positive result.

items.statement: Gold price volatility affects consumer sentiment; demand may be postponed but not denied in occasion wear; no tariff impact seen yet
items.quote: Because of the geographical tension, the gold prices are volatile in nature. And this has a relation with the customers' mind and everything. So still being on the occasion side of the jewellery segment, the demand is sure going to be there. It can get postponed, but not denied.

items.statement: Harit Zaveri continuing as interim CFO; permanent CFO to be promoted internally after 2-3 years experience in company
items.quote: So, I think right now, I'll be continuing the role for again an interim -- but it will be an interim role. If not, it will be sooner or later passed on to a professional. And we are wanting that the person who comes as a role of CFO has to have a 2, 3 years o f experience when it comes to -- in RBZ itself and then has to be promoted to the role of CFO

items.statement: Focus remains on antique occasion wear; daily wear growing but not aggressive in studded/diamond (10-15% of retail); in-house daily wear development underway
items.quote: In studded jewellery we are not much aggressive. We understand how is the Indian consumer. So Indian consumers they are lovers of gold. We intend to stay in this segment. It is a safe segment. Because of manufacturing capability, it is a profitable segment to us.

items.statement: Structural shift: pan-India retailers building in-house manufacturing; RBZ has manufacturing advantage and moving into retail forward integration
items.quote: What you yourself mentioned itself is a structural shift. This is a very nice point Harshit. So there are pan-India players who are going ahead with manufacturing facilities. They have their front end. They are now aggressively moving towards their back end. So we have back end, which is prepared. We can go for front end.

items.statement: Retail store potential: Ahmedabad INR323 cr (FY25) targeting INR350-400 cr (FY26); new stores INR400 cr potential each
items.value: INR350-400 cr Ahmedabad, INR400 cr per new store
items.quote: Retail in Ahmedabad is right now INR323 crores. This year, we are hopeful to reach by around INR350 crores to INR400 crores or so. So I think we are on -- Surat is almost 90% or 80% to Ahmedabad and Rajkot is 70% or 65%, 70% to Ahmedabad, Surat.

items.statement: E-commerce via Instagram (163k followers); no own marketplace yet; focus on Gujarat expansion first
items.quote: E-commerce, see, we have a very strong Instagram presence. As of now, Instagram has 163,000 followers. None of our peers who are independent jewellers or mid -sized corporates have such a kind of Instagram or a social media presence.

items.statement: Security concerns for jewellery showrooms; 100% insurance coverage; past unforeseen incidents occurred; company remains cautious
items.quote: See, we have gotten security measures. Some unforeseen events in our showroom has also happened previously. But with that, we have a complete 100% insurance. So -- and again, I think, one cannot -- you are true with this statement that one has to be very alert when it comes to the security nature.

items.statement: No plans for face value split or liquidity measures; first time receiving such feedback on earnings call
items.quote: So as of now, this is the first time I've received the remark on the earnings call. Right now we do not have any such plans. But once the remark or the feedback has come, let us understand it more -- going in more deeper.

items.statement: Standalone guidance: 50% revenue growth and 2.5x EBITDA growth for FY26; consolidated revenue growth guidance of 100% may see shortfall due to Tritium, but standalone guidance maintained
items.quote: So we had given a guidance of 50% increase in the revenue and 2.5x of the EBITDA. And that guidance still holds good. We are confident that for the remaining 9 months, we'll be able to hold on to the guidance.

items.statement: Consolidated profitability guidance only for FY27, not FY26, due to Tritium losses
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, I think profitability guidance will only be for FY '27, not for FY '26 on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Order backlog exceeds INR1,500 crores including services; hardware supply orders exceed INR1,200 crores
items.value: INR1,500 crores total, INR1,200 crores hardware
items.quote: But on the positive side, we secured major wins from Middle East, from Africa, which is giving us hope for some of our best export business this year. We have a strong outlook given the order backlog, which is more than INR1,500 crores. A lot of that is service in future years, but just the hardware supply orders also exceed about INR1,200 crores.

items.statement: EV passenger car sales grew 72% QoQ and 15% YoY in Q1 FY26 to ~40,000 units; electric bus momentum improving due to payment security mechanism
items.quote: So in Q1 of '25, there were about 23,000 cars which were sold, which is almost 40,000 in Q1 FY '26, that's a 15% growth compared to last quarter, 72% growth quarter-on-quarter and that's because of new model launches, new premium SUV launches by major OEMs, Hyundai, Mahindra, the new models by Tata.

items.statement: New tower installations flat QoQ at ~7,500 but down 26% YoY; telecom infrastructure in replacement phase
items.quote: Overall, new tower installations remained flattish compared to Q4 FY '25 at about 7,500 and it was a 26% decline compared to Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin improved to 32.7% from 21.3% QoQ due to richer product mix and cost optimization; adjusted EBITDA margin 8.6%
items.quote: Despite the softer top line, gross margin improved to 32.7% from 21.3% last quarter, which is a very healthy positive up, driven by a richer product mix, cost optimization that we've done.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin healthy at 39.4% aided by higher-margin products and geography mix
items.quote: Gross margin remained healthy. We were at 39.4%, aided by higher-margin products that we sold and the geography mix that we got.

items.statement: Hyderabad integrated manufacturing plant to start production in October 2025; full transition over 2 quarters; IPO funds INR108 crores balance as of June 30, majority to be utilized by end of September
items.quote: And we are really hoping that we'll be able to start the production here in late September, early October. This is kind of something we're very proud of. It will represent not only one of the leading electronic plans in the country, but a lot of the thinking behind automation, digitization, industry 4.0 concepts, which will allow us to be really high quality and lean cost manufacturer of our produ

items.statement: Hyderabad plant utilization expected north of 70-75% with current machinery; plant built for future capacity with modular expansion
items.quote: So with the current plant and machinery that we are putting, our utilization will absolutely be north of 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Harmony Gen 2 EV charger launched with better features, aesthetics, durability and higher gross margins; 6 of top 10 customers switched entirely; DC charger deliveries >50% converted to Gen 2, targeting 100% by year-end
items.quote: I can't give you exact specific numbers, but this is the first time where we have been able to give a better value product in terms of features, more things, better aesthetics, better durability and increase our gross margin at the same time.

items.statement: Secured exclusive business with largest electric trucking operator in India; won OEM business from German luxury automaker; signed global framework agreement with largest clean energy player in Southeast Asia for EV chargers across Malaysia
items.quote: For the first time, an Indian company has signed, which is Exicom, our company has signed a global framework agreement with one of the largest clean energy players in Southeast Asia for EV Chargers. Subsidiary of this company is putting charging networks in countries of Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

items.statement: Export revenues from Africa and Southeast Asia contributed 30% of Critical Power revenue in Q1; major wins from Middle East and Africa
items.quote: Revenues from Africa and Southeast Asia contributed to 30% of our current quarter's revenue. And in these markets, also, we acquired new customers and also increase wallet share of existing customers.

items.statement: Rights issue of INR260 crores completed: INR55 crores unsecured debt repaid, INR107 crores promoter loan converted to equity, INR85 crores for Tritium investment, INR12 crores general purpose; debt-equity improved from 0.7 to 0.35; net wort
items.quote: We recently completed a rights issue of INR260 crores, which was successfully subscribed rather a little oversubscribed on the rights issue. The breakup of the rights issue of INR260 crores was that we were paying unsecured debt of INR55 crores, repaying back that. This is the object of the rights issue. We are converting promoter given loan into equity of INR107 crores. Investment in Tritium to s

items.statement: Tritium turnaround taking longer than expected but strategic for global footprint; $8 million bookings in Q1 FY26 including repeat and service orders; TRI-FLEX product pipeline building; lifetime warranty on power module introduced as indus
items.quote: We had almost $8 million of booking in Q1 of FY '26, including repeat orders, including service orders, but hopefully, we can expand this much more rapidly than we have in the past. We are confident about some of our action, and that's why we are enabling Tritium to take some industry-first actions as well.

items.statement: Rare earth material supply delays from China affected ~5-10 components; one charger category production at 80% last month; overall impact not significant enough to change guidance
items.quote: For one of our charger categories, for example, last month, production was 80% of what we expected because of delay in these materials. But on an overall year basis, quarter basis, I don't think the impact will be significant, which will make a difference in numbers for us.

items.statement: EV charger revenue: standalone INR53 crores (+61% YoY), consolidated INR103 crores; supplied >15,000 chargers in Q1, industry-leading
items.quote: Overall, Q1 is always not the hottest quarter in automobile, the time around festive season, end of date calendar year is -- but you see our Q1 FY '25 performance, we did on a standalone basis, INR33 crores versus which this quarter, we have done 61% more, which is about INR53 crores in this quarter.

items.statement: Critical Power revenue: standalone INR98 crores, consolidated INR102 crores; ~70% market share in rural infrastructure project; lithium-ion battery shift accelerating
items.value: INR98 crores standalone, INR102 crores consolidated
items.quote: Our standalone Critical Power revenue was about INR98 crores and consolidated was INR102 crores. As I mentioned, this revenue is below expectations, but the primary reason for this was some of the key projects we are supplying to, including Bharat Net, including a couple of other projects, including some large lithium-ion battery upgradation project.

items.statement: VRS for 100+ employees at older facility transitioning to newer facilities; Tritium redundancies as part of resizing
items.quote: We say adjusted because of an exceptional item for VRS of about 100-plus employees in one of our older facilities, which we are transitioning its production to our newer facilities, that's why the adjusted exceptional item.

items.statement: Working capital funds from IPO proceeds to be utilized in Q2 as project revenue builds up
items.quote: Working capital funds, we'll see utilization in Q2. As I mentioned, a lot of the key projects, the revenue buildup will be from this quarter.

items.statement: Tritium losses weighing on consolidated profitability: adjusted EBITDA -INR38.6 crores, adjusted PAT -INR71 crores; consolidated profitability guidance pushed to FY27
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA was negative by INR38.6 crores and compared to minus INR17 crores in the previous quarter. And this is primarily, of course, because of Tritium operational costs, which continue to weigh on profitability of ours.

items.statement: EV charging market intensely competitive with prices fallen beyond expectations; Exicom claims industry-leading margins and largest continuous EV charging provider in India
items.quote: Yes, it's going through very intense competition. Prices have fallen way beyond what we would have expected. But as I mentioned in the previous question, at Exicom, we believe in giving great value to the customers. And by doing that, yes, there has been margin compression, I won't lie, but it is still maintaining, let's say, in my opinion, industry-leading margins compared to our peers.

items.statement: PM E-DRIVE policy now includes incentives for electric trucking enabling entry into truck segment; government payment security mechanism for electric buses accelerating deployments
items.quote: For the first time, we could make an entry into Electric Trucking segment. That's partly also because PME drive policy allows for incentives for Electric Trucking, which was not the case before. And because of this, some truck makers are investing heavily to go electric, we secured some exclusive business with one of the largest electric trucking operators in the country.

items.statement: Rights issue of INR260 crores successfully completed, slightly oversubscribed; promoter holding reduced from 69.5% to 66.5%
items.quote: We recently completed a rights issue of INR260 crores, which was successfully subscribed rather a little oversubscribed on the rights issue.

items.statement: R&D expense 3-5% of cost of sales; ~160 R&D staff evenly split between EV charging and Critical Power; 60% EV charging, 40% Critical Power allocation; only Indian company designing and manufacturing own charger controller
items.quote: So our expense of R&D as a cost of sales would be between 3% and 5%. And not exactly equal, but broadly, EV charging would be, let's say, 60% of the expense, critical power would be 40% of the expense.

items.statement: Developing battery energy storage integration with EV charging for high-power charging where grid support is limited; pilot done last year, now scaling up
items.quote: So a battery -- an integration of battery energy storage system and EV charging is something we are looking at. We did have a pilot product last year in that, but with all those learnings, etcetera, scaling up of that.

items.statement: Board approved INR 100 crore Greenfield capex for 40,000 MTPA Zinc chemicals facility at Dahej, Gujarat, fully funded through internal accruals
items.quote: I am pleased to share with you that yesterday our Board has approved the Greenfield capital expenditure of approximately INR 100 crores fully funded through internal accruals for a 40,000 metric ton per annum Zinc chemicals facility at Dahej, Gujarat.

items.statement: Combined installed capacity expected to reach 110,000 MTPA of Zinc chemicals after full capex completion across existing units and Gujarat plant
items.quote: So, after the entire capital expenditure program is completed, we expect that the installed capacity of both the existing units and the Gujarat plant, basis the plans that we have today, would be about 1,10,000 metric tons of Zinc chemicals.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit volume growth on consolidated level for current fiscal, consistent with last fiscal performance
items.quote: As a Company, we have always maintained our objective to have double-digit volume growth on a consolidated level, which is what we have been able to achieve in the last fiscal, and which is what we aspire to achieve in the current fiscal as well.

items.statement: Core EBITDA margin 10-11%; blended EBITDA margin expected to improve by 200-300 bps over next few years driven by value-added products
items.quote: We expect that the EBITDA margin should increase by 200 to 300 basis points over the next few years.

items.statement: Non-rubber revenue share increased from 10% to 15%; targeting 30% over next 4-5 years driven by ceramics, specialty chemicals, pharma, cosmetics, agriculture
items.quote: We intend to expand our presence very aggressively into the non-rubber market also and expect to increase the share of non-rubber products from the current 15% to over 30% over the next four to five years.

items.statement: Good demand across all end-user industries in Q1; favorable monsoon outlook supports strong demand in upcoming quarters
items.quote: On the operational front during the quarter, the Company continued to witness good demand across all end-user industries. With a favorable monsoon seasonal outlook, we expect demand to remain strong in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Zinc oxide and scrap prices directly linked to LME Zinc; monthly average pricing creates natural hedge; exchange rate automatically covered via Hindustan Zinc pricing
items.quote: So, the price of Zinc scrap and Zinc oxide is directly linked to the price of Zinc on the London Metal Exchange. Change in the price of Zinc metal directly has a corresponding impact on the price of both Zinc scrap and Zinc oxide.

items.statement: Export revenue historically 10-15% of total; Q1 FY26 in same range; expected to remain in this range going forward
items.quote: Our export revenues have historically been in the 10% to 15% range. And even for this quarter, it was more or less in the same range. And we expect it to remain in this range itself going forward as well.

items.statement: Working capital cycle about three months; acts as significant entry barrier for new entrants
items.quote: But another important aspect of our business which is critical to understand is that it is a working capital heavy business and the working capital cycle is about three months.

items.statement: No plans for QIP, rights issue or fundraising; company is cash-rich; INR 45 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilized
items.quote: At the moment, we have no such plans. The Company is fairly cash-rich at the moment. Should there be a need, we will definitely explore. But at the moment, we don't have any such plans.

items.statement: India Zinc oxide consumption estimated at 140,000 tons annually; imports negligible at ~5,000 tons
items.quote: Today, the estimated consumption of Zinc oxide in India would be about 1,40,000 tons on an annual basis. And as far as imports are concerned, it is absolutely negligible. Hardly about 5,000 tons would be imported, even less than that as on today.

items.statement: Cater to 200+ domestic and 50+ international clients including 9 of 10 top global tire companies and all 10 Indian tire companies
items.quote: We cater to over 200 domestic customers and more than 50 international clients. This includes 9 of the 10 top global tire companies and also all the 10 Indian leading tyre companies.

items.statement: No dumping from China due to LME-linked pricing globally; Chinese cost competitiveness neutralized by Shanghai Futures Exchange pricing tied to LME
items.quote: So, given that the mother index is the LME for both India as well as China and all other geographies, so there is no competitive edge which China has vis-à-vis any Indian producer or any other producer from any other country.

items.statement: No direct tariff impact as US sales negligible; scrap import duty structure unchanged; short-term volatility from global tariff wars averages out long-term
items.quote: So, generally speaking, we do not have any direct impact of tariffs because our sales to the U.S. is next to negligible, almost zero. And the duty structure, the tariffs have not impacted the duty structure on the scraps that we import from U.S.

items.statement: Sufficient management bandwidth for Dahej capex; bulk of investment in existing product lines; nurturing in-house talent plus external recruitment by HR
items.quote: So, the Company has enough and more bandwidth as far as the management of the Zinc oxide and the Zinc chemicals facilities are concerned. We believe in nurturing talent in-house and obviously, when a CAPEX comes into play, there is also recruitment from outside the Company, which the HR is duly taking care of.

items.statement: Dahej capex to be executed in two phases over 3-4 years; roughly 50-50 split between Zinc oxide and non-Zinc oxide products; land cost included in INR 100 crore
items.quote: The INR 100 crores include the land as well.

items.statement: Current utilization at ~70% of achievable capacity; Naidupeta capacity sufficient for coming year until Gujarat plant commissioned
items.quote: Utilization levels, approximately, we operate at 70% of achievable capacity. Historically, also, we like to do that.

items.statement: Internal target to double revenues every 3-4 years; profitability and return metrics to scale with revenue growth from current initiatives
items.quote: So, you see, we have always mentioned that our target is to double our revenues every three years to four years. That is what our internal targets are.

items.statement: Ceramics market estimated 25,000-30,000 MTPA; targeting 15-20% market share after Gujarat plant operational; India ceramic industry growing double-digits
items.quote: The ceramics market, according to our estimates, is approximately about 25,000 to 30,000 metric tons per annum. Again, India is turning out to be a large ceramic hub. This industry, we expect, should grow well in double digits in India over the next few years due to a sharp rise in housing market and exports of ceramic products from India.

items.statement: Tyre industry expecting double-digit growth over next few years per ATMA/PwC; India tyre exports grew from INR 14,000 crore (FY21) to INR 25,000 crore (FY25)
items.quote: If you would have read a recent report which was released by the ATMA, which is the Apex body regulating the tire business, and also I think PwC mentioned it, the tyre industry is actually expecting a double-digit growth over the next few years.

items.statement: Actively evaluating recycling opportunities aligning with core strengths; initiatives support long-term expansion and ESG commitment
items.quote: We are actively evaluating several exciting opportunities in the recycling space that align with our core strengths. These initiatives will not only support long-term business expansion but also reinforce our commitment to ESG.

items.statement: Sharp zinc price movements cause inventory knock-on effects quarter-on-quarter; pace and duration of price changes matter more than direction; medium-term averages out
items.quote: But you would appreciate that any business carries an inventory, which is almost a perpetual inventory. So, if there is sharp movements in Zinc prices, that inventory takes a knock and you could see the effect of that on the quarter's performance.

items.statement: New rubber chemical product in R&D with customers; expected to contribute ~10% of revenue from next year; not standard rubber chemicals (accelerators/antioxidants)
items.quote: But however, having said that, it may be safe to assume that from next year it should start contributing to the revenues of the Company.

items.statement: Zinc scrap sourced globally in varied shapes, sizes, purity; large buyer status ensures scrap availability for blending 80+ specialized grades
items.quote: Because if your capacity is, say, only 500 tons a month, and you stock for one month, and this being scrap, it is not that when you want, it will be available. You may not have the entire variety of the scrap profile to particularly manufacture a particular grade.

items.statement: Pharma/healthcare customers include large global names as sole supply partners; details under NDA
items.quote: In the pharmaceutical and healthcare space, we are catering to few very large global names who are working solely with us as their global supply partners. Due to a NDA being in place, we are unable to share more details and names for the same.

items.statement: Acquired 2.96 acres adjacent to Naidupeta for future Brownfield expansion into advanced recycling products
items.quote: Additionally, we have acquired a 2.96 acres land parcel adjacent to our existing Zinc oxide and Zinc sulphate facility in Naidupeta for future Brownfield expansion plans into advanced recycling products.

items.statement: Content per tyre: ~1% by value, 3-4% by weight; targeting increase via specialized grades and recycling-related products
items.quote: So, content per tyre as far as zinc oxide is concerned in terms of value, it is about 1%. And in terms of weight, it would be close to 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Naidupeta plant is only IATF-certified zinc oxide plant globally; WHO GMP approved for pharma/cosmetics
items.quote: Our Naidupeta facility, which is our largest facility today, is globally recognized as the only IATF-certified zinc oxide plant, and we are also WHO GMP approved.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 40-50% and EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% maintained for FY26
items.quote: The guidance for the yearly growth of revenue and the EBITDA margin remains the same. What you have mentioned, we still stick to that.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target of 13-15% post legacy project completion
items.quote: And the EBITDA margin guidance that we had given of somewhere between 13% to 15%, that we can consider once these legacy projects are over.

items.statement: Order book of INR 9,828 million as of June 30, 2025 with 90.9% domestic orders
items.quote: As of June 30, 2025, the company's order book stood at INR 9,828 million, comprising 79.4% from heating systems, 12.8% from process plants and 7.8% from flares, incinerators and other renewables.

items.statement: Order finalization of ~INR 3,000 crores expected in FY26 with historical 25% hit rate
items.quote: There is an order finalization expected in this financial year, which is about, say, INR 3,000 crores or so. And out of that, now how much share we will get is what we'll have to see.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 7% vs 13.4% in Q1 FY25 and 13.8% in Q4 FY25 due to legacy projects
items.quote: The EBITDA stood at INR 72 million, translating to a margin of 7% compared to 13.4% in quarter Q1 FY25. And 13.8% in quarter Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Legacy project margin impact to continue in Q2 FY26, improvement expected from Q3 FY26
items.quote: The impact of higher costs related to the earlier projects is likely to continue in Q2 FY26 as well.

items.statement: No additional capex required for potential large orders, existing capacity sufficient
items.quote: So far as capex is concerned, I would like to inform you that there would not be any additional capex required.

items.statement: JV formed with Chemdist Group founders for green hydrogen and chemical equipment, JNK holds 51% stake
items.quote: The company has entered into a joint venture agreement post the quarter with Mr. Sunil Dhole and Mr. Tushar Wagh, founders of Chemdist Group to develop green hydrogen and other sustainable fuel technologies and also critical engineered equipment in chemical and pharma industry.

items.statement: JV initial investment INR 10 crores preference capital plus INR 51 lakhs equity, working capital support ~INR 50 crores first year
items.value: INR 10 crores preference capital, INR 51 lakhs equity
items.quote: The extent of working capital support could be about INR 50 crores or so in the first year. And initial equity is about INR 51 lakhs and also the initial investment is about INR 10 crores in the company.

items.statement: JV expected to contribute 8-10% of JNK revenue in FY26, 10-15% in 2-3 years, 15-25% in 5 years with 10-12% EBITDA margin
items.quote: In this financial year itself, we would see a certain amount of revenue which could be about, say, around 8% to 10% of JNK India's revenue. So going forward, in 2 to 3 years' time, we look forward to a revenue growth in the new company, the new JV business, which is about 10% to 15% of JNK India's revenue. And maybe up to 5 years, we can look at something like 15% to 25% of JNK India's revenue in

items.statement: Reliance and HPCL projects on track for Q3-Q4 FY26 revenue delivery, completion by Q1 FY27 latest
items.quote: The project execution is going on in full swing and both the sites at HPCL and Reliance, we've deployed the necessary manpower at site to ensure that the things go on track and go on time. So definitely, would be delivering the revenues in terms of Q3, Q4. And worst case in the Q1 of next financial year, we'll be able to complete both the projects, yes.

items.statement: Employee cost up 15.5% YoY net of ESOP due to annual increments and added execution manpower
items.quote: On the employee cost front, the employee cost net of ESOP expenses in Q1 FY25 as compared to the employee cost in Q1 FY26, there is an increase of 15.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue INR 1,030 million, up 13.5% YoY
items.quote: Total revenue for the quarter stood at INR 1,030 million, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 13.5%.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline extends to Q1 FY27
items.quote: The current order book would get executed up to quarter 1 of next financial year, that is Q1 of '27.

items.statement: Single competitor in each major bid: Thermax for HPCL, Technip for Reliance, L&T for BPCL Bina
items.quote: HPCL was Thermax and Reliance was Technip. And in BPCL Bina, it is Larsen & Toubro. So practically there was only one competitor in all these 3 bids.

items.statement: One large order finalization lost in Q1 FY26, but expecting better hit rate on remaining opportunities
items.quote: In the quarter 1, there was one large finalization, which unfortunately didn't come in our way. And in quarter 2, there are 2 finalizations are expected any time.

items.statement: Working capital facilities can be enhanced if orders materialize, no static limit
items.quote: Current working capital facilities can be enhanced if we get the orders. So we can't say that, there is no staticness in that.

items.statement: FY26 seat addition target of ~40,000 seats, same as FY25
items.quote: So, broadly speaking, our guidance remains the same as last year. So, what we have done last year, about 40-odd-thousand seats is the guidance for FY '26 as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 similar to FY25 with slight upward bias
items.quote: And the overall guidance around on the margins, which also factor in some kind of operating leverage from corporate overheads is supposed to be same as of FY '25 with a bit of an upward bias.

items.statement: Confident of meeting full year guidance for construction fit-out segment
items.quote: We see this segment gaining significant traction in the coming quarters, buoyed by a healthy order pipeline and a favorable market outlook and remain confident of meeting our full year guidance.

items.statement: Strong demand from first-time GCC entrants and existing GCC expansions in Bengaluru and Hyderabad
items.quote: Our Enterprise segment continues to be a key growth driver, fueled by strong momentum from first-time midsized GCC entrants, especially across our centers in Bengaluru and Hyderabad.

items.statement: Signed 15,000 new seats in Q1 FY26 vs 11,000 in Q1 FY25; 18,000 seats signed for Q2-Q3 move-in
items.quote: On the demand side, we've signed contracts for 15,000 new seats in Q1 FY '26, demonstrating strong performance on the demand front versus 11,000 seats in Q1 of FY 2025.

items.statement: No demand slowdown seen from IT/ITES sector despite layoff news; churn remains ~1%
items.quote: We are not seeing any kind of decline in terms of demand coming up from the sector, I mean, despite what we hear about the commentary.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 37.8% (Ind AS) and 14.5% (IGAAP), up 710 bps and 300 bps YoY respectively
items.quote: EBITDA rose by 60% year -on-year to INR127 crores with margins expanding to 37.8%, marking a significant improvement of 710 basis points compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Structural margin expansion expected over 2-3 years from occupancy maturation, operating leverage, premiumization, and Allied Services growth
items.quote: So, structurally, we are in a trajectory for margin expansion over the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Mature center EBITDA margins 30-35% (straight lease) and 23-25% (managed aggregation); blended ~27-28%
items.quote: Any center which hits a mature stage, so let's say, a 12 -month plus kind of a vintage for us in a straight lease model, we generally look at center EBITDA margins of about 30% to 35% for that center.

items.statement: Corporate overhead efficiency expected to improve margins 0.2-0.5% annually
items.quote: The way we look at it is almost about annually 0.2% to 0.5% -odd kind of improvement in margins because of corporate overhead efficiencies.

items.statement: Construction fit-out order book of INR100+ crores; Q1 revenue INR58 crores
items.quote: Currently our underlying demand is looking healthy, and we have a strong execution pipeline of over INR100-plus crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex ~INR50 crores; FY26 capex expected similar to FY25
items.quote: So, for the quarter, the capex what we have incurred is around INR50 crores. And the guidance is that we continue to see very strong momentum across all our sectors.

items.statement: Added 6,065 operational seats in Q1; total operational capacity 140,186 seats across 220 centers; total pipeline 165,000+ seats across 246 centers
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 6,065 new operational seats, bringing our total capacity to about 140,186 operational seats across 220 centers Pan-India as of June 2025.

items.statement: Signed LOIs for 14 new centers adding ~9,800 seats and 0.5M sq ft
items.quote: Looking ahead, we have a pipeline with signed LOIs for 14 new centers, adding approxima tely 9,800 seats and 0.5 million square feet of chargeable area

items.statement: 100% of new centers signed Jun'24-Jun'25 in Grade A assets; Tier 2 capacity up ~25% YoY with 4 new centers
items.quote: A key pillar of this expansion has been our focus on premium positioning with 100% of our new centers signed between June 2024 and June 2025 located in Grade A commercial assets.

items.statement: No decrease in average seat price; realization trending up due to commercial rental increases
items.quote: So, there is no underlying decrease in the average seat price, over the last couple of quarters, what we have seen is a constant increase in the same center seat pricing because the underlying rentals in commercial real estate have increased.

items.statement: Allied Services revenue INR36 crores in Q1, up 43% YoY; driven by F&B, TechLabs, mobility, employee transport
items.quote: in Q1 FY '26, the Allied Services revenue grew about 43% year -on-year. Approximately, it's about INR45-odd crores

items.statement: Elite portfolio: 3 live centers (~2,800-3,000 seats); adding 3-4 more centers in FY26
items.quote: So, as of now, we have 3 centers live in Elite, which are approximately closer to about, you could say, 2,800 to 3,000 -odd seats would be across these 3 centers.

items.statement: 3,200+ active clients; 41% multi-center clients (up from 36%); avg tenure 36 months, lock-in 24 months
items.quote: Our client base remains highly diversified with more than 3,200 active clients as of June 30, 2025.

items.statement: IT/ITES share 35-37% (Amit) or 45-47% (Sumit); GCCs and India-facing IT offsetting offshoring weakness
items.quote: We currently have about 35% to about 37% of our business comes from IT/ITES.

items.statement: No pricing pressure from new IPO competitors; differentiated model (65% MA, 35% SL, profit-share) sustains expansion
items.quote: I don't think the competition intensity has not been there. It's been there for the last, I would say, 5-odd years since we have had a great run post the blip in COVID.

items.statement: Locked-in revenue of INR463 crores from 18,000 seats signed for Q2-Q3 move-in
items.quote: This translates to a locked -in revenue of INR463 crores.

items.statement: Gross debt INR7 crores; debt-to-equity 0.02 (down from 0.08); net debt-to-equity -0.18
items.quote: Our gross debt stood at around INR7 crores, resulting in a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02, a notable improvement from 0.08 in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Revenue-to-rent multiple 2.2-2.5x for ideal mature centers
items.quote: Generally, on an ideal center basis, our rental revenue ratios range from about 2.2 to 2.5.

items.statement: Mature centers deliver 3-5% annual escalation (larger cohorts) and 5-7% (smaller cohorts)
items.quote: So, on average, from every customer, we end up getting or a blended average about 5%-odd kind of an annual escalation.

items.statement: ~30-32% of seats <12 months vintage creating margin drag; occupancy buildup takes 9-10 months to reach 80-85%
items.quote: If you look at our current center profile as of 30th June, approximately 30% to 32% of our seats would be under the bucket, which would be less than 12 months.

items.statement: Furniture vertical investment of INR7-10 crores in FY26 for own consumption then third-party solutioning
items.quote: This year, we anticipate somewhere around INR7-odd crores, INR10-odd crores of investment that will go towards establishing the capacity, firstly, for our own consumption and then obviously expand into third-party solutioning as well for furniture.

items.statement: Target to become Rs 1,000 crore company in next 3 years
items.quote: So sir, last time you alluded that our target would be to become Rs. 1,000 crore company in next 3 years, correct? Sunil Suresh: Correct.

items.statement: Plan to open 15 new stores in FY26 with focus on COCO format
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain on track to open 15 new stores in FY '26 with emphasis on high potential real estate catchments in major cities and emerging urban clusters.

items.statement: Three new COCO stores planned in Hyderabad in next 2 quarters
items.quote: We have plan to open three stores in the next 2 quarters. So we are going to go a lot more stronger in Hyderabad going forward.

items.statement: Store maturity ramp-up: Year 1 at 55-60%, Year 2 at 65-70%, Year 3 at 80-85%, Year 4 at 95-100% of potential
items.quote: So normally, what we have seen as a trend is when we open a store in a new market, the first year, the revenue is roughly about 55% - 60% of the true potential of that store. Second year goes to about 65% - 70%. Third year, about 80% - 85%. And finally, on the fourth year is where we say it's around 95% to 100%.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 428 bps to 57.4% in Q1 FY26 driven by localization and manufacturing efficiency
items.quote: On profitability, gross profit increased by 16.6% year-on-year to Rs. 624 million, with margins expanding 428 basis points to 57.4%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 2.7% in Q1 FY26, up 11.9% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA grew 11.9% to Rs. 225 million with a margin of 2.7%.

items.statement: Rental expense 12-13% of retail revenue, 6-8% of total company revenue
items.quote: So on our complete Retail business that we have on the top line, it is somewhere in the tune of 12% to 13% on my retail revenue. On overall which if I can see on a complete company level, it will be somewhere into the tune of 6% to 8%.

items.statement: Revenue from operations Rs 1,087 million, up 7.9% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Revenue from operations was Rs. 1,087 million, an increase of 7.9% over Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth varying from high single digit to double digits depending on store and region
items.quote: So generally, this is one of the key metrics which we track for our SSSG. So this SSSG growth has been varying somewhere from higher single digit to double digits depending on the stores and the locality and the region, etcetera.

items.statement: Stanley Level Next grew 20% and Sofas & More grew 50.7% YoY in Q1 FY26
items.quote: led by the performance of Stanley Level Next, and Sofas & More, which grew by 20% and 50.7%, respectively.

items.statement: Acquired complete ownership of Shrasta Decor Private Limited to strengthen Hyderabad presence
items.quote: We have made a strategic advance in line with our growth vision with Stanley Retail Limited acquiring complete ownership of Shrasta Decor Private Limited.

items.statement: B2B contract manufacturing discussions for domestic and Middle East requirements, not US, so no tariff impact
items.quote: Luckily for us, despite it being an American customer, the discussion what we are doing is for the domestic requirement as well as for their Middle East requirement and not for American requirements. So we have not been impacted in any way as of now.

items.statement: DRI raid on luxury furniture importers for under-invoicing and QCO gazette passed, positive for compliant players
items.quote: The recent raid being conducted by DRI on luxury furniture importers who were under invoicing and the gazette for QCO on import furniture having been passed, we remain buoyant about our future growth.

items.statement: J.K. Sharath appointed as Group CFO to drive transformation agenda
items.quote: Additionally, we are pleased to welcome Mr. J.K. Sharath: as our Group CFO. His deep understanding of the company, along with his strong financial and strategic skills experience will be a great addition to our leadership team.

items.statement: COCO stores 43, FOFO stores 25, total 68 stores as of June 30, 2025; COCO contributes 60% of revenue
items.quote: As of the 30th June 2025, Stanley Lifestyles operates 68 stores, compr ising 43 COCO stores and 25 FOFO stores. The COCO stores accounting for 60% of the revenue in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Secondary sales in franchisee business grew ~2% YoY
items.quote: Secondary sales, we have seen a growth of about 2%.

items.statement: B2B2C model changed from credit to cash-and-carry, stabilized at Rs 2.5 crore revenue with no credit risk
items.quote: That business has stabilized. For the quarter, we have done about Rs. 2.5 crores because of a change in the model from credit to cash, there was some disturbance in the overall revenue growth there. But now we see that, that market is sort of stabilizing an d we have collected all the old money plus now all the customers we have our own cash, so we don't carry any credit

items.statement: Luxury housing sales in Rs 10-20 cr range up 128% and Rs 20-50 cr homes doubled YoY in H1 2025, but property handover delays defer purchase decisions
items.quote: In H1 2025, luxury housing recorded significant expansion with sales in the Rs. 10 crores to RS. 20 crores price range rising by 128% and the RS. 20 crores to RS. 50 crores homes doubling year-on-year. However, delays in property handover, a trend that has been persisted over recent quarters, continues to defer purchase decisions for premium home interior.

items.statement: Localization of leather and manufacturing efficiency improvements driving gross margin expansion, further gains expected with scale
items.quote: Localization as far as leather has continued and played out well, and there is a lot more to do. We believe that there will be a constant improvement with scale improving as we expand our business going forward.

items.statement: No material impact expected from US tariff policies as product portfolio not directly exposed to impacted categories
items.quote: While broader market sentiment remains cautious, our product portfolio is not directly exposed to the categories impacted by the US tariffs. We do not expect any material impact on our business from these changes.

items.statement: Franchisee & Accessories revenue dropped 40% QoQ due to D8 brand exit (Rs 9.6 crore last year), Stanley brand franchisee down 11%
items.quote: This is mainly on account of the D8 brand, which moved out of the company. So last year, we clocked in Rs.10 crores on account of this. On a Franchisee model of a brand, Stanley, there is 11% degrowth that has happened in Franchise and Accessory business.

items.statement: CDMO revenue growth guidance revised to mid-single-digit for FY26 from earlier mid-to-high single-digit due to API price decline
items.quote: What we observed in the Q1 was 2.5% decline in our API pricing-led growth, right? So, while that growth is still achievable, I would rather say from mid-to-high, we would target a mid-single-digit growth as of now.

items.statement: EU CDMO contract to start commercial supplies from April 2027 with annual revenue of at least Rs 300 crore
items.quote: So, this is an established product, so there should be no ramp-up phase. So, we should do at least Rs. 300 crores annually from this contract. And yes, April '27 is when we start commercial supplies.

items.statement: Export formulation revenue target of $100 million over 5 years from current $15 million run rate
items.quote: So, over the five years time, we should target maybe $100 million in exports.

items.statement: Domestic branded formulation EBITDA margin expected around 18% for full year FY26
items.quote: Overall, EBITDA margin for the year is expected to remain similar to last year at around 18%.

items.statement: International branded formulation expected to deliver high-teen growth for full year FY26
items.quote: Despite the weaker growth, we continue to expect high teen growth in this segment for the full year.

items.statement: Jammu plant CAPEX to start by end of FY26, targeting commercial operations by March 2027
items.quote: So, towards the end of this year, we will start CAPEX and over the next 12-13 months, we will do the CAPEX and subsequently, March'27, we should be ready to go live from that facility.

items.statement: Baddi facility to commence commercial liquid supplies in H2 FY26, oncology products first, steroidal block in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our Baddi facility will commence commercial supplies of liquid this quarter in H2. We will commercialize oncology products from this site. And Q1 next year, we will start steroidal block.

items.statement: European GMP audit for plant expected in Q2 FY26, commercial supplies from April 2027
items.quote: The European GMP audit for the plant is expected this quarter. We will begin commercial supplies from April '27.

items.statement: Received €100 million as part consideration for European CDMO contract in Q1 FY26
items.quote: As informed during the last call, Akums has received €100 million as part consideration for the European contract this quarter.

items.statement: CDMO EBITDA margin maintained at 14.7% in Q1 FY26 driven by improved product mix despite 2.5% API price impact
items.quote: The company was able to maintain the EBITDA margins of 14.7%, driven by improved product mix.

items.statement: CDMO margins typically operate in 14-15% range annually; Q1 dip to 14.7% considered a quarterly blip
items.quote: So, a 14% to 15% margin is what we usually deliver in this business. That should be the zip code in which we operate.

items.statement: API prices declined 10-12% on average over last 12 months, with top 200 APIs showing double-digit decline
items.quote: On an average, the API prices have declined 10% to 12% in the last 12 months.

items.statement: API price decline caused 2.5% revenue impact in CDMO segment in Q1 FY26
items.quote: What we observed in the Q1 was 2.5% decline in our API pricing-led growth, right?

items.statement: Niche formulation share growing vs simple dosage forms; commercialized triple-layer tablets first time in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So, as you would remember from our annual presentation of FY25, we really portrayed that our niche formulation, the share of our niche formulation is growing compared to the simple dosage forms, right?

items.statement: Received 27 DCGI approvals in Q1 FY26 vs 31 in full FY25; includes Trelagliptin, Relugolix, Dapagliflozin combinations
items.quote: During the quarter, we received 27 DCGI approvals. This is a significant improvement as compared to the 31 approvals we received during the entire last year.

items.statement: Filed 24 new patents in CDMO business in Q1 FY26; granted one patent for Doxylamine-Pyridoxine nausea formulation
items.quote: Additionally, we filed 24 new patents this quarter in our CDMO business. We further commercialized triple-layered tablets for the first time this quarter, a novel formulation to improve patients' compliance.

items.statement: Received ANVISA Brazil approval for injectable plant 3 and GMP Russia for hormone plant 4 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: We received the ANVISA Brazil approval for our injectable plant 3 and GMP Russia for our hormone plant 4.

items.statement: On track to file 3 CEP dossiers over next 12-15 months; Cefuroxime Axetil CEP validation completed
items.quote: We are on track to file 3 CEP dossier over the next 12 to 15 months. The CEP filing for Cefuroxime Axetil is on track. Validation has been completed for the CEP filing.

items.statement: Entered Nigerian market with Cephalosporin APIs in Q1 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, we mark our entry in the Nigerian market and Cephalosporin APIs with Cephalosporin API.

items.statement: Received first European dossier approval for Rivaroxaban (USD 15B+ global market); filed Dapagliflozin combination in Switzerland
items.quote: We received approvals of our first European Dossier approval for Rivaroxaban, USD 15 billion plus market globally. We also filed our first dossier in Switzerland for Dapagliflozin plus combination.

items.statement: Trade generic segment inventory and receivables exposure at Rs 54 crore; working capital investment at Rs 18 crore
items.value: Rs 54 crore exposure, Rs 18 crore WC
items.quote: Our current exposure on inventory and receivables is at Rs. 54 crores. And our working capital investment is at Rs. 18 crores.

items.statement: M&A framework targets acquiring missing dosage form capabilities or market access for global expansion, open to India or overseas
items.quote: One is if we can acquire a dosage form capability we Akums Drugs & currently don't have. So, there are still few dosage forms which we don't have capabilities on and we are targeting them. Secondly, if it could give me access to other markets

items.statement: Strengthened leadership team with senior hires in IT and finance in Q1 FY26
items.quote: We strengthened our leadership team this quarter with addition of senior executives in IT, finance.

items.statement: Industry volume growth below 0.40% in Q1 FY26; IPM growth driven largely by price growth
items.quote: The Q1FY26 continued to see tepid volume growth with industry volume growth of below 0.40% and IPM growth being driven largely by price growth.

items.statement: CDMO volumes grew 1% YoY in Q1 FY26, faster than market but modest due to industry slowdown
items.quote: Coming to quarter, while CDMO volumes grew faster than the market, they were modest at 1% driven by continued slowdown in the overall industry.

items.statement: Trade generic business being consolidated; may retain only 1-2 profitable units, not a focus segment for investment
items.quote: We believe that this is not the right segment for us to stay invested in. And hence, trade generics, gradually we are bringing it down. We might retain one or two business units within this, but those should be profitable and no more bleeding.

items.statement: Semaglutide not a priority molecule; most Indian players doing in-house, limiting CDMO addressable market
items.quote: So, this is not a core segment for us. So, the reason also I will say because this is a question which comes again and again. I think there are two reasons for it. One is that most of the Indian formulation players are doing it in-house only. So, the total addressable market for a CDMO gets squeezed down.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 15%-18% for FY26, confident of hitting higher end
items.quote: I would still keep it between 15% and 18%, but I am confident of going and hitting the higher range of this 15%-18% range that I have said.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 13%-15% for FY26
items.quote: Excluding these provisions, our margin stood at around 14%, which is within our guiding range of 13%-15%.

items.statement: Total trip volumes grew around 20% year-on-year in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The total trip volumes grew around 20% year-on-year.

items.statement: Onboarded 53 new clients in Q1 FY26, active client base now 1,189
items.quote: We onboarded 53 new clients during the quarter, taking our active client base to 1,189.

items.statement: Added 7 ETS customers in Q1 FY26, 5 of which were GCCs
items.quote: We added around 7 customers in employee transportation, out of which I think around 5 customers were GCCs only.

items.statement: 59% of Q1 FY26 revenue from clients with over 5-year tenure
items.quote: 59% of our Q1 FY '26 revenue came from clients who have been with us over 5 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.07% in Q1 FY26 vs 13.9% in Q1 FY25, 183 bps moderation due to provisions
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 12.07% in Q1 FY '26 compared to 13.9% in Q1 FY '25 with 183 bps moderation reflecting new practice of provisioning expenses like employee engagement, annual bonuses, whose impact on the EBITDA is 0.70%, along with prudent provisioning of doubtful debts from a government client whose impact is 1.10% over the EBITDA for strengthening the long-term business resilience.

items.statement: Gross margin between 27% and 28% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So gross margin is somewhere around 27.5% on between 27% and 28%.

items.statement: CCR gross margin 8%-9% higher than ETS
items.quote: I would say there would be around 8%-9% difference in the margins at the gross level.

items.statement: Other expenses include exceptional doubtful debt provision, run rate to normalize
