items.quote: So the Rs. 8 crores are something which includes an exceptional item which we have provided against the doubtful debts. So it will remain minus to that. It will remain within the same parameters during this coming quarter as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex Rs 13 crore for 113 own vehicles, additional Rs 6 crore orders placed for 60-70 vehicles for Q2
items.quote: So in this quarter, we have done CAPEX of around Rs. 13 Cr. So far, we have procured around 113 vehicles. So our CAPEX is Rs. 13 Cr for this quarter. Also, during this quarter, we have placed orders around Rs. 6 crores with around 60-70 vehicles, they will deliver during this 2nd quarter.

items.statement: Annual capex run rate around Rs 35 crore based on previous year trend
items.quote: So it should be around Rs. 35 Cr. If we see the previous, it is not fixed, it may be on the higher side also and around that also. But keeping the previous year trend, it should be around Rs. 35 Cr.

items.statement: Fleet capacity expanded to 15,000+ vehicles with 946 own fleet, added 113 own vehicles in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our fleet capacity also expanded to 15,000 plus vehicles with 946 own fleet. This enables agile, asset light scalability. We also added 113 own fleet during Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Own vehicle utilization over 90%
items.quote: So our own vehicles that we have, we have more than 90% utilization of our own vehicles.

items.statement: Receivable days around 45 days as of June 2025
items.quote: It is around 45 days for our company.

items.statement: Net cash position Rs 123 crore as of June 2025
items.quote: Its availability is Rs. 123 crores.

items.statement: Actively looking for acquisition targets that are culturally fit and add value
items.quote: We are still looking for the right fit for an acquisition. Beyond buying the own cars, that is one goal that we have, but it is only the right fit both culturally and in point of view of returns.

items.statement: ETS:CCR revenue mix 60:40 in Q1 FY26 vs 55:45 in Q4 FY25, expected to remain in 40-60 range
items.quote: However, it has declined sequentially from Q1 FY '25. It is mainly on account of a change in the mix of ETS and CCR, which is 60 to 40 in Q1 FY '26, in comparison with 55 to 45 in Q4 FY '25.

items.statement: GCCs contribute around 60% of ETS revenue
items.quote: So GCCs are our large clients in the ETS segment. And I would say the contribution of GCCs in the ETS would be around 60%.

items.statement: 30% of Q1 FY26 bookings via CabDrive Pro, API integrations, and customer app
items.quote: 30% of this quarter's bookings were powered by CabDrive Pro, by API integrations, and our customer app, which our technology channels to receive bookings.

items.statement: New version of full-stack technology RentNet implementation started
items.quote: Implementation of a new version of our full-stack technology, RentNet, has also started, which will result in greater efficiencies.

items.statement: Doubtful debt provision 1.10% EBITDA impact from government client, not expected to recur
items.quote: Along with prudent provisioning of doubtful debts from a government client whose impact is 1.10% over the EBITDA for strengthening the long-term business resilience.

items.statement: No recurring doubtful debt cost expected, bad debts historically minimal
items.quote: There is no such recurring cost we are expecting as of now.

items.statement: Revenue grew 21.65% YoY to Rs 1,811.19 million in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The revenue from operation for this quarter stood at Rs. 1,811.19 million as compared to Rs. 1,488.89 million in Q1 FY '25, reflecting year-on-year growth of 21.65%.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 5.59% YoY to Rs 218.55 million in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA increased by 5.59% in Q1 FY '26 to Rs. 218.55 million as compared to Rs. 206.98 million in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: PAT flat at Rs 132.87 million in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The PAT for this quarter stood same in line with the last year quarter around Rs. 132.87 million.

items.statement: Targets 3x EBITDA increase from FY25 to FY29 driven by ethanol capacity and bio-based specialty chemicals
items.quote: I think what we have announced is from FY '25 to FY '29, this 3x increase in margins in EBITDA and we have identified two pivots.

items.statement: Bio-based specialty chemicals EBITDA margin target over 15% by FY29
items.quote: Ma'am, in that presentation, we have identified in FY '29, the biobased specialty chemicals, we are saying EBITDA to sales margin in excess of 15% is what we have articulated.

items.statement: Grain distillery EBITDA contribution from Q4 FY26; major 3x EBITDA impact from FY27 onwards
items.quote: with this expansion of 200 kilo liters per day of the grain distillery plant, this will start giving me the EBITDA from Q4 of FY '26 and the de-bottlenecking of the bio-based chemicals what we are doing, you see a transition in the financial year 2026. items.statement: Imperial Blue funding: ~Rs. 2,300 crore preferential issue (board approved, pending shareholder approval) + debt; target net debt/EBITDA <1.0x by FY29

items.statement: Pro forma portfolio post-Imperial Blue: ~two-thirds Whisky, >30% Brandy saliency
items.quote: Essentially you are looking at two-thirds of the business being Whisky in steady state, current state business. Brandy having a more than 30% saliency on top of that.

items.statement: Luxury/super-premium portfolio expanding: Monarch Legacy Edition Brandy in 3 states; Samsara brands (Gin, Rum, Vodka) distribution commenced via Spaceman Spirits Lab usership agreement
items.quote: Monarch Legacy Edition Brandy, our first luxury foray, is now available in Maharashtra, Goa, and Puducherry. Q1 has also seen the commencement of our distribution of Samsara brands on the back of our usership agreement with Spaceman Spirits Lab, our investee company.

items.statement: Invested >Rs. 10 crore in Spaceman Spirits Lab, raising stake to 21.36% from 12.98%; option to acquire additional stake at pre-determined valuation upon milestones
items.quote: you would have also seen the disclosure last week wherein we have announced our investment of more than Rs. 10 crore in Spaceman, taking our shareholding to 21.36% from 12.98%. items.statement: Bombay High Court upheld TI's ownership of Mansion House and Savoy Club trademarks, ensuring exclusive sale
items.quote: it gives me great pleasure to reiterate that the Honourable Bombay High Court has upheld TI's ownership of Mansion House and Savoy Club trademarks, ensuring continued, uninterrupted, and exclusive sale under these brands.

items.statement: Maharashtra MML policy circular recently issued; eligibility under examination; current Maharashtra saliency low single-digit
items.quote: Maharashtra recently they have come out with an MML policy- Maharashtra Made Liquor which would be available for distilleries and bottling unitsin Maharashtra. We are still examining because the circular has come out very recently. We are examining the eligibility criterion, but that could perhaps be an interesting segment for us to operate in provided, of course, we are eligible.

items.statement: ENA and Glass prices stable; conducive input cost environment expected to continue
items.quote: On the input side, ENA and Glass prices have remained stable and we are hopeful of a continued conducive input cost environment.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs. 163 crore; subsidy income booked as received (Rs. 38.6 crore in Q1)
items.quote: Our focus drive on cash flow management continues and we now stand at a net cash level of Rs. 163 crore, showcasing our balance sheet strength.

items.statement: Target net debt/EBITDA <1.0x by FY29 post Imperial Blue acquisition funding
items.quote: the balance will be funded through debt and further expect to reduce debt over time such that the Net Debt to EBITDA falls below 1.0x by FY29.

items.statement: Income tax appeal pending; assume full tax incidence from July 1, 2025 for prudence
items.quote: Our appeal with additional income tax is still under discussion. We don't have any update on that. For prudent purpose, we suggest that from 1st July, you may assume full incident of tax And as and when we have an update from CITF, we will get back.

items.statement: Imperial Blue integration timeline ~6 months post-closing; details limited due to confidentiality and pre-closing restrictions
items.quote: I think as we move along, we will know. But yes, you can consider that 6 months is the integration time that we are looking at.

items.statement: No combined margin guidance for FY26/FY27 including Imperial Blue; will provide post-closing
items.quote: Sincerely, we are very sorry but we are not guiding towards the combined business as it stands today. We will be more than happy to answer any questions once the closing happens.

items.statement: Revenue guidance revised to Rs 1,650-1,700 crore for FY26, implying 15-16% growth
items.quote: But our expectation is that although we have said that 20 % - 22% is our expectation in the last quarter call, but I think we will be going towards between 15% - 16%. This is roughly about Rs. 1,650 crores – Rs. 1,700 crores is what we are expecting.

items.statement: Revenue growth now expected at 15-17% for FY26
items.quote: I think now we are looking at maybe range of 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Q1 beer volume down 2.5% YoY; industry down 2-3% due to unseasonal rains and Karnataka policy
items.quote: Beer volume is 8.5 million cases. IMFL registered 4 lakh cases and with a growth of 58% versus last year Q1 , beer is down by around 2.5%, mainly led by industry and some issues in Karnataka in terms of unfavorable policy for us.

items.statement: Karnataka industry volumes declined over 20% in Q1 due to unseasonal rains and higher excise duties
items.quote: Industry has declined by 20-odd percentage vis-à-vis last year quarter.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin at 13.6%; net profit margin at 7.9%
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was at Rs. 721 million with a margin of close to 13.6%. Furthermore, net profit for the quarter stood at Rs. 421 million with a margin of 7.9%.

items.statement: Margins expected to be maintained or higher than last year in coming quarters
items.quote: Yes, yes. We will be able to maintain the margin. In fact, post higher margin as compared to last year. That is how it looks as of now.

items.statement: UP plant Phase-I beer capacity of 1 crore cases per annum; commissioning expected by H1 FY27 (Aug-Sep 2026)
items.quote: So, we are coming up with a beer capacity of 1 crore cases per annum. Hiten Boricha: Okay. Nakul Sethi: And we expect that by the first half of 2026 - 2027, the beer capacity would be on stream

Now it is a composite. So, beer is available now has gone up by about 2,000 outlets or 3,000 outlets

items.statement: Karnataka additional excise duty rolled back from Rs 1,050 to Rs 750-800 per case for affordable beer

items.quote: Yes, we have roughly lost about 4 % - 5% and we have recovered 1% of that. The trend is showing that 1% is possible to gain and 2% - 3% is possible in this quarter, I think. It is possible.

items.statement: UBL growth driven by Andhra Pradesh where SOM is not present; SOM tender pending in AP

So, the growth is coming from there. Mukund Agarwal: Okay. Diwakaran S.: And we are not present there. Our tender is pending

items.statement: Inducted independent directors with good repute to improve corporate governance
items.quote: And it is our endeavor to have good corporate governance, and we are working towards it. That is why we have got, we have inducted independent directors who have got good repute in the market.

items.statement: Child labour issue pertained to private limited company; no pending litigation; company claims it was unnecessarily targeted
items.quote: So, there is number one, as we have given out press release, also it pertains to our private limited company. And I think nothing has come out of it. I think it was, I mean, we were unnecessarily targeted. So, as of now, there is nothing about it.

items.statement: Beer realization Rs 566 per case in Q1, up from Rs 550 in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Beer realization stood at Rs. 566 per case, up from Rs. 550 in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Premium beer segment growing at 25-30%; Woodpecker targeting 12-15% of market
items.quote: Almost 12 % - 15% of the market is growing at 25 % - 30%. And in that market is where Woodpecker is playing.

items.statement: Telangana re-entry under consideration but lower priority than Andhra Pradesh due to profitability concerns
items.quote: Yes, it is in the cards and we are constantly in touch with the government there and the authorities. But in terms of priority, I w ould rather get it to AP first than Telangana , because Telangana continues to be not very profitable for the existing business.

items.statement: Bangalore airport T2 and T1 brand visibility effort underway; expect execution in 6-8 months
items.quote: There is an effort to set up there in T2 and T1. There is an effort, we will do it sir. We can do it in the next 6 months - 8 months.

items.statement: Single Malt whisky in pipeline; premium IMFL focus over next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: We have a few more premium SOM Distilleries & products in the pipeline, including a Single Malt. I think that is where the growth is going to lie in the next three quarters to four quarters

items.statement: Completed Rs 381 crore rights issue and Rs 911 crore preferential issue in Q1FY26
items.value: Rs 381 crore rights issue and Rs 911 crore preferential issue

items.statement: Expect disbursement momentum to pick up from Q2FY26 as seasonal effects subside
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect disbursement momentum to pick up from Q2 as seasonal effects subside.

items.statement: Target embedded finance to be 10-12% of total AUM in next 2-3 years
items.quote: We would like to be around 10% to 12% of the total AUM.

items.quote: Our emerging market business at end of March '25 was about 22% contribution to the overall portfolio. And we want to take it to around 35% by end of the year.

items.statement: Foresee yields to go up by 0.25% to 0.5% in coming year due to mix shift
items.quote: So, we foresee the yields to go up by 0.25 % to 0.5% in the coming year.

items.statement: Target steady state ROA of 4% in next 6-8 quarters with Profectus acquisition and operational leverage
items.quote: And we have talked about that earlier as well, is that at a steady state, we want to reach 4% ROA levels with Profectus acquisition and operational leverage which we are getting.

items.statement: Expect ROA to increase by 0.2% to 0.3% each quarter on steady state basis in interim period
items.quote: In the interim for about a year, it would increase on a steady state level. Each quarter about 0.2% to 0.3%, that is what the estimate is.

items.statement: Expanded emerging market footprint from 150 locations in FY24 to 309 locations as of June 2025
items.quote: In this journey, we have expanded our footprint from 150 locations in FY '24 to 309 locations as of June '25.

items.statement: Emerging market network near full rollout with 286 operational branches by June 2025 and clear path for more expansion by September 2025
items.quote: Our emerging market business expanded to 286 operational branches by June with a clear path for more expansion by September 2025.

items.quote: So, out of total 286 branches, 121 branches have already broken even and others in next 12 months to 15 months are on the path of breaking even.

items.statement: AUM closed at Rs 12,081 crore, up 31% year-on-year
items.quote: Now on business update, our AUM closed at Rs. 12,081 crores, up 31% year -on-year.

items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter were Rs. 1,599 crores compared to Rs. 1,146 crores in Q1FY'25, the sequential decline from Rs. 2,436 crores in Q4 FY '25 was by design and in line with our budgets.

items.statement: Total income grew 40% YoY to Rs 421.8 crore; net total income grew 31% YoY to Rs 216.5 crore; PAT up 12% YoY to Rs 34.1 crore
items.quote: Our total income grew 40% year-on-year to Rs. 421.8 crores. Our net total income stood at Rs. 216.5 crores, a 31% year -on-year growth. Our PAT came at Rs. 34.1 crores for the quarter, up by 12% year -on-year.

items.statement: ROA excluding branch expansion impact at 2.3% in Q1FY26, in line with internal estimates
items.quote: ROA for Q1FY'26, if we exclude the branch expansion impact, would be at 2.3%, which is in li ne with our internal estimates.

items.quote: Our unsecured portfolio though has witnessed some stress on account of over -leveraging. As mentioned earlier, we have tightened our underwriting and have curtailed disbursements in last two quarters. (Rs. 186 crores in Q1FY '26 vs peak Rs. 623 crores in Q2FY '25).

items.statement: Credit cost was Rs 47.7 crore in Q1FY26, up 44% YoY but lower than Q4FY25's Rs 54.3 crore
items.quote: Our credit cost was Rs. 47.7 crores, representing a 44% year -on-year increase, but lower than Q4FY'25, which was Rs. 54.3 crores.

items.quote: Our GNPA for vintage branches is at this point in time 2.4%, well within the estimates and for newer branches , it is 0.2%. Similarly, for credit costs, for greater than 18 months, the average credit cost is about 1%. For newer branches at this point in time, it is 0.3%.

items.statement: Profectus Capital maintains gross NPA of 1.6% and net NPA of 1.1% as of March 2025
items.quote: Profectus has demonstrated stable portfolio expansion, building its access under management to Rs. 3,468 crores as of March 2025 with presence across 7 states through a 28-branch network and over 800 member teams, all while maintaining a gross NP A of 1.6% and a net NP A of 1.1%.

items.statement: Total debt at Rs 7,586 crore as of June 30 with over 50 lenders; long-term rating A+ with positive outlook from India Ratings
items.quote: Total debt at Rs. 7,586 crores as of June '30 and with over 50 lenders, we have a very diversified liability profile. Our long-term rating is A+ rating watch with positive implications, assigned by India Ratings.

items.quote: One of the biggest input to our ROA journey, which is less in our control is our cost of borrowing. Our cost of borrowing vis-à-vis our peer set has remained elevated. It's roughly around 150 to 200 basis point more than most of our peer set.

So, today, if any state bank of India or a large NBFC is a co-lending partner, they have to take, carry the risk of the total co-origination based co-lending which they do. Now, because of that, they charge a certain

items.quote: My view is that from January to two quarters, there would be disruption to reset the new process. I don't think so the technology is a challenge because in most, at least in o ur case, with most of the banks, we are fully integrated both in simultaneous lending and post disb

items.statement: Portfolio LTV at 55% at portfolio level; prime secured loans up to 80% LTV on self-occupied residential, commercial, industrial properties

items.quote: No, we do not do buy now, pay later. We do not do PL. UGRO is a 100% business loan company. We only give loan to a Udyam Aadhar registered MSME customer.

items.quote: This quarter, we also elevated Anuj as our CEO. He has been with me since UGRO's very inception. When we started UGRO, the organizational design was to have a CEO for the business so that I can focus on strategic things which are investor interface, lender interface, organic and inorganic business growth opportunity and CEO can focus on core operating performance.

items.statement: CFO Kishore and Amit exited; Shilpa Bhatter elevated from Deputy CFO to CFO as pre-planned succession
items.quote: On CFO again, it's a personal choice. Obviously, a CFO role in UGRO is a difficult role. items.statement: Industry facing higher stress in certain unsecured segments; UGRO exposure limited and ring-fenced with tightened underwriting
items.quote: The industry is currently facing higher stress in certain unsecured segments, but our exposure there is limited and ring -fenced. Approximately 70% of our book is secured and our underwriting filters are sharper than ever.

items.statement: Anticipate certain market pockets will show stress; proactively pivoted asset engine as a measure
items.quote: Our continuous endeavor has been to deliver consistent growth, consistent performance, but we continue to believe that certain pockets of the market would show some amount of stress. We have been anticipating that and we have pivoted some of our asset engine accordingly as a proactive measure.

items.statement: Expects Q2 revenue and profitability to be substantially higher than Q1 sequentially
items.quote: Sequentially also, we are looking at very, very healthy growth in revenue and profitability.

items.statement: Projects healthy double-digit revenue and profitability growth for engineering services in FY26
items.quote: As I previously guided, we project very healthy double-digit growth in revenue and profitability for this business unit in this fiscal.

items.statement: Targets finance cost as percentage of revenue to return to 3.xx% range in next 2 quarters
items.quote: We can commit to you that, that is definitely not a number that you're going to see next quarter. You will see it get below that to 3.xx, and we will maintain it at that.

items.statement: Targets working capital days to reduce from 76 to 60 days long-term
items.quote: We believe that the long-term potential steady state, that is about 60 days.

items.statement: Expects Raebareli plant utilization to reach 70% in Q2 and 80% by year-end
items.quote: We are at 65%. I think in the next quarter, we hit 70%. Our goal is to hit 80% by the end of this year.

items.statement: Committed to double-digit revenue and profitability growth long-term across 5 prioritized BUs
items.quote: We are committed to double-digit growth in revenue and profitability over the long term.

items.statement: PEB order backlog strong and growing with INR200 crore order from JSW and INR300+ crore from Reliance
items.quote: We have received a INR200 crores order from JSW. We've received from Tata Electronics. We performed in excess of INR100 crores, INR150 crores, I think, INR157 crores. So, Reliance has been in excess of INR300 crores.

items.statement: Body-in-White secured new clients including Hyundai, Sears Automotive, TIVOLT, Ashok Leyland
items.quote: We had mentioned last time that we now have -- other than Stellantis, we have Hyundai, we have Sears Automotive, we have TIVOLT, Ashok Leyland, and there are several others also that are coming in.

items.statement: Boilers and process equipment order backlog grown strongly to INR110 crores with further additions expected
items.quote: Order backlog has grown strongly to INR110 crores, with further additions expected.

items.quote: Order backlog is good. So, we maintain something called an active order backlog, which is a very good lead indicator for what our revenue for the next quarter is going to be.

items.statement: PBT margin at 4.75% in Q1 due to labor issues, expects improvement in Q2 as mix shifts to higher-margin businesses
items.quote: Our PBT margin for the first quarter stands at 4.75%. items.statement: India PEB margins 200-300 bps below competitors on PBT basis, working to improve
items.quote: Our PEB India margins are lower than our competitors. So, we are hard at work trying to get that up. We are about 200, 300 basis points less than our competitors on a PBT basis.

items.statement: Raebareli plant commissioned with 20,000 tons/year capacity, INR300 crore revenue potential at 80-85% utilization
items.quote: Raebareli firing on all cylinders gives us INR300 crores of revenue.

items.statement: US hydraulics faces 50% tariff from August 27, making cost structure not viable, redirecting volumes to Europe, Canada, Australia, New Zealand
items.quote: The upcoming 50% tariff, which is set to be effective August 27, well, it makes the cost structure not really viable. So, it could affect our US sales. Our mitigation plans are in place, and we are redirecting volumes to Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.

items.quote: Working capital days currently stands at 76. This is higher than planned, again, the same labor issue that I had mentioned.

items.statement: Finance cost at 4.16% of revenue vs guided 4%, expects to return to 3.xx% in next 2 quarters as working capital normalizes
items.quote: The overall finance costs as a percentage is 4.16%, while we have guided you to 4%. These are due to the delayed dispatches that we had at Raebareli plant and due to the lower revenue, which are now behind us.

items.quote: All of that will come with keeping our debt equity at the 0.7, 0.6 number, keeping our overall interest cost as a percentage of revenue at the 3.xx number is the way we intend to manage this company.

items.quote: I do want to guide that this revenue stream represents about 2.2% of Pennar's entire revenue. So we do not, on an overall basis, expect a significant impact.

items.quote: If you include our India and US revenue, about 40% of our overall revenue for the company is metal buildings and pre-engineered buildings and high-rise buildings.

items.statement: Labor supply constraint in Q1 caused INR100 crore revenue loss, resolved by mid-June with expanded labor pool from West Bengal, Orissa and more contractors
items.quote: I think we have lost close to INR100 crores in revenue in Q1 because of that.

items.statement: ROCE at 22.3% using EBIT/(total assets - current liabilities), evaluating inclusion of short-term borrowings
items.quote: Now in relation to ROCE, we've always used a definition of EBIT divided by capital employed. We've been in touch with some of you. We've been talking to our investors and discussing this internally.

items.statement: ROE at 12.12% annualized for Q1, projects improvement through the year
items.quote: Our ROE, of course, will remain unchanged calculation-wise, and it's at 12.12% for the quarter annualized, and we project improvements on this in the course of this financial year.

items.statement: PEB India order book near INR855 crores, US PEB at USD54 million, both trending upward with INR200+ crores new orders booked recently
items.quote: The order book now stands at USD54 million and India PEB order book close to INR855 crores.

items.statement: Expects margin improvement as portfolio mix shifts to higher-margin businesses (PEB, Body-in-White, boilers, engineering services)
items.quote: We absolutely expect our margins to improve well once our portfolio mix shift to higher-margin businesses continues.

items.quote: Other expenses increased by INR37 crores. The variance is predominantly account of -- in stand-alone by INR26 crores, which comes through higher erection expenses, subcontract expense and spare consumables.

items.statement: Y-o-Y total revenues and total income declined 10.4% to INR 661 crores due to U.S. tariff uncertainties

items.statement: Spinning utilization at 99%, Sheeting at 60%, Terry at 68%, largely range bound with minor realization fluctuations

items.statement: India market revenue streams growing Y-o-Y across three brands (Himeya, Atmosphere, Liv) covering broad price points and categories
items.quote: We continue to see Y-o-Y growth in our revenue streams from our India market.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 2,405 crores from INR 2,425 crores at March 31, 2025
items.quote: During the first quarter, we continued to bring our debt down vis-à-vis March. Our net debt stood at INR 2,405 crores versus INR 2,425 crores during the end of March 31, 2025.

items.statement: India business expected to close to double from previous fiscal; targeting INR 800-1,000 crores over next few years
items.quote: We expect our India business -- India business to close to double from the previous fiscal. And we seem to be broadly on track vis-a-vis our vision of taking India to close to INR 1,000 crores, INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores over the next few years.

items.statement: Servicing 35 non-U.S. jurisdictions and over 70 non-U.S. clients; priority to expand presence in non-U.S. jurisdictions
items.quote: We currently service 35 non-U.S. jurisdictions. And we are taking and making additional efforts to enhance our presence across these jurisdictions to reduce some of our dependence on the U.S. given the volatility.

items.statement: Up to 25% tariffs not seen as material challenge; India 5% better than China, 6% worse than Pakistan; wait-and-watch on tariffs above 25%
items.quote: We believe that up to 25% of tariffs shouldn't create any material disturbance or any stir of any kind or any interruption of any kind because we will be comparable to other competing home textile geographies such as China and Pakistan.

items.statement: No clients have pulled back orders or asked to stop production; clients in wait-and-watch mode on tariffs above 25%
items.quote: The customers have not -- as we speak, we haven't seen any clients pull back on any orders nor have we seen any clients ask us to stop production at this point.

items.statement: No specific plans to relocate manufacturing facilities due to regulatory limitations and asset constraints
items.quote: There are limitations in doing so, Survankar, because of the underlying regulations and the assets that are involved in the process. So we don't have any specific plans of relocating any manufacturing facilities at this point.

items.statement: EBITDA margin band 18-22% shared as model expectation, not FY26 guidance; 150-200 bps tariff impact share expected on first 10%
items.quote: As far as margins is concerned, we have shared with stakeholders earlier that our EBITDA margin band is 18% to 22%, and that's where we believe our model should deliver. That's not a guidance for '26, but that's more a band guidance that we believe we should be at, at any given time.

items.statement: First 10% tariff phase: clients shared some burden, rest absorbed by retailers or passed to consumers; 10-25% bucket to follow similar pattern with slightly lower impact
items.quote: we expect 150 basis to 200 basis point share somewhere in that range. And of course, it's dependent on product mix. And we had also said that as far as the first phase of 10% went, the clients have reached out on sharing some of the burden on tariffs, and we said that we will share a little bit of burdens of the total.

items.statement: No conclusive discussions on 25-50% tariff bucket; unprecedented situation being digested; wait-and-watch mode
items.quote: The last 25 to 50 bucket, there has been no discussions yet because quite honestly, it's been just a week since it's been imposed. And everybody is just digesting how to handle an uncertainty and a phenomenon of this nature, which is unprecedented and sort of as far as India is concerned, and we haven't seen something as absurd as this before.

items.statement: No order cancellations for Himatsingka; media reports on cancellations may cover other categories like apparel
items.quote: There is no such things as client cancelling orders of Indian exporters. That's a broad and sweeping comment, Bhavin. I cannot say that nothing has occurred. I can say that nothing has occurred vis-à-vis Himatsingka.

items.statement: Brands used as total solution providers, not to mitigate B2B risk; margin impact neutral (100-200 bps max); brands add value in India, e-comm, Qcom channels
items.quote: we use, at least as far as Himatsingka is concerned, brand portfolios to optimally position ourselves as total solution providers and make sure that we are available to clients with a more holistic portfolio of solutions than without it.

items.statement: U.S. revenue share ~60% and reducing; target below 50% in 18-24 months in normalized scenario
items.quote: pure U.S. should be in the region of 60% going south. Over the last 2 fiscals, it has corrected substantially because of our Terry division ramping up in other jurisdictions as well and so on, plus our foray into India and things like that. So 60% and reducing.

items.statement: Himeya brand at 3,500-4,000 points of sale; Liv brand targeting 10,000-12,000 points of sale; expanding across bedding, bath, drapery, upholstery
items.quote: Our footprint for our Himeya brand is in the region of 4,000 -- around 3,500 to 4,000 points of sale. And we intend to take our Liv brand to over 10,000, 12,000 points of sale at this point.

items.statement: Revenue loss from key customer exits (BBB) and brand recalibration caused headwinds; growth appears sluggish due to making up lost revenue
items.quote: we were also unfortunately in a position where we had to face revenue loss because of key customers that were not part of our portfolio anymore vis-à-vis BBB and things of that nature. And we also had to face revenue loss on account of brand recalibration.

items.statement: Capex program concluded except annual organic needs; 2-year timeframe to optimize utilization to high 90s and deliver ~INR 4,000 crores revenue within 18-22% EBITDA band
items.quote: we believe that in a 2-year timeframe, we were looking at essentially sweating our capacities, and we felt that we should be able to optimize our utilization levels, take it to the high 90s and be in a position to deliver revenues of approximately INR4,000 crores and stay within our EBITDA band of 18% to 22%.

items.statement: Other expenses down 30% Y-o-Y due to brand cost reduction; expected to remain range bound unless unusual tariff-related events
items.quote: We believe it should be range bound. It's reflective of some of the reduction in brand costs and things of that nature. So we believe, Nirav, that this -- I mean, this proportion should be range bound now unless there is an event of some kind as a result of these tariffs, which causes us to enhance certain expenditure.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin target of 18% average, with FY27 target of 19-20%
items.quote: Yes, we definitely expect it to grow from the current 13.3% levels to an average of 18% for the full year and we are quite confident of that both in the domestic and international market.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target of 19-20%
items.quote: If we are expecting 18% for the full year, we are confident that next year this will improve further and believe margins in the range of 19% to 20% are achievable going forward.

items.statement: Total FY26 capex of Rs. 150 crore including Rs. 25-30 crore maintenance capex
items.quote: The maintenance CAPEX is expected to be Rs. 25 to Rs. 30 crore and the total CAPEX to be around Rs. 150 crore.

items.statement: Rs. 60 crore investment plan in Thailand under implementation
items.quote: For the future, we have a Rs. 60 crore investment plan in Thailand which is under implementation.

items.statement: Ranchi expansion 70% commissioned, full completion by end of Q2 FY26, adding 40,000 tons overall capacity including 20,000 tons rope capacity
items.quote: As of now, we have already installed about 70% of the capacity and the remaining 30% installation will be completed by end of Q2, around October.

items.statement: Sizable US tender secured providing strong order visibility for rest of FY26
items.quote: We have secured a sizable tender that provides strong order visibility for the rest of the year alongside our regular business in the US.

items.statement: Oceanfibre synthetic sling secured heavy lift offshore wind order, expected to become meaningful vertical in 18-24 months
items.quote: We will be supplying heavy lift sling for the critical offshore wind market, which is a high value, high margin product, and we have already secured the order, and we will be supplying it in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 operating EBITDA margin 16.3%, EBITDA per ton Rs. 28,502
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 145 crore, with a margin of 16.3% and an EBITDA per ton of Rs. 28,502 per ton.

items.statement: Wire rope EBITDA per ton Rs. 55,000-60,000, wire segment Rs. 12,000-15,000, LRPC Rs. 2,000-3,000 per ton
items.quote: But if we do a rough calculation for wire ropes, it will be in the range of Rs. 55,000 to Rs. 60,000 per ton, as most of the fixed cost is allocated to the wire ropes.

items.statement: US tariff impact largely passed through to distributors and end customers for high-value products
items.quote: In most cases, we have been able to pass on a large part of the tariff increase to our distributors or to our end customers.

items.statement: Employee costs reduced from Rs. 118.6 crore quarterly average in FY25 to Rs. 113.2 crore in Q1 FY26, further savings expected
items.quote: Employee costs have reduced from an average of Rs. 118.6 crore per quarter in FY25 to Rs. 113.2 crore in Q1 FY26, with further savings expected as we expand our shared services back office in India.

items.statement: Repaid US$3.4 million Singapore loan and plan to repay €2 million Netherlands loan, impact from Q2 onwards
items.quote: We have repaid the entire US$3.4 million loan in Singapore and plan to fully repay €2 million loan in Netherlands, with the impact of these actions expected to reflect from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced from 209 days peak in Sep'24 to 196 days in Q1 FY26, targeting further 10-day reduction
items.quote: In September last year it was at 209 days at its peak and now it has come down to 196 days as of this last quarter. We are confident that this positive trajectory will continue.

items.statement: Operating cash flow at 95% of EBITDA in Q1 FY26, targeting >100% by year-end
items.quote: We converted about 95% of the operating EBITDA to cash and by the end of the year we are targeting to take this even more than 100% levels which we are confident of achieving through overall better financial discipline and working capital management.

items.statement: Achieved consolidated net cash position of Rs. 14 crore as of June 2025 vs net debt of Rs. 63 crore in March 2025
items.quote: As of 30th June 2025, we have achieved a consolidated net cash position of Rs. 14 crore compared to a net debt of Rs. 63 crore on March '25.

items.statement: European demand strong across wind energy, renewable energy, oil & offshore, crane and elevator segments
items.quote: Demand remains fairly strong across wind energy, renewable energy, oil & offshore, and the crane and elevator segments. We expect to see decent growth in Europe in this financial year.

items.statement: Domestic elevator segment growing fast due to multi-storied construction in tier 2/3 cities, crane market also strong
items.quote: The elevator segment is definitely growing fairly fast in the domestic market. With the construction of multi-storied buildings in tier two and tier three cities, we are seeing a lot of demand coming up.

items.statement: Wire segment 32.3% YoY growth driven by auto sector, door springs, zinc-aluminum wires for rockfall barriers
items.quote: We are also working on door springs, as one example, and zinc-aluminum wires, which are used for rockfall barriers and certain critical spring applications. These areas are our focus, and we believe this will continue to be an important vertical going forward.

items.statement: LRPC segment declining, focus shifting to plasticated LRPC for better margins
items.quote: Yes, we expect it to be at similar levels or would be declining, and the plasticated LRPC which is the value added should gradually be going up.

items.statement: Domestic wire rope market share 65-70%, maintained through strong dealer network and technical team
items.quote: In the domestic wire rope segment, Usha Martin holds about 65% to 70% market share. We have a very strong dealer network and a highly capable technical team that supports customer service along with our dealers.

items.statement: US market tariff creates level playing field at 50% for all importers except UK at 25%, domestic US producers unlikely to add capacity due to uncertainty
items.quote: While 50% is the tariff, it is the same for others as well. We compete with the Koreans and we compete with other people in the India market. So, for everyone, it is 50% as opposed to the reciprocal tariff, where it is different tariff for different countries.

items.statement: US Section 232 tariffs at 50% for steel wire rope, UK at 25%, reciprocal tariffs separate
items.quote: So, with regard to the U.S. market for steel wire rope, which fall under the Sec. 232, the tariffs are 50% across the board. So, the reciprocal tariff is separate and this 50% tariff for our particular product category is different and applies to all countries except UK, which is at 25%.

items.statement: Direct shipments of high-value segments from India to European customers started, repeat orders received
items.quote: We have also successfully increased direct shipments of high-value segments from India to the European customers, which demonstrates acceptance of our products in these quality-conscious markets. It is encouraging to see that we have already started to get repeat orders.

items.statement: UK plant retained with flexibility to shift 10-15% of US volumes if economics favorable, no additional capex needed
items.quote: If an opportunity arises to supply from the UK, we can definitely shift 10% to 15% of the volume through our UK plant. However, we do not foresee that situation occurring in the near term.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 consolidated revenue Rs. 887 crore, 7.4% YoY growth; wire rope 72% revenue share, 7.9% YoY growth
items.quote: In Q1 of FY26, our consolidated net revenue from operations stood at Rs. 887 crore, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 7.4% over Rs. 826 crore in Q1 of FY25.

items.statement: US tariff environment uncertain and changing daily, company remains cautiously optimistic
items.quote: So, all in all, while the environment still remains uncertain, we do not know how things will evolve overall in terms of the tariff environment. Things change every day. But as of now, we are feeling cautiously optimistic.

items.statement: Targets 12%-13% EBITDA margin by Q4 FY26 and annually next year
items.quote: we are quite confident that our profitability should k eep on increasing, and we are in line with our target of achieving 12%- 13% of EBITDA margins

items.statement: Expects INR2,652 crore revenue in FY26 per Board budget
items.quote: Now INR2,652 crores is the bud get that we declared to our Board. And that's what we are working on quarter-by-quarter, the Board is monitoring

items.statement: Expects grey iron foundry utilisation 60%-65% by FY26 year-end
items.quote: Yes, 60% to 65% by the year-end, yes.

items.statement: Targets INR1,000-1,200 crore shareholder benefit from land monetisation
items.quote: And our target is between INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores in profitability that we should get from the sale of land.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by new products and cost cutting, not Defence/Railways yet
items.quote: the EBITDA margin is going up is not because o f Defense at the moment or the Railways, it is mainly because of the new products which have been introduced and also the cost cutting, which has happened

items.statement: Order book pending execution exceeds INR1,000 crore per annum at peak
items.quote: We have given our order book that is pending for execution is already more than INR1,000 crores per annum. At the peak level, this is the business that is already on.

items.statement: New auto component business adds INR156 crore in FY26, INR550 crore next year, INR800 crore in FY28
items.quote: This year, there's an addition of INR156 crores on the new businesses. And next year, the same business translates into INR550 crores. And the year after that is around INR800 crores.

items.statement: Foundry mix shifting: iron share rising to 24%-25% by end of next year, targeting ~90% utilisation
items.quote: when we are touching 25%, which is by next yea r -- actually end of next year, we'll be almost 90% of utilization of our foundry

items.statement: Won significant export orders for iron foundry; SOP this year and Q1 next year, peak next year
items.quote: We have won significant business for our iron foundry from the export side. And those programs are under development currently, which wil l go into the SOP this year and some of them early in Q1 of the next year. Arvind Kapur: The peaking phase is next year

items.statement: RDSO registration for first Railway product expected by end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: So we'll be registering ourselves again and again -- for the first product would be by the end of Q3.

items.statement: Magnet shortage caused INR30-35 crore revenue loss in Q1; ramp-up now underway
items.quote: because of the magnet shortage and the introduction of the new component, which did not co me in because of the magnet shortage, we did lose about INR30 crores of revenue -- INR30-35 crores of revenue

items.statement: Key volume growth from alloy wheels, EV/hybrid components and pump business
items.quote: The key products on which we h ave made significant volume progress are the alloy wheel and the EV and the hybrid compo nents, and the pump business, which we are doing with our key

items.statement: OEM relationships sticky; vendor change takes 2-3 years with testing and certifications
items.quote: It's not easy to introduce new vendors. It's a time-taking proposition. So it takes 2 to 3 years. And a lot of cost and a lot of testing, etc, a lot of certifications are required to be there.

items.statement: Evaluating alternative supply routes (e.g., Vietnam) to mitigate U.S. tariff risk
items.quote: We will also look at alternatives like to give you an example, the garment industry, a lot of them have started setting up in Vietnam and other places so that we will go from here to Vietnam as there is duty free and from there, it is repackaged and sold further.

items.statement: No new deferred tax benefits expected beyond accumulated loss utilisation post-merger
items.quote: The Only thing is that our accumulated losses will be utilized. Other than that, not much profit, whatever profit is there that we have already gained, because in new scheme, there is no deferred tax thing that is going to be there additionally.

items.statement: Arvind Kapur is Chairman, CEO and MD; Kaushalendra Verma and R.K. Miglani are Executive Directors; Rakesh Sharma is CFO; Ruchika Gupta is Company Secretary
items.quote: From the managemen t, we have with us Mr. Arvind Kapur, Chairman, CEO and MD; Mr. Kaushalendra Verma, Execu tive Director; Mr. R.K. Miglani, Executive Director; Mr. Rakesh Sharma, Chief Financ ial Officer; and Ms. Ruchika Gupta, Company Secretary

items.statement: Railways: ~24-25 components delivered or sampled; 13-14 more under development for registered suppliers
items.quote: s about, I think, 24 or 25, if I remember correctly. These are mainly cast components and the ferrous foundry is utilized fully on this. items.statement: Revenue grew 8% YoY; EBITDA came in at ~1,200 million vs expected ~1,500 million due to higher employee and other expenses from digital/IT/finance transformation initiatives.
items.quote: Our revenue grew by about 8% and for that 8% our EBITDA should have been 1500 and odd million, whereas we came in at 1200.

items.statement: Contribution and gross profits remain healthy; operating profitability is strong despite higher expenses from strategic initiatives.
items.quote: Our contribution and gross profits have been quite healthy, continue to be strong.

items.statement: Employee cost rose 10% YoY; normal increments 5-6%, balance from planned headcount increase for transformation initiatives.
items.quote: Our employee cost as you will notice; its a 10% increase but the actual increment is not 10%. The normal increase has been in the range of 5% to 6% in a global context and the balance of the increase has been primarily headcount increase that we have planned and done as part of the initiatives.

items.statement: All regions grew except Europe and Australia; Europe remains economically challenging, Australia weak but recovering.
items.quote: Moving on to the sales highlight; all of our regions and countries grew except Europe and Australia. Europe continues to remain challenging economically and there are things that we need to do as well, which we have initiated as part of shifting direction. Australia, the economy has been weak, but it's coming back, and we are quite confident that with some of the things that we are doing, we will

items.statement: PBT grew 18% YoY; net cash position healthy; working capital initiatives beginning to yield results, expecting improving cash positions in coming quarters.
items.quote: At a PBT level we have grown 18% and you will see it towards the end of this presentation when you look at the consolidated or the overall financials. We have done very well in terms of our cash position, and we have managed that cash very well through our treasury and that has contributed also to a healthy PBT besides the operations.

items.statement: Inventory, receivables and overall working capital management initiatives beginning to yield results; expect improving cash positions in coming quarters.
items.quote: In my earlier call we were talking about managing our inventory, managing our receivables, managing overall working capital - all these are beginning to yield results. What you're seeing now a big contribution does not come from all the initiatives that we have kicked off for better working Capital Management. Therefore, I expect to see improving cash positions in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven by balanced mix of volume, exchange rate and price increases; volume is the largest contributor.
items.quote: Our revenue has in terms of our growth we have had, just give me a minute, quite a bit of it has been our volume growth. There has been a balance between volume growth, exchange rate as well as price increases. So, I wouldn't say that any one has been a huge contributing factor, but a large piece, a big contribution has come from volume.

items.statement: India remains strong but seeing hesitation and deferred finalizations due to US tariff uncertainty; inquiry levels strong but investments on hold.
items.quote: India has been a strong story for us, continues to remain strong, but we are beginning to see some hesitation in markets, some tentativeness brought about by all these conflicts in the different parts of the world, but more importantly the tariff situation in the US, the inquiry levels continue to be strong, but finalizations are getting deferred because people are wanting to wait and see where th

items.quote: Now with this additional 25% duty, the current initiatives that we are running and the current options that are available are not adequate. items.statement: Revenue guidance of $450 million for the year on track structurally; FX impact (rupee at 87 vs assumed) may affect reported INR revenue.
items.quote: As far as the guidance of 450 million, we are on track towards achieving it. But the question really is if the rupee becomes 90 or 87, now it's already 87. You shouldn't hold us accountable for that division. Right. So, you know, if you divide it by a larger number, obviously our India revenue is going to become smaller. But general direction structurally, yes, we are there.

items.statement: Sales mix between businesses and geographies stable, vacillating 2-3% quarter to quarter; expected to remain same going forward.
items.quote: Sales mix both between the businesses, between the two businesses and geographically has roughly been the same. It kind of vacillates 2% or 3% up and down from quarter to quarter. So, it continues to be at the same level, and we expect that this will be the case going forward as well.

items.statement: Middle East and Africa regions show strong revenue and profitability; small but robust operations.
items.quote: Moving further West into Middle East and Africa, both those regions have done well for us in the past and they continue to do well; Strong revenue and strong profitability. From a region point of view, they're still small, but they are quite robust in their operations and profits.

items.statement: Europe loss in INR terms due to strong Euro; in Euro terms keeping head above water, working on initiatives to protect bottom line and grow top line significantly.
items.quote: Europe has been a challenge. We are working towards various initiatives that will kick start for us Europe all over again. items.quote: Most of our equipment sale and aftermarket sale comes from India. There's very little, very little you can on average take about 15% as bought out there.
