items.statement: Polystyrene capex not included in current INR350 crore guidance; engineering study ongoing
items.quote: PS capex, as announced earlier, the engineering study is going on. Once it is completed, we'll let you know more details about it.

items.statement: India capacity for FY26 expected at 210,000-215,000 tons for all products
items.quote: With regards to capacity for FY '26, it will be in line with what we had given in the earlier investor presentation, which I think is to the tune of about 210,000, 215,000 tons for all the products that we produce in India.

items.statement: Thailand plant operating at 50-55% utilization with significant scope to increase
items.quote: It's between 50% to 55%.

items.statement: Thailand plant could increase revenue by 70-80% at peak utilization with current product mix
items.quote: Essentially, if you look at the revenue in Thailand that we have and you assume a similar product mix, you can see that we can essentially increase re venue by close to 70% to 80% additionally, right, from where we are at

items.statement: Q1 volumes highest ever at 51.8 KT standalone, up 8.1% QoQ despite early monsoon impact on appliances
items.quote: The volumes in India, we did close to around 51,000 tons, which is the highest sales ever done by the company.

items.statement: Air conditioning demand down ~30% due to early monsoon; two-wheeler and four-wheeler grew
items.quote: In fact, air conditioning has been down by about 30%. And that again has to do with kind of lower demand due to the early monsoon. The two-wheeler, in fact, has grown and four wheeler also has grown a little bit.

items.statement: ABS spreads historically stable on annualized basis despite monthly volatility
items.quote: So overall, they are in line with what have been historically there, barring certain factors which can influence, say, a month or two. But on an annualized basis, I think we are very much exactly where we have been for the last few years.

items.statement: Thailand margin expansion depends on capacity utilization and product mix optimization
items.quote: So, in terms of margin expansion in Thailand, again, like I mentioned, it is a function of capacity utilization. So, we will get some operating leverage over there.

items.statement: Specialty ABS share 60-70% of total ABS sales in India
items.quote: In terms of specialty ABS, again, we have close to 60% to 70% market -- our share of specialty ABS is about 60% to 70% within our total ABS that we sell and that continues to be the case.

items.statement: Thailand offers unique grades: bimodal rubber (MAC 50), refrigerant ABS, food-grade SAN, high-heat ABS
items.quote: There is a refrigerant ABS that we do from Thailand, which is a unique and value-added product. There are certain SAN grades that we make like a food-grade SAN, which goes into certain appliances where there is direct food contact, which has a higher margin.

items.statement: Added new customers in both Thailand and India; leveraging cross-approvals between geographies
items.quote: In terms of new customers in Thailand, yes, in fact, we have added quite a few customers in Thailand. In fact, both ways, we are adding new customers in India as well as Thailand.

items.statement: Almost no ABS exported from India; Thailand supplies to China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam, Thailand
items.quote: Almost no ABS, very little, if any.

items.statement: Medium to long-term export opportunity to EU from India as European plants shut due to high power costs
items.quote: But medium to long term, yes, there will be opportunities for export from India as well, which we are looking at.

items.statement: Hybrid power SPV to be active by year-end to reduce power costs in India
items.quote: We have signed, by the way, an SPV as already is publicly known to go into hybrid power from our current power source. So that, I think, will be active by the end of the year. So that will reduce our power cost also.

items.statement: Thailand conversion cost nearly double India's; reduction via process improvements and higher utilization, not major capex
items.quote: The conversion cost in Thailand is higher than India. And this is something that our team is working on. In terms of reducing it, it is not as straightforward as one would imagine. There is a lot of work that needs to happen in order to try and reduce that conversion cost.

items.statement: Inventories ramped up in March quarter for Thailand asset validation and INEOS agreement; reducing in Q1
items.quote: In India, again, we have, in fact, reduced those inventories in this quarter, there is a reduction between the March ending and the June ending quarter.

items.statement: Dividend of INR50-55 crores paid despite capex plans; philosophy to return cash when not immediately needed
items.quote: We do believe that if the capex requirements or the cash requirements of the company come at a specific time, and we had cash on hand, then the best use of that cash is back to the shareholders.

items.statement: No speculation on further inorganic acquisitions
items.quote: No, we can't -- we cannot speculate on that right now. So, I would refrain from answering that question.

items.statement: ASALAC and PC ABS volumes at 100-150 tons/month; targeting significant growth in 1 year
items.value: 100 tons of product every month or 150 tons per month
items.quote: ASALAC and PC ABS, there is a good growth. In terms of volumes, we are still not where we want to be. We are doing close to 100 tons of product every month or 150 tons per month.

items.statement: Tariff impacts limited for India operations; Thailand may face some impact but market opportunity remains
items.quote: If we look at the Thailand operation also, yes, we are supplying to countries like China and also other areas where the final product might be being sold to the U.S and there might be some impact of it. But we believe in the context of the market opportunity which exists over there that we will still be fine.

items.statement: Domestic ABS capacity additions (including 390 KTPA by FY28) expected to balance with demand over 2-3 years; imports still significant
items.quote: We do believe that there will be a healthy balance of capacity and demand over the next 2 to 3 years as all the capacities that we have outlined come into play and as well as the other capacities which have been announced.

items.statement: Added sales teams in Shanghai, Vietnam, Japan, South Korea, Indonesia for Thailand business
items.quote: We've opened offices, like I mentioned, in Shanghai. And also, we have a sales team now in Vietnam and Japan, South Korea as well as Indonesia.

items.statement: Revenue target of Rs 1,700-1,800 crore by FY27 at risk due to lower raw material prices; focus on absolute gross profit growth
items.quote: But having said that, the ra w material prices itself has come down because of which that Rs. 1,700-Rs. 1,800 number is defi nitely at risk

items.statement: Internal target of around 20% volume growth for current financial year
items.quote: Around 20% is what we are expecting internally.

items.statement: Q1 margin drop due to product mix shift to lower-margin chili, garlic and cheaper mango variety
items.quote: The reason for the margin drop is that the product mix actually changed this quarter. So if you see, we did a lot more of chili, garlic, and all those products which are actually lower margin products as such.

items.statement: Business follows cost-plus model; targets absolute gross profit growth not margin percentage
items.quote: We generally don't guide on the margin profile at all, b asically because we are a cost-plus model that we follow as a business. So absolute growth in g ross profit is the only thing that we target

items.statement: Tomato-based product sales expected to grow from Rs 75-80 crore last year to Rs 130-140 crore this year
items.quote: Last year, our tomato, particularly tomato-based product sale made in the range of Rs. 75-Rs. 80 crores. This financial year we are expecting it should grow to around Rs. 130-Rs. 140 crores.

items.statement: Tomato capacity expanded; commercial production started December last year
items.quote: As of December last year, we have expanded our capacity and commercia l production started on expanded capacity

items.statement: Exploring spray-dried powder capacity expansion of 4-5 MT/day from current 6 MT/day; decision pending
items.quote: So we are looking or exploring a line, which will maybe around 4-5 metric ton per day capacity. Currently, our capacity is around 6 metric ton per day.

items.statement: All previously planned capex completed; new spray dryer expansion under evaluation; eligible for government cluster development scheme
items.quote: Currently, all the CAPEX which were planned is already up and running. And as Mr. Moloy mentioned, however, there are new schemes that the government keeps coming up with and there is currently something called the cluster development and we seem to be eligible for it.

items.statement: Working capital deployment per tonnage expected to be lower due to Totapuri price drop from Rs 27/kg to Rs 8/kg
items.quote: So with respect to working capital, definitely yes, we are expecting lower working capital to be deployed on per tonnage basis this year, basically because the Totapuri prices, which were approximately Rs. 27 per kg on procurement last year, have come down to around Rs. 8 per kg.

items.statement: Working capital debt should have peaked at current processing levels due to lower raw material prices
items.quote: So the working capital debt should have already peaked with the current level of processing that we have already done.

items.statement: Blended average cost of interest around 9.75% last year; total debt Rs 427 crore
items.quote: Last year was around 9.75 or something.

items.statement: Export share 35-38% of turnover (40% last year); participate in Anuga, SIAL, Gulf Food exhibitions; exploring US fair
items.quote: Our export turnover out of our total turnover is around 35%-38%.

items.statement: Top 12 customers (Fortune 500 companies) contribute 65-70% of revenue; long-term relationships with Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Unilever
items.quote: If you see our top 10 customers or top 12 c ustomers, these are all Fortune 500 companies who contribute more than 65%-70

items.statement: No large conglomerate entered pulp manufacturing; market consolidation happening
items.quote: No large conglomerate has actually entered the pulp manufacturing space. In fact, there is a lot of consolidation which is actually happening in the market.

items.statement: Received Rs 50 crore PLI incentive under Category 1; Rs 95 crore pending over next 3 years; did not claim Category 3 branding incentive
items.quote: under category 1 of PLI, under which we are supposed to get Rs. 145 odd crores, we have already received Rs. 50 crores from the government of India and anoth er Rs. 95 crores is pending to be received in the next 3 years

items.statement: Portfolio includes mango, tomato, guava, banana, papaya, chili, garlic; expanding frozen vegetables and Jamun; spices underperformed but targeting larger scale
items.quote: Apart from mango, tomato and guava are the major ones, but we also do banana, papaya, chili, garlic, all these products are also there in our portfolio.

items.statement: US tariff impact uncertain; customers holding orders pending clarity on final duties for Indian food products
items.quote: But for the time being, everything is on hold, basically for any future projected volume is on hold till everybody has a clarity on what will be the final duty applicable for Indian food products which you are supplying.

items.statement: New centralized R&D center in Nashik likely operational in one month to jointly develop products with customers
items.quote: new R&D center is likely to start in operation in another one month's time. It is in Nasik, wh ere we are doing a centralized R&D where all our product R&D center will be centralized and we will be jointly working with the customer to develop their product

items.statement: Exploring farmer tie-ups through FPOs and government cluster development program similar to Sahyadri Farms model
items.quote: We are exploring the similar kind of tying up for other fruits and vegetables in other parts and through FPOs. Now, as you know, FPOs is one of the instruments which will be very effective to have a larger kind of, tying up with larger number of farmers.

items.statement: No immediate equity raise plans; exploring opportunities as they arise
items.quote: We always explore all the opportunities, which is good f or the organization. So as and when any development, definitely all of you will come to know. But as of now, we have nothing to say more than that

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% for coming quarters
items.quote: So, the sustainable margin will remain between 9% to 10%.

items.statement: FY28 FIBC revenue target of INR425-450 crores
items.quote: The FIBC last year we did about INR285 crores. This will remain our main focus and by 2028 we would like to do between INR425 crores and INR450 crores.

items.statement: Acquired 76.19% stake in UK-based Valex Ventures for INR8.02 crores
items.quote: this quarter marked a significant milestone with the acquisition of a 76.19% stake in a UK-based Valex Ventures Limited for a value of INR8.02 crores.

items.statement: Valex acquisition to add INR4-5 crores to consolidated top line immediately
items.quote: the net increase in the top line would be about INR4 crores to INR5 crores on a consolidated way.

items.statement: Raised INR20.50 crores via preferential warrants to repay debt; second issue of INR13.15 crores underway
items.quote: We have successfully raised INR20.50 crores through the preferential issue of 17,60,000 warrants which has been utilized to repay the debts and second preferential issue of INR13.15 crores for 10,12,000 warrants is underway.

items.statement: Debt reduced from INR190 crores to target INR125 crores by end of FY26
items.quote: By end of this year, we should be in a position of having about INR15 crores of long-term debt and about INR110 crores of working capital limit. So that is about INR125 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 8.51% from 5.20% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA increased to INR15.54 crores with margins improving to 8.51% from 5.20%.

items.statement: Food grade FIBC EBITDA ~12% vs standard FIBC ~7%
items.quote: One could be around 12% of EBITDA, the other could be around 7% EBITDA.

items.statement: Strong order book and healthy demand outlook for coming quarters
items.quote: With a strong order book, healthy demand outlook, disciplined execution, and loyal relationships with our clients, we are confident that Kanpur Plastipack is on track to deliver consistent, profitable, and sustainable growth in the quarters ahead.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization at 75-77% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: So as a whole when we see the capacity utilization for the last financial year was about 75%. The last quarter was also between 75% and 77% depending on how we calculated.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 product mix: FIBC 51%, Fabric 31.36%, Multifilament 9.65%, Others 6.22%, Small bags 1.77%
items.quote: FIBC contributed the largest share at 51%, about INR74.82 crores. Fabric accounted for 31.36%, which was INR46.01 crores, while other products formed 6.22% and Multifilament, which is MFI, brought about 9.65%. The small bulb s contributed 1.77

items.statement: Exports 74% of manufacturing sales in Q1 FY26; Europe 48.75%, South America 30.44%, North America 18.31%
items.quote: exports accounted for nearly 74% of all the revenue, and the domestic was about 26%. Within the 74% revenue, Europe remained our largest market and our stronghold at 48.75%, followed by South America at 30.44% and North America only contributing to 18.31%.

items.statement: US tariff impact limited as North America is 18% of exports; no order cancellations yet
items.quote: our 18% turnover is in North America, out of which about 14% is in US and 4% is in Canada. So, it is not a very significant volume that is getting affected. There are no orders on hold. There are no order cancellations.

items.statement: Polymer prices stable in dollar terms; raw material and ocean freight stable for 12 months
items.quote: We have also seen a significant stability in the raw material and the ocean freight over the last 12 months.

items.statement: Structural demand shift from China to India driving FIBC sector buoyancy
items.quote: as China and Far East continue to enhance their manufacturing capabilities into electronics and pharma and other products, their focus on labor-intensive manufacturing goes down. And then the only other alternative that's there today is in India.

items.statement: Geotextiles revenue grew from INR40 crores to INR60 crores in FY26, targeting INR60-80 crores next year
items.quote: On geotextiles, we are already present and we did about 2,000 tons, so that is about INR40 crores last year in geotextiles. This year it would be closer to INR60 crores. And the next year that it's planned, it would be between INR60 crores to INR80 crores.

items.statement: Customer base diversified with no single client >5% of revenue
items.quote: Our loyal customer base is well diversified across sectors such as food, agriculture, chemicals, mining, and construction, with no single client contributing more than 5% of the total revenue.

items.statement: UK-India FTA to enhance margins and demand for Valex acquisition
items.quote: The UK India FTA will help this acquisition and it will help the profitability there.

items.statement: Trading revenue INR35 crores in Q1 from polymer trading; small margin contribution
items.quote: INR182 crores was the total revenue. Out of it, INR35 crore was stock and trade. This came out of an opportunity during the period and this week, this keeps on coming.

items.statement: Forex risk acknowledged; managed via defined policy but remains a risk in global uncertainty
items.quote: Forex, we have a well -defined forex management polic y. I happen to handle that personally directly with my CFO on that. But in the global uncertainty situation that we lie in today, have to frankly admit that forex will always remain a risk

items.statement: Solar power meets 47% of energy needs; target 60%
items.quote: 47% of energy needs are currently met through solar power and our proposed target is to reach 60%.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to Crisil BBB+ stable (long-term) and Crisil A2 (short-term)
items.quote: Our credit rating was upgraded to Crisil BBB plus stable for long-term facilities and to Crisil A2 for short-term facilities, highlighting our strong financial risk profile.

items.statement: New BOPP line to ramp to 100% capacity in 2-3 months; specialty mix to increase over time
items.quote: The new BOPP line will ramp up to 100% capacity within the next two to three months. We will be filling up with specialty films over a period of time.

items.statement: Zigly demerger likely by 2028-29, could be earlier; no immediate partner search
items.quote: more than likely it will be anywhere by latest by 2028, or 29 it can happen even earlier than that, but it's too early to predict anything on this.

items.statement: Rigid packaging EBITDA breakeven expected in September-October; positive PBT by Q3/Q4
items.quote: What we expect is that the rigid packaging should start making positive EBITDA. Let's say in September month of most likely in September month, it could be September or October. And we expect that Quarter 3 should have positive EBITDA coming from rigid packaging.

items.statement: Annual cost reduction target of Rs.40 crore for FY26, similar to FY25
items.quote: The last year we saved around Rs.40 crores on cost reduction exercises. So, this year also we are targeting to achieve Rs.40 crore cost reduction.

items.statement: Commissioned new 81,000 MT BOPP line in June (45% capacity addition) and window film line in May under Sunshield brand
items.quote: During June '25 quarter, the company has commissioned two key assets: First new BOPP line with annual capacity of close to 81,000 metric tons, which started operations from June beginning and added close to 45% to the company BOPP capacity.

items.statement: Existing lines to de-bottleneck for 6-7% more production via total quality management project
items.quote: The company is running a total quality management project. And we do expect that our earlier lines will be able to do 6%, 7% more production over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Specialty film sales growing at ~10% CAGR over last 6 years; trend expected to continue
items.quote: The company is growing specialty film sales by close to 10% CAGR growth over last six years, and we expect this trend to continue.

items.statement: BOPP film margins at Rs.25/kg in Q1 FY26 vs Rs.21/kg in Q4 FY25 and Rs.19/kg in Q1 FY25
items.quote: BOPP film margins have been running close to Rs.25 per kg during June '25 quarter as against Rs.21 per kg in March '25 quarter and Rs.19 per kg in June 24 quarter.

items.statement: Exit margin for BOPP segment expected closer to Rs.30/kg
items.quote: So, exit will be closer to Rs.30 or so.

items.statement: Current BOPP margins decent: tape textile +30, non-tape +45; imports temporary, market to normalize in 30-45 days
items.quote: Right now, the margin despite this import is quite decent. The value add in tape textile film is +30, while in the non-tape is close to +45, these are decent margins.

items.statement: Specialty prices higher than commodity; specialty/semi-specialty 68% by volume, 80%+ by value in Q1
items.quote: This is by volume? Management: It is (+80%) by value. Vipulkumar Shah: For value it is +80%? Management: Yes. Management: This speciality prices are always higher compared to the commodity, that's why in value terms, it would always be higher

items.statement: New BOPP line initially commodity, shifting to specialty; target significant specialty share in 3 years
items.quote: Right now, that number is still small, we are also adding many assets alongside in the coming months to increase the specialty sales Cosmo First Limited August 14th ,2025 from this asset. So, eventually, in three years’ time we want a very significant part of this line to be sold into specialty film

items.statement: Window film (Sunshield) targeting domestic first with 50+ distributors; exports to Americas, Europe, Middle East
items.quote: target is the domestic market. We feel there is a very significant potential to make a brand here, and we have already started with certain ATL and BTL activities to create the brand, it's starting of the journey it will take its own time. And we are also looking at exports in multiple markets to begin with. Our focus is America's and Europe

items.statement: Net debt at peak; significant reduction expected over next 2 years as no major capex planned for next year
items.quote: But we also expect this to be close to the peak level. As the CAPEX plan for this year, although there is a reasonable number, but for the next year there is no major CAPEX plan, so we see a very significant reduction in the net debt level over the next two years or so.

items.statement: New BOPP line incremental fixed cost Rs.6-8 crore annually at full ramp
items.quote: So, we do not expect that the incremental fixed cost because of this new line will be more than Rs.6 to Rs.8 crores in a year.

items.statement: Specialty chemical subsidiary record quarterly EBITDA Rs.12 crore on sales Rs.49 crore in Q1
items.quote: The specialty chemical business continues to achieve traction and posted record EBITDA of Rs.12 crore on quarterly sales of Rs.49 crore in Quarter 1, June '25.

items.statement: US tariffs at 55% unsustainable; may shift sales to other markets if sustained; BIS standards on imports possible
items.quote: See, the current tariffs are quite crazy, and what we feel are unsustainable, if it remains at the current level, then it is a precarious position. A significant part of our sales can be impacted to America.

items.statement: Renewable power >50% in FY25; target ~two-thirds in 1-2 years; aids cost rationalization
items.quote: In FY’25 company has used more than 50% of its power consumption from renewable sources, which we expect to further increase to about two third in one to two years period. Besides the environment, this also facilitates cost

items.statement: Zigly omni-channel implementation caused temporary online sales dip due to marketplace cancellations; retail growth strong
items.quote: when we implemented this omni channel in February month, February, March, we had 30%, 30% growth in online orders. But then we had account blockages from Amazon and Flipkart because of more cancelations than their standard cancelation of 1.5%, almost for two months we were not able to sell on these platforms.

items.statement: Competitor capacity loss ~15,000 MT; new industry capacity additions ~10,000-12,000 MT; net reduction 3,000-4,000 MT; domestic consumption 65,000-70,000 MT
items.quote: we understand that 15,000 tons was what they were producing on average. We have to also remind the investors and the listeners here that in this year four lines have to be added, out of which three have already been added and the fourth line will be added soon. These four lines put together will add 10,000 to 12,000 tons of additional capacity. So, on a net basis, right now the reduction is 3000 t

items.statement: Target to double revenue with 15% EBITDA margin by 2027
items.quote: In our annual report, I think we have mentioned about the Vriddhi Council and our guidance of doubling of revenue with an EBITDA margin of 15% by 2027.

items.statement: No forward-looking revenue guidance provided for FY26
items.quote: We don't give forward looking guidance on revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 9.7% in Q1 FY26; target 15% by FY27
items.quote: EBITDA is at 6.25 crores, and EBITDA margin is at 9.7 %.

items.statement: Material cost at 48%, target to reduce to 45% to drive EBITDA to 15%
items.quote: The biggest factor is material cost, which is at 48% right now, we need to bring it to 45%.

items.statement: Targeting Rs 1.5 crore savings from cost of poor quality reduction this year
items.quote: We're targeting about 1.5 crores of savings from COPQ reduction for the year.

items.statement: FY26 capex budget of Rs 25 crore approved; Rs 4 crore received in Q1
items.quote: Last quarter, I had highlighted that we have a budget of 25 crores approved by the CapEx allocation committee and the board. This is for FY26

items.statement: Forging installed capacity Rs 500 crore; OEE capacity Rs 150-200 crore; target 60-65% OEE
items.quote: We have installed capacity in forgings of close to 500 crores. But this is at 100% OEE i.e. overall equipment efficiency. When we look at the OEE capacity of forgings, we are currently at 150 to 200 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 utilization: forging ~40%, machining ~80%
items.quote: On the forging side, the utilization is around 40% and on the machining side, it is around 80%.

items.statement: Forging OEE tonnage ~10,000 tons; target 20,000-25,000 tons in 1.5-2 years
items.quote: Tonnage currently is at close to 10,000 tons in terms of OEE capacity. And it should be increasing. It can go up to 20,000- 25,000 tons.

items.statement: New business order wins: Rs 95 crore in FY24, Rs 115 crore in FY25 (peak annual revenue)
items.quote: We have had new business order wins in FY25 of 115 crores, and this has been probably a historic high for us.

items.statement: Closing order book ~Rs 260 crore as of March 2025
items.quote: Closing order book is close to 260 crores for last year.

items.statement: Revenue up 12% YoY, 9% QoQ in Q1 FY26 driven by machine conrods, driveline, axle
items.quote: Revenue is up by 12% year-on-year and 9% quarter-on-quarter, driven by ramp-up in machine conrods, driveline and axle businesses.

items.statement: Machining content 60% of revenue; target 65-70% in FY26
items.quote: Yes, machining is from 60%. Our target is to go to 70% this year, or 65 to 70%.

items.statement: Sales split: Engine 59%, Driveline 18%, Axle 9%, Others 14% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: this is the split of sales by different product groups which is 59 % is engine, 18 % is driveline, 9 % is axle, and 14 % are other products.

items.statement: ~40-50 active customers
items.quote: Roughly around 40 to 50.

items.statement: Energy audit completed; implementing recommendations to reduce power cost
items.quote: We did a very detailed energy audit last quarter and this quarter we have started implementing on the recommendations from that audit.

items.statement: Senior leadership promotions on merit; restructured roles for plant accountability; enhanced trainee program
items.quote: Key senior leadership promotions based on merit have taken place. We have restructured roles to strengthen plant accountability and foster a high-trust and performance-driven culture. Future-ready workforce: We have enhanced the trainee program to build a shop floor-based leadership pipeline

items.statement: Asset turnover ~4x (sales to fixed assets); competitors at 2x or below
items.quote: Our current asset turnover is very high compared to our competitors, which means our asset base, net asset value is still very low. The typical ratio is two is to one, that is sales to fixed assets should be in the ratio of two is to one, and we are currently at close to four

items.statement: EV transition slowing; multi-fuel future expected; engine business (truck/off-road) to continue growing
items.quote: has met with a lot of challenges, and a lot of the realities are coming out now as a lot of electric cars get into implementation phase. A lot of customers have rolled back on their EV programs, a lot of governments as well have rolled back on subsidies and so on and there's more and more consensus on a multi-fuel future

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR1,500 crores and surpassing FY25 bottom line
items.quote: So as of now, we are giving the guidance of about INR1,500 crores in view of the present circumstances and the situation prevailing.

items.statement: Peak debt level expected around INR700 crores in FY27-FY28
items.quote: We are looking around INR700 crores of the debt, peak level.

items.statement: INR125 crores Warangal capex funded via internal accruals and promoter warrant conversion
items.quote: No. So we are not taking any debt for this INR125 crores. It is entirely from the internal accruals and the cash balances available with the company, including this conversion of warrants from promoters recently done INR104 crores we got it.

items.statement: Current approved rPET capacity industry-wide is 1.67 lakh tons; company approved capacity 1.5 lakh tons
items.quote: With new approvals in place, the current approved capacity now stands to around 1.67 lakh tons and thus easing the fear of packaging industry about the availability of required volume of rPET material for complying to the regulatory guidelines.

items.statement: Sale visibility for rPET granules finalized until December with improved uptakes from brand owners
items.quote: Sale visibility until the December has been finalized to us by our existing customers with much improved uptakes by all the brand owners that we are currently working with.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 challenging due to raw material price spike, export demand for flakes, and suppressed user industry demand
items.quote: The first quarter of FY '26 was a challenging quarter for us due to some unprecedented events that led to spike in raw material prices, which further put pressure on the RPSF prices vis-a-vis the virgin materials.

items.statement: Demand improving in current quarter with festival season orders picking up for September-October deliveries
items.quote: With onset of forthcoming festival season, demand is also improving slightly and the orders for September, October deliveries have picked up significantly, and we are expecting that demand will return back to normal levels in subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Legacy business raw material cost rose to 70% of revenue vs 64% previous quarter; rPET granule margins maintained
items.quote: And the raw material cost swelled to 70% of the revenue as against 64% during the last quarter. Higher scrap bottle prices, lower sale prices and lower capacity utilization, coupled with the demand slowdown majorly contributed to the decline in this profitability.

items.statement: rPET granule premium over virgin PET reduced by ~20% with scrap price normalization
items.quote: Yes. So the premium has come down by about 20% with the decrease in the prices of the PET bottle scrap.

items.statement: PET bottle scrap prices spiked to INR55-56/kg in April-May'25, now normalized to INR41-44/kg
items.quote: Prices of the pet bottle scrap, key feedstock for our products reached at an unprecedented levels of INR55 to INR56 per kg for some time during April and May'25.

items.statement: Recycled PSF sold at 10-12% discount to virgin PSF; could not pass on raw material cost increase due to demand slowdown
items.quote: So basically, the raw material prices increased, but because there remains a gap of 10% to 12% in the pricing of the virgin and the recycled PSF. Recycled PSF is sold cheaper by 10% to 12%.

items.statement: MoEF draft notification allows FY26 rPET shortfall carryforward over 3 years capped at 10-15%; FSSAI licenses broadened recycler base
items.quote: Basis the draft notification, the brands who were already using rPET granules and also those who were to start the consumption very soon slightly lowered down their purchases. Set-off allowed to the bottlers for their past consumptions of rPET granules during last financial year against the stipulated targets of FY '26 was also leveraged by the brands to postpone their purchases slightly to subseq

items.statement: EPR targets not deferred; only FY26 shortfall carryforward allowed over and above future year targets
items.quote: So basically, the draft notification issued on 3rd of June by MoEF is allowing only the carryover for the shortfall of the first year, the year we are in, '25-'26. The remaining target for next years are intact. They have not been allowed to carry over. And even this carryover will be over and above the target for the next year.

items.statement: Exports 12% of revenue in Q1 FY26 vs 9% previous year; targeting 15-20% for FY26
items.quote: Yes. So barring that, we are expecting -- we would be making around 15% to 20% of our total revenue from exports.

items.statement: rPET flakes and granules exempt from US tariffs; Europe SUPD impacted flake exports
items.quote: So yes, it is --till date, it is --so all petroleum products, basically, all petroleum products are coming under Annexure 2. So any Trump tariff is not being attracted to any petroleum product till now. And these rPET flakes and rPET granule are out of this tariff imports.

items.statement: Current debt ~INR550 crores at 8.5% blended cost; no new debt for Warangal capex
items.quote: So currently, the debt is in the region of around INR550 crores. And the average cost is about 8.5%.

items.statement: Promoters infused INR104 crores via equity warrant conversion in July
items.quote: Promoters have infused INR104 crores by conversion of their equity warrants in July, reinforcing their commitment towards the growth of company's business.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix guided at 65% legacy (RPSF/yarn) and 35% subsidiary (rPET granules)
items.quote: Total revenue mix that would be around 35% from the subsidiary and 65% from the legacy business.

items.statement: Brand owners maintaining offtake commitments for FY26 despite temporary Q1 deferral due to high rPET premium
items.quote: No, no. Obviously, so all our customers are offtaking the quantities that they had estimated for this year. Although obviously, it's not nowhere even close to 30% requirement as per the mandate. But yes, they are maintaining their given targets to us for the quantity offtake.

items.statement: Management confident of maintaining competitive advantage via sourcing, operations, and sales efficiency despite new entrants
items.quote: And we think that still we are very, efficient in our operations from any of our competitors currently operating in the Indian market, be it about sourcing, be it about operations, be it about sales and volumes. So we think that we will always be able to remain -- be able to maintain that alpha from the competition no matter what.

items.statement: Industry rPET demand ~200,000 tons for FY26 (organized sector) vs 1.5 lakh tons approved capacity
items.quote: So basically, looking to the total consumption of 1.2 million tons of PET in India for packaging, especially in the bottles, the food packaging, the demand should be 3.6 lakh tons for the first year itself because you have -- so the demand would be 3.6 lakh tons, but if we exclude the unorganized sector, so roughly the demand is around 200,000 tons for this '25, '26.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty impacting textile export orders; management expects medium-term mitigation via government incentives and supply chain shifts
items.quote: The demand has already been discounted because of the U.S. tariff. And -- but exact picture will emerge once the things are finalized as of the things are changing every day. But yes, the new orders from the America to the suppliers is on halt. So the demand is already affected.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; leadership team includes CFO Gopal Agarwal, SVP Prashant Khandelwal, Director Yash Sharma
items.quote: We have leadership team represented by Mr. Gopal Agarwal, CFO; Mr. Prashant Khandelwal, Senior Vice President; and Mr. Yash Sharma, Director, Ganesha Ecopet.

items.statement: Management expects operating leverage to play out as core platform investments mature, with top-line growth falling to bottom line, while continuing to invest in Spice Pay and credit engines.
items.quote: However, I believe that our core platform business today in terms of the investments that we have made both in fee t-on-street as well as the backend is kind of more or less matured in terms of the investments. So, any growth in top line should fall to the bottom line from the Spice Money Adhikari platform business

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBIT was Rs 10.2 crore (8% of revenue), up ~50% QoQ from Rs 5.2 crore; PAT was Rs 6.9 crore (5% of revenue) vs Rs 1.5 crore previous quarter.
items.quote: And on the EBIT side, we have clocked Rs. 10.2 crores EBIT number against Rs. 5.2 crores in the previous quarter, which is also almost a 50% growth.

items.statement: Customer GTV (cross-transaction value) grew 28% YoY to Rs 32,760 crore in Q1 FY26; monthly AePS GTV ~Rs 5,000 crore, CMS GTV ~Rs 4,000 crore, bill payments ~Rs 450 crore, credit disbursements ~Rs 40 crore monthly run-rate.
items.quote: For the quarter ended June ' 26*, we have closed at Rs. 32,760 crores, which is a 28% year -on-year growth over the same quarter last year.

items.statement: AePS industry grew ~3.4% QoQ and 10% YoY; Spice Money outpaced industry, gaining Off-Us market share to >18% (up 7% YoY).
items.quote: Looking at our overall A ePS cash withdrawal numbers , we have seen on the industry side that the industry has grown by approximately 3.4% quarter-on- quarter and 10% year-on-year, while our growth in Spice Money has been more than the industry growth, which has led to the growth in our overall market share in this business.

items.statement: Gross margin mix shifted: AePS+Micro ATM fell to 55% from 63.6% YoY; subscription packs rose to 12.4% from ~8%; collections ~20%; financial services distribution ~10.5% from ~6% YoY.
items.quote: A ePS and Micro ATM, which were our key business attracting the customer footfall, was almost covering 70% of our gross margins a couple of years back. But today, if we see the numbers, we have approximately 55% of our gross margin still coming from A ePS and M icro ATM. But this was approximately 63.6% in the last year same quarter.

items.statement: Agent base reached 15.8 lakh across 2.5 lakh villages and 6,500 blocks; 85% in North/East/Central, 15% in South/West; monthly active customers ~2.5 crore.
items.quote: And now at the end of Quarter 1, FY '26, we are approximately a base of 15.8 lakh agents who are sitting across 2.5 lakh villages and approximately 6,500 blocks across pan-India.

items.statement: AePS transaction success rate improved from 63.8% in FY24 to 71.3% in Q1 FY26; subscription pack renewals ~65% monthly.
items.quote: And we have been significantly able to grow our success rate of transactions from approximately 63.8% in Financial Year ' 24 to now touching 71.3% in Q1 Financial Year ' 26.

items.statement: Platform modernization underway; expect ~1 year to fully move off legacy stacks; AI in customer service already driving cost savings.
items.quote: I think it will take another year or so to be able to completely be able to move out of legacy into more modern kind of platforms. And of course, this will going forward as we will scale translate into better economics as well.

items.statement: Secured PPI license in perpetuity from RBI for Spice Pay wallet; new AePS Touchpoint Operator category and face-auth guidelines provide clarity.
items.quote: One big call out that we want to do is the fact that now the company has secured a PPI license in perpetuity from the Reserve Bank of India.

items.statement: Key risks: regulatory/fraud in AePS, supply-side partner constraints, competition from urban players moving rural, consumer shift to digital reducing cash withdrawals.
items.quote: Lots of risks. There is r egulatory, as Aastha outlined, A ePS as an industry, there are issues around fraud that we have to constantly look out for

items.statement: Sales force app with geo-tagged daily beat plans deployed for real-time monitoring of partners and field teams to drive productivity and accountability.
items.quote: We have put in place a daily beat plan, which is geo-tagged to improve visibility, accountability, and coverage.

items.statement: CASA float balances grew 57% YoY to Rs 225 crore (avg balance >Rs 2,000); 11.4 lakh lifetime accounts opened, 145% YoY growth in Q1.
items.quote: And the closing float as at June has touched Rs. 225 crores with the average balance of more than Rs. Rs. 2,000 that reflects a healthy average balance that is bein g maintained in the accounts that we are opening for India.

items.statement: Discontinued business costs negligible (~Rs 10 lakh loss last quarter); legal entity closures in Africa/SE Asia ongoing but costs kept very tight.
items.quote: So, yes, Utsav, as you can see from the numbers, our discontinued business numbers from a kind of closure cost perspective have significantly come down , only about Rs. 10 lakhs loss for the previous quarter.

items.statement: Banks' kiosk banking is direct competition; large fintechs (Paytm, Jio) not yet visible in rural; differentiation via phygital model, agent trust, and unit economics.
items.quote: I would say that we are seeing that there is opportunity because we see the banks as a collaborative partner for us to extend their reach of banking . So, we are hoping that we would be able to work with banks to reduce their cost of rolling out physical access points.

items.statement: Collections business faces high price competition but maintains GTV/margin growth; subscription packs improve agent stickiness and throughput.
items.quote: Though this business has been seeing some huge margin pressures due to some competitive pricing that is happening in this space overall , we have been still being able to maintain a sustained growth in our GTVs and gross margins in the collections business.

items.statement: Hardware procurement largely domestic; shifting to face-auth and QR-based UPI reduces dependence on biometric devices and global supply chains.
items.quote: We work with companies that work domestically. Most of the components now we are able to procure domest ically. So, I don't think in the whole biometric space, this is a challenge.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; no merger plans with WSFx (separate listed entity).
items.quote: Magesh, no, there is no such plan to merge. These are two independent listed companies and there is no such plan in place.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback discussed; face value change suggestion (Rs 3 to Rs 10) acknowledged but no commitment.
items.quote: Understood, Pankaj. Thank you for your...

items.statement: No acquisitions or divestments discussed beyond legacy entity closures.
items.quote: We are going through the process of either closure or sale of those entities , country by country.

items.statement: No export or FX exposure discussed; business is domestic rural India focused.
items.quote: We at DiGiSPICE have a unique opportunity of focusing on a part of India that many fintechs are not.

items.statement: Agent network capacity expanding in South/West (lower density districts); target 1 lakh new CASA accounts monthly.
items.quote: And our target is that we can touch 1 lakh accounts on a monthly basis that we open as we drive growth in this product.

items.statement: Credit disbursements Rs 110 crore in Q1 (165% YoY); 70% gold loans (Rs 68 crore); using Spice Money/Spice Pay data and AI for underwriting.
items.quote: Overall, we have dis bursed approximately Rs. 110 crores loans including the unsecured business.

items.statement: Spice Pay (PPI wallet) and credit are two new growth engines; UPI economics challenging but targeting next 100 million users.
items.quote: Spice Pay is our contribution or our journey towards enabling new to UPI consumers to come on board today. UPI is the success story coming out of India, nearly 400 million consumers now in UPI. We want to contribute to the next 100 million.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin improved 140 bps YoY and 240 bps QoQ to 56.6% driven by mix, pricing and reduced trade spend
items.quote: The gross margin for the quarter on a stand-alone basis stood at 56.6%, an improvement of 140 basis points year -on-year and 240 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved 130 bps YoY and 340 bps QoQ to 17.5%
items.quote: EBITDA on a stand -alone basis grew by 11.6% to deliver INR 42.8 crores at a healthy margin of 17.5%.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margin improvement towards sectoral average of low-to-mid 20s from current 17-18% range
items.quote: I think for the step one is for us to target that rather than to get into a number which is beyond that. And that is the first, which would be the next few hundred basis points of movement.

items.statement: ADHO grew 4% YoY with broad-based growth across packs including small packs and sachets signaling consumption revival
items.quote: We've delivered a growth of 4% on ADHO and have arrested the volume decline on the brand after several quarters.

items.statement: General trade channel returned to growth driven by urban segment and Almond Drop hair oil
items.quote: During the quarter, we saw some green shoots in general trade channel, which came back to growth after the significant gap.

items.statement: Organized trade grew strong double-digit YoY with saliency near 29%; modern trade and e-commerce both grew in 20s
items.quote: Organized trade registered a strong double-digit growth year -on-year in quarter 1 FY '26. The saliency of this channel now stands close to 29%.

items.statement: International business declined 20% YoY due to tariff uncertainty, weak demand and distributor transitions in GCC markets
items.quote: Our international business had a weak quarter with revenue declining 20% year-on-year, which was linked to the external headwinds like tariff uncertainty and slowdown in rest of world markets.

items.statement: Nepal and Bangladesh (direct markets) grew double-digit; MEA and rest of world (distributor markets) declined sharply
items.quote: First, the businesses which have direct representation, that is the countries where we have team on ground, primarily Nepal and Bangladesh. Both of these countries showed resilient performance, growing double digit.

items.statement: LLP prices range-bound last 2-3 quarters; RMO up 25%, copra nearly doubled; overall basket expected to remain range-bound
items.quote: On the input cost, LLP prices have been moving in a narrow range in the last 2 or 3 quarters. In the other key raw material prices, we are witnessing a 25% inflation in RMO and nearly doubling of prices in copra.

items.statement: Selective price increases taken in oil portfolio; further corrective pricing in process for subsequent quarters
items.quote: We have taken corrective pricing, which is not fully in market, which is in process, which will happen in there and subsequent quarters, which is basically leading to a market expansion.

items.statement: Coconut oil grew 20%+ YoY despite steep inflation and portfolio pruning; gained market share
items.quote: In coconut, Bajaj Coconut Oil continued its growth in Q1 FY '26. As we are aware, this category has seen very steep inflation and resulted price increases. Despite the pricing action and the pruning of certain nonprofitable portfolio, we've been able to hold our ground and continue to gain market share in this segment.

items.statement: Coconut volume growth lower than market leader due to focus on profitable sustainable revenues; offtake market share gains holding
items.quote: Our growth would be lower than the market leader. We have taken certain corrections to ensure that whatever revenues we are delivering are profitable and sustainable revenues.

items.statement: No significant capex commitment for next 2-3 years; plants have capacity headroom for 2-3 years growth
items.quote: So if you're wanting the question, is there any going to be significant CapEx commitment over the next couple of years? The answer is no.

items.statement: Own plants in Dehradun, Guwahati, Paonta Sahib; one large third-party facility plus smaller third parties
items.quote: In terms of -- if you were to look at our own plants, we have in Dehradun, Guwahati, and Paonta. And we have one large basically third-party facility, which is there.

items.statement: Completed 51% acquisition of Vishal Personal Care in Q1 FY26; now fully owned subsidiary; Q1 revenue INR 15.5 cr, ~10% YoY growth, low-teens EBITDA margin ex-one-offs
items.quote: For quarter 1 FY '26 on a like -to-like basis, VPL registered a top line of INR 15.5 crores with a nearly 10% growth on a Y -o-Y basis.

items.statement: Distribution integration with Banjara's (VPCL) to take 4-6 quarters; pilot phase started; leveraging South distribution for BCCL brands and North for Banjara's
items.quote: So this distribution integration is going to be, from my estimate, around a 4-quarter exercise to a 5-quarter exercise. And we will do it gradually as to ensure that we do not disrupt the strength and the advantages of the system.

items.statement: Aarohan program extended to core markets; added 25,000+ new outlets; UP and MP showing positive trends
items.quote: So far, we've already added more than 25,000 new outlets and continue to work on this agenda.

items.statement: Rural GT sluggishness due to internal Aarohan distribution changes; disruption expected to resolve in next couple of quarters
items.quote: And right now, we are in a phase wherein we are executing the changes in the rural and hence, there is a certain amount of disruption in our current business there. We will basically be working and fixing this, which should happen in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Focus on reviving double-digit growth with calibrated pricing; target sustainable profitable growth balancing revenue and margin improvement
items.quote: Looking ahead, we continue to focus on reviving double -digit growth for the business with a strong focus and support to our core brand Almond Drops.

items.statement: Hair oil category $2B, 92-93% penetration, moderate growth; oiling is generational habit in India; category salience strong
items.quote: It has a very high frequency of usage. It has a very high salience. This is a product category you will find in every single home of the country.

items.statement: US exports under question due to tariffs; no multi-country manufacturing to reroute; impact immaterial to overall revenue
items.quote: So yes, we do export to the U.S. and right now, that market and the export to that market is under question and we are trying to figure out what do we do.

items.statement: Naveen Pandey joined as MD; aims to bring agility and nimbleness to organization for sustainable profitable growth
items.quote: What -- if I were to say one thing, which I would try and get in is I think I would try and get in a bit more agility. And I think that's something which we can learn from a lot of organizations.

items.statement: Standalone sales INR 244.5 cr (+3.2% YoY); consolidated sales INR 259.5 cr (+7.4% YoY); ex-Vishal consolidated growth 3.7%
items.quote: The stand- alone sales for the company stood at INR 244.5 crores, registering a growth of 3.2% on a Y -o-Y basis, whereas the consolidated sales stood at INR259.5 crores with a value growth of 7.4%.

items.statement: Standalone PAT INR 39 cr (16% margin); consolidated PAT INR 37.9 cr (14.6% margin)
items.quote: Stand-alone PAT stood at INR39 crores with a margin of 16%. And at a consolidated basis, PAT was INR37.9 crores with a margin of 14.6%.

items.statement: ADHO advertising investment over 3,000 GRP TV campaign delivered; digital reach 4 crore consumers; influencer engagement rates above industry benchmark
items.quote: We've been focusing our advertising on ADHO for the past few months and an extensive TV campaign with an investment of over 3,000 GRP has just got delivered.

items.statement: Capex may cross ₹800 crore in FY26; FY27 capex not expected to decline
items.quote: Looking at the capacities which we need to sweat, the CAPEX might be crossing ₹ 800 crores in this year. For FY 27, this figure is very difficult to say. We believe in sweating our assets, that's why you see operational efficiency is quite good, since the beginning. So, we only spend when there is a requirement to spend. But as we look at inorganic growth opportunities also, both in India and Euro

items.quote: If you see Q1 in India, we have spent ₹ 286 crores on Capex. And as you know, there are 3 big projects which I have already mentioned. The big ones are the AURIC Shendra, starting in Q4. And then you have the AURIC Bidkin, which is starting in week 4 of this month. And also, we have the battery-pack plant, which is starting in January 26.

items.statement: ABS capacity 640k units; adding 2.4 million by March 2026; target 25% market share
items.quote: As far as Endurance is concerned, of course, our capacity is 640,000. We are expecting a tenfold growth for sure. items.quote: I am pleased to inform you that the SOP at our 2W alloy wheel plant in AURIC Bidkin will start in week 4 of this month. The plant has an installed capacity of 3.6 million wheels per annum, and bulk of this capacity has been booked with orders from OEM clients.

items.quote: near Pune, civil work and statutory consents are in place. Machinery has been ordered and will be installed at our plant in early next quarter. items.statement: New disc brake assembly plant planned in Chennai for South OEMs (TVS, Royal Enfield, Yamaha)
items.quote: We are planning to set-up a new plant for disc brake assembly including for master cylinder, caliper, brake disc and brake hoses in Chennai, where we already have a land bank. This plant will cater to the South Indian OEM clients, including TVS, Royal Enfield and Yamaha India amongst other OEMs.

items.statement: Fifth aluminium forging press ordered for new Waluj plant; existing setup to move there
items.quote: Increased demand would require setting up of more aluminum forging presses. We have ordered our fifth press now, which we would install next year in our new aluminum forging plant at Waluj. Our existing aluminum forging setup will also be moved to this new plant, where the civil work is on.

items.statement: Adding SMT lines and testing capacity at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for BMS and ABS ECU demand
items.quote: We have recently installed additional end-of-the-line testing lines and in due course, 2 new high-speed surface-mounted technology lines will also be set up to cater to this increased demand.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 India order booking ₹252 crore (₹247 crore new business); excludes ₹300 crore battery pack LOI
items.quote: Overall order booking in Q1FY26 in India business was ₹ 252 crores of which ₹ 247 crores is new business. This is excluding the ₹ 300 crores per annum business, which we have won for battery packs.

items.statement: Total RFQs in hand ₹3,225 crore; cumulative EV orders ₹864 crore (₹1,017 crore with Bajaj)
items.quote: We have a total of ₹ 3,225 crores worth of RFQs in hand. Cumulative India business orders for EV segment till date stand at ₹ 864 crores. And with Bajaj Auto, this figure is now at ₹ 1,017 crores per annum.

items.statement: Inverted front fork orders from Hero MotoCorp and leading Chinese OEM; SOP this FY; KTM demand expected to rise with Bajaj control
items.quote: We have orders from Hero MotoCorp and a leading Chinese OEM, for which SOPs will start in this financial year. The KTM export offtake has been lower than the earlier years. Now, with Bajaj in full control over the global KTM operations, we expect demand to increase in the next quarters.

items.statement: Aluminium forging supplies to Jaguar Land Rover from Jan 2026; orders from Royal Enfield, Hero MotoCorp; multiple RFQs
items.quote: Our supplies to Jaguar Land Rover are expected to begin in January 2026. We now have orders also from Royal Enfield and Hero MotoCorp, and multiple RFQs are being addressed from Indian and international OEMs.

items.statement: Hero MotoCorp clutch SOP May 2025; peak 100k/month by Q4 FY26; APTC clutch SOP Sep 2025 for Royal Enfield, Bajaj
items.quote: We have begun SOP in May 25 for the first Hero MotoCorp clutch, for which peak requirement will reach 100k clutch assemblies per month, which we hope to do in Q 4 of this financial year. In September, we will begin SOP for the first assist-and-slip APTC clutches to Royal Enfield and Bajaj Auto.

items.statement: Solar tracking system order ₹200 crore from Spanish client; peak next year; non-auto inorganic growth explored
items.quote: At the end of last month, we started production of solar suspension or solar tracking system. We won ₹ 200 crores order from a Spanish client, which will reach peak next year. And now, we are talking to somebody else. I mean there is a huge business opportunity for profitable growth in non-auto also.

items.quote: In the Automotive sector, as per SIAM, 2W sales reached 5.81 million units in Q1 FY 26, down 1.6% year -on-year, with Motorcycles at 1.8% degrowth and scooters at 0.8% degrowth. items.quote: In our European Union, new car sales saw a year-on-year drop of 1.8% in Q1 FY 26, while our Endurance Europe total income growth was significantly higher at 28.5%. items.quote: We closed EBITDA at €18 million, which means 17.4% EBIDTA margin compared to €13.3 million in the previous financial year with 16.5% margin. And so, we grew €4.7 million, which is 35.1% YoY growth. In terms of net results, we closed with €6.4 million, which means 6.2% margin compared to €4.9 million of the previous financial year with 6.1% margin.

items.statement: Content addition in brakes and suspension with TVS, Royal Enfield, HMSI, Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp drove standalone growth
items.quote: This growth comes majorly from content addition, as the industry volumes were tepid in this quarter. The major content addition comes in new business, especially in brakes and suspension segments with OEMs such as TVS, Royal Enfield, HMSI, Suzuki and Hero MotoCorp.

items.statement: Maharashtra PSI 2019 scheme: ₹606 crore eligibility certified till Sep 2025; ₹32.91 crore incentive booked in Q1 FY26
items.quote: under the Ma harashtra PSI 2019 scheme, we received an eligibility certificate of ₹ 606 crores for CAPEX incurred till September 2025. items.statement: Acquired balance 38.5% stake in Maxwell; now 100% owner; cornerstone of electronics/energy business

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 34% in Q1 FY26, up 164 bps YoY and 382 bps QoQ, supported by farm gate price correction and higher realizations
items.quote: In Q1 of FY 26, gross profit increased by 47% year-on-year and 48% quarter-on-quarter to INRSS crores with a gross margin of 34%. The margin improved by 164 bps year-on-year and 382 bps quarter-on-quarter, supported by the correction in farm gate prices mainly and also the growth in realizations.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 66% YoY and 137% QoQ to INR 18 crores in Q1 FY26

items.quote: In Q1 of FY '26, the average gross shrimp purchase prices were around INR320 per kilo, which is up by 8% year-on-year, but down 11% quarter-on-quarter, with prices correcting sharply in April 2025 following the global trade uncertainties before recovering thereafter.

items.statement: Part of realization growth attributed to currency depreciation, though marginal

items.statement: Renewable curtailment risk; prioritizing project locations to avoid curtailment; BESS at Barauni on cost-plus basis for grid stability

items.statement: Management expects FY25-26 to be a very robust year with strong growth
items.quote: We are quite confident that FY25-26 will be a very robust year.

items.quote: Q1FY25-26 Revenue is Rs. 26.08 crore which is higher by 25.5% as compared to last year's Q1 revenue of Rs. 20.77 crore.

items.quote: EBITDA is Rs. 1.58 crore for the Q1 of FY25-26. EBITDA of the last year's Q1 was Rs. 27 lakh.

items.statement: Q1 FY25-26 PBT turned positive at Rs 1.3 crore versus slightly negative previous quarter

items.statement: Q2 FY25-26 is also looking good supporting confidence in strong full year

items.statement: Website traffic grew 90% year-on-year with 11 million users and strong social media engagement

items.statement: Founder family holds 61.79% entitlement; son drives digital transformation and heads subsidiary

items.statement: Four-year revenue CAGR of 22.6% with FY24 revenue at Rs 87.7 crore

items.statement: US business expected to perform exceptionally well for FY26

items.quote: Biogas in India, a lot of activity is going on by government incentives to set up more and more biogas plants for waste management.

items.quote: We are supplying products in the sector. Only thing is, these are new sectors. So, like everything new begins, small, but we see a great potential future in this also.

items.statement: Chinese imports in India not significant or large

items.statement: Exploring AI for plant process efficiency improvements
items.quote: We are definitely exploring AI as the aspect of improving our processes and more efficiency at the plant level.

items.statement: UAE business facing headwinds, expected to remain moderate

items.statement: Q1 consolidated revenue Rs 386.9 crore, up 12.9% YoY

items.quote: PAT for the quarter stood at Rs. 51.6 crore, up 84.9% YoY. This includes an exceptional gain of Rs. 12.6 crore representing an Employee Retention Credit (ERC) received by CP Industries, our US subsidiary.

items.statement: Q1 standalone revenue Rs 237 crore, up 20.9% YoY, PAT Rs 26.1 crore, up 122.8% YoY

items.statement: US revenue Rs 109 crore, up 21% YoY, EBIT Rs 27 crore, up 83% YoY
items.quote: The US business also performed remarkably well with revenues of Rs. 109 crores, up 21% YoY and EBIT at Rs. 27 crores, up 83% YoY.

items.quote: The Company continues to invest in network and will accelerate broader capex plans of Rs. 500–550 billion over three years that we have been mentioning previously once we tie up the bank debt.

items.statement: Post-September 2025 capex limited to internal cash generation (~Rs 21-22 billion per quarter) unless new funding secured
items.quote: Broadly, yes, there are other pluses and minuses. But yes, directionally, yes.

items.quote: the subscriber decline was restricted to 0.5 million during the quarter i.e. ~90% lower compared to ~5 million each in Q2 and Q3 of last financial year, marking our strongest performance since merger.

items.statement: 4G subscribers reached 127.4 million; added 1 million 4G subscribers in Q1 FY26 despite overall subscriber loss
items.quote: The number of 4G subscribers has also reached 127.4 mn during the quarter.

items.statement: Data traffic grew 10.4% YoY overall and 11.2% YoY per 4G subscriber
items.quote: On the back of these plans, the data traffic has grown by 10.4% YoY at overall level and 11.2% at per 4G subscriber level.

items.statement: Consumer ARPU increased 14.9% YoY to Rs 177
items.quote: The Consumer ARPU has shown a YoY increase of 14.9% reaching Rs. 177.

items.statement: Launched Non-Stop Hero Plan with Unlimited Data 24x7 pan-India; expanded Vi Guarantee Program to unlimited voice users with extra validity
items.quote: Our portfolio of digital -first offerings for prepaid users gained momentum, w ith the Non -Stop Hero Plan offering Unlimited Data 24x7 now active pan India.

items.statement: Added Netflix subscription to Vi Max Family Plan (Rs 871) with 120GB monthly data pool, unlimited night data and data rollover up to 400GB
items.quote: For postpaid customers, catering to the growing demand for best -in-class OTT experience, we have added a Netflix subscription as a fixed recurring benefit to Vi Max Family Plan.

items.statement: International roaming packs now available in 144 countries (up from 129); unlimited data and calls in 40 countries (up 11); partnered with Blue Ribbon Bags for baggage protection
items.quote: Our roaming packs are now available in 144 countries worldwide vs 129 earlier. I am very pleased to share that we are the only operator offering truly unlimited data and calls, and with 11 countries added to this category the total count with unlimited data and calls has increased to 40.

items.statement: AI engine flagged over 450 million SMSes as spam Jan-Jun 2025; launched industry-first feature displaying country of origin for incoming international calls
items.quote: From Jan - June this year, our AI engine flagged over 450 Mn SMSes as spam, protecting users before any harm could reach them.

items.statement: Secured 10-year contract with Genus Power Infrastructure for 5 million smart meters — India's largest smart metering win
items.quote: We secured a 10-year contract with Genus Power Infrastructure Ltd for 5 million smart meters—India's largest smart metering win.

items.statement: Postpaid subscriber base grew ~1.1 million QoQ, largely driven by M2M with positive consumer postpaid additions
items.quote: As far as the postpaid subscribers are concerned, we have a growth of about 1.1 million quarter-on-quarter. Large part of this comes from the M2M, which is a fast -growing stream, but it also has positive additions on the consumer postpaid side.

items.statement: Strategic collaboration with AST SpaceMobile for satellite-based mobile broadband to all smartphones
items.quote: we announced a strategic collaboration with AST SpaceMobile to deliver satellite -based mobile broadband to all smartphones.

items.statement: Partnership with Airtel for eSIM strategy enabling dual SIM functionality for resilient enterprise deployments
items.quote: We also enhanced our ESIM strategy through a partnership with Airtel, enabling dual SIM f unctionality to support resilient, future -ready enterprise deployments.

items.statement: Managed services agreement with Hewlett Packard Enterprise for comprehensive managed WLAN and security solutions
items.quote: We also advanced our capabilities in enterprise networking through a strategic managed services agreement with Hewlett Packard Enterprise.

items.statement: Partnership with Genesys and Startele for Vi Business CCaaS (AI-powered cloud contact centre as a service)
items.quote: Our partnerships with Genesys and Startele underscore our commitment to best-in-class technology.

items.statement: Google Workspace rollout with Professional Services for modern workplace solutions
items.quote: In cloud and collaboration, the rollout of Google Workspace with Professional Services strengthens our proposition for modern workplace solutions.

items.statement: Vi Finance launched on Vi App offering Personal Loans, Fixed Deposits and Credit Cards via partnership with Aditya Birla Capital
items.quote: we have just rolled out 'Vi Finance' on Vi App where we are now off ering Personal Loans, Fixed Deposits and Credit Cards to our users. For loans, we have entered into a strategic partnership with Aditya Birla Capital.

items.statement: Bank debt reduced to Rs 19.3 billion as of June 30, 2025 from Rs 23.3 billion previous quarter
items.quote: The debt from banks has further reduced to Rs. 19.3 billion as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Deferred spectrum liability ~Rs 119,000 crore and AGR liability ~Rs 76,000 crore as of June 2025, totaling ~Rs 195,000 crore
items.quote: The outstanding as of end of June is about INR 1 19,000 crores for deferred payment towards spectrum, and about INR 76,000 crore for the AGR. So, totalling up to about INR 195,000 crores.

items.statement: Actively engaged with lenders for debt funding; recent spectrum dues conversion to equity and credit rating upgrade supporting discussions
items.quote: We remain actively engaged with our lenders for tying up debt funding towards the execution of our long -term network expansion plan. The recent conversion of spectrum auction dues into equity an d the credit rating upgrade have supported these discussions to move forward.

items.statement: Also exploring non-banking funding sources for shorter timeframe to maintain capex continuity
items.quote: we are looking at nonbanking sources of funding also, not the full amount of INR 25,000 crores that we have talked about, but a lesser amount so that we can continue with the Capex cycle.

items.statement: Akshaya Moondra stepping down as CEO; Abhijit Kishore appointed new CEO effective this call
items.quote: Talking about Abhijit, he has been the Chi ef Operating Officer of the Company since November 2021. In this role he has created a steady and focused impact on the business, and driven operational rigor.

items.statement: Revenue grew 4.9% YoY to Rs 110.2 billion; cash EBITDA improved 3.7% YoY to Rs 21.8 billion; reported EBITDA Rs 46.1 billion vs Rs 42 billion in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The revenue for the quarter was Rs. 110.2 billion registering a growth of 4.9% on YoY basis. The cash EBITDA of Rs. 21.8 billion improved by 3.7% on YoY basis. The reported EBIDTA for the quarter was Rs. 46.1 billion as compared to Rs. 42 billion in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Bank funding discussions require clarity on AGR dues; seeking resolution before March 2026 deadline to enable bank financing
items.quote: The banks are currently looking for some clarity on the AGR front. So that is where we are engaged with the government.

items.statement: Smart meter order book stands at over ₹3,000 crore backed by RDSS and AMISP orders
items.quote: Our smart meter order book stands at over ₹3,000 crore, backed by the government's push on RDSS with major AMISP orders lined up for us.

items.statement: Metering revenues lower in Q1 due to dispatch clearance delays and monsoon slowdowns; expect pickup in H2 FY26
items.quote: In Q1, revenues were a bit lower as a few dispatch clearances got delayed, with slowdowns due to the monsoon as well. These are timing issues, not structural ones, and we expect things to pick up immediately in H2 of FY26, as these projects move forward.

items.statement: Expect sequential growth from Q1 to Q2 FY26 with H2 stronger; July was a good month
items.quote: Based on how Q2 is shaping up, we expect it to be much stronger than Q1, and historically H2 has always been better. I don't see any reason for delays this time.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margins expanded 230 bps, EBITDA margin up 85 bps, PAT up 8.5% to ₹18.5 crore
items.value: 230 bps gross, 85 bps EBITDA, PAT ₹18.5 crore
items.quote: At the consolidated level, revenues were down slightly by 2.5%, but profitability improved. Gross margins expanded by 230 basis points, EBITDA margin by 85 basis points, and PAT was up 8.5% to ₹18.5 crore.

items.statement: C&I segment margins crossed 11% driven by stable commodity prices, design improvements, centralised procurement and volume leverage
items.quote: Yes, we have seen a slight improvement in margins. Commodity prices have been fairly stable, particularly in the Wires and Cables segment. Copper remains somewhat volatile, but in this industry, any movement in copper prices, whether up or down, eventually gets passed on to the consumer.

items.statement: Debtor days reduced by 28 days and net working capital down ₹60 crore in last 12 months despite sales growth
items.value: 28 days debtor reduction, ₹60 crore net WC reduction
items.quote: In the past 12 months alone, our debtor days have reduced by 28 days, and overall net working capital is down by about ₹60 crores, despite sales growth.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio comfortable at 0.69; borrowings reduced over last 12 months; two rating upgrades lowered borrowing costs
items.quote: Our debt-equity ratio is comfortable at 0.69. Interest costs have also come down, and if you look at our borrowings over the last 12 months, they have reduced as well. This has been a conscious decision.

items.statement: Target C&I revenue to cross ₹1,000 crore by FY28; retailer target of 100,000 by FY26 (currently 85,000+)
items.quote: by FY28, we expect the Consumer & Industrial business to cross ₹1,000 crore in revenues, which would make it a very meaningful part of our overall business. Channel expansion remains a priority, three years ago we set ourselves the target of reaching 100,000 retailers, and with over 85,000 already onboard, we should achieve that by FY26.

items.statement: Smart meter program at ~10% penetration: 3 crore installed out of 22.5 crore sanctioned; final requirement expected to exceed 30 crore meters
items.quote: About 3 crore meters have been installed so far, out of roughly 22.5 crore sanctioned meters. By the time the program reaches its final stages, requirements are expected to exceed 30 crore meters. That means we are only about 10% into the opportunity.

items.statement: Open market with new entrants but quality and 30-year experience provide edge; AMISPs prioritize meter reliability due to 7-8 year SLAs
items.quote: Designing and manufacturing smart meters is highly specialized work. Our strength lies in over 30 years of active experience, which has enabled us to consistently deliver zero-defect products that can be deployed with any AMISP or utility.

items.statement: Strengthened R&D team with senior experts; over 100 engineers in metering R&D; dedicated R&D teams across all verticals
items.quote: We had over 100 engineers dedicated to metering alone, working on communication and related technologies. Building on that, we recently opened a new R&D centre at our Kundli facility focused on switchgear and lighting. Today, every one of our product verticals, wires and cables, domestic switchgear, lighting, and metering, has dedicated R&D teams in place.

items.statement: Investing in backward integration for critical smart meter components; value addition higher than government mandates
items.quote: On the component side, especially for smart metering, we are committed to backward integration for all critical parts. Our value addition in India is already higher than government mandates, and we continue to expand in that direction.

items.statement: Copper price volatility passed on to consumers with short time lag; stable commodity prices supporting margins
items.quote: Copper remains somewhat volatile, but in this industry, any movement in copper prices, whether up or down, eventually gets passed on to the consumer. The impact on us is therefore minimal, apart from a short time lag.

items.statement: Zero-defect process implemented across factories; meters built for 10-year life cycles meeting warranty requirements
items.quote: In fact, over the last two to three years, we've implemented a zero-defect process across our factories, and we can confidently claim our meters are built for 10-year life cycles. This gives us the confidence that our products can meet international quality standards, including in developed markets.

items.statement: Revenue recognized at time of supply to AMISP; installation by AMISP does not impact revenue recognition
items.quote: Our revenue is booked at the time of supply. Once we bill and deliver the meters to the AMISP, the revenue is recognized. The actual installation of the meters at the consumer end is managed by the AMISP and does not impact our revenue recognition.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 25% year-on-year for current year FY26
items.quote: In terms of top line, we see ourselves growing at 25% year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion guidance of 75-100 bps year-on-year for next few years
items.quote: For bottom line, we see margin of opportunity of 75 bps to 100 bps year-on-year each year for the next few years.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 gross margin expanded to 21.4% from 20.2% YoY and 15% QoQ
items.quote: Gross margin expanded to 21.4% up from 20.2% year-on-year and a sharp improvement from 15% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 11.3% vs 10.8% YoY and 6.8% QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margin at 11.3% compared to 10.8% in Q1 FY25 and 6.8% in Q4 FY25, demonstrating operating leverage.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 PAT margin improved to 5.94% with PAT of INR185 million up 55% YoY
items.quote: Consequently, profitability is scaled up meaningfully with PAT at INR185 million of 55% year-on-year and 28% quarter-on-quarter and PAT margins improved to 5.94%.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue INR3,123 million, up 22% YoY on robust demand and improved realization
items.quote: In Q1 FY26 company has delivered a revenue of INR3,123 million, marking healthy 22% growth year-on-year on the back of robust demand and improved realization.

items.statement: Volume growth of 17-18% YoY in Q1 FY26 with 127,000 ICT devices refurbished
items.quote: So, in quarter one, we have done a total volume of about 1,27,000-odd ICT devices.

items.statement: Volume growth trajectory expected at 25-27% similar to revenue growth
items.quote: So, we anticipate that this number in terms of numeric numbers of units is likely to be in a similar trajectory in terms of growth rate 25% to 27-odd-percent.

items.statement: Incremental capex for 25% growth over next 2-3 years not beyond INR15 crores
items.quote: Over the next 2 to 3 years, the total incremental cost that we see for setting up the incremental facility to cater towards this growth is not likely to be beyond INR15 crores.

items.statement: Capacity not a constraint; modular expansion possible in 2-3 months with rented facilities
items.quote: Our ability to expand capacities, the cost of expanding these capacities and capabilities is not a significant, significant cost. This is something that can be done in the next expansion of capacities can be done in two, three months time.
