items.statement: Next year can be glorious with GST cuts and export momentum
items.quote: The second half can be better and the next year can be glorious I can say.

items.statement: US dairy imports unlikely to threaten due to vegetarian consumer preferences and feeding differences
items.quote: I am doubtful about the US entry of dairy products into India. The type of feeding what they do is different and consumer here is vegetarian and they have their own reservation for any US product.

items.statement: New Zealand poses bigger import threat than US if dairy sector opens up
items.quote: New Zealand will be a bigger threat if imports ar e going to take place. I don't expect US to be

items.statement: Current 12% GST results in 108 rupees tax per liter versus 888 rupees farmer gets for ghee/SNP
items.quote: It is almost 108 rupees for a liter of sorry 108 rupees tax versus 888 the farmer gets if you are converting it to ghee and also SNP.

items.statement: Ice cream sees 73% of price paid as GST to government
items.quote: If you take ice cream , for example, if we are paying about 888 almost 73% is paid as GST to the government.

items.statement: GST reduction will bridge urban-rural gap and improve farmer cash flow for better production
items.quote: If we are reducing it, we can be a world power in exports and farmer will also be benefited and the urban rural gap will be bridged in a big way and farmer ultimately will start spending on other commodities once when the cash flow improves.

items.statement: FY26 bitumen volume guidance maintained at around 6 lakh tons, implying ~10% growth over FY25
items.quote: As explained in my last concall also, though we have a shortfall of 50,000 MT in the Ist Quarter, we assume that by the end of this year, we should be able to achieve the growth as predicted in the earlier con-call. So, we should be able to do around 6 lakh tons.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA per ton guidance maintained at minimum Rs 4,300 for the year
items.quote: EBITDA still remains around same level that we had given in the lst Quarter, more than 4,300 for the year.

items.statement: FY28 volume doubling target from FY25 levels remains unchanged despite Q1 disruptions
items.quote: Given these factors, the guidance for FY28 still remains the same because this last quarter was one of the quarters which is affected due to geopolitical situation which may not arise every year. Hence, our guidance remains the same for FY28.

items.statement: Q1 bitumen demand softened due to early monsoon onset slowing construction activity
items.quote: The early onset of the monsoon season in India further slowed construction activities, leading to a softer demand for bitumen.

items.statement: No structural demand problem; lower Q1 consumption was weather-driven and temporary
items.quote: As I have explained, there is no problem in terns of demand for the product. But if you are Seeing tthe weather conditions, which from the month of May, the monsoons have arrived earlier this year, hence there was a low demand of product because construction activities do

items.statement: Shipping EBITDA margin fell because fixed costs remained while vessels were idle due to geopolitical disruptions
items.quote: Fixed costs remain the same in any business that you do. Even in the shipping side, your fixed cost of wages, crew, the shipping operation, everything remains the same irrespective whether the vessel is moving or not. As explained due to the geopolitical situations, when the vessels were not moving, but your fixed cost remains the same and you tend to lose on the revenues because the voyages are n

items.statement: Shipping margins expected to bounce back in Q3-Q4 as vessel utilization improves
items.quote: It will bounce back. As and when we start increasing the volumes and the vessels are utilized 100%. all the numbers and EBITDA that we used to see in the earlier quarters, you will be able to see in the next three quarters.

items.statement: Government targets Rs 7 lakh crore project awards in FY26 and Rs 10 lakh crore annually thereafter, supporting bitumen demand
items.quote: The government has set ambitious targets with projects award expected to reach Rs. 7 lakh crores by FY26 and scaling up to Rs. 10 lakh annually thereafter.

items.statement: Acquired Konkan Storage Systems for over Rs 30 crore capex; facility has 24,000+ ton capacity with B&C class licenses
items.quote: The new acquisition is having existing capacity of more than 24,000 tons and the total Capex will be more than Rs. 30 crores in this.

items.statement: Mangalore 40,000 MT storage build and Karwar acquisition funded entirely from internal accruals
items.quote: That is one of the reasons we are putting Mangalore and Karwar projects wherein as on date the Company is funded all the cost of these two projects through their internal accruals.

items.statement: Current vessel capacity can handle 5-6 lakh tons annually; third-party vessels still used to supplement
items.quote: We can easily do five to six lakh tons.

items.statement: Vessel fleet operates ~8 months/year due to monsoon; east coast voyages take 40-45 days per cycle
items.quote: when we are going to the eastern coast of India, it takes around 40 to 45 days for us to complete the one cycle of bitumen supply towards east and we are working only during eight months in the year, four months of the monsoons, we are not bringing any product into India or you can say lower volumes moved into India.

items.statement: Company will continue acquiring vessels opportunistically as third-party charters are still needed
items.quote: Yes, as explained in all my earlier concall, as and when we get any good opportunity for acquiring any new vessels, the Company will definitely go for it, because we still require vessels as we are taking from third-parties.

items.statement: Bitumen segment contributed Rs 496 crore (83.5% of revenue) at 1,24,600 MT; shipping contributed Rs 72 crore (12.1%)
items.quote: During the quarter, bitu1men volumes were at 1,24,600 MT, which were lower than anticipated volumes due to certain external factors. Despite these challenges, the bitumen segment remain the largest contributor, generating Rs. 496 crores in revenue. The shipping segment also played a key role, contributing Rs. 72 crores or 12.1% of total revenue.

items.statement: Tax provisioning variance between quarters due to advance tax norms linked to volume levels, not tax law changes
items.quote: The difference between Q1 and Q4 is basically due to the volumes. As we assume in Q4, when we see that the volumes are high, as does the taxation, we have to pay higher taxes as per the advance tax norms by the income tax. Hence, you see the differences. But the tax slab remains the sane.

items.statement: Acquired 100% of Konkan Storage Systems (Karwar, Karnataka) to save rental costs at existing leased tankages
items.quote: We are already operating at both the places, even in Karwar and Mangalore, both the places are giving almost 35% to 40% of the Company's revenue every year, and at both the places, we are having tankages on lease. Hence, we have acquired existing Company in Karwar and building our own storage in Mangalore. That will cotribute in saving of our rental expenses that we are paying towards the operatio

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions (India-Pakistan, Middle East) caused ~15-day trade loss and ~1 month shipping impact in Q1
items.quote: Geopolitical tensions, particularly between India and Pakistan, led to disruption in trade flows and shipping schedules, resulting in an estimated loss of 1 5-days. Additionally, geopolitical tensions across the USA, Iran, the Middle East and Israel disrupted regional trade, particularly affecting the UAE and the wider Middle East, causing nearly one month of impact on shipping movements.

items.statement: Dry docking of two vessels completed in FY26; 15,000-30,000 MT capacity impact per vessel per year is normal
items.quote: This year dry dock of two vessels is already being completed as on date.

items.statement: Private sector bitumen market share nearly 20%; bulk imports fell 89-90% in Q1 while drum imports rose 3%
items.quote: With a private sector bitumen market share of nearly 20%, AICL is strategically positioned to capture the opportunities arising from India's growing intrastructure demand.

items.statement: No liquidity issues; internal accruals funding all current capex projects
items.quote: Absolutely no problem in terms of liquidity.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton was Rs 4,100 in FY25; guidance maintained at minimum Rs 4,300 for FY26 despite higher depreciation from new vessel
items.quote: We had around 4.100 in FY24-25. The guidance earlier was given at 4,500. We still maintain. However, we would be adding a disclaimer at minimum 4,300.

items.statement: Market share loss in Q1 attributed to bulk import decline (89-90%) not drum imports; no structural share erosion
items.quote: The increase that you are saying is in terms of drums, not in bulk, and the bulk volune still was lower by almost 89% to 10% in the lst Quarter.

items.statement: Konkan Storage acquisition subject to regulatory approvals and share purchase agreement execution
items.quote: Subject to regulatory approvals and the execution of the share purchase agreement, Konkan Storage Systems will become the Wholly owned subsidiary of AICL.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs.21,100 crores including Rs.1,500 crores ship repair and Rs.19,600 crores shipbuilding across 75 vessels
items.quote: Our order book remains good at about Rs.21 ,100 crores. This includes ship repair order book also of approximately Rs.1,500 crores. The balance out of the Rs.21,100 crores is the shipbuilding order book which is about Rs.19,600 crores across 75 vessels in the Kochi facility, the Udupi CSL and the Hooghly CSL.

items.statement: Guided FY26 top line growth of 14-15% and PAT margin around 15%
items.quote: Top line, for the current year from where we were last year, we consider 14 % to 15% top line growth.

items.statement: Guided FY26 EBITDA margin around 20% and PAT margin around 15%, lower than FY24 due to absence of aircraft carrier projects
items.quote: So, the EBITDA will be around 20%, that is what we guide overall.

items.statement: Completed Rs.3,250 crores capex cycle over last seven years; further capex planned over next five years for growth beyond 2030-31
items.quote: We have already complete d almost a Rs.3,250 crores of CAPEX cycle across the two facilities and some of our subsidiaries. So, that has been done over the last, say, about seven years, that is completed.

items.quote: The new ISRF, as we are speaking, we have… Rajesh, how many vessels? Rajesh Gopalakrishnan: 14 vessels. Shri Madhu S Nair: 14 vessels are under various stages of repair in the ISRF. When we say this, we say that the total strength of ISRF is 82 ships per

items.quote: On the HD KSOE side, as we are moving forward, there will be CAPEX in, as I said, new workstation facilities. We are discussing this. We are not in a position to comment at this stage, but there will be more CAPEX.

items.quote: So, for ISRF, we hope in about the initial 18 to 24 months we sh ould go to about Rs.250 crores of extra revenue. And then, full blown condition, we go to about a Rs.600-plus crores.

items.quote: Exports are very important as part of our long -term strategy because we are focused on a specialist vessel export into Europe and we are also now along with potential partners like HD KSOE from Korea we are looking at the merchant vessel export segment also.

items.quote: With Drydocks World UAE, M oU was signed to explore the development of ship repair clusters at Kochi and Vadinar. items.quote: IAC -2, again, we are not in a position to convey anything. I can say that there are no fresh developments to report. That is all I can say. I think we are hopeful, but we are not in a position to hazard a guess on the timelines.

items.quote: Again, as I said, we are not building to stock. It is actually we bid for projects and once the projects come in we tap our supply chain. So, we are exposed only between the bidding stage and till the construction phase.

items.statement: Continuous multi-level skilling for workmen and capability development for officers and supervisors ongoing
items.quote: Yes, Very much. We have continuously the multiple levels of skilling for the workmen. There are capability and capacity development for the officers and supervisors. So, that is an ongoing process and we are putting in quite some effort in that direction.

items.quote: It is not yet completed. In fact, we are facing some challenges in the delivery timelines on that vessel. But in the next one month, we are launching that vessel. That vessel is at advanced stages of construction.

items.statement: US Navy Master Ship Repair Agreement discussions ongoing; no concluded repair engagement yet
items.quote: We have the master ship repair agreement with the US Navy. There are discussions ongo ing, but we are probably not in a position to comment. We have not concluded any ship repair engagement with them as of today.

items.statement: Long-term guidance 10-12% growth over 5-10 years; confident to double turnover by 2030-31
items.quote: Generally, we say a guidance of 10 % to 12%, which is what we have seen in this industry. This industry has got a cyclical nature. Factoring all of those, we are confident to guide a 10 to 12 -year growth prospects over the next five to 10 years or more.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 demand was muted due to unpredictable weather and global developments impacting consumer sentiment
items.quote: The 1st Quarter of FY '26 brought a mix of external factors, including unpredictable weather and certain global developments, which had some impact on overall consumer sentiment, resulting in muted demand during the quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin was 47.7% in Q1 FY26, impacted by promotional discounts to support volumes in soft demand
items.quote: Gross profit stood at Rs. 456.4 million, with a gross margin of 47.7%. The margin was affected by promotional discounts offered during the quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to improve in Q2 FY26 as festive season starts with no discounts, then remain in 48-49% range for H2

items.quote: But in the next quarter, there will be improvement in the gross margin because the festive week there will be no discount. But during the 3rd Quarter and 4th Quarter, depending on the market, we have to decide on the discount. And the margin will remain more or less in the range of 48% to 49%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin potential of 15-16% achievable if sales value remains constant
items.quote: But had it been the same sale, 15% to 16% was easily achievable. So if the value of the sales remains constant, then again we have the potential of doing around 16% EBITDA margin in retail business.

items.quote: We entered into a strategic partnership with Skechers during the quarter. items.quote: Because since the franchisee sale, in the secondary sale of franchises has already is dipping, so the primary sales from our side was little bit less compared to the last quarter. Because otherwise it tantamounts to holding stock at the franchisee level.

items.quote: Below Rs. 1,000 would be around 70%.

items.quote: So, this year we are opening some Company-owned outlets, around 7 to 10 Company-owned outlets. But more aggressive opening has been planned, we have started these TFM franchises, so we are planning more aggressive store launches in that.

items.quote: We have already submitted the application to the BSE and NSE. Now the BSE will come up with any questions. So, if they come with questions, then we will reply to them. I think by the end of this month or early September we will have approval from BSE or NSE.

items.statement: Non-BIS inventory mostly cleared; remaining being liquidated through discounts
items.quote: Mostly we have cleared all the BIS. Some element will be there, means, now we are giving good discount so it will be liquidated, if there is some Non-BIS.

items.quote: Recently, we crossed this Rs.1,000 crores consolidated order book milestone with marquee clients such as CPWD, NPCC and TCIL, many of which are repeated orders. Nearly 90% of our portfolio comprises funded central government projects, ensuring strong cash flow visibility and reduced working capital risk.

items.statement: New projects are direct contracts with no JV expenses, expected to maintain current EBITDA margins and add 1-2% from direct execution.
items.quote: pattern, we will be able to maintain the EBITDA and PAT margin, that will also increase because now the projects are coming directly to our company not through JVs, so, that will also add some percentage by 1% or 2% by this

items.statement: Repeat clients include NBCC (third project), CPWD, NPCC, TCIL; new clients IIT Kanpur and Haryana Cricket Association.
items.quote: See, like this Rs.450 crores, one order book is for NBCC. It Is a repeat customer. We are doing two projects and this is the third project in hand of NBCC and we have completed two old projects of NBCC also. So, these are repeat customers. IIT Kanpur is not a repeat customer. We are doing first time in IIT Kanpur. But again

items.statement: Selective bidding on complex, high-profitability projects; targets single projects of Rs.300-400 cr while maintaining EBITDA thresholds.
items.quote: We always look to bid a single project of Rs.300-400 crores. That is what our next target is, but again, keeping our EBITDA and margin in line. So until we get that threshold we do not bid and we do not quote.

items.statement: Focus on institutional, healthcare, railway, airport, stadium projects; no immediate plan to enter roads sector.
items.quote: We are already doing that. We have done metro. We are already doing airport. We are already doing railway station. So, we are already in fact, in these sectors. The roads is one sector which we are not into and we do not have an immediate plan of entering into that.

items.statement: Head office cost is minor fixed cost; staff and labor transferred across 15 sites to manage project delays.
items.quote: Most fixed prices are staff, if one project gets delayed, we transfer our staff to different locations and transfer the labor. So, as such, the head office cost is only fixed cost, which is very minor and there is no threshold of fixed cost and maybe one month we see if the project is stopped due to any reason, any political, anything, any issue, then we transfer our staffto a different location w

items.statement: Targeting overall topline growth of over 25% in FY26 and at least 20% year-over-year from FY27 onwards
items.quote: We are targeting an overall topline growth of over 25% in FY 2026. Further, with a strong increase in the exports expected in the current fiscal, we are confident of further improving our EBITDA margins in FY 2026.

items.statement: Targeting at least 20% export mix of topline in next 2 years (FY27) over and above domestic growth
items.quote: Next 2 years, we want to target at least 20% of our topline to come from exports, even after factoring full domestic growth.

items.statement: Order book of Rs. 843 crores as of July 1, 2025: PEB Rs. 634 crores, Proflex Rs. 209 crores; export orders Rs. 123 crores
items.quote: As it is seen, we have a strong order book of around Rs. 843 crores as of July 1st of 2025, comprising of Phoenix which is our PEB division that has an order book of Rs. 634 crores and Proflex division which is our self-supported roofing having pending orders of around 209.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 new order intake: Proflex Rs. 80 crores, Phoenix Rs. 196.80 crores, total Rs. 277.62 crores; targeting minimum Rs. 1,200 crores new orders for full year
items.quote: So 1st quarter, we have got new order intake in Proflex division to the tune of Rs. 80 crores and in Phoenix Rs. 196.80 crores, so totaling to Rs. 277.62 crores.

items.statement: Sanand Brownfield expansion of 20,000 tons/year for North American exports targeting Q1 FY27 operational; Cheyyar Brownfield expansion of 20,000 tons/year targeting Q1 FY28; Proflex adding mobile units in FY26 and FY27
items.quote: We have also decided to augment our Proflex capacity by procuring additional mobile units in the current fiscal over and above our existing 14 mobile units. Thus, we are committed to fully capitalize on the available growth opportunities in India as well as outside of India.

items.statement: Total estimated CAPEX of Rs. 130 crores for Sanand and Cheyyar expansions plus Rs. 25-30 crores additional from cash accruals, total around Rs. 150 crores
items.quote: We have done Rs. 130 crores estimated CAPEX. There will be another Rs. 20, Rs. 25-Rs. 30 crores of CAPEX, which is not planned as a part of IPO, but which we will do. So you can take it around Rs. 150 crores

items.statement: Sanand PEB capacity 72,000 tons, Cheyyar 32,000 tons; Cheyyar to add 15,000-18,000 tons incremental production in FY26; Sanand expansion 20,000 tons by Q1 FY27; Cheyyar expansion 20,000 tons by Q1 FY28
items.quote: In the current fiscal year, Cheyyar will be operating for the full year, and therefore we will get the benefit of the incremental production from Cheyyar anywhere in between 15,000-18,000 metric tons in the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Optimal utilization 75-78% of installed capacity; revenue potential ~4x of CAPEX; Sanand utilization target 60-70% in Cheyyar this year
items.quote: So both our businesses, optimally, we can push at about between 75% and 78% of our installed capacity, depending on the product mix that we receive.

items.statement: Export margins 1.5-2x domestic margins; blended margin improvement expected but not committing to specific 2% improvement; directionally northward
items.quote: So I have a rider here. So, Malav made a general statement. All orders will not come but his margin profile in export is at least 1.5-2x than what we are getting in India, which order may be a little more competitive.

items.statement: Domestic PEB realization ~Rs. 119,000-120,000/ton; export realization $2,500-2,700/ton vs US competitors $3,500-3,600/ton; Proflex realization ~Rs. 1,900/sqm
items.quote: Around Rs. 119,000 to Rs. 120,000 on the domestic front, export will be definitely higher.

items.statement: FY25 exports Rs. 65 crores; targeting 3x increase in FY26; Rs. 125 crores export orders on hand plus equal amount expected in 2-3 months; Canada market entry with CWB certification; Africa potential in 1-2 years
items.quote: As against FY 2025 exports of around Rs. 65 crores, this year we are targeting to increase the exports by more than three times to the US.

items.statement: Sectoral tariff 50% on steel/aluminum applies to all countries; customer bears tariff; no order cancellations; still price competitive vs US manufacturers with $4,000-5,000/ton arbitrage
items.quote: We believe that in spite of the tariff and the higher freight cost that is involved in delivering the PEBs to the US, we are still price competitive as compared to the prices quoted by the US manufacturers, and our margins in the US are still higher than the margins earned in India.

items.statement: Strong demand from US market with presence on East Coast working with GCs; Canada market entry after CWB certification; India demand from railways (Vande Bharat sheds, RUBs), agri warehousing (PACS), SME segment, Southern states industrial
items.quote: We have been working quite extensively, quite hard in developing the US market over the last few years, and I am happy to state that as we speak, we have a strong presence in the East Coast of the US and I am closely working with a large number of general contractors.

items.statement: Railway opportunity: Rs. 35 crores Proflex order book for Vande Bharat/platforms; 20,000 level crossings to be converted to RUBs; agri warehousing via PACS massive opportunity
items.quote: Yes, the railway part is about Rs. 35 crores of Proflex. It would be a mix of Vande Bharat plus some platforms, etc., but Rs. 35 crores of Proflex outstanding.

items.statement: Net working capital 55 days as of June 30, 2025 vs 32 days March 31, 2025; creditors 98 days (90 days open credit + 180 days buyers credit); Proflex carries 4-4.5 months raw material inventory
items.quote: The net working capital stood at 55 days as of 30 June 2025 as against 32 days as of 31 March 2025.

items.statement: Working capital well managed with 5-6 turns; practically debt free with CC utilization 0.5-0.8%; using low-cost buyers credit (6-7%) for flexibility
items.quote: Sir, if you see my working capital days, we are easily doing more than 5 or 6 turns, easily. And we are practically today debt free, even our CC utilization is 0.53.08___.

items.statement: Repaid Rs. 40 crores loan by June and Rs. 20 crores recently; debt almost zero now; IPO proceeds Rs. 259 crores net, Rs. 104 crores utilized by Aug 25
items.quote: I have repaid my loan Rs. 40 crores till June and another Rs. 20 crores we have recently repaid. And then our debt part is almost 0 now as we speak.

items.statement: IPO net proceeds Rs. 259 crores; Rs. 104 crores utilized by Aug 25 for loan repayment and CAPEX; balance deployed in money market instruments
items.quote: If you see my presentation, we have already utilized about Rs. 104 crores after listing on 6th August and we are on 25th August out of Rs. 259 crores of net money available out of my primary portion.

items.statement: PEB sales volume: 14,822 metric tons in Q1 FY26 vs 6,579 in Q1 FY25; Proflex sales volume: 321,050 sqm in Q1 FY26 vs 260,271 in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Phoenix division, sales quantity in Q1 FY '26 was 14,822 metric ton as against 6579 metric ton in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Proflex gross margin 32-33%, domestic PEB 30-32%, export gross margin 40%+; Q1 FY26 console gross margin 33% vs 36% in Q1 FY25 due to low export revenue recognition
items.quote: But I think as a thumb rule, Mr. Vandit Shah, for our domestic business, PEB around 30%-32% is a sustainable gross margin. In Proflex also around 32%-33% and in exports definitely gross margin will be higher, at least 40% and up.

items.statement: 60-70% repeat business from large key clients; preferred supplier to EPC contractors for railway and agri projects; US GC relationships built over 5 years
items.quote: Second, more importantly, I think we are sort of known to handle more complex jobs. And we have an element of repeat business, 60%-70% of large key clients generally are repeat, where there are L3 and L4, we are preferred.

items.statement: Only Indian PEB player with AISC and CWB certifications for US/Canada exports; 5-year US market development with 5-person ground team; early mover advantage from 2017 Swaminarayan Temple project
items.quote: As you may be aware, our Sanand Gujarat facility is the only PEB facility in India which has a certification by the American Institute of Steel Construction, also known as AISC.

items.statement: Proflex approved by Indian Railway Board for Vande Bharat sheds, platforms, and RUBs; PACS mandate for agri warehousing roofing; sectoral tariff 50% applies globally not just India
items.quote: Further, you may be aware our Proflex roofing are now approved by the Indian Railway Board, not only for the Vande Bharat shed or the railway platform, but also for the railway underbridges, which are commonly called RUBs.

items.statement: Trump policy uncertainty on tariffs; conservative guidance due to volatile conditions; potential margin impact if additional duties imposed; working capital cycle elongation risk
items.quote: Our philosophy is to remain a little conservative in guiding. And we have said over 25%. So let us see. See, again, please understand, we are working under extremely volatile conditions. Nobody knows after a few days what Mr. Trump is going to do.

items.statement: Sanand only AISC/CWB certified plant; Cheyyar new territory requiring customer acquisition; HR and manpower balancing for expansions; US team of 5 people on ground
items.quote: Cheyyar plant was set up only last year. So this year, my target is to reach 60%-70% in Cheyyar, for which we have deployed people. There are people working there, there is new territory for us.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of ₹360 crores
items.quote: we have given guidance of around 360 Crores on the top line for the this financial year which still remains in top policy.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 15-15.5% for FY26
items.quote: EBITDA, we are looking at around 15-15.5%, with a PAT of around 5 to 5.5%.

items.statement: Olive Ecopak JV break-even expected in Q3 or Q4 FY26
items.quote: We definitely foresee to break even in quarter three or quarter four.

items.statement: Debt reduction target of ₹15 crores over next 4-5 quarters
items.quote: We expect to bring it down by at least 15 crores in next 4 to 5 quarters.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 12-14 months; focus on debt reduction
items.quote: we'll not be doing any major capex, we'll be doing small capex at Rajshree for next 12 to 14 months. We'd like to consolidate and reduce the debt.

items.statement: Thermoforming capacity expanded by 600 MT to 12,120 MT total
items.quote: we expanded our thermoforming capacity by 600 MT, taking the total to 12,120 MT

items.statement: Unit III at Daman commenced production for PET packaging
items.quote: the company has commenced production at Unit III in Daman during the quarter. This unit shall primarily focus on manufacturing PET packaging products

items.statement: Added 1,800 MTPA sheet extrusion and 650 MTPA thermoforming at Unit III in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We have also added sheet extrusion capacity of 1,800 MTPA and thermoforming capacity of 650 MTPA in the ongoing quarter at Unit III.

items.statement: Sleeving capacity of 500 million pieces per annum and paper wrap-around of 240 million pieces per annum to be added within next two quarters
items.quote: Plus, we look forward to adding Capacity of Sleeving. of 500 Million Pieces Per Annum in 2 months. Ramswaroop Thard: And a new, innovative, technology of paper wrap-around. Ramswaroop Thard: of 240 Million Pieces Per annum

items.quote: extrusion is at 94.22%. Ramswaroop Thard: Thermoforming is approximately at 82%, printing is at 93%, and injection molding, we stretched to 115

items.statement: Added 31 new international and domestic customers in Q1 FY26
items.quote: We also added nearly 31 new international and domestic customers in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: US exports ~₹9-10 crores last quarter; 50% revenue impact feared from tariffs but mitigable via domestic/other markets
items.quote: Our overall export to USA last quarter was around Rupees 9 to 10 Crores. Ramswaroop Thard: So, we, … In short term, we foresee 50% of the revenue may be impacted, but we can cover that through the change in domestic market and other countries

items.statement: Injection moulding revenue expected ₹65-70 crores in FY26 vs ₹42 crores in FY25
items.quote: And we expect this to go to 65 to 70 crores.

items.statement: New capacity lines (injection, sleeving, paper wrap) expected to add ₹20-25 crores and ₹10-15 crores revenue respectively in FY26
items.quote: for the injection molding, we expect around 20-25 Crores of revenue. Ramswaroop Thard: And, additional Thermoforming, Sleeving and paper wrap around In addition, 10 to 15 crores of revenue

items.quote: we are expecting, doing in same line of around 45 to 50 crores for this year also. So, the overall capacity for the barrier is around 65 to 70 crores. Suresh Jain: Correct. Ramswaroop Thard: So, we'll be approximately utilizing 70% of the capacity

items.value: 39 crores equity, 37 crores term loans, 30 crores CC

items.quote: Short run, there can be an impact, but long run, definitely, we have something in place to take care of this

items.statement: Olive Ecopak capacity utilisation: 454 MT converting, 393 MT coating in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Capacity utilisation for the Olive Ecopak , remained at 454 MT for converting and 393 MT for coating.

items.statement: Rajshree Q2 FY26 revenue guidance ₹85-90 crores
items.quote: Q2, we are looking anywhere between 85 to 90 crores of revenue for Rajshree.
